documents.title: 28 Days Later
documents.tagline: His fear began when he woke up alone. His terror began when he realised he wasn't.
documents.overview: Twenty-eight days after a killer virus was accidentally unleashed from a British research facility, a small group of London survivors are caught in a desperate struggle to protect themselves from the infected. Carried by animals and humans, the virus turns those it infects into homicidal maniacs -- and it's absolutely impossible to contain.
documents.plot: Twenty-eight days after a killer virus was accidentally unleashed from a British research facility, a small group of London survivors are caught in a desperate struggle to protect themselves from the infected. Carried by animals and humans, the virus turns those it infects into homicidal maniacs -- and it's absolutely impossible to contain.

documents.title: Saw
documents.tagline: Live or die. Make your choice.
documents.overview: Obsessed with teaching his victims the value of life, a deranged, sadistic serial killer abducts the morally wayward. Once captured, they must face impossible choices in a horrific game of survival. The victims must fight to win their lives back, or die trying...
documents.plot:
Saw is a 2004 American psychological horror film directed by James Wan and written by Leigh Whannell. The film stars Cary Elwes, Danny Glover, Michael Emerson, Ken Leung, and Donnie Wahlberg.

The movie begins with Dr. Lawrence Gordon (Cary Elwes), a successful surgeon who finds himself chained in a run-down industrial bathroom with no recollection of how he got there. He soon discovers that he is not alone, as another prisoner, Adam Faulkner (Leigh Whannell), has also been left chained in the room. The two men are informed by a mysterious figure known as Jigsaw (Tobin Bell) through a video message that they have 60 minutes to escape the room or face a gruesome death.

As the game begins, Gordon and Faulkner realize that they must work together to find a way out of the room. However, their efforts are hindered by the fact that they do not know each other's skills or expertise. The two men start to suspect that Jigsaw is using them in some twisted experiment, but they cannot figure out what it is.

As time runs out, Gordon and Faulkner discover a series of clues left behind by Jigsaw, including a cryptic message on the wall and a hidden key. They also learn that Jigsaw has a personal connection to their lives, having been a successful surgeon himself who became disillusioned with his work.

Throughout the film, the tension builds as Gordon and Faulkner try to outsmart each other and find a way out of the room. However, it becomes clear that one of them will not survive. The film's climax features a shocking twist: Adam is revealed to be Jigsaw's son, who was killed in an accident involving his father.

In the end, Gordon manages to escape the room by using the key to unlock the door and making a desperate bid for freedom. However, as he emerges from the bathroom, he realizes that he has lost his sense of purpose and is now haunted by the memories of what happened in the room.

The film's ending sets the stage for the rest of the Saw franchise, introducing the character of Jigsaw and establishing the theme of the series: that people must face their own mortality and make difficult choices to survive. The movie's success can be attributed to its clever plot twists, tense atmosphere, and memorable performances from the cast.

Overall, Saw is a gripping horror film that explores themes of survival, sacrifice, and redemption. Its twisty plot and suspenseful atmosphere have made it a classic in the horror genre, and its influence can still be seen in many modern horror films.

documents.title: The Interpreter
documents.tagline: The truth needs no translation.
documents.overview: After Silvia Broome, an interpreter at United Nations headquarters, overhears plans of an assassination, an American Secret Service agent is sent to investigate.
documents.plot:
In the fictional Southern African country of Matobo, rebel leader Ajene Xola drives two men, Simon Broome and Philippe, to an abandoned stadium. They discuss how President Edmond Zuwanie's regime has ruthlessly exterminated most of the population and intimidated the survivors into silence. Upon their arrival at the stadium, they find three schoolboys, who point Xola and Simon in the direction of corpses left by Zuwanie's security apparatus, while Philippe stays in the car. When Xola and Simon return to the playing field, they are executed by the boys whose actions connect them to Zuwanie's secret police. Philippe clambers out of the car and hides, taking pictures of a car arriving carrying Zuwanie's lackeys, and then escapes.
Simon's sister, Silvia, works at the United Nations Interpretation Service in New York. A white African born in the United States to a British mother and white Matoban father, she was raised in Matobo and studied in France. Her diverse background leads to UN Security Chief Lee Wu wryly describing her as "being the UN".
The UN is considering indicting Zuwanie, to stand trial in the International Criminal Court. Initially a liberator, over the past 20 years he has become as corrupt and tyrannical as the government he overthrew, and is now responsible for ethnic cleansing. Zuwanie is soon to visit the UN and put forward his own case to the UN General Assembly, in an attempt to avoid the indictment.
A random security scare forces the evacuation of the UN headquarters. When Silvia returns at night to retrieve some personal belongings, she overhears two men discussing an assassination plot in Ku (the Matoban lingua franca). She runs from the building when the men become aware of her presence. The next day, while interpreting in a meeting, Silvia recognizes words from the phrases she overheard the night before. She reports the incident to UN security; the plot's target appears to be Zuwanie.
The US Secret Service assigns Dignitary Protection Division (DPD) agents Tobin Keller and Dot Woods to investigate, as well as protect Zuwanie when he arrives. Zuwanie's personal head of security, former Dutch mercenary Nils Lud, arrives in New York. Keller, whose estranged wife was killed in a car accident just weeks earlier, learns Silvia's parents and sister were killed by landmines laid by Zuwanie's men in the past, and that she has dated Xola. Although Keller is suspicious of Silvia's backstory, the two grow close, in part because of their shared grief, and Keller ends up protecting her from attacks.
Philippe calls Silvia to meet and informs her of Xola's death, but lies and says he does not know what happened to Simon. She attempts to obtain information by way of Kuman-Kuman, an exiled Matoban minister living in New York, only to almost be killed in a bus bombing perpetrated by Lud's right-hand man, Jean Gamba; Kuman-Kuman, along with Keller's subordinate Doug, are amongst the dead.

documents.title: Lucky Number Slevin
documents.tagline: Wrong Time. Wrong Place. Wrong Number.
documents.overview: Slevin is mistakenly put in the middle of a personal war between the city’s biggest criminal bosses. Under constant watch, Slevin must try not to get killed by an infamous assassin and come up with an idea of how to get out of his current dilemma.
documents.plot:
Two bookies are separately ambushed and murdered. In a bus terminal, a young man is approached by Goodkat, who tells the story of Max: two decades earlier, Max borrowed money from the Mob to bet on a fixed horse race after eavesdropping on conversations between mobsters, only for the horse to collapse and die just short of the finish line. To set an example to make sure nobody else will try to bet on a fixed race, the Mob killed Max, his wife, and his son Henry. Goodkat then describes the "Kansas City Shuffle", a misleading double bluff, and kills the young man, taking the body in a truck.
In New York City, Slevin Kelevra is staying in his friend Nick Fisher's apartment and, upon being visited by neighbor Lindsey, discusses Nick's disappearance and why the apartment was unlocked. Lindsey suggests that Nick might be missing. After she leaves, Slevin is kidnapped by two henchmen who, mistaking Slevin for Nick, take him to "The Boss". The Boss orders him to repay a gambling debt or kill the son of his rival, "The Rabbi". Believing The Rabbi is responsible for assassinating his son (seen in the intro), The Boss wants The Rabbi's gay son, Yitzchok "The Fairy", to be killed in revenge. Slevin returns to the apartment but is kidnapped again, this time by two of The Rabbi's Jewish henchmen. The Rabbi also mistakes Slevin for Nick and also demands he repay a gambling debt. Slevin tells The Boss he will kill Yitzchok. Meanwhile, it becomes apparent that Goodkat is involved with both sides, that he is responsible for Nick's debts being called in, and that he plans to kill Slevin after Yitzchok dies and make it look like they both committed suicide.
Slevin is approached by Detective Brikowski, who is investigating The Boss and The Rabbi. Brikowski has also been informed that Goodkat is back in town for the first time in twenty years and thinks there is a connection between The Boss, The Rabbi, Goodkat, and Slevin. After pretending to be gay, Slevin gets invited to Yitzchok's apartment, where he kills Yitzchok, and Goodkat (revealed to be working with Slevin) kills the bodyguards. They use the man Goodkat killed in the airport (revealed to be Fisher) in Slevin's place. The two then kidnap The Boss and The Rabbi, whom they restrain in The Boss's penthouse. There, Slevin reveals he is Henry, Max's son. The mobsters who killed Max were The Boss and The Rabbi. Goodkat was the assassin hired to kill young Henry. After an attack of conscience, Goodkat raised Henry as his own. They planted Slevin as Nick (the man in the bus terminal) to get him close to them; Goodkat killed the bookies while Slevin killed The Boss' son. Slevin suffocates The Rabbi and The Boss by taping plastic bags over their heads, killing them the same way they killed his father. Since Lindsey photographed Goodkat while investigating Nick's disappearance, Goodkat shoots her to protect his identity.

documents.title: Sin City: A Dame to Kill For
documents.original_title: Sin City: A Dame to Kill For
documents.tagline: There is no justice without sin.
documents.overview: Some of Sin City's most hard-boiled citizens cross paths with a few of its more reviled inhabitants.
documents.plot:
Sin City: A Dame to Kill For is a 2014 American neo-noir crime anthology film directed by Robert Rodriguez and Frank Miller and written by Miller, the follow-up to the 2005 film Sin City. Its central story adapts A Dame to Kill For, the second book of Miller's comic series, a shorter segment comes from "Just Another Saturday Night", and two tales, "The Long Bad Night" and "Nancy's Last Dance", were written for the film. Mickey Rourke, Jessica Alba, Rosario Dawson, Jaime King, Powers Boothe and Bruce Willis return, joined by Josh Brolin, Joseph Gordon-Levitt, Eva Green, Dennis Haysbert, Christopher Meloni, Jeremy Piven, Christopher Lloyd, Ray Liotta and Lady Gaga.

In the brief opening story, the brutish Marv wakes beside a wrecked police car surrounded by bodies and pieces together how he chased a group of rich college boys who had set a homeless man on fire. In "The Long Bad Night", a cocky young gambler, Johnny, wins a fortune from the ruthless Senator Roark at a backroom poker game. Roark, who recognizes him as his illegitimate son, has his fingers broken and his money taken, and later murders the waitress Johnny had taken out. Johnny scrapes together enough cash to challenge Roark again, humiliating him at the table a second time knowing the senator will kill him for it.

The title story, set before the events of the first film, follows Dwight McCarthy, a private detective struggling to keep his violent impulses in check, who is drawn back into the life of his former lover Ava Lord. Claiming that her wealthy husband, Damien, and his giant chauffeur, Manute, are abusing her, she persuades Dwight to help her, and with Marv's aid he storms the Lord estate and kills Damien, only for Ava to shoot him and reveal that she has manipulated him to gain her husband's fortune. Rescued and given a new face in Old Town with the help of Gail and the assassin Miho, Dwight returns for revenge, while Ava's seduction of a detective, Mort, ends in murder and suicide. In "Nancy's Last Dance", Nancy Callahan, haunted by the death of John Hartigan, whose ghost watches over her, scars herself and enlists Marv to help her storm Roark's compound and take her revenge.

After a premiere at Hollywood's TCL Chinese Theatre on August 19, 2014, The Weinstein Company opened it three days later. Unlike its predecessor, it was a box-office disappointment, earning about 40.7 million dollars against a production budget of around 65 million, and it received mixed reviews from critics.

documents.title: Amélie
documents.tagline: One person can change your life forever.
documents.overview: At a tiny Parisian café, the adorable yet painfully shy Amélie accidentally discovers a gift for helping others. Soon Amelie is spending her days as a matchmaker, guardian angel, and all-around do-gooder. But when she bumps into a handsome stranger, will she find the courage to become the star of her very own love story?
documents.plot:
Amélie is a 2001 French romantic comedy film directed by Jean-Pierre Jeunet, produced by Canal+, and written by Jean-Pierre Jeunet and Guillaume Laurant. The film stars Audrey Tautou as the titular character, Amélie Poulain.

The story begins with Amélie, a shy and introverted young woman living in Paris with her mother, who is dying of cancer. After her mother's death, Amélie decides to take matters into her own hands and start making small changes in the lives of those around her, hoping to find her own place in the world.

Amélie works as a waitress at a café, where she observes the lives of her customers and begins to make subtle interventions. She helps an elderly man find his lost love, buys a piano for a lonely neighbor, and even sets up a blind date between two people who are meant to be together. Through these small acts of kindness, Amélie starts to feel more connected to the world around her.

As Amélie's actions become more confident and bold, she begins to attract the attention of a mysterious and handsome stranger, Nino Quincampoix (played by Mathieu Kassovitz). Despite their initial awkwardness, the two start to develop feelings for each other. However, their relationship is complicated by Nino's troubled past and his reluctance to open up.

Throughout the film, Jeunet uses vibrant colors, quirky characters, and whimsical settings to bring Paris to life. The cinematography is stunning, capturing the beauty of the city's streets, cafes, and landmarks. The score, composed by Yann Tiersen, adds to the film's enchanting atmosphere.

As Amélie navigates her relationships with Nino and others, she begins to confront her own feelings about love, loss, and identity. In a poignant and emotional climax, Amélie must decide whether to follow her heart or stay true to herself.

The film ends on a hopeful note, with Amélie finding a sense of belonging and purpose in the world. She and Nino share a tender moment, and Amélie finally feels like she has found someone who understands her. The final shot of the film is of Amélie walking alone through the streets of Paris, but this time, she looks happy and at peace.

Overall, Amélie is a charming and whimsical film that celebrates the beauty of human connection and the power of small acts of kindness. With its stunning visuals, quirky characters, and poignant storyline, it's no wonder that Amélie has become a beloved classic around the world.

documents.title: Back to the Future Part III
documents.original_title: Back to the Future Part III
documents.tagline: They've saved the best trip for last... But this time they may have gone too far.
documents.overview: The final installment finds Marty digging the trusty DeLorean out of a mineshaft and looking for Doc in the Wild West of 1885. But when their time machine breaks down, the travelers are stranded in a land of spurs. More problems arise when Doc falls for pretty schoolteacher Clara Clayton, and Marty tangles with Buford Tannen.
documents.plot:
Back to the Future Part III is a 1990 American science fiction Western directed by Robert Zemeckis and the final instalment of the Back to the Future trilogy. Picking up immediately after Part II, it sends Marty McFly to the Old West to rescue his friend Doc Brown, who is stranded in 1885 and fated to be shot by Biff's great-grandfather. Michael J. Fox, Christopher Lloyd, Mary Steenburgen, Thomas F. Wilson and Lea Thompson star.

On November 12, 1955, just after Doc vanishes in the DeLorean, Marty learns from a 70-year-old letter that his friend is living in 1885. With the help of the 1955 Doc, he recovers the car Doc hid, but nearby he finds Doc's gravestone, which records that he was shot by Buford "Mad Dog" Tannen over 80 dollars six days after writing the letter. Ignoring the warning, Marty travels to September 1885, landing amid a cavalry chase and damaging the fuel line. Knocked out while fleeing a bear, he is taken in by his Irish immigrant great-great-grandparents Seamus and Maggie, then, calling himself Clint Eastwood, rides into the young town of Hill Valley, where Doc saves him from being lynched by Buford's gang. With no gasoline to reach 88 miles per hour, Doc plans to have a steam locomotive push the DeLorean, but he falls in love with schoolteacher Clara Clayton after saving her from plunging into a ravine. Marty, provoked by Buford into accepting a duel, is warned by Doc that his rashness leads to a life-changing accident in the future. Doc reluctantly leaves Clara, who refuses to believe his story. On the morning of the showdown, Marty survives Buford's shot by wearing a stove door as armour, knocks him into a manure wagon and sees him arrested. Clara, realising Doc told the truth, races after the train; Doc saves her using Marty's hoverboard as the DeLorean reaches 88 mph and the locomotive plunges into the ravine. Back in 1985, Marty sees the car destroyed by a train, then avoids the street race that would have ruined his future. Doc arrives in a flying time-travelling locomotive with Clara and their sons, tells Marty and Jennifer their future is unwritten, and departs.

Fox plays Marty, with Lloyd as Doc, Steenburgen as Clara and Wilson as Buford. Shot back to back with Part II in 1989, it was filmed in California and Arizona on a $40 million budget. Released on May 25, 1990, it grossed about $245 million worldwide, earned 79% on Rotten Tomatoes as a sweeter finale, and won Saturn Awards for Alan Silvestri's music and Wilson.

documents.title: Braveheart
documents.tagline: Every man dies. Not every man truly lives.
documents.overview: Enraged at the slaughter of Murron, his new bride and childhood love, Scottish warrior William Wallace slays a platoon of the local English lord's soldiers. This leads the village to revolt and, eventually, the entire country to rise up against English rule.
documents.plot:
Braveheart is a historical epic film directed by and starring Mel Gibson, released in 1995. The movie is set in Scotland during the late 13th century and tells the story of William Wallace, a Scottish warrior who led a rebellion against the English army.

The film begins with a young William Wallace (played by Stellan Skarsgård) as a child, witnessing his father's brutal murder at the hands of English soldiers. This traumatic event sets the tone for Wallace's future actions and fuels his desire for revenge against the English.

As the story unfolds, we see Wallace grow into a strong and determined young man, who eventually becomes a skilled warrior and leader among the Scottish clans. He meets and falls in love with Murron (played by Sophie Marceau), a beautiful and kind-hearted woman from a neighboring clan. However, their happiness is short-lived, as English soldiers arrive at her village and brutally murder her.

This event sparks Wallace's desire for revenge against the English, whom he holds responsible for Murron's death. He becomes a key figure in the Scottish resistance movement, using his bravery and strategic thinking to rally the clans against the English army.

As the conflict escalates, Wallace faces off against the ruthless English commander, King Edward "Longshanks" (played by Patrick McGoohan). The two engage in a series of intense battles, with Wallace emerging as a formidable opponent. However, their rivalry is complicated by the fact that Longshanks is also Wallace's uncle.

Despite the odds against him, Wallace continues to fight for Scottish independence, using guerrilla tactics and clever strategies to outmaneuver his enemies. He becomes a symbol of hope for the Scottish people, who see him as a champion of freedom and self-determination.

The film's climax features an epic battle between the Scots and the English at Stirling Bridge. Wallace leads the charge against the English army, using his knowledge of the terrain to outflank and defeat them. However, he is eventually captured by Longshanks' men and put on trial for treason.

In a dramatic and emotional courtroom scene, Wallace delivers a powerful speech, condemning the English monarchy and pleading for Scottish independence. He is ultimately found guilty and sentenced to death. As he stands on the scaffold awaiting his execution, Wallace declares "Freedom!" and dies with his head held high.

The film ends with a sense of hope and renewal, as the Scottish people vow to continue their fight for freedom in the face of overwhelming odds. The final shot features a young William Wallace, who has grown up watching his father's story and is now determined to carry on his legacy.

Overall, Braveheart is a powerful and moving film that explores themes of patriotism, sacrifice, and the human spirit. Mel Gibson's performance as William Wallace is particularly noteworthy, bringing depth and nuance to the character. The film's epic scope and stunning cinematography make it a must-see for fans of historical dramas and action-adventure films.

documents.title: Hotel Rwanda
documents.tagline: When the world closed its eyes, he opened his arms.
documents.overview: Inspired by true events, this film takes place in Rwanda in the 1990s when more than a million Tutsis were killed in a genocide that went mostly unnoticed by the rest of the world. Hotel owner Paul Rusesabagina houses over a thousand refuges in his hotel in attempt to save their lives.
documents.plot: Inspired by true events, this film takes place in Rwanda in the 1990s when more than a million Tutsis were killed in a genocide that went mostly unnoticed by the rest of the world. Hotel owner Paul Rusesabagina houses over a thousand refuges in his hotel in attempt to save their lives.

documents.title: Saw III
documents.tagline: Suffering? You Haven't Seen Anything Yet...
documents.overview: Jigsaw has disappeared. Along with his new apprentice Amanda, the puppet-master behind the cruel, intricate games that have terrified a community and baffled police has once again eluded capture and vanished. While city detective scramble to locate him, Doctor Lynn Denlon and Jeff Reinhart are unaware that they are about to become the latest pawns on his vicious chessboard.
documents.plot:
Saw III is a 2006 American horror film directed by Darren Lynn Bousman and written by Leigh Whannell and Josh Stolberg. The film stars Tobin Bell, Angus Macfadyen, Shawnee Smith, and Bahar Soomekh.

The story begins with Dr. Lawrence Gordon (Cary Elwes), a successful surgeon who is being held captive in a run-down industrial bathroom by Jigsaw (Tobin Bell). Jigsaw forces Gordon to play a deadly game of survival, where he must use his medical skills to save the life of Adam Faulkner (Angus Macfadyen), a young man with a terminal illness. The catch is that Gordon's own life is also at stake, and if he fails to save Adam's life within 60 minutes, he will die.

As the game progresses, it becomes clear that Jigsaw has set up a series of traps and puzzles for Gordon to solve in order to save Adam's life. However, things take a dark turn when it is revealed that Adam is not who he claims to be. In reality, Adam is actually Jeff Denlon (Angus Macfadyen), the son of Detective Eric Matthews (Bahar Soomekh).

Meanwhile, Detective Matthews is investigating a series of gruesome murders linked to Jigsaw's games. As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Jigsaw has set up a complex web of traps and puzzles for Matthews to solve in order to rescue his son.

As the game reaches its climax, Gordon discovers that Adam is actually Jeff Denlon, and that he has been playing a deadly game with his own father. In the end, Gordon manages to save Adam's life by solving the final puzzle, but not before Jigsaw reveals that he has one last trick up his sleeve.

The film ends with Jigsaw's iconic twist: Dr. Gordon is actually the one who will die, and not Adam. The camera pans out to reveal a new game board, as Jigsaw's voiceover says "You're next." The final shot of the film shows Jigsaw's face, as he reveals that he has been manipulating events from behind the scenes all along.

Throughout the film, the tension builds as the characters navigate the deadly traps and puzzles set by Jigsaw. The film's climax is both shocking and terrifying, leaving the audience on the edge of their seats until the very end.

Overall, Saw III is a masterclass in building tension and suspense, with a complex web of plot twists and turns that keep the viewer guessing until the very end.

documents.title: Indiana Jones and the Kingdom of the Crystal Skull
documents.original_title: Indiana Jones and the Kingdom of the Crystal Skull
documents.tagline: The adventure continues . . .
documents.overview: Set during the Cold War, the Soviets—led by sword-wielding Irina Spalko—are in search of a crystal skull which has supernatural powers related to a mystical Lost City of Gold. Indy is coerced to head to Peru at the behest of a young man whose friend—and Indy's colleague—Professor Oxley has been captured for his knowledge of the skull's whereabouts.
documents.plot:
Indiana Jones and the Kingdom of the Crystal Skull is a 2008 action-adventure film directed by Steven Spielberg, produced by George Lucas and Kathleen Kennedy, and written by David Koepp.

The movie takes place in 1957, four years after the events of Raiders of the Lost Ark (1981). Indiana Jones (Harrison Ford), now an older and wiser archaeologist, is working at Marshall College in Princeton, New Jersey. He is married to Marion Ravenwood (Karen Allen), with whom he has a son named Henry.

The story begins with a mysterious crystal skull that has been stolen from the U.S. government by Irina Spalko (Cate Blanchett), a Soviet agent who seeks to use its supposed supernatural powers to gain control over the world's nuclear arsenals. The skull is later recovered by Indy, but not before it is used in a ritual to awaken an ancient Sankara Stones' energy.

As Indy delves deeper into the mystery of the crystal skull, he discovers that it is connected to an alien spacecraft that has been hidden beneath the U.S. government's secret research facility at Area 51. The aliens, led by Mutt Williams (Shia LaBeouf), a young man who claims to be Indy's son with Marion, reveal that they have been watching Earth for centuries and are searching for a way to harness the power of the Sankara Stones.

Indy joins forces with Mutt, Marion, and a new character, Dr. Wilkins (John Hurt), an old friend of Indy's who has been working on the government project. Together, they embark on a perilous journey across the globe, from Peru to Egypt, in search of the remaining Sankara Stones.

As they navigate treacherous jungles, ancient ruins, and Soviet agents, Indy and his team face numerous challenges and obstacles. Along the way, Indy also confronts his own past and the consequences of his actions as a young adventurer.

The movie culminates in an epic showdown between Indy and Spalko at the Sankara Stones' energy source, where they engage in a fierce battle to control the power of the stones. In the end, Indy emerges victorious, but not before realizing that Mutt is indeed his son with Marion.

The film concludes with Indy returning home to his family, reflecting on his adventures and the lessons he has learned about the importance of family and responsibility. The movie ends on a hopeful note, as Indy looks forward to a new chapter in his life, one that will be filled with excitement, danger, and adventure.

Overall, Indiana Jones and the Kingdom of the Crystal Skull is an action-packed, thrilling ride that pays homage to the classic Indiana Jones films while introducing new characters and plot twists. The movie's blend of humor, adventure, and science fiction elements makes it a fun and entertaining watch for fans of the franchise and newcomers alike.

documents.title: The Terminator
documents.tagline: Your future is in his hands.
documents.overview: In the post-apocalyptic future, reigning tyrannical supercomputers teleport a cyborg assassin known as the 'Terminator' back to 1984 to kill Sarah Connor, whose unborn son is destined to lead insurgents against 21st century mechanical hegemony. Meanwhile, the human-resistance movement dispatches a lone warrior to safeguard Sarah. Can he stop the virtually indestructible killing machine?
documents.plot:
In the year 2029, Earth is a post-apocalyptic wasteland ruled by intelligent machines led by an AI called Skynet. After launching a nuclear holocaust known as Judgment Day, Skynet wages war on the remnants of humanity. The human resistance, led by a man named John Connor, manages to turn the tide. In a last-ditch effort to defeat the resistance, Skynet sends a Terminator—a nearly indestructible cyborg assassin—back in time to 1984 Los Angeles. Its mission is to kill Sarah Connor, John’s mother, before he can be born.

The Terminator, disguised as a human (played by Arnold Schwarzenegger), arrives in 1984 and begins systematically killing every woman named Sarah Connor listed in the phone book. Meanwhile, the resistance sends back one of their own, Kyle Reese (Michael Biehn), to protect the correct Sarah Connor (Linda Hamilton).

Kyle finds Sarah and explains the situation: the Terminator is a cybernetic organism designed to infiltrate and exterminate; it will never stop hunting her. Sarah, understandably skeptical, becomes convinced after witnessing the Terminator’s relentless attack. The pair go on the run, with Kyle providing knowledge of the future and Sarah beginning to accept her crucial role in humanity’s survival.

During their escape, Kyle and Sarah grow close, and she learns that John Connor deliberately chose Kyle to be sent back because Kyle is, in fact, John’s father. They conceive John during their time together.

The Terminator relentlessly pursues them, leading to a climactic showdown in a factory. Kyle sacrifices himself to destroy the Terminator by blowing it up with a pipe bomb. Though badly injured, the Terminator’s torso continues to crawl after Sarah. She manages to crush it in a hydraulic press, finally ending the threat.

In the aftermath, Sarah, now pregnant, prepares for a future that only she knows is coming. She begins recording audio tapes for her unborn son, warning him about the coming war and the role he must play. She drives into the desert, determined to survive and protect her child.

documents.title: Rebel Without a Cause
documents.tagline: The bad boy from a good family.
documents.overview: After moving to a new town, troublemaking teen Jim Stark is supposed to have a clean slate, although being the new kid in town brings its own problems. While searching for some stability, Stark forms a bond with a disturbed classmate, Plato, and falls for local girl Judy. However, Judy is the girlfriend of neighborhood tough, Buzz. When Buzz violently confronts Jim and challenges him to a drag race, the new kid's real troubles begin.
documents.plot: After moving to a new town, troublemaking teen Jim Stark is supposed to have a clean slate, although being the new kid in town brings its own problems. While searching for some stability, Stark forms a bond with a disturbed classmate, Plato, and falls for local girl Judy. However, Judy is the girlfriend of neighborhood tough, Buzz. When Buzz violently confronts Jim and challenges him to a drag race, the new kid's real troubles begin.

documents.title: Young Adam
documents.tagline: Everyone has a past. Everyone has a secret.
documents.overview: A young drifter working on a river barge disrupts his employers' lives while hiding the fact that he knows more about a dead woman found in the river than he admits.
documents.plot: A young drifter working on a river barge disrupts his employers' lives while hiding the fact that he knows more about a dead woman found in the river than he admits.

documents.title: The Godfather
documents.tagline: An offer you can't refuse.
documents.overview: Spanning the years 1945 to 1955, a chronicle of the fictional Italian-American Corleone crime family. When organized crime family patriarch, Vito Corleone barely survives an attempt on his life, his youngest son, Michael steps in to take care of the would-be killers, launching a campaign of bloody revenge.
documents.plot:
In the mid-1940s, Michael Corleone is a World War II veteran and the youngest son of Don Vito Corleone. Vito is head of the Corleone mafia family and runs it with his eldest son Santino a.k.a. Sonny and adopted son Tom Hagen, a lawyer who is the family's consigliere. At his sister Connie's wedding to Carlo Rizzi, Michael introduces his family to his girlfriend, Kay Adams. Michael tells Kay stories of his family but makes it clear that he wants no part in his family's business.
Vito fulfils the Sicilian tradition of granting favors on his daughter's wedding day to a succession of hopeful visitors. One is his godson, singer and actor Johnny Fontane, who cannot get an upcoming film role because studio owner and producer Jack Woltz has a grudge against Fontane. Vito sends Hagen to LA to persuade Woltz to relent but Woltz will not budge. Hagen departs and the next morning, Woltz wakes to find the severed head of his prized $600,000 racehorse Khartoum in his bed with him. A terrified Woltz relents and Fontane gets the role.
Approaching Christmas, Michael becomes embroiled in family affairs when Vito is gunned down by two assailants. Vito had earlier refused to offer protection to drug baron Virgil "The Turk" Sollozzo for dealing narcotics in the city. Sollozzo has the support of the Tattaglia family, who garrote notorious Corleone enforcer Luca Brasi when he attempts to become a mole in Sollozzo's operation. While Vito survives the attempt and recovers at the hospital, hot-tempered Sonny takes over the family as acting boss. He has Michael live at the house for his protection, as his successful revenge hit on Tattaglia's son Bruno has led to war between the two gangs. Michael visits his father in hospital to be told that NYPD Captain McCluskey has had Vito's bodyguards ejected from the hospital, clearing the way for a second attempt on Vito's life. Michael visits his father and, realizing his jeopardy, moves him to another hospital room then stands guard outside the hospital. He scares Sollozzo's assassins off but an angry McCluskey returns and breaks Michael's jaw for defying him. Soon after, Hagen arrives with more bodyguards and McCluskey backs down to the lawyer's demands. Being an outsider to the family business and seen as harmless, Michael later proposes a meeting between himself, Sollozzo and McCluskey at which he'll kill them both to keep his father safe. Initially amused, the family approve his plan and have a gun planted at the meeting place: a restaurant. At the meeting, Michael shoots both men dead then flees the country. He takes refuge in his family's native Sicily to escape the NYPD and the ire of the other gangs until the heat dies down. He falls in love with a local woman, Apollonia Vitelli, and marries her.
Back in New York, war has broken out between the Five Families. Sonny discovers that Connie was being abused by Carlo. At first, Sonny pummels Carlo in public and warns him never to touch Connie again.

documents.title: Some Like It Hot
documents.tagline: The movie too HOT for words!
documents.overview: Two musicians witness a mob hit and struggle to find a way out of the city before they are found by the gangsters. Their only opportunity is to join an all-girl band as they leave on a tour. To make their getaway they must first disguise themselves as women, then keep their identities secret and deal with the problems this brings - such as an attractive bandmate and a very determined suitor.
documents.plot:
Some Like It Hot is a classic American comedy film directed by Billy Wilder, released in 1959 by United Artists. The movie stars Tony Curtis, Jack Lemmon, and Marilyn Monroe.

The story begins with Joe Carter (Tony Curtis) and Jerry Parker (Jack Lemmon), two struggling musicians who are forced to flee their home after being threatened by a rival gangster, Spats Colombo (George Raft). They disguise themselves as women, with the help of a transvestite named Daphne (Joan Crawford's character in her earlier film "Mildred Pierce"), and join an all-female band on a train headed to Chicago.

In Chicago, Joe and Jerry adopt female personas, becoming Josephine and Daphne respectively. They quickly become part of the band and gain popularity as musicians. However, their new lives are threatened when Spats Colombo discovers their true identities and tries to kill them.

Meanwhile, Jerry falls in love with Sugar Kane (Marilyn Monroe), a beautiful singer who is engaged to be married to the wealthy and arrogant Osgood Fielding III (Joe E. Brown). As Jerry gets closer to Sugar, he must navigate his feelings for her while keeping his true identity hidden from her.

As the story unfolds, Joe and Jerry's disguises are put to the test as they try to avoid Spats Colombo and his henchmen. Along the way, they get into various misadventures, including a memorable scene where they accidentally join Sugar's wedding party dressed in their female attire.

In the end, Jerry must confront his feelings for Sugar and decide whether to reveal his true identity or continue living as Daphne. In a surprising twist, Joe and Jerry are able to outsmart Spats Colombo and win Sugar's heart, with Jerry ultimately choosing to leave Chicago and start a new life with Sugar.

Throughout the movie, Billy Wilder's direction and the witty dialogue by I.A.L. Diamond provide plenty of comedic moments, while Tony Curtis and Jack Lemmon deliver standout performances as the two lead characters. The film's blend of humor, romance, and music makes it a timeless classic that continues to entertain audiences to this day.

Some Like It Hot has been recognized for its cultural significance and influence on popular culture. It was selected for preservation in the National Film Registry by the Library of Congress in 1999 and has been named one of the greatest films of all time by various publications, including the American Film Institute and IMDb.

documents.title: The Godfather Part III
documents.tagline: All the power on earth can't change destiny.
documents.overview: In the midst of trying to legitimize his business dealings in 1979 New York and Italy, aging mafia don, Michael Corleone seeks forgiveness for his sins while taking a young protege under his wing.
documents.plot:
The Godfather Part III is a 1990 American epic gangster film produced and directed by Francis Ford Coppola from a screenplay he co-wrote with Mario Puzo. It stars Al Pacino, Diane Keaton, Talia Shire, Andy Garcia, Eli Wallach, Joe Mantegna, Bridget Fonda, George Hamilton and Sofia Coppola. The sequel to The Godfather Part II (1974) and the final installment of the trilogy, it concludes the story of Michael Corleone as he tries to make his criminal empire legitimate, and it weaves in fictionalized versions of the 1978 death of Pope John Paul I and the Papal banking scandal of 1981 and 1982.

In 1979, Michael Corleone, now nearing sixty and tormented by guilt over his rise to power, above all for ordering the murder of his brother Fredo, is donating millions to charity and receives a papal honor. Divorced from Kay, he has a strained relationship with their children, Anthony and Mary, who live with Kay; Anthony announces that he is abandoning law school to become an opera singer. At the celebration, Vincent Mancini, the hot-tempered illegitimate son of Michael's late brother Sonny, clashes with the rival mobster Joey Zasa, and Michael, impressed by his loyalty, takes him into the family business. Seeking to leave crime behind, Michael offers to cover a huge deficit at the Vatican Bank in exchange for a controlling stake in the international real estate company Internazionale Immobiliare, a deal that requires the Pope's approval. When he refuses to let his old Mafia partners share in the venture, a helicopter attack on a meeting of the bosses nearly kills him, and Michael realizes that the elderly Don Altobello is betraying him. While Michael recovers from a diabetic stroke, Vincent begins a romance with his cousin Mary and takes revenge on Zasa. The family then travels to Sicily for Anthony's operatic debut at the Teatro Massimo in Palermo, where Michael seeks Kay's forgiveness and makes his first confession in thirty years, even as enemies both inside and outside the Church close in around him and his family.

The film received mostly positive reviews, although it was considered inferior to its predecessors; critics praised Pacino's and Garcia's performances and Coppola's direction but criticized the plot and Sofia Coppola's performance. It grossed $136.8 million and received seven Academy Award nominations, including Best Picture. A recut version, The Godfather Coda: The Death of Michael Corleone, was released in 2020.

documents.title: High Fidelity
documents.tagline: A comedy about fear of commitment, hating your job, falling in love and other pop favorites.
documents.overview: When record store owner and compulsive list-compiler Rob Gordon gets dumped by his long-time girlfriend, Laura, because he hasn't changed since they met, he revisits his top five breakups of all time in order to figure out what went wrong. As he examines his failed attempts at romance and happiness, the process finds him being dragged, kicking and screaming, into adulthood.
documents.plot: After his long-time girlfriend dumps him, a thirty-year-old record store owner seeks to understand why he is unlucky in love while recounting his "top five breakups of all time".

documents.title: About a Boy
documents.tagline: Growing up has nothing to do with age.
documents.overview: Will Freeman is a good-looking, smooth-talking bachelor whose primary goal in life is avoiding any kind of responsibility. But when he invents an imaginary son in order to meet attractive single moms, Will gets a hilarious lesson about life from a bright, but hopelessly geeky 12-year-old named Marcus. Now, as Will struggles to teach Marcus the art of being cool, Marcus teaches Will that you're never too old to grow up.
