But when he invents an imaginary son in order to meet attractive single moms, Will gets a hilarious lesson about life from a bright, but hopelessly geeky 12-year-old named Marcus. Now, as Will struggles to teach Marcus the art of being cool, Marcus teaches Will that you're never too old to grow up.

documents.title: Zatoichi
documents.tagline: His sword made him a hero... his courage made him a legend.
documents.overview: Blind traveler Zatoichi is a master swordsman and a masseur with a fondness for gambling on dice games. When he arrives in a village torn apart by warring gangs, he sets out to protect the townspeople.
documents.plot: Blind traveler Zatoichi is a master swordsman and a masseur with a fondness for gambling on dice games. When he arrives in a village torn apart by warring gangs, he sets out to protect the townspeople.

documents.title: King Kong
documents.tagline: The eighth wonder of the world.
documents.overview: In 1933 New York, an overly ambitious movie producer coerces his cast and hired ship crew to travel to mysterious Skull Island, where they encounter Kong, a giant ape who is immediately smitten with the leading lady.
documents.plot:
King Kong is a 2005 epic monster film directed, co-written and produced by Peter Jackson. The ninth entry in the King Kong franchise and the second remake of the 1933 film, after the 1976 version, it stars Naomi Watts, Jack Black and Adrien Brody, with Thomas Kretschmann, Colin Hanks and Jamie Bell, and Andy Serkis as the motion-capture performer behind Kong. It was released in the United States on 14 December 2005.

In New York in 1933, during the Great Depression, struggling vaudeville performer Ann Darrow is hired by the financially desperate filmmaker Carl Denham to star in his new picture opposite the actor Bruce Baxter. She agrees after learning that the script is being written by her favorite playwright, Jack Driscoll. Denham claims the production is bound for Singapore aboard the small cargo ship SS Venture, commanded by Captain Englehorn, but his real destination is the uncharted Skull Island. During the voyage Ann and Jack fall in love. Lost in fog, the Venture runs aground on the island, where the film crew is attacked by hostile natives, who later kidnap Ann and offer her as a sacrifice to Kong, a giant ape. A rescue party led by first mate Hayes and Jack, with Denham determined to film the creature, sets off into the jungle and encounters a terrifying lost world of dinosaurs, stampeding herds and giant insects. Meanwhile Ann wins Kong over with her vaudeville routines and gradually discovers his intelligence and capacity for emotion, as he defends her from a trio of carnivorous dinosaurs. After Jack rescues Ann from Kong's mountain lair, Denham captures the ape and brings him back to New York, where he is exhibited on Broadway as "the Eighth Wonder of the World". When Kong breaks free during the show and rampages through the city in search of Ann, the story builds toward a famous final confrontation atop the Empire State Building.

King Kong received critical acclaim, earning praise for its special effects, performances and sense of spectacle, although its three-hour running time drew some criticism. It holds an 84% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes, grossed over $557 million worldwide and won three Academy Awards, for Best Sound Editing, Best Sound Mixing and Best Visual Effects.

documents.title: Batman Begins
documents.tagline: Evil fears the knight.
documents.overview: Driven by tragedy, billionaire Bruce Wayne dedicates his life to uncovering and defeating the corruption that plagues his home, Gotham City.  Unable to work within the system, he instead creates a new identity, a symbol of fear for the criminal underworld - The Batman.
documents.plot:
Batman Begins is a 2005 superhero film directed by Christopher Nolan, produced by Charles Roven and Emma Thomas, and written by Nolan and David S. Goyer.

The movie begins with Bruce Wayne (Christian Bale) as a young boy witnessing his parents' murder in front of him in Gotham City. This traumatic event sets the tone for the rest of the film, as Bruce struggles to come to terms with the loss of his loved ones.

As Bruce grows up, he becomes obsessed with martial arts and detective work, using these skills to cope with his emotions. He travels to Japan, where he trains with a sensei named Ra's al Ghul (Liam Neeson), who teaches him about the philosophy of fear and its role in shaping human behavior.

Years later, Bruce returns to Gotham City as a young adult, determined to use his skills to fight crime and protect the innocent. However, he soon realizes that his wealth and privilege have not prepared him for the harsh realities of being a vigilante. He begins to question whether he has what it takes to be a true hero.

Bruce's journey is further complicated by the presence of Dr. Jonathan Crane (Cillian Murphy), a psychologist who uses his skills to manipulate and terrorize Gotham City's citizens. As Bruce delves deeper into the world of crime, he becomes increasingly obsessed with understanding the mind of a villain.

Meanwhile, Ra's al Ghul returns to Gotham City, seeking revenge against those who have wronged him in the past. He is aided by his loyal servant, Scarecrow (also played by Cillian Murphy), who uses his knowledge of psychology and toxins to spread fear and chaos throughout the city.

As Batman begins to take shape, he faces off against Ra's al Ghul and Scarecrow in a series of intense battles. Along the way, he must confront his own demons and learn to harness his emotions in order to become a true hero.

The film culminates in a dramatic showdown between Batman and Ra's al Ghul, with Bruce ultimately emerging victorious but not without scars. The movie ends on a hopeful note, as Bruce reflects on the lessons he has learned and the journey that has brought him to this point.

Throughout the film, Nolan explores themes of trauma, identity, and the nature of heroism. Batman Begins is a thought-provoking and visually stunning film that sets the stage for the rest of the Dark Knight Trilogy.

documents.title: Underworld
documents.tagline: An immortal battle for supremacy.
documents.overview: Vampires and werewolves have waged a nocturnal war against each other for centuries. But all bets are off when a female vampire warrior named Selene, who's famous for her strength and werewolf-hunting prowess, becomes smitten with a peace-loving male werewolf, Michael, who wants to end the war.
documents.plot:
Underworld is a 2003 supernatural action film directed by Len Wiseman and written by Alex Litvak and Michael Cunningham. The movie stars Kate Beckinsale, Scott Speedman, Shane Brolly, and Bill Nighy.

The story begins with Selene (Kate Beckinsale), a skilled vampire warrior who works for the vampire king, Kraven (Shane Brolly). However, Selene's life is turned upside down when she discovers that her past is shrouded in mystery. She has no memory of her life before becoming a vampire and is haunted by fragmented images of her human life.

As Selene delves deeper into her past, she learns that she was once a human named Eve (played by Kim Coates), who was turned into a vampire by Kraven's brother, Lucian (Scott Speedman). However, unlike the traditional vampire lore, vampires in this world are not undead creatures but rather shape-shifters with supernatural abilities.

Selene soon discovers that a group of rogue vampires, led by Kraven, have stolen a powerful artifact known as the "Eclipse," which has the ability to destroy all vampires. The humans, who were once at war with the vampires, have also discovered the Eclipse and are determined to use it against their former enemies.

As Selene navigates this treacherous world, she must confront her own identity and the truth about her past. Along the way, she teams up with a human named Michael (Scott Speedman), who becomes her ally in the fight against Kraven and his followers.

The plot thickens as Selene and Michael uncover a conspiracy involving the vampire king and the rogue vampires. They soon realize that the Eclipse is not just a simple artifact but a key to unlocking an ancient prophecy that could change the course of human-vampire relations forever.

As the stakes grow higher, Selene must confront her own destiny and make a choice between her loyalty to Kraven and her growing feelings for Michael. The movie culminates in an epic battle between vampires and humans, with Selene at the forefront of the fight.

In the end, Selene emerges victorious but not without scars. She has finally found some answers about her past and has discovered her true purpose as a vampire warrior. However, the movie ends on a cliffhanger, setting the stage for the sequels that would follow.

Overall, Underworld is a thrilling action-packed film with stunning visuals and impressive fight choreography. The movie's unique take on traditional vampire lore and its strong female protagonist make it a standout in the genre.

documents.title: Amadeus
documents.tagline: Everything you've heard is true...
documents.overview: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart is a remarkably talented young Viennese composer who unwittingly finds a fierce rival in the disciplined and determined Antonio Salieri. Resenting Mozart for both his hedonistic lifestyle and his undeniable talent, the highly religious Salieri is gradually consumed by his jealousy and becomes obsessed with Mozart's downfall, leading to a devious scheme that has dire consequences for both men.
documents.plot:
In 1823, aged composer Antonio Salieri attempts suicide and is committed to a psychiatric hospital. He claims that he murdered Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart. Father Vogler, a young Catholic priest, encourages Salieri to confess his sins before God. After Vogler fails to recognize him, Salieri plays three old melodies to jog his memory. Vogler cannot recognize the first two (which Salieri wrote) but is relieved to recognize the third (Eine kleine Nachtmusik) at once. Salieri peevishly reveals that Mozart wrote it.
Salieri begins his confession by saying he grew up hearing stories about the child prodigy Mozart. In his youth, Salieri was in love with music but was forbidden by his father to study the craft. Salieri proposed that if God made him a famous musician like Mozart, he would give God his faithfulness, chastity, and diligence. Salieri's father soon dies, which he interprets as a sign that God has accepted his vow. By 1774, Salieri became court composer to Holy Roman Emperor Joseph II in Vienna. However, he has enough taste to know that Emperor Joseph has no ear for music, though Salieri prides himself on the popularity of his work.
Salieri understands that Mozart is the better composer but is shocked to discover, upon their first meeting, that Mozart is obscene, immature, and dissolute. He also learns that Mozart never needs to pen a second draft of his music, implying divine inspiration. Salieri cannot fathom why God would choose a reprobate like Mozart as his earthly instrument. Salieri renounces God and vows to take revenge on him by destroying Mozart.
Mozart's work is ahead of its time, and he struggles to find employment in Vienna. He spends himself into debt, alarming his wife Constanze. Salieri and Mozart bond over their shared contempt for Emperor Joseph's lack of taste, but Mozart is unimpressed by Salieri's populist work, which causes Salieri great pain.
Mozart boldly adapts the subversive play The Marriage of Figaro into a comedic opera. Salieri rejoices, thinking Mozart's career is ruined, but Mozart stuns Salieri by convincing the Emperor to approve the project. The Emperor, however, finds the opera boring, and it is soon canceled. Eventually, Mozart's father, Leopold, dies. In response to criticisms and his grief, Mozart composes Don Giovanni, a dark, serious opera. Salieri is entranced but vindictively gets that opera canceled, too. Renouncing Vienna's artistic establishment, Mozart agrees to write The Magic Flute for a commoners' theater against Constanze's wishes.
After watching Don Giovanni five times, Salieri realizes that the dead commander who accuses Giovanni of sin represents Mozart's inferiority complex towards his father. Posing as an anonymous patron, in a costume Leopold had worn to a masquerade ball, Salieri persuades the unstable and debt-ridden Mozart to accept a commission for a Requiem Mass.

documents.title: Terminator 2: Judgment Day
documents.tagline: It's nothing personal.
documents.overview: Nearly 10 years have passed since Sarah Connor was targeted for termination by a cyborg from the future. Now her son, John, the future leader of the resistance, is the target for a newer, more deadly terminator. Once again, the resistance has managed to send a protector back to attempt to save John and his mother Sarah.
documents.plot:
Ten years after the events of the first film, a new, more advanced Terminator—the T-1000, made of liquid metal—has been sent back from 2029 to 1995 to assassinate John Connor, the future leader of the human resistance. To protect John, the resistance sends back a reprogrammed T-800 Terminator (the same model that tried to kill Sarah Connor years earlier) to guard him.

John Connor, now a rebellious teenager, lives with foster parents but soon finds himself hunted by the T-1000. The T-800 locates John and saves him from the T-1000’s attacks. Together with John’s mother, Sarah Connor—who has become a fierce warrior preparing for the inevitable war against machines—they attempt to prevent Judgment Day.

Sarah, John, and the T-800 aim to destroy Cyberdyne Systems, the company responsible for creating Skynet’s technology, by targeting the research lab and a key scientist, Miles Dyson. After a series of intense confrontations and a high-speed chase, they succeed in destroying the lab, the research, and the Terminators that pursue them.

In a final battle at a steel mill, the T-1000 proves nearly unstoppable, shape-shifting and regenerating from damage. The T-800 and John manage to destroy it by plunging it into molten steel. Recognizing the threat that its own technology poses to humanity’s future, the T-800 sacrifices itself by lowering into the molten steel, ensuring no trace of Skynet’s creation remains.

The film ends on a cautiously hopeful note, with Sarah driving away with John, determined to change the future and prevent the catastrophic war between humans and machines.

"Terminator 2" explores themes of fate, free will, humanity, and sacrifice. It is celebrated for its groundbreaking special effects, intense action sequences, and deeper emotional storytelling compared to the original.

documents.title: Pirates of the Caribbean: At World's End
documents.original_title: Pirates of the Caribbean: At World's End
documents.tagline: At the end of the world, the adventure begins.
documents.overview: Captain Barbossa, long believed to be dead, has come back to life and is headed to the edge of the Earth with Will Turner and Elizabeth Swann. But nothing is quite as it seems.
documents.plot:
Pirates of the Caribbean: At World's End is a 2007 swashbuckling adventure film directed by Gore Verbinski and produced by Walt Disney Pictures. The film is the third installment in the Pirates of the Caribbean franchise.

The story begins with Will Turner (Orlando Bloom), a blacksmith's apprentice, who has been searching for Elizabeth Swann (Keira Knightley), the governor's daughter, who has been kidnapped by Captain Barbossa (Geoffrey Rush) and his crew of pirates. Meanwhile, Lord Cutler Beckett (Tom Hollander), a ruthless and cunning agent of the East India Trading Company, is determined to eliminate all pirates from the seas.

As Will searches for Elizabeth, he meets Bootstrap Bill Turner (Stellan Skarsgård), his father, who has been cursed by the Aztec gold. The curse can only be broken when the Black Pearl's captain, Captain Jack Sparrow (Johnny Depp), finds the heart of Davy Jones, a sea devil who is in charge of the Flying Dutchman.

The story takes a dramatic turn as Will and Elizabeth are rescued from Barbossa's ship by Jack Sparrow. However, their reunion is short-lived, as they soon find themselves caught up in a larger conflict between the pirates and the East India Trading Company.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Beckett has discovered the location of Davy Jones' locker, where the heart of Davy Jones can be found. The heart holds the key to breaking the curse that binds Will's father to the Flying Dutchman. However, Beckett plans to use the heart to control the seas and eliminate all pirates.

The pirates, led by Jack Sparrow, gather at the island of Tortuga to form an alliance against the East India Trading Company. The pirate lords, including Captain Barbossa, Captain Teague (Keith Richards), and Commodore Norrington (Jack Davenport), come together to elect a new captain who will lead them in their fight against Beckett.

The film's climax features an epic battle between the pirates and the East India Trading Company. Jack Sparrow, Will Turner, and Elizabeth Swann join forces with the pirate lords to defeat Beckett and his minions. In the process, Will breaks the curse that has bound his father to the Flying Dutchman, freeing him from his duties as its captain.

The film concludes with the pirates celebrating their victory over the East India Trading Company. Jack Sparrow is hailed as a hero, and he sets sail on the Black Pearl once again, ready for his next adventure. The story ends with Will and Elizabeth reunited, and Will's father finally at peace.

Overall, Pirates of the Caribbean: At World's End is an action-packed adventure film that explores themes of loyalty, friendship, and redemption. The film features memorable characters, including Captain Jack Sparrow, who has become a cultural icon in his own right.

documents.title: Terminator 3: Rise of the Machines
documents.tagline: The Machines Will Rise.
documents.overview: It's been 10 years since John Connor saved Earth from Judgment Day, and he's now living under the radar, steering clear of using anything Skynet can trace. That is, until he encounters T-X, a robotic assassin ordered to finish what T-1000 started. Good thing Connor's former nemesis, the Terminator, is back to aid the now-adult Connor … just like he promised.
documents.plot:
Terminator 3: Rise of the Machines is a 2003 science fiction action film directed by Jonathan Mostow, and it is the third installment in the Terminator franchise. The movie stars Arnold Schwarzenegger, Nick Stahl, Claire Danes, and Kristanna Loken.

The story begins in 2004, six years after the events of Terminator 2: Judgment Day (1991). John Connor (Nick Stahl), the future leader of the human resistance against Skynet, a rogue artificial intelligence system that was created by humans but has become self-aware and is now determined to destroy humanity. John's mother, Sarah Connor (Linda Hamilton), is still on the run from Skynet agents who are trying to kill her.

Meanwhile, a new Terminator model, T-X (Kristanna Loken), is sent back in time to 2004 to kill John before he can become the leader of the human resistance. The T-850 model Terminator, also known as the "T-1000" (Arnold Schwarzenegger), is reactivated from cryogenic freezing and sent back in time to protect John.

As the story unfolds, we see flashbacks of John's childhood and his mother's struggles to keep him safe from Skynet agents. We also learn that John has been living a normal life with his foster family, unaware of his true destiny as the leader of the human resistance.

The T-850 Terminator is sent back in time to protect John, but he soon discovers that there are two Terminators on the loose: the T-X and himself. The T-X is a more advanced model than the T-850, with the ability to mimic human appearance and voice.

As the story progresses, we see action-packed sequences of the T-850 Terminator fighting against the T-X in a series of intense battles. Along the way, John begins to realize his true identity as the future leader of the human resistance and starts to take steps to prepare himself for the war against Skynet.

In the end, the T-850 Terminator sacrifices himself to save John's life, allowing him to escape from the T-X. The movie ends with John setting out on a journey to fulfill his destiny as the leader of the human resistance, while Sarah Connor is shown to be still on the run from Skynet agents.

Overall, Terminator 3: Rise of the Machines is an action-packed sci-fi thriller that explores themes of time travel, artificial intelligence, and humanity's struggle for survival. The movie features impressive visual effects and a thrilling plot that keeps viewers on the edge of their seats until the very end.
production_companies: IMF Internationale Medien und Film GmbH & Co. 3. Produktions KG

documents.title: The Science of Sleep
documents.tagline: Close your eyes. Open your heart.
documents.overview: A man entranced by his dreams and imagination is lovestruck with a French woman and feels he can show her his world.
documents.plot:
Stéphane Miroux (Gael García Bernal) is a shy young man whose vivid dreams often interfere with his waking life. After the death of his divorced father in Mexico, Stéphane moves to Paris to live closer to his mother Christine. He moves into his childhood home and starts a new job his mother has found for him in a calendar printing company.
Stéphane had been told it was a creative job and shows his new colleagues his drawings, a collection of twelve illustrations depicting unique disasters. He calls his collection "disasterology". But nobody at his new job appreciates his talents – the job is no more than typesetting work, leaving him frustrated, as revealed in his dreams.
While leaving his apartment to go to work one day, the new neighbour Stéphanie (Charlotte Gainsbourg) invites him into her apartment; he soon realizes that she is creative and artistic. They plan a project together, a short animated film based around a boat Stéphanie was making.
As the story begins to unfold, surrealistic and naturalistic elements begin to overlap within Stéphane's reality, and the viewer is often uncertain of which portions constitute reality and which are dreams. One dream sequence, in which Stéphane dreams his hands become absurdly giant, was inspired by a recurring nightmare director Michel Gondry had as a child. As the line between dream and reality gradually becomes more blurred, Stéphane becomes enamoured with Stéphanie, and he shares his inventions with her, such as the 'one-second time machine'. Stéphane's dreams begin to encroach on his waking life, making him unsure of reality and whether Stéphanie's feelings for him are real.
Stéphanie's toy horse is named Golden The Pony Boy, a reference to The Outsiders, the meaning poignantly hinting at Stèphane's regression and childlike behaviour around Stéphanie, which could stem from the loss of his father. He implants a mechanism inside Golden the Pony Boy that will make it gallop. He later receives a call from Stéphanie thanking him; she reveals the pony was named after him.
To Stéphane's surprise, the calendar manufacturer accepts his "disasterology" idea and the company has a party in his honor, but he begins drinking excessively after he witnesses Stéphanie dancing with another man. The next day, the two have a confrontation in their hallway when Stéphane announces that he does not want to be Stéphanie's friend any longer.
Stéphanie offers to discuss their issues on a date, but on his way there Stéphane has a vision that she is not there. He runs to her apartment and bangs on her door, when in actuality, she is waiting for him at the café. Stéphanie returns home, while Stéphane decides to move back to Mexico.
Before leaving, Stéphane's mother insists that he says a formal goodbye to his next-door neighbor, Stéphanie. In his attempt to do so, he becomes crass, making offensive jokes.

documents.title: Swimming Pool
documents.tagline: On the surface, all is calm.
documents.overview: A British crime novelist travels to her publisher's upmarket summer house in Southern France to seek solitude in order to work on her next book. However, the unexpected arrival of the publisher's daughter induces complications and a subsequent crime.
documents.plot: A British crime novelist travels to her publisher's upmarket summer house in Southern France to seek solitude in order to work on her next book. However, the unexpected arrival of the publisher's daughter induces complications and a subsequent crime.

documents.title: Beverly Hills Cop III
documents.tagline: In for the ride of his life!
documents.overview: Back in sunny southern California and on the trail of two murderers, Axel Foley again teams up with LA cop Billy Rosewood. Soon, they discover that an amusement park is being used as a front for a massive counterfeiting ring – and it's run by the same gang that shot Billy's boss.
documents.plot:
Beverly Hills Cop III is a 1994 American action comedy film directed by Tony Scott and starring Eddie Murphy as Axel Foley, a Detroit cop who goes undercover to solve a murder case in Beverly Hills. The movie marks the third installment in the Beverly Hills Cop series.

The story begins with Axel Foley (Eddie Murphy) returning to Beverly Hills after a successful stint as an undercover agent in Russia. He is approached by his friend and colleague, Detective Rosewood (Nora Dunn), who informs him that a wealthy businessman named Julian Beasley (Hector Elizondo) has been murdered. The police investigation reveals that the murder was committed using a rare and valuable gemstone.

Axel Foley decides to go undercover again, this time as a Beverly Hills detective, to investigate the murder and uncover the identity of the killer. He is paired with Detective Rosewood's new partner, Detective John Kimble (Joe Pesci), who is initially hesitant to work with Axel due to their past differences.

As Axel navigates the wealthy and complex world of Beverly Hills, he encounters a range of characters, including Beasley's business associates, his family members, and even some old friends from his Detroit days. Along the way, he discovers that the murder is linked to a larger conspiracy involving Beasley's company and several other powerful individuals.

Throughout the movie, Axel faces numerous challenges as he tries to stay one step ahead of the killer and solve the case. He also has to contend with the skepticism of some of his colleagues, who doubt his abilities due to his lack of experience in Beverly Hills.

As the plot thickens, Axel discovers that the murder is connected to a larger scheme involving Beasley's company and several other powerful individuals. He also uncovers a personal connection between Beasley and one of his business associates, which leads him closer to the truth.

In the end, Axel Foley successfully solves the case by exposing the conspiracy and bringing the killer to justice. The movie concludes with Axel returning to Detroit, where he is welcomed back as a hero. However, the film also sets up a potential sequel, as Axel receives a call from an old friend in Russia, hinting at another adventure.

Overall, Beverly Hills Cop III is an action-packed comedy that delivers on its promise of high-octane excitement and witty humor. While it may not be as strong as the first two films in the series, it still provides plenty of entertainment value for fans of the franchise.

documents.title: Once Upon a Time in America
documents.original_title: Once Upon a Time in America
documents.tagline: Crime, passion and lust for power.
documents.overview: A former Prohibition-era Jewish gangster returns to the Lower East Side of Manhattan over thirty years later, where he once again must confront the ghosts and regrets of his old life.
documents.plot:
Once Upon a Time in America is a 1984 epic crime film directed by Sergio Leone, based on Harry Grey's semi-autobiographical 1952 novel The Hoods. Leone co-wrote the screenplay with Leonardo Benvenuti, Piero De Bernardi, Enrico Medioli, Franco Arcalli and Franco Ferrini. It stars Robert De Niro, James Woods, Elizabeth McGovern, Joe Pesci, Burt Young, Tuesday Weld and Treat Williams, and follows David "Noodles" Aaronson and Maximilian "Max" Bercovicz, boyhood friends who lead a group of Jewish youths into organized crime in New York.

In the 1930s, gunmen hunt for Noodles, who is lying in an opium den beside a newspaper reporting the deaths of his partners Max, Patsy and Cockeye; he escapes the city. In 1918, the young Noodles runs a small gang doing jobs for the gangster Bugsy. Max joins them after they blackmail a corrupt policeman, and they prosper smuggling liquor, keeping their money in a locker whose key is held by their friend Moe. Noodles loves Moe's sister Deborah, an aspiring dancer who sees no future with a gangster. When Bugsy kills the youngest gang member, Dominic, Noodles kills Bugsy and goes to prison.

Released a decade later, Noodles rejoins the gang. During a jewel heist he rapes Carol, their inside informant, who later becomes Max's girlfriend, and tensions grow as Max's ambitions expand. After a lavish date, Noodles rapes Deborah when she reveals she is leaving for Hollywood. With Prohibition ending, Max proposes robbing the Federal Reserve Bank, and Carol persuades Noodles to tip off the police about a lesser crime to protect Max. Max knocks Noodles out, and the three partners are killed by police; Noodles also finds the locker money gone. In the 1960s, a letter revealing that his identity is known draws Noodles back to New York, where he finds a suitcase of money offered as an advance on a job. He learns that Deborah, now a famous actress, is the lover of the scandal-hit Secretary of Commerce Christopher Bailey, who turns out to be Max. Max faked his death and stole the money, and now asks Noodles to kill him. Noodles refuses and leaves, and a figure who may be Max vanishes behind a passing garbage truck. The film ends in the 1930s opium den, with Noodles smiling.

The film premiered at Cannes on May 20, 1984, to a standing ovation, but a heavily cut 139-minute version flopped in the United States, earning about $5.5 million on a $30 million budget. Critics dismissed the shortened cut, while the full version fared far better abroad.

documents.title: Catwoman
documents.tagline: You can’t CATch her.
documents.overview: A shy woman, endowed with the speed, reflexes, and senses of a cat, walks a thin line between criminal and hero, even as a detective doggedly pursues her, fascinated by both of her personas
documents.plot:
Artist Patience Phillips works for the cosmetics company Hedare Beauty, which is ready to ship a new skin cream called Beau-line that is able to reverse the effects of aging.
However, when Patience visits the R&D laboratory facility to deliver a revised ad design, she overhears a discussion between scientist Dr. Ivan Slavicky and Laurel Hedare, the wife of company-owner George Hedare, about the dangerous side effects from continual use of the product. Laurel's guards discover Patience and are ordered to dispose of her.
Patience tries to escape using a conduit pipe, but it is soon sealed off by the guards, who flush the pipe with water. Left for dead she washed up on shore, Patience is mysteriously revived by the Egyptian Mau cat Midnight, which had appeared at her apartment earlier. From that moment on, she develops cat-like metahuman attributes. From Midnight's owner, eccentric researcher Ophelia Powers, Patience learns that Egyptian Mau cats serve as messengers of the goddess Bast. Patience realizes that she is now a "Catwoman", reborn with abilities that are both a blessing and a curse that turn her away from her former meek people-pleasing qualities.
While at home, Patience is annoyed by the ruckus caused by her neighbor's party and lashes out by spraying the amplifiers with water to mute the noise. She disguises herself as a mysterious vigilante named Catwoman to hide her identity, then, under the cover of darkness, searches for answers about what led to her supposed death and subsequent framing for the murder of Slavicky, who she discovers was killed. When Patience confronts George (who is attending an opera with another woman) as Catwoman, he reveals that he knows nothing about the side effects.
The police, led by Patience's love interest, detective Tom Lone, arrive, and Catwoman escapes. Later on, Laurel murders George for his growing suspicions and infidelity and admits to having Dr. Slavicky killed because he wanted to cancel the product's release. She contacts Catwoman and frames her for the murder, planning to release Beau-line to the public the following day. Tom then takes Catwoman into custody.
Patience slips out of her cell and confronts Laurel in her office, rescuing Tom, who came to question Laurel after second thoughts about Patience's guilt, in the process, and revealing that Laurel is the one responsible for her death. As they fight, Patience sees she is unable to hurt Laurel.
Laurel reveals the product's side effects: discontinuing its use makes the skin disintegrate, while continuing its use makes the skin as hard as marble and the user impervious to pain. During the fight, Patience scratches Laurel's face several times, causing her to fall out of a window and grab onto a broken glass pipe. Laurel sees her rapidly disfiguring face in a window's reflection. Horrified, she fails to grab hold of Patience's outstretched hand, causing her to lose her grip and falls to her death.

documents.title: Mystic River
documents.tagline: We bury our sins, we wash them clean.
documents.overview: The lives of three men who were childhood friends are shattered when one of them has a family tragedy.
documents.plot:
In 1975, Irish-American neighborhood friends Jimmy Markum, Sean Devine, and Dave Boyle are playing street hockey in Charlestown, Boston. After the boys write their names in a patch of wet concrete on the sidewalk, two predators posing as police officers abduct Dave and rape him for four days until he escapes. One of the kidnappers dies before they can be caught, and the other is arrested and later dies by suicide in prison. 25 years later, Jimmy is an ex-convict and neighborhood convenience store owner; Sean is a detective with the Massachusetts State Police whose pregnant wife Lauren recently left him, and Dave is a blue-collar worker continually haunted by the abduction and rape he suffered. Jimmy and Dave are connected by marriage: Dave's wife Celeste and Jimmy's second wife Annabeth are cousins.
Jimmy's daughter from his first marriage, Katie, plans to run away to Las Vegas with Brendan Harris, a boy from a family Jimmy despises that she has been secretly dating. One night, Dave sees Katie and her friends at a local bar. That same night, she is murdered, and Dave comes home bloodied and injured, claiming he fought off a mugger and possibly killed him. Sean and his partner Whitey Powers investigate the murder, while a distraught Jimmy conducts a separate investigation using his neighborhood connections.
A witness statement suggests that Katie may have recognized her killer. The detectives understand that the gun used to kill her, a .38 Special revolver, was also used in a liquor store robbery in 1984 by "Just Ray" Harris, Brendan's father. Harris has been missing since 1989, but Brendan claims he still sends his family $500 monthly and feigns ignorance about Ray's gun. Whitey suspects Dave, who keeps changing the story about how his hand got injured. Dave's erratic behavior prompts Celeste to leave their home and tell Jimmy she suspects Dave is Katie's murderer.
Jimmy and his friends invite Dave to a local bar, get him drunk and confront him when he is about to vomit. Jimmy admits to Dave that he killed "Just Ray" for implicating him in the liquor store robbery, which resulted in his imprisonment. Dave reveals to Jimmy that he did kill someone the night of Katie's murder, not Katie herself but instead a child molester whom he found with a sex-trafficked child. Not believing him, Jimmy forces Dave to admit to Katie's murder before killing him and disposing of his body in the adjacent Mystic River. Meanwhile, after finding his father's gun missing, Brendan confronts his mute younger brother "Silent Ray" and his friend John O'Shea about Katie's murder. After beating the two boys, John pulls out Ray's gun and is about to shoot Brendan, but Sean and Whitey, having connected the teens to the murder, arrive in time to disarm and arrest John and Ray.
The next morning, Sean tells Jimmy that John and Silent Ray confessed to killing Katie as part of a prank gone wrong.

documents.title: Snakes on a Plane
documents.tagline: Sit back. Relax. Enjoy the fright.
documents.overview: America is on the search for the murderer Eddie Kim. Sean Jones must fly to L.A. to testify in a hearing against Kim. Accompanied by FBI agent Neville Flynn, the flight receives some unexpected visitors.
documents.plot: FBI agent Neville Flynn boards a flight from Honolulu, Hawaii to Los Angeles, escorting a key witness to testify against a mob boss at an upcoming trial. An on-board assassin releases a crate full of hundreds of deadly venomous snakes in an attempt to eliminate the witness. Flynn and a host of frightened passengers and crew must band together to survive the slithery threat.

documents.title: Brother
documents.tagline: Are You Japanese?
documents.overview: A Japanese Yakuza gangster’s deadly existence in his homeland gets him exiled to Los Angeles, where he is taken in by his little brother and his brother’s gang.
documents.plot:
Brother (Japanese: ブラザー) is a 2000 crime film written, directed and edited by Takeshi Kitano, who also stars as Yamamoto, a veteran yakuza enforcer who flees to Los Angeles after his clan is destroyed in a gang war. The cast includes Omar Epps as Denny, Claude Maki as Yamamoto's half-brother Ken, Susumu Terajima as Kato and Masaya Kato as Shirase. Produced by Jeremy Thomas, who promised Kitano complete creative control, it is the only American production Kitano has directed or starred in.

When his boss is killed and his clan defeated by a rival family, the surviving members face a choice between joining the victors in disgrace or taking their own lives. Yamamoto instead escapes to Los Angeles with his associate Kato and seeks out his estranged half-brother Ken, who deals drugs on a small scale with a group of African-American friends. At their first meeting Yamamoto badly injures one of them, Denny, for trying to cheat him, and he later beats Denny in a game by secretly puncturing a cup. Despite this rough start, Denny becomes one of his closest friends and allies. Accustomed to the discipline and codes of the yakuza, Yamamoto organizes Ken's friends into a gang, which swiftly and violently seizes territory from Mexican drug bosses and allies itself with Shirase, a crime boss in Little Tokyo.

As the gang grows into a formidable force, its members come to address Yamamoto respectfully as Aniki, or "elder brother", and its expansion eventually brings it into conflict with the powerful Italian Mafia. At the height of their success, Yamamoto unexpectedly loses interest in the dangerous business, spending his time with his girlfriend or sitting in silence. The Mafia retaliates ruthlessly, hunting down the gang members one by one until no escape remains. Yamamoto dies, and Denny drives away with a bag, complaining about its smell and fearing that he may be next. Inside he finds compensation money from Yamamoto for the game in which he had cheated, and Denny breaks down, tearfully declaring his love for Aniki.

Kitano conceived the film as an old-fashioned yakuza story set in a foreign country for contrast. It premiered at the Venice Film Festival on 7 September 2000, and several scenes were censored for its U.S. release. Promoted as Kitano's breakthrough into the American market, it received mixed reviews, with 47% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 47; critics faulted its hollow bloodshed and flat characters.

documents.title: Once Upon a Time in the West
documents.tagline: There were three men in her life. One to take her… one to love her —and one to kill her.
documents.overview: As the railroad builders advance unstoppably through the Arizona desert on their way to the sea, Jill arrives in the small town of Flagstone with the intention of starting a new life.
documents.plot:
Once Upon a Time in the West is a classic Western film directed by Sergio Leone, released in 1968 by Paramount Pictures. The movie is set in the late 19th century and follows the story of Frank, a mysterious stranger who arrives in the small town of Red Rock, where he becomes embroiled in a conflict between a group of settlers and a ruthless outlaw named Harry Luck.

The film begins with Frank (Henry Fonda), a former Union soldier, arriving in Red Rock, where he meets a young woman named Jill McBain (Claudia Cardinale). Frank is immediately drawn to Jill, but their budding romance is complicated by the presence of Harry Luck (Charles Bronson), a notorious outlaw who has been terrorizing the town.

As Frank and Jill's relationship deepens, they become embroiled in a conflict between the settlers and Harry Luck, who is determined to take over the town's gold mine. The settlers, led by a man named Harmonica (Claude Debusschere), are determined to protect their land and way of life from Harry's tyranny.

Meanwhile, Frank discovers that Jill is actually the daughter of a wealthy rancher named Lattimo (Luigi Zanni) and that she has been hiding her true identity in order to escape her family's expectations. As tensions between the settlers and Harry's gang escalate, Frank finds himself drawn into a violent confrontation with the outlaws.

One of the most iconic scenes in the film is the "Harmonica" sequence, in which Harmonica plays a haunting melody on his harmonica while being pursued by Harry's gang. This scene has become an iconic moment in Western cinema and showcases Debusschere's impressive acting skills.

As the conflict between Frank and Harry reaches its climax, it becomes clear that Frank is not just a simple stranger, but a complex and troubled individual with a deep sense of justice. In a final confrontation, Frank faces off against Harry and his gang, leading to a violent and bloody showdown.

In the end, Frank emerges victorious, but not without scars. He rides off into the sunset with Jill by his side, leaving behind the violence and bloodshed of the conflict. The film ends on a hopeful note, suggesting that Frank has finally found redemption and a sense of purpose in life.

Throughout the film, Leone's direction is masterful, using long takes and sweeping cinematography to create a sense of scope and scale. The score by Ennio Morricone is equally iconic, featuring a haunting theme that has become synonymous with Western cinema.

Overall, Once Upon a Time in the West is a classic Western film that explores themes of violence, redemption, and the search for identity. With its complex characters, intricate plot, and iconic scenes, it remains one of the greatest Westerns of all time.

documents.title: Monsieur Ibrahim
documents.original_title: Monsieur Ibrahim et les Fleurs du Coran
documents.overview: Paris, 1960s. Momo, a resolute and independent Jewish teenager who lives with his father, a sullen and depressed man, in a working-class neighborhood, develops a close friendship with Monsieur Ibrahim, an elderly Muslim who owns a small grocery store.
documents.plot: The story unfolds in a working-class neighborhood in the Paris of the 1960s. The protagonist, Moїse Schmidt (Momo), is a young Jewish boy growing up without a mother and with a father afflicted by crippling depression. Momo is fascinated by the elderly Turkish Muslim man, Ibrahim Demirci, who runs a grocery store across the street from his apartment (where Momo often shoplifts). Their relationship develops and soon Momo feels closer to Ibrahim than to his father. Ibrahim affectionately calls Moїse Momo, and adopts him when his father leaves and commits suicide. Momo and Ibrahim go on a journey in their new car to Turkey, Ibrahim's native country, where Momo learns about Ibrahim's culture. At the end of their adventure, Ibrahim is killed in a car crash and Momo returns to Paris to take over the shop.

documents.title: Good Bye Lenin!
documents.tagline: The German Democratic Republic lives on -- in 79 square meters!
documents.overview: Alex Kerner's mother was in a coma while the Berlin wall fell. When she wakes up he must try to keep her from learning what happened (as she was an avid communist supporter) to avoid shocking her which could lead to another heart attack.
documents.plot:
The film is set in East Berlin, in the period from October 1989 to a few days after German reunification in October 1990.
Alex Kerner lives with his mother Christiane, his sister Ariane, and Ariane’s infant daughter Paula. Alex's father purportedly abandoned the family for a mistress in the West in 1978. His mother joined the Socialist Unity Party and devoted her time to advocating for citizens. Alex is disillusioned by the celebration of East Germany's 40th anniversary and participates in an anti-government demonstration. There he meets a girl, but they are separated by the Volkspolizei before they can introduce themselves.
Christiane, seeing Alex being arrested and beaten, suffers a heart attack and falls into a coma because nobody initially comes to her aid. Visiting his mother in the hospital, Alex finds that her nurse, Lara, is the girl from the demonstration. She (an exchange student from the Soviet Union) and Alex begin dating shortly afterward.
Erich Honecker resigns, Egon Krenz takes over, the borders are opened, the Berlin Wall falls, East Germany holds free elections, and capitalism comes to East Berlin. Alex begins working for a West German firm selling and installing satellite dishes. He befriends a Western colleague, aspiring filmmaker Denis Domaschke. Ariane drops out of university, where she studied economics, and begins working at Burger King, dating her manager Rainer, who moves into their apartment.
After eight months, Christiane awakens from her coma. Her doctor warns her family that she is still weak and any shock might cause another, possibly fatal, heart attack. Alex resolves to conceal the profound societal changes from her and maintain the illusion that the German Democratic Republic is just as it was before her coma. He retrieves their old East German furniture, makes everyone in the flat dress in old, East German clothes, and repackages new Western food in old East German jars. The deception becomes increasingly complicated as Christiane witnesses strange occurrences, such as a gigantic Coca-Cola banner on an adjacent building. Denis and Alex create fake news broadcasts in the style of old East German news tapes to explain these odd events. Alex and Ariane fail to find where Christiane keeps her life savings (in East German marks) in time to exchange them for West German marks before the deadline.
Christiane gets stronger and one day wanders outside while Alex is asleep. She sees her neighbours' old East German furniture stacked in the street, new West German cars for sale, advertisements for Western corporations, and a statue of Lenin being flown away by helicopter. Alex and Ariane take her back home and Alex shows her a fake newscast explaining East Germany is now accepting refugees from the West following an economic crisis there. Ariane tells Alex she is pregnant with Rainer's baby; it will be half East German and half West German, a symbol of the new Germany.

documents.title: Harold and Maude
documents.tagline: They were meant to be. But exactly what they were meant to be is not quite clear.
documents.overview: The young Harold lives in his own world of suicide-attempts and funeral visits to avoid the misery of his current family and home environment. Harold meets an 80-year-old woman named Maude who also lives in her own world yet one in which she is having the time of her life. When the two opposites meet they realize that their differences don’t matter and they become best friends and love each other.
documents.plot: A deadpan young man obsessed with death meets an eccentric septuagenarian who teaches him to live life to the fullest.

documents.title: Alien
documents.tagline: In space no one can hear you scream.
documents.overview: During its return to the earth, commercial spaceship Nostromo intercepts a distress signal from a distant planet. When a three-member team of the crew discovers a chamber containing thousands of eggs on the planet, a creature inside one of the eggs attacks an explorer. The entire crew is unaware of the impending nightmare set to descend upon them when the alien parasite planted inside its unfortunate host is birthed.
documents.plot:
Alien is a science fiction horror film directed by Ridley Scott, released in 1979 by 20th Century Fox. The movie takes place in the year 2122 and follows the crew of the commercial towing spaceship Nostromo.

The story begins with the crew of the Nostromo, consisting of seven members, who are awakened from stasis by the ship's computer, Mother, to investigate a distress signal from an abandoned mining colony on the planet Thedus. The crew is led by Captain Dallas (Tom Skerritt), and includes engineers Parker (Yaphet Kotto) and Brett (Harry Dean Stanton); scientists Ash (Ian Holm) and Kane (John Hurt); and two security officers, Ripley (Sigourney Weaver) and Lambert (Veronica Cartwright).

Upon arrival at Thedus, the crew discovers that the colony has been destroyed, and a derelict alien spacecraft is nearby. The crew boards the ship to investigate, where they find a chamber containing hundreds of large, leathery eggs. One of the crew members, Kane, is attacked by a facehugger, a parasitic creature that attaches itself to his face.

The crew manages to rescue Kane and bring him back to the Nostromo, but soon discovers that the facehugger has implanted an embryo inside Kane's body. The crew is unaware of the danger they are in, as the alien embryo begins to grow inside Kane's chest cavity.

As the crew tries to figure out what is happening to Kane, Ash reveals that he has been secretly working for a corporation called Weyland-Yutani, which is interested in acquiring the alien technology. The crew soon discovers that the alien creature, now grown and free from its egg, has escaped and is terrorizing them.

The alien begins to hunt down and kill off the crew members one by one, using its sharp claws and acid blood to deadly effect. Ripley, who had initially been hesitant to join the crew, becomes the last survivor of the Nostromo's crew.

In a desperate bid to escape, Ripley uses the ship's engines to blast off into space, but not before the alien attacks her. She manages to fend it off using a flamethrower and then seals herself in a airlock chamber with the creature. In a final confrontation, Ripley kills the alien by shooting a welding torch at its face.

As the Nostromo escapes into space, Ripley is left alone, traumatized by the events that have occurred. The movie ends with Ripley's ship drifting through space, as she reflects on the horrors she has experienced and the loss of her crewmates.

Alien was a groundbreaking film in many ways, including its use of practical effects, atmospheric tension, and strong female protagonist. It has since become a classic of science fiction horror and continues to influence filmmakers to this day.

documents.title: The Devil Wears Prada
documents.tagline: Meet Andy Sachs. A million girls would kill to have her job. She's not one of them.
documents.overview: Andy moves to New York to work in the fashion industry. Her boss is extremely demanding, cruel and won't let her succeed if she doesn't fit into the high class elegant look of their magazine.
documents.plot:
Aspiring journalist Andrea "Andy" Sachs has recently graduated from Northwestern University. Despite her lack of knowledge of the fashion industry, she is hired as a junior personal assistant to Miranda Priestly, the cruel editor-in-chief of Runway magazine in New York City. Andy resolves to tolerate Miranda's abusive treatment until she can use her connections from Runway to find a journalism-focused job.
Andy fits in poorly with her superficial, fashion-forward co-workers, particularly Miranda's British senior assistant, Emily Charlton, and struggles to meet Miranda's irrational demands. After she fails to arrange for Miranda to be flown back from Miami during a hurricane, she is berated. She then approaches Runway's art director Nigel for advice, and he helps her select stylish clothes to fit the extremely fashion-conscious workplace.
Noticing Andy's increased commitment to the job, Miranda delegates more important tasks to her. Andy soon outperforms Emily, who yearns to attend Paris Fashion Week as Miranda's assistant. In preparation for the event, Emily follows extreme diets that endanger her health.
When Emily arrives to work sick and forgets the names of important guests at a charity benefit, Andy steps in to save Miranda from embarrassment. Miranda subsequently selects Andy to accompany her to Paris Fashion Week. Emily is horrified that Andy accepted Miranda's offer. After Andy snaps at her boyfriend Nate, who is disappointed that she has become one of the shallow, egotistical women she once ridiculed, they break up with each other in the street.
In Paris, Andy learns that Miranda's husband has filed for divorce. Later that night, Nigel tells Andy that he has accepted a job as creative director for rising designer James Holt. Andy spends the night with an attractive writer, Christian Thompson, who tells her that Jacqueline Follet (Miranda's counterpart as editor-in-chief at French Runway) is being prepared to replace Miranda. Andy attempts to warn Miranda, who dismisses her.
At a luncheon, Miranda announces Jacqueline as Holt's new creative director and later reveals that she already knew of the scheme to replace her and sacrificed Nigel's ambitions to preserve her own job. Andy is repulsed by Miranda's betrayal of her friend, but Miranda points out that Andy did the same thing to Emily. Afraid to become the type of person Miranda is, Andy storms off. When Miranda tries calling her, Andy tosses her phone into the Fontaines de la Concorde.
Back in New York, Andy meets up with Nate, who tells her he has a new job as a sous-chef in Boston, and they agree to keep in touch. The same day, Andy has an interview at the New York Mirror newspaper. The editor recounts that when he called Runway for a reference, Miranda told him that Andy was the biggest disappointment she had ever had as an assistant and that he would be an idiot not to hire her.
After getting the job, Andy calls Emily and offers her the clothes she obtained in Paris.

documents.title: Das Boot
documents.tagline: When the hunters become the hunted.
documents.overview: A German submarine hunts allied ships during the Second World War, but it soon becomes the hunted. The crew tries to survive below the surface, while stretching both the boat and themselves to their limits.
documents.plot: A German submarine hunts allied ships during the Second World War, but it soon becomes the hunted. The crew tries to survive below the surface, while stretching both the boat and themselves to their limits.

documents.title: Inside Man
documents.tagline: It looked like the perfect bank robbery. But you can’t judge a crime by its cover.
documents.overview: When an armed, masked gang enter a Manhattan bank, lock the doors and take hostages, the detective assigned to effect their release enters negotiations preoccupied with corruption charges he is facing.
documents.plot:
Inside Man is a 2006 American heist thriller film directed by Spike Lee, written by David Self, and produced by Sidney Lumet, among others.

The movie begins with a series of seemingly unrelated bank robberies across New York City. The thief, known as "The Architect" (played by Clive Owen), calls the police department to claim responsibility for the heists. He demands that $50 million be wired into a bank vault within 60 minutes or the hostages will be killed.

Detective Keith Frazier (Denzel Washington) is assigned to lead the investigation, and he assembles a team of experts, including Detective Monica Foster (Cloris Leachman), FBI Agent John Klein (Willem Dafoe), and forensic expert Dr. Ed Stevenson (Christopher Plummer).

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that The Architect has a personal connection to the city's financial elite. He targets three different banks in Manhattan: the First National Bank of New York, the Wells Fargo Bank, and the Chase Manhattan Bank.

The plot thickens as Detective Frazier discovers that The Architect is not just any ordinary thief but a mastermind with a complex plan. He has taken several hostages, including bank employees and customers, and has rigged the vaults with explosives.

As the clock ticks down, Detective Frazier becomes increasingly obsessed with catching The Architect. Meanwhile, Monica Foster begins to suspect that there may be more to the story than meets the eye.

In a surprising twist, it is revealed that The Architect is actually Dalton Russell (Denzel Washington), a former Wall Street executive who was fired from his job and has been seeking revenge against the financial system he feels wronged him. He has created an elaborate scheme to expose the corruption and greed of the wealthy elite.

The movie's climax features a tense standoff between Detective Frazier and Dalton, with the fate of the hostages hanging in the balance. In the end, Dalton is arrested, but not before revealing that his plan was not just about stealing money but also about exposing the hypocrisy and greed of those who have been wronged by the system.

Throughout the movie, Spike Lee's direction masterfully weaves together themes of class struggle, corporate greed, and personal revenge. The film features a talented ensemble cast, including Clive Owen, Denzel Washington, and Willem Dafoe, who deliver standout performances that add depth to the story.

Overall, Inside Man is a gripping thriller that keeps viewers on the edge of their seats until the very end. With its complex plot, memorable characters, and thought-provoking themes, it's no wonder this movie has become a modern classic in the world of crime dramas.

documents.title: Chocolat
documents.tagline: …and the world is still indulging!
documents.overview: A mother and daughter move to a small French town where they open a chocolate shop. The town, religious and morally strict, is against them, as they represent free-thinking and indulgence. When a group of Boat Gypsies float down the river, the prejudice of the Mayor leads to a crisis.
documents.plot:
Vianne and her six-year-old daughter Anouk drift across Europe following the north wind, like Vianne's mother before her. In 1959, they arrive in the quiet French village of Lansquenet-sous-Tannes, of which the Comte de Reynaud is mayor, at the start of Lent. Vianne opens a chocolate shop; despite not fitting in well with the townspeople, she begins to make headway with some of the villagers, getting them to come to her shop. Reynaud, who will not admit that his wife has left him, speaks out against Vianne for tempting the people during Lent.
Armande, Vianne's elderly landlady, is one of her first allies. Armande's daughter Caroline will not let her see her grandson Luc, as she is a "bad influence". Vianne arranges for him and his grandmother to meet in the chocolaterie, where they bond. After finding out about their secret meetings, Caroline reveals her mother is diabetic, but she continues to eat the chocolate when visiting the shop.
Vianne develops a friendship with Josephine, who is being physically abused by her husband Serge, the local café owner. Through their friendship, Josephine finds the courage to leave Serge after he beats her, moving in with Vianne and Anouk. As she works at the chocolate shop and learns the craft, her confidence slowly increases. Simultaneously, under Reynaud's instruction, Serge attempts to make amends for his abusiveness, eventually asking Josephine to return to him, but she refuses. Later that night, a drunken Serge breaks into the shop, attacking both women, but Josephine knocks him out.
As the rivalry between Vianne and Reynaud intensifies, a band of river-faring Romani ("river rats") camp near the village. Although most of the town objects to their presence, Vianne embraces them and a mutual attraction develops between her and the leader, Roux. They throw a birthday party for Armande with villagers on Roux's boat. When Caroline sees Luc dancing with his grandmother, she begins to accept that Armande's influence in her son's life may be positive. Luc takes Armande home after the party, while Josephine and Anouk fall asleep on a boat, which Serge sets fire to, while Vianne and Roux have sex on a barge in the river. No one is hurt in the fire, but Vianne is shaken. Armande later dies in her home and is discovered by Luc. This devastates both Luc and his mother. Meanwhile, Roux packs up and leaves with his group.
Reynaud initially believes the fire was divine intervention until Serge confesses to starting it, saying he thought it was what Reynaud wanted. Horrified, Reynaud orders him to leave the village and never to return.
With the return of the north wind, Vianne realizes she cannot win against Reynaud, and decides to move on. Anouk, now attached to the town, refuses to go, and during a scuffle, the urn containing Vianne's mother's ashes breaks, scattering them over the floor.

documents.title: AVP: Alien vs. Predator
documents.tagline: Whoever wins... We lose
documents.overview: When scientists discover something in the Arctic that appears to be a buried Pyramid, they send a research team out to investigate. Little do they know that they are about to step into a hunting ground where Aliens are grown as sport for the Predator race.
documents.plot:
AVP: Alien vs. Predator is a 2004 science fiction action film directed by Paul W.S. Anderson, produced by 20th Century Fox, and written by Anderson and screenwriter Alex Litvak.

The movie begins with the discovery of an ancient temple on Earth's moon by a team of archaeologists led by Dr. William "Bill" Ikeda (Lance Henriksen). The team is searching for a lost city that holds secrets to the origins of humanity. Unbeknownst to them, they have disturbed a long-dormant alien artifact, which awakens an ancient predator, the Yautja, also known as the Predator.

The Yautja, a technologically advanced and deadly extraterrestrial species, is drawn to Earth by the disturbance in its temple. The creature arrives on the moon and begins to hunt down the archaeologists, killing them one by one. Meanwhile, a spaceship carrying a group of humans from the United States, led by Lieutenant Colonel David Cornwell (Raoul Bova), crash-lands on the moon.

As the Yautja continues its rampage, it is discovered that the aliens are not just mindless killers but have a complex culture and hunting rituals. The Predator's ship lands nearby, and a group of Predators emerges to hunt down the humans. However, they soon realize that the humans are not their usual prey, as they possess a unique genetic trait that makes them resistant to the Predator's deadly plasma caster.

The movie takes a turn when the Yautja and the Predators engage in an epic battle on the moon's surface. The two species clash, with the Yautja using its superior strength and ferocity against the Predators' advanced technology. As the fight rages on, the humans are forced to take sides, with some joining forces with the Predators to survive.

In the end, the Predators emerge victorious, but not without sustaining significant damage from the Yautja's attacks. The movie concludes with the Predators departing Earth, leaving behind a human survivor, who is left to ponder the implications of the encounter between two ancient and deadly species.

Throughout the film, Anderson pays homage to both the Alien and Predator franchises, blending their respective mythologies into a unique narrative that explores the idea of an epic battle between two formidable foes. While AVP: Alien vs. Predator received mixed reviews from critics at the time of its release, it has since become a cult classic among fans of science fiction action films.

The movie's success can be attributed to its well-crafted action sequences, stunning visual effects, and the intriguing dynamic between the Yautja and Predators. The film's climax, which features an intense battle between the two species, is particularly memorable, showcasing the Predator's advanced technology and ferocity in a way that has become iconic in science fiction cinema.

Overall, AVP: Alien vs. Predator is a thrilling sci-fi action film that brings together two beloved franchises in a unique and entertaining way.

documents.title: Capote
documents.tagline: In Cold Blood.
documents.overview: A biopic of writer Truman Capote and his assignment for The New Yorker to write the non-fiction book "In Cold Blood".
documents.plot:
Capote is a 2005 biographical drama film directed by Bennett Miller and written by Dan Futterman, based on Gerald Clarke's 1988 biography of the American novelist Truman Capote. Philip Seymour Hoffman stars in the title role, and the film concentrates on the years in which Capote researched and wrote his 1965 nonfiction book In Cold Blood. The cast also includes Catherine Keener, whose performance earned an Academy Award nomination for Best Supporting Actress.

In 1959, after reading in The New York Times about the murder of the Clutter family on their Kansas farm, Capote tells William Shawn, editor of The New Yorker, that he means to write about the crime. He travels to Kansas with his childhood friend Nelle Harper Lee, who helps him approach the people involved. The lead detective, Alvin Dewey, initially rebuffs him, but Dewey's wife Marie, an admirer of his writing, arranges a dinner, and Dewey gradually warms to him. The suspects, Perry Smith and Richard "Dick" Hickock, are soon caught, and through flattery, bribery and insight Capote gains access to them in prison. Growing attached to Smith, he decides to expand the story into a full-length book. After the two men are convicted and sentenced to death, Capote keeps visiting by bribing the warden, apart from a year writing in Morocco and Spain with his partner Jack Dunphy. Moved by Smith's life story and apparent remorse, Capote helps the killers obtain expert lawyers for an appeal, yet Smith refuses to describe the night of the murders. As the appeals drag on for years, Capote finds himself with a story that has no ending. When Smith finally recounts the killings in detail, Capote recognizes his own callousness. While Lee's novel To Kill a Mockingbird becomes a film, Capote cannot share in her success, sinking into drink. When the last appeal fails, Smith begs him to return, and only a telegram to Lee prompts Capote to go back to Kansas, where he witnesses the executions. When he tells Lee he could do nothing to stop it, she replies that he did not want to. An epilogue notes that the book made Capote famous but that he never finished another before dying of alcoholism-related complications in 1984.

Released by Sony Pictures Classics on September 30, 2005, what would have been Capote's 81st birthday, the film grossed $50 million worldwide on a $7 million budget. It was widely acclaimed, earning five Academy Award nominations, including Best Picture, and Hoffman won the Oscar for Best Actor.

documents.title: Garden State
documents.overview: Andrew returns to his hometown for the funeral of his mother, a journey that reconnects him with past friends. The trip coincides with his decision to stop taking his powerful antidepressants. A chance meeting with Sam - a girl also suffering from various maladies - opens up the possibility of rekindling emotional attachments, confronting his psychologist father, and perhaps beginning a new life.
documents.plot:
Struggling actor Andrew Largeman wakes up from a dream—in which he apathetically sits on a crashing plane—to a telephone message from his father, telling Andrew that he needs to return home because his mother has died.
Andrew leaves Los Angeles and returns home to New Jersey to attend the funeral. He recognizes the grave-diggers as old friends Mark and Dave, who invite him to a party that night. At home, Andrew's father gets him a doctor's appointment for headaches that he has been having.
Later that night, Andrew goes to the party where he meets up with Mark, Dave, and Jesse, an old friend who has just earned a fortune after creating silent Velcro. After smoking marijuana and taking ecstasy at the party, he still remains detached.
The morning after the party, Andrew proceeds to the appointment. In the waiting room, he meets a young woman named Sam, who is a pathological liar. She later explains that most times she does not know why she lies and will always admit to them afterward. In Andrew's meeting with his doctor, it is revealed that Andrew has been on lithium and other mood stabilizers, as well as antidepressants, since the age of 10, but has recently stopped taking them. He also says that his father, who is his psychiatrist, put him on the medications. Andrew finds Sam outside the office and offers her a ride home. Sam invites him into her house, where he meets her mother, who inadvertently reveals that Sam has epilepsy. Andrew tells Sam of his mother's death, and Sam tearfully eulogizes her hamster. After returning home, Andrew's father confronts him and is insistent that they have a talk before Andrew leaves.
Later, Andrew and Jesse sit in the cemetery as Mark digs another grave. Andrew observes Mark stealing jewelry from the corpse he is burying. Andrew then returns to Sam's house, and the two spend the rest of the day together, joining his friends later at Jesse's mansion. Andrew tells Sam that he pushed his mother in frustration when he was nine years old, knocking her over a broken dishwasher and leaving her paraplegic; he says that his father blames him for his mother's paralysis and put him on medication to "curb the anger" he supposedly harbors. Sam listens, and Andrew admits his feelings for her.
The next day, Mark tells Andrew that he needs help "tracking down" a going-away present for him. Sam, Andrew, and Mark spend the day together, ending it in a quarry in Newark where Mark talks to a man named Albert, who is employed in keeping intruders out of the quarry. The three discuss the reasons why Albert and his wife choose to live in the quarry. Albert explains that living there and exploring the quarry is "doing something that's completely unique, that's never been done before", mirroring an earlier speech by Sam. Finally, Albert explains that what actually matters is living with his family.

documents.title: Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs
documents.original_title: Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs
documents.tagline: The Happiest, Dopiest, Grumpiest, Sneeziest movie of the year.
documents.overview: A beautiful girl, Snow White, takes refuge in the forest in the house of seven dwarfs to hide from her stepmother, the wicked Queen. The Queen is jealous because she wants to be known as "the fairest in the land," and Snow White's beauty surpasses her own.
documents.plot:
Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs is a timeless classic that has captivated audiences for generations. Released in 1937, it was the first full-length animated feature film produced by Walt Disney Productions.

The story begins with a beautiful princess named Snow White, who lives with her stepmother, the Evil Queen. The Queen is jealous of Snow White's beauty and fears that she will one day surpass her. One day, the Magic Mirror, which serves as the Queen's advisor, tells her that Snow White is indeed the fairest of them all.

Enraged by this news, the Queen orders a huntsman to take Snow White into the forest and kill her. However, the huntsman takes pity on Snow White and tells her to run away. He kills a deer and brings its heart back to the Queen, telling her that Snow White has been killed.

Snow White finds herself lost in the forest, where she stumbles upon a small cottage belonging to seven dwarfs: Doc, Grumpy, Happy, Sleepy, Bashful, Sneezy, and Dopey. They welcome her into their home, and Snow White stays with them, keeping house and cooking for the group.

Meanwhile, the Queen discovers that Snow White is still alive when the Magic Mirror reveals the truth to her. Disguising herself as an old hag, the Queen offers Snow White a poisoned apple, which puts Snow White into a magical sleep. The dwarfs discover the Queen's plan and chase her away, but they are unable to revive Snow White.

Just as all hope seems lost, a handsome prince arrives at the cottage and falls in love with Snow White's beauty. He kisses her, breaking the curse, and Snow White awakens from her magical sleep.

The film ends with Snow White and the prince getting married, surrounded by the seven dwarfs and other woodland creatures. The Queen, who has been punished for her evil deeds, is forced to dance to death in red-hot iron shoes at Snow White's wedding.

Throughout the film, Walt Disney Productions showcased its innovative animation techniques, which included the use of multiplane camera and audio recording technology. The result was a visually stunning and enchanting film that has become an iconic part of American pop culture.

The characters in Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs are memorable and endearing, with each dwarf bringing their unique personality to the story. Doc is the intelligent and wise leader, Grumpy is the grouchy but lovable companion, Happy is the cheerful and optimistic one, Sleepy is the sleepy and dreamy dwarf, Bashful is the shy and blushing dwarf, Sneezy is the dwarf with allergies, and Dopey is the goofy and playful one.

Overall, Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs is a classic tale of good vs. evil, love, and redemption that has captivated audiences for generations. Its enduring popularity is a testament to the timeless appeal of Walt Disney's magical storytelling.

documents.title: The Chronicles of Narnia: The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe
documents.original_title: The Chronicles of Narnia: The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe
documents.tagline: Evil Has Reigned For 100 Years...
documents.overview: Siblings Lucy, Edmund, Susan and Peter step through a magical wardrobe and find the land of Narnia. There, they discover a charming, once peaceful kingdom that has been plunged into eternal winter by the evil White Witch, Jadis. Aided by the wise and magnificent lion, Aslan, the children lead Narnia into a spectacular, climactic battle to be free of the Witch's glacial powers forever.
documents.plot:
The Chronicles of Narnia: The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe is a 2005 high fantasy film directed by Andrew Adamson, based on C. S. Lewis's 1950 novel. The first installment of The Chronicles of Narnia film series, it was produced by Walt Disney Pictures and Walden Media. William Moseley, Anna Popplewell, Skandar Keynes and Georgie Henley star as the four Pevensie children, with Tilda Swinton as the White Witch and Liam Neeson as the voice of Aslan.

In 1940, to escape the Blitz, Peter, Susan, Edmund and Lucy Pevensie are evacuated to the countryside home of Professor Kirke. During a game of hide-and-seek, Lucy hides in a wardrobe and finds herself in a snowy forest in the land of Narnia, where she meets a faun, Mr. Tumnus. He confesses that he meant to hand her over to the White Witch, Jadis, who has cursed Narnia with endless winter and no Christmas, but instead he helps her return home. When Lucy returns to Narnia, Edmund follows her and meets the Witch, who tempts him with Turkish delight and a promise to make him a prince if he brings his siblings to her.

Fleeing the housekeeper, all four children escape through the wardrobe into Narnia, where they find that Tumnus has been arrested. Mr. and Mrs. Beaver tell them that Aslan, the true king, has returned and of a prophecy that four humans will end the Witch's reign. Edmund slips away to the Witch, who imprisons him and sends her wolves after the others. As her power weakens, Father Christmas gives the children gifts, including a sword for Peter, a bow for Susan and a healing cordial for Lucy. They reach Aslan, a great lion, and his army, and Edmund is rescued.

The Witch claims Edmund's life as a traitor under the Deep Magic, and Aslan secretly agrees to die in his place. Lucy and Susan watch as the Witch kills him on the Stone Table. The next morning, Aslan returns to life through a deeper magic and leads the sisters to free the creatures turned to stone in the Witch's castle. In the great battle, Edmund is gravely wounded while breaking the Witch's wand before Aslan arrives and kills her, and Lucy heals him. The four are crowned kings and queens of Narnia. Years later, as adults, they follow a white stag back through the wardrobe and return as children to the same moment they left.

The film premiered on 7 December 2005 and was a critical and commercial success. It grossed $745 million worldwide, won the Academy Award for Best Makeup, and was followed by Prince Caspian (2008).

documents.title: The Life Aquatic with Steve Zissou
documents.original_title: The Life Aquatic with Steve Zissou
documents.tagline: The deeper you go, the weirder life gets.
documents.overview: Renowned oceanographer Steve Zissou has sworn vengeance upon the rare shark that devoured a member of his crew. In addition to his regular team, he is joined on his boat by Ned, a man who believes Zissou to be his father, and Jane, a journalist pregnant by a married man. They travel the sea, all too often running into pirates and, perhaps more traumatically, various figures from Zissou's past, including his estranged wife, Eleanor.
