documents.title: The Last Samurai
documents.tagline: In the face of an enemy, in the heart of one man, lies the soul of a warrior.
documents.overview: Nathan Algren is an American hired to instruct the Japanese army in the ways of modern warfare, which finds him learning to respect the samurai and the honorable principles that rule them. Pressed to destroy the samurai's way of life in the name of modernization and open trade, Algren decides to become an ultimate warrior himself and to fight for their right to exist.
documents.plot:
The Last Samurai is a 2003 American epic period action drama directed by Edward Zwick, who wrote the screenplay with John Logan and Marshall Herskovitz from a story by Logan. Tom Cruise, who also produced the film, stars as Captain Nathan Algren, with Ken Watanabe as Lord Katsumoto, Koyuki as Taka, Hiroyuki Sanada as Ujio, Timothy Spall as Simon Graham, Billy Connolly as Zebulon Gant and Tony Goldwyn as Colonel Bagley. The story was inspired by the 1877 Satsuma Rebellion led by Saigō Takamori and by the rapid Westernization of Meiji Japan.

In 1876, Nathan Algren is a former U.S. Army captain who drinks heavily to escape the memory of atrocities committed against Native Americans during the Indian Wars. His former commanding officer, Colonel Bagley, recruits him to train the new conscript army of the Japanese emperor on behalf of the businessman Omura, who wants to crush a rebellion by samurai opposed to modernization. Despite his contempt for Bagley, Algren accepts the job for money and travels to Japan with his old comrade Sergeant Gant.

Forced to lead the poorly trained conscripts into battle before they are ready, Algren sees them routed by the samurai. Gant is killed, and the wounded Algren is spared and taken prisoner by the rebel leader Katsumoto. Over the winter in Katsumoto's mountain village, he is cared for by Taka, Katsumoto's sister, whose husband he killed in the battle. Gradually, Algren overcomes his alcoholism and his guilt, learns the language and the way of the samurai, and develops a deep respect for Katsumoto and his followers. When he returns to the capital, he must choose between the government that hired him and the samurai who have given him a new sense of purpose, as Omura's modern army prepares to destroy the last of them.

The film explores honor, redemption and the clash between tradition and modernity, though it also drew criticism for its idealized portrayal of the samurai and for centering the story on an American outsider.

The Last Samurai premiered in Tokyo in November 2003 and was released worldwide by Warner Bros. on December 5, 2003. It grossed about 456.8 million dollars, performing especially well in Japan, and received mixed to positive reviews, with about 65 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes. It earned four Academy Award nominations, including Best Supporting Actor for Watanabe.

documents.title: The Bodyguard
documents.tagline: Never let her out of your sight. Never let your guard down. Never fall in love.
documents.overview: A former Secret Service agent grudgingly takes an assignment to protect a pop idol who's threatened by a crazed fan. At first, the safety-obsessed bodyguard and the self-indulgent diva totally clash. But before long, all that tension sparks fireworks of another sort, and the love-averse tough guy is torn between duty and romance.
documents.plot:
The Bodyguard is a romantic thriller film released in 1992, directed by Mick Jackson and starring Whitney Houston and Kevin Costner. The movie follows the story of two individuals from different worlds who find love in the midst of danger.

The film begins with Rachel Marron (Whitney Houston), a famous pop singer, preparing for her concert tour. Unbeknownst to her, she has been receiving threatening letters and gifts from an unknown stalker. Desperate for protection, Rachel hires two bodyguards, Frank Farmer (Kevin Costner) and his partner, Sy Spector (Gary Kemp). 

Initially, the two men are skeptical of their new assignment but soon realize that they need to take Rachel's safety seriously. As they begin to work together, a strong bond develops between them, and it becomes clear that there is more to Frank than meets the eye.

As the tour progresses, Rachel starts to open up to Frank about her fears and insecurities. Meanwhile, she also begins to develop feelings for him, which complicates their professional relationship. The stalker's threats escalate, putting both Rachel and Frank in grave danger.

Throughout the film, the tension builds as Frank becomes increasingly protective of Rachel. He discovers that the stalker is none other than her former lover, Sy Spector, who has been seeking revenge against Rachel for leaving him. 

In a thrilling climax, Frank confronts Sy at Rachel's concert venue, and in the ensuing fight, Sy is killed. The film ends with Rachel and Frank sharing a romantic moment, as they finally acknowledge their feelings for each other.

The Bodyguard was a commercial success, grossing over $410 million worldwide. It also received positive reviews from critics, who praised the chemistry between Houston and Costner. The movie's soundtrack, featuring Whitney Houston's hit single "I Will Always Love You," became one of the best-selling albums of all time.

Overall, The Bodyguard is a classic romantic thriller that explores themes of love, danger, and protection. With its memorable performances, catchy soundtrack, and suspenseful plot, it remains a beloved film to this day.

documents.title: Bridget Jones's Diary
documents.tagline: Health Warning: Adopting Bridget's lifestyle could seriously damage your health.
documents.overview: A chaotic Bridget Jones meets a snobbish lawyer, and he soon enters her world of imperfections.
documents.plot:
Bridget Jones's Diary is a romantic comedy film directed by Sharon Maguire, based on the novel of the same name by Helen Fielding. The movie was produced by Working Title Films and released in 2001.

The story revolves around Bridget Jones (played by Renée Zellweger), a single woman living in London. She's a bit of an awkward and clumsy person, struggling with her love life, career, and overall well-being. Bridget keeps a diary to record her thoughts, feelings, and experiences, which becomes a confidant for her.

Bridget's life is marked by her on-again, off-again relationship with Daniel Cleaver (played by Hugh Grant), a charming but unreliable man who is also her boss at the office. Despite his womanizing ways, Bridget finds herself drawn to him repeatedly. However, their relationship is complicated, and Bridget often finds herself torn between her desire for him and her need for self-improvement.

As the story unfolds, we meet Bridget's friends, including Shazzer (played by Sally Phillips), Jude (played by Shirley Henderson), and Mark Darcy (played by Colin Firth). Mark is a successful lawyer who initially appears to be an unsuitable match for Bridget due to his stuffy demeanor. However, as the story progresses, we see glimpses of his vulnerable side.

Throughout the film, Bridget faces various challenges, including her struggles with weight, self-acceptance, and relationships. She also has to navigate her complicated feelings towards Daniel and Mark, while trying to improve herself and find happiness.

One of the most significant plot points in the movie is when Bridget meets a new man, Jack (played by Jim Broadbent), who becomes a source of comfort and support for her. However, their relationship is also complicated, as Jack has his own set of emotional baggage.

As the story reaches its climax, Bridget must confront her feelings and make some difficult choices about her relationships and personal growth. In the end, she finds herself with Mark Darcy, who has come to realize his true feelings for her. The film concludes on a hopeful note, as Bridget begins a new chapter in her life with Mark by her side.

Overall, Bridget Jones's Diary is a charming and witty romantic comedy that explores themes of love, self-acceptance, and personal growth. With its strong performances from the cast, particularly Renée Zellweger and Colin Firth, the film has become a beloved classic in the rom-com genre.

documents.title: Catch Me If You Can
documents.tagline: The true story of a real fake.
documents.overview: A true story about Frank Abagnale Jr. who, before his 19th birthday, successfully conned millions of dollars worth of checks as a Pan Am pilot, doctor, and legal prosecutor. An FBI agent makes it his mission to put him behind bars. But Frank not only eludes capture, he revels in the pursuit.
documents.plot:
Catch Me If You Can is a 2002 American biographical crime comedy-drama directed and produced by Steven Spielberg. Leonardo DiCaprio stars as the young con artist Frank Abagnale Jr. and Tom Hanks as the FBI agent pursuing him, with Christopher Walken, Martin Sheen, Nathalie Baye, Amy Adams and James Brolin in supporting roles. Jeff Nathanson's screenplay is based on Abagnale's semi-autobiographical book, which claims that before his nineteenth birthday he carried out cons worth millions of dollars while posing as an airline pilot, a doctor and a lawyer. The real Abagnale makes a cameo as a French police officer arresting his on-screen counterpart.

The film begins in 1969, when FBI agent Carl Hanratty arrives in Marseille to collect Frank, who has fallen ill in a squalid French prison. A flashback returns to 1963 in New Rochelle, New York, where the teenage Frank lives with his father, Frank Sr., and his French mother, Paula. He admires his father's charm and petty schemes, but tax problems force the family to move into a small apartment, and Frank discovers that his mother is having an affair with one of his father's friends. When his parents divorce, Frank runs away from home.

Needing money, Frank turns to confidence tricks that grow steadily more audacious. Posing as a Pan Am pilot, he forges payroll cheques worth millions of dollars and travels the world for free. Carl begins tracking him, but when he catches up with Frank at a motel, the young man convinces him that he is a Secret Service agent and slips away. Frank then poses as a doctor in Atlanta, falls in love with Brenda, a naïve young nurse played by Adams, and passes the bar exam in her father's state while preparing to marry her. As Carl closes in, Frank's elaborate life begins to unravel. The relationship between hunter and hunted gradually becomes something like friendship, with Frank calling Carl every Christmas Eve, and the lonely FBI agent becoming the closest thing Frank has to a father figure.

Set to a jazzy score by John Williams and stylised 1960s design, the film is both a caper and a portrait of a lonely young man trying to restore his broken family.

Catch Me If You Can was a critical and commercial success, earning more than 350 million dollars worldwide. Walken received an Academy Award nomination for Best Supporting Actor and Williams was nominated for Best Original Score.

documents.title: Requiem for a Dream
documents.tagline: A look into addiction and how it overcomes the mind and body.
documents.overview: The hopes and dreams of four ambitious people are shattered when their drug addictions begin spiraling out of control. A look into addiction and how it overcomes the mind and body.
documents.plot:
Requiem for a Dream is a 2000 American psychological drama directed by Darren Aronofsky, who wrote it with Hubert Selby Jr. from Selby's 1978 novel. Ellen Burstyn, Jared Leto, Jennifer Connelly, Marlon Wayans and Christopher McDonald star as people whose lives are destroyed by addiction. Noted for its rapid editing, split screens and Clint Mansell's score, it premiered at the 2000 Cannes Film Festival and opened in the United States on October 6, 2000.

Sara Goldfarb, a lonely widow in Brighton Beach, spends her days in front of the television. Her son Harry and his friend Tyrone are heroin users who start dealing to fund their dreams: Harry and his girlfriend Marion want to open a shop for her clothing designs, while Tyrone longs to escape the ghetto and win his mother's pride. When Sara is told she may appear on her favourite game show, she resolves to fit into the red dress she wore at Harry's graduation, and a doctor prescribes her amphetamines to curb her appetite. She loses weight and feels full of energy, and when Harry recognises the signs and pleads with her to stop, she says the dream of being on television is all she has left.

The young men's business collapses after Tyrone is caught up in a gang shooting and arrested, and Harry spends their savings on his bail. A drug war dries up the heroin supply, and the price of a big shipment from Florida is beyond them. Harry pushes Marion to sleep with her psychiatrist for money, straining their relationship. Sara, increasing her doses as the invitation never arrives, develops amphetamine psychosis and hallucinates being mocked by the show and attacked by her refrigerator.

The four lives disintegrate together. Sara wanders into the casting office in Manhattan and is committed to a psychiatric ward, where she is given electroconvulsive therapy and left in a catatonic state. Harry and Tyrone drive to Miami to buy drugs, but Harry's infected arm forces them into a hospital, where they are reported and arrested; Harry's gangrenous arm is amputated, and Tyrone endures withdrawal and abuse in a prison camp. Marion trades sex for drugs at a degrading party. Each curls up alone, and Sara dreams of winning the game show with a successful Harry at her side.

Burstyn's performance earned her an Academy Award nomination for Best Actress, and the film has a 79% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes.

documents.title: A.I. Artificial Intelligence
documents.tagline: David is 11 years old. He weighs 60 pounds. He is 4 feet, 6 inches tall. He has brown hair. His love is real. But he is not.
documents.overview: David, a robotic boy—the first of his kind programmed to love—is adopted as a test case by a Cybertronics employee and his wife. Though he gradually becomes their child, a series of unexpected circumstances make this life impossible for David. Without final acceptance by humans or machines, David embarks on a journey to discover where he truly belongs, uncovering a world in which the line between robot and machine is both vast and profoundly thin.
documents.plot: Steven Spielberg’s A.I. Artificial Intelligence, based on a concept by Stanley Kubrick, is a futuristic fairy tale that explores the emotional and existential consequences of artificial intelligence. Set in a distant future where climate change has drastically altered Earth and rising seas have submerged major cities, society relies heavily on humanoid robots known as Mechas.The story centers on David, a childlike robot played by Haley Joel Osment. David is a prototype created by the company Cybertronics. Unlike other robots, he is programmed to feel genuine, unconditional love. He is adopted by a couple, Monica and Henry Swinton, whose real son, Martin, is in cryogenic suspension due to illness. Monica activates David's emotional imprinting protocol, and he begins to love her as his true mother.When Martin unexpectedly recovers and returns home, tensions develop between him and David. After a series of incidents that put Martin in danger, the family views David as a threat. Monica, unable to return or deactivate David due to his emotional bond, abandons him in the woods rather than have him destroyed. This betrayal marks the beginning of David’s journey — a quest to become real, so Monica will love him again.David teams up with Gigolo Joe, a robot designed for adult companionship played by Jude Law. Together they navigate a world hostile to robots. They escape a violent event called the Flesh Fair, where obsolete robots are destroyed for entertainment, and search for the legendary Blue Fairy from the story of Pinocchio, whom David believes can turn him into a real boy.David eventually finds his creator, Professor Hobby, in the flooded ruins of Manhattan. However, he learns that he is not unique; many Davids have been made. Heartbroken but still determined, David continues his quest and ends up trapped underwater in front of a statue of the Blue Fairy. He remains there, silently praying to be made real, until his power runs out.Thousands of years later, advanced non-human AIs — evolved descendants of Mechas — resurrect David in a future where humanity is extinct. Using DNA from a lock of Monica’s hair, they recreate her for one final day. David spends that perfect day with her, finally experiencing the love he always longed for. At the end of the day, Monica dies, and David peacefully shuts down beside her.

documents.title: Dr. No
documents.tagline: Now meet the most extraordinary gentleman spy in all fiction!
documents.overview: In the film that launched the James Bond saga, Agent 007 battles mysterious Dr. No, a scientific genius bent on destroying the U.S. space program. As the countdown to disaster begins, Bond must go to Jamaica, where he encounters beautiful Honey Ryder, to confront a megalomaniacal villain in his massive island headquarters.
documents.plot:
Dr. No is a 1962 British spy film directed by Terence Young, produced by Kevin McClory and Harry Saltzman, and starring Sean Connery as James Bond. The movie was released by United Artists.

The film begins with the introduction of James Bond (Sean Connery), a secret agent working for MI6, Britain's intelligence agency. Bond is sent to Jamaica to investigate the disappearance of a fellow agent, Felix Leiter (Jack Palance). Upon arrival, Bond meets his new contact, Honey Ryder (Ursula Andress), a beautiful and resourceful beachcomber who becomes entangled in Bond's mission.

As Bond delves deeper into the mystery, he discovers that the villainous Dr. No (Joseph Wiseman) is behind the disappearance of Leiter and is threatening to disrupt the American space program by sabotaging their satellite launch from Jamaica. Dr. No is a ruthless and cunning scientist who has built a secret nuclear missile site on his island, where he plans to sell the technology to the highest bidder.

Bond's investigation leads him to confront Dr. No, who reveals that he has been using his island as a testing ground for his nuclear missiles. Bond also discovers that Dr. No is being backed by the Soviet Union and that his ultimate goal is to sell the missiles to the Soviets in exchange for a large sum of money.

As the story unfolds, Bond and Honey Ryder work together to stop Dr. No's plans. They face numerous challenges, including treacherous terrain, deadly traps, and Dr. No's henchmen. In one memorable scene, Bond and Honey Ryder escape from Dr. No's island by boat, while Dr. No is left stranded on the island.

The film culminates in a dramatic showdown between Bond and Dr. No at the nuclear missile site. Bond uses his wits and cunning to outsmart Dr. No and destroy the missiles, saving the American space program and foiling Dr. No's plans.

In the end, Bond and Honey Ryder escape from the island, and Bond returns to London as a hero. The film ends with Bond reflecting on his adventure and looking forward to his next mission.

Dr. No was a critical and commercial success, and it marked the beginning of Sean Connery's iconic portrayal of James Bond. The film's success can be attributed to its blend of action, suspense, and style, as well as the chemistry between Connery and Andress.

documents.title: Final Fantasy VII: Advent Children
documents.tagline: Is it for the children, for a memory, or for himself?
documents.overview: Two years have passed since the final battle with Sephiroth. Though Midgar, city of mako, city of prosperity, has been reduced to ruins, its people slowly but steadily walk the road to reconstruction. However, a mysterious illness called Geostigma torments them. With no cure in sight, it brings death to the afflicted, one after another, robbing the people of their fledgling hope.
documents.plot:
Final Fantasy VII: Advent Children is a 2005 Japanese animated science fantasy film directed by Tetsuya Nomura and produced by Square USA (now Square Enix). The movie takes place one year after the events of Final Fantasy VII.

The story begins with Cloud Strife, the main protagonist, who has been living in seclusion on the island of Cosmo Canyon. He is haunted by his past and struggles to come to terms with the loss of his friends and the weight of his responsibilities as a hero. Meanwhile, a new threat emerges in the form of Sephiroth, who has returned from the dead and seeks revenge against Cloud.

Sephiroth's return sets off a chain reaction of events that draws together a group of former members of AVALANCHE, including Barret Wallace, Tifa Lockhart, and Red XIII. They soon discover that Sephiroth is seeking to control the planet by using a powerful being known as Jenova, which has been awakened from its slumber.

As the story unfolds, Cloud is forced to confront his past and rejoin his friends in order to stop Sephiroth's plans. Along the way, he must also come to terms with his own identity and the true nature of his connection to Sephiroth.

Throughout the movie, the characters face numerous challenges and obstacles as they battle against Sephiroth's forces. The film features a mix of action, drama, and emotional depth, exploring themes such as friendship, sacrifice, and the consequences of playing god.

Ultimately, Cloud and his allies launch a final assault on Sephiroth, who has become increasingly powerful due to his connection to Jenova. In a climactic battle, Cloud faces off against Sephiroth in a struggle that will determine the fate of the planet.

The ending of the movie is bittersweet, with Cloud emerging victorious but at great personal cost. The film concludes on a hopeful note, suggesting that Cloud has finally found a sense of peace and closure, but also leaving room for speculation about his future and the possibilities that lie ahead.

Overall, Final Fantasy VII: Advent Children is a thought-provoking and emotionally resonant film that expands on the world and characters introduced in Final Fantasy VII. The movie's themes of friendship, sacrifice, and redemption are timeless and universal, making it a compelling watch for fans of the series and newcomers alike.

documents.title: Troy
documents.tagline: For passion. For honor. For destiny. For victory. For love.
documents.overview: In year 1250 B.C. during the late Bronze age, two emerging nations begin to clash. Paris, the Trojan prince, convinces Helen, Queen of Sparta, to leave her husband Menelaus, and sail with him back to Troy. After Menelaus finds out that his wife was taken by the Trojans, he asks his brother Agamemnom to help him get her back. Agamemnon sees this as an opportunity for power. So they set off with 1,000 ships holding 50,000 Greeks to Troy. With the help of Achilles, the Greeks are able to fight the never before defeated Trojans.
documents.plot:
Troy is a 2004 epic historical drama film directed by Wolfgang Petersen, produced by Jerry Bruckheimer, and based on Homer's ancient Greek epic poem, the Iliad. The movie stars Brad Pitt as Achilles, Eric Bana as Hector, and Orlando Bloom as Prince Odysseus.

The film begins with King Agamemnon (Brian Cox), the leader of the Greeks, who is determined to reclaim Helen (Diane Kruger), the wife of King Menelaus (Brendan Gleeson). The Greeks assemble a massive army, led by Achilles, the greatest warrior in Greece. However, their plans are threatened when Agamemnon takes Achilles' war prize, Briseis (Saffron Burrows), as his own concubine.

Achilles is outraged and refuses to fight alongside the Greeks, leading to a rift between him and his comrades. Meanwhile, Prince Odysseus, who has been tasked with infiltrating Troy by disguising himself as a Trojan prince, becomes embroiled in the conflict when he falls in love with Helen.

As the war rages on, Achilles' rage grows, and he seeks revenge against Agamemnon. He kills Agamemnon's brother, King Diomedes (Peter O'Toole), and then sets his sights on Agamemnon himself. However, just as Achilles is about to kill Agamemnon, the god Apollo intervenes, sparing the king's life.

The Trojans, led by Hector, launch a counterattack against the Greeks, and the two armies clash in a series of intense battles. Meanwhile, Odysseus and his men devise a plan to infiltrate Troy by hiding inside a giant wooden horse.

As the war reaches its climax, Achilles' rage is finally satiated when he kills Hector, but not before the Trojan prince's father, King Priam (Boris Kodjoe), comes to Achilles' camp to beg for his son's body. The scene is a poignant moment in the film, as it highlights the humanity of both sides and the devastating consequences of war.

In the end, the Greeks emerge victorious, but at great cost. Odysseus and his men enter Troy by hiding inside the wooden horse, which is then set on fire, allowing them to escape. Achilles' body is taken back to Greece, where he is mourned as a hero.

The film ends with Prince Paris (David Thewlis), who had sparked the war by abducting Helen, being killed by Philoctetes (Dominic West), a Greek warrior. The final shot of the film shows Odysseus standing alone on the beach, reflecting on the cost of war and the futility of human conflict.

Overall, Troy is a visually stunning film that brings to life the epic story of the Trojan War. While it takes some creative liberties with Homer's original tale, the film remains faithful to the spirit of the ancient Greek poem.
