documents.title: Gattaca
documents.tagline: There is no gene for the human spirit.
documents.overview: In a future society in the era of indefinite eugenics, humans are set on a life course depending on their DNA. Young Vincent Freeman is born with a condition that would prevent him from space travel, yet is determined to infiltrate the GATTACA space program.
documents.plot:
Gattaca is a thought-provoking science fiction film directed by Andrew Niccol, released in 1997 by Columbia Pictures. The movie takes place in a future where genetic engineering has become a dominant force in society.

The story begins with Vincent Freeman (played by Ethan Hawke), an "invalid" who was born naturally without any genetic enhancements. In this world, people can choose to enhance their genes to achieve perfection, and those who do are considered superior. The main character's father, Maurice (played by James Cromwell), is a former test pilot who died in a tragic accident.

Vincent dreams of becoming an astronaut, but his "invalid" status makes it impossible for him to join the prestigious Gattaca Corporation's space program. He decides to impersonate a genetically perfect individual named Eugene Morrow (played by Jude Law) and applies for a job at Gattaca. Vincent uses advanced technology to create a fake identity and genetic profile, which he hopes will fool the corporation's sophisticated DNA testing system.

As Vincent navigates his new life as Eugene, he meets Irene Cassini (played by Uma Thurman), a beautiful and intelligent woman who is also an employee of Gattaca. The two begin a romantic relationship, but their love is threatened when Vincent's true identity is discovered by the corporation's security team.

Meanwhile, the story unfolds through a series of flashbacks, which reveal the tragic events that led to Maurice's death. It is revealed that he was involved in a conspiracy to sabotage the space program and prevent genetically enhanced individuals from taking over. The truth behind his death is slowly uncovered throughout the film, adding depth to Vincent's character.

As the story progresses, Vincent becomes embroiled in a complex web of intrigue and deception. He must confront the consequences of his actions and decide whether to continue living as Eugene or reveal his true identity. In the end, Vincent chooses to come clean about his past, but not before he has a profound impact on Irene's life.

The film explores themes of identity, free will, and what it means to be human in a world where genetic engineering has become the norm. The title "Gattaca" refers to the corporation's motto, which reads: "Genetic testing is mandatory." Throughout the movie, Vincent struggles with the idea that his existence is defined by his genetic code, rather than his own choices and actions.

Ultimately, Gattaca is a thought-provoking commentary on the consequences of playing God with human genetics. The film raises important questions about the ethics of genetic engineering and the importance of individual freedom in a world where technology seems to be controlling every aspect of our lives.

documents.title: Almost Famous
documents.tagline: Experience it. Enjoy it. Just don't fall for it.
documents.overview: In 1973, 15-year-old William Miller's unabashed love of music and aspiration to become a rock journalist lands him an assignment from Rolling Stone magazine to interview and tour with the up-and-coming band, Stillwater.
documents.plot: In 1973, a precocious 15-year-old aspiring rock journalist lands a dream assignment from Rolling Stone to tour with a rising rock band, embarking on a coming-of-age journey as he discovers the exhilarating and heartbreaking realities behind rock stardom.

documents.title: Mr. & Mrs. Smith
documents.tagline: Smart and sexy
documents.overview: After five (or six) years of vanilla-wedded bliss, ordinary suburbanites John and Jane Smith are stuck in a huge rut. Unbeknownst to each other, they are both coolly lethal, highly-paid assassins working for rival organisations. When they discover they're each other's next target, their secret lives collide in a spicy, explosive mix of wicked comedy, pent-up passion, nonstop action and high-tech weaponry.
documents.plot:
Mr. & Mrs. Smith is a 2005 American action comedy directed by Doug Liman from a screenplay by Simon Kinberg. Brad Pitt and Angelina Jolie star as a bored suburban married couple who discover that each is secretly an assassin working for a rival agency, with Vince Vaughn, Adam Brody and Kerry Washington in supporting roles. The production became widely known for marking the start of Pitt and Jolie's real-life relationship.

The story opens with John Smith, ostensibly a construction executive, and his wife Jane, who claims to be an IT recruiter, attending marriage counseling. Five or six years into their marriage, their relationship is suffering from poor communication and small acts of passive aggression. In flashback, the couple recall meeting in Bogotá, Colombia, where they pretended to be together to avoid questioning by the authorities, followed by a whirlwind courtship and a quick wedding. Unknown to one another, both are elite contract killers employed by competing firms, and each has become expert at hiding the truth. They live in a large house in the New York suburbs, keeping up appearances among their wealthy neighbors while quietly balancing a dull home life against their dangerous careers.

Everything changes when both are assigned to eliminate the same target, a prisoner named Benjamin "The Tank" Danz, during a transfer. Their paths collide on the job, the hit is botched, and each soon realizes who the other really is. Ordered by their employers to clean up the mistake, John and Jane turn their considerable skills against each other, and the marriage erupts into a series of escalating ambushes, car chases and shootouts, culminating in a destructive fight inside their own home. Forced to confront the lies at the heart of their relationship, they ultimately find themselves allied against the agencies that now want both of them dead.

The film was a major commercial hit, ranking among the highest-grossing releases of 2005. Critics were divided on its plotting but frequently praised the chemistry and playful banter between its two stars, along with its stylish action sequences. Its blend of romantic comedy and spy thriller later inspired a 2024 television series of the same name.

documents.title: The Fog
documents.tagline: Their PAST Has Come Back To HAUNT THEM
documents.overview: Trapped within an eerie mist, the residents of Antonio Bay have become the unwitting victims of a horrifying vengeance. One hundred years earlier, a ship carrying lepers was purposely lured onto the rocky coastline and sank, drowning all aboard. Now they're back – long-dead mariners who've waited a century for their revenge.

documents.title: Persona
documents.tagline: Ingmar Bergman's most personal and original film.
documents.overview: A young nurse, Alma, is put in charge of Elisabeth Vogler: an actress who is seemingly healthy in all respects, but will not talk. As they spend time together, Alma speaks to Elisabeth constantly, never receiving any answer. The time they spend together only strengthens the crushing realization that one does not exist.
documents.plot:
Persona is a 1966 Swedish psychological drama written, directed and produced by Ingmar Bergman. Bibi Andersson stars as the young nurse Alma and Liv Ullmann as Elisabet Vogler, a celebrated actress who has suddenly stopped speaking, with Margaretha Krook, Gunnar Björnstrand and Jörgen Lindström. A landmark of modernist cinema, its exploration of identity, duality and the act of filmmaking itself has been the subject of extensive critical debate, and it is often ranked among the greatest films ever made.

The film opens with a rapid montage as a projector starts up, including images of a crucifixion, a spider and the slaughter of a lamb, before a boy wakes in what looks like a hospital or morgue and reaches towards a blurred image of two women's faces. Elisabet Vogler fell silent in the middle of a performance of Electra, and doctors conclude that her muteness is an act of will rather than illness. Alma is assigned to care for her. In the hospital Elisabet is horrified by television footage of a monk burning himself in protest during the Vietnam War, and she tears up a photograph of her son sent by her husband.

The doctor sends the two women to her seaside cottage to recover. There Alma, flattered by Elisabet's attentive silence, talks freely about herself, her fiancé Karl-Henrik and, in a long confession, an erotic encounter on a beach with another woman and two boys, which left her pregnant and led to an abortion she still regrets.

When Alma reads a letter Elisabet has written, she discovers that the actress has been studying her and repeating her secrets. Hurt and angry, Alma turns on her, almost scalding her with boiling water, which makes Elisabet cry out. The film itself appears to tear and burn before resuming. The women's identities increasingly blur: Elisabet's husband arrives and, addressing Alma as his wife, sleeps with her. Alma recounts Elisabet's own story, of how she longed to be a mother, tried to end her pregnancy and came to despise the son who craves her love, and as she speaks their faces merge into a single image.

Alma insists that she is not Elisabet, coaxes her to say the word "nothing", and leaves the cottage, as a film crew is glimpsed and the projector winds down. Persona received favourable reviews on release and is now regarded as one of Bergman's masterpieces.

documents.title: Rosemary's Baby
documents.tagline: It's not what you're expecting
documents.overview: A young couple, Rosemary and Guy, moves into an infamous New York apartment building, known by frightening legends and mysterious events, with the purpose of starting a family.

documents.title: The Omen
documents.tagline: A new generation of terror
documents.overview: A diplomatic couple adopts the son of the devil without knowing it. A remake of the classic horror film of the same name from 1976.
documents.plot:
Robert Thorn, an American diplomat stationed in Italy, is told that his son was stillborn. Unknown to his unconscious wife, Katherine, Robert adopts an orphaned newborn at the suggestion of the hospital's chaplain Catholic priest, Father Spiletto. Naming him Damien, Robert and Katherine raise the boy. Robert's career ascends over the next 5 years. He is named Deputy Ambassador to the Court of St. James's in the United Kingdom. Following the death of the previous ambassador in a suspicious vehicle fire caused by a vagrant, Robert assumes his position and settles in a large estate just outside London. However, disturbing events begin to occur.
At Damien's birthday party, his nanny is seemingly hypnotised by a mysterious black dog loitering in the estate gerdens. She makes sure she has the attention of the children and families in attendance, then dramatically hangs herself.
Robert is approached by Father Brennan, who claims to have been involved with events surrounding Damien's birth. Meanwhile, photographer Keith Jennings finds that several of his photographs contain mysterious omens, including premonitions of people's deaths. A new nanny, Mrs. Baylock, is hired. Tension rises when Mrs. Baylock starts to make decisions without the consent of the Thorns, including adopting a Rottweiler for Damien's protection.
Following an incident near a chapel in which Damien attacks Katherine, she begins experiencing vivid dreams about her son, one of these involving a red-hooded jackal skeleton. When the Thorns visit a zoo, the animals react violently at the sight of Damien. Katherine begins to wonder if there is something wrong with Damien. Father Brennan confronts Robert, telling him that Damien's mother was a jackal and that the boy is the Antichrist. He explains that Damien must die, and a man named Bugenhagen, located in Megiddo, can help. After being rebuked, Father Brennan is killed during a lightning storm.
Katherine discovers she is pregnant and is determined to get an abortion, in fear of having a child similar to Damien. Soon afterward, Damien causes an accident in which Katherine is severely injured, resulting in her miscarriage. While in the hospital, Katherine confides in Robert that she has suspicions that Damien is evil. Jennings meets with Robert and shows him the photographs, including a new omen of his death. Robert decides to rendezvous with Jennings and search for Damien's biological mother. The pair discovers the hospital where Damien was delivered has since been demolished after a fire. They travel to Subiaco and meet a deformed Father Spiletto, who directs them to a graveyard. There, they find the grave of Damien's mother, who is revealed to have indeed been a jackal. In the neighboring tomb, Robert discovers the corpse of his murdered biological son. He and Jennings are attacked by a pack of dogs and barely escape.
Mrs. Baylock visits Katherine in the hospital and causes her to have an air embolism, which kills her.

documents.title: Shrek
documents.tagline: The greatest fairy tale never told.
documents.overview: It ain't easy bein' green -- especially if you're a likable (albeit smelly) ogre named Shrek. On a mission to retrieve a gorgeous princess from the clutches of a fire-breathing dragon, Shrek teams up with an unlikely compatriot -- a wisecracking donkey.
documents.plot:
Shrek is an asocial ogre who loves the solitude of his swamp and enjoys fending off mobs and intruders. One day, his life is interrupted after he inadvertently saves a talkative Donkey from some soldiers, prompting Donkey to forcibly stay with him. Donkey is one of many fairy tale creatures that are being exiled by the dwarfish Lord Farquaad of Duloc to beautify his land. However, the creatures inadvertently end up in the swamp. Angered by the intrusion, Shrek resolves to visit Farquaad and demand that he move the creatures elsewhere, reluctantly allowing Donkey to accompany him as he is the only one who knows where Duloc is.
Meanwhile, Farquaad asks a magic mirror if he has the most perfect kingdom; the mirror tells him he is not a king and would need to marry a princess in order to become one. Presented with three options, Farquaad chooses Princess Fiona, who is imprisoned in a castle guarded by a Dragon. Unwilling to rescue Fiona himself, he organizes a tournament, the winner receiving the "privilege" of rescuing her on his behalf. When Farquaad sees Shrek and Donkey in his castle, he announces that whoever kills Shrek will win the tournament; however, Shrek and Donkey defeat Farquaad's knights with relative ease. Amused, Farquaad proclaims Shrek his champion, and agrees to relocate the fairy tale creatures in exchange for Shrek rescuing Fiona.
Shrek and Donkey travel to the castle and Dragon attacks them. Shrek locates Fiona, who is bewildered by his lack of romanticism; they flee the castle after rescuing Donkey from Dragon, who is revealed to be female and has fallen in love with him. When Shrek removes his helmet and reveals he is an ogre, Fiona stubbornly refuses to go to Duloc, demanding Farquaad arrive in person to save her, but Shrek carries Fiona against her will. That night, after setting up camp, and with Fiona alone in a cave, Shrek admits to Donkey that he is asocial because he grew frustrated over being constantly judged for his appearance. Fiona overhears this and becomes kinder to Shrek. The next day, Robin Hood and his band of Merry Men harass the three, but Fiona easily defeats them in physical combat. Shrek becomes impressed with Fiona, and they begin to fall in love.
When the trio nears Duloc, Fiona takes shelter in a windmill for the evening. Donkey enters alone and discovers that Fiona has transformed into an ogress. She explains that during her childhood, she was cursed to transform into an ogress at night but retain her human form during the day. She tells Donkey that only "true love's first kiss" will break the spell and allow her to "take love's true form". Meanwhile, Shrek is about to confess his feelings to Fiona, when he overhears Fiona referring to herself as an "ugly beast". Thinking that she is talking about him, Shrek angrily leaves and returns the next morning with Farquaad.

documents.title: Shrek 2
documents.tagline: Once upon another time...
documents.overview: Shrek, Fiona and Donkey set off to Far, Far Away to meet Fiona's mother and father. But not everyone is happy. Shrek and the King find it hard to get along, and there's tension in the marriage. The fairy godmother discovers that Shrek has married Fiona instead of her Son Prince Charming and sets about destroying their marriage.
documents.plot:
Newlyweds Shrek and Princess Fiona return from their honeymoon to find they have been invited by Fiona's parents to a royal ball to celebrate their marriage. Though Shrek is mortified about visiting the kingdom as an ogre, and resents Fiona's parents for locking her in the tower, Fiona convinces him to attend, and they travel to the kingdom of Far Far Away with Donkey in tow and the fairy tale creatures house sitting. They meet Fiona's parents, King Harold and Queen Lillian, who are repulsed to see they are ogres. At dinner, Shrek and Harold get into a heated argument, and afterwards, Fiona encounters Fairy Godmother, a celebrity potions saleswoman who offers to help Fiona but is mortified to see she is married to Shrek. Shrek worries he is losing Fiona, especially after finding her childhood diary and reading that she was once seemingly infatuated with Prince Charming.
Harold is secretly reprimanded by Fairy Godmother, who had arranged with Harold for her son—Charming—to be the one to rescue and marry Fiona; she hopes to use the marriage to rule Far Far Away through Charming. She orders Harold to get rid of Shrek or else lose his own happy ending, so Harold hires swashbuckling outlaw and mercenary Puss in Boots to assassinate Shrek.
Unable to overpower Shrek, Puss reveals that he was paid by Harold and offers to help him in gratitude for having his own life spared. Shrek, Donkey, and Puss meet with Fairy Godmother at her potions factory to find something to help Shrek appeal to Fiona, but she coldly rejects his request, insisting ogres do not deserve happy endings. They retaliate by stealing a potion labeled "Happily Ever After" and accidentally trashing the factory. Shrek and Donkey drink the potion and soon fall asleep. Back in Far Far Away, Fiona notices Shrek is missing and tries to find him, but she too falls asleep.
The next morning, Shrek and Fiona awaken to find they are now human, and Donkey is a white stallion. To make the change permanent, Shrek must kiss Fiona by midnight. Shrek, Donkey, and Puss return to the castle; however, Fairy Godmother, having discovered the theft, has sent Charming to pose as human Shrek and win Fiona's love. At Fairy Godmother's urging, Shrek leaves the castle, believing that the best way to make Fiona happy is to let her go.
Fiona is skeptical of Charming; therefore, to ensure the two will wed, Fairy Godmother gives Harold a love potion to put into Fiona's tea. This exchange is overheard by Shrek, Donkey, and Puss, who are arrested by the royal knights after Donkey inadvertently exposes them. While the ball begins, the fairy tale creatures - having seen the arrest on the news - rescue the trio from the dungeon. They all storm the castle with the help of Mongo, a monstrous living gingerbread man created by the Muffin Man.
Though Mongo is destroyed, the group manages to break into the ball. Shrek fails to prevent Charming from kissing Fiona, but instead of falling in love, Fiona knocks him out.

documents.title: Shrek the Third
documents.tagline: He’s in for the Royal Treatment.
documents.overview: The King of Far Far Away has died and Shrek and Fiona are to become King & Queen. However, Shrek wants to return to his cozy swamp and live in peace and quiet, so when he finds out there is another heir to the throne, they set off to bring him back to rule the kingdom.
documents.plot:
Shrek the Third is a 2007 American computer-animated fantasy comedy produced by DreamWorks Animation and loosely based on William Steig's 1990 picture book Shrek!. Directed by Chris Miller, co-directed by Raman Hui and written by Jeffrey Price, Peter S. Seaman, Miller and Aron Warner, it is the third installment in the Shrek series. Mike Myers, Eddie Murphy, Cameron Diaz, Antonio Banderas, Rupert Everett, Julie Andrews and John Cleese return to their voice roles, joined by Justin Timberlake as Arthur Pendragon and Eric Idle as Merlin.

Shrek and Princess Fiona are next in line to succeed Fiona's father, King Harold, but Shrek's attempts to stand in for the ailing king end in disaster, since he has no interest in ruling Far Far Away. On his deathbed Harold reveals that there is another heir: Fiona's cousin Arthur, known as Artie. Meanwhile, Prince Charming, seeking revenge for the death of his mother, the Fairy Godmother, rallies fairy-tale villains at the Poison Apple tavern, persuading them to fight for their own "happily ever after" and help him seize the kingdom.

Shrek sets sail with Donkey and Puss in Boots to find Artie. As they depart, Fiona tells Shrek that she is pregnant, and he is terrified at the prospect of fatherhood. At Worcestershire Academy, a medieval boarding school, they find Artie to be a scrawny teenage outcast. He is thrilled to learn he will be king until Donkey and Puss scare him with talk of the job's responsibilities, and he tries to turn the ship around, causing it to crash on an island where they meet Artie's eccentric former teacher, the wizard Merlin. Back in Far Far Away, Charming's villains storm the castle during Fiona's baby shower, and Fiona, Queen Lillian and the fairy-tale princesses, including Snow White, Cinderella, Sleeping Beauty and Rapunzel, must fight back. Shrek and Artie return to confront Charming, who plans to stage a theatrical show ending with Shrek's death.

Shrek the Third received mixed reviews, with critics finding it less inventive and funny than its predecessors, though its animation and voice cast were praised. It was a major commercial success, grossing over $800 million worldwide, and was followed by Shrek Forever After in 2010.

documents.title: Aladdin
documents.tagline: Wish granted!
documents.overview: Princess Jasmine grows tired of being forced to remain in the palace, so she sneaks out into the marketplace, in disguise, where she meets street-urchin Aladdin.  The couple falls in love, although Jasmine may only marry a prince.  After being thrown in jail, Aladdin becomes embroiled in a plot to find a mysterious lamp, with which the evil Jafar hopes to rule the land.
documents.plot:
Aladdin is a timeless Disney classic released in 1992, directed by Ron Clements and John Musker. The film is set in the fictional city of Agrabah, inspired by Middle Eastern architecture and culture.

The story begins with Aladdin (voiced by Scott Weinger), a poor but kind-hearted street urchin who lives in the marketplace of Agrabah. Aladdin's life takes a dramatic turn when he stumbles upon a mysterious cave containing a magical lamp. When he rubs the lamp, a wisecracking genie (voiced by Robin Williams) appears, granting Aladdin three wishes.

However, their encounter is soon discovered by Jafar (voiced by Jonathan Freeman), the power-hungry advisor to the Sultan of Agrabah. Jafar seeks to use the genie's powers to overthrow the Sultan and rule Agrabah himself. The Sultan, unaware of his advisor's true intentions, tasks Aladdin with retrieving a magic lamp from the Cave of Wonders.

As Aladdin navigates the challenges of the cave, he meets Princess Jasmine (voiced by Linda Larkin), who is also searching for the lamp. They form an instant connection, and Aladdin must balance his growing feelings for the princess with his newfound wealth and status.

Meanwhile, Jafar's true intentions are revealed, and he attempts to steal the magic lamp from Aladdin. The genie intervenes, and a thrilling chase ensues as Aladdin and Jasmine try to outwit Jafar. Along the way, Aladdin learns about the importance of honesty, bravery, and selflessness.

As the story unfolds, Aladdin's wishes become increasingly complicated, leading to comedic misunderstandings and unexpected consequences. In the end, Aladdin must confront his own identity and decide whether to use his newfound wealth and power for personal gain or to protect the people he cares about.

The film culminates in a dramatic showdown between Aladdin, Jasmine, and Jafar. With the help of the genie, Aladdin defeats Jafar and saves Agrabah from destruction. The Sultan, realizing his advisor's treachery, banishes Jafar from the kingdom. Aladdin and Jasmine confess their love for each other, and the film ends with a grand celebration in the palace.

Throughout its runtime, Aladdin features memorable characters, catchy music, and stunning animation. The film's themes of self-discovery, friendship, and the importance of staying true to oneself have made it a beloved classic among audiences worldwide.

documents.title: Austin Powers in Goldmember
documents.tagline: He's still evil... He's still deadly... and he's still surrounded by frickin' idiots!
documents.overview: The world's most shagadelic spy continues his fight against Dr. Evil. This time, the diabolical doctor and his clone, Mini-Me, team up with a new foe—'70s kingpin Goldmember. While pursuing the team of villains to stop them from world domination, Austin gets help from his dad and an old girlfriend.
documents.plot:
Austin Powers in Goldmember is a 2002 spy comedy film directed by Jay Roach and written by Mike Myers, Seth MacFarlane, and Jay Roach. The movie is the third installment in the Austin Powers film series.

The story begins with Austin Powers (Mike Myers), international man of mystery, who has retired from his spy days to live a peaceful life with his wife, Vanessa Kensington (Mary Jo Catlett). However, their happiness is short-lived as they are kidnapped by the villainous Dr. Evil (Mike Myers) and his accomplice, Number Two (Robert Wagner).

Dr. Evil reveals that he plans to steal the world's gold reserves and hold the world hostage for $1 billion. Austin Powers must escape from captivity and stop Dr. Evil's plan.

Along the way, Austin teams up with his old nemesis, Felix Leiter (John Cleese), who has retired from the CIA and is now working as a bartender. Together, they embark on a mission to stop Dr. Evil and save the world.

As Austin delves deeper into the plot, he discovers that Dr. Evil's plan involves using a device called the "Shark Tank," which can extract gold from any material. The team must navigate through various obstacles, including Dr. Evil's henchmen, the Fembots, and the villainous Goldmember (Will Ferrell), who is revealed to be Dr. Evil's long-lost brother.

Throughout the movie, Austin's character undergoes significant development as he confronts his own identity crisis and learns to accept himself for who he is. He also rekindles his romance with Vanessa and must balance his spy life with his personal life.

The film features a range of memorable characters, including Mini-Me (Verne Troyer), Dr. Evil's miniature clone, and the enigmatic Goldmember, who provides comedic relief throughout the movie.

In the climactic final act, Austin and his team face off against Dr. Evil in an epic battle at the 1969 Woodstock music festival. The movie culminates with a showdown between Austin and Dr. Evil, resulting in the defeat of the villain and the saving of the world.

Overall, Austin Powers in Goldmember is a hilarious and action-packed comedy that pays homage to the spy genre while also exploring themes of identity and acceptance. With its witty dialogue, memorable characters, and over-the-top humor, the movie has become a cult classic and cemented Mike Myers' status as a comedic genius.

documents.title: Jin-Roh: The Wolf Brigade
documents.tagline: A story of a man burdened with the destiny of a beast and a woman who dreamed of love.
documents.overview: A member of an elite paramilitary counter-terrorism unit becomes traumatized after witnessing the suicide bombing of a young girl and is forced to undergo retraining. However, unbeknownst to him, he becomes a key player in a dispute between rival police divisions, as he finds himself increasingly involved with the sister of the girl he saw die.
documents.plot:
In an alternate 1950s Tokyo, the Self-Police respond to a riot in Akasaka that escalates into violence. In the storm sewers below, members of the Sect deliver Molotov cocktails and satchel charges to the rioters, aided by Nanami Agawa, a young Sect "Little Red Riding Hood" courier. When several riot police officers are incapacitated by a Sect-provided satchel charge, the Self-Police move in on the rioters, while the Capital Police deploys Kerberos, who easily wipe out the cell and destroy their explosives. Kerberos member Kazuki Fuse confronts Nanami as she flees, but freezes up when ordered to execute her instead of apprehend her. Rather than surrender, Nanami detonates her satchel charge, killing herself and causing a power outage that leads to the Self-Police losing control of the situation above. The incident damages Kerberos's reputation and deeply affects Fuse, who is reprimanded for his inaction and ordered to redo training under drill instructor Hachiroh Tohbe.
A remorseful Fuse, acting on information from his friend, Public Security head Atsushi Henmi, visits Nanami's grave and meets Kei Amemiya, a girl who claims to be Nanami's older sister and does not hold him responsible for her demise; they quickly develop a bond. However, Kei is revealed to not be Nanami's sister, but a former Little Red Riding Hood courier coerced into acting on behalf of Public Security, who seek to dissolve Kerberos and merge with the Self-Police to shift their counterterrorism strategies from brute force to intelligence. Public Security attempts to use Kei to entrap Fuse at a museum with the goal of discrediting Kerberos, but he sneaks in, incapacitates the Public Security agents, and escapes with Kei, evading the Self-Police. Kei reveals her role in the deception and suggests they run away together, but Fuse insists on staying, and they fall in love.
Fuse and Kei seek refuge in the same sewers from the riot shootout and are met by members of "Jin-Roh" ("Wolf Brigade" in English), a secret deep-cover counterintelligence group led by Tohbe and Hajime Handa that protects Kerberos from organizational threats like Public Security. They provide Fuse with an MG 42 and a full set of Protect Gear, and reveal they knew of Kei's role and consider her living proof of Public Security's conspiracy, before leaving with Kei. Public Security teams led by Henmi arrive, having followed a tracking device hidden in Kei's bag, but are met by a fully armored Fuse, who slaughters the agents in a shootout and finishes off a mortally wounded Henmi in a duel.
Fuse reunites with Kei and Jin-Roh in a junkyard, but is distraught when he is ordered to kill Kei to ensure she is never recaptured by Public Security. Kei embraces Fuse and tearfully repeats the words of Little Red Riding Hood, describing the grotesque appearance of a wolf disguised as a loved one. Horrified at what he has to do, Fuse has a crisis, before he shoots and kills Kei.

documents.title: Moulin Rouge!
documents.tagline: No Laws. No Limits. One Rule. Never Fall In Love.
documents.overview: A celebration of love and creative inspiration takes place in the infamous, gaudy and glamorous Parisian nightclub, at the cusp of the 20th century. A young poet, who is plunged into the heady world of Moulin Rouge, begins a passionate affair with the club's most notorious and beautiful star.
documents.plot:
Moulin Rouge! is a 2001 musical romantic drama film directed by Baz Luhrmann, starring Nicole Kidman and Ewan McGregor. The film is set in Paris in the late 19th century and is loosely based on the life of Christian Beraducci, an Italian writer who lived in Paris during that time.

The story begins with a young Christian (played by Jim Broadbent) who has just arrived in Paris to write about the city's vibrant nightlife. He meets a young woman named Satine (played by Nicole Kidman), who is a courtesan at the Moulin Rouge, a famous cabaret in Paris. Satine is also being pursued by the Duke de Monroth (played by Richard Roxburgh), a wealthy and powerful nobleman.

As Christian becomes more involved with Satine, he begins to write about her life and the world of the Moulin Rouge. He falls deeply in love with Satine, but their social differences make it impossible for them to be together. Meanwhile, the Duke is determined to win Satine's heart and will stop at nothing to achieve his goal.

The plot develops as Christian becomes more and more obsessed with Satine, and he begins to write a musical about her life. The musical, which features many of the famous songs from the Moulin Rouge, including "Lady Marmalade" and "Your Song," becomes a huge success, but it also brings attention to Satine's situation and puts pressure on her to choose between Christian and the Duke.

As the story unfolds, Christian's obsession with Satine grows, and he begins to see her as his muse. He writes more and more about her, and his musical becomes a sensation. However, the Duke's plans become more and more sinister, and Satine is forced to make a choice between her love for Christian and her duty to the Duke.

In the end, Satine chooses the Duke, but at a great cost. Christian's obsession with her has consumed him, and he dies of a broken heart after realizing that she will never truly be his. The film ends with Satine singing "Your Song" alone on stage, surrounded by the empty seats of the Moulin Rouge.

Throughout the film, Baz Luhrmann uses many creative and innovative techniques to bring the story to life. He incorporates many famous songs from the 20th century into the musical, and he uses a mix of traditional and modern dance styles to create a unique and captivating visual style. The film's costumes, sets, and cinematography are also highly praised for their creativity and attention to detail.

Overall, Moulin Rouge! is a beautiful and tragic love story that explores the themes of obsession, duty, and the power of art to transcend time and circumstance.

documents.title: Forbidden Planet
documents.tagline: Earthmen on a fabulous, peril-journey into outer space!
documents.overview: Starship C57D travels to planet Altair 4 in search of the crew of spaceship "Bellerophon," a scientific expedition that has been missing for 20 years, only to find themselves unwelcome by the expedition's lone survivor and warned of destruction by an invisible force if they don't turn back immediately.
documents.plot:
Forbidden Planet is a science fiction film directed by Fred M. Wilcox, produced by Charles H. Schneer, and released by Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer (MGM) in 1956.

The story begins with the crew of the spaceship C57D, led by Captain John J. Adams, receiving a distress signal from the planet Altair IV. The crew is sent to investigate and rescue any survivors. Upon arrival, they discover that the planet's surface is uninhabitable due to a toxic atmosphere. However, they soon realize that the real challenge lies within the planet's interior.

As the crew explores the planet, they come across an ancient temple dedicated to the goddess Caliban, who was once worshipped by the native inhabitants of Altair IV. The crew discovers a strange energy field surrounding the temple and decides to investigate further. They soon learn that the energy field is connected to the planet's unique properties and is believed to be the source of its deadly radiation.

The crew encounters various obstacles, including treacherous terrain, toxic gas, and malfunctioning equipment. As they delve deeper into the planet's interior, they begin to experience strange visions and hallucinations, which are later revealed to be caused by the energy field's effects on their minds.

One of the crew members, Dr. Edward Morbius, begins to exhibit unusual behavior, suggesting that he may have been affected by the energy field in a more profound way than initially thought. As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Morbius has become possessed by the spirit of Caliban, who is seeking revenge against humanity for its treatment of her people.

The crew soon realizes that they must find a way to stop Morbius and escape the planet before it's too late. They discover that the only way to neutralize the energy field is to destroy the temple and sever the connection between the planet and Caliban's spirit.

In the climactic final act, the crew faces off against Morbius, who has become a vessel for Caliban's wrath. The captain and his crew must use all their skills and ingenuity to defeat Morbius and shatter the energy field, allowing them to escape the planet.

The film ends with the crew returning to Earth, where they are hailed as heroes for their bravery and ingenuity in overcoming the challenges of Altair IV. However, the ending also leaves room for interpretation, as some viewers may wonder if the crew truly escaped the planet's influence or if Morbius's spirit still lingers, waiting to be unleashed once again.

Overall, Forbidden Planet is a thought-provoking science fiction film that explores themes of identity, humanity, and the dangers of playing with forces beyond human control. The film's blend of adventure, suspense, and philosophical introspection has made it a classic of the genre, continuing to captivate audiences to this day.

documents.title: Underworld: Evolution
documents.tagline: My God. Brother, what have you done?
documents.overview: As the war between the vampires and the Lycans rages on, Selene, a former member of the Death Dealers (an elite vampire special forces unit that hunts werewolves), and Michael, the werewolf hybrid, work together in an effort to unlock the secrets of their respective bloodlines.
documents.plot:
Underworld: Evolution is a 2006 supernatural action film directed by Patrick Tatopoulos and written by Len Wiseman and Danny McBride. The movie serves as a sequel to the 2003 film Underworld, starring Kate Beckinsale as Selene, a vampire warrior.

The story begins with Selene (Kate Beckinsale) being resurrected from her death in the first film by a group of vampires who believe she is destined to fulfill an ancient prophecy. The prophecy states that Selene will be the one to bring about the end of the war between humans and vampires, as well as the destruction of both species.

As Selene awakens, she finds herself in a desolate wasteland, surrounded by a group of vampires who claim to have been sent by her maker, Kraven (Shane Brolly). They inform her that she has been chosen to fulfill the prophecy and that she must find the Lycan leader, Lucian (Scott Speedman), who is also destined for greatness.

Selene soon discovers that she is not alone in her quest. A group of humans, led by Alexander Corvinus (Tom Cruise), are also searching for Lucian, believing him to be the key to their survival. As Selene navigates this treacherous landscape, she must confront her own destiny and the true nature of her existence as a vampire.

Throughout the film, Selene encounters various characters who aid or hinder her progress. These include Michael Corvin (Scott Speedman), Alexander's son, who becomes embroiled in the conflict; Kraven, who seeks to use Selene for his own purposes; and the Lycan leader, Lucian, who is torn between his loyalty to his pack and his growing feelings for Selene.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that the prophecy is more complex than initially thought. The true nature of the war between humans and vampires is revealed, as well as the motivations behind Alexander's actions. Ultimately, Selene must make a choice between her own existence and the fate of humanity, leading to a climactic showdown with Kraven and Lucian.

The film concludes with Selene emerging victorious but not without scars. She has come to terms with her destiny and is ready to face whatever challenges lie ahead. The ending sets the stage for potential future sequels, leaving audiences wondering what the future holds for this iconic vampire warrior.

Overall, Underworld: Evolution offers a thrilling and action-packed ride, exploring themes of identity, loyalty, and the blurred lines between good and evil.

documents.title: Duel
documents.tagline: The most bizarre murder weapon ever used!
documents.overview: Traveling businessman David Mann angers the driver of a rusty tanker while crossing the California desert. A simple trip turns deadly, as Mann struggles to stay on the road while the tanker plays cat and mouse with his life.
documents.plot:
Duel is a 1971 television film directed by Steven Spielberg, produced by Universal Television, and written by Richard Matheson.

The story begins with David Mann (played by Dennis Weaver), a middle-aged family man who is driving home from a business trip on the New Mexico State Highway. As he drives, he notices a black Peterbilt semi-truck following him at a distance. The truck's driver, known only as "The Driver" (played by Martin Mull), seems to be mirroring David's every move.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that The Driver is not just following David; he is also taunting and intimidating him. The Driver begins to make menacing gestures, such as flashing his headlights or making sudden stops, which causes David to become increasingly anxious and frustrated.

David tries to lose The Driver by taking various detours and changing lanes, but the truck always seems to be one step ahead of him. As the chase continues, David becomes more and more agitated, and his family back home begins to worry about his safety.

As the tension builds, it becomes clear that The Driver is not just a random driver; he has a personal vendetta against David. The Driver's actions become increasingly sinister, and David realizes that he must find a way to escape before it's too late.

In a thrilling climax, David uses his wits and resourcefulness to outsmart The Driver. He sets up a trap for the truck by driving into a narrow canyon, where The Driver is forced to slow down or risk crashing. As The Driver tries to pass David, he loses control of the truck and crashes into a rock face.

The film ends with David finally safe at home, but shaken by his terrifying experience on the road. The Driver's true identity remains a mystery, leaving the audience to wonder about the motivations behind his sinister actions.

Throughout the film, Spielberg uses suspenseful camera angles and editing techniques to create a sense of tension and unease. The film's score, composed by Lalo Schifrin, adds to the overall sense of anxiety and fear.

Overall, Duel is a masterclass in suspenseful storytelling, with a simple yet effective plot that keeps viewers on the edge of their seats until the very end.

documents.title: In the Mood for Love
documents.tagline: Feel the heat, keep the feeling burning, let the sensation explode.
documents.overview: Hong Kong, 1962: Chow Mo-Wan and Su Li-Zhen move into neighboring apartments on the same day. Their encounters are formal and polite—until a discovery about their spouses creates an intimate bond between them.
documents.plot:
In 1962 British Hong Kong, Shanghainese expatriates Chow Mo-wan, a journalist, and Su Li-zhen (Mrs. Chan), a secretary at a shipping company, rent rooms in adjacent apartments. Each has a spouse who often works late, leaving them alone during overtime shifts. Due to the friendly but overbearing presence of Su's Shanghainese landlady, Mrs. Suen, and their bustling, mahjong-playing neighbours, Chow and Su are frequently left alone in their rooms and rarely dine with the other tenants.
Although they are initially polite out of necessity, they grow closer as they realise their spouses are having an affair with each other. Chow notices that his wife owns a handbag available only overseas—one that Su's husband had purchased for her. Su, in turn, observes that her husband wears a tie identical to one Chow owns, a gift from Chow's wife. As they piece together the truth, they begin to reenact how the affair may have begun. While both accept that their spouses have betrayed them, they strive to avoid making the same mistake themselves.
Chow invites Su to help him write a martial arts serial. Their increased time together draws the attention of their neighbours, prompting Chow to rent a hotel room where they can work in private. As time passes, they acknowledge their growing feelings for each other. They continue reenacting scenes from their spouses' affair, but the emotional toll unsettles Su. They sometimes stop speaking, only to reconnect later. When Chow receives a job offer in Singapore, he asks Su to come with him. She agrees, but arrives at the hotel too late and breaks down in his empty room.
The following year, in Singapore, Chow tells a friend an old story: when someone had a secret, they would climb a mountain, carve a hollow in a tree, whisper the secret into it, and seal it with mud. Su later visits Chow's apartment in Singapore. She calls him but says nothing when he answers. Afterward, Chow notices a lipstick-stained cigarette butt in his ashtray and realises she had been there.
Three years later, Su visits Mrs. Suen, who is preparing to immigrate to the United States, and inquires about renting her old apartment. Some time afterward, Chow returns to Hong Kong to visit his former landlords, the Koos, who have moved to the Philippines. He asks about the Suen family next door, and the new owner informs him that a woman and her son now live there. Chow leaves.
During the Vietnam War, Chow travels to Cambodia and visits Angkor Wat. As a monk looks on, he whispers into a hollow in a wall and seals it with mud.

documents.tagline: Are you still in the mood for love?
documents.overview: Women enter and exit a science fiction author's life over the course of a few years after the author loses the woman he considers his one true love.
documents.plot: Women enter and exit a science fiction author's life over the course of a few years after the author loses the woman he considers his one true love.

documents.title: The X Files
documents.tagline: Fight the Future
documents.overview: Mulder and Scully, now taken off the FBI's X Files cases, must find a way to fight the shadowy elements of the government to find out the truth about a conspiracy that might mean the alien colonization of Earth.
documents.plot: Mulder and Scully, now taken off the FBI's X Files cases, must find a way to fight the shadowy elements of the government to find out the truth about a conspiracy that might mean the alien colonization of Earth.

documents.title: Willow
documents.tagline: Adventure doesn't come any bigger than this.
documents.overview: The evil Queen Bavmorda hunts the newborn princess Elora Danan, a child prophesied to bring about her downfall. When the royal infant is found by Willow, a timid farmer and aspiring sorcerer, he's entrusted with delivering her from evil.
documents.plot:
Willow is a 1988 American high fantasy film directed by Ron Howard, produced by George Lucas, and written by Bob Dolman.

In a mystical realm, a young farmer named Willow Ufgood lives on the outskirts of a village with his adoptive family. Willow's life takes an unexpected turn when a sorceress named Madmartigan arrives at their doorstep, seeking refuge from the evil Queen Bavmorda, who is determined to destroy all newborns with magical abilities.

The queen believes that the child will grow up to be a powerful sorcerer and use his powers for evil. Willow's adoptive mother dies soon after giving birth to her son, and Willow takes on the responsibility of caring for him. However, when Madmartigan arrives, he convinces Willow to take the infant to the safety of the Sorceress Elora Danan, who is said to be able to protect the child from the queen's wrath.

As they embark on their perilous journey, Willow and Madmartigan encounter various obstacles, including fierce creatures, treacherous landscapes, and rival sorcerers. Along the way, Willow discovers his own hidden potential as a sorcerer and forms an unlikely bond with Elora Danan, who becomes a mentor to him.

Throughout their quest, Willow must confront his own identity and the true nature of his destiny. He learns that he is not just a simple farmer but a chosen one, destined to wield great power and protect the child from those who seek to harm him.

The film features a richly detailed world, memorable characters, and a narrative that explores themes of friendship, sacrifice, and self-discovery. The special effects, although dated by today's standards, still hold up remarkably well, bringing the fantastical creatures and landscapes to life in a way that immerses the viewer in the world of Willow.

Overall, Willow is a classic fantasy film that has captivated audiences for decades with its engaging story, memorable characters, and stunning visuals.

documents.title: Black Hawk Down
documents.tagline: Leave No Man Behind.
documents.overview: When U.S. Rangers and an elite Delta Force team attempt to kidnap two underlings of a Somali warlord, their Black Hawk helicopters are shot down, and the Americans suffer heavy casualties, facing intense fighting from the militia on the ground.
documents.plot:
Black Hawk Down is a 2001 war film directed by Ridley Scott, produced by Jerry Bruckheimer Films, and based on the book "Black Hawk Down: A Story of Modern War" by Mark Bowden. The film tells the true story of the Battle of Mogadishu, which took place during the Somali Civil War in October 1993.

The movie begins with a prologue that sets the stage for the events of the film. It shows the aftermath of the battle and introduces the main characters, including Delta Force operative Norm "Hoot" Gibson (played by Josh Hartnett), Sergeant First Class Mike Steele (played by Tom Sizemore), and Lieutenant Colonel Mike Steele's son, also named Mike (played by Ewan McGregor).

The story then flashes back to October 3, 1993, when a U.S. military operation aimed at capturing two top Somali warlords, Mohamed Farrah Aidid and Hassan Abdullah Hersi Gabane, goes awry. A team of U.S. soldiers from the 1st Battalion, 75th Ranger Regiment, led by Lieutenant Colonel Mike Steele, is sent to capture Aidid's bodyguards.

The operation begins with a helicopter assault, but things quickly go wrong when the Black Hawk helicopters are ambushed by Somali militiamen. The pilots, including Staff Sergeant Gary "Falcon" Gordon (played by Eric Bana), struggle to escape the city, but their aircraft are severely damaged and begin to take fire from the ground.

As the situation spirals out of control, the U.S. soldiers are forced to abandon ship and make a desperate bid for safety on foot. The movie's intense action sequences follow the soldiers as they navigate through the treacherous streets of Mogadishu, fighting off waves of Somali militiamen and trying to reach the relative safety of their extraction point.

The film's climax features an epic battle between the U.S. soldiers and the Somali militiamen, with both sides suffering heavy casualties. The movie ends with a poignant scene showing the aftermath of the battle, as the surviving soldiers are left to mourn their fallen comrades and grapple with the trauma they have experienced.

Throughout the film, Ridley Scott's direction brings a sense of realism and intensity to the action sequences, while also conveying the emotional toll that the battle takes on the soldiers. The cast delivers strong performances, particularly Josh Hartnett and Tom Sizemore, who bring depth and nuance to their characters.

Overall, Black Hawk Down is a gripping and intense war film that brings the true story of the Battle of Mogadishu to life with stunning action sequences and powerful performances.

documents.title: The Running Man
documents.tagline: 2019. A game nobody survives. This year might be the exception.
documents.overview: By 2017, the global economy has collapsed and U.S. society has become a totalitarian police state, censoring all cultural activity. The government pacifies the populace by broadcasting a number of game shows in which convicted criminals fight for their lives, including the gladiator-style The Running Man, hosted by the ruthless Damon Killian, where “runners” attempt to evade “stalkers” and certain death for a chance to be pardoned and set free.
documents.plot:
In 2017, following a worldwide economic collapse and resource scarcity, the USA has become a totalitarian police state. The government maintains control through propaganda and censorship of unsanctioned art, music, and communication. The state-controlled broadcaster ICS runs the nation's most popular program, "The Running Man," a game show in which prisoners can earn their freedom by surviving as "runners" against lethal "stalkers".
Captain Ben Richards is arrested after refusing orders to open fire on an unarmed food riot in Bakersfield. His fellow officers massacre the rioters and frame Richards for the incident, branding him the "Butcher of Bakersfield". Eighteen months later, Richards escapes from a prison labor camp with resistance fighters Harold Weiss and William Laughlin. They ask him to join their cause, but Richards declines, focused only on surviving.
Richards travels to his brother's former apartment but discovers that ICS composer Amber Mendez now lives there after his brother was taken for "re-education". Richards forces Amber to help him bypass airport security, but thinking he is the "Butcher", she alerts the authorities. After his capture, Amber sees news reports falsely claiming that Richards murdered people during the incident and begins to doubt his guilt.
Damon Killian, host of The Running Man, approaches Richards hoping to use his notoriety to revive the show's ratings. He threatens to send the recaptured Weiss and Laughlin into the game unless Richards agrees to participate. As the show begins, Killian betrays Richards by sending him, Weiss, and Laughlin into the game zone—an abandoned section of L.A.—via rocket sleds.
The group is hunted by Subzero, a hockey-themed stalker whom Richards kills, marking the first time a runner has ever killed a stalker. Meanwhile, Amber is caught retrieving the uncut Bakersfield footage and is sent into the zone. Killian sends in two more stalkers—the chainsaw-wielding Buzzsaw and the electricity-shooting Dynamo. Richards kills Buzzsaw, though Laughlin is fatally wounded. Elsewhere, Weiss discovers that the satellite uplink controlling government broadcasts is located inside the zone, and he cracks the access code for Amber to memorize before Dynamo kills him. Richards incapacitates Dynamo but refuses to kill him while he is defenseless, shocking the audience.
When Killian secretly offers Richards a job as a stalker, Richards angrily refuses. Amber later finds the corpses of the show's past "winners", realizing their victories were fabricated, and Richards kills the flamethrower-wielding Fireball. The audience begins cheering for Richards.
Richards and Amber are found by resistance leader Mic and taken to their command center. Killian tries to force retired stalker Captain Freedom to fight Richards, but he refuses unless he can fight him honorably. ICS instead fabricates footage showing Freedom killing Richards and Amber.

documents.title: Finding Neverland
documents.tagline: Where will your imagination take you?
documents.overview: During a writing slump, playwright J.M. Barrie meets a widow and her four children, all young boys—who soon become an important part of Barrie’s life and the inspiration that lead him to create his masterpiece. Peter Pan'.
documents.plot: During a writing slump, playwright J.M. Barrie meets a widow and her four children, all young boys—who soon become an important part of Barrie’s life and the inspiration that lead him to create his masterpiece. Peter Pan.

documents.title: Planet of the Apes
documents.tagline: You'll be sorry you were ever born human.
documents.overview: After a spectacular crash-landing on an uncharted planet, brash astronaut Leo Davidson finds himself trapped in a savage world where talking apes dominate the human race. Desperate to find a way home, Leo must evade the invincible gorilla army led by Ruthless General Thade.
documents.plot:
Planet of the Apes is a 2001 American science fiction adventure film from director Tim Burton, written by William Broyles Jr., Lawrence Konner and Mark Rosenthal. Loosely based on Pierre Boulle's 1963 novel, it remakes the 1968 film. Mark Wahlberg plays the astronaut Leo Davidson, with Tim Roth as General Thade, Helena Bonham Carter as Ari, Michael Clarke Duncan as Colonel Attar, Paul Giamatti as Limbo, Estella Warren as Daena and Kris Kristofferson.

In 2029, Leo works with apes trained for spaceflight aboard the space station Oberon. When an electromagnetic storm nears the station, his favourite chimpanzee, Pericles, is sent into it in a probe pod and vanishes. Leo follows in another pod without permission and crash-lands in the year 5021 on Ashlar, a planet where intelligent apes rule and keep humans as slaves. Ari, a chimpanzee who opposes this cruelty, buys Leo and a young woman, Daena, as servants in the house of her father, Senator Sandar. Leo breaks free and liberates other humans, taking the orangutan slave dealer Limbo prisoner to keep him quiet, while the ruthless chimpanzee General Thade and his gorilla deputy Attar lead an army in pursuit.

Leo reaches Calima, the forbidden temple of Semos, the first ape, whom the apes worship and expect to return one day. It proves to be the ancient wreck of the Oberon: Leo realises that the storm hurled him forward in time while the station, searching for him, crashed on the planet thousands of years earlier. Its logs show that the apes aboard, led by Semos, mutinied after the crash; the survivors of both species are the ancestors of the planet's people. As the apes attack the gathered humans, Leo uses the ship's remaining fuel to strike their first wave. The fighting halts when Pericles' pod descends from the sky, having also been carried through time; the apes take him for Semos and lay down their arms. Thade follows Leo into the wreck and grabs his gun, but Leo traps him on the pilot's deck. Leaving Pericles with Ari, Leo flies the pod back through the storm. Crashing in Washington, D.C., he finds the Lincoln Memorial now honours Thade, and the police and reporters who surround him are apes.

Released by 20th Century Fox on July 27, 2001, the film grossed $362.2 million worldwide, the ninth-highest total of the year. Reviews were mixed: critics faulted the screenplay and twist ending but praised Rick Baker's makeup, the visuals and the score, giving it 42% on Rotten Tomatoes.

documents.title: Planet of the Apes
documents.tagline: Somewhere in the Universe, there must be something better than man!
documents.overview: Astronaut Taylor crash lands on a distant planet ruled by apes who use a primitive race of humans for experimentation and sport. Soon Taylor finds himself among the hunted, his life in the hands of a benevolent chimpanzee scientist.
documents.plot:
Planet of the Apes is a groundbreaking science fiction film directed by Franklin J. Schaffner, released in 1968 by 20th Century Fox. The movie is set in a post-apocalyptic future where intelligent apes have evolved to become the dominant species on Earth.

The story begins with astronaut George Taylor (played by Charlton Heston), who crash-lands on a mysterious planet along with a group of astronauts, including Lieutenant Parker (James Franciscus) and Dr. Zaius (Lloyd Nolan). As they explore their surroundings, they discover that the planet is inhabited by intelligent apes, who seem to be living in a sophisticated society.

The apes are led by Zira (Kim Hunter), a scientist who is studying the human species. She is particularly interested in Taylor and his crew, as she believes they may hold the key to understanding the evolution of humanity. The apes also have a leader named Caesar (Roddy McDowall), who is intelligent and charismatic.

As Taylor and his crew try to find a way off the planet, they are captured by the apes and taken to their city. There, they meet Zira and Caesar, who reveal that the planet was once Earth but was devastated by nuclear war. The humans were wiped out, and the apes evolved from the survivors of the war.

The apes have created a complex society with their own culture, language, and customs. However, as Taylor and his crew learn more about the apes' world, they begin to realize that something is not quite right. They discover that the apes are hiding a dark secret: they have been using human embryos in their own breeding program.

Taylor becomes increasingly disillusioned with the apes' society and begins to question Zira's motives. He also forms a bond with Caesar, who is torn between his loyalty to Zira and his growing sense of humanity.

As the story unfolds, Taylor and Caesar embark on a perilous journey through the ape city, seeking answers about their past and the fate of humanity. Along the way, they encounter various obstacles and challenges, including treacherous terrain and hostile apes.

Ultimately, Taylor and Caesar reach the heart of the ape city, where they discover a shocking truth: the planet is actually a post-apocalyptic Earth, and the humans who survived the nuclear war were brought to this planet as infants and raised by the apes. The movie ends with Taylor, now an ape himself, sitting on a throne, surrounded by his new family.

The ending is intentionally ambiguous, leaving the audience to ponder the implications of the story. Is Taylor still human, or has he truly become one of them? The final shot of the movie shows a statue of a human figure with the inscription "Caesar's Head," suggesting that even in this post-apocalyptic world, humanity's legacy lives on.

Overall, Planet of the Apes is a thought-provoking and visually stunning film that explores themes of identity, morality, and the nature of humanity. Its influence can still be seen in science fiction today, and it remains one of the most iconic and enduring films of all time.

documents.title: Coffee and Cigarettes
documents.overview: Coffee And Cigarettes is a collection of eleven films from cult director Jim Jarmusch. Each film hosts star studded cast of extremely unique individuals who all share the common activities of conversing while drinking coffee and smoking cigarettes.
documents.plot: An anthology of eleven vignettes featuring star-studded casts of extremely unique individuals who all share the common activities of conversing while drinking coffee and smoking cigarettes.

documents.title: The Best Years of Our Lives
documents.original_title: The Best Years of Our Lives
documents.tagline: Three wonderful loves in the best picture of the year!
documents.overview: It's the hope that sustains the spirit of every GI: the dream of the day when he will finally return home. For three WWII veterans, the day has arrived. But for each man, the dream is about to become a nightmare.
documents.plot:
Three returning World War II veterans meet on a flight to their midwestern hometown of Boone City. USAAF bombardier captain Fred Derry had been a drugstore soda jerk who lived with his father and stepmother on the wrong side of the tracks. Before shipping out, Fred married Marie after a whirlwind romance. Marie has since been working in a nightclub to fill her time despite receiving Fred's combat pay as an Air Force officer. U.S. Army sergeant Al Stephenson is a bank executive; he, his wife Milly and their children Peggy and Rob live in a luxury apartment. U.S. Navy petty officer Homer Parrish was a star high school athlete living with his middle-class parents and younger sister, and dating his next-door neighbor Wilma, whom he intended to marry upon his return from the war.
Each man faces challenges integrating back into civilian life. Homer lost both hands in the war; he is reluctant to return home and face his well-meaning parents and their friends, who have a hard time seeing past his disability. Homer can deftly use his mechanical hooks, but hesitates to display affection for Wilma as he cannot believe she will still want to marry him. Al, tired and jaded, returns to the bank and is given a promotion, but wrestles with alcohol. Fred suffers from PTSD flashbacks and struggles to find a job beyond menial work, befitting a military officer.
Fred arrives home and cannot locate his party girl wife, who does not expect him. The Stephensons and Peggy invite Fred to join them, bar-hopping to celebrate Al's return. An inebriated Fred keeps asking Peggy who she is; she humorously reminds him she's "Al's daughter." When Fred can't get into his apartment, the Stephensons offer him a bed for the night. Later, Peggy calms Fred during a nightmare and they develop a mutual attraction. After meeting Marie during an outing orchestrated by Peggy, she concludes Marie is shallow and materialistic. Peggy determines to break up Fred's marriage, much to Al's consternation.
Frustrated and depressed by his loss of independence; and concerned that Wilma doesn't fully understand the difficulties of being married to him, Homer demonstrates how she'll need to assist him when he removes his prosthetic hands at bedtime, leaving him helpless. Wilma reaffirms her love and vows her commitment to a grateful and emotional Homer, who finally embraces her.
Widely respected by the bank's senior management for his past business acumen, Al is admonished after approving an unsecured loan to a farmer and fellow veteran without collateral (never realizing the land the farmer wishes to purchase could be collateral for the loan). With inhibitions lowered by excessive drinking, Al gives a speech at a work banquet that satirizes requiring a veteran to provide collateral before risking his life to take a hill in battle.
With little work experience and unable to find a better job than soda jerk, Fred returns to the same drugstore and is now supervised by his former protege.

documents.title: Bullitt
documents.tagline: There are bad cops, good cops - and then there's Bullitt.
documents.overview: Senator Walter Chalmers is aiming to take down mob boss Pete Ross with the help of testimony from the criminal's hothead brother Johnny, who is in protective custody in San Francisco under the watch of police lieutenant Frank Bullitt. When a pair of mob hitmen enter the scene, Bullitt follows their trail through a maze of complications and double-crosses. This thriller includes one of the most famous car chases ever filmed.
documents.plot:
Bullitt is a 1968 American action thriller film directed by Peter Yates and produced by Solar Productions. The movie stars Steve McQueen as Frank Bullitt, a tough and skilled FBI agent tasked with protecting the key witness in a murder case.

The story begins with the introduction of Frank Bullitt (Steve McQueen), an experienced and skilled FBI agent who is assigned to protect Richard "Rich" Boyer (Robert Vaughn), a wealthy businessman whose testimony could bring down notorious crime boss Samson Pope (Pat Renella). The two men are on their way to Los Angeles when they are ambushed by Pope's henchmen, resulting in the death of Boyer.

Bullitt is left shaken but determined to solve the case and bring justice to Boyer's family. He teams up with Chico Gonzalez (Estelito Aguilar), a Mexican-American informant who provides him with crucial information about Pope's organization. As Bullitt delves deeper into the case, he becomes increasingly obsessed with finding the killer.

The plot thickens as Bullitt discovers that Pope is involved in a large-scale money laundering operation and that Boyer was getting close to exposing it. With the help of Gonzalez, Bullitt sets out to track down Pope's men and bring them to justice.

As the story unfolds, Bullitt becomes more and more determined to solve the case, often putting himself in harm's way. He is aided by his partner, Lee (Robert Beatty), who provides him with support and guidance throughout the investigation.

The climax of the movie takes place during a high-speed car chase through San Francisco, where Bullitt pursues Pope's henchmen in a white Mustang. The chase is intense and suspenseful, with both drivers pushing their cars to the limit.

In the end, Bullitt finally tracks down Pope and his men, leading to a tense showdown between the two. However, just as Bullitt thinks he has solved the case, it becomes clear that there are still many loose ends. The movie ends with Bullitt reflecting on the case and the toll it has taken on him.

Throughout the movie, Steve McQueen delivers a memorable performance as Frank Bullitt, bringing depth and nuance to the character. The film's action sequences, particularly the iconic car chase, have become legendary in the world of cinema.

Overall, Bullitt is a gripping and suspenseful thriller that showcases Steve McQueen's acting abilities and Peter Yates' direction. The movie's blend of action, drama, and intrigue has made it a classic of American cinema.

documents.title: Blood: The Last Vampire
documents.tagline: Where evil grows, she preys.
documents.overview: In Japan, the vampire-hunter Saya, who is a powerful original, is sent by her liaison with the government, David, posed as a teenage student to the Yokota High School on the eve of Halloween to hunt down vampires. Saya asks David to give a new katana to her. Soon she saves the school nurse Makiho Amano from two vampires disguised of classmates and Makiho witnesses her fight against the powerful demon.
documents.plot:
The story is set in 1966. Its main protagonist is a girl named Saya, who hunts bat-like vampiric creatures called Chiropterans. Saya is introduced on a subway train, where she assassinates a man in a suit. Her American contacts or handlers arrive. One of them, David, begins to brief Saya on another mission, while the other, Louis, discovers that the man Saya has just killed was probably not a Chiropteran.
Saya's next mission begins at the American Yokota Air Base, which is active in the buildup to the Vietnam War. At least one Chiropteran has managed to infiltrate the air base, and it is only a matter of time before they feed again, go into hibernation, and become untraceable. Saya is to pose as a school girl, infiltrate the high school adjacent to the base, and then track and kill the Chiropterans.
At the school, Saya runs into a meek nurse, Amino Makiho, on the eve of the school's annual Halloween party. Two of Saya's classmates, Sharon and Linda, make a visit to Makiho at the nurse's office. Suddenly, Saya bursts into the room, killing Linda and wounding Sharon, breaking her sword in the process. Both girls are revealed to be Chiropterans. Makiho goes into shock at the revelation. Meanwhile, a third Chiropteran reveals itself and begins making its way to the base. Back at the school, Makiho regains her nerve and pursues Sharon into a room full of dancing Americans in costume, where she finds Sharon transformed. Saya saves her and both flee into a nearby motor pool. The Chiropterans trap them inside and attack.
David delivers a new sword, and Saya uses it to kill Sharon. The final Chiropteran then decides to flee, attempting to stow away on a departing cargo plane. David and Saya give chase and she manages to strike the Chiropteran and mortally wound it. She then stands over the dying creature and lets some of her blood trickle into its mouth. Louis arrives and recovers Makiho before the local police reach her.
Afterward, Makiho is seen in an interview with government officials who question her about the night's events. However, it's revealed that all evidence of the battle between Saya and the Chiropterans has been covered up and both David and Saya have disappeared, leaving Makiho with nothing to prove the veracity of her story. Her interviewer then asks her to identify Saya in a picture which has a girl that looks identical to her, except the picture was taken in 1892. The only other description of the picture is the word "VAMPIRE". Makiho then returns to the school, where she narrates that she never really discovered the full truth behind Saya and the Chiropterans, and wonders if she's still out there fighting them.

documents.title: Cars
documents.tagline: Ahhh... it's got that new movie smell.
documents.overview: Lightning McQueen, a hotshot rookie race car driven to succeed, discovers that life is about the journey, not the finish line, when he finds himself unexpectedly detoured in the sleepy Route 66 town of Radiator Springs. On route across the country to the big Piston Cup Championship in California to compete against two seasoned pros, McQueen gets to know the town's offbeat characters.
documents.plot:
Cars is a computer-animated comedy-adventure film released in 2006 by Walt Disney Pictures. The movie takes place in a world where cars are living beings, and it follows the story of Lightning McQueen, a hotshot rookie race car who gets stranded in a small town called Radiator Springs.

The film begins with Lightning McQueen (voiced by Owen Wilson), a talented but arrogant racing car from North Carolina. He is on his way to California to participate in the Piston Cup Championship, a prestigious racing competition that will make him a legend in the racing world. During his journey, he gets lost due to a faulty GPS system and ends up in Radiator Springs, a small town on Route 66.

Initially, McQueen is reluctant to stay in Radiator Springs, as he believes it's not a place for high-performance cars like himself. However, he soon befriends the town's residents, including Mater (voiced by Larry the Cable Guy), a rusty but lovable tow truck; Sally Carrera (voiced by Bonnie Hunt), a sleek and sophisticated Porsche; and Doc Hudson (voiced by Paul Newman), a wise and aged Hudson Hornet.

As McQueen spends more time in Radiator Springs, he learns about the town's history and the struggles its residents have faced due to the decline of Route 66. He also discovers that his arrival has brought new life to the town, but at the cost of its former glory. McQueen decides to help the townspeople by participating in the annual "Cozy Cone" festival, which is a celebration of the town's heritage.

However, things take a turn when McQueen's rival, Chick Hicks (voiced by Michael Keaton), arrives in Radiator Springs, seeking to sabotage McQueen's chances of winning the Piston Cup. As the championship approaches, McQueen must balance his racing ambitions with his newfound friendships and sense of responsibility towards the people of Radiator Springs.

In the end, McQueen learns a valuable lesson about the importance of friendship, community, and being true to oneself. He decides to abandon his original plan to win the Piston Cup and instead focuses on helping Radiator Springs revitalize its economy and restore its former glory. The film concludes with McQueen's return to Radiator Springs as a champion, but not just for winning the championship – for being a part of a community that has become like family to him.

Throughout the movie, Cars features stunning animation, lovable characters, and a heartwarming story that explores themes of friendship, perseverance, and finding one's true purpose. The film was a critical and commercial success, grossing over $462 million worldwide and spawning two sequels, Cars 2 (2011) and Cars 3 (2017).

documents.title: Cinderella Man
documents.tagline: One man's extraordinary fight to save the family he loved.
documents.overview: The true story of boxer Jim Braddock who, in the 1920s following his retirement, makes a surprise comeback in order to get him and his family out of a socially poor state.
documents.plot: The true story of boxer Jim Braddock who, following his retirement in the 1930s, makes a surprise comeback in order to lift his family out of poverty.

documents.title: Dawn of the Dead
documents.tagline: When there’s no more room in HELL, the dead will walk the EARTH!
documents.overview: During an ever-growing epidemic of zombies that have risen from the dead, two Philadelphia SWAT team members, a traffic reporter, and his television-executive girlfriend seek refuge in a secluded shopping mall.
documents.plot:
Dawn of the Dead is a 1978 zombie horror film written, directed and edited by George A. Romero and produced by Richard P. Rubinstein. An American-Italian co-production, it is the second film in Romero's series of zombie films after Night of the Living Dead (1968), and depicts a zombie apocalypse on a much larger scale. David Emge, Ken Foree, Scott Reiniger and Gaylen Ross star as survivors who barricade themselves inside a suburban shopping mall.

The dead are rising and attacking the living across the United States, and society is collapsing. At a Philadelphia television station, the traffic reporter Stephen and his pregnant girlfriend, the producer Francine, plan to escape in the station's helicopter. Across the city, a SWAT team raids a housing project whose tenants have refused to hand over their dead to the authorities, and the operation descends into a bloodbath. Disillusioned, the SWAT officer Roger, a friend of Stephen's, and Peter, an officer from another unit, decide to desert and join the couple. The four flee the city by helicopter and, after a few close calls while refueling, land on the roof of a deserted shopping mall.

Finding everything they need inside, they decide to stay. The men block the entrances with trucks and clear the building of zombies, but Roger grows reckless and is bitten. After he dies and reanimates, Peter shoots him. The survivors build a hidden refuge and settle into a comfortable but empty life of consumer abundance as emergency broadcasts end. Fran has Stephen teach her to fly the helicopter.

Months later, a gang of marauding bikers spots the helicopter and breaks into the mall to loot it, letting in hundreds of zombies. Stephen, refusing to give up what he regards as theirs, opens fire on the bikers, setting off a battle in which many of them are devoured. Stephen is shot and killed by the zombies, and after reanimating he leads the undead to the hideout. Peter kills him and prepares to take his own life, but changes his mind and fights his way to the roof, where he joins Fran in the helicopter as they fly off, low on fuel, toward an uncertain future.

Inspired by Romero's visit to the Monroeville Mall in Pennsylvania, the film was co-financed by Dario Argento, who edited his own cut featuring music by Goblin, and its gore effects launched the career of Tom Savini. Released unrated in the United States after receiving an X rating, it was acclaimed by critics, with Rotten Tomatoes reporting 92% approval.

documents.title: Dawn of the Dead
documents.tagline: When the undead rise, civilization will fall.
documents.overview: A group of survivors take refuge in a shopping mall after the world is taken over by aggressive, flesh-eating zombies.
documents.plot:
Dawn of the Dead is a 2004 American zombie horror film directed by Zack Snyder, starring Ving Rhames, Mena Suvari, and Jake Weber. The movie is a remake of George A. Romero's 1978 film of the same name.

The story begins with a montage of news clips showing the rapid spread of a mysterious virus that turns people into zombies.
