We then see a group of survivors, including Jim (Jake Weber), Steve (Michael Kelly), and Peter (Ty Burrell), who are trying to escape the chaos in Philadelphia. They eventually find themselves at a shopping mall, where they barricade themselves inside.

As the days pass, the group tries to maintain some semblance of normalcy, with Jim attempting to hold down a job as a security guard while Steve and Peter try to scavenge for food and supplies. However, their attempts are constantly thwarted by hordes of zombies that seem to be attracted to the mall.

The group soon realizes that they are not alone in the mall. They discover a mysterious woman named Ana (Mena Suvari), who is initially hostile towards them but eventually becomes an ally. As the days turn into weeks, the group begins to experience strange and terrifying occurrences, including visions of a zombie-like creature that seems to be watching them.

As tensions rise within the group, Jim's leadership is challenged by Steve, who wants to take more drastic measures to survive. Meanwhile, Ana's past is slowly revealed, showing her to be a former model who was infected with the virus and has since become a zombie herself.

The movie takes a dark turn when the group discovers that the mall is being overrun by an even larger horde of zombies. In a desperate bid to escape, they set fire to the mall, hoping to create a diversion that will allow them to make their way out.

However, as they attempt to flee, Jim becomes increasingly unhinged, and his actions become more erratic. The group eventually splits up, with some members making it out of the mall while others are left behind.

The movie ends with Ana, who has been bitten by a zombie, being taken away by a group of survivors who have managed to escape the mall. As she is carried off into the distance, we see Jim standing alone in the ruins of the mall, his eyes fixed on the camera with a mixture of horror and despair.

Throughout the movie, Snyder's direction adds a layer of social commentary, using the zombie apocalypse as a metaphor for consumerism and the breakdown of society. The film's use of satire and irony is evident in its portrayal of the zombies as mindless consumers who are drawn to the mall like moths to a flame.

Overall, Dawn of the Dead is a tense and unsettling horror movie that explores themes of survival, leadership, and the human condition. While it received mixed reviews from critics at the time of its release, it has since become a cult classic and is widely regarded as one of the best zombie movies of all time.

documents.title: Godzilla
documents.tagline: Size does matter.
documents.overview: French nuclear tests irradiate an iguana into a giant monster that viciously attacks freighter ships in the Pacific Ocean. A team of experts, including Niko Tatopoulos, conclude that the oversized reptile is the culprit. Before long, the giant lizard is loose in Manhattan as the US military races to destroy the monster before it reproduces and it's spawn takes over the world.
documents.plot:
Godzilla is a 1998 American monster film directed by Roland Emmerich, who co-wrote it with producer Dean Devlin as an American reboot of Toho's Godzilla franchise. Matthew Broderick stars as the biologist Nick Tatopoulos and Jean Reno as a French secret agent, with Maria Pitillo, Hank Azaria, Kevin Dunn, Michael Lerner and Harry Shearer. The film is dedicated to Godzilla co-creator Tomoyuki Tanaka. TriStar Pictures released it on May 20, 1998, in a then-record 3,310 theatres in North America.

Fallout from French nuclear tests in Polynesia mutates an iguana nest. Years later a huge creature sinks a Japanese fishing ship, and a traumatised survivor, questioned by a mysterious Frenchman, can only repeat "Gojira". Nick Tatopoulos, studying earthworms at Chernobyl, is drafted by the US government to analyse the trail of destruction and concludes that the animal is a radiation-born mutant, not a dinosaur. The creature then comes ashore in Manhattan, flattening streets as the city is evacuated.

The army lures it out with a mountain of fish but fails to kill it. Nick discovers that the animal reproduces asexually and is about to lay eggs. He reunites with his former girlfriend Audrey Timmonds, an ambitious junior reporter, who steals a classified tape from him; her boss, Charles Caiman, claims the story and names the monster Godzilla. Nick is dismissed from the operation and recruited by Philippe Roaché, an agent of the French secret service trying to cover up France's role. Audrey and her cameraman Victor "Animal" Palotti tag along.

After a second strike, Godzilla is attacked by submarines in the Hudson and believed dead. Nick's group locates its nest inside Madison Square Garden, where hundreds of offspring hatch and attack. They broadcast a warning from the arena, escaping just before air strikes destroy it. Godzilla, still alive and enraged by the loss of its young, pursues them across Manhattan until it becomes tangled in the cables of the Brooklyn Bridge and is killed by missiles. Audrey quits her job, and Philippe departs with Animal's footage. In the ruins, one surviving egg hatches.

The film earned about 379 million dollars worldwide but was widely panned, with a 20% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes, and won Golden Raspberry Awards including Worst Remake or Sequel.

documents.title: Ice Age: The Meltdown
documents.tagline: Kiss Your Nuts Goodbye
documents.overview: Diego, Manny and Sid return in this sequel to the hit animated movie Ice Age. This time around, the deep freeze is over, and the ice-covered earth is starting to melt, which will destroy the trio's cherished valley. The impending disaster prompts them to reunite and warn all the other beasts about the desperate situation.
documents.plot:
Ice Age: The Meltdown is a 2006 animated adventure comedy film produced by Blue Sky Studios and distributed by 20th Century Fox. The movie serves as a sequel to the original Ice Age film.

The story begins with Manny, a woolly mammoth, Sid, a sloth, and Diego, a saber-toothed tiger, living in their respective habitats during the Pleistocene era. However, due to climate change, the ice caps are melting, causing chaos throughout the world. The trio is forced to embark on an epic journey to reach the fabled "Paradise Falls," a lush oasis that has been hidden beneath the melting ice.

As they travel through treacherous landscapes and encounter various obstacles, Manny, Sid, and Diego begin to realize that their friendship is more important than their individual goals. Along the way, they meet new characters, including Buck, a weasel who becomes an unlikely ally, and Scrat, Manny's obsessive acorn-loving companion.

As the group nears Paradise Falls, they discover that it has been taken over by a group of ruthless pirates led by Captain Gutt, a giant prehistoric crocodile. The pirates are determined to claim the falls' resources for themselves, putting the entire ecosystem at risk.

Manny, Sid, and Diego must use their unique skills and work together to defeat the pirates and save Paradise Falls. Along the way, they learn valuable lessons about teamwork, trust, and the importance of preserving their natural habitats.

The movie features stunning animation, witty humor, and lovable characters that have become iconic in popular culture. The voice cast, including Ray Romano, John Leguizamo, Denis Leary, and Queen Latifah, delivers memorable performances that bring the characters to life.

In the end, Manny, Sid, and Diego successfully defeat Captain Gutt and his pirates, saving Paradise Falls and restoring balance to the ecosystem. The movie concludes with a heartwarming moment of friendship and camaraderie between the three main characters as they look out upon their newly preserved home.

Overall, Ice Age: The Meltdown is a fun, action-packed adventure that explores themes of friendship, teamwork, and environmentalism. With its engaging storyline, lovable characters, and stunning animation, it's no wonder this movie has become a beloved classic among both children and adults alike.

documents.title: Madagascar
documents.tagline: Someone’s got a zoo loose.
documents.overview: Alex the lion is the king of the urban jungle, the main attraction at New York's Central Park Zoo. He and his best friends—Marty the zebra, Melman the giraffe and Gloria the hippo—have spent their whole lives in blissful captivity before an admiring public and with regular meals provided for them. Not content to leave well enough alone, Marty lets his curiosity get the better of him and makes his escape—with the help of some prodigious penguins—to explore the world.
documents.plot:
Madagascar is a computer-animated comedy film released in 2005 by DreamWorks Pictures. The movie follows the story of four main characters: Alex the lion, Marty the zebra, Gloria the hippopotamus, and Melman the giraffe.

The film begins with Alex (voiced by Ben Stiller), Marty (voiced by Chris Rock), Gloria (voiced by Jada Pinkett Smith), and Melman (voiced by David Schwimmer) living in the Central Park Zoo in New York City. The animals are content with their lives, but they often fantasize about exploring the wild.

One day, a group of zoo employees plan to relocate the animals to a theme park called "Madagascar" in Africa. Alex is excited at the prospect of experiencing the wild, while Marty is more concerned about being separated from his friends. Gloria and Melman are hesitant, but ultimately agree to go along with the move.

Upon arrival in Madagascar, the animals discover that they have been transported to a remote island, far from their home in New York City. They soon realize that they must survive on their own and adapt to their new surroundings. Marty, being the curious and adventurous one, takes the lead in exploring the island and finding food.

As the group navigates their new environment, they encounter various obstacles, including treacherous terrain, wild predators, and rival animals. Along the way, Alex struggles with his identity as a lion, feeling pressure to live up to his role as the "king" of the zoo. Marty, on the other hand, finds himself in a series of comedic misadventures, often getting into trouble due to his impulsive nature.

As the story unfolds, the animals form an unlikely friendship with a group of lemurs, led by King Julian (voiced by Sacha Baron Cohen). The lemurs are initially hostile towards the newcomers but eventually warm up to them. However, their friendship is put to the test when they discover that the zoo employees who brought them to Madagascar have abandoned them.

In the end, Alex and his friends must work together to survive on the island and find a way back home. Along the way, they learn valuable lessons about teamwork, loyalty, and embracing their true selves. The movie culminates in a thrilling finale where the animals outsmart the zoo employees and escape the island, returning to New York City.

Throughout the film, the characters' personalities shine through, with Marty's humor and wit providing much of the comedic relief. The animation is vibrant and colorful, bringing the characters and their world to life. Overall, Madagascar is a heartwarming and entertaining film that explores themes of friendship, identity, and belonging.

documents.title: Mission: Impossible II
documents.tagline: Expect the impossible again.
documents.overview: With computer genius Luther Stickell at his side and a beautiful thief on his mind, agent Ethan Hunt races across Australia and Spain to stop a former IMF agent from unleashing a genetically engineered biological weapon called Chimera. This mission, should Hunt choose to accept it, plunges him into the center of an international crisis of terrifying magnitude.
documents.plot:
Mission: Impossible II is a 2000 action spy film directed by John Woo and starring Tom Cruise as Ethan Hunt. The movie takes place two years after the events of the first film.

The story begins with Ethan Hunt, who has been presumed dead after his last mission went awry. However, he is revealed to be alive and working undercover in the Middle East, where he infiltrates a terrorist organization known as the Syndicate. The Syndicate is led by a ruthless woman named Nyah Nordoff-Hall (Thandie Newton), who is also Ethan's love interest.

As Ethan delves deeper into the Syndicate, he discovers that they are planning to sell a deadly virus called the "Chimera" to the highest bidder. The Chimera is a genetically engineered virus that can kill millions of people and has the potential to wipe out entire cities.

Ethan soon realizes that the true mastermind behind the Syndicate is Sean Ambrose (Dougray Scott), a former CIA operative who was thought to be dead. Ambrose has been working with Nyah, who is revealed to be his sister, and together they plan to sell the Chimera virus to the highest bidder.

As Ethan navigates through the complex web of intrigue, he must also contend with the IMF (Impossible Mission Force), which is now led by Jim Phelps (Jon Voight). However, it soon becomes clear that Phelps has been compromised by Ambrose and is working against Ethan's interests.

The plot thickens as Ethan discovers that Nyah is being manipulated by her brother and that she is not what she seems. In a thrilling twist, Ethan and Nyah team up to take down the Syndicate and prevent the sale of the Chimera virus.

In the climactic final act, Ethan faces off against Ambrose in a high-stakes battle at a nightclub. The two engage in an intense fight, with Ethan using his wits and agility to outmaneuver Ambrose's henchmen.

As the dust settles, Ethan emerges victorious, but not without sacrifices. Nyah is revealed to be a double agent who was working to take down her brother from within. In the end, Ethan and Nyah share a moment of tenderness, suggesting that their relationship may have a future.

The movie concludes with Ethan returning to the IMF, where he is welcomed back as a hero. However, the film ends on a somber note, hinting that there are still many more missions ahead for Ethan Hunt.

Overall, Mission: Impossible II is an action-packed thrill ride that delivers on its promise of high-octane excitement and espionage intrigue. Tom Cruise's performance as Ethan Hunt is as charismatic as ever, and the movie's twists and turns keep viewers on the edge of their seats until the very end.

documents.title: Mission: Impossible III
documents.tagline: The mission begins 05:05:06.
documents.overview: Retired from active duty to train new IMF agents, Ethan Hunt is called back into action to confront sadistic arms dealer, Owen Davian. Hunt must try to protect his girlfriend while working with his new team to complete the mission.
documents.plot:
Mission: Impossible III is a 2006 action spy film directed by J.J. Abrams and starring Tom Cruise as Ethan Hunt. The movie marks the third installment in the Mission: Impossible film series.

The story begins with Ethan Hunt, a secret agent working for the Impossible Mission Force (IMF), who has retired from active duty after a successful mission. However, he is pulled back into service when his protégée, Lindsey Farris (Keri Russell), is kidnapped by Owen Davian (Philip Seymour Hoffman), a rogue IMF agent.

Ethan soon discovers that Davian is working with the arms dealer, August Walker (Philip Dance), to sell nuclear warheads on the black market. As Ethan delves deeper into the mission, he must navigate his complicated past and confront his own demons in order to rescue Lindsey and prevent a global catastrophe.

Throughout the film, Ethan's skills as an agent are put to the test as he faces off against Davian and Walker in a series of intense action sequences. The movie features a mix of high-stakes espionage, heart-pumping stunts, and witty banter between Ethan and his allies.

One of the standout aspects of Mission: Impossible III is its exploration of Ethan's character development. As he navigates the complex web of intrigue, he must confront his own mortality and the consequences of his actions. The film also introduces a new character, Benji Dunn (Simon Pegg), who becomes Ethan's trusted ally and provides comic relief in an otherwise tense situation.

The movie's climax features an epic showdown between Ethan and Davian, with the two agents engaging in a high-speed car chase through the streets of Paris. In the end, Ethan emerges victorious, but not without sacrifices. The film concludes on a bittersweet note, as Ethan comes to terms with his past and looks towards a uncertain future.

Overall, Mission: Impossible III is an action-packed thrill ride that delivers on its promise of high-octane espionage and heart-pumping stunts. With Tom Cruise delivering a standout performance, the movie sets the stage for the next installment in the franchise.

documents.title: Dirty Harry
documents.tagline: Detective Harry Callahan. He doesn't break murder cases. He smashes them.
documents.overview: When a madman dubbed 'Scorpio' terrorizes San Francisco, hard-nosed cop, Harry Callahan – famous for his take-no-prisoners approach to law enforcement – is tasked with hunting down the psychopath. Harry eventually collars Scorpio in the process of rescuing a kidnap victim, only to see him walk on technicalities. Now, the maverick detective is determined to nail the maniac himself.
documents.plot: When a madman dubbed 'Scorpio' terrorizes San Francisco, hard-nosed cop, Harry Callahan – famous for his take-no-prisoners approach to law enforcement – is tasked with hunting down the psychopath.

documents.title: The China Syndrome
documents.tagline: Sometimes it’s too late to tell the truth.
documents.overview: While doing a series of reports on alternative energy sources, opportunistic reporter Kimberly Wells witnesses an accident at a nuclear power plant. Wells is determined to publicize the incident, but soon finds herself entangled in a sinister conspiracy to keep the full impact of the incident a secret.
documents.plot:
While visiting the Ventana nuclear power plant outside Los Angeles, television news reporter Kimberly Wells, her cameraman Richard Adams and their soundman Hector Salas witness the plant going through a turbine trip and corresponding SCRAM (emergency shutdown). Shift Supervisor Jack Godell notices an unusual vibration in his cup of coffee.
In response to a gauge indicating high water levels, Godell begins removing water from the core, but the gauge remains high as operators open more valves to dump water. Another operator notices a second gauge indicating low water levels. Godell taps the first gauge, which immediately unsticks and drops to indicate very low levels. The crew urgently pumps water back in and celebrates in relief at bringing the reactor back under control.
Adams has surreptitiously filmed the incident, despite being asked not to film for security reasons. Wells' superior refuses to broadcast her report on the incident. Adams steals the footage and shows it to experts who conclude that the plant came perilously close to meltdown‍—‍‌the China syndrome.
During an inspection of the plant before it is brought back online, Godell discovers a puddle of radioactive water that has apparently leaked from a pump. He pushes to delay restarting the plant, but the plant superintendent wants nothing standing in the way of the restart.
Godell finds that a series of radiographs supposedly verifying the welds on the leaking pump are identical‍—‍‌the contractor simply kept resubmitting the same picture. He brings the evidence to the plant superintendent, who brushes him off as paranoid, stating that new radiographs would cost $20 million. Godell confronts Royce, an employee of Foster-Sullivan who built the plant, as it was he who signed off on the radiographs. Godell threatens to go to the Nuclear Regulatory Commission, but Royce threatens him; later, a pair of men from Foster-Sullivan park outside his house.
Wells and Adams confront Godell at his home and he voices his concerns. Wells and Adams ask him to testify at the NRC hearings over Foster-Sullivan's plans to build another nuclear plant. Godell agrees to obtain, through Salas, the false radiographs to take to the hearings.
Salas' car is run off the road and the radiographs are taken from him. Godell is chased by the men waiting outside his home. He takes refuge inside the plant, where he finds that the reactor is being brought up to full power. Grabbing a gun from a security guard, he forces everyone out, including his friend and co-worker Ted Spindler, and demands to be interviewed by Wells on live television. Plant management agrees to the interview in order to buy time as they try to regain control of the plant.
Minutes into the broadcast, plant technicians deliberately cause a SCRAM so they can distract Godell and retake the control room. A SWAT team forces its way in, the television cable is cut, and Godell is shot. Before dying, he feels the unusual vibration again.

documents.title: Mulholland Drive
documents.tagline: An actress longing to be a star. A woman searching for herself. Both worlds will collide… on Mulholland Drive.
documents.overview: Blonde Betty Elms has only just arrived in Hollywood to become a movie star when she meets an enigmatic brunette with amnesia. Meanwhile, as the two set off to solve the second woman's identity, filmmaker Adam Kesher runs into ominous trouble while casting his latest project.
documents.plot:
Mulholland Drive is a 2001 surrealist neo-noir mystery written and directed by David Lynch. Naomi Watts stars as Betty Elms, an aspiring actress newly arrived in Los Angeles, and Laura Harring as an amnesiac car crash survivor, with Justin Theroux as a film director, Ann Miller and Dan Hedaya. Originally conceived as a television pilot for ABC, it was shot in 1999, but after the network rejected Lynch's cut, he secured funding from the French company StudioCanal to shoot additional scenes and complete it as a feature film.

The film begins with images of jitterbug dancers and a smiling young blonde woman receiving applause. At night on Mulholland Drive, a dark-haired woman in an evening dress is about to be shot by her driver when another car crashes into theirs. Suffering from amnesia, she stumbles down into Los Angeles and hides in an empty apartment. The next morning she is discovered by Betty, a cheerful, optimistic young woman from Deep River, Ontario, who is staying in her aunt's apartment while pursuing an acting career. The stranger takes the name "Rita" from a poster of Rita Hayworth and remembers only that she is in danger. The two women become friends and find a large sum of money and a mysterious blue key in Rita's purse.

In parallel stories, a man at a diner describes a nightmare about a terrifying figure behind the building and collapses in shock when the figure appears. Adam Kesher, a film director, is pressured by sinister, mob-connected men to cast an unknown actress named Camilla Rhodes in his new film; when he refuses, his production is shut down and his life falls apart. Betty and Rita investigate Rita's identity, a search that leads them to an apartment where they find a decomposing body, and the two women fall in love. After a late-night visit to an eerie theater called Club Silencio, a blue box opened by the key transforms the story, and the film shifts into a darker reality in which the characters reappear in different roles, revealing a tale of ambition, jealousy, failure and despair in Hollywood.

Mulholland Drive initially divided some viewers with its puzzling structure but received wide critical acclaim. Lynch shared the Best Director award at the Cannes Film Festival and was nominated for the Academy Award for Best Director. The film launched Watts's career and has since been named in critics' polls as one of the greatest films of the 21st century.

documents.title: The Leopard
documents.tagline: Luchino Visconti's enduring romantic adventure
documents.overview: As Garibaldi's troops begin the unification of Italy in the 1860s, an aristocratic Sicilian family grudgingly adapts to the sweeping social changes undermining their way of life. Proud but pragmatic Prince Don Fabrizio Salina allows his war hero nephew, Tancredi, to marry Angelica, the beautiful daughter of gauche, bourgeois Don Calogero, in order to maintain the family's accustomed level of comfort and political clout.
documents.plot:
The Leopard (Italian: Il Gattopardo) is a 1963 epic historical drama directed by Luchino Visconti and adapted from Giuseppe Tomasi di Lampedusa's 1958 novel. Burt Lancaster stars as Don Fabrizio Corbera, Prince of Salina, with Alain Delon as his ambitious nephew Tancredi and Claudia Cardinale as Angelica. Paolo Stoppa plays Don Calogero Sedara. It was an Italian-French co-production between Titanus and Pathé.

In Sicily in 1860, as Garibaldi's redshirts fight the Bourbon king Francis II, the Prince tolerates his rebel nephew Tancredi with wry affection. After Garibaldi's forces take Palermo, the Prince reflects that change is inevitable: the middle class will replace the old ruling class, even if on the surface everything stays the same. He retreats to his summer palace at Donnafugata, where a plebiscite on unification passes unanimously, helped by the corruption of the town's leading citizen, Calogero. Calogero's beautiful daughter Angelica captivates both the Prince and Tancredi. Knowing Tancredi needs Calogero's money, the Prince blesses their engagement. When Tancredi switches from Garibaldi's army to the new royal army of Victor Emmanuel, the Prince recognizes him as the kind of opportunist who will thrive in the new Italy.

An envoy, Chevalley, invites the Prince to sit in the senate of the new Kingdom of Italy. He declines, saying Sicilians are too proud of their ancient heritage to want modernity, and predicts that the leopards and lions of his class will be replaced by jackals and hyenas. He suggests Calogero instead. At a lavish ball that marks Angelica's entry into high society, the melancholy Prince wanders through the rooms, disillusioned with the nouveau riche, until Angelica invites him to dance. For a moment he regains the grace of his youth, but his disenchantment soon returns. At dawn he walks home alone, pausing as a priest hurries by to give last rites, and disappears into a dark alley, a symbol of the fading past to which he belongs.

The Leopard won the Palme d'Or at the 1963 Cannes Film Festival and opened in Italy on March 28, 1963. It succeeded in Europe, but the shortened, English-dubbed version Fox released in the United States was panned by most American critics. The restored 185-minute version reached American theaters in 1983 to warm reviews, with Pauline Kael calling it intelligent and rapturous. It is now widely regarded as one of the greatest films ever made,.

documents.title: Whale Rider
documents.tagline: In the ways of the ancients she found a hope for the future.
documents.overview: On the east coast of New Zealand, the Whangara people believe their presence there dates back a thousand years or more to a single ancestor, Paikea, who escaped death when his canoe capsized by riding to shore on the back of a whale. From then on, Whangara chiefs, always the first-born, always male, have been considered Paikea's direct descendants. Pai, an 11-year-old girl in a patriarchal New Zealand tribe, believes she is destined to be the new chief. But her grandfather Koro is bound by tradition to pick a male leader. Pai loves Koro more than anyone in the world, but she must fight him and a thousand years of tradition to fulfill her destiny.
documents.plot:
The film's plot follows the story of Paikea Apirana (Pai for short). In her village, the leader is traditionally a first-born son, a direct patrilineal descendant of Paikea, the Whale Rider who rode on top of a whale from Hawaiki. Pai is originally born a twin, but her twin brother and her mother died during childbirth. Pai is female and so technically cannot inherit the leadership. While her grandfather, Koro, later forms an affectionate bond with his granddaughter, carrying her to school every day on his bicycle, he also condemns and resents her for conflicts within the tribe.
After the death of his wife and despite overwhelming pressure from Koro, Pai's father refuses to assume traditional leadership or finish the waka that he had started building for the baby son; instead, he moves to Germany to pursue a career as an artist. At one point, Paikea decides to live with her father because her grandfather says he doesn't want her. However, as they are driving away, she finds that she cannot bear to leave the sea as the whale seems to be calling her back. Pai tells her father to return her home.
Koro leads a cultural school for the village's first-born boys, hoping to find a new leader. He teaches the boys to use a taiaha (fighting stick), which is traditionally reserved for males. Pai is interested in the lessons, but is discouraged sternly by Koro for doing so. Pai feels that she can become the leader (although no woman has ever done so) and is determined to succeed. Her grandmother, Nanny, tells Pai that her second son, Pai's uncle, had won a taiaha tournament in his youth while he was still slim and so Pai secretly learns from him. She also secretly follows Koro's lessons. One of the students, Hemi, is also sympathetic towards her.
Koro is furious when he finds out, particularly when she wins a taiaha fight against Hemi. However, Koro's frustration turns to horror when none of the boys succeed at the traditional task of recovering a whale tooth (rei puta) that he threw into the ocean - the mission that would prove one of them worthy of becoming leader. With the loss of the rei puta, Koro (in despair) calls out the ancient ones: the whales. In an attempt to help, Pai also calls out to them and they hear her call.
One day Pai, her uncle, her uncle's girlfriend Shilo, and others take the boat to where Koro flung the rei puta into the sea. Pai confidently declares she'll find it and dives into the water. She finds the rei puta, which means that she is the rightful leader. Nanny does not think Koro is ready to accept this and does not tell him. Pai, in an attempt to bridge the rift that has formed, invites Koro to be her guest of honor at a concert of Māori chants that her school is putting on. Unknown to all, she had won an interschool speech contest with a touching dedication to Koro and the traditions of the village.

documents.title: Escape from New York
documents.tagline: 1997. New York city is now a maximum security prison. Breaking out is impossible. Breaking in is insane.
documents.overview: In the future, crime is out of control and New York City's Manhattan is a maximum security prison. Grabbing a bargaining chip right out of the air, convicts bring down the President's plane in bad old Gotham. Gruff Snake Plissken, a one-eyed lone warrior new to prison life, is coerced into bringing the President, and his cargo, out of this land of undesirables.
documents.plot: In a world ravaged by crime, the entire island of Manhattan has been converted into a walled prison where brutal prisoners roam free. After the US president crash-lands inside, war hero Snake Plissken has 24 hours to bring him back.

documents.title: The Wind That Shakes the Barley
documents.original_title: The Wind That Shakes the Barley
documents.tagline: War has cost them their innocence... Freedom will cost them their blood.
documents.overview: In 1920s Ireland young doctor Damien O'Donovan prepares to depart for a new job in a London hospital. As he says his goodbyes at a friend's farm, British Black and Tans arrive, and a young man is killed. Damien joins his brother Teddy in the Irish Republican Army, but political events are soon set in motion that tear the brothers apart.
documents.plot:
In County Cork in Ireland, in 1920, Damien O'Donovan is about to leave his native village to practice medicine in a London hospital. Meanwhile, his brother Teddy commands the local flying column of the Irish Republican Army. After a hurling match, Damien witnesses the summary execution of his friend Micheál Ó Súilleabháin, by British Black and Tans, for refusing to say his name in English and punching an officer. Although shaken, Damien rebuffs his friends' entreaties to stay in Ireland and join the IRA, saying that the war is unwinnable. As he is leaving town, Damien witnesses the British Army vainly trying to intimidate a railway employee for refusing to permit the troops to board. In response, Damien decides to stay and is sworn into Teddy's IRA brigade.
After drilling in the mountains, the column raids the village's Royal Irish Constabulary barracks to acquire more arms, then uses them to assassinate four Auxiliaries. In the aftermath, Anglo-Irish landowner Sir John Hamilton coerces one of his servants, IRA member Chris Reilly, into passing information to the British Army's Intelligence Corps. As a result, the entire brigade is arrested. In their cell, Damien meets the train driver, Dan, a union official who shares Damien's socialist views.
Meanwhile, British officers interrogate Teddy, pulling out his fingernails when he refuses to give them the names of IRA members. Johnny Gogan, a British soldier of Irish descent, helps the prisoners escape, but three are left behind. After the actions of Sir John and Chris are revealed to the IRA's intelligence network, both are taken hostage. As Teddy is still recovering, Damien is temporarily placed in command. News arrives that the three remaining IRA prisoners have been tortured and shot. Simultaneously, the brigade receives orders to "execute the spies".
Even though Chris is a lifelong friend, Damien shoots both him and Sir John. Later, the IRA ambushes and wipes out a convoy of the Auxiliary Division, though Gogan dies as the IRA's sole casualty. Shortly after, another detachment of Auxiliaries loots and burns the farmhouse of Damien's sweetheart, Cumann na mBan member Sinéad Sullivan. Sinéad is held at gunpoint while her head is roughly shorn, her scalp being wounded in the process. Later, as Damien treats her, a messenger arrives with news of a formal ceasefire between Britain and the IRA.
After the Anglo-Irish Treaty is signed, the brigade learns that a partitioned Ireland will only be granted Dominion status within the British Empire. As a result, the brigade divides over accepting the terms of the Treaty. Teddy and his allies argue that accepting the Treaty will bring peace now while further gains can be made later. Others oppose the Treaty, proposing to continue fighting until a united Irish Republic can be obtained. Dan and Damien further demand the collectivisation of industry and agriculture.

documents.title: The Prestige
documents.tagline: Are You Watching Closely?
documents.overview: A mysterious story of two magicians whose intense rivalry leads them on a life-long battle for supremacy -- full of obsession, deceit and jealousy with dangerous and deadly consequences.
documents.plot:
Note: Though the movie contains multiple flash-forwards and flash-backs throughout, the story is told here in chronological order.
In 1890s London, Robert Angier, Alfred Borden, and Angier's wife, Julia, work as magician's assistants under the mentorship of John Cutter. During a water tank trick, Julia drowns after Borden, seemingly, incorrectly ties her wrists. Angier blames Borden, and the two men become bitter rivals.
Both men pursue separate careers in magic. Borden, a gifted inventor of illusions, marries a woman named Sarah, with whom he has a daughter named Jess, and hires an enigmatic assistant, Fallon. Angier, whose strength lies more in showmanship, continues working with Cutter and takes on a new assistant, Olivia. The feud escalates as Angier and Borden visit and sabotage each other's acts. Borden loses two fingers after being shot by Angier during a pistol trick, and Borden violently thwarts Angier's bird act in front of a live audience, harming an attendee.
Borden next debuts a spectacular illusion, The Transported Man, in which he appears to teleport from one side of the stage to the other almost instantly. Angier becomes obsessed with discovering the trick's secret and, with Cutter's help, roughly recreates the act using a lookalike named Root, a failed actor. Though Angier's version is successful, he resents remaining hidden beneath the stage while Root takes the applause. Desperate to outdo Borden, he sends Olivia to spy on him. Olivia, however, falls in love with Borden and defects, though she still passes Borden's coded diary to Angier.
After Angier kidnaps Fallon, Borden reveals to Angier that the key word, TESLA, supposedly decrypts the diary and reveals his method. Seeking answers, Angier travels to Colorado Springs to meet the inventor Nikola Tesla. Believing Tesla built a teleportation device for Borden, Angier commissions Tesla to make one. Tesla eventually delivers a working machine but warns that it will bring only misery. When used, the device creates a duplicate of its subject while leaving the original person intact. In London, Angier uses the machine in a new illusion, The Real Transported Man, which earns him acclaim. Sarah, suspicious of Borden's secrecy and affair with Olivia, hangs herself.
Determined to uncover Angier's method, Borden sneaks backstage during a performance of The Real Transported Man and witnesses Angier fall into a water tank and drown. He attempts to open the tank and save Angier, but is arrested for Angier's murder, convicted, and sentenced to death. While awaiting execution, Borden is approached by a solicitor for a wealthy Lord Caldlow, who offers to care for Borden's daughter Jess in exchange for the secret behind the original Transported Man. When Caldlow visits the prison, Borden is horrified to discover that he is actually Angier. Borden passes Angier a note revealing the secret, but Angier tears it up, leaving him to hang.

documents.title: Dreamgirls
documents.tagline: All you have to do is dream.
documents.overview: A trio of female soul singers cross over to the pop charts in the early 1960s, facing their own personal struggles along the way.
documents.plot:
In 1962 Detroit, car salesman Curtis Taylor Jr. meets a Black girl group called "The Dreamettes", consisting of lead singer Effie White and backup singers Deena Jones and Lorrell Robinson, at an R&B amateur talent show at the Detroit Theatre. Presenting himself as their new manager, he hires them as backup singers for Chitlin' Circuit R&B star Jimmy "Thunder" Early. He soon starts his own record label, Rainbow Records, out of his Cadillac dealership, appointing Effie's brother C.C. as head songwriter. When their first single "Cadillac Car" fails after white pop group "Dave and the Sweethearts" releases a cover version, Curtis, C.C., and their producer Wayne turn to payola to make "Jimmy Early & The Dreamettes" mainstream pop stars, beginning with their follow-up single "Steppin' to the Bad Side". Offstage, Effie falls in love with Curtis while the married Jimmy has an affair with Lorrell.
Jimmy's manager, Marty Madison, grows weary of Curtis' plans to make his client more pop-friendly and walks out. When Jimmy fails to connect with an all-white Miami Beach supper club audience, Curtis sends him out on the road alone, keeping The Dreamettes (whom he renames "The Dreams") behind to headline in his place. Feeling that Effie's plus size figure and distinctive, soulful voice will not attract white audiences, he appoints the slimmer, more conventionally attractive Deena as the new lead singer, as Deena's voice, although more basic and generic, is more marketable.
Aided by new songs and a new image, Curtis and C.C. transform The Dreams into a top-selling mainstream pop group. By 1965, however, Effie begins acting out, particularly when Curtis' affections also turn towards Deena. After Effie storms off during a CBS performance, Curtis decides to replace her with his secretary Michelle Morris, beginning with their 1966 New Year's Eve debut in Las Vegas as "Deena Jones & the Dreams". Effie learns she is pregnant with his child, but is fired before she can tell him. Though Effie defiantly and desperately appeals to Curtis, he, C.C., and The Dreams abandon her, forging ahead to stardom.
By 1973, Effie has become an impoverished single mother living on welfare in Detroit with her daughter Magic. To restart her music career, she appoints Marty as her manager and begins performing at a local nightclub. Meanwhile, Deena Jones & the Dreams have become superstars and Rainbow, now headquartered in Los Angeles, has become the biggest pop label in the nation. Curtis, now Deena's husband, pitches a film about Cleopatra to feature her in the title role. However, Deena clandestinely hopes the film will never be greenlit, wanting to pursue other acting gigs.
By 1974, Jimmy has become a drug addict due to Curtis's preoccupation with Deena and his rejection of Jimmy's politically charged charity single "Patience" with C.C. and Lorrell.

documents.title: Babel
documents.tagline: If You Want to be Understood...Listen
documents.overview: In Babel, a tragic incident involving an American couple in Morocco sparks a chain of events for four families in different countries throughout the world. In the struggle to overcome isolation, fear, and displacement, each character discovers that it is family that ultimately provides solace. In the remote sands of the Moroccan desert, a rifle shot rings out  detonating a chain of events that will link an American tourist couples frantic struggle to survive, two Moroccan boys involved in an accidental crime, a nanny illegally crossing into Mexico with two American children and a Japanese teen rebel whose father is sought by the police in Tokyo. Separated by clashing cultures and sprawling distances, each of these four disparate groups of people are nevertheless hurtling towards a shared destiny of isolation and grief.
documents.plot:
Babel is a 2006 psychological drama directed by Alejandro González Iñárritu and written by Guillermo Arriaga. It completes their "Death Trilogy" after Amores perros (2000) and 21 Grams (2003). The ensemble cast includes Brad Pitt, Cate Blanchett, Gael García Bernal, Kōji Yakusho, Adriana Barraza and Rinko Kikuchi. Four interlinked stories in Morocco, the United States, Mexico and Japan are told out of chronological order.

In the Moroccan desert, a goatherd buys a rifle to protect his flock from jackals and gives it to his young sons, Yussef and Ahmed. Testing its range, Yussef fires at a passing tour bus and seriously wounds Susan, an American tourist traveling with her husband, Richard. The couple are struggling after the death of their infant son. Stranded in a remote village while the other tourists demand to leave, Richard waits desperately for help. The American government calls the shooting terrorism, and Moroccan police hunt down the family. In a shootout, Ahmed is badly hurt, and Yussef surrenders, confessing to the shooting. A helicopter finally takes Susan to a hospital in Casablanca.

In San Diego, the couple's Mexican nanny, Amelia, cannot find anyone to look after their children so she can attend her son's wedding. She takes them with her across the border to a village near Tijuana. On the way back, her drunk nephew Santiago panics at the border checkpoint, speeds off and leaves Amelia and the children in the desert. Amelia goes for help and is arrested by the Border Patrol. The children are found alive, but Amelia, who has been working illegally for years, is deported.

In Tokyo, Chieko, a deaf teenager, is lonely and grieving her mother's suicide, and she seeks attention through provocative sexual behavior. Police come to ask about her father, Yasujiro. The connection is the rifle: he had given it as a gift to his hunting guide in Morocco. Chieko tries to seduce a detective, who gently turns her down, and her father finally comforts her on their balcony.

Babel competed at the 2006 Cannes Film Festival, where González Iñárritu won Best Director. It grossed $135.3 million worldwide on a $25 million budget. It won the Golden Globe for Best Motion Picture – Drama and received seven Academy Award nominations, including Best Picture and supporting actress nominations for Barraza and Kikuchi. Gustavo Santaolalla won the Oscar for Best Original Score. Roger Ebert later added it to his Great Movies list.

documents.title: The Queen
documents.tagline: Our Leaders. Ourselves.
documents.overview: The Queen is an intimate behind the scenes glimpse at the interaction between HM Elizabeth II and Prime Minister Tony Blair during their struggle, following the death of Diana, to reach a compromise between what was a private tragedy for the Royal family and the public's demand for an overt display of mourning.
documents.plot:
The Queen is a 2006 docudrama directed by Stephen Frears and written by Peter Morgan, depicting the aftermath of the death of Diana, Princess of Wales, in 1997. While the royal family treats Diana's death as a private matter, the new prime minister Tony Blair and Prince Charles side with a public demanding an official display of grief. Helen Mirren stars as Queen Elizabeth II and Michael Sheen as Blair, with James Cromwell as Prince Philip, Helen McCrory as Cherie Blair, Alex Jennings as Prince Charles, Sylvia Syms and Roger Allam.

In 1997 Blair and the Labour Party sweep to power promising reform and modernisation, and the Queen wonders whether he intends to modernise the monarchy too. Less than four months later, Diana is killed in a car crash in a Paris tunnel, raising the question of how to honour a future king's mother who is no longer a royal. The Spencer family asks for a private funeral, and the Queen, determined to shield her grieving grandsons, stays on at Balmoral, making no public gesture. When Blair calls Diana the "People's Princess", the phrase is taken up by the press, and the nation's mourning swells into vast floral tributes outside Buckingham and Kensington Palaces.

As the royal family's popularity collapses, Blair's soars. His attempts to steer the Queen are rebuffed as giving in to hysteria, and Philip shares her disdain for the public displays of sympathy, but the private secretaries to both the Queen and Prince Charles quietly encourage Blair to keep trying. Finally he tells the Queen that seventy per cent of the country thinks her conduct is damaging the monarchy and that one in four people favour abolishing it, and urges her to fly a flag at half-mast over Buckingham Palace, pay her respects in person and address the nation. Shaken, she accepts that the country has changed during her reign and returns to London with Philip. Her live televised tribute to Diana helps calm the public mood, and the family attends the funeral at Westminster Abbey. At their next meeting, the Queen reflects with Blair on what has passed and warns him that public opinion may one day turn on him just as abruptly.

The film exceeded expectations at the box office, earning $56.4 million in the United States and Canada on a $15 million budget. Critics acclaimed it, with 97% on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 91, and Mirren swept the major acting prizes, winning the Academy Award, BAFTA, Golden Globe and Screen Actors Guild Award for Best Actress.

documents.title: Rocky Balboa
documents.tagline: It ain't over 'til it's over.
documents.overview: His Wife is dead and his Son hates him but this old man still has fight in him!  When he loses a highly publicized virtual boxing match to ex-champ Rocky Balboa, reigning heavyweight titleholder Mason Dixon retaliates by challenging Rocky to a nationally televised, 10-round exhibition bout. To the surprise of his son and friends, Rocky agrees to come out of retirement and face an opponent who's faster, stronger, and thirty years his junior.
documents.plot:
Rocky Balboa is a 2006 American sports drama film directed by Sylvester Stallone, who also co-wrote and starred in the movie.

The film takes place several years after the events of the previous Rocky films. Rocky Balboa (Sylvester Stallone) has retired from boxing and is living a quiet life with his wife Adrian (Brenda Blethyn). However, when a new heavyweight champion, Mason "The Line" Dixon (Antonio Tarver), emerges, Rocky's spirit is reignited.

Mason Dixon is a formidable boxer who has been dominating the ring for years. He is also a ruthless and arrogant fighter who sees himself as above the law. When Adrian passes away, Rocky is devastated, but he finds solace in training with a young and talented boxer named Mason's protégé, Tommy Gunn (Antonio Tarver).

As Rocky trains Tommy, he begins to see a lot of himself in the young fighter. However, when Tommy becomes disillusioned with his life under Mason's guidance, he turns against Rocky and joins forces with Mason.

Rocky is heartbroken when he discovers that Tommy has betrayed him, but he refuses to give up on his friend. He decides to come out of retirement one last time to fight for the heavyweight championship of the world against Mason Dixon.

The film's plot development revolves around Rocky's journey as he trains for the big fight. Along the way, he faces numerous challenges and setbacks, including a serious injury that leaves him unable to train. Despite this, Rocky perseveres and finds new ways to push himself to his limits.

As the fight approaches, Rocky's determination and spirit inspire those around him, including Tommy, who begins to question his loyalty to Mason. In the end, Rocky faces off against Mason in an intense and emotional battle.

The film's climax features a thrilling boxing match between Rocky and Mason, which ends with Rocky emerging victorious but at great personal cost. The movie concludes with Rocky standing alone in the ring, having given everything he has to prove that he still has what it takes to be a champion.

Throughout the film, Stallone delivers a powerful performance as Rocky Balboa, bringing depth and nuance to the character. The supporting cast, including Brenda Blethyn and Antonio Tarver, also deliver strong performances that add to the film's emotional impact.

Overall, Rocky Balboa is a heartwarming and inspiring film that explores themes of redemption, perseverance, and the power of the human spirit.

documents.title: The Good Shepherd
documents.tagline: The untold story of the most powerful covert agency in the world.
documents.overview: Edward Wilson, the only witness to his father's suicide and member of the Skull and Bones Society while a student at Yale, is a morally upright young man who values honor and discretion, qualities that help him to be recruited for a career in the newly founded OSS. His dedication to his work does not come without a price though, leading him to sacrifice his ideals and eventually his family.

His dedication to his work does not come without a price though, leading him to sacrifice his ideals and eventually his family.

documents.title: Ghost Rider
documents.tagline: Hell is about to be unleashed.
documents.overview: In order to save his dying father, young stunt cyclist Johnny Blaze sells his soul to Mephistopheles and sadly parts from the pure-hearted Roxanne Simpson, the love of his life. Years later, Johnny's path crosses again with Roxanne, now a go-getting reporter, and also with Mephistopheles, who offers to release Johnny's soul if Johnny becomes the fabled, fiery 'Ghost Rider'.
documents.plot:
Ghost Rider is a supernatural action film directed by Mark Steven Johnson, released in 2007. The movie is based on the Marvel Comics character of the same name.

The story begins with Johnny Blaze (played by Nicolas Cage), a talented stunt motorcycle rider who makes a deal with the devil, Mephisto (played by Peter Fonda), to save his mentor's life. Unbeknownst to Johnny, this deal comes with a terrible price: his soul will be bound to a hellish contract that forces him to become the Ghost Rider, a supernatural entity with hellfire powers.

As the years pass, Johnny becomes a successful stuntman and motorcycle rider, but he is haunted by the ghost of his mentor, who appears to him as a warning. The ghost tells Johnny that Mephisto's deal has come due, and Johnny must fulfill his end of the bargain. However, when Johnny tries to break free from the contract, Mephisto reveals that he has taken over Johnny's soul, and Johnny is now doomed to become the Ghost Rider.

The Ghost Rider is a supernatural entity with hellfire powers, but also with a human conscience. He is forced to roam the earth, seeking out those who have committed evil deeds, and punishing them by setting their souls on fire. The Ghost Rider's appearance is that of a motorcycle-riding, hellish creature with flames for eyes.

As Johnny struggles to come to terms with his new identity as the Ghost Rider, he meets Roxanne Simpson (played by Eva Mendes), a beautiful and kind-hearted woman who becomes his love interest. However, Mephisto has other plans, and he uses Roxanne's life to lure Johnny into a trap.

The plot thickens when the Ghost Rider discovers that Mephisto is using an ancient artifact to gain control over the world. The Ghost Rider must stop Mephisto and break free from his contract before it's too late. Along the way, he teams up with a group of allies, including a mysterious woman named St. John (played by Sam Elliott) who claims to be able to help him.

The movie culminates in an epic showdown between the Ghost Rider and Mephisto, with the fate of the world hanging in the balance. In the end, Johnny is able to break free from his contract and defeat Mephisto, but not before he sacrifices himself to save Roxanne's soul.

In a surprising twist, it is revealed that St. John was actually a manifestation of Johnny's own subconscious, created by his guilt and regret over his deal with Mephisto. The movie ends with Roxanne finding the Ghost Rider's motorcycle, which has been left behind as a symbol of their love and connection.

Overall, Ghost Rider is an action-packed supernatural thriller that explores themes of redemption, sacrifice, and the power of love. While it received mixed reviews from critics, the movie has developed a cult following over the years, and its unique blend of horror and action has made it a fan favorite among comic book enthusiasts.

documents.title: Letters from Iwo Jima
documents.tagline: The battle of Iwo Jima seen through the eyes of the Japanese soldiers.
documents.overview: The story of the battle of Iwo Jima between the United States and Imperial Japan during World War II, as told from the perspective of the Japanese who fought it.
documents.plot:
Letters from Iwo Jima is a 2006 American war film in Japanese, directed and co-produced by Clint Eastwood and starring Ken Watanabe and Kazunari Ninomiya. It depicts the Battle of Iwo Jima from the Japanese side and serves as a companion to Eastwood's Flags of Our Fathers, which shows the same battle from the American viewpoint; the two were shot back to back.

In 2005, archaeologists on Iwo Jima dig up something buried. In 1944, Private First Class Saigo, a conscripted baker who longs for his family, is digging beach trenches when Lieutenant General Tadamichi Kuribayashi takes command of the garrison. Kuribayashi spares Saigo a beating for unpatriotic remarks and orders a network of tunnels and mountain bunkers, a strategy that he and Lieutenant Colonel Baron Nishi, an Olympic champion equestrian, defend against other officers. Dysentery spreads, and Saigo suspects a new arrival, Shimizu, of being a military police spy.

After days of bombardment, U.S. Marines land and assault Mount Suribachi. Ordered by his colonel to commit suicide rather than retreat, Saigo persuades Shimizu to flee with him, and Lieutenant Ito nearly executes them for cowardice until Kuribayashi confirms that he ordered the retreat. Ito leads a failed attack against orders and, rebuked by Nishi, sets off with land mines intending to throw himself under an American tank. Nishi reads aloud a letter found on a dying Marine, and later, blinded by shrapnel, orders a withdrawal and kills himself. Shimizu surrenders but is executed by his captors. Kuribayashi orders Saigo to stay behind and destroy documents, saving his life for a third time, then leads a final night attack in which he is gravely wounded. Ito, who never carried out his mission, is captured. When his aide is shot, Kuribayashi asks Saigo to bury him where he cannot be found and shoots himself with a pistol given to him in the United States before the war. When Saigo sees a Marine carrying that pistol he attacks, but is subdued and taken to the beach with the wounded. In the present, the archaeologists open the bag of letters Saigo had buried, and the soldiers' voices are heard.

Filmed mainly in California and Iceland, it opened in Japan on December 9, 2006, and in the United States on December 20 through Warner Bros. It was acclaimed, scoring 91% on Rotten Tomatoes and 89 on Metacritic, grossed $68.7 million on a $19 million budget, and earned four Academy Award nominations, including Best Picture, winning Best Sound Editing.

documents.title: Breaking and Entering
documents.overview: Set in a blighted, inner-city neighbourhood of London, Breaking and Entering examines an affair which unfolds between a successful British landscape architect and Amira, a Bosnian woman – the mother of a troubled teen son – who was widowed by the war in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

documents.title: The Host
documents.tagline: Monsters are real.
documents.overview: Following the dumping of gallons of toxic waste in the river, a giant mutated squid-like creature appears and begins attacking the populace. Gang-du's daughter Hyun-seo is snatched up by the creature; with his family to assist him, he sets off to find her.
documents.plot: A teenage girl is captured by a giant mutated squid-like creature that appears from Seoul's Han River after toxic waste was dumped in it, prompting her family into a frantic search for her.

documents.title: Because I Said So
documents.tagline: She's just your normal, overprotective, overbearing, over-the-top mother.
documents.overview: In an effort to prevent family history from repeating itself, meddlesome mom Daphne Wilder attempts to set up her youngest daughter, Milly, with Mr. Right. Meanwhile, her other daughters try to keep their mom's good intentions under control.
documents.plot: In an effort to prevent family history from repeating itself, meddlesome mom Daphne Wilder attempts to set up her youngest daughter, Milly, with Mr. Right. Meanwhile, her other daughters try to keep their mom's good intentions under control.

documents.title: Notes on a Scandal
documents.tagline: One woman's secret is another woman's power. One woman's fear is another woman's weapon. One woman's life is in another woman's hands....
documents.overview: A veteran high school teacher befriends a younger art teacher, who is having an affair with one of her 15-year-old students. However, her intentions with this new "friend" also go well beyond platonic friendship.
documents.plot:
Barbara Covett is a history teacher at a comprehensive school in London. She is unpopular with the students and her fellow teachers, for whom she has contempt. Having never married and nearing retirement, her only comfort is her diary. When a new art teacher, Sheba Hart, joins the staff, Barbara is immediately attracted to her and they strike up a friendship. In Barbara, this friendship quickly turns into infatuation and obsession. Sheba is married to the much older Richard, and is just re-entering the work force after devoting herself to her special needs son.
Barbara later witnesses Sheba in a sexual encounter with a 15-year-old student named Steven Connolly at the school. When Barbara confronts her, Sheba recounts all the details of her involvement with the boy, but asks Barbara not to tell the school administration until after Christmas, as she wants to be with her family. Barbara claims she has no intention of reporting her, providing Sheba ends the relationship immediately, but Barbara secretly plans to use the affair as a means of manipulating Sheba. Over the Christmas break, Barbara visits her sister, who asks her about another young teacher Barbara befriended. Barbara stiffly says that the young teacher moved away. Barbara's sister asks if she has any other female "friends", strongly implying Barbara is a lesbian; Barbara insists she has no idea what her sister is talking about.
Sheba tells Steven that the affair is over, yet finds herself unable to stop seeing him. However, when she refuses to give in to Barbara's increasing demands on her time and attention, Barbara reveals the secret to a male teacher who has told her that he is attracted to Sheba. The teacher informs the student's parents and the school. After the affair becomes public, the headmaster accuses Barbara of knowing about the affair and not notifying the authorities. He also learns that a former teacher at the school, the young woman Barbara mentioned at Christmas, had taken out a restraining order against Barbara for stalking her and her fiancé. Sheba is fired and Barbara is forced into early retirement by the headmaster.
Sheba's husband asks her to move out of their home, so she moves into Barbara's house, unaware that Barbara is the reason she was found out and believing the affair became known because Steven confessed it to his mother. When Sheba discovers Barbara's diary and learns it was Barbara who leaked the story of the affair, she confronts Barbara and strikes her in anger. A row ensues, and Sheba runs outside to a crowd of reporters and photographers. When she becomes hemmed in by them, Barbara rescues her.
Sheba's emotions spent, she quietly tells Barbara that she had initiated the friendship with her because she liked her and that they could have been friends. Barbara says, "I need more than a friend." Sheba leaves Barbara, placing the journal on the table as a mute reminder that she had kept its contents secret, and returns to her husband.

documents.title: Bridge to Terabithia
documents.tagline: Close your eyes, but keep your mind wide open.
documents.overview: Jesse Aarons trained all summer to become the fastest runner in school, so he's very upset when newcomer Leslie Burke outruns him and everyone else. Despite this and other differences, including that she's rich, he's poor, and she's a city girl, he's a country boy, the two become fast friends. Together, they create Terabithia, a land of monsters, trolls, ogres, and giants and rule as king and queen.
documents.plot:
Bridge to Terabithia is a heart-wrenching drama film released in 2007, directed by Gábor Csupó and produced by Walt Disney Pictures. The movie is based on the novel of the same name by Katherine Paterson.

The story revolves around two young friends, Jesse Oliver Aarons (played by Josh Hutcherson) and Leslie Burke (played by AnnaSophia Robb), who live in rural Virginia. Jesse is an 11-year-old boy who loves to draw and paint, while Leslie is a new student in his class who has recently moved to the area with her family.

Initially, Jesse is hesitant to befriend Leslie due to his fear of rejection and his desire to fit in with his peers. However, after they meet on the first day of school, they quickly form an unlikely friendship. They discover that they share a love for fantasy and imagination, which leads them to create their own magical kingdom called Terabithia.

Terabithia is a fantastical world built by Jesse and Leslie in the woods near their homes. It's a place where they can escape the troubles of their everyday lives and be themselves without fear of judgment. The kingdom is filled with imagination, creativity, and adventure, and it becomes a sanctuary for both Jesse and Leslie.

As the story progresses, we see Jesse and Leslie grow closer, sharing their deepest secrets and fears with each other. They find comfort in each other's company, and their friendship deepens. However, their happiness is short-lived, as tragedy strikes when Leslie dies in an accident while they are playing in Terabithia.

The film takes a poignant turn as Jesse struggles to cope with the loss of his dear friend. He becomes withdrawn and isolated, unable to paint or create anything without feeling Leslie's presence. The movie shows how grief can be overwhelming, and how it can affect even the strongest relationships.

In the end, Jesse finds a way to honor Leslie's memory by creating a bridge in Terabithia, symbolizing the connection between their two worlds. The film concludes with Jesse standing on the bridge, looking out at the woods where he and Leslie shared so many adventures together.

Bridge to Terabithia is a powerful and emotional film that explores themes of friendship, loss, and the importance of imagination in our lives. The movie features outstanding performances from Josh Hutcherson and AnnaSophia Robb, who bring depth and nuance to their characters. The film's cinematography and score are also noteworthy, capturing the beauty and wonder of Terabithia.

Overall, Bridge to Terabithia is a heart-wrenching drama that will leave audiences moved and contemplative long after the credits roll.

documents.title: Street Kings
documents.tagline: Their city. Their rules. No prisoners.
documents.overview: Tom Ludlow is a disillusioned L.A. Police Officer, rarely playing by the rules and haunted by the death of his wife. When evidence implicates him in the execution of a fellow officer, he is forced to go up against the cop culture he's been a part of his entire career, ultimately leading him to question the loyalties of everyone around him.
documents.plot:
Thomas "Tom" Ludlow, an alcoholic undercover detective for the LAPD's Vice-Special unit, arranges an arms deal with Korean gangsters suspected of kidnapping two teenage girls. He provokes the gangsters into beating him and stealing his car, allowing him to track them to the gang's hideout. Ludlow storms the hideout and kills the gangsters, staging the scene to make the shootings appear justified, and rescues the captive girls.
While Captain Jack Wander and the rest of his unit congratulate him, Ludlow is confronted by his former partner, Terrence Washington, who disapproves of the unit's corrupt tactics. Ludlow is later approached by Captain James Biggs of Internal Affairs. Wander warns that Washington has reported Ludlow to Biggs.
Ludlow follows Washington to a convenience store, where they are ambushed by two gunmen under the pretense of a robbery. Accidentally shot when Ludlow returns fire, Washington is killed by the gunmen. The clerk is killed as well. Wander advises Ludlow to remove the surveillance footage, telling the press Ludlow was first on the scene but too late to save Washington. Temporarily reassigned to fielding civilian complaints, Ludlow enlists the cooperation of investigator Paul Diskant, determined to find the killers himself. Washington is implicated in stealing drugs from the evidence room and selling them to the gunmen, identified as criminals Fremont and Coates.
Joined by a reluctant Diskant, Ludlow brutalizes informants until local drug dealer Scribble leads them to the bodies of the real Fremont and Coates in a shallow grave, killed long before Washington. Giving the surveillance footage to Washington's widow, Linda, Ludlow reveals that he lost his own wife recently and vows to avenge Washington.
Ludlow and Diskant pose as dirty cops, forcing Scribble to arrange a meeting with the killers masquerading as Fremont and Coates. Diskant recognizes them, but he and Scribble are killed in the ensuing gunfight. Ludlow kills both assailants, but sees on the news that they were Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department deputies.
Declared a "cop killer", Ludlow is arrested by fellow detectives Santos and Demille, who admit to killing the real Fremont and Coates and planting evidence to frame them for Washington's murder. He realizes that Washington was actually informing on Wander, who is the one behind the evidence room theft. Before Santos and Demille can execute him, Ludlow manages to break free and kill both of them. He saves Linda from Sergeant Mike Clady, sent by Wander to recover the surveillance footage and kill her, subduing him and locking him in his trunk.
Ludlow confronts Wander at home, handcuffing him after a brawl. Wander confesses that he has incriminating evidence against high-ranking officials to use to become LAPD chief and, eventually, mayor.

documents.title: Meet the Robinsons
documents.tagline: Think your family's weird?
documents.overview: Lewis, a brilliant young inventor, is keen on creating a time machine to find his mother, who abandoned him in an orphanage. Things take a turn when he meets Wilbur Robinson and his family.
documents.plot:
Meet the Robinsons is a 2007 American animated science fiction comedy film produced by Walt Disney Pictures. The movie follows the story of Lewis, an orphan boy who dreams of becoming a great inventor.

The film begins with Lewis, a shy and awkward 12-year-old boy, living in an orphanage. He spends most of his time daydreaming about inventing incredible gadgets and machines that will change the world. However, his life takes a dramatic turn when he meets Wilbur, a mysterious and eccentric old man who claims to be his long-lost father.

Wilbur reveals to Lewis that he is actually the son of a brilliant inventor named Cornelius Robinson, who created a time machine called the "Time Machine 3000." The Time Machine 3000 allows its user to travel through time, but it also has a mind of its own and can be unpredictable. Wilbur warns Lewis that his father's inventions have been stolen by a rival inventor named Bowler Hat Guy, who is using them for evil purposes.

Lewis decides to embark on a journey with Wilbur to find Cornelius Robinson and retrieve the stolen inventions. Along the way, they meet a cast of eccentric characters, including Wilbur's wife, Mrs. Robinson, and their son, Lewis Jr., who becomes Lewis's rival in inventing.

As they travel through time, Lewis and his companions encounter various historical figures, including Leonardo da Vinci, Benjamin Franklin, and Albert Einstein. However, Bowler Hat Guy is always one step ahead, using the stolen inventions to alter historical events for his own gain.

The plot thickens as Lewis and his friends discover that Bowler Hat Guy's ultimate plan is to steal Cornelius Robinson's most prized invention: a machine that can create an army of robotic clones. The movie builds up to a thrilling climax as Lewis and his companions must stop Bowler Hat Guy and his minions from carrying out their evil plan.

In the end, Lewis and his friends succeed in defeating Bowler Hat Guy and restoring the timeline to its original course. Along the way, Lewis learns valuable lessons about perseverance, teamwork, and believing in himself. The movie ends with Lewis returning to the present, where he is reunited with Wilbur and becomes a confident inventor in his own right.

Throughout the film, the animation is vibrant and colorful, with a unique blend of steampunk and sci-fi elements. The characters are well-developed and quirky, adding to the movie's humor and charm. Meet the Robinsons is a heartwarming and entertaining film that celebrates the power of imagination and creativity.

documents.title: Mr. Bean's Holiday
documents.tagline: Disaster is just a small step away.
documents.overview: Mr. Bean wins a trip to Cannes where he unwittingly separates a young boy from his father and must help the two reunite. On the way he discovers France, bicycling and true love, among other things.
documents.plot:
Mr. Bean's Holiday is a 2007 comedy film directed by Steve Bendelack and produced by Universal Pictures. The movie marks the fourth installment in the Mr. Bean series, following Bean (1997) and Mr. Bean's Diner (2002), which was initially intended to be a television special but was later expanded into a feature film.

The story begins with Mr. Bean (played by Rowan Atkinson), a bumbling and eccentric British gentleman, who is on his way to Paris for a vacation. However, he soon discovers that the flight has been cancelled due to bad weather, leaving him stranded in Nice, France.

In an attempt to find a new flight to London, Mr. Bean decides to embark on a road trip across Europe with his trusty companion, Teddy (a small stuffed teddy bear). Along the way, they encounter various misadventures and cultural differences that lead to comedic misunderstandings.

As they travel through France, Italy, Austria, and Germany, Mr. Bean becomes fascinated by the idea of making it to the famous film festival in Cannes, where he hopes to meet his idol, a French actress named Fanny (played by Emma de Caunes). Believing that attending the festival will bring him fame and fortune, Mr. Bean sets out on a series of misadventures to get there.

Throughout their journey, Mr. Bean's antics cause chaos and confusion wherever they go. He gets into a series of humorous misadventures, including accidentally joining a group of Italian tourists, getting caught up in a wild goose chase through the streets of Nice, and even inadvertently causing a scene at a German beer festival.

Despite the many mishaps, Mr. Bean's determination to reach Cannes never wavers, and he eventually makes it to the film festival, where he meets Fanny and wins her heart. The movie ends with Mr. Bean returning home to London, but not before sharing a romantic moment with Fanny on the plane ride back.

Throughout the film, Rowan Atkinson's physical comedy and facial expressions provide much of the humor, as well as his ability to convey emotions without speaking. The supporting cast, including Emma de Caunes and Max Baldry, add to the comedic mayhem, making Mr. Bean's Holiday a delightful and entertaining ride for audiences.

Overall, Mr. Bean's Holiday is a lighthearted and entertaining film that showcases the beloved character's signature blend of physical comedy and wit. With its colorful European landscapes and hilarious misadventures, it's a must-see for fans of the series and comedy enthusiasts alike.

documents.tagline: Spartans, prepare for glory!
documents.overview: Based on Frank Miller's graphic novel, "300" is very loosely based the 480 B.C. Battle of Thermopylae, where the King of Sparta led his army against the advancing Persians; the battle is said to have inspired all of Greece to band together against the Persians, and helped usher in the world's first democracy.
documents.plot:
In the year 480 BCE, during the Persian Empire's invasion of Greece, King Leonidas of Sparta is faced with an impossible decision: defend his city-state against the invading forces or flee and save his people.

The film opens with a prologue that sets the stage for the story. The Spartans are preparing to face the invading army, led by King Xerxes I (Rodrigo Santoro). Leonidas (Gerard Butler) is chosen to lead a small contingent of 300 Spartans against the Persian army, which is estimated to be in the hundreds of thousands.

As the battle begins, the Spartans hold their ground against the seemingly endless horde of Persians. The film's iconic "This is Sparta!" speech by King Leonidas sets the tone for the rest of the battle. Despite being vastly outnumbered, the Spartans fight with bravery and honor, using their phalanx formation to devastating effect.

Meanwhile, Queen Gorgo (Lena Headey), Leonidas' wife, tries to persuade him to reconsider his decision to lead the 300 against the Persians. She is worried about the fate of her husband and the future of Sparta.

As the battle rages on, the Spartans begin to tire. Many are killed or wounded, including several high-ranking officers. However, Leonidas remains steadfast, refusing to yield even when faced with the prospect of defeat.

The turning point of the film comes when a group of Persian warriors, led by King Xerxes' son, Xerxes II (Toby Kebbell), infiltrate the Spartan lines and kill several key officers. This allows the Persians to gain the upper hand, and it seems that all is lost for the Spartans.

However, in a stunning display of bravery and sacrifice, the 300 Spartans launch a final, desperate attack against the Persians. The film's climax features an intense and bloody battle, with the Spartans fighting valiantly against overwhelming odds.

In the end, the Spartans emerge victorious, but at great cost. King Leonidas is killed in action, and many of his men are either killed or taken prisoner. The film ends with a somber tone, as Queen Gorgo mourns the loss of her husband and the future of Sparta hangs in the balance.

Throughout the film, director Zack Snyder's use of innovative camera techniques and stunning visuals brings the epic battle to life. The film's score, composed by Tyler Bates, adds to the sense of tension and drama, perfectly capturing the mood of the film.

Overall, 300 is a gripping and intense film that explores themes of honor, duty, and sacrifice. Despite its historical inaccuracies, the film remains an exciting and visually stunning adaptation of Frank Miller's graphic novel.

documents.title: Sunshine
documents.tagline: If the sun dies, so do we.
documents.overview: Fifty years into the future, the sun is dying, and Earth is threatened by arctic temperatures. A team of astronauts is sent to revive the Sun — but the mission fails. Seven years later, a new team is sent to finish the mission as mankind’s last hope.

documents.title: TMNT
documents.tagline: A Whole New Breed of Heroes.
documents.overview: After the defeat of their old arch nemesis, The Shredder, the Turtles have grown apart as a family. Struggling to keep them together, their rat sensei, Splinter, becomes worried when strange things begin to brew in New York City.
