documents.title: All the King's Men
documents.tagline: Some people will do anything to gain power. Some will do anything to keep it.
documents.overview: The story of an idealist's rise to power in the world of Louisiana politics and the corruption that leads to his ultimate downfall. Based on the1946 Pulitzer Prize-winning novel written by Robert Penn Warren, loosely based on the story of real-life politician Huey Long.
documents.plot:
Jack Burden, a Louisianan news reporter, takes a personal interest in Willie Stark, an idealistic small-town lawyer and parish treasurer. Circumstances develop that result in Tiny Duffy, a local political leader Burden knows, urging Stark to run for governor. Burden's upbringing makes him familiar with the undercurrent of politics – he was raised by his loving godfather Judge Irwin, a former state attorney general, while his good friend, Dr. Adam Stanton, and his sister Anne Stanton—also Burden's former lover—are the children of a former governor. Burden therefore decides to take Duffy's advice and travels as a reporter on Stark's campaign for governor.
The politically astute Burden soon deduces, and Duffy's strategist (and Stark's mistress), Sadie Burke, confirms that Duffy is using Stark to split his party's vote and thus allow the opposing party to win. They tell Stark, who begins to give speeches in a straightforward manner to appeal to the public, in defiance of the advice given to him by Duffy. His vigorous strategy attacks the corruption of the existing players and promises schools and roads for his "fellow ignorant hicks", resulting in Stark winning the election. He manages Duffy by making him his lieutenant governor. Stark recruits Burden to work for him as an adviser.
Stark proves to be a very persuasive governor, delivering on many of his new projects. Irwin disapproves of Stark and publicly supports an investigation of possible graft in the new spending. Burden points out that graft is the elite's word for what the previous politicians had always done, while Stark openly tells his crowds that his "crooks, unlike theirs, are itty bitty" compared to the elite's. Stark convinces Stanton to head a new public hospital while he begins having an affair with Anne, provoking Burke's jealousy and Burden's disappointment.
Irwin continues criticizing Stark as political controversies begin to unfold. Stark demands that Burden seek information on the judge to be used against him. Jack insists that there is no such information, but eventually discovers evidence of a bribe that Irwin used to get his appointment many years prior, leading an opponent to commit suicide. Following this revelation, Irwin himself commits suicide. Burden's mother then tells him that Irwin treated him with such love because he was his biological father, which causes a great amount of guilt for Burden.
Stark uses many methods of corruption to consolidate his power, including patronage and intimidation. Adam is told that Stark is using the hospital project to rob the state and is framing him in the process. Burden and Anne both assure Adam that this is false. Adam also becomes enraged when he learns of Stark's affair with his sister. Adam waits at the state capitol and assassinates Stark, only to be immediately killed by the governor's bodyguard. It is later revealed that Adam was influenced by Duffy and Burke to murder Stark, allowing Duffy to succeed Stark as governor.

documents.title: Captain Corelli's Mandolin
documents.overview: When a fisherman leaves to fight with the Greek army during World War II, his fiancée falls in love with the local Italian commander.
documents.plot:
Greece's Ionian Islands are occupied by the Italian Army when it brings a large garrison along with a few Germans to the tranquil island of Cephalonia, whose inhabitants surrender immediately. Captain Antonio Corelli, an officer of the Italian 33rd Acqui Infantry Division, has a jovial personality and a passion for the mandolin and trains his battery of men (who have never fired a shot) to choral sing. Initially, he alienates a number of villagers, including Pelagia, the daughter of the village doctor. She is an educated and strong-willed woman. At first offended by the Italian soldier's behaviour, she slowly warms to Corelli's charm, and mandolin playing, as they are forced to share her father's home after the doctor agrees to put him up in exchange for medical supplies.
When Pelagia's fiancé, Mandras, a local fisherman, heads off to war on the mainland, the friendship between Antonio and Pelagia grows. Her beauty and intelligence have captured Corelli's heart, and his fondness for the village's vibrant community has caused him to question his reasons for fighting. Corelli and his battery of musical troops become a part of the villagers' lives, but the moment is fleeting. As the war draws closer, Antonio and Pelagia are forced to choose between their allegiances and love for one another.
The Italian government surrenders to the Allies, and the Italian troops happily prepare to return home. However, their erstwhile allies, the Germans, insist on disarming them, intemperately and violently. The Greeks are also exposed to the brutality of the incoming Germans and arrange with the Italians to use their arms in a brief but futile resistance. For this, the German High Command has thousands of Italian troops shot as traitors. Corelli survives when one of his soldiers shields him from the fusillade of the German executioners' bullets with his body and falls dead on top of him. Mandras finds Corelli, still alive among the pile of massacred soldiers and takes him to Pelagia and the doctor for treatment and recovery, and then to a boat to escape the island. As a result of Pelagia's questioning, Mandras admits that he rescued Corelli from the heap of dead soldiers because he wanted to rekindle their love. But it does no good and tears the couple part. Earlier, on one of Mandras's return visits to Cephallonia, he admits to Pelagia that he never replied to her many love letters because he is illiterate.
In 1947, Pelagia receives a parcel from Italy containing a record of the tune Corelli wrote for her, but no note. An earthquake destroys much of the village including the doctor's house, but island life continues, and, soon after, Corelli returns to Pelagia.

documents.title: The Incredible Hulk
documents.tagline: You'll like him when he's angry.
documents.overview: Scientist Bruce Banner scours the planet for an antidote to the unbridled force of rage within him: the Hulk. But when the military masterminds who dream of exploiting his powers force him back to civilization, he finds himself coming face to face with a new, deadly foe.
documents.plot:
At Culver University in Virginia, U.S. military general Thaddeus Ross meets with Dr. Bruce Banner, the colleague and boyfriend of his daughter Betty, regarding an experiment that Ross claims is meant to make humans immune to gamma radiation. This is part of Ross's attempts to recreate a World War II-era "super soldier" program. The experiment fails, and Banner is exposed to high levels of gamma radiation, causing him to transform into the Hulk if enraged or if his heart rate rises above 200 beats per minute. The Hulk destroys the lab and injures the general, Betty, and others outside. Banner becomes a fugitive from Ross, who wants to weaponize the Hulk.
Five years later, Banner works at a bottling factory in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, and has not transformed in five months. He trains in yoga and breathing techniques while collaborating anonymously with an internet user called "Mr. Blue" in his search to cure his condition. After Banner accidentally cuts his finger, a drop of his blood falls into a bottle of soda, which is eventually ingested by an elderly consumer in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, giving him gamma sickness. Using the bottle to track Banner, Ross sends a special forces team led by Emil Blonsky to capture him. Banner transforms into the Hulk and defeats Blonsky's team, though Blonsky survives. After Ross explains how Banner became the Hulk, Blonsky agrees to be injected with a similar serum, gaining enhanced speed, strength, and agility.
Banner returns to Culver University and reunites with Betty. Her new boyfriend, Dr. Leonard Samson, contacts Ross, who soon arrives with his forces and Blonsky. They attack Banner at the university, and he transforms into the Hulk again. Blonsky, whose judgment is impaired by the serum, attacks and mocks the Hulk. The Hulk severely injures Blonsky, but the serum allows him to heal quickly. Betty is almost killed by military fire and is saved by the Hulk, who flees with Betty and eventually reverts to Banner. The pair go on the run, and Banner contacts Mr. Blue, who urges them to meet him in New York City. Mr. Blue is cellular biologist Dr. Samuel Sterns, who has developed a possible antidote to Banner's condition. After a seemingly successful test, he warns Banner that the antidote may only reverse an initial transformation. Sterns reveals that he has synthesized Banner's blood samples, which Banner sent from Brazil, into a large supply, and wants to apply its "limitless potential" to medicine. Fearful of the Hulk's power falling into the wrong hands, Banner wants to destroy the supply.
Blonsky and Ross's forces take Banner into custody. As Banner and Betty are taken away in a helicopter, Blonsky stays behind and orders Sterns to inject him with Banner's blood, as he covets the Hulk's power. The experiment mutates Blonsky into the Abomination, a monstrous creature that surpasses the Hulk in size and strength.

documents.title: Iron Man
documents.tagline: Heroes aren't born. They're built.
documents.overview: After being held captive in an Afghan cave, billionaire engineer Tony Stark creates a unique weaponized suit of armor to fight evil.
documents.plot:
Iron Man is a 2008 superhero film directed by Jon Favreau, based on the Marvel Comics character of the same name. The movie follows the story of Tony Stark, a billionaire inventor and industrialist who becomes the armored superhero Iron Man.

The film begins with Tony Stark (played by Robert Downey Jr.) as a brilliant engineer working for Stark Industries, a company that develops advanced military technology. While demonstrating his latest missile system in Afghanistan, Stark is kidnapped by a terrorist group led by Obadiah Stane (played by Jeff Bridges). The terrorists demand that Stark build a Jericho missile system for them, but instead, he secretly builds a powered exoskeleton suit to escape.

Stark successfully escapes and returns to the United States, where he perfects his suit. He also begins to question the ethics of his company's military contracts and the true intentions of his business partner, Obadiah Stane. Meanwhile, Stark's assistant, Pepper Potts (played by Gwyneth Paltrow), tries to help him deal with the emotional trauma of his captivity.

As Stark continues to work on his suit, he also begins to develop a sense of responsibility and purpose. He decides to use his technology to create a superhero alter ego, Iron Man, who will fight against injustice and protect the innocent. With the help of his friend James "Rhodey" Rhodes (played by Terrence Howard), Stark perfects the suit's design and capabilities.

However, Stane becomes increasingly jealous of Stark's success and begins to secretly work on a rival suit of his own. As Iron Man's popularity grows, so does Stane's resentment, leading him to become a villainous mastermind. In a climactic battle, Iron Man faces off against Stane, who has become the armored villain, Iron Monger.

The final confrontation between Iron Man and Iron Monger ends with Stark defeating his former business partner and destroying his suit. However, in the process, Stark is severely injured and left for dead. Pepper Potts finds him and nurses him back to health, while also helping him to come to terms with the consequences of his actions.

The movie concludes with Tony Stark reflecting on his experiences as Iron Man and realizing that he has a responsibility to use his powers for good. The film ends with Stark's iconic line, "I am Iron Man," as he looks out at the city skyline, ready to face new challenges as the armored superhero.

Overall, Iron Man is a thrilling and action-packed movie that explores themes of identity, power, and responsibility. Robert Downey Jr.'s performance as Tony Stark/Iron Man is widely praised for its wit, charm, and depth, setting the stage for the Marvel Cinematic Universe's iconic character.

documents.title: The Forbidden Kingdom
documents.tagline: The battle for eternity is the fantasy of a lifetime.
documents.overview: An American teenager who is obsessed with Hong Kong cinema and kung-fu classics makes an extraordinary discovery in a Chinatown pawnshop: the legendary stick weapon of the Chinese sage and warrior, the Monkey King. With the lost relic in hand, the teenager unexpectedly finds himself travelling back to ancient China to join a crew of warriors from martial arts lore on a dangerous quest to free the imprisoned Monkey King.
documents.plot:
The Forbidden Kingdom is a fantasy wuxia film of 2008 directed by Rob Minkoff and written by John Fusco, loosely inspired by the 16th-century Chinese novel Journey to the West. Michael Angarano plays Jason Tripitikas, an American teenager, while Chan plays the drunken scholar Lu Yan and the shopkeeper Old Hop, and Li plays the Silent Monk and the Monkey King, Sun Wukong. Liu Yifei plays Golden Sparrow, Li Bingbing plays the White-Haired Witch Ni Chang and Collin Chou plays the Jade Warlord.

In South Boston, Jason, a fan of martial arts films, dreams of the Monkey King battling celestial soldiers in the clouds. At a Chinatown pawn shop he spots a golden staff like the one in his dream. A gang of local thugs led by Lupo forces him to help them rob the shop, and Lupo shoots the owner, Hop, who urges Jason to return the staff to its rightful owner. Cornered on a rooftop, Jason is pulled over the edge by the staff and wakes up in ancient China.

When soldiers attack a village to seize the staff, he is rescued by Lu Yan, a drunken traveling scholar who claims to be an immortal. Lu explains that the Jade Warlord tricked the Monkey King into setting down his staff and turned him to stone, but the Monkey King flung the staff away first; a prophecy foretells that a Seeker will return it and free him. Joined by Golden Sparrow, whose family the Warlord murdered, and by the mysterious Silent Monk, Jason sets out for Five Elements Mountain, learning kung fu on the way. The Warlord promises Ni Chang the elixir of immortality if she retrieves the staff. Ni Chang wounds Lu with an arrow, and at a monastery the companions learn that he is not immortal after all and only the Warlord's elixir can save him.

Jason goes alone to trade the staff for the elixir and must duel Ni Chang for it until his friends arrive. Jason throws the elixir to Lu, who recovers and sends Ni Chang plunging from a balcony. The dying Silent Monk passes the staff to Jason, who shatters the statue and frees the Monkey King, revealing that the monk was one of his clones. Sparrow is killed seeking revenge, and after the Monkey King defeats the Warlord, Jason stabs him and he falls into lava. Granted a wish by the Jade Emperor, Jason chooses to return home, where he beats Lupo; Hop, who survived, hints that he is Lu Yan.

Filmed partly around the Gobi Desert in Mongolia, the film opened at number one in North America and grossed about $128 million worldwide. Critics liked the fights but not the filler.

documents.title: Inland Empire
documents.tagline: A woman in trouble.
documents.overview: An actress’s perception of reality becomes increasingly distorted as she finds herself falling for her co-star in a remake of an unfinished Polish production that was supposedly cursed.
documents.plot: When actress Nikki Grace gets the lead role in a cursed film, her world becomes more and more surreal, blending realities and ideas of infidelity, reincarnation, and supernatural forces.

documents.title: The Mummy Returns
documents.tagline: The most powerful force on earth is about to be unleashed by the two people who should know better.
documents.overview: Rick and Evelyn O’Connell, along with their 8-year-old son Alex, discover the key to the legendary Scorpion King’s might: the fabled Bracelet of Anubis. Unfortunately, a newly resurrected Imhotep has designs on the bracelet as well, and isn’t above kidnapping its new bearer, Alex, to gain control of Anubis’s otherworldly army.
documents.plot:
The Mummy Returns is a 2001 American action-adventure horror film directed by Stephen Sommers and produced by Sean Daniel. The movie serves as a sequel to the 1999 film The Mummy.

Beginning:
The film starts with Rick O'Connell (Brendan Fraser), Evelyn Carnahan (Rachel Weisz), Jonathan Carnahan (John Hannah), and their friend Ardeth Bay (Oded Fehr) on an expedition in Egypt. They discover a hidden tomb, but it's too late; the Scorpion King (Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson) has already found it first.

Plot Development:
The Scorpion King is revealed to be Imhotep's (Arnold Vosloo) half-brother and the ruler of the Nubian kingdom. He seeks revenge against the world that wronged him, particularly the pharaoh who killed his father. The group soon learns that the Scorpion King has been resurrected by the power of the Staff of Ra.

As the story unfolds, Evelyn becomes pregnant with the son of Imhotep, and the Scorpion King's resurrection sets off a chain reaction of events that threaten to destroy the world. The group must navigate treacherous tombs, fight against the Scorpion King's army, and prevent the Staff of Ra from falling into the wrong hands.

The Mummy Returns features an array of memorable characters, including the Scorpion King, who becomes a fan favorite for his charisma and action-packed sequences. The film also explores themes of identity, power, and redemption as the characters grapple with their own destinies.

Ending:
In the climactic final battle, Rick O'Connell and Evelyn must face off against the Scorpion King to save the world from destruction. Along the way, they discover that Imhotep's resurrection is tied to the Staff of Ra, which has the power to bring about a new era of peace and prosperity.

Ultimately, the Scorpion King is defeated, but not before he reveals his true intentions: to use the Staff of Ra to resurrect Imhotep and rule the world. The film concludes with Rick O'Connell and Evelyn embracing their newfound love for each other, while Jonathan Carnahan finds redemption by sacrificing himself to save the day.

The Mummy Returns received mixed reviews from critics but was a commercial success, grossing over $415 million worldwide. Despite its flaws, the film remains a beloved entry in the Mummy franchise, thanks to its memorable characters, action-packed sequences, and epic scope.

documents.title: The Mummy: Tomb of the Dragon Emperor
documents.original_title: The Mummy: Tomb of the Dragon Emperor
documents.tagline: A New Evil Awakens.
documents.overview: Archaeologist Rick O'Connell travels to China, pitting him against an emperor from the 2,000-year-old Han dynasty who's returned from the dead to pursue a quest for world domination. This time, O'Connell enlists the help of his wife and son to quash the so-called 'Dragon Emperor' and his abuse of supernatural power.
documents.plot:
In ancient China, the warlord Qin Shi Huang unified Qin and became the founder of the Qin dynasty, known as the Dragon Emperor. Fearing his death would end all he had accomplished, the Emperor summoned the sorceress Zi Yuan and sent her to a monastery with his second-in-command, General Ming, to find the long-lost Oracle Bones, which hold the key to immortality. When Yuan and Ming fell in love, the Emperor had Ming executed and wounded Yuan out of jealousy. In retaliation, a fleeing Yuan cursed the Emperor and his army, turning them into the Terracotta Army.
In 1946, thirteen years after the deaths of Imhotep and the Scorpion King, Alex O'Connell, Rick and Evelyn O'Connell's son, and his archaeology professor, Roger Wilson, find the Emperor's tomb. Though attacked by a mysterious woman, they bring the sarcophagus to Shanghai. Meanwhile, the British government entrusts Rick and Evelyn to retrieve a gemstone called the "Eye of Shangri-La" and return it to China. During the Chinese New Year in Shanghai, the reunited O'Connells learn that Wilson works for a rogue military faction led by General Yang and his assistant, Colonel Choi, who provided the financial backing for Alex's expedition. Yang believes the Emperor can lead China out of the chaos following World War II and the Chinese Civil War, resurrecting him using the "Eye of Shangri-La," which contains mystical water. The revived Emperor accepts Yang's services but kills Wilson. The O'Connells try to stop him with the help of Lin, the woman who earlier attacked Alex, but he escapes. Lin reveals that she possesses the only weapon that can kill the Emperor—a cursed dagger.
Along with Evelyn's brother, Jonathan Carnahan, the O'Connells and Lin travel to a stupa in the Himalayas that will reveal the path to Shangri-La. With help from yetis summoned by Lin, the group holds off Yang's forces, but the Emperor discovers Shangri-La's location. The Emperor gravely wounds Rick while Alex triggers an avalanche, slowing the Emperor's pursuit. Lin takes them to Shangri-La, where Zi Yuan still lives. Lin is Yuan's daughter, both rendered immortal by the mystical waters, which Yuan uses to heal Rick's wound. The Emperor and Yang arrive, and he bathes in the waters, restoring his human form and granting him supernatural power. Morphing into a three-headed dragon, he steals the dagger, kidnaps Lin, and flies back to his tomb. The Emperor revives the Terracotta Army for world domination and directs them to breach the Great Wall, after which they will be invincible.
The O'Connells and Yuan pursue the Emperor to the Great Wall, where Yuan, using the Oracle Bones, sacrifices her own and Lin's immortality to raise an undead army of the Emperor's enemies, led by a revived General Ming. As the two undead armies clash, Alex rescues Lin. Yuan fights the Emperor and steals the dagger from him before he mortally wounds her. While dying, she gives the blade to Rick and Alex.

documents.title: Next
documents.tagline: If you can see the future, you can save it.
documents.overview: Las Vegas showroom magician Cris Johnson has a secret which torments him: he can see a few minutes into the future. Sick of the examinations he underwent as a child and the interest of the government and medical establishment in his power, he lies low under an assumed name in Vegas, performing cheap tricks and living off small-time gambling "winnings." But when a terrorist group threatens to detonate a nuclear device in Los Angeles, government agent Callie Ferris must use all her wiles to capture Cris and convince him to help her stop the cataclysm.

documents.title: Captain America: The First Avenger
documents.tagline: When patriots become heroes
documents.overview: During World War II, Steve Rogers is a sickly man from Brooklyn who's transformed into super-soldier Captain America to aid in the war effort. Rogers must stop the Red Skull – Adolf Hitler's ruthless head of weaponry, and the leader of an organization that intends to use a mysterious device of untold powers for world domination.
documents.plot:
In the present day, scientists in the Arctic uncover an old aircraft with someone frozen inside and a circular shield. In March 1942, during World War II, Nazi lieutenant general and Hydra leader Johann Schmidt steals a mysterious relic called the Tesseract, which possesses untold godly powers, from the town of Tønsberg in German-occupied Norway.
In New York City, Steve Rogers is rejected for U.S. Army recruitment due to his small stature and poor health. While attending the Stark Expo, an event held by famous engineer Howard Stark, Rogers attempts to enlist again. Overhearing Rogers tell his best friend, James "Bucky" Barnes, that he wants to fight for his country, Dr. Abraham Erskine allows Rogers to enlist. He is recruited into the Strategic Scientific Reserve as part of a "super-soldier" experiment under Erskine, Stark, Colonel Chester Phillips, and British MI6 agent Peggy Carter. Phillips is not convinced by Erskine's claims that Rogers is the right person for the procedure until Rogers selflessly jumps on a grenade as part of a test. Erskine reveals to Rogers that he was a scientist under Schmidt, until the latter took a prototype version of the super-soldier formula that gave him superhuman strength but painfully changed his appearance.
Schmidt and Dr. Arnim Zola harness the energies of the Tesseract to fuel Zola's inventions and Hydra's planned worldwide offensive. Schmidt discovers Erskine's location and sends an assassin, Heinz Kruger, to kill him. Erskine and Stark put Rogers through the super-soldier treatment, injecting him with the formula and dosing him with "vita-rays". After Rogers emerges from the experiment taller and more muscular, Kruger kills Erskine and flees with the last vial of the formula. Rogers pursues and captures Kruger, but the assassin avoids interrogation by killing himself with a cyanide capsule. The vial is destroyed during the chase. With Erskine dead and his formula lost, U.S. Senator Brandt has Rogers tour the nation as the mascot "Captain America" to promote war bonds while scientists study his blood and attempt to reverse-engineer the formula. In 1943, while on tour in Italy performing for active servicemen, Rogers learns that Barnes's unit is MIA following a battle against Schmidt's forces. Carter arranges for Stark to fly Rogers behind enemy lines to mount a rescue. Rogers infiltrates Schmidt's fortress, frees Barnes and the other prisoners, and confronts Schmidt. The latter escapes, but first he removes a mask to reveal his red, skull-like visage that has earned him the sobriquet "Red Skull".
Rogers recruits Barnes and other freed prisoners to form the Howling Commandos. Stark outfits Rogers with an upgraded uniform and a circular shield made of a rare, nearly indestructible metal called vibranium. Rogers and his team sabotage various Hydra operations while he and Carter begin to fall in love. In 1945, the team assaults a train carrying Zola.

documents.title: Fahrenheit 9/11
documents.tagline: Controversy...What Controversy?
documents.overview: Michael Moore's view on how the Bush administration allegedly used the tragic events on 9/11 to push forward its agenda for unjust wars in Afghanistan and Iraq.
documents.plot: Michael Moore's view on how the Bush administration allegedly used the tragic events on 9/11 to push forward its agenda for unjust wars in Afghanistan and Iraq.

documents.title: An Inconvenient Truth
documents.tagline: By far the most terrifying film you will ever see.
documents.overview: A documentary on Al Gore's campaign to make the issue of global warming a recognized problem worldwide.
documents.plot:
An Inconvenient Truth is an American documentary of 2006 directed by Davis Guggenheim that follows former United States vice president Al Gore's campaign to educate the public about global warming. Built around the illustrated lecture Gore estimates he has given more than a thousand times around the world, it was produced by Laurie David, who was inspired after seeing his presentation at a town hall meeting with Lawrence Bender.

Gore, who began giving the talk in 1989 with flip charts and now uses a computer slide show, opens with his familiar joke that he "used to be the next president of the United States." He admits he feels he has so far failed to get his message across. The lecture combines detailed graphs, charts and striking images, beginning with photographs of Earth taken from space, such as Earthrise and The Blue Marble, which he credits with helping to spark the modern environmental movement. Interwoven are personal episodes that shaped his concerns: his studies at Harvard under the early climate scientist Roger Revelle, the death of his sister from lung cancer, his young son's near-fatal car accident and his defeat in the 2000 presidential election, which he calls a hard blow that sharpened his sense of mission. A clip from the animated series Futurama provides a comic explanation of the greenhouse effect.

Gore presents the scientific consensus on climate change and argues that it is a moral rather than a political issue. He shows Antarctic ice-core data indicating that carbon dioxide levels are higher than at any point in the past 650,000 years, and documents retreating glaciers around the world. He warns that the collapse of the ice sheets of Greenland or West Antarctica could raise sea levels by about 20 feet, flooding coastlines and creating some 100 million refugees, and that meltwater from Greenland could disrupt the ocean currents that keep northern Europe warm. Segments rebut critics who call warming unproven or trivial, as Gore urges deep cuts in emissions.

After premiering at the 2006 Sundance Film Festival, the film opened in New York and Los Angeles on 24 May 2006 and grossed about $50 million worldwide, among the top-grossing documentaries in the United States. Rated 93% on Rotten Tomatoes, it won two Oscars, for Best Documentary Feature and for Melissa Etheridge's song "I Need to Wake Up". In 2007 Gore shared the Nobel Peace Prize with the IPCC.

documents.title: Stuck on You
documents.tagline: Whatever happens to the boys, one thing is certain. Nothing will ever come between them.
documents.overview: In Martha's Vineyard, Mass., conjoined twins Walt and Bob Tenor make the best of their handicap by being the fastest grill cooks in town. While outgoing Walt hopes to one day become a famous actor, shy Bob prefers to stay out of the spotlight. When a fading Hollywood actress, Cher, decides to get her show "Honey and the Beaze" cancelled, she hires Walt -- and his brotherly appendage -- as her costars. But their addition surprisingly achieves the opposite.

documents.title: Elephant
documents.tagline: An ordinary high school day. Except that it's not.
documents.overview: Several ordinary high school students go through their daily routine as two others prepare for something more malevolent.
documents.plot: Several ordinary high school students go through their daily routine as two others prepare for something more malevolent.

documents.title: The Devil's Advocate
documents.tagline: Evil has its winning ways.
documents.overview: Aspiring Florida defense lawyer Kevin Lomax accepts a job at a New York law firm. With the stakes getting higher every case, Kevin quickly learns that his boss has something far more evil planned.
documents.plot:
The Devil's Advocate is a 1997 American supernatural thriller film directed by Taylor Hackford and starring Al Pacino, Keanu Reeves, Charlize Theron, and Jeff Bridges.

The story begins with Kevin Lomax (Keanu Reeves), a young and ambitious lawyer who has just landed a job at the prestigious law firm of Bendini, Lambert & Locke in New York City. The firm is known for its ruthless tactics and high-profile clients, but what Kevin doesn't know is that his new boss, John Milton (Al Pacino), is actually the devil himself.

As Kevin becomes more entrenched in the firm's inner workings, he begins to notice strange occurrences and eerie feelings that something is off about his job. He also starts to develop a close relationship with Mary Ann Lomax (Charlize Theron), his wife who has been struggling with her own demons.

Meanwhile, John Milton is revealed to be working for the devil, Satan, who is trying to tempt Kevin into joining him in Hell. As Kevin becomes more and more entrenched in the firm's dark world, he begins to question his own morality and values.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Kevin has made a Faustian bargain by accepting a job at the firm, which comes with a terrible cost: his soul. The devil's plan is to corrupt Kevin and turn him into one of his minions, forcing him to work against humanity.

In a thrilling climax, Kevin discovers the truth about John Milton and the firm's true nature. He must then make a choice between joining the devil or fighting against him. In the end, Kevin chooses to reject the devil's offer and instead finds redemption by turning against John Milton and saving his wife from the clutches of evil.

The film features stunning performances from Al Pacino and Keanu Reeves, as well as a haunting score that perfectly captures the sense of foreboding and dread. The Devil's Advocate is a gripping tale of temptation and corruption, with themes that resonate long after the credits roll.

Overall, The Devil's Advocate is a masterclass in suspenseful storytelling, with a complex plot that keeps viewers on the edge of their seats until the very end.

documents.title: Phone Booth
documents.tagline: No options. No lies. No fear. No deals. Just keep talking.
documents.overview: A slick New York publicist who picks up a ringing receiver in a phone booth is told that if he hangs up, he'll be killed... and the little red light from a laser rifle sight is proof that the caller isn't kidding.
documents.plot:
Phone Booth is a psychological thriller film directed by Joel Schumacher, released in 2002 (not 2003) by Fox 2000 Pictures. The movie stars Colin Farrell as Stu Shepard, a radio talk show host who finds himself trapped in his phone booth during a hijacking.

The story begins with Stu Shepard, a successful and arrogant radio talk show host, who is on the air at 4:00 AM, discussing current events and taking calls from listeners. As he's about to wrap up his show, a man, played by Kiefer Sutherland, enters the booth and takes Stu hostage, claiming that he has a bomb strapped to his body.

The hijacker, who is revealed to be a former Marine named Phil (Sutherland), demands that Stu call 911 and report his location. However, when Stu tries to call for help, he realizes that his phone is dead, and the only way to get out of the booth is to answer Phil's demands.

As the situation escalates, Stu begins to realize that Phil is not just a random hijacker but someone who has a personal vendetta against him. Through a series of flashbacks, it becomes clear that Stu was responsible for Phil's wife's death in a car accident several years ago.

Throughout the film, Stu tries to negotiate with Phil, while also trying to find ways to escape. He uses his radio show as an opportunity to manipulate Phil and try to get him to reveal more about himself. Meanwhile, Detective Bannion (Kiefer Sutherland) is investigating a series of hijackings across the city, unaware that he's dealing with the same person.

As the standoff continues, Stu begins to question his own morality and the consequences of his actions. He starts to feel guilty for not taking responsibility for Phil's wife's death and begins to see himself as a victim of circumstance.

In the end, Stu manages to outsmart Phil by using his radio show to lure him into a trap. However, just as it seems like Stu has escaped, he realizes that he may have made things worse for himself. The film ends with Stu being taken away by police, but not before he reflects on the events of the night and the consequences of his actions.

Overall, Phone Booth is a tense and suspenseful thriller that explores themes of guilt, responsibility, and redemption. Colin Farrell delivers a strong performance as Stu Shepard, bringing depth and nuance to a complex character. The film's twist ending adds an extra layer of complexity to the story, leaving audiences questioning what really happened in the phone booth that night.

documents.title: You, Me and Dupree
documents.tagline: Two's company. Dupree's a crowd.
documents.overview: After standing in as best man for his longtime friend Carl Petersen, Randy Dupree loses his job, becomes a barfly and attaches himself to the newlywed couple almost permanently -- as their houseguest. But the longer Dupree camps out on their couch, the closer he gets to Carl's bride, Molly, leaving the frustrated groom wondering when his pal will be moving out.
documents.plot: After standing in as best man for his longtime friend Carl Petersen, Randy Dupree loses his job, becomes a barfly and attaches himself to the newlywed couple almost permanently -- as their houseguest. But the longer Dupree camps out on their couch, the closer he gets to Carl's bride, Molly, leaving the frustrated groom wondering when his pal will be moving out.

documents.title: 50 First Dates
documents.tagline: Imagine having to win over the girl of your dreams... every friggin' day.
documents.overview: Henry is a player skilled at seducing women. But when this veterinarian meets Lucy, a girl with a quirky problem when it comes to total recall, he realizes it's possible to fall in love all over again…and again, and again. That's because the delightful Lucy has no short-term memory, so Henry must woo her day after day until he finally sweeps her off her feet.
documents.plot:
"50 First Dates" is a romantic comedy film released in 2004, directed by Peter Segal and produced by Adam Sandler Productions, Inc., in association with Columbia Pictures.

The movie tells the story of Henry Roth (played by Adam Sandler), a veterinarian who falls in love with Lucy Whitmore (played by Drew Barrymore) at a Hawaiian luau. However, their romance is short-lived as Lucy suffers from short-term memory loss due to a head injury she sustained in an accident. As a result, she wakes up every day thinking it's the day of her accident and doesn't remember Henry or their time together.

Henry tries to win Lucy over every day, but his efforts are met with confusion and frustration. Despite this, he continues to visit her every day, hoping that eventually she'll remember him. The situation becomes a daily routine for both Henry and Lucy, as Henry tries to make the most of each day they spend together.

As the days go by, Henry starts to notice small changes in Lucy's behavior, suggesting that she may be starting to develop some memories of their time together. However, these moments are fleeting, and Lucy still doesn't remember Henry consistently.

Henry decides to take matters into his own hands and comes up with a plan to win Lucy over once and for all. He enlists the help of his friend Ula (played by Sean Astin) and his brother Rob (played by Rob Schneider), who also have their own romantic misadventures.

As Henry tries to make Lucy fall in love with him, he must confront his own feelings and learn to accept that Lucy's condition may be permanent. Along the way, he learns valuable lessons about love, loss, and the importance of living in the present moment.

The movie takes a heartwarming turn when Henry finally succeeds in making Lucy remember him, but not before she realizes that she has fallen in love with him. The film ends on a hopeful note, as Henry and Lucy look forward to building a life together, despite the challenges they face.

Overall, "50 First Dates" is a charming romantic comedy that explores themes of love, loss, and memory. With its witty dialogue, engaging characters, and beautiful Hawaiian setting, it's no wonder this movie has become a beloved classic among rom-com fans.

documents.title: Lord of War
documents.tagline: Where there's a will, there's a weapon
documents.overview: Yuri Orlov is a globetrotting arms dealer and, through some of the deadliest war zones, he struggles to stay one step ahead of a relentless Interpol agent, his business rivals and even some of his customers who include many of the world's most notorious dictators. Finally, he must also face his own conscience.
documents.plot:
Lord of War is a 2005 crime drama film written, produced and directed by Andrew Niccol. It stars Nicolas Cage as Yuri Orlov, an unscrupulous Ukrainian-American arms dealer, with Jared Leto as his brother Vitaly, Bridget Moynahan as his wife Ava, Ethan Hawke as Interpol agent Jack Valentine and Eamonn Walker as the Liberian dictator André Baptiste. The film follows Yuri's career in the global arms trade in the years before and after the dissolution of the Soviet Union, and was released in the United States by Lions Gate Films on September 16, 2005.

In the early 1980s, Yuri, whose family posed as Jews in order to emigrate from the Soviet Union, works in a restaurant in Brighton Beach. After witnessing a shootout between Russian mobsters, he decides that selling weapons is a business as essential as feeding people, and through a contact at his father's synagogue he makes his first sale of an Uzi. He persuades his reluctant younger brother Vitaly to become his partner, and their big break comes with the Lebanese Civil War. As his fortune grows, Yuri sees his weapons fueling atrocities around the world, yet he never stops, all the while being doggedly pursued by Valentine, an incorruptible agent who cannot be bribed or intimidated. A deal with a Colombian drug lord leaves the brothers paid in cocaine, and Vitaly falls into addiction, while Yuri uses his wealth to win over Ava, a supermodel he has admired since adolescence, and starts a family. The collapse of the Soviet Union in 1991 gives Yuri access, through his uncle Dmitri, a Soviet general, to vast stockpiles of military equipment in Ukraine, and he expands into Africa, where he becomes a supplier to Baptiste, a ruthless dictator who uses child soldiers. When Valentine reveals Yuri's real business to Ava, Yuri briefly tries to go legitimate, but the lure of a huge payday in blood diamonds draws him back, setting in motion a deal in West Africa that will test his family, his brother's conscience and his own capacity to look away.

Lord of War received mixed reviews. Critics praised its opening sequence and Cage's performance, but faulted its lack of focus; on Rotten Tomatoes, 62% of 148 critics' reviews are positive, with a consensus calling it an intelligent examination of the gun trade that is too scattershot to connect. It grossed $72.6 million, a box-office disappointment, but enjoyed strong DVD sales.

documents.title: Rent
documents.tagline: No day but today.
documents.overview: This rock opera tells the story of one year in the life of a group of bohemians struggling in late 1980s East Village, New York, USA. The film centers around Mark and Roger, two roommates. While a  tragedy has made Roger numb to new experiences, Mark begins capturing their world through his attempts to make a personal movie. In the year that follows, they and their friends deal with love, loss, and working together.
documents.plot:
Rent (2005) is a poignant and powerful film that explores the lives of artists struggling with love, loss, and the pursuit of one's passion in the face of adversity.

At its core, Rent is a story about the human experience, delving into themes of community, found family, and the power of art to transcend suffering. The characters, all living with HIV/AIDS in 1980s New York City, form a tight-knit circle that supports each other through the ups and downs of life.

The film also grapples with the harsh realities of poverty, addiction, and the struggle for survival in a city that seems determined to crush its inhabitants. Yet, amidst the darkness, Rent shines a light on the resilience of the human spirit, highlighting the ways in which art can be both a source of comfort and a means of resistance.

One of the most striking aspects of Rent is its exploration of love and relationships. The characters' experiences with romance, heartbreak, and loss are deeply nuanced and relatable, making it easy to become invested in their stories. Through the lens of these complex relationships, the film sheds light on the ways in which we find meaning and connection in our lives.

Ultimately, Rent is a powerful tribute to the artists and activists who fought for justice and equality during this tumultuous period in American history. The film's message of hope, acceptance, and the transformative power of art continues to resonate with audiences today, making it a timeless classic that lingers long after the credits roll.

documents.title: Entrapment
documents.tagline: The trap is set.
documents.overview: Two thieves, who travel in elegant circles, try to outsmart each other and, in the process, end up falling in love.
documents.plot:
Entrapment is a 1999 American heist film directed by Jon Amiel and written by Ronald Bass. It stars Sean Connery as master thief Robert "Mac" MacDougal and Catherine Zeta-Jones as insurance investigator Virginia "Gin" Baker, with Will Patton as her boss Hector Cruz, Ving Rhames and Maury Chaykin. The story follows the uneasy partnership between the two as they plan an audacious robbery timed to the turn of the millennium. It was filmed in Britain and Malaysia, with a score by Christopher Young.

In December 1999, Gin Baker investigates the theft of a valuable Rembrandt painting from a New York apartment and convinces her employer that the culprit is Mac, a legendary aging thief who steals for the challenge. Sent to London to catch him, she poses as a fellow thief and proposes that he help her steal a priceless Chinese mask from the heavily guarded Bedford Palace. After she passes his tests, Mac takes her to his isolated castle in Scotland, where the two train intensively for the job, clashing over his meticulous methods and trying to resist their growing attraction.

The theft of the mask succeeds, but Mac suspects Gin's true allegiance. She insists that her job as an investigator is merely a cover and that she needs him for a far bigger job: robbing the International Clearance Bank in Kuala Lumpur's Petronas Towers. At midnight on New Year's Eve, the bank's computers will shut down briefly to check for millennium bugs, giving the pair a window in which to transfer billions of dollars. As they prepare for the heist in Malaysia, both must decide whether they can trust each other, while the FBI and Gin's employer close in and loyalties are tested until the very end.

The film is remembered for its elaborate set pieces, particularly Zeta-Jones's sequence weaving through a web of laser beams and the climactic scenes in and around the Petronas Towers, and for its playful use of fears about the Y2K computer bug.

Entrapment was a box-office success, grossing 87 million dollars in the United States and about 212 million worldwide. Critics were less enthusiastic: it holds 40 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus said that a poorly developed plot weighs down the leads' chemistry, and a Metacritic score of 54.

documents.title: World Trade Center
documents.tagline: The world saw evil that day. Two men saw something else.
documents.overview: Two police officers struggle to survive when they become trapped beneath the rubble of the World Trade Center on September 11, 2001.
documents.plot:
World Trade Center is a 2006 American biographical drama film directed by Oliver Stone, based on the true story of two Port Authority police officers who were trapped in the rubble of the World Trade Center on September 11, 2001.

The film begins with the introduction of two Port Authority police officers, WTC Police Officers John McLoughlin (played by Nicolas Cage) and Will Jimeno (played by Michael Peña), who are part of a team that patrols the underground tunnels beneath the World Trade Center. The story takes us back to 1993, when McLoughlin is still a rookie cop, and he meets his future partner, Jimeno.

The film then cuts to September 11, 2001, as the two officers are on duty in the underground tunnels. As the first plane hits the North Tower, they quickly realize that something catastrophic has occurred. The situation escalates rapidly, and the two officers find themselves trapped beneath the rubble of the World Trade Center.

The plot development is intense and suspenseful as McLoughlin and Jimeno struggle to survive against all odds. They use their training and ingenuity to navigate through the treacherous terrain, avoiding falling debris and toxic gases. As they search for a way out, they come across other survivors who are also trapped in the rubble.

As the hours tick by, McLoughlin and Jimeno face numerous challenges, including a collapsed elevator shaft that separates them, and a massive concrete slab that threatens to crush them. Despite these obstacles, they remain determined to find each other and escape alive.

The film's climax features an intense and emotional rescue effort, as McLoughlin is finally pulled out of the rubble by his colleagues. However, Jimeno remains trapped beneath the debris, and McLoughlin must make a desperate decision to save his partner. In a heart-wrenching moment, McLoughlin chooses to stay with Jimeno, refusing to leave him behind.

The ending is both poignant and uplifting, as McLoughlin's bravery and selflessness are celebrated by his colleagues and the public. The film concludes with a tribute to the real-life heroes who were trapped in the World Trade Center on that fateful day, including John McLoughlin and Will Jimeno.

Throughout the film, Oliver Stone masterfully weaves together the true story of McLoughlin and Jimeno's bravery and sacrifice, creating a powerful and emotional cinematic experience. The performances by Nicolas Cage and Michael Peña are outstanding, bringing depth and nuance to their characters. Overall, World Trade Center is a gripping and inspiring drama that honors the memory of those who lost their lives on September 11, 2001.

documents.title: Transformers
documents.tagline: Their war. Our world.
documents.overview: Young teenager Sam Witwicky becomes involved in the ancient struggle between two extraterrestrial factions of transforming robots – the heroic Autobots and the evil Decepticons. Sam holds the clue to unimaginable power and the Decepticons will stop at nothing to retrieve it.
documents.plot:
Transformers is a 2007 American science fiction action film based on Hasbro's toy line. Directed by Michael Bay from a screenplay by Roberto Orci and Alex Kurtzman, and executive produced by Steven Spielberg, it is the first installment of the live-action Transformers film series. Shia LaBeouf stars as Sam Witwicky, a teenager caught up in a war between the heroic Autobots and the evil Decepticons, two factions of shape-shifting alien robots. Tyrese Gibson, Josh Duhamel, Anthony Anderson, Megan Fox, Rachael Taylor, John Turturro and Jon Voight co-star, while Peter Cullen and Hugo Weaving voice Optimus Prime and Megatron.

The robots' home planet, Cybertron, has been devastated by civil war between the Autobots, led by Optimus Prime, and the Decepticons, led by Megatron. Both sides seek the AllSpark, a cube-shaped artifact that is the source of their race's life. Megatron tracked the AllSpark to Earth long ago but crashed in the Arctic and was frozen in the ice, where he was found in 1897 by the explorer Captain Archibald Witwicky, whose eyeglasses were accidentally imprinted with the cube's location. A secret government agency, Sector 7, later recovered both the AllSpark and Megatron's frozen body and hid them beneath the Hoover Dam.

In the present day, Decepticons attack a US military base in Qatar and try to hack into military networks to locate the cube, while the surviving soldiers, led by Captain Lennox, flee across the desert. Meanwhile Sam, Archibald's great-great-grandson, buys his first car, a battered yellow Camaro that turns out to be the Autobot Bumblebee, sent to protect him. When other Autobots arrive on Earth, they explain that the glasses Sam is trying to sell online hold the key to finding the AllSpark before the Decepticons do. Sam and his classmate Mikaela are drawn into the conflict, along with the soldiers, a team of analysts and the agents of Sector 7, culminating in a destructive battle through the streets of a city.

Transformers received mixed reviews; critics praised its visual effects, action sequences and sound but criticized its length, humor and thin characters. It was a major commercial success, grossing more than $700 million worldwide, and it received three Academy Award nominations, for Sound Mixing, Sound Editing and Visual Effects. It launched a franchise of sequels and spin-offs.

documents.title: Pirates of the Caribbean: On Stranger Tides
documents.original_title: Pirates of the Caribbean: On Stranger Tides
documents.tagline: Live Forever Or Die Trying.
documents.overview: Captain Jack Sparrow crosses paths with a woman from his past, and he's not sure if it's love -- or if she's a ruthless con artist who's using him to find the fabled Fountain of Youth. When she forces him aboard the Queen Anne's Revenge, the ship of the formidable pirate Blackbeard, Jack finds himself on an unexpected adventure in which he doesn't know who to fear more: Blackbeard or the woman from his past.
documents.plot:
Pirates of the Caribbean: On Stranger Tides is a 2011 adventure film directed by Rob Marshall, produced by Jerry Bruckheimer, and distributed by Walt Disney Pictures.

The story follows Captain Jack Sparrow (played by Johnny Depp), who is on a quest to find the Fountain of Youth. He teams up with Angelica (played by Penélope Cruz), the daughter of the infamous pirate Blackbeard (played by Ian McShane). Together, they embark on a perilous journey across the seas in search of the elusive fountain.

As they navigate through treacherous waters, Jack and Angelica are pursued by the Royal Navy, led by Captain Norrington (played by Jamaine Rich), who is determined to capture Blackbeard. Along the way, they encounter the enigmatic and beautiful Syrena (played by Astrid Bergès-Frisbey), a mermaid who possesses magical powers.

As Jack and Angelica delve deeper into their quest, they discover that the Fountain of Youth holds the key to eternal life, but it also comes with a terrible curse. The trio must confront Blackbeard's ghostly spirit, as well as the Royal Navy, in order to reach the fountain before it falls into the wrong hands.

Throughout the film, Jack Sparrow's wit and cunning are put to the test as he navigates complex moral dilemmas and confronts his own demons. His relationship with Angelica is also explored, revealing a deeper side to their complicated past.

The film features stunning visual effects, impressive action sequences, and memorable performances from the cast. However, it received mixed reviews from critics, who felt that the story was convoluted and lacked the charm of previous Pirates of the Caribbean installments.

Despite this, On Stranger Tides remains a thrilling adventure that explores themes of power, identity, and the consequences of playing with forces beyond human control. The film's climax features an epic battle between Jack, Angelica, and Blackbeard, which sets the stage for the next installment in the franchise.

Overall, Pirates of the Caribbean: On Stranger Tides is a visually stunning and action-packed adventure that expands on the Pirates of the Caribbean universe while introducing new characters and themes.

documents.title: Rise: Blood Hunter
documents.tagline: They didn't leave her alive. They left her UNDEAD.
documents.overview: A reporter on the trail of a sinister cult wakes up in a morgue to find herself a member of the undead. She goes on a personal vendetta for a group a cultists that are responsible for her death.
documents.plot:
Reporter Sadie Blake has just published a notable article featuring a secret Gothic party scene. The night following the publication, one of Sadie's sources, Tricia Rawlins, is invited by her friend Kaitlyn to an isolated house in which such a party is to take place. Tricia is reluctant to enter with the curfew set by her strict father, so Kaitlyn goes in alone. When she does not return, Tricia becomes worried and enters the house as well. To her horror, she finds Kaitlyn in the basement with two vampires hanging onto her and drinking her blood. She tries to hide, but the vampires find her quickly.
The next day, Sadie learns of the girls' deaths and decides to investigate the matter. She soon attracts the interest of the vampire cult, and she is eventually kidnapped, raped and murdered by them. To her surprise, Sadie abruptly awakes inside the cold box of a morgue. She escapes, but in the course of the following hours she finds to her horror that she has turned into a vampire herself. After wandering the streets, she ends up in a homeless shelter, where she soon gives in to temptation, killing an old sick man and drinking his blood. She then runs out of the shelter when a young girl notices her, causing her to break down. She attempts suicide by throwing herself off a bridge, but is found and taken in by fellow vampire Arturo, who is less bloodthirsty and more benevolent than his brethren. Though his true motives are unclear — a power struggle between Arturo and the leader of Sadie's killers, Bishop, is mentioned — he helps Sadie to cope with her new condition and trains her to fight when she announces her intent to get revenge on her murderers.
Sadie tracks the vampires across the state, killing them one by one, while at the same time fighting the urge to consume blood from human victims. She soon crosses paths with Detective Clyde Rawlins, Tricia's father, who has taken it upon himself to avenge his daughter's death despite the objections of his superiors and colleagues. At first he takes Sadie for an enemy, but in time he recognizes that she is not of the same breed as Tricia's killers, and they team up in their pursuit of Bishop, the last survivor of the band. They track him to an abandoned stable complex, where they find not only Bishop but also Tricia, now a vampire, who openly voices her resentment and anger for her father. A hard fight ensues in which the evil vampires temporarily gain the upper hand. Along with two other women, Sadie is stripped naked and suspended by her ankles, with her wrists bound behind her back, to slowly drip blood. She is saved by Rawlins, and the two of them turn the tables against their enemies.
After Tricia and Bishop are killed, Sadie asks Rawlins to kill her too. She cannot bear the thought of having to give in to her bloodthirst and that she, since she is already dead, can never see her mother and sister again. Reluctantly, Rawlins grants her request and stabs her with a silver crossbow bolt.

documents.title: Marie Antoinette
documents.tagline: Rumor. Scandal. Fame. Revolution.
documents.overview: A retelling of France's iconic but ill-fated queen, Marie Antoinette, from her betrothal and marriage to Louis XVI at 15 to her reign as queen at 19 and ultimately the fall of Versailles.
documents.plot: A retelling of the story of France’s iconic but ill-fated queen, Marie Antoinette - from her betrothal and marriage to Louis XVI at fifteen to her reign as queen at nineteen and ultimately the fall of Versailles.

documents.title: Return of the Jedi
documents.tagline: The Empire Falls...
documents.overview: Luke Skywalker leads a mission to rescue his friend Han Solo from the clutches of Jabba the Hutt, while the Emperor seeks to destroy the Rebellion once and for all with a second dreaded Death Star.
documents.plot:
Return of the Jedi is a 1983 space opera film directed by Richard Marquand and written by Lawrence Kasdan, George Lucas, and Leigh Brackett. The film is the final installment in the original Star Wars trilogy.

The story takes place three years after the events of The Empire Strikes Back (1980). The Rebel Alliance, led by Princess Leia Organa (Carrie Fisher), has established a new base on the forest moon of Endor. Meanwhile, the Galactic Empire, under the command of Emperor Palpatine (Ian McDiarmid) and Darth Vader (David Prowse, voiced by James Earl Jones), is determined to crush the Rebel Alliance once and for all.

The film begins with Luke Skywalker (Mark Hamill), a young Jedi Knight, who has become increasingly disillusioned with his mentor, Yoda (Frank Oz). Luke's father, Anakin Skywalker/Darth Vader, appears in a vision, revealing that he was seduced by the dark side of the Force and became Darth Vader. This revelation sets Luke on a path to confront his father and ultimately redeem him.

The Rebel Alliance launches a massive attack on the new Death Star, while Luke, Han Solo (Harrison Ford), Chewbacca (Peter Mayhew), C-3PO (Anthony Daniels), and R2-D2 embark on a mission to disable the shield generator on Endor. Along the way, they encounter Boba Fett (Jeremy Bulloch) and his bounty hunter ship.

As the battle rages on, Luke confronts Darth Vader, who reveals that he has been trying to turn Luke to the dark side. However, Luke resists, and Vader ultimately redeems himself by throwing Emperor Palpatine down a reactor shaft, sacrificing himself in the process.

The film's climax features an epic battle between the Rebel Alliance and the Empire on Endor. The Ewoks, small, bear-like creatures native to the forest moon, join forces with the Rebels, using their primitive technology to disable the Imperial shield generator. Meanwhile, Luke confronts Vader, who reveals that he has been searching for a way to save his son.

In a final confrontation, Luke and Vader engage in a lightsaber duel. Just as it seems that Vader is about to kill Luke, the Emperor intervenes, attempting to turn Luke to the dark side. However, Luke resists, and with the help of his friends, he ultimately defeats the Emperor and Vader.

The film concludes with a celebration on Endor, as the Rebel Alliance declares victory over the Empire. Luke, now a confident Jedi Knight, reflects on his journey, realizing that his father's redemption was not just about saving him but also about finding peace within himself.

Return of the Jedi received mixed reviews from critics at the time of its release but has since become a beloved classic in the Star Wars franchise. The film's themes of redemption, sacrifice, and the power of friendship have made it a timeless tale that continues to captivate audiences around the world.

documents.title: Star Wars: Episode II - Attack of the Clones
documents.original_title: Star Wars: Episode II - Attack of the Clones
documents.tagline: A Jedi Shall Not Know Anger. Nor Hatred. Nor Love.
documents.overview: Following an assassination attempt on Senator Padmé Amidala, Jedi Knights Anakin Skywalker and Obi-Wan Kenobi investigate a mysterious plot that could change the galaxy forever.
documents.plot:
Ten years after the Battle of Naboo, the Galactic Republic is threatened by a Separatist movement organized by Count Dooku, a former Jedi Master who mentored Qui-Gon Jinn. Senator Padmé Amidala, the former Queen of Naboo, travels to Coruscant to vote against a motion to create an army to assist the Jedi against the growing menace. After narrowly avoiding an assassination attempt from bounty hunter Zam Wessell upon arrival, she is placed under the protection of Jedi Knight Obi-Wan Kenobi and his Padawan apprentice Anakin Skywalker. Zam attempts to assassinate Padmé again, but is thwarted and subdued by the Jedi pair. Zam's employer, a jetpack-wearing bounty hunter, kills her before she can reveal his identity. The Jedi Council instructs Obi-Wan to find the bounty hunter, while Anakin is tasked with protecting Padmé and escorting her to Naboo. Despite the Jedi Code forbidding attachments, Anakin and Padme fall in love.
Obi-Wan's search leads to the ocean planet Kamino, located beyond the galaxy, where he discovers a clone army is being produced for the Republic. The Kaminoans claim the army was commissioned by Sifo-Dyas, a Jedi Master who died ten years earlier, with the bounty hunter Jango Fett serving as the clones' genetic template. Obi-Wan deduces Jango is the bounty hunter he is seeking and places a homing beacon on Jango's ship before following Jango and his clone son Boba to the canyon planet Geonosis. Meanwhile, Anakin is troubled by visions of his mother Shmi in pain and returns to his homeworld of Tatooine with Padmé to save her. His former owner Watto reveals that he sold Shmi to a moisture farmer named Cliegg Lars, who then freed and married her. Cliegg says Tusken Raiders abducted Shmi one month earlier, and she is likely dead. Anakin finds her at the Tusken campsite, barely alive. After she dies in his arms, an enraged Anakin massacres the entire tribe. He later confesses his actions to Padmé and vows to prevent the deaths of those he loves.
On Geonosis, Obi-Wan discovers a factory building battle droids for Count Dooku's Separatist army, funded by several mega-corporations including the Trade Federation, whose leader Nute Gunray ordered the assassination attempts on Padmé in exchange for his support. Obi-Wan reports to the Jedi Council but is captured by Separatist droids. Dooku meets Obi-Wan in his cell and reveals that the Republic is under the control of the Sith Lord Darth Sidious. He attempts to persuade Obi-Wan to join the dark side, but Obi-Wan refuses. Senate Representative Jar Jar Binks proposes a successful vote to grant emergency powers to Supreme Chancellor Palpatine, allowing the clone army to be officially mobilized.
Having also received Obi-Wan's message, Anakin and Padmé head to Geonosis to rescue him, but Jango captures them. Dooku sentences the trio to be killed by alien beasts in their arena.

documents.title: Star Wars: Episode III - Revenge of the Sith
documents.original_title: Star Wars: Episode III - Revenge of the Sith
documents.tagline: The saga is complete.
documents.overview: The evil Darth Sidious enacts his final plan for unlimited power -- and the heroic Jedi Anakin Skywalker must choose a side.
documents.plot:
Three years after the start of the Clone Wars, Jedi Master Obi-Wan Kenobi and Knight Anakin Skywalker lead a mission to rescue Supreme Chancellor Palpatine from the cyborg Separatist commander General Grievous. After infiltrating Grievous's flagship in Coruscant's orbit, Obi-Wan and Anakin battle the Sith Lord Count Dooku, whom Anakin disarms and then executes at Palpatine's insistence. Grievous escapes the damaged ship before Obi-Wan and Anakin crash-land it on Coruscant. Anakin reunites with his wife, Padmé Amidala, who tells him she is pregnant. Soon after, Anakin is haunted by visions of Padmé dying in childbirth, similar to the vision he had of his mother before her death.
Palpatine appoints Anakin to the Jedi Council as his representative. Distrusting Palpatine, the Council agrees but refuses to make Anakin a Jedi Master. They instead instruct him to spy on Palpatine, diminishing Anakin's faith in the Jedi. Meanwhile, on Utapau, Grievous relocates the Separatist leaders to the volcanic planet Mustafar. Obi-Wan travels to Utapau and battles Grievous, ultimately killing him.
Meanwhile, Palpatine tempts Anakin with the dark side of the Force, promising that it can save Padmé's life. Anakin deduces that Palpatine is the Sith Lord, Darth Sidious, and the one who orchestrated the Clone Wars. He reports this to Mace Windu, who confronts and subdues Sidious. Desperate to save Padmé, Anakin maims Windu to prevent him from killing Sidious, allowing Sidious to kill Windu with his Force lightning. Although horrified by his actions, Anakin pledges himself to the Sith in return for Sidious' help in saving Padmé. Sidious christens Anakin as the Sith Lord Darth Vader. Sidious issues Order 66, which makes the obedience-conditioned clone troopers kill their commanding Jedi generals across the galaxy, while Vader commands a battalion of clone troopers to massacre the remaining Jedi in the Jedi Temple. Vader then assassinates the Separatist leaders on Mustafar, while Sidious publicly denounces the Jedi as traitors and declares himself Emperor before the Galactic Senate, transforming the Republic into the Galactic Empire.
Obi-Wan and Yoda survive Order 66 and learn that Anakin has turned to the dark side. On Coruscant, Yoda instructs Obi-Wan to confront Vader while he faces Sidious. Obi-Wan seeks out Padmé to learn Vader's whereabouts and to reveal his treachery. Padmé travels to Mustafar—unaware that Obi-Wan has stowed aboard her ship—and pleads with Vader to abandon the dark side. When Obi-Wan emerges, an enraged Vader believes Padmé has betrayed him and strangles her with the Force. Obi-Wan and Vader engage in a lightsaber duel, before Obi-Wan defeats Vader and severs his remaining limbs. Obi-Wan remorsefully denounces his former friend, who is then burned alive by a nearby lava flow. Obi-Wan retrieves Vader's lightsaber and leaves him for dead.
Meanwhile, Yoda battles Sidious on Coruscant, culminating in a stalemate.

documents.title: Traffic
documents.tagline: No one gets away clean
documents.overview: An exploration of the United States of America's war on drugs from multiple perspectives. For the new head of the Office of National Drug Control Policy, the war becomes personal when he discovers his well-educated daughter is abusing cocaine within their comfortable suburban home. In Mexico, a flawed, but noble policeman agrees to testify against a powerful general in league with a cartel, and in San Diego, a drug kingpin's sheltered trophy wife must learn her husband's ruthless business after he is arrested, endangering her luxurious lifestyle.
documents.plot:
Traffic is a 2000 American crime drama directed by Steven Soderbergh and written by Stephen Gaghan, adapted from the 1989 British Channel 4 miniseries Traffik. It examines the illegal drug trade from the viewpoints of users, enforcers, politicians and traffickers through three interwoven stories whose characters rarely meet. The ensemble includes Michael Douglas, Benicio del Toro, Catherine Zeta-Jones, Don Cheadle, Luis Guzmán, Dennis Quaid, Erika Christensen, Topher Grace, Tomas Milian and Benjamin Bratt, with dialogue in both English and Spanish.

In Mexico, police officer Javier Rodriguez (del Toro) and his partner Manolo Sanchez are recruited by General Salazar to capture Francisco Flores, a hitman for the Tijuana cartel of the Obregón brothers. Their campaign cripples the Obregóns, but Javier discovers that Salazar secretly works for the rival Juárez cartel. After Salazar has Manolo murdered, Javier helps the DEA expose him in exchange for electricity for a neighbourhood baseball park.

In Ohio, conservative judge Robert Wakefield (Douglas) is appointed the nation's drug czar, despite warnings that the war on drugs cannot be won, while his teenage daughter Caroline is sinking into addiction. When she runs away, Robert searches the streets of Cincinnati and finds her being exploited by a dealer. Faltering in the middle of a speech presenting his anti-drug plan, he declares that he cannot wage a war on his own family, and later joins Caroline at a support meeting.

In San Diego, DEA agents Montel Gordon (Cheadle) and Ray Castro (Guzmán) arrest a dealer who agrees to testify against the distributor Carl Ayala. Ayala's pregnant wife Helena (Zeta-Jones), discovering her husband's real business, takes matters into her own hands. She hires Flores to kill the witness, an attack that kills Castro instead, and then strikes a deal with the cartel that frees her husband, though Gordon quietly plants a listening device in Ayala's home.

Soderbergh, who shot the film himself under a pseudonym, gave each storyline a distinctive colour treatment. Released in December 2000, Traffic was acclaimed for its direction, complexity and performances, especially del Toro's, and earned over $200 million worldwide. It won four Academy Awards, for Best Director, Best Supporting Actor for del Toro, Best Adapted Screenplay and Best Film Editing.

documents.title: Vanilla Sky
documents.tagline: LoveHateDreamsLifeWorkPlayFriendshipSex.
documents.overview: David Aames has it all: wealth, good looks and gorgeous women on his arm. But just as he begins falling for the warmhearted Sofia, his face is horribly disfigured in a car accident. That's just the beginning of his troubles as the lines between illusion and reality, between life and death, are blurred.
documents.plot:
Vanilla Sky is a 2001 American science fiction psychological thriller film written and directed by Cameron Crowe, an English-language remake of Alejandro Amenábar's 1997 Spanish film Open Your Eyes. Tom Cruise, who produced it with Crowe and Paula Wagner, stars as a magazine publisher who begins to question reality after being disfigured in a car crash, with Penélope Cruz reprising her role from the original, Cameron Diaz, Kurt Russell and Jason Lee.

David Aames, heir to a publishing company, is in prison wearing a prosthetic mask and tells his story to court psychologist Dr. Curtis McCabe. A Manhattan playboy who leaves the business to his late father's associates, David meets Sofia Serrano at a party through his best friend, Brian Shelby, and they fall in love. His jealous lover, Julie Gianni, offers him a ride and deliberately crashes the car, killing herself and leaving David disfigured. Surgeons cannot repair his face, and he becomes withdrawn and depressed. After a drunken night out with Brian and Sofia ends with David passed out in the street, Sofia returns, they begin a relationship and his life improves; surgeons even find a way to restore his face. Yet strange things happen: a mysterious man in a bar tells David he is omnipotent, and one morning David finds Julie in bed with him. In shock, he suffocates her and is arrested, his disfigurement mysteriously returning.

With McCabe's help, David recalls the name "Life Extension," a company offering cryonic suspension in which clients live on in a lucid dream. Realizing that his world is a dream that has turned into a nightmare, he escapes his guards and meets the man from the bar, who explains that he is "tech support" and that David has been frozen for 150 years. Overwhelmed by the loss of Sofia and his injuries, David had overdosed after signing up for a lucid dream that would begin the morning after he passed out in the street, but a glitch let his subconscious distort it. On a rooftop above the clouds, he is offered the choice of returning to the dream or waking to real life through a leap of faith. Saying goodbye to visions of Brian and Sofia, he jumps, and a voice tells him to open his eyes.

Released by Paramount Pictures on December 14, 2001, Vanilla Sky opened at number one and grossed $203 million worldwide on a $68 million budget. Reviews were mixed (41% on Rotten Tomatoes), but Diaz received Golden Globe and SAG nominations, and Paul McCartney's title song an Academy Award nomination.

documents.title: Memoirs of a Geisha
documents.tagline: My world is as forbidden as it is fragile; without its mysteries, it cannot survive.
documents.overview: A sweeping romantic epic set in Japan in the years before World War II, a penniless Japanese child is torn from her family to work as a maid in a geisha house.
documents.plot:
Memoirs of a Geisha is a 2005 epic romantic drama film directed by Rob Marshall, based on the 1997 novel of the same name by Arthur Golden. The movie stars Zhang Ziyi as Chiyo Sakamoto, a young Japanese girl sold into prostitution in Gion, Kyoto, and Colin Firth as John Norman Howard, an American businessman.

The story begins in 1929 with Chiyo, a young orphaned girl who is sold to the Gion Courtesan School by her father. She is renamed Sayuri and trained in the traditional arts of geisha-hood, including music, dance, and poetry. As she grows older, Sayuri becomes a skilled geisha and attracts the attention of several wealthy clients.

One of these clients is Hatsumomo, a cruel and abusive geisha who resents Sayuri's natural beauty and talent. Despite this, Sayuri catches the eye of Nobu, a young geisha who becomes her closest friend and confidant. The two women form a strong bond, but their friendship is put to the test when they are both forced to compete for the affections of the wealthy and charming Noboru.

Noboru is a young nobleman who has recently returned from World War I and is looking for a geisha to be his companion. Sayuri is chosen as his favorite, and she becomes deeply involved in his life. However, their relationship is complicated by Hatsumomo's continued harassment of Sayuri and Nobu's own emotional baggage.

As the story unfolds, Sayuri finds herself torn between her loyalty to Nobu and her growing feelings for Noboru. Meanwhile, John Norman Howard, an American businessman, becomes a key figure in Sayuri's life, as he falls deeply in love with her. However, their social differences and cultural misunderstandings threaten to tear them apart.

The movie builds towards a tragic conclusion, as Sayuri is forced to make a choice between her two loves and the life she has built for herself. In the end, Sayuri sacrifices her own happiness for the sake of those she loves, leading to a heart-wrenching finale that will leave audiences in tears.

Throughout the film, the cinematography and costumes are stunning, capturing the beauty and elegance of traditional Japanese culture. The performances by the cast, particularly Zhang Ziyi and Colin Firth, are also noteworthy, bringing depth and nuance to their characters.

Overall, Memoirs of a Geisha is a powerful and emotional film that explores themes of love, loyalty, and sacrifice in the context of Japan's traditional geisha culture. While it has received some criticism for its portrayal of cultural stereotypes and historical inaccuracies, the movie remains a captivating and unforgettable epic romance.

documents.title: The Beach
documents.tagline: Somewhere on this planet it must exist.
documents.overview: Twenty-something Richard travels to Thailand and finds himself in possession of a strange map. Rumours state that it leads to a solitary beach paradise, a tropical bliss - excited and intrigued, he sets out to find it.
