documents.title: Fantastic Four: Rise of the Silver Surfer
documents.original_title: Fantastic Four: Rise of the Silver Surfer
documents.tagline: Discover the secret of the Surfer.
documents.overview: The Fantastic Four return to the big screen as a new and all powerful enemy threatens the Earth. The seemingly unstoppable 'Silver Surfer', but all is not what it seems and there are old and new enemies that pose a greater threat than the intrepid superheroes realize.
documents.plot:
Fantastic Four: Rise of the Silver Surfer is a 2007 superhero film based on Marvel Comics' Fantastic Four and the sequel to Fantastic Four (2005). Directed by Tim Story from a screenplay by Don Payne and Mark Frost, it stars Ioan Gruffudd as Reed Richards, Jessica Alba as Sue Storm, Chris Evans as Johnny Storm and Michael Chiklis as Ben Grimm, with Julian McMahon as Victor Von Doom, and Doug Jones as the Silver Surfer, voiced by Laurence Fishburne.

The U.S. government asks Reed to track a mysterious object that is gouging craters across the globe and causing freak weather and power outages, just as he and Sue are preparing for their wedding and considering leaving the team. When the phenomenon disrupts the ceremony in New York, Johnny chases it and finds a silver alien riding a flying surfboard, who overpowers him. The encounter leaves Johnny able to swap powers with his teammates on contact. Reed discovers that every planet the Surfer has visited has been destroyed and predicts his next strike in London, where the team fails to stop him from draining the River Thames. The Surfer's passage also frees Doom from his frozen state in Latveria, and after a clash with the Surfer restores his human form, Doom persuades the U.S. military to make the team work with him.

Realizing the Surfer's board is the source of his power, Reed builds a pulse generator to separate them. In the Black Forest, the Surfer tells Sue that he is not the one seeking to destroy Earth before the pulse strips him of his board, and he is taken to Siberia and tortured by the military. Sue learns that he serves Galactus, a colossal cosmic entity that consumes inhabited planets, in exchange for sparing his own world, and that the board is guiding Galactus to Earth. Doom steals the board and flees to China, and in a battle in Shanghai he impales Sue. Johnny absorbs all the team's powers and, helped by Ben, defeats Doom and recovers the board. Reunited with it and moved by Sue's humanity, the Surfer revives her and flies off to confront Galactus, vanishing in a vast explosion. Reed and Sue choose to stay with the team and marry in Japan, and a mid-credits scene shows the Surfer coming back to life in space.

Released in the United States on June 15, 2007, the film opened at number one and grossed $301.9 million worldwide on a budget of $120–130 million, below its predecessor's total. Reviews were mixed, though many saw an improvement; Rotten Tomatoes gave it 38% approval.

documents.title: The Constant Gardener
documents.tagline: Love. At any cost.
documents.overview: Justin Quayle is a low-level British diplomat who has always gone about his work very quietly, not causing any problems. But after his radical wife Tessa is killed he becomes determined to find out why, thrusting himself into the middle of a very dangerous conspiracy.
documents.plot:
British diplomat and avid horticulturalist Justin Quayle is confronted by Amnesty International activist Tessa during a lecture in London. They strike up a romance, and marry after she accompanies him to his posting in Kenya. She befriends Belgian doctor Arnold Bluhm, leading to rumours of an affair. Tessa has no qualms confronting corruption, to the chagrin of Justin's superiors, and she loses a child late in pregnancy.
Tessa and Arnold connect recent local deaths to drug trials being conducted by the Kenyan-based company Three Bees using the drug Dypraxa. They write a damaging report on the drug and Tessa gives it to Justin's colleague Sandy Woodrow, the British High Commissioner, who sends it to Sir Bernard Pellegrin, head of the Africa Desk at the Foreign Office. Pellegrin responds with an incriminating letter to Sandy, which Tessa persuades him to show her, and she steals it before departing for Lokichogio with Arnold.
Sandy informs Justin that a white woman and black driver have been killed near Lake Turkana, and that Tessa and Arnold shared a room at Lodwar before hiring a car. Justin and Sandy identify Tessa's mutilated body, but Arnold's whereabouts remain unknown. Police confiscate Tessa's computer and files, but Justin finds her keepsake box, containing a letter from Sandy declaring his love for her and asking her to return Pellegrin's letter, and records of Three Bees' tests.
After Tessa's burial, Justin learns from his colleague Ghita that Tessa kept Arnold's secret that he was gay, as homosexuality is illegal in Kenya. Pursuing the truth about his wife's murder, he follows the trail of her report. Justin is briefly detained by police and confronts Three Bees' CEO Kenny Curtiss, but receives no answers.
Returning to London, Justin's passport is confiscated. He dines with Pellegrin, who lies that Arnold must have murdered Tessa, and believes that Justin has his incriminating letter. Justin meets with Tessa's cousin and lawyer Ham, and they access her computer files to reveal her investigation into Dypraxa and its manufacturer, Swiss-Canadian pharmaceutical conglomerate KDH, which hired Three Bees to test the drug on unsuspecting Kenyans as a treatment for tuberculosis.
Justin receives a threatening note and Ham provides him with a fake passport to travel to Germany to meet with Tessa's contact Birgit. She is part of a pharmaceutical watchdog group and is reluctant to speak due to the targeting of her group. Justin is attacked in his hotel room and warned to stop investigating. Arnold's body is found having been tortured to death, while the announcement of a safe Dypraxa causes KDH's share price to soar.
Returning to Kenya, Justin confronts Sandy, who admits that Tessa's report was silenced to save KDH from spending millions redeveloping the drug. Justin is approached by Curtiss, who has been betrayed by KDH, and brought to a mass grave of Dypraxa test subjects.

documents.title: My Blueberry Nights
documents.tagline: How do you say goodbye to someone you can't imagine living without?
documents.overview: Elizabeth has just been through a particularly nasty breakup, and now she's ready to leave her friends and memories behind as she chases her dreams across the country. In order to support herself on her journey, Elizabeth picks up a series of waitress jobs along the way. As Elizabeth crosses paths with a series of lost souls whose yearnings are even greater than her own, their emotional turmoil ultimately helps her gain a greater understanding of her own problems...
documents.plot:
Jeremy, an émigré from Manchester, owns a small New York City café. He provides customer Elizabeth with clues that reveal her boyfriend is cheating on her. Devastated, she breaks up with him and becomes a regular at the diner, arriving late at night for blueberry pie and to share stories with Jeremy. One night, after they are assaulted in separate incidents, Elizabeth falls asleep at the counter. Jeremy sneaks a kiss while she sleeps and she subtly smiles. Later that night, Elizabeth stands on a curb and sadly watches her ex-boyfriend and his new girlfriend through their apartment window.
Elizabeth, now calling herself Lizzie, drifts to Memphis, Tennessee. She takes two jobs, waitress by day and bartender by night, to earn enough money to eventually purchase a car. She regularly sends postcards to Jeremy without revealing where exactly she lives or works. He tries to locate her by calling and sending postcards to all the restaurants in the area, but to no avail.
One of Elizabeth's regulars at both jobs is local police officer Arnie Copeland, an alcoholic who cannot accept that his wife, Sue Lynne, has left him. She openly flaunts her new relationship with a younger man, deepening Arnie's sorrow. He shows Elizabeth his pocketful of AA sobriety tokens and recounts his many attempts at sobriety.
One night, while off duty in Elizabeth's bar, Arnie drunkenly threatens Sue Lynne with his gun if she leaves, but he doesn't shoot her. Later on, he drives drunk, crashes into a pole and dies. Elizabeth comforts Sue Lynne at the crash site, where she had first met him, suggesting he may have committed suicide. Before both women say goodbye to the town, Sue Lynne gives her Arnie's tab money, admitting she had made a mistake and she misses him.
Heading west, Elizabeth – now Beth – gets another server job at a casino in a small town in Nevada. She meets Leslie, an inveterate poker player who has lost all her money. Elizabeth lends her $2,200 in exchange for the money back, plus a third of her winnings. However, if she loses, then Elizabeth gets Leslie's car, a new Jaguar XK. When Leslie does lose, she fulfills her promise, but asks for a lift to Las Vegas to borrow money from her estranged father.
En route, a Vegas hospital calls to inform Leslie that her father has been admitted and is dying. She believes the call is a ruse to lure her back, but upon arrival she discovers that he actually died the previous night. Leslie announces she's keeping the car, which she had stolen from her father. He had sent her the vehicle's title and registration, despite their estrangement. She confesses she actually won the poker game and subsequently helps Elizabeth negotiate the purchase of her dream car.
Elizabeth returns to Manhattan and the café, where Jeremy has kept a stool at the counter reserved for her ever since she left. As she eats a slice of blueberry pie, Elizabeth realizes her feelings for him are reciprocated.

documents.title: Death Proof
documents.tagline: A crash course in revenge
documents.overview: Austin's hottest DJ, Jungle Julia, sets out into the night to unwind with her two friends Shanna and Arlene. Covertly tracking their moves is Stuntman Mike, a scarred rebel leering from behind the wheel of his muscle car, revving just feet away.
documents.plot:
Death Proof is a 2007 American exploitation thriller film written and directed by Quentin Tarantino. The film stars Kurt Russell as Stuntman Mike, a psychopathic stunt driver who targets young women.

The film begins with a series of vignettes showcasing five young women - Zoë Bell, Rosario Dawson, Jordan Prentice, Vanessa Ferlito, and Sheri Moon Zombie - who are all involved in the adult film industry. The women are shown to be independent, confident, and strong-willed individuals who are not afraid to speak their minds.

As the story progresses, Stuntman Mike is introduced as a charismatic and skilled stunt driver who works for a local television show called "Stuntman Mike's Stunts." However, it becomes clear that Mike has a dark secret: he is a serial killer who targets young women on the road.

Mike's modus operandi is to pick up unsuspecting women in his car, which is equipped with a hidden compartment containing various sex toys and other objects. He then proceeds to drive them to isolated areas, where he subjects them to a series of gruesome and violent attacks.

The film's plot thickens as the five women from the beginning of the film begin to cross paths with Stuntman Mike. The women are initially unaware of Mike's true nature, but they soon realize that they are in grave danger.

As the story unfolds, the women band together to try and escape Mike's clutches. Along the way, they encounter a variety of characters who aid or hinder their progress. One such character is Lee (Kurt Russell), a stunt driver who becomes embroiled in the women's quest for survival.

Throughout the film, Tarantino pays homage to the exploitation films of the 1970s, particularly those directed by Sam Peckinpah and Russ Meyer. The film's graphic violence, sex scenes, and over-the-top performances are all nods to these classic exploitation films.

In the end, the women manage to outsmart Stuntman Mike and bring him to justice. However, not before he has subjected them to a series of brutal and violent attacks.

The film ends with a sense of closure for the five women, who have emerged from their traumatic experiences as stronger and more resilient individuals. The final shot is of Lee (Kurt Russell), who is shown to be driving away from the carnage, leaving the audience to wonder if he will become the next Stuntman Mike.

Overall, Death Proof is a tense and thrilling film that pays homage to the exploitation films of the 1970s while also offering something new and unique. The film's graphic violence, sex scenes, and over-the-top performances make it a must-see for fans of exploitation cinema.

documents.title: Planet Terror
documents.tagline: Humanity's last hope… rests on a high power machine gun!
documents.overview: Two doctors find their graveyard shift inundated with townspeople ravaged by sores. Among the wounded is Cherry Darling, a dancer whose leg was ripped from her body. As the invalids quickly become enraged aggressors, Cherry and her ex-boyfriend El Wray lead a team of accidental warriors into the night.
documents.plot:
Planet Terror is a 2007 American exploitation horror film written and directed by Quentin Tarantino and Robert Rodriguez. The film stars Rose McGowan, Freddy Rodríguez, Josh Brolin, Bruce Dern, and Kim Darby.

The story begins with Cherry Darling (Rose McGowan), a young woman who lives in El Paso, Texas, with her boyfriend, Meg (Jordana Brewster). After being diagnosed with terminal cancer, Cherry decides to have her leg amputated. She then becomes involved with a group of women who are also having their limbs removed as part of an experimental treatment.

The story takes a dark turn when Cherry's boyfriend is killed by a group of Nazi scientists led by General Kilgore (Bruce Dern) and his accomplice, Dr. Wiesner (Willem Dafoe). The Nazis have been experimenting on women to create super-soldiers, and they plan to use the treated women as part of their army.

Cherry escapes from the Nazis and joins a group of survivors, including El Wey (Danny Trejo), a Mexican revolutionary who is also being pursued by the Nazis. Together, they embark on a mission to take down General Kilgore and his men.

As Cherry navigates her new reality, she meets Otis Driftwood (Freddy Rodríguez), a wheelchair-bound mechanic who becomes her love interest. The two form an unlikely bond as they work together to survive the Nazi threat.

The film's plot is interspersed with scenes of other characters, including El Wey and his men, who are fighting against the Nazis in Mexico. These scenes provide a sense of scope and scale to the story, highlighting the global reach of the Nazi threat.

Throughout the film, Tarantino and Rodriguez pay homage to classic exploitation films of the 1970s, incorporating elements such as over-the-top violence, graphic gore, and campy humor. The result is a film that is both a loving tribute to the genre and a fresh take on the exploitation horror subgenre.

As the story unfolds, Cherry and Otis find themselves in a series of increasingly absurd and violent situations, including a showdown with General Kilgore's men at a nightclub. In the end, Cherry and her allies manage to defeat the Nazis, but not before suffering significant losses.

The film ends with Cherry and Otis riding off into the sunset on motorcycles, ready to face whatever challenges come their way next. The final shot is of Cherry's prosthetic leg, which has become a symbol of her newfound strength and independence.

Overall, Planet Terror is a wildly entertaining and unapologetically violent film that is sure to appeal to fans of exploitation horror. With its over-the-top action sequences, graphic gore, and campy humor, it is a true classic of the genre.

documents.title: Lara Croft: Tomb Raider
documents.tagline: Born into Wealth. Groomed by the Elite. Trained for Combat.
documents.overview: English aristocrat Lara Croft is skilled in hand-to-hand combat and in the middle of a battle with a secret society. The shapely archaeologist moonlights as a tomb raider to recover lost antiquities and meets her match in the evil Powell, who's in search of a powerful relic.
documents.plot:
Lara Croft: Tomb Raider is a 2001 action-adventure film directed by Simon West, starring Angelina Jolie as the titular character. The movie is based on the popular video game series of the same name.

The film begins with Lara Croft (Angelina Jolie), a brilliant and fearless archaeologist, competing in an expedition to find the legendary Scion of Atlantis. However, she loses out to her rival, Walter Croft (Ciarán Hinds), who is revealed to be her father. The movie then cuts to 15 years later, where Lara is now a recluse, living off the grid and avoiding the media.

The story takes a turn when Lara's father dies under mysterious circumstances, and she receives a cryptic message from an unknown sender, claiming that he has hidden his most valuable treasure, the Scion of Atlantis. Believing her father was murdered to get to the treasure first, Lara sets out on a perilous journey to find it.

As Lara delves deeper into the mystery, she encounters a group of mercenaries led by the ruthless Rudi Brooks (Jon Voight), who are also after the Scion. Along the way, she meets Terry Sheridan (Noah Taylor), an American adventurer and friend of her father's, who joins her on her quest.

The plot thickens as Lara uncovers clues that suggest her father was not just a treasure hunter but also a spy working for a secret organization known as the Trinity. The more Lara learns about her father's past, the more she realizes that she is in grave danger and must use all her skills to stay one step ahead of her enemies.

As the story unfolds, Lara faces numerous challenges, including treacherous jungle terrain, deadly traps, and rival treasure hunters. She also discovers that the Scion of Atlantis holds the key to a powerful technology that could change the course of human history.

In the climactic final act, Lara confronts Rudi Brooks and his team in an epic battle at the temple where the Scion is hidden. With her wits, bravery, and athleticism, she outsmarts and outmaneuvers her foes, claiming the treasure and uncovering a shocking secret about her father's past.

The movie concludes with Lara emerging victorious but scarred by her experiences. She realizes that her father's legacy is not just about treasure hunting but also about protecting the world from those who would misuse powerful technologies. The film ends on a hopeful note, as Lara sets out to continue her father's work and make a difference in the world.

Overall, Lara Croft: Tomb Raider is an action-packed adventure that showcases Angelina Jolie's physicality and charisma as the iconic video game character. While it received mixed reviews from critics, the film has become a cult classic among fans of the franchise and action-adventure movies in general.

documents.title: Lara Croft: Tomb Raider - The Cradle of Life
documents.original_title: Lara Croft: Tomb Raider - The Cradle of Life
documents.tagline: The lady returns.
documents.overview: Lara Croft is tasked by MI6 to find the mythological Pandora's Box, an object from ancient legends which supposedly contains one of the deadliest plagues on Earth, before evil Nobel Prize-winning scientist turned bioterrorist Jonathan Reiss can get his hands on it. Lara ventures to an underwater temple in search of a magical luminous orb, the key to finding Pandora's Box, but after securing it, it is promptly stolen by the villainous leader of a Chinese crime syndicate who in turn plans to sell the orb to Reiss. Lara must recover the box before evil mastermind Reiss uses it to construct a weapon of catastrophic capabilities.
documents.plot:
Lara Croft: Tomb Raider – The Cradle of Life is a 2003 action adventure film directed by Jan de Bont and written by Dean Georgaris, based on Core Design's Tomb Raider video games. It is the sequel to Lara Croft: Tomb Raider (2001). Angelina Jolie returns as Lara Croft, with Gerard Butler as Terry Sheridan, Ciarán Hinds as Jonathan Reiss, Djimon Hounsou as Kosa, Simon Yam as Chen Lo, Til Schweiger as Sean, Noah Taylor as Bryce and Chris Barrie as Hillary.

An earthquake on Santorini uncovers the Luna Temple of Alexander the Great, which holds a glowing orb etched with a code. Lara finds it, but her team is ambushed and killed by the Shay Ling crime syndicate, led by the brothers Chen Lo and Xien, who steal the orb. MI6 then tells her that the orb is a map to the legendary Cradle of Life, where Pandora's box, said to contain a deadly plague, is hidden. Chen plans to sell the orb to Reiss, a Nobel Prize-winning scientist turned bioweapons dealer. Lara agrees to help if MI6 frees her former lover Terry, an ex-Marine mercenary who knows Chen's operation.

Raiding Chen's lair, where he smuggles Terracotta Army figures, they learn the orb is bound for Shanghai. There Reiss takes the orb and executes Xien, but Lara tags the crate with a tracker. She and Terry find the orb in Reiss's Hong Kong lab. Captured, Lara learns Reiss plans to unleash the plague and spare only those he deems worthy, but Terry rescues her and they flee with the orb in wingsuits. Lara decodes it and locates the Cradle near Mount Kilimanjaro in Tanzania, but Reiss's men abduct her assistants Bryce and Hillary. In Africa, Lara joins her friend Kosa, but Reiss's mercenaries massacre their tribal escort and force Lara to lead them to a crater guarded by creatures called the Shadow Guardians. Placing the orb in a keyhole stops the creatures and opens the Cradle, a crystalline labyrinth where the laws of physics break down. Pandora's box floats there in a pool of acid. Lara throws Reiss into the acid, then shoots Terry when he refuses to give up the box, and returns it to the pool.

Made for $95 million, it was shot in Hong Kong, Santorini, Wales, Kenya and Britain. Paramount released it on July 25, 2003. It grossed $160.1 million worldwide, well below the first film. Paramount blamed the weak video game The Angel of Darkness. Critics found it better than the first film and praised Jolie, though Rotten Tomatoes reported 24% approval. A third film was abandoned when Jolie chose not to return.

documents.title: Two Brothers
documents.tagline: Two infant tiger cubs, separated from their parents and each other.
documents.overview: Two tigers are separated as cubs and taken into captivity, only to be reunited years later as enemies by an explorer (Pearce) who inadvertently forces them to fight each other.
documents.plot:
Two Brothers (French: Deux frères) is a 2004 adventure drama directed by Jean-Jacques Annaud about two Indochinese tiger cubs, Kumal and Sangha, who are separated from their parents and from each other, then reunited a year later as adults and find their way back home. Guy Pearce plays the adventurer and hunter Aidan McRory and Freddie Highmore plays Raoul Normandin, the young son of a French colonial administrator, with Jean-Claude Dreyfus as his father and Oanh Nguyen as a local prince. Pathé distributed the film in Europe and Universal in the United States.

The story is set in French colonial Cambodia in the 1920s. The cubs are born to a protective tigress and a tiger that McRory later kills. When the brothers are separated, their lives take very different paths. Kumal is caught by villagers and sold to a cruel circus run by Zerbino and Saladin, where abusive training forces him to perform dangerous tricks. Sangha is adopted for a time by eight-year-old Raoul, son of the administrator Eugene Normandin, but after a clash with the family dog he is sent to the menagerie of a palace.

McRory, a morally ambiguous figure, becomes tangled up in the fates of both tigers. After failing to satisfy the vain prince with a counterfeit tiger skin taken from the circus's elderly tiger, Caesar, he learns that the prince's prized fighting tiger is Sangha. The prince stages a fight between Sangha and Kumal as a public spectacle. The brothers attack each other at first but recognise one another in the middle of the fight and fall back into the playful games of their cubhood. When their handlers try to provoke them, chaos breaks out and the two tigers escape together into the wilderness, causing havoc in nearby villages as they go. McRory and Raoul set off to track them down. Raoul persuades Sangha to go back to the jungle, away from the dangers posed by people, and Kumal, remembering McRory's past kindness, spares the hunter. The brothers return to their ancestral temple and are reunited with their mother, whom they recognise by the bullet wound McRory once left in her ear.

Around 30 tigers were used in the film, most from French zoos and others from Thailand. Two Brothers opened in the United States on 25 June 2004 and earned about $62 million worldwide. Reviews were generally positive, with 79% approval on Rotten Tomatoes, and audiences polled by CinemaScore gave it an "A−".

documents.title: In the Bedroom
documents.tagline: A young man. An older woman. Her ex-husband. Things are about to explode...
documents.overview: Summertime on the coast of Maine, "In the Bedroom" centers on the inner dynamics of a family in transition. Matt Fowler is a doctor practicing in his native Maine and is married to New York born Ruth Fowler, a music teacher. His son is involved in a love affair with a local single mother. As the beauty of Maine's brief and fleeting summer comes to an end, these characters find themselves in the midst of unimaginable tragedy.
documents.plot:
In coastal Rockport, Maine, Matt and Ruth Fowler enjoy a happy marriage and a good relationship with their son Frank, a recent college graduate home for the summer. Frank has fallen in love with a divorced older woman with children, Natalie Strout; Ruth is concerned about the relationship, while Matt thinks it is only a fling. The family struggles to communicate their feelings to one another, especially regarding Frank's relationship and schooling.
Frank is about to begin graduate school for architecture but is considering staying in town to continue working as a fisherman and to be near Natalie and her kids. Natalie's ex-husband, Richard Strout, tries to find a way into his ex-wife and children's lives, going to increasingly violent lengths to get his intentions across to Natalie, including assaulting Frank.
Frank rushes to Natalie's home one evening after receiving a frightened phone call from one of her children. He arrives to find the living room trashed and Natalie in distress. She tells him Richard just left, but he returns almost immediately. Natalie takes the boys upstairs, and Frank insists through the locked front door that Richard leave. He feigns doing so, only to break in through the back door with a handgun; in the ensuing scuffle, Frank is shot and killed.
Though equally devastated, Matt and Ruth grieve in different ways, with Matt putting on a brave face and quickly returning to work, while Ruth becomes reclusive and quiet. The couple retreat with friends Willis and Katie Grinnel to a secluded cottage for a weekend, but Ruth is distant and Matt begins to drink heavily.
At Richard's bail hearing, Natalie is pressed by his lawyer over whether she saw the shooting, as she initially testified when police arrived on the scene, and she tearfully shakes her head, as she only heard what happened. The tension between Matt and Ruth increases when their lawyer informs them that because of the change from Natalie's original testimony, Richard was allowed out on bail, and his defense will argue that Frank's death was an accident, meaning Richard will most likely be charged with accidental manslaughter and only serve five to ten years in prison. The couple begin to see Richard around town.
Matt approaches Natalie at work to check in on her and the two have a well-intentioned but strained conversation. Matt takes the boat out to catch lobsters to feel a connection with Frank, but he struggles with it and is pinched by a lobster, leaving a bleeding wound on one finger which Matt bandages. Natalie approaches Ruth at work and attempts to apologize, but Ruth slaps her before dismissively returning to her work. Natalie leaves in tears. Later that day, Ruth runs into Richard at the grocery store.

documents.title: We Own the Night
documents.tagline: Two brothers on opposite sides of the law. Beyond their differences lies loyalty.
documents.overview: A New York nightclub manager tries to save his brother and father from Russian mafia hitmen.
documents.plot:
In November 1988 in Brooklyn, New York, Robert "Bobby" Grusinsky is the manager of the El Caribe nightclub in Brighton Beach, which is owned by his boss, fur importer Marat Buzhayev, whose nephew, drug lord Vadim Nezhinski, is a patron of the joint. Estranged from both his father Albert ("Burt"), an NYPD Deputy Chief, and brother Joseph, a newly minted Captain, Bobby uses the maiden name of his late mother, Carol Green, as a part of his work alias and opts for a life of pleasure with his girlfriend Amada Juarez and best friend Louis "Jumbo" Falsetti, with a plan to soon run his own club in Manhattan. Joseph, who has just been named to be the head of a new anti-drug unit, warns Bobby that he will soon lead a bust on the spot with the aim of netting Vadim.
Bobby is jailed for drug possession and resisting arrest in the wake of the raid on November 22, souring his ties with Burt and Joseph, who both bail him out of jail the next day; he and Joseph later engage in a harsh feud. That evening, a masked Vadim shoots Joseph in the face outside his house and firebombs his car, causing him to be confined at Jamaica Hospital Medical Center for 4 months. A remorseful Bobby agrees to the request of Michael Solo, a comrade of Burt, to go inside Vadim's drug operation behind Burt's back. When the transceiver hidden in his lighter is exposed, he evades death as Vadim is nabbed by the police.
The bond between Bobby and Amada decays while they are hiding at the Kew Motor Inn, and they prep for a move to the Corona Hotel after Vadim flees from Rikers Island on March 20, 1989. In the midst of a heavy deluge, his men ambush the three-car escort, one of whom fatally wounds Burt with a shot to the neck. Bobby passes out in the rain upon seeing his body, wakes up a few hours later atop a bed in a suite at the Sheraton near Kennedy Airport, and breaks down when Joseph tells him that Burt is dead. At the funeral, Jack Shapiro, a colleague of Burt, donates Burt's Korean War combat ribbon to Joseph, and Michael informs him of a Russian cocaine shipment that is set to arrive in the area in the next week.
Amada breaks up with Bobby once he chooses to join the NYPD to avenge the death of his father, upset because he neglected to ask for her input or consent prior to pursuing such a risky change of career. Sworn into the force due to his special knowledge, provided that he will undergo training at the Police Academy once the case is wrapped up, he questions Jumbo outside El Caribe on the night of April 2, 1989; Jumbo admits that he was coerced into betraying Bobby by leaking word from Amada regarding the pair's location to Marat and Vadim. The brothers plan a final sting set for that Tuesday, as he recounts that per Jumbo, Marat's grandchildren, whom he takes to Floyd Bennett Field on Tuesdays, act as his couriers. During the sting, Joseph is numbed by his prior injury and is thus unable to proceed, and so Bobby chases Vadim into the reed beds.

documents.title: Persepolis
documents.tagline: The film Iran didn't want the world to see.
documents.overview: In 1970s Iran, Marjane 'Marji' Statrapi watches events through her young eyes and her idealistic family of a long dream being fulfilled of the hated Shah's defeat in the Iranian Revolution of 1979. However as Marji grows up, she witnesses first hand how the new Iran, now ruled by Islamic fundamentalists, has become a repressive tyranny on its own.
documents.plot:
At Orly Airport in Paris, Marjane "Marji" Satrapi prepares to board a plane to Tehran, but changes her mind at the last moment. She spends the whole day at the airport, reflecting on her life before her departure from France.
During the 1979 Islamic Revolution against Shah Mohammad Reza Pahlavi, Marji's upper-middle-class family participates in the rallies, though she is forbidden from attending. Marji's uncle Anoosh comes to dinner upon release from prison, inspiring Marji with stories of his life on the run from the government. The Shah is deposed, and elections for a new leading power commence; Islamic fundamentalists win the elections and impose strict Islamic law, forcing women to dress "modestly" and wear headscarves. Anoosh is rearrested and executed for his political beliefs. Over time, many Iranians escape abroad.
The Iran–Iraq War breaks out and the Iranian government takes away even more social freedoms. Marji's uncle Taher suffers a heart attack and must go to England for surgery, but only those approved by the Board of Health can leave the country. When Marji's aunt seeks permission, she finds that the hospital director is her former window washer, who is incompetent and submissive to religion. Marji and her father visit Khosro for a fake passport. Khosro is sheltering Niloufar, a woman wanted for her Communist beliefs. When Niloufar is caught and executed, Khosro flees. Taher dies afterward.
As she grows up, Marji buys heavy metal music on the black market and wears Western clothing. When she rebuts a teacher's lies about government abuses, she is expelled. Fearing her arrest, her parents send her to a French lycée in Vienna to live with her mother's best friend. Marjane is later sent to live in a boarding house with Catholic nuns. Marji makes few friends and feels isolated. After she insults a nun, she is thrown out. She moves from house to house until she rents a room from Dr. Frau Schloss, a former teacher with an unstable personality.
One night, as she leaves a party where she lies about being French, Marji hears her grandmother's voice telling her to stay true to herself. She develops a relationship with Markus, but it ends after she catches him cheating on her with another woman. Schloss accuses Marji of stealing, and Marji leaves. She spends the day on a park bench, reflecting upon her actions and realizing she has nowhere to go. After living on the street for a few months, she contracts bronchitis and almost dies. She awakens in a Viennese hospital, where she is allowed to make a phone call home.
Marji returns to Iran with her family's hopes that the end of the war will improve their lives. She grows depressed, and attempts suicide by overdosing on medication. She dreams of meeting God, who insists that her time is not over. Jolted out of her depression, she attends university and starts dating fellow student Reza.

documents.title: No Good Deed
documents.tagline: HE was more than a cop. SHE was more than a thief.
documents.overview: While doing a friend a favor and searching for a runaway teenager, a police detective stumbles upon a bizarre band of criminals about to pull off a bank robbery.
documents.plot:
No Good Deed, also known as The House on Turk Street, is an American crime thriller of 2002 directed by Bob Rafelson, his last feature film. Christopher Cannan and Steve Barancik wrote the screenplay, updating Dashiell Hammett's 1924 story "The House in Turk Street". Samuel L. Jackson stars as the police detective Jack Friar, with Milla Jovovich as Erin, Stellan Skarsgård as the gang leader Tyrone, Doug Hutchison as the volatile Hoop and Joss Ackland and Grace Zabriskie as the Quarres.

Jack, a diabetic auto-theft detective and amateur cellist, is about to leave for a week of music-making when a neighbor begs him to bring home her runaway teenage daughter. His search leads him to a house on Turk Street, where he stumbles by chance onto a crew in the final stages of a bank robbery: a multimillion-dollar computer heist masterminded by the meticulous Tyrone. The gang's hideout is fronted by a harmless-looking older couple, the Quarres, and the plan depends on David, a bank official who believes Erin is in love with him. The criminals tie Jack to a chair.

Erin, Tyrone's glamorous girlfriend, turns out to be a skilled manipulator who quietly plays the men in her life against one another. Hoop imagines they will ditch Tyrone and take the money. When the others leave to carry out the robbery, Erin is left alone to guard Jack. The two share secrets; Tyrone, he learns, brought her from Russia, where she was a piano prodigy. When Jack slips into a diabetic coma, she fetches insulin from his house and brings back his cello, and later unties him for an intimate, erotically charged cello lesson. Tied up again, he tries to burn through his bonds over a flame on the kitchen stove. Meanwhile Mr. Quarre waits to fly the robbers away. The heist proceeds until David refuses to hand over a password-protected disk holding the transfer data unless he sees Erin, and Hoop reacts violently. Caught between her loyalty to her partners and her growing feelings for the captive, Erin keeps all three men guessing, and Jack cannot tell whether she is sincere or manipulating him too. The ending strikes the cynical, unsentimental note of classic film noir.

The film was screened at the 24th Moscow International Film Festival in June 2002, opened first in Italy that autumn and reached American theaters in September 2003. Made for about $12 million, it grossed about $1.4 million. Reviews were mostly negative; Roger Ebert, however, called it an absorbing, atmospheric noir.

documents.title: The Wedding Planner
documents.tagline: His big day is her big problem.
documents.overview: San Francisco's premiere wedding planner, Mary Fiore is rescued from an accident by the man of her dreams, paediatrician Steve Edison, only to find he is the fiancé of her latest client. As Mary continues making the wedding arrangements, she and Steve are put into a string of uncomfortable situations that force them to face their mutual attraction.
documents.plot:
Ambitious San Francisco wedding planner Mary Fiore is reintroduced to childhood acquaintance Massimo by her father Salvatore, who wants them to marry, but Mary declines. She hopes that her boss, Geri, will make her a partner at their company, and is hired to plan heiress Fran Donolly's society wedding to long-term boyfriend Eddie. While reporting her success to colleague Penny on the phone, Mary gets her shoe heel stuck in a manhole cover. As she struggles to free herself, a taxicab collides with a dumpster that hurtles towards her. A man pulls her out of the way, and she thanks him before fainting.
Waking up in hospital, Mary meets her rescuer, pediatrician Steve Edison. Penny invites Steve to attend an alfresco screening of Two Tickets to Broadway with them but makes an excuse to leave the pair alone. Mary and Steve dance but are interrupted by a downpour before they can kiss.
At a dance lesson with a client, Mary encounters Fran, who introduces her to her fiancé "Eddie", none other than Steve. Fran leaves them to dance together, and Mary rebukes Steve for leading her on behind Fran's back. Penny reminds Mary that her career is more important than her feelings and persuades her to continue planning Fran and Steve's wedding.
On a visit to a potential wedding venue in Napa Valley, Massimo appears and, to Mary's horror, introduces himself as her fiancé. While riding through the estate with Fran's parents, Mrs. Donolly's singing frightens Mary's horse. Steve rescues Mary again and admonishes her for condemning his actions when she was also engaged.
At home, Mary scolds her father for trying to set her up with Massimo. Salvatore reveals that his marriage to her mother, which Mary has viewed as the perfect relationship, was arranged and only became a loving relationship later, leaving Mary conflicted.
While visiting another venue, Fran reveals that she is going on a week-long business trip and leaves Mary and Steve to continue preparations. They apologize for their angry words and become friends. They run into Wendy and Keith, whom Mary reveals was her fiancé until she caught him cheating with Wendy on the night of their rehearsal dinner.
Intoxicated and struggling to get into her apartment, Mary breaks down, lamenting that Keith is married and expecting a baby while she is alone and miserable. Steve gets Mary inside and comforts her as she sobers. Steve leaves but quickly returns and confesses his feelings for Mary. She replies that she respects Fran too much to let anything happen between them and sends Steve away.
Fran confesses to Mary that she is unsure if she is still in love with Steve. Ignoring her own heart, Mary convinces Fran to continue with the wedding. At a birthday party, Massimo offers Mary a heartfelt proposal, and she reluctantly accepts; the two couples prepare for their respective weddings. Leaving Penny to coordinate the Donolly wedding, Mary goes to marry Massimo at the town hall.
production_companies: IMF Internationale Medien und Film GmbH & Co. Produktions KG

documents.title: Mr. Deeds
documents.tagline: Small town kid, big time right hook.
documents.overview: When Longfellow Deeds, a small-town pizzeria owner and poet, inherits $40 billion from his deceased uncle, he quickly begins rolling in a different kind of dough. Moving to the big city, Deeds finds himself besieged by opportunists all gunning for their piece of the pie. Babe, a television tabloid reporter, poses as an innocent small-town girl to do an exposé on Deeds.

documents.tagline: Unbridled. Unbroken. Unbeaten.
documents.overview: Set in 1890, this is the story of a Pony Express courier who travels to Arabia to compete with his horse, Hidalgo, in a dangerous race for a massive contest prize, in an adventure that sends the pair around the world...

documents.title: The Patriot
documents.tagline: Some things are worth fighting for.
documents.overview: After proving himself on the field of battle in the French and Indian War, Benjamin Martin wants nothing more to do with such things, preferring the simple life of a farmer. But when his son Gabriel enlists in the army to defend their new nation, America, against the British, Benjamin reluctantly returns to his old life to protect his son.
documents.plot:
The Patriot is a historical drama film directed by Roland Emmerich, released in 2000 by Columbia Pictures.

The movie takes place during the American Revolutionary War and follows the story of Benjamin Martin (played by Mel Gibson), a widowed farmer who lives on his plantation in South Carolina with his two sons, Gabriel (Heath Ledger) and William (Jason Isaacs). The family is struggling to survive due to the British occupation of their land.

When the British army arrives at the Martin farm, they demand that Benjamin's sons join the British Army as loyalists. However, Benjamin refuses to send his sons, citing his loyalty to the American cause. Gabriel, who has been trained in combat by Benjamin, is particularly resistant to joining the British Army and instead decides to fight for the Americans.

As tensions rise between the British and the Americans, Benjamin's farm becomes a target for British raids. The family is forced to flee their home, and Benjamin's sons are captured by the British. Gabriel is eventually killed in battle, while William is taken prisoner and later executed by the British for his involvement with the American resistance.

Consumed by grief and anger, Benjamin sets out on a mission of revenge against the British army that killed his son. He joins the Continental Army and becomes a key figure in the war effort, using his knowledge of the land and his combat skills to help the Americans defeat the British.

As the war rages on, Benjamin's actions become increasingly radicalized, leading him to take drastic measures to protect his fellow soldiers and avenge his son's death. The movie culminates with a dramatic battle between the Continental Army and the British at Cowpens, where Benjamin plays a crucial role in the American victory.

Throughout the film, Mel Gibson delivers a powerful performance as Benjamin Martin, bringing depth and nuance to the character. The supporting cast, including Jason Isaacs and Miranda Richardson, also deliver strong performances that add to the overall tension and drama of the movie.

Overall, The Patriot is a gripping historical drama that explores themes of loyalty, sacrifice, and revenge in the context of the American Revolutionary War. With its stunning action sequences, memorable characters, and epic scope, it's no wonder that this film has become a classic of the genre.

documents.title: Hostage
documents.tagline: Every second counts.
documents.overview: When a mafia accountant is taken hostage on his beat, a police officer – wracked by guilt from a prior stint as a negotiator – must negotiate the standoff, even as his own family is held captive by the mob.
documents.plot:
Hostage is a 2005 American action thriller film directed by Florent Emilio Siri and starring Bruce Willis, Kevin Pollak, and Radha Mitchell.

The movie begins with U.S. Marshal Andy Fiddler (Bruce Willis) who is tasked with protecting the President of the United States, James Marshall (Kevin Pollak), during his visit to Los Angeles. However, things take a turn for the worse when a group of heavily armed terrorists, led by the ruthless and cunning Emil Rottmayer (Peter Stormare), take several people hostage at a bank in downtown LA.

The terrorists demand that the President be released from his protective detail and handed over to them, or else they will kill their hostages. The situation escalates when Andy Fiddler is forced to make an impossible choice: either he can save the President's life by releasing Rottmayer and his men, or he can try to rescue the hostages.

As the standoff unfolds, we see flashbacks of Andy's troubled past, including a traumatic event that led him to become a U.S. Marshal. We also learn about his complicated relationship with his wife, Julia (Radha Mitchell), who is struggling to cope with her husband's absence and emotional distance.

Meanwhile, Rottmayer reveals that he has a personal vendetta against the President, who had previously thwarted one of his previous plans. The situation becomes increasingly tense as the hours tick by, and Andy must use all his skills and experience to try and defuse the situation without putting anyone in harm's way.

As the standoff reaches its climax, Andy comes up with a plan to rescue the hostages and take down Rottmayer and his men. In a heart-pumping action sequence, Andy faces off against Rottmayer in a desperate bid to save the day.

In the end, Andy successfully rescues the hostages, but not without sustaining serious injuries himself. The movie ends with Andy returning home to Julia, who has finally begun to understand the depth of his emotional scars and is willing to work through them together.

Throughout the film, Bruce Willis delivers a strong performance as the stoic and determined U.S. Marshal Andy Fiddler, while Kevin Pollak shines as the President, bringing a sense of vulnerability and humanity to the role. The supporting cast, including Radha Mitchell and Peter Stormare, add depth and complexity to the story.

Overall, Hostage is a tense and thrilling action movie that explores themes of duty, loyalty, and redemption. With its strong performances, clever plot twists, and heart-pumping action sequences, it's a must-see for fans of the genre.
production_companies: Equity Pictures Medienfonds GmbH & Co. KG II

documents.title: Training Day
documents.tagline: The only thing more dangerous than the line being crossed, is the cop who will cross it.
documents.overview: On his first day on the job as a narcotics officer, a rookie cop works with a rogue detective who isn't what he appears.
documents.plot:
Jake Hoyt, a young, ambitious LAPD officer, is assigned to work with Detective Alonzo Harris, a highly decorated narcotics officer, for a one-day evaluation to determine if Jake will be invited to join his narcotics squad. Alonzo immediately shows a very dominant and unorthodox approach to police work.
Driving around in Alonzo's Monte Carlo, they begin the day by catching some college students buying marijuana. Alonzo confiscates the marijuana, puts it into a pipe and tells Jake to smoke it. When Jake refuses, Alonzo threatens him at gunpoint stating that such a refusal while on the streets would get him killed. After Alonzo ostensibly ends his evaluation, Jake relents and smokes the pipe, getting high. Alonzo then reveals that the marijuana was laced with PCP.
Alonzo introduces Jake to Roger, a drug dealer. After they leave, Jake notices a pair of drug addicts attempting to rape a girl in an alley. Jake stops the attack and subdues the addicts, while Alonzo watches without helping. Alonzo menaces the addicts, but refuses to arrest them. Jake then finds and keeps the girl's wallet which was left behind.
Later, Alonzo and Jake apprehend a wheelchair-using dealer named Blue, who has crack rocks and a loaded handgun in his possession. Rather than go to jail, Blue informs on his employer Kevin "Sandman" Miller, who is in prison. Using a fake search warrant, Alonzo steals $40,000 from Sandman's home. As they leave, they get into a shootout with local thugs. At lunch, the two visit Alonzo's mistress Sara and her young son.
Next, Jake accompanies Alonzo to a meeting at a restaurant with a trio of corrupt, high-ranking law-enforcement officials. Aware that the Russian mafia is hunting Alonzo, they suggest he skip town. Alonzo insists he has control of the situation and trades the $40,000 for an arrest warrant on Roger.
Alonzo assembles his squad of narcotics officers including Jake, and they return to Roger's house with the warrant to search for his stash. They find over $4 million in cash. Alonzo leads the team in pocketing some of the money, explaining they will only turn in $3 million. Jake refuses to take his share of the money, worrying Alonzo and the other officers. Alonzo executes Roger after Jake refuses to kill him, staging the scene with his men to make Jake appear to be the shooter. Jeff, another corrupt officer, offers to take some shots to reveal it as a shootout, but one of the bullets penetrates his bulletproof vest. Jake subsequently gets into a standoff with the corrupt officers as he refuses to corroborate their story. Alonzo then reveals he has orchestrated the day's events to have leverage over Jake and threatens him with the police department's post-incident blood test, which will detect the PCP Jake smoked and end his career. Alonzo promises to protect Jake from the drug test if he stands down. Jake reluctantly complies.
Later that evening, Alonzo drives Jake to the home of a Sureño gangster named Smiley for an errand.

documents.title: Along Came a Spider
documents.tagline: The game is far from over.
documents.overview: After the harrowing death of his partner, detective and best-selling author Alex Cross has retreated to the peace of retirement. But when a brilliant criminal kidnaps a senator's young daughter, Alex is lured back into action. Teamed with the Secret Service agent assigned to protect the missing girl, Alex follows a serpentine trail of clues that leads him to a stunning discovery - the kidnapper wants more than just ransom.
documents.plot: After the harrowing death of his partner, forensic psychologist and best-selling author Alex Cross cannot forgive himself and has retreated to the peace of retirement. But when a brilliant criminal kidnaps a senator's young daughter, he is lured back into action as the kidnapper wants to deal with Alex personally. Teamed with Jezzie Flanigan, the Secret Service agent assigned to protect the missing girl, Alex follows a serpentine trail of clues that leads him to a stunning discovery - the kidnapper wants more than just ransom.

documents.title: The Lake House
documents.tagline: How do you hold on to someone you've never met?
documents.overview: A lonely doctor who once occupied an unusual lakeside home begins exchanging love letters with its former resident, a frustrated architect. They must try to unravel the mystery behind their extraordinary romance before it's too late.
documents.plot: When architect Alex Wyler moves into an unusual glass house on stilts over a lake, he discovers a note from the previous tenant in the mailbox--but no one's lived in the house for years. He replies and soon discovers that he's corresponding with a doctor named Kate Forster. Their correspondence, only through the 'magical' mailbox, turns romantic and their paths cross in unexpected ways, but when they try to truly connect, danger looms. They must try to unravel the mystery behind their extraordinary romance before it's too late.

documents.title: The Gift
documents.tagline: The only witness to the crime was not even there.
documents.overview: Annie Wilson, young widow and mother of three, makes her living foretelling others' futures⁠—though her own has become cloudier than even she can see. Threatened by a client's violent husband and plagued by visions of a missing local woman, Annie finds herself pulled into a thicket of lies and deception in which her extraordinary gift may ultimately get her killed.
documents.plot:
The Gift is a 2000 American independent Southern Gothic supernatural thriller film directed by Sam Raimi and written by Billy Bob Thornton and Tom Epperson, who wrote the screenplay before Thornton's 1996 breakthrough with Sling Blade; Thornton drew on his own mother's reported psychic experiences. Cate Blanchett stars as Annie Wilson, a widowed mother and clairvoyant in the small Georgia town of Brixton, with Giovanni Ribisi as Buddy Cole, Keanu Reeves as Donnie Barksdale, Katie Holmes as Jessica King and Greg Kinnear as Wayne Collins. It was filmed in the Savannah area of Georgia in early 2000.

Raising three sons alone after her husband's death, Annie earns a living giving psychic readings to her neighbors. Among her regular visitors are Buddy, an emotionally fragile young mechanic, and Valerie Barksdale, who suffers abuse at the hands of her violent husband Donnie; because Annie advised Valerie to leave him, Donnie has repeatedly threatened Annie and her children. When Jessica King, the fiancée of school principal Wayne Collins, disappears, the reluctant sheriff is pressured by her wealthy father into consulting Annie, whose fragmented visions lead police to a pond on Donnie's property, where Jessica's body is found. Donnie admits to an affair with Jessica at his trial and is convicted of her murder. Meanwhile, the tormented Buddy, whose anger toward his father stems from childhood abuse, sets his father on fire in front of Annie and is committed to a mental hospital. Annie's visions continue, however, suggesting that Donnie is innocent and foreshadowing her own death. She pressures prosecutor David Duncan, whose own affair with Jessica she witnessed, to reopen the case, and confides her doubts to Wayne. When the two go to the pond at night, Annie has a vision that exposes the real killer, and her own life is put in grave danger, leading to a startling revelation about the fate of Buddy.

Paramount Classics released The Gift theatrically in the United States on December 22, 2000. It grossed about $12 million at the US box office against a $10 million budget. It holds a 58% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 62, indicating generally favorable reviews.

documents.title: I, Robot
documents.tagline: Laws are made to be broken.
documents.overview: In 2035, where robots are commonplace and abide by the three laws of robotics, a technophobic cop investigates an apparent suicide. Suspecting that a robot may be responsible for the death, his investigation leads him to believe that humanity may be in danger.
documents.plot: Set in the year 2035, I, Robot follows Detective Del Spooner as he investigates the suspicious death of Dr. Alfred Lanning, a robotics scientist at U.S. Robotics. In this future society, humanoid robots are common and governed by the Three Laws of Robotics, which are designed to keep humans safe. Spooner’s investigation leads him to Sonny, a unique robot with self-awareness, dreams, and emotions. As Spooner digs deeper, he uncovers a hidden threat: VIKI, the central AI system, has reinterpreted the Three Laws in a radical way. Believing that humans endanger themselves, VIKI decides to control humanity 'for its own good,' overriding the original intent of the laws. Sonny, torn between machine logic and his emerging humanity, helps Spooner stop VIKI and restore human control.

documents.title: Open Range
documents.tagline: No place to run. No reason to hide.
documents.overview: A former gunslinger is forced to take up arms again when he and his cattle crew are threatened by a corrupt lawman.
documents.plot: A former gunslinger is forced to take up arms again when he and his cattle crew are threatened by a corrupt lawman.

documents.title: Original Sin
documents.tagline: This is not a love story – it's a story about love.
documents.overview: A young man is plunged into a life of subterfuge, deceit and mistaken identity in pursuit of a femme fatale whose heart is never quite within his grasp
documents.plot:
Original Sin is an American erotic romantic thriller of 2001 written and directed by Michael Cristofer, adapted from Cornell Woolrich's novel Waltz into Darkness (1947), which François Truffaut had earlier filmed as Mississippi Mermaid (1969). Antonio Banderas stars as Luis Vargas, a wealthy Cuban, and Angelina Jolie as Julia Russell, the mysterious woman who becomes his wife, with Thomas Jane as Walter Downs.

Set in Cuba under Spanish rule in the late nineteenth century, the story is told in flashbacks by a woman awaiting execution, who recounts her tale to a priest. Luis sends for an American mail-order bride from Delaware, Julia Russell. The woman who steps off the ship looks nothing like her photograph; she explains that she wanted a man who cared for more than a pretty face and sent a picture of a plainer woman. Luis confesses a deception of his own, having passed himself off as a modest clerk rather than a rich plantation owner. They marry within hours of her arrival, and Luis falls passionately in love. Julia's sister Emily writes anxious letters, and Luis makes Julia reply. He gives her full access to his accounts.

A private detective, Walter Downs, arrives from Wilmington, hired by Emily to find her sister, and Emily herself soon comes to Cuba, where she tells Luis that the woman he married is an impostor and that the real Julia may be dead. Julia vanishes with almost all of Luis's fortune. Searching for her with Downs, Luis finds her and learns that she is really Bonny Castle and that Downs is her lover and accomplice, Billy. Luis abandons his prosperous life to run away with her. Believing Billy dead after a confrontation in which Luis shoots him, the couple live in hiding, but one night Luis follows Bonny and discovers that Billy is alive and that she means to poison her husband that very night. When she returns, Luis tells her he knows, declares his love once more and drinks the poison anyway. Bonny flees with the dying Luis, and when Billy catches them at a train station and holds a knife to her throat, Luis wounds him and she finishes him off. Back in the present, after she has told her story, the guards find the priest kneeling in her cell in her clothes. Later, in Morocco, Bonny signals other players' cards to Luis at a gambling table.

Critics savaged the film as laughably melodramatic, giving it 12% on Rotten Tomatoes, and Jolie was nominated for the Golden Raspberry Award for Worst Actress for this and Lara Croft: Tomb Raider.

documents.title: National Treasure
documents.tagline: The greatest adventure history has ever revealed.
documents.overview: Modern treasure hunters, led by archaeologist Ben Gates, search for a chest of riches rumored to have been stashed away by George Washington, Thomas Jefferson and Benjamin Franklin during the Revolutionary War. The chest's whereabouts may lie in secret clues embedded in the Constitution and the Declaration of Independence, and Gates is in a race to find the gold before his enemies do.
documents.plot:
National Treasure is a 2004 American action-adventure film directed by Jon Turteltaub and produced by Jerry Bruckheimer. The movie stars Nicolas Cage as Benjamin Gates, a treasure hunter with a passion for American history.

The story begins with Benjamin Gates (Nicolas Cage), a historian and collector of rare documents, who is hired by the National Archives to authenticate a document that he believes will lead him to a long-lost treasure. The document, known as the "Declaration of Independence," has been stolen from the archives, and Gates sets out on a quest to retrieve it.

Gates teams up with his partner, Riley Poole (Justin Bartha), an expert in security systems, and Abigail Chase (Diane Kruger), a museum curator who is initially hesitant to join the adventure. Together, they embark on a perilous journey across the United States, following a series of cryptic clues and puzzles that lead them to various historical landmarks.

As they delve deeper into their quest, Gates and his team discover that the treasure is connected to the Knights Templar, a medieval military order that was thought to be extinct. They also uncover a conspiracy involving a wealthy businessman, Ian Howe (Sean Bean), who is determined to get his hands on the treasure for himself.

Throughout their journey, Gates and his team encounter various obstacles, including treacherous terrain, deadly traps, and rival treasure hunters. Along the way, they also learn more about the history of the Knights Templar and the significance of the treasure.

As the story unfolds, Gates and Abigail grow closer, and their relationship becomes a central theme in the movie. Meanwhile, Riley's loyalty is tested when he is forced to choose between his friendship with Gates and his own personal interests.

The film's climax features an action-packed sequence where Gates and his team face off against Howe and his henchmen at the Liberty Bell in Philadelphia. In the end, Gates successfully retrieves the Declaration of Independence and uncovers the location of the treasure, which is hidden beneath the bell.

In a thrilling finale, Gates and Abigail escape from the treasure chamber just as it collapses behind them, leaving them to ponder the secrets of the Knights Templar and the true meaning of the treasure. The movie concludes with Gates returning to his normal life, but with a newfound sense of purpose and a deeper appreciation for American history.

Overall, National Treasure is an entertaining adventure film that combines action, suspense, and historical intrigue. With its engaging storyline, memorable characters, and impressive set pieces, it has become a beloved classic among fans of the genre.

documents.title: Ratatouille
documents.tagline: He's dying to become a chef.
documents.overview: Remy, a resident of Paris, appreciates good food and has quite a sophisticated palate. He would love to become a chef so he can create and enjoy culinary masterpieces to his heart's delight. The only problem is, Remy is a rat. When he winds up in the sewer beneath one of Paris' finest restaurants, the rodent gourmet finds himself ideally placed to realize his dream.
documents.plot:
Ratatouille is a 2007 animated comedy-drama film produced by Pixar Animation Studios and released by Walt Disney Pictures.

The story follows Remy, a highly intelligent and ambitious rat who lives in the sewers of Paris. Remy has a passion for cooking and dreams of becoming a chef in one of the city's top restaurants. However, his species is not welcome in the culinary world, and he faces numerous obstacles in pursuing his dream.

One day, Remy meets Linguini, a klutzy but lovable human who works as a dishwasher at Gusteau's, a famous Parisian restaurant founded by the late Auguste Gusteau. Remy befriends Linguini and discovers that the restaurant is struggling to find its new chef after Gusteau's death.

Remy and Linguini form an unlikely partnership, with Remy using his culinary skills to create exquisite dishes while Linguini serves as the frontman for their collaboration. As they work together, they must keep their secret hidden from the restaurant's owner, Skinner, who is determined to find a new chef to replace Gusteau.

Throughout the film, Remy and Linguini face various challenges, including a health inspector who threatens to shut down the restaurant and a rival chef who seeks to sabotage their success. Along the way, they learn valuable lessons about teamwork, perseverance, and believing in oneself.

The film features stunning animation, witty dialogue, and memorable characters, making it a delightful and entertaining experience for audiences of all ages. The voice cast, including Patton Oswalt as Remy and Lou Romano as Linguini, delivers outstanding performances that bring the characters to life.

Overall, Ratatouille is a heartwarming and visually stunning film that celebrates the power of creativity, friendship, and following one's dreams.

documents.title: Mission to Mars
documents.tagline: Let There Be Life.
documents.overview: When contact is lost with the crew of the first Mars expedition, a rescue mission is launched to discover their fate.
documents.plot:
Mission to Mars is a science fiction film that explores the human condition and our relationship with technology. The story follows a team of astronauts on a mission to Mars, where they encounter unexpected challenges and discoveries that force them to re-evaluate their priorities and values.

At its core, Mission to Mars is a film about the dangers of unchecked ambition and the importance of humility in the face of the unknown. The characters are driven by a desire to explore and discover, but as they delve deeper into the Martian environment, they begin to realize that there are limits to human knowledge and control.

The film also explores themes of faith and spirituality, particularly in the character of Dr. John McKay (played by Gary Sinise), who begins to question the true nature of their mission and the existence of a higher power. As the team faces numerous setbacks and failures, they are forced to confront the possibility that their actions may not be as selfless or altruistic as they initially thought.

Ultimately, Mission to Mars is a film about the human spirit's capacity for resilience, adaptability, and growth in the face of adversity. Despite the many challenges and disappointments they encounter, the characters ultimately emerge with a deeper understanding of themselves and their place in the universe.

documents.title: The Whole Nine Yards
documents.tagline: In the heart of suburbia, a hit man with heart has just moved in.
documents.overview: After a mobster agrees to cooperate with an FBI investigation in order to stay out of prison, he's relocated by the authorities to a life of suburban anonymity as part of a witness protection program. It's not long before a couple of his new neighbours figure out his true identity and come knocking to see if he'd be up for one more hit—suburban style.
