documents.title: Halloween
documents.tagline: Evil has a destiny.
documents.overview: After being committed for 17 years, Michael Myers, now a grown man and still very dangerous, escapes from the mental institution (where he was committed as a 10 year old) and he immediately returns to Haddonfield, where he wants to find his baby sister, Laurie. Anyone who crosses his path is in mortal danger.
documents.plot:
Halloween is a 2007 American slasher film written, produced and directed by Rob Zombie. A remake of John Carpenter's 1978 film and the ninth installment in the Halloween franchise, it was conceived as both a remake and an origin story for Michael Myers. Malcolm McDowell plays Dr. Samuel Loomis, Daeg Faerch the ten-year-old Michael and Tyler Mane the adult Michael, with Scout Taylor-Compton, Sheri Moon Zombie, Brad Dourif, Danielle Harris and William Forsythe also in the cast.

On Halloween 1990 in Haddonfield, Illinois, ten-year-old Michael, who has already shown psychopathic tendencies, murders a school bully, his abusive stepfather Ronnie, his older sister Judith and her boyfriend, sparing only his baby sister, whom he calls "Boo". He is committed to Smith's Grove Sanitarium under the care of the child psychologist Loomis. Michael gradually withdraws into making papier-mâché masks, even from his devoted mother Deborah. When he kills a nurse at the end of one of her visits, Deborah cannot cope and takes her own life. Fifteen years later, after Loomis has closed his case, Michael escapes, killing guards and staff, returns to Haddonfield and retrieves the kitchen knife and mask he hid beneath the floorboards of his abandoned childhood home. Teenager Laurie Strode notices him watching her during the day. That night he kills her friend Lynda and Lynda's boyfriend Bob at his old house, then murders Laurie's parents while she is babysitting Tommy Doyle. Arriving in town with a handgun, Loomis warns Sheriff Leigh Brackett, who reveals that Laurie is in fact Michael's baby sister, adopted by the Strodes after their mother's suicide. Michael kills Paul, boyfriend of Laurie's friend Annie Brackett, and leaves Annie badly injured, then pursues Laurie and carries her to the old Myers house, where he shows her a photograph of the two of them. Not understanding, she stabs him and flees. Loomis shoots Michael, but Michael recovers, recaptures Laurie and crushes the doctor's skull. Laurie hides inside the walls until Michael corners her and both fall from a balcony; she wakes over his body and, as he grabs her wrist, fires the gun and screams as sirens approach.

Released in the United States by Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer on August 31, 2007, Halloween set a Labor Day weekend record and grossed $80 million worldwide on a $15 million budget despite generally negative reviews, including a 28% Rotten Tomatoes rating. A sequel, Halloween II, followed in 2009.

documents.title: Birthday Girl
documents.tagline: Be careful what you wish for
documents.overview: A shy bank clerk orders a Russian mail order bride, and finds his life turned upside down.
documents.plot: John is a mild-mannered banker who has never been lucky in love. Fed up with waiting for the right girl to come along, John takes a chance on a Russian mail-order bride arranged via the Internet, where he is introduced to Nadia. John's fondness for Nadia grows... until the sudden arrival of Nadia's gregarious cousins makes John realize that he's in over his head.

documents.title: Romeo Must Die
documents.tagline: In the city ruled by criminals, two families have forgotten their fear. He will make them remember.
documents.overview: Two warring gang families (one African-American, the other Chinese) maneuver for bragging rights to the Oakland, California, docks. Hang Sing and Trish O'Day uncover a trail of deceit that leaves most of the warring factions dead … or worse!
documents.plot:
Romeo Must Die is a 2000 martial arts action film directed by Andrzej Bartkowiak and starring Jet Li, Aaliyah, and Jason Statham.

The movie begins with the introduction of Han Song (Jet Li), a Chinese-American martial artist who seeks revenge against the Triads for killing his father. Han's quest for vengeance is motivated by a personal tragedy: his father was killed in a fight with the Triads when he was just a child, and Han has been training to avenge him ever since.

Meanwhile, in Los Angeles, a young woman named Trish O'Day (Aaliyah) becomes embroiled in a gang war between the Chinese and Japanese Yakuza. The conflict escalates into violence, with both sides seeking to gain control of the city's underworld.

As Han navigates the treacherous world of organized crime, he meets Keiko (Mai Takara), a Japanese woman who is somehow connected to his father's death. Through her, Han discovers that his father was involved in a secret alliance between the Chinese and Japanese Triads, which aimed to take down their common enemy: the Yakuza.

As tensions rise, Han finds himself caught in the middle of a deadly conflict between the two rival gangs. With the help of Keiko and her brother, Jax (Jason Statham), Han must use his martial arts skills to survive and bring justice to those responsible for his father's death.

Throughout the movie, the action unfolds at a breakneck pace, with intense fight scenes that showcase Jet Li's impressive martial arts abilities. The film also explores themes of loyalty, honor, and family, as Han struggles to reconcile his own identity as a Chinese-American with his desire for revenge against the Triads.

As the story reaches its climax, Han confronts the leader of the Triads, Tiger Chen (John Lone), in an epic showdown that will determine the fate of both gangs. In the end, Han emerges victorious, but not without scars – both physical and emotional.

Ultimately, Romeo Must Die is a classic action movie with a richly detailed world and memorable characters. While it received mixed reviews from critics at the time of its release, the film has since become a cult classic, celebrated for its innovative blend of martial arts and gangster cinema.

documents.title: The Last Castle
documents.tagline: A Castle Can Only Have One King
documents.overview: A court-martialed general rallies together 1200 inmates to rise against the system that put him away.
documents.plot:
The Last Castle is a 2001 American prison action drama directed by Rod Lurie and starring Robert Redford as Lieutenant General Eugene Irwin, James Gandolfini as Colonel Winter, Mark Ruffalo as Yates and Delroy Lindo as Brigadier General Wheeler. The film depicts a struggle between the inmates and the commandant of a maximum-security military prison modeled on the United States Disciplinary Barracks at Fort Leavenworth.

Eugene Irwin, a highly decorated three-star general, is court-martialed and sentenced to ten years in prison for disobeying a presidential order by sending his troops on a rescue mission in Burundi that cost the lives of eight soldiers. The prison's commandant, Colonel Winter, initially admires Irwin, but is deeply offended when he overhears the general dismissing his collection of military artifacts as something no real combat veteran would keep. Winter, who has never seen combat, rules the prison harshly, insisting that the inmates are no longer soldiers and must not observe military customs.

Irwin gradually earns the respect of the prisoners, who begin to rediscover their pride and sense of unity. He organizes them to build a stone wall in the prison yard, resembling the wall of a castle, but Winter orders it destroyed, and a young inmate, Corporal Aguilar, is killed by a rubber bullet fired on Winter's orders. Outraged, Irwin demands Winter's resignation and secretly organizes the prisoners into a disciplined military unit, planning a revolt designed to seize control of the prison and prove to Winter's superior, General Wheeler, that the commandant is unfit for command. Winter, aided by Yates, a cynical inmate he bribes to become his informant, prepares to crush the uprising by any means necessary.

The film explores themes of honor, leadership and the meaning of military duty, culminating in the symbolic act of raising the American flag over the prison.

The Last Castle was released in October 2001 and was a financial disappointment, grossing about 27.6 million dollars against a 72 million dollar budget. It received mixed reviews, with 52 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus called it well acted and rousing but unable to stand up to close scrutiny, and a Metacritic score of 43.

documents.title: Solaris
documents.tagline: How far will you go for a second chance?
documents.overview: A troubled psychologist is sent to investigate the crew of an isolated research station orbiting a bizarre planet.
documents.plot: A troubled psychologist is sent to investigate the crew of an isolated research station orbiting a bizarre planet.

documents.title: American Pie
documents.tagline: There's nothing like your first piece.
documents.overview: At a high-school party, four friends find that losing their collective virginity isn't as easy as they had thought. But they still believe that they need to do so before college. To motivate themselves, they enter a pact to all "score" by their senior prom.
documents.plot:
American Pie is a coming-of-age comedy film released in 1999, directed by Paul Weiland and written by Adam Herz. The movie follows the lives of four high school friends - Jim Levenstein (Jason Biggs), Finch (Eddie Kaye Thomas), Oz (Chris Klein), and Kevin (Thomas Ian Nicholas) - as they navigate love, friendship, and growing up in the suburban town of Chappaqua, New York.

The film begins with the introduction of the main characters, showcasing their unique personalities and quirks. Jim is a naive and awkward teenager who has just moved to Chappaqua from Chicago with his family. Finch is a brainiac who is obsessed with sex and relationships. Oz is a charismatic athlete who is struggling to find his place in the world. Kevin is a laid-back jock who is trying to balance his athletic career with his desire for love.

The story takes a turn when Jim's parents announce that they are getting divorced, leaving Jim feeling lost and uncertain about his future. The group of friends decides to take matters into their own hands and create a "pie" - a sex manual - to help Jim lose his virginity before he leaves for college.

As the movie progresses, the friends embark on a series of misadventures, including a disastrous trip to the local water park, a botched attempt at seduction, and a wild party that ends in chaos. Along the way, they learn valuable lessons about friendship, loyalty, and growing up.

One of the most memorable aspects of American Pie is its portrayal of male adolescence, capturing the awkwardness, insecurity, and humor that defines this stage of life. The film's script is full of witty one-liners, clever references, and hilarious situations that have become iconic in pop culture.

Throughout the movie, the characters face various challenges, including romantic relationships, family drama, and peer pressure. Jim's journey to lose his virginity becomes a central plot point, as he navigates his feelings for his crush, Michelle (Alyson Hannigan). The film's climax features a memorable scene in which Jim finally loses his virginity, but not before learning valuable lessons about himself and his relationships.

American Pie was a critical and commercial success, grossing over $235 million worldwide. The movie spawned two sequels, American Pie 2 (2001) and American Wedding (2003), as well as several spin-offs and merchandise. The film's impact on popular culture is undeniable, cementing its place as a classic coming-of-age comedy of the late 1990s.

Overall, American Pie is a hilarious and relatable movie that captures the essence of male adolescence with humor, wit, and heart. Its memorable characters, witty script, and iconic moments have made it a beloved favorite among audiences for generations.

documents.title: Wasabi
documents.tagline: For those who take their action raw.
documents.overview: Hubert is a French policeman with very sharp methods. After being forced to take 2 months off by his boss, who doesn't share his view on working methods, he goes back to Japan, where he used to work 19 years ago, to settle the probate of his girlfriend who left him shortly after marriage without a trace.

documents.title: Final Fantasy: The Spirits Within
documents.tagline: Unleash a new reality
documents.overview: Led by a strange dream, scientist Aki Ross struggles to collect the eight spirits in the hope of creating a force powerful enough to protect the planet. With the aid of the Deep Eyes Squadron and her mentor, Dr. Sid, Aki must save the Earth from its darkest hate and unleash the spirits within.
documents.plot:
Final Fantasy: The Spirits Within is a 2001 computer-animated science fiction film directed by Hironobu Sakaguchi, the creator of the Final Fantasy video game series. A Japanese-American co-production made by Square Pictures, it was the first feature film to attempt photorealistic computer-generated humans and, for nearly a decade, the most expensive film inspired by a video game. The voice cast includes Ming-Na Wen as Dr. Aki Ross, Alec Baldwin as Captain Gray Edwards, Donald Sutherland as Dr. Sid, James Woods as General Hein, Ving Rhames, Peri Gilpin and Steve Buscemi.

In 2065, Earth has been overrun by alien beings known as Phantoms, which kill living creatures on contact by consuming their spirit, while lesser contact can cause infection. The surviving humans live in "barrier cities" protected by energy shields. Aki, who has been infected by a Phantom, works with her mentor, Dr. Sid, who believes that the Phantoms can be neutralized by combining eight spirit waves, unique energy patterns found in various life forms. While searching for the sixth spirit in the ruins of New York City, Aki is rescued by Gray, her former lover, and his squad, the Deep Eyes, consisting of Ryan Whittaker, Neil Fleming and Jane Proudfoot.

Before the ruling council, Aki and Sid clash with General Hein, who wants to use the Zeus cannon, a powerful space-based weapon, to destroy the Phantoms at the site of the meteor on which they arrived. Sid warns that firing the cannon could harm the Earth's own spirit, or Gaia. Hein, embittered by the loss of his family to the Phantoms, manipulates events to win approval for the weapon, including allowing Phantoms into the barrier city. As Aki's infection worsens, her dreams reveal the truth about the Phantoms: they are the spirits of the inhabitants of a destroyed alien planet, still trapped in the throes of their death. With Hein determined to fire the cannon regardless of the consequences, Aki, Gray and Sid race to gather the final spirits and save the planet.

The film was celebrated for its technical achievement, but critics found its story dull and emotionally distant; it holds a 44 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 49. It grossed about $85 million worldwide against a budget of around $137 million, becoming one of the biggest animated box-office failures and contributing to the closure of Square Pictures.

documents.title: Out of Time
documents.tagline: The Clock Is Ticking...
documents.overview: Matt Lee Whitlock, respected chief of police in small Banyan Key, Florida, must solve a vicious double homicide before he himself falls under suspicion. Matt Lee has to stay a few steps ahead of his own police force and everyone he's trusted in order to find out the truth.
documents.plot:
Out of Time is a 2003 American crime thriller directed by Carl Franklin and starring Denzel Washington as Matt Lee Whitlock, the police chief of a small town in the Florida Keys. The film, Franklin and Washington's second collaboration after Devil in a Blue Dress (1995), co-stars Eva Mendes as Matt's estranged wife Alex, Sanaa Lathan as Ann Merai-Harrison and Dean Cain as Ann's husband Chris, with John Billingsley as the medical examiner Chae.

Matt Whitlock is the respected chief of police in Banyan Key. Going through a divorce from Alex, a homicide detective, he is having an affair with his high school sweetheart Ann, who is trapped in an abusive marriage to Chris, a former professional football player. When Ann tells him she has been diagnosed with terminal cancer and names him the beneficiary of her million-dollar life insurance policy, Matt wants to help her pay for an experimental treatment abroad. In a moment of desperation, he takes nearly half a million dollars in drug money from the police evidence room and gives it to her.

Soon afterward, Ann and Chris's house burns down, and two bodies are found inside. The money has disappeared, and Matt learns that Ann's cancer diagnosis was a lie and that he has been set up. To make matters worse, Alex is assigned to investigate the double homicide, and every clue she uncovers, including the insurance policy, points to Matt as the prime suspect. At the same time, federal agents arrive to collect the evidence money for a case. Racing against the clock, Matt must stay one step ahead of his own wife's investigation, destroy or explain the evidence against him and find out who framed him before his career and freedom are lost.

The film is a twisting neo-noir set against the sun-drenched backdrop of the Florida Keys, relying on suspense, misdirection and Washington's charismatic lead performance.

Out of Time was released in the United States on October 3, 2003. It received generally positive reviews, with 65 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus called it a fun and stylish thriller if one can get past its contrivances, and a Metacritic score of 63. At the Black Reel Awards it won Best Theatrical Film, and Lathan won Best Actress.

documents.title: The Whole Ten Yards
documents.tagline: They missed each other. This time, their aim is better.
documents.overview: Jimmy "The Tulip" Tudeski now spends his days compulsively cleaning his house and perfecting his culinary skills with his wife, Jill, a purported assassin who has yet to pull off a clean hit. Suddenly, an uninvited and unwelcome connection to their past unexpectedly shows up on Jimmy and Jill's doorstep; it's Oz, and he's begging them to help him rescue his wife, Cynthia.

documents.title: Me, Myself & Irene
documents.tagline: From gentle to mental.
documents.overview: Rhode Island State Trooper Charlie Baileygates has a multiple personality disorder. One personality is crazy and aggressive, while the other is more friendly and laid back. Both of these personalities fall in love with the same woman named Irene after Charlie loses his medication.
documents.plot:
Me, Myself & Irene is a 2000 American black comedy film directed by the Farrelly brothers, written by Bobby Moresco and Peter Farrelly, and starring Jim Carrey. The movie was produced by 20th Century Fox.

The story revolves around Charlie McMillan (played by Jim Carrey), a state trooper who suffers from multiple personality disorder (MPD). He has two distinct personalities: Charlie McMillan, the mild-mannered and responsible police officer, and Hank Evans, a rough-around-the-edges, hot-headed, and violent individual.

The movie begins with Charlie's arrest for drunk driving. During his arrest, he is taken to a psychiatric hospital, where he meets Dr. Lillian Hurst (played by Renée Zellweger), a psychiatrist who specializes in treating MPD patients. She agrees to help Charlie manage his condition, and they begin therapy sessions together.

As the story progresses, we see glimpses of both personalities, with Hank's aggressive behavior causing trouble for Charlie at work and home. However, when a young woman named Irene (played by Renée Zellweger) is kidnapped by a group of armed robbers, Charlie must use his unique skills to track them down.

As the investigation unfolds, we see more of Charlie's dual personality, with Hank taking over in situations that require aggression and violence. Meanwhile, Dr. Hurst tries to help Charlie understand and control his condition, while also developing feelings for him.

The plot thickens when it is revealed that Irene is actually a woman who was kidnapped by the robbers, and she has been hiding out at a remote cabin. Charlie must use both personalities to infiltrate the robbers' hideout and rescue Irene.

In the climactic final scene, Charlie faces off against the leader of the robbers, a ruthless individual known as "The Kid" (played by George Segal). With Hank's help, Charlie is able to overpower The Kid and save Irene. However, in the process, he also loses control of his condition, leading to a chaotic and violent confrontation.

In the end, Charlie is able to reconcile with both personalities, and Dr. Hurst helps him find a way to manage his MPD. The movie concludes with Charlie and Irene sharing a romantic moment, as Charlie finally finds a sense of peace and stability in his life.

Throughout the movie, Jim Carrey delivers a standout performance, showcasing his impressive range as an actor. His portrayal of both Charlie and Hank is nuanced and convincing, making it easy to become invested in their story. The supporting cast, including Renée Zellweger and George Segal, also deliver memorable performances that add to the film's humor and charm.

Overall, Me, Myself & Irene is a hilarious and heartwarming movie that explores themes of identity, relationships, and personal growth. With its unique blend of comedy and drama, it has become a cult classic that continues to delight audiences to this day.

documents.title: The Perfect Storm
documents.tagline: The storm is coming.
documents.overview: In October 1991, a confluence of weather conditions combined to form a killer storm in the North Atlantic. Caught in the storm was the sword-fishing boat Andrea Gail. Magnificent foreshadowing and anticipation fill this true-life drama while minute details of the fishing boats, their gear and the weather are juxtaposed with the sea adventure.
documents.plot:
The Perfect Storm is a biographical drama film directed by Wolfgang Petersen, released in 2000 by Warner Bros. Pictures.

The movie is based on the non-fiction book of the same name by Sebastian Junger and is inspired by the true story of the commercial fishing boat Andrea Gail, which was caught in the infamous Hurricane Grace in 1991 off the coast of New England.

The film begins with a dramatic opening sequence showing the stormy weather conditions, setting the tone for the rest of the movie. We are introduced to Billy Tyne (played by George Clooney), a young and ambitious fisherman who is part of a crew on the Andrea Gail, a commercial fishing boat that sets sail from Gloucester, Massachusetts.

The crew, led by Captain Bobby Shatford (played by Mark Wahlberg), includes seasoned fishermen like First Mate Dale "Murph" Murphy (played by Diane Lane) and Deckhand Bobby's brother, Mike (played by John C. Reilly). The crew is on a mission to catch the largest lobster in history, but their journey takes an unexpected turn when they are caught in Hurricane Grace.

As the storm intensifies, the crew faces numerous challenges, including treacherous seas, equipment failure, and personal conflicts. Despite these obstacles, Captain Shatford's leadership skills and experience prove invaluable as he navigates the boat through the raging tempest.

Meanwhile, Billy Tyne finds himself drawn to First Mate Murphy, who becomes a love interest for him. The tension between them is palpable, but their relationship is put to the test as they face the harsh realities of being at sea during a hurricane.

As the storm rages on, the crew faces an unprecedented challenge: the boat is taking on water at an alarming rate, and it's unclear if they'll make it back to shore. The tension builds as the crew fights to keep their vessel afloat, but ultimately, the Andrea Gail succumbs to the fury of the hurricane.

The film's climax is both heart-wrenching and awe-inspiring, as the crew members fight for survival against all odds. In the end, only one member of the crew survives: First Mate Murphy, who finds herself washed up on the shore, her body battered but alive.

The Perfect Storm is a gripping drama that explores themes of courage, sacrifice, and the human spirit in the face of nature's fury. The film features outstanding performances from its cast, particularly Mark Wahlberg as Captain Bobby Shatford, who brings depth and nuance to his portrayal of the seasoned fisherman.

Overall, The Perfect Storm is an intense and emotional ride that will keep you on the edge of your seat from start to finish.

documents.title: The Time Machine
documents.tagline: The greatest adventure THROUGH all time!
documents.overview: Hoping to alter the events of the past, a 19th century inventor instead travels 800,000 years into the future, where he finds mankind divided into two warring races.
documents.plot:
The Time Machine is a 2002 American science fiction adventure film directed by Simon Wells, great-grandson of H. G. Wells, and loosely adapted by John Logan from Wells's 1895 novel and George Pal's 1960 film. Moving the story from London to New York, it adds a romantic subplot, a new explanation for the fall of civilization and new characters including a holographic librarian and a Morlock leader. It stars Guy Pearce, Orlando Jones, Samantha Mumba in her film debut, Mark Addy and Jeremy Irons, with a cameo by Alan Young from the 1960 version.

In 1899, Alexander Hartdegen is an inventor teaching at Columbia University who, unlike his friend David Philby, prefers pure research to business. When a mugger kills his fiancée, Emma, he spends four years building a time machine, returns to 1899 and saves her, only for her to die in a road accident instead. Realizing that she cannot be saved, he travels to 2030, where a holographic librarian, Vox 114, at the New York Public Library tells him that changing the past is impossible. Stopping in 2037, he finds that lunar colonization has shattered the Moon, threatening Earth, and is knocked unconscious as he restarts the machine.

He wakes 800,000 years later. The planet has healed, and the surviving humans, the Eloi, live a simple life in cliffside dwellings above what was Manhattan. Mara, one of the few who speak English, nurses him back to health. The Eloi are hunted by ape-like Morlocks, who drag Mara underground. Guided by Kalen, Mara's younger brother, and the still-working Vox 114, Alex enters the Morlocks' lair, where a telepathic Über-Morlock explains that the Morlocks descend from humans who went underground after the Moon broke apart and now breed the Eloi as food. He adds that Alex can never save Emma, since her death is why he built the machine. Ordered home, Alex instead drags the Über-Morlock into the time stream, where he ages to death. Glimpsing a desolate far future, Alex returns to free Mara and sabotages the machine with his pocket watch, and the resulting time distortion destroys the Morlocks' caves. He stays to build a new life with Mara and the Eloi, and in 1903 Philby concludes that his friend has found peace.

Postponed from December 2001 to March 2002, partly to avoid The Lord of the Rings, the film opened at number one and grossed $123 million worldwide. Critics were unimpressed, giving it 28% on Rotten Tomatoes and finding its shift from lost love to confusing action weak.

documents.title: Reindeer Games
documents.tagline: The trap is set. The game is on.
documents.overview: After assuming his dead cellmate's identity to get with his girlfriend, an ex-con finds himself the reluctant participant in a casino heist.

documents.overview: The prospects for continuing life on Earth in the year 2058 are grim. So the Robinsons are launched into space to colonize Alpha Prime, the only other inhabitable planet in the galaxy. But when a stowaway sabotages the mission, the Robinsons find themselves hurtling through uncharted space.

documents.title: Fantastic Voyage
documents.tagline: A Fantastic and Spectacular Voyage... Through the Human Body... Into the Brain.
documents.overview: In order to save an assassinated scientist, a submarine and its crew are shrunk to microscopic size and injected into his bloodstream.
documents.plot:
The U.S.A. and the U.S.S.R. have both developed technology that can miniaturize matter by shrinking individual atoms, but only for one hour. A scientist, Dr. Jan Benes, working behind the Iron Curtain, has figured out how to make the process work indefinitely. With the help of American intelligence agents, including agent Charles Grant, he escapes to the Western world and arrives in NYC, but an attempted assassination leaves him comatose with a blood clot in his brain that no surgery can remove from the outside.
To save his life, Grant, U.S. Navy submariner Captain Bill Owens, medical chief and circulatory specialist Dr. Michaels, surgeon Dr. Peter Duval, and his assistant Cora Peterson are placed aboard a Navy ichthyology submarine at the Combined Miniature Deterrent Forces (CMDF) facilities. The submarine, named Proteus, is then miniaturized to "about the size of a microbe" and injected into Benes' body. The team has 60 minutes to get to the clot, remove it, and exit Benes' body; if they do not get out in time, the Proteus and its crew will begin reverting to their normal size, which will either place them under attack from Benes' immune system or kill Benes himself.
The crew faces many obstacles during the mission. An undetected AV fistula forces them to detour through the heart, where they must induce SCA to reduce turbulence strong enough to destroy the Proteus. The crew faces an unexplained loss of oxygen and must replenish their supply in the lungs. They notice "rocks" that are actually carbon particles from smoke. Grant finds the surgical laser needed to destroy the clot was damaged from the turbulence in the heart, as it was not fastened down as it had been before; this, and his safety line snapping loose while the crew was refilling their air supply, led Grant to suspect a saboteur. The crew must cannibalize their wireless radio to repair the laser, cutting off all communication and guidance from the outside, although because the submarine is nuclear-powered, surgeons and technicians outside Benes's body can still track their movements via a radioactive tracer, allowing General Alan Carter and Colonel Donald Reid, the officers in charge of CMDF, to figure out the crew's strategies as they make their way through the body.
The sub enters the lymphatic system, but the reticular fibers start to interfere. This forces the crew to pass through the inner ear, requiring all outside personnel to make no noise to prevent destructive shocks, but while the crew is removing reticular fibers clogging the submarine's vents and making the engines overheat, a fallen surgical tool causes the crew to be thrown about and Peterson to be nearly killed by antibodies, but they are able to reboard the submarine in time. By the time they finally reach the clot, the crew has only six minutes remaining to operate and then exit the body.

documents.title: The Glass House
documents.tagline: The glass is about to be shattered...
documents.overview: When Ruby and Rhett's parents are killed in a car accident, their carefree teenage lives are suddenly shattered. Moving to an incredible house in Malibu with the Glasses', old friends of the family, seems to be the beginning of a new life for them.
documents.plot:
The Glass House is a psychological thriller film that revolves around the complex relationships and dark secrets within a wealthy family. At its core, the movie explores the theme of toxic family dynamics, where the pursuit of power, status, and material wealth can lead to corruption, manipulation, and ultimately, destruction.

The film delves into the idea of how the past can come back to haunt the present, and how the actions of one individual can have far-reaching consequences for those around them. The main character, Rachel Kemp, is a prime example of this, as her seemingly perfect life begins to unravel, revealing a web of deceit and betrayal that threatens to destroy everything she holds dear.

The movie also touches on the theme of identity and how it can be shaped by external forces. As the characters navigate their complex relationships and confront their dark pasts, they are forced to question who they truly are and what they want from life.

Furthermore, The Glass House critiques the excesses of wealth and privilege, highlighting the emptiness and superficiality that can result from a life of luxury. The film's portrayal of the wealthy elite as morally bankrupt and self-absorbed serves as a commentary on the darker aspects of the American Dream.

Overall, The Glass House is a gripping thriller that explores the complexities of human relationships, the destructive power of secrets and lies, and the corrupting influence of wealth and privilege.

documents.title: Tenacious D in The Pick of Destiny
documents.original_title: Tenacious D in The Pick of Destiny
documents.tagline: An epic quest. A magical guitar pick. A chance to put the D in Destiny.
documents.overview: In Venice Beach, naive Midwesterner JB bonds with local slacker KG and they form the rock band Tenacious D. Setting out to become the world's greatest band is no easy feat, so they set out to steal what could be the answer to their prayers... a magical guitar pick housed in a rock-and-roll museum some 300 miles away.

documents.title: Death at a Funeral
documents.tagline: Last rites... and wrongs.
documents.overview: A myriad of outrageous calamities befall an eccentric English clan with more than a few skeletons in its closets, when its patriarch dies an unexpected death. Soon, every complication imaginable befall the grief-stricken mourners.
documents.plot:
Death at a Funeral is a 2007 comedy film that explores the complexities of family dynamics and cultural differences through the lens of a traditional African funeral. The movie delves into the theme of cultural identity, highlighting the tensions between the protagonist's desire to honor his father's heritage and the expectations of his more modern, Westernized relatives.

The film also examines the concept of grief and mourning, showcasing how different cultures approach death and bereavement in unique ways. Through the character of Zahir (played by Simon Pegg), a well-meaning but awkward British man who is struggling to navigate his father's funeral, we see the challenges of bridging cultural divides and finding common ground with those from different backgrounds.

Furthermore, Death at a Funeral touches on the theme of identity and belonging. As Zahir tries to reconcile his own sense of self with the expectations of his family and community, he begins to question what it means to be a good son, a good friend, and a good person in the face of death and loss.

Ultimately, the movie presents a nuanced exploration of the human experience, revealing that even in the midst of chaos and cultural confusion, there is room for love, laughter, and connection.

documents.tagline: 1 witness… 118 minutes…
documents.overview: An aging cop is assigned the ordinary task of escorting a fast-talking witness from police custody to a courthouse, but they find themselves running the gauntlet as other forces try to prevent them from getting there.

documents.title: The Last Mimzy
documents.tagline: The future is trying to tell us something.
documents.overview: Two siblings begin to develop special talents after they find a mysterious box of toys, and soon their parents and even their teacher are drawn into a strange new world – and find a task ahead of them that is far more important than any of them could imagine.
documents.plot:
The Last Mimzy is a 2007 American fantasy drama film directed by Paul McGuigan. The story revolves around a young boy named Josh Baskin, who discovers that he has inherited a mysterious toy from his recently deceased grandmother.

As Josh delves deeper into the world of the toy, known as "Mimzy," he learns about its incredible powers and the responsibility that comes with it. Through his journey, Josh must navigate the complexities of growing up, family secrets, and the consequences of playing with forces beyond human control.

At its core, The Last Mimzy explores themes of identity, belonging, and the struggle to find one's place in the world. As Josh grapples with the weight of his newfound powers, he is forced to confront the challenges of adolescence, including self-discovery, peer pressure, and the desire for independence.

The film also touches on the idea of legacy and the importance of understanding where we come from. Through Josh's connection to his grandmother, the story highlights the significance of family history and the lessons that are passed down through generations.

Ultimately, The Last Mimzy is a heartwarming and thought-provoking tale about a young boy's journey towards self-discovery, growth, and acceptance.

documents.title: The Golden Compass
documents.tagline: There are worlds beyond our own - the compass will show the way.
documents.overview: After overhearing a shocking secret, precocious orphan Lyra Belacqua trades her carefree existence roaming the halls of Jordan College for an otherworldly adventure in the far North, unaware that it's part of her destiny.
documents.plot:
The Golden Compass is a fantasy adventure film directed by Chris Weitz, based on the novel of the same name by Philip Pullman. The movie was released in 2007 and produced by New Line Cinema.

In a parallel universe, humans and talking animals coexist, with humans divided into castes. The story follows Lyra Belacqua (played by Nicole Kidman), a young orphan girl who lives in a world where people's souls take the form of animal companions called daemons. Lyra's daemon is a monkey named Pantalaimon.

The movie begins in a world where humans are forced to wear special uniforms and live in a society controlled by the Magisterium, a powerful organization that seeks to control all aspects of life. The story takes place in a future England, where the Magisterium has outlawed talking animals and anyone who can see them is persecuted.

Lyra's world is turned upside down when she discovers that her friend Roger (played by Dakota Blue Richards) has been kidnapped by the Gobblers, a mysterious organization that is rumored to be experimenting on children. Lyra sets out on a journey to find Roger, accompanied by her daemon Pantalaimon and a group of allies, including Lord Asriel (played by Daniel Craig), a charismatic and enigmatic figure who claims to be her uncle.

As they embark on their perilous journey, Lyra and her companions encounter various obstacles, including the armored bears of the Gyptians, a nomadic people who live in the frozen tundra. They also meet Lee Scoresby (played by Sam Elliott), a Gyptian aeronaut who becomes an ally to Lyra.

Throughout their journey, Lyra learns about the secrets of the Gobblers and the true nature of the Magisterium's control over society. She discovers that the Gobblers are searching for children with special abilities, known as Dust, which is a magical substance that allows humans to breathe in the air of other worlds.

As they near their destination, Lyra and her companions face numerous challenges, including fierce battles with armored bears and treacherous landscapes. Along the way, Lyra also learns about her own destiny and the secrets of her past.

The movie culminates in a dramatic showdown between Lyra and the Gobblers' leader, Mrs. Coulter (played by Jennifer Connelly), who is revealed to be a powerful and ruthless adversary. In the end, Lyra and her companions succeed in defeating the Gobblers and freeing Roger from their clutches.

However, the movie ends on a cliffhanger, with Lyra learning that she has been given a choice: to return to her own world or to enter a parallel universe where she can explore the secrets of Dust. The ending sets the stage for the next installment in the series, which was not produced due to the negative reception of the film.

Overall, The Golden Compass is a thrilling adventure film that explores themes of power, control, and self-discovery. With its richly imagined world and memorable characters, it has become a beloved classic among fans of fantasy literature and cinema.

documents.title: Day Watch
documents.tagline: The second chapter in the epic fantasy trilogy
documents.overview: A man who serves in the war between the forces of Light and Dark comes into possession of a device that can restore life to Moscow, which was nearly destroyed by an apocalyptic event.
documents.plot:
Day Watch (Russian: Дневной дозор) is a 2006 Russian dark fantasy film directed and co-written by Timur Bekmambetov, the sequel to Night Watch (2004). Although it shares its title with the second novel in Sergei Lukyanenko's series, it is based on the later parts of the novel Night Watch. Konstantin Khabensky returns as Anton Gorodetsky, with Mariya Poroshina as Svetlana, Vladimir Menshov as Gesser, Viktor Verzhbitsky as Zavulon, Dmitriy Martynov as Yegor, Galina Tyunina as Olga and Zhanna Friske as Alisa.

In the first film, Anton discovered he was an Other after asking a witch in 1992 to win back his unfaithful wife at the cost of her unborn child. Years later he learned that the boy, Yegor, was in fact his own son, and the teenager, an immensely powerful Other, sided with the Dark after realising his father had once tried to have him killed.

Now a member of the Night Watch, Anton is training the gifted Svetlana while secretly covering up Yegor's attacks on ordinary people, trying to protect his son and preserve the fragile truce between Light and Dark. He also hunts for the Chalk of Fate, a legendary artefact once owned by Tamerlane that can rewrite history. Zavulon, head of the Day Watch, frames Anton for the murders of several Dark Others, and Gesser hides him by swapping his body with that of the sorceress Olga. Unaware of the switch, Svetlana confesses her love for Anton to "Olga", and Anton is eventually pushed into admitting he loves her too.

Anton retrieves the Chalk and uses it to summon Yegor, but their reconciliation collapses when the boy learns of his father's feelings for Svetlana and leaves with the artefact, which Zavulon passes to his lover Alisa. At Yegor's birthday party, Anton tries to expose the true killer, but Svetlana quarrels with Yegor and draws a drop of his blood, giving Zavulon a pretext to break the truce. Yegor unleashes destruction on Moscow, and a battle between Light and Dark erupts.

Persuading Alisa to hand over the Chalk, which can only undo the user's own choices, Anton returns to the ruined building where he met the witch and writes "No" on the wall. History resets to 1992: the young Anton walks away from the deal, never becomes an Other, and Moscow is spared, yet he still recognises Svetlana as she passes and follows her.

Fox Searchlight acquired international rights, and the film opened in the United States in 2007, earning 62% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 59.

documents.title: Stardust
documents.tagline: This Summer A Star Falls. The Chase Begins.
documents.overview: In a countryside town bordering on a magical land, a young man makes a promise to his beloved that he'll retrieve a fallen star by venturing into the magical realm. His journey takes him into a world beyond his wildest dreams and reveals his true identity.

documents.title: The Seeker: The Dark Is Rising
documents.original_title: The Seeker: The Dark Is Rising
documents.tagline: Even the smallest of light... shines in the darkness
documents.overview: A boy's life is turned upside down when he learns that he is the last of a group of immortal warriors who have dedicated their lives to fighting the forces of the dark.
documents.plot:
The Seeker: The Dark Is Rising, also released simply as The Seeker, is a 2007 American fantasy adventure film loosely adapted from Susan Cooper's 1973 children's novel The Dark Is Rising, the second book in her series of the same name. Directed by David L. Cunningham, it stars Alexander Ludwig as Will Stanton, with Ian McShane, Frances Conroy, Gregory Smith, Jonathan Jackson, Amelia Warner, James Cosmo and Christopher Eccleston as the Rider.

On the eve of his fourteenth birthday, Will Stanton, an American boy recently moved with his large family to a village in England, is invited with his siblings to a Christmas party by Miss Greythorne, the mistress of the local manor, and her butler Merriman Lyon. After leaving the party, Will is pursued by a sinister figure on a white horse. He is rescued by Miss Greythorne, Merriman and two local farmers, Dawson and Old George, who reveal that they are Old Ones, ancient warriors who serve the Light in its eternal war against the Dark. The figure is the Rider, the Dark's champion, who warns that in five days his power will rise.

The Old Ones explain that Will is the last of their kind to be born, the seventh son of a seventh son, whose powers awaken on his fourteenth birthday. Will doubts this, believing he is only the sixth son, and the mystery of a missing brother becomes part of the story. As the Seeker, Will must find six hidden Signs, which together will give the Light the power to defeat the Dark. To recover them he learns to travel through time, while the Rider and his agents try to tempt, deceive and threaten him and his family. At the same time Will must cope with ordinary troubles: rivalry with his older brothers, a crush on a local girl named Maggie and the feeling of being an outsider in a new country.

The film was a critical and commercial failure, earning about $31 million worldwide against a budget of around $45 million. Fans of the novels objected to the many changes from the source, including making Will American and adding a romance subplot, and Susan Cooper publicly expressed her disappointment with the script. Critics also found it derivative of other fantasy films of the period.

documents.title: Mr. Magorium's Wonder Emporium
documents.tagline: You have to believe it to see it.
documents.overview: Molly Mahoney is the awkward and insecure manager of Mr. Magorium's Wonder Emporium—the strangest, most fantastic and most wonderful toy store in the world. After Mr. Magorium bequeaths the store to her, a dark and ominous change begins to take over the once-remarkable Emporium.
documents.plot:
Mr. Magorium's Wonder Emporium is a 2007 American family fantasy comedy written and directed by Zach Helm in his directorial debut. Dustin Hoffman stars as Edward Magorium, the eccentric 243-year-old owner of a magical toy store, with Natalie Portman as its manager Molly Mahoney, Jason Bateman as the accountant Henry Weston and Zach Mills as Eric Applebaum, a lonely young customer. Kermit the Frog makes a cameo.

Molly, a former child piano prodigy, is stuck: she dreams of becoming a concert pianist and composer but cannot finish her first concerto. At the Emporium she works with the bookbinder Bellini and Eric, who visits daily and acts like an employee. Magorium gives Molly a plain block of wood called the Congreve Cube, telling her it will lead her to a new life if she has faith in it. He then announces that he intends to "leave" and give the store to Molly, hiring Henry, a buttoned-up accountant, to sort out his finances. Henry refuses to believe that the store is magical. When Molly panics about running it, the Emporium throws a tantrum, turning its toys against everyone inside until Magorium calms it.

Realizing that Magorium means he is about to die, Molly rushes him to the hospital, where doctors find nothing wrong. She tries to show him the joys of life, but he assures her that he has lived fully. Using the stage directions of King Lear to show how simple death is, he encourages her and dies. Convinced she cannot run the shop, Molly puts it up for sale, and it loses its magic. Henry, now Eric's friend, meets Molly to sign the papers. When she admits her faith in the store, the block flies around the room, and Henry faints. He realizes that it was Molly who made it fly, and he tells her she can do anything if she believes in herself. Confident at last, Molly conjures and conducts her finished concerto, reviving the store. In a post-credits scene, Magorium paints The Son of Man on a wall.

The film was shot in Toronto in 2006 and released by 20th Century Fox and Walden Media on November 16, 2007. It underperformed, grossing under $70 million worldwide. Reviews were mixed. Rotten Tomatoes reported 40% approval, finding its colorful visuals and talented cast unable to overcome a bland story, and Rolling Stone named it the year's worst family film. Roger Ebert, however, gave it three stars and called it charming, especially for young viewers. Helm later disowned the film as a "Technicolor train-wreck".

documents.title: Closer
documents.tagline: If you believe in love at first sight, you never stop looking.
documents.overview: Two couples disintegrate when they begin destructive adulterous affairs with each other.
documents.plot:
Closer is a 2004 American romantic drama film directed by Mike Nichols, starring Julia Roberts, Jude Law, Natalie Portman, and Clive Owen.

The story revolves around four main characters: Dan (Jude Law), Alice (Julia Roberts), Larry (Clive Owen), and Mary (Natalie Portman). The narrative is presented in a non-linear fashion, jumping back and forth between the characters' past and present.

The film begins with Dan, a writer who has recently lost his wife to cancer. He meets Alice, a single mother who is struggling to cope with her own personal demons. They begin an affair, which becomes intense but ultimately unfulfilling for both of them.

Meanwhile, Larry, a novelist, is having an affair with Mary, a young and beautiful woman. However, their relationship is complicated by the fact that they are both married to other people. As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that all four characters are struggling with feelings of loneliness and disconnection in their personal lives.

As the narrative progresses, we see flashbacks of each character's past relationships and experiences. We learn about Dan's troubled marriage and his inability to connect with his wife on an emotional level. We also see glimpses of Alice's difficult childhood and her struggles to raise her son as a single mother.

Through a series of twists and turns, the story reveals that all four characters are connected in unexpected ways. It becomes clear that each character has been hurt by past relationships and is struggling to move on. However, as they navigate their complicated web of emotions, they begin to realize that they have more in common than they initially thought.

Ultimately, the film builds towards a poignant and emotional conclusion. Dan and Alice's affair comes to an end, but not before they both come to terms with their own vulnerabilities and weaknesses. Larry and Mary's relationship also reaches a breaking point, forcing them to confront the reality of their own desires and needs.

Throughout the film, Mike Nichols masterfully weaves together the complex narratives of his characters, creating a rich and nuanced exploration of love, loss, and human connection. The performances from the cast are outstanding, with each actor bringing depth and nuance to their respective roles.

In the end, Closer is a powerful and moving film that explores the complexities of human relationships and the ways in which we hurt and heal each other. With its non-linear narrative and complex characters, it's a thought-provoking and emotionally resonant film that lingers long after the credits roll.

documents.title: Cold Mountain
documents.tagline: Find the strength. Find the courage. No matter what it takes... find the way home.
documents.overview: In this classic story of love and devotion set against the backdrop of the American Civil War, a wounded Confederate soldier named W.P. Inman deserts his unit and travels across the South, aiming to return to his young wife, Ada, who he left behind to tend their farm. As Inman makes his perilous journey home, Ada struggles to keep their home intact with the assistance of Ruby, a mysterious drifter sent to help her by a kindly neighbor.
documents.plot:
Cold Mountain is a poignant and powerful tale that delves into the human spirit's capacity for resilience, hope, and redemption. Set against the backdrop of the American Civil War, the film follows W.P. Inman, a wounded Confederate soldier who deserts his unit to return to his beloved home in Cold Mountain, North Carolina.

As Inman navigates the treacherous terrain of war-torn America, he encounters various characters who challenge his perceptions and force him to confront the harsh realities of his past. The film's narrative is marked by a sense of longing and yearning, as Inman searches for a sense of belonging and connection in a world torn apart by conflict.

One of the primary themes of Cold Mountain is the struggle for identity and self-discovery. Inman's journey is a metaphor for the search for one's true purpose and meaning in life. As he encounters various characters who embody different aspects of himself, he begins to uncover fragments of his own identity and reconcile with his past.

The film also explores the theme of love and relationships, particularly the complex bond between Inman and Ruby Thewes, a strong-willed and independent woman who becomes his unlikely companion on his journey. Through their interactions, the film highlights the transformative power of human connection and the ways in which love can heal even the deepest wounds.

Furthermore, Cold Mountain is a powerful exploration of the human cost of war and the devastating impact it has on individuals and communities. The film's portrayal of the brutal realities of war serves as a stark reminder of the need for compassion, empathy, and understanding in the face of conflict.

Ultimately, Cold Mountain is a movie about the human spirit's capacity to persevere in the face of adversity, to find hope and redemption even in the darkest of times. The film's narrative is marked by a sense of hope and renewal, as Inman and Ruby navigate the challenges of their journey and discover new paths forward.

documents.title: Jay and Silent Bob Strike Back
documents.original_title: Jay and Silent Bob Strike Back
documents.tagline: Hollywood had it coming
documents.overview: When Jay and Silent Bob learn that their comic-book alter egos, Bluntman and Chronic, have been sold to Hollywood as part of a big-screen movie that leaves them out of any royalties, the pair travels to Tinseltown to sabotage the production.
documents.plot:
Jay and Silent Bob Strike Back is a 2001 comedy film that explores several themes that are characteristic of its irreverent and satirical tone. At its core, the movie is a commentary on the commercialization of art and the commodification of pop culture.

The film's protagonists, Jay and Silent Bob, are two comic book store clerks who become embroiled in a series of misadventures that take them from their mundane lives to a surreal world of Hollywood excess. Through their experiences, the movie critiques the ways in which the entertainment industry exploits its creators and reduces art to a marketable commodity.

The film also explores themes of identity, as Jay and Silent Bob navigate their own sense of self and purpose in a world that seems determined to erase them. Their struggles to maintain their individuality in the face of external pressures serve as a commentary on the fragility of artistic expression and the importance of staying true to one's vision.

Furthermore, Jay and Silent Bob Strike Back is also a film about the power of friendship and loyalty. Despite their differences, Jay and Silent Bob are united by their shared experiences and values, and their bond serves as a source of strength and inspiration in the face of adversity.

Overall, Jay and Silent Bob Strike Back is a movie that uses humor and satire to explore complex themes and ideas, often with a irreverent and subversive tone.

documents.title: Beowulf
documents.tagline: Evil breeds pain.
documents.overview: A 6th-century Scandinavian warrior named Beowulf embarks on a mission to slay the man-like ogre, Grendel.
documents.plot:
Beowulf is a 2007 American animated epic fantasy film produced and directed by Robert Zemeckis and written by Neil Gaiman and Roger Avary, loosely based on the Old English poem Beowulf. Made with performance-capture animation, the technique Zemeckis had used for The Polar Express, it features Ray Winstone as Beowulf, Anthony Hopkins as King Hrothgar, Robin Wright Penn as Queen Wealtheow, Brendan Gleeson as Wiglaf, John Malkovich as Unferth, Crispin Glover as Grendel, Alison Lohman and Angelina Jolie as Grendel's mother. The film reinterprets the poem, changing several elements of its story.

In 507 AD, the Danish king Hrothgar's mead hall, Heorot, is terrorized by Grendel, a monstrous creature tormented by the noise of the king's celebrations, which slaughters his warriors. The Geatish hero Beowulf sails to Denmark with his men to destroy the monster, boasting of his past exploits. To lure Grendel out, Beowulf's men hold a loud feast in the hall, and Beowulf fights the creature naked and unarmed so that the contest will be equal. Discovering that Grendel has extremely sensitive hearing, Beowulf injures his ear and tears off his arm, and Grendel crawls home to die in his mother's arms.

In gratitude, Hrothgar gives Beowulf a golden drinking horn. That night Grendel's mother, a seductive water demon, takes revenge by killing Beowulf's men. Hrothgar sends Beowulf to her cave, where, instead of killing her, Beowulf succumbs to her offer of wealth and power in exchange for a son, and returns with a false tale of victory. Hrothgar, who reveals that he once made the same bargain, names Beowulf his heir and takes his own life. Decades later, the aging King Beowulf rules a prosperous kingdom but is haunted by his secret, which returns in the form of a dragon that attacks his land, forcing him into a final battle to atone for the sins of his youth.

Beowulf premiered in London in November 2007 and was released in 3D and IMAX 3D as well as conventional formats. It received generally positive reviews; critics praised its visual effects, its action sequences and Gaiman and Avary's darker, more adult reworking of the poem, though some found the motion-capture characters unsettling. It grossed about $196 million worldwide against a budget of around $150 million.

documents.title: Field of Dreams
documents.tagline: If you believe the impossible, the incredible can come true.
documents.overview: Ray Kinsella is an Iowa farmer who hears a mysterious voice telling him to turn his cornfield into a baseball diamond. He does, but the voice's directions don't stop -- even after the spirits of deceased ballplayers turn up to play.
documents.plot:
Field of Dreams is a 1989 American sports fantasy drama film written and directed by Phil Alden Robinson, based on W. P. Kinsella's 1982 novel Shoeless Joe. Kevin Costner stars as Ray Kinsella, an Iowa farmer who builds a baseball diamond in his cornfield that draws the ghosts of baseball legends, including Shoeless Joe Jackson (Ray Liotta) and the Chicago Black Sox. Amy Madigan plays his wife Annie, with James Earl Jones and Burt Lancaster, in his final film role.

Ray lives on a corn farm in Dyersville, Iowa, with Annie and their daughter Karin, haunted by his broken relationship with his late father, John, a devoted baseball fan. One evening he hears a voice whispering "If you build it, he will come" and envisions a ballfield. Despite the financial risk, he plows under part of his crop to build it. Shoeless Joe appears, soon joined by other banned Black Sox players, though Annie's brother Mark, who cannot see them, warns that the family is going bankrupt. The voice next urges Ray to "ease his pain," which he takes to mean Terence Mann, a reclusive 1960s author. Ray drives to Boston and takes Mann to a game at Fenway Park, where both hear the voice say "go the distance" and see statistics for Moonlight Graham, who played one game for the New York Giants in 1922 without ever batting.

In Chisholm, Minnesota, they learn that Graham became a beloved doctor and died years earlier. Ray slips back to 1972 to meet the elderly Graham, who declines his invitation. On the way home, they pick up a young hitchhiker who turns out to be Archie Graham. Ray confesses that he stopped playing catch with his father at 14 and mocked his hero, Joe, and never reconciled with him before his death. At the farm, Graham finally gets to bat, but when Mark demands that Ray sell, a scuffle knocks Karin off the bleachers. Graham steps off the field to save her from choking, becoming old Doc Graham again, and leaves without regret. Mark suddenly sees the players and urges Ray to keep the farm, as Karin and Mann predict that people will come to watch. Mann is invited into the corn, and the catcher removes his mask, revealing Ray's father as a young man. Ray asks his father to play catch as a line of cars approaches the field.

Released by Universal Pictures on April 21, 1989, the film grossed $84.5 million on a $15 million budget, received positive reviews and was nominated for three Academy Awards, including Best Picture. In 2017, it was selected for the National Film Registry.

documents.title: Taxi 4
documents.overview: Before being extradited to Africa to stand trial, a notorious Belgian criminal is entrusted to the Marseilles police department for less than 24 hours. But the wily crook convinces bumbling policeman Emilien he's a lowly Belgian embassy employee who got railroaded by the brilliant master criminal.
documents.plot:
Taxi 4, stylized T4XI, is a 2007 French action comedy directed by Gérard Krawczyk from a screenplay by producer Luc Besson, the fourth installment of the Taxi series after Taxi 3 (2003). Samy Naceri returns as Marseille taxi driver Daniel Morales, now driving a Peugeot 407, alongside Frédéric Diefenthal as hapless policeman Émilien Coutant-Kerbalec, Bernard Farcy as Commissioner Gibert, Emma Sjöberg as Petra and Jean-Christophe Bouvet as General Bertineau, with footballer Djibril Cissé as himself.

With all of Marseille obsessed with football, Daniel races the newly signed Cissé to the stadium. Soon after, Gibert's squad is assigned to hold a notorious Belgian bank robber wanted by Interpol, Albert Van den Bosch, for a few hours before his transfer to the Congo to stand trial. Their bungling begins at once: they arrive late at the airport and wreck their own convoy. Meanwhile Daniel leaves his son, Léo, and Émilien's son, Maxime, at the station, where the boys unwittingly help one of the robber's accomplices alter his file on Gibert's computer. During the prisoner's processing, Gibert knocks himself out with a tranquilizer dart meant for bears, and Émilien, fooled by the doctored wanted notice and a phone call to a gang member, releases the Belgian, who promptly hails Daniel's taxi.

Fired by Gibert, Émilien turns to Daniel, who remembers where he dropped off his passenger. They follow the gang to Monaco, where the Belgian robs a bank after taking the place of his timid twin brother, Édouard, and they discover that Petra, Émilien's wife, has infiltrated the gang undercover to retrieve compromising documents from one of the vaults. Gibert's men arrest the innocent twin instead, while the real robber escapes toward Cannes to the lavish villa of a Colombian former associate. Émilien is captured sneaking in, and Petra must stall for time until Gibert's assault team storms the villa. Launched over the wall, the commissioner lands in a pile of cocaine and goes on a deranged shooting spree with assault rifles and a rocket launcher, before Daniel drives his taxi into the living room, locks the robber in the trunk and rescues the couple. Petra's mission succeeds, and a still-intoxicated Gibert ends up on the pitch at a Marseille match.

Released in France in February 2007, the film drew more than 4.5 million admissions there. Critics and audiences panned it, faulting its thin plot, slack pacing and lack of the car chases that had defined the earlier films.

documents.title: Reign Over Me
documents.tagline: Let in the unexpected.
documents.overview: A man who lost his family in the September 11 attack on New York City runs into his old college roommate. Rekindling the friendship is the one thing that appears able to help the man recover from his grief.
documents.plot:
Reign Over Me is a poignant and powerful drama that delves into the complexities of grief, loss, and redemption. The film tells the story of Charlie Fineman, a man who lost his entire family in the 9/11 attacks, and his journey to come to terms with his past and find a new sense of purpose.

At its core, Reign Over Me is a movie about the devastating effects of trauma and the struggle to heal. Charlie's character is a complex and nuanced portrayal of a man who has been shattered by tragedy, and his story serves as a powerful exploration of the human capacity for resilience and survival in the face of unimaginable pain.

The film also explores themes of guilt, anger, and regret, as Charlie grapples with the what-ifs and maybes that haunt him. His relationship with Norman, a fellow survivor who has found a way to move on from his trauma, serves as a catalyst for Charlie's own journey towards healing and redemption.

Through its thoughtful and introspective portrayal of its characters, Reign Over Me raises important questions about the nature of grief, the power of human connection, and the possibility of finding meaning and purpose in the midst of unimaginable loss. Ultimately, the film is a powerful exploration of the human spirit's capacity for hope, forgiveness, and transformation.

documents.title: Astérix at the Olympic Games
documents.overview: Astérix and Obélix have to win the Olympic Games in order to help their friend Alafolix marry Princess Irina. Brutus uses every trick in the book to have his own team win the game, and get rid of his father Julius Caesar in the process.
documents.plot:
Asterix at the Olympic Games (French: Astérix aux Jeux olympiques) is a 2008 French fantasy comedy co-directed by Frédéric Forestier and Thomas Langmann and written by Langmann, Alexandre Charlot and Franck Magnier, based on the Asterix comics by René Goscinny and Albert Uderzo. The third live-action Asterix film, following Asterix & Obelix: Mission Cleopatra (2002), it stars Clovis Cornillac, who replaced Christian Clavier as Asterix, and Gérard Depardieu, returning as Obelix, with Benoît Poelvoorde as Brutus and Alain Delon as Julius Caesar.

In the village of indomitable Gauls, the young and lovesick Lovesix is smitten with Irina, a Greek princess. But Irina has been promised to Brutus, the scheming son of Julius Caesar, who also wishes to marry her. To win her hand, Lovesix decides to compete against Brutus in the Olympic Games in Greece, and Asterix and Obelix, along with the druid Getafix, accompany him to help. The Gauls must face not only formidable athletes from across the known world but also the ruthless Brutus, who will stop at nothing, including cheating, sabotage and doping his own Roman team, to ensure victory. At the same time Brutus plots to get rid of his father and seize power. Complicating matters, the Gauls are forbidden from using their magic potion, the source of their superhuman strength, and must find other ways to triumph. The climax unfolds during a spectacular chariot race.

The film is a loose adaptation of the 1968 comic book Asterix at the Olympic Games. The love story between Lovesix and Irina was invented for the film, and Brutus, who plays a much larger role here than in the comics, serves as the comic villain. The film features cameo appearances by sports stars including Michael Schumacher as a charioteer, Zinedine Zidane, Tony Parker and Amélie Mauresmo. It was Alain Delon's last film role as an actor and the final film of Jean-Pierre Cassel, who played Getafix, and of Sim, who played Geriatrix. It was filmed in Alicante, Spain.

At the time of its release in January 2008, it was the most expensive French film and the most expensive non-English-language film ever made. Critics responded negatively, but the film was a commercial success in several European countries, topping the box office in France, Spain and Poland and grossing about $23 million in France in its opening weekend. It was followed by Asterix and Obelix: God Save Britannia in 2012.

documents.title: The Chronicles of Narnia: Prince Caspian
documents.original_title: The Chronicles of Narnia: Prince Caspian
documents.tagline: Everything you know is about to change forever.
documents.overview: One year after their incredible adventures in the Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe, Peter, Edmund, Lucy and Susan Pevensie return to Narnia to aid a young prince whose life has been threatened by the evil King Miraz. Now, with the help of a colorful cast of new characters, including Trufflehunter the badger and Nikabrik the dwarf, the Pevensie clan embarks on an incredible quest to ensure that Narnia is returned to its rightful heir.
documents.plot:
The Chronicles of Narnia: Prince Caspian is a 2008 high fantasy film directed by Andrew Adamson and written by Adamson, Christopher Markus and Stephen McFeely. Based on Prince Caspian (1951), the second published novel in C. S. Lewis's series, it is the second installment in The Chronicles of Narnia film series. Ben Barnes stars as Caspian, with Georgie Henley, Skandar Keynes, William Moseley and Anna Popplewell reprising their roles as the Pevensie children, Sergio Castellitto as King Miraz, Peter Dinklage as Trumpkin, and Liam Neeson voicing Aslan.

Nearly 1,300 Narnian years after the Pevensie siblings ruled as kings and queens and returned to their own world, Narnia has been conquered by the Telmarines. Caspian, a young Telmarine prince, is woken one night by his tutor, Doctor Cornelius, who warns him that his uncle, Lord Miraz, has just had a son and now intends to kill Caspian to secure the throne for his own heir. Cornelius gives him an ancient magical horn that once belonged to Queen Susan and tells him to use it only in great need. Fleeing into the woods, Caspian is rescued by surviving Narnians, the dwarfs Trumpkin and Nikabrik and the talking badger Trufflehunter; Trumpkin is captured by soldiers. Caspian blows the horn.

In wartime England, a year after their first adventure, the four Pevensies are waiting on a London Underground platform when they are suddenly pulled back into Narnia. They find their castle, Cair Paravel, in ruins and rescue Trumpkin from execution, learning how much time has passed. Lucy glimpses Aslan pointing the way, but her older siblings do not believe her. The Pevensies join Caspian and the Narnians, who have taken refuge at Aslan's How, and tensions arise between Peter and Caspian over leadership. A disastrous night raid on Miraz's castle leaves many Narnians dead, and Nikabrik's plot to summon the White Witch is narrowly thwarted. As Miraz's army advances, Peter challenges him to single combat to buy time, while Lucy sets out to find Aslan and bring help.

The film received generally positive reviews, though many considered it darker and less charming than the first film. It grossed about $419 million worldwide, a significant decline from its predecessor, which prompted Disney to withdraw from the series before the third film was made with 20th Century Fox.
