documents.title: Shall We Dance?
documents.tagline: Step out of the ordinary.
documents.overview: Upon first sight of a beautiful instructor, a bored and overworked estate lawyer signs up for ballroom dancing lessons.
documents.plot:
Shall We Dance is a poignant and thought-provoking film that explores the complexities of love, relationships, and personal growth. The movie delves into the emotional journey of its protagonist, John Clark, as he navigates his midlife crisis and grapples with feelings of restlessness and discontentment in his marriage.

At its core, Shall We Dance is a nuanced exploration of the human desire for connection, intimacy, and meaning. Through John's interactions with Chiyo Sakamoto, a vibrant and free-spirited dance instructor, the film reveals the tension between conformity and individuality, tradition and innovation, and the constraints of societal expectations versus personal aspirations.

As the story unfolds, Shall We Dance masterfully weaves together themes of identity, belonging, and the search for purpose. The film raises essential questions about the nature of love, relationships, and personal fulfillment, inviting viewers to reflect on their own values, desires, and priorities.

Ultimately, Shall We Dance is a moving and introspective drama that encourages audiences to reevaluate their own lives, relationships, and aspirations, and to consider the importance of embracing change, taking risks, and pursuing one's passions.

documents.title: The Brave One
documents.tagline: How many wrongs to make it right?
documents.overview: A woman struggles to recover from a brutal attack by setting out on a mission for revenge.
documents.plot:
The Brave One is a psychological thriller that delves into the darker aspects of human nature and the effects of trauma on an individual. The film follows Jules Lander, a young woman who witnesses a brutal murder in Central Park, which leaves her with severe emotional scars.

As Jules navigates her new reality, she becomes increasingly isolated and withdrawn, adopting a persona that allows her to cope with her surroundings. However, this newfound sense of power and control comes at a cost, as she begins to lose touch with her humanity and empathy for others.

The film explores the theme of trauma and its lasting impact on individuals, particularly women. Jules's experiences serve as a catalyst for her transformation, forcing her to confront the darker aspects of human nature and the world around her. The movie also touches on the idea of vigilantism and the blurred lines between justice and revenge.

Through Jules's character, the film raises questions about the nature of power and control, highlighting the dangers of allowing fear and anger to consume us. As Jules becomes more entrenched in her persona, she begins to lose sight of what is truly important, leading to a downward spiral of violence and self-destruction.

Ultimately, The Brave One is a thought-provoking exploration of the human condition, delving into the complexities of trauma, power, and the fragility of the human psyche.

documents.title: Aśoka
documents.tagline: Only the dead have seen the end of war
documents.overview: A young Prince Asoka works to perfect his skills in battle and also deals with family conflict. During a struggle with one of his step-brothers, his mother urges Asoka to escape to stay alive. While away, Asoka meets Kaurwaki and falls in love, but must use his skills as a warrior to protect her. A dangerous and heartbreaking web of conspiracy follows, which leads Asoka to embrace a Buddhist path.
documents.plot: A young Prince Asoka works to perfect his skills in battle and also deals with family conflict. During a struggle with one of his step-brothers, his mother urges Asoka to escape to stay alive. While away, Asoka meets Kaurwaki and falls in love, but must use his skills as a warrior to protect her. A dangerous and heartbreaking web of conspiracy follows, which leads Asoka to embrace a Buddhist path.

documents.title: The Brothers Grimm
documents.tagline: Eliminating Evil Since 1812.
documents.overview: Folklore collectors and con artists, Jake and Will Grimm, travel from village to village pretending to protect townsfolk from enchanted creatures and performing exorcisms. However, they are put to the test  when they encounter a real magical curse in a haunted forest with real magical beings, requiring genuine courage.
documents.plot:
The Brothers Grimm is a 2005 fantasy adventure film directed by Terry Gilliam that reimagines the famous folklorists as travelling con artists in Napoleonic French-occupied Germany, who encounter a genuine fairy-tale curse requiring real courage rather than their usual fake exorcisms. Matt Damon, Heath Ledger and Lena Headey star, with Peter Stormare, Jonathan Pryce and Monica Bellucci in supporting roles. A British-Czech co-production shot in the Czech Republic, it was written by Ehren Kruger.

In 1811, Will and Jake Grimm and their assistants Hidlick and Bunst use Jake's deep knowledge of folklore to persuade villagers that they can banish the supernatural. Captured by the Italian torturer Mercurio Cavaldi and brought before the French general Delatombe, they are offered amnesty if they investigate the disappearance of young girls from the village of Marbaden. With the help of Angelika, a fur trapper whose younger sisters were the first to vanish, they learn of a tower in the nearby forest built centuries earlier by a vain Thuringian queen trying to escape the plague. That night an enchanted horse swallows a girl and carries her into the forest. Back in the forest, Jake climbs the tower, ringed by twelve crypts, and finds the ancient, decaying Queen, kept alive by a magic mirror that shows her youthful reflection. When a mud creature takes another girl, Sasha, a wolf-like huntsman places her in a crypt. The brothers rescue her and take the huntsman's axe, and Jake concludes that the girls are part of a ritual timed to a lunar eclipse to restore the Queen's youth. Delatombe executes Hidlick and Bunst, denounces the brothers as frauds and orders the forest burned with them inside, but Angelika frees them and recognizes the axe as her father's, revealing that the huntsman is her father under the Queen's spell. Angelika then becomes the twelfth and final victim. The Queen's wind puts out the fire, Will kills Delatombe, and when the Queen bewitches Will, Jake smashes the mirror; Angelika's father leaps from the tower with the rest of it, destroying the Queen. Jake revives Angelika with a kiss, the girls return home, and a raven flies off with a shard of the mirror.

Delayed for months by disputes between Gilliam and the Weinsteins, the film was released on 26 August 2005 and competed at the Venice Film Festival. It received mixed reviews, with a 38% Rotten Tomatoes rating, and grossed $105.3 million worldwide.

documents.title: Seabiscuit
documents.tagline: The hopes of a nation rode on a long shot.
documents.overview: True story of the undersized Depression-era racehorse whose victories lifted not only the spirits of the team behind it but also those of their nation.
documents.plot:
Seabiscuit is a heartwarming and inspiring film that delves into the underdog story of a small but spirited horse who defies the odds to achieve greatness. The movie, directed by Gary Ross, explores the themes of perseverance, determination, and the unbreakable bond between humans and animals.

At its core, Seabiscuit is a tale of overcoming adversity and proving oneself against all expectations. The film's protagonist, Seabiscuit, faces numerous challenges, from his humble beginnings as an undersized and unproven horse to his struggles with injuries and setbacks on the track. However, through the unwavering support of his trainer, Red Pollard (played by Tobey Maguire), and his owner, Charles Howard (played by Jeff Bridges), Seabiscuit perseveres and ultimately achieves greatness.

The movie also explores the theme of redemption, as Seabiscuit's journey is intertwined with that of Red Pollard, who seeks to redeem himself after a troubled past. Through their shared struggles and triumphs, the film highlights the transformative power of friendship and the human spirit.

Furthermore, Seabiscuit touches on the theme of class and social status, as embodied by the contrast between Charles Howard's wealth and privilege and that of Red Pollard's humble beginnings. The film shows how these differences can be bridged through mutual respect, trust, and a shared passion for horse racing.

Ultimately, Seabiscuit is a movie about hope, resilience, and the power of the human (and animal) spirit to overcome seemingly insurmountable obstacles.

documents.title: Elizabeth: The Golden Age
documents.tagline: Woman. Warrior. Queen.
documents.overview: When Queen Elizabeth's reign is threatened by ruthless familial betrayal and Spain's invading army, she and her shrewd adviser must act to safeguard the lives of her people.
documents.plot: When Queen Elizabeth's reign is threatened by ruthless familial betrayal and Spain's invading army, she and her shrewd adviser must act to safeguard the lives of her people.

documents.title: Enchanted
documents.tagline: This fairytale princess is about to meet a real Prince Charming.
documents.overview: The beautiful princess Giselle is banished by an evil queen from her magical, musical animated land and finds herself in the gritty reality of the streets of modern-day Manhattan. Shocked by this strange new environment that doesn't operate on a "happily ever after" basis, Giselle is now adrift in a chaotic world badly in need of enchantment. But when Giselle begins to fall in love with a charmingly flawed divorce lawyer who has come to her aid - even though she is already promised to a perfect fairy tale prince back home - she has to wonder: Can a storybook view of romance survive in the real world?
documents.plot:
Enchanted is a 2007 American musical fantasy comedy film produced by Walt Disney Pictures. The movie follows the story of Giselle, a princess from the magical kingdom of Andalasia, who is engaged to Prince Edward.

The film begins with Giselle's wedding day, where she is about to marry Prince Edward. However, her life takes an unexpected turn when her evil stepmother, Queen Narissa, and her advisor, Morgan, plot to sabotage the wedding. In a dramatic twist, Giselle falls off a castle balcony and lands in the real world of New York City.

In the real world, Giselle meets Robert, a lawyer who is initially unaware of his royal connection. As they spend more time together, Giselle's innocence and naivety clash with the harsh realities of the modern world. Despite this, Robert finds himself falling for Giselle's charm and kindness.

Meanwhile, Queen Narissa and Morgan continue to pursue their evil plans, seeking to capture Giselle and use her as leverage to gain control over Prince Edward's kingdom. As Giselle navigates her new life in New York, she must also confront the reality of her own destiny and the true nature of her relationship with Prince Edward.

As the story unfolds, Robert becomes increasingly entangled in Giselle's world, and they begin to develop feelings for each other. However, their love is threatened by Queen Narissa's schemes, which lead to a dramatic confrontation between the two kingdoms.

In the end, Giselle must make a choice between her life in the real world with Robert or returning to her kingdom as the princess she was meant to be. Ultimately, Giselle decides to stay with Robert and find happiness in the real world, rather than conforming to the expectations of her royal duties.

The film features a range of memorable characters, including Morgan, who provides comedic relief, and the villainous Queen Narissa, whose evil plans drive much of the plot. The movie's blend of fantasy and reality creates a unique and engaging narrative that explores themes of love, identity, and the power of true connection.

Overall, Enchanted is a charming and entertaining film that offers a fresh take on traditional fairy tale tropes. With its witty dialogue, catchy musical numbers, and lovable characters, it has become a beloved classic among Disney fans and beyond.

documents.title: The Darjeeling Limited
documents.tagline: I want us to be brothers again, like we used to be.
documents.overview: Three American brothers who have not spoken to each other in a year set off on a train voyage across India with a plan to find themselves and bond with each other -- to become brothers again like they used to be. Their "spiritual quest", however, veers rapidly off-course (due to events involving over-the-counter pain killers, Indian cough syrup, and pepper spray).
documents.plot:
The Darjeeling Limited is a poignant and introspective film that explores the complexities of family relationships, identity, and spiritual seeking. The movie follows three estranged brothers, Francis, Peter, and Jack, as they embark on a journey through India in search of enlightenment and healing.

At its core, the film delves into the theme of family dynamics and the struggles that arise from unresolved conflicts and unexpressed emotions. The brothers' complicated past is slowly revealed throughout their travels, exposing deep-seated wounds and unrequited love. As they navigate the spiritual landscapes of India, they are forced to confront their own personal demons and the consequences of their choices.

The movie also explores the theme of identity and self-discovery, as each brother grapples with his own sense of purpose and belonging. Francis, the eldest, is a successful businessman struggling to find meaning in his life; Peter, the middle child, is a free-spirited artist searching for creative expression; and Jack, the youngest, is a troubled soul trying to escape his past.

Through their experiences, the film highlights the tension between spiritual seeking and material success. The brothers' quest for enlightenment is often at odds with their own desires and expectations, leading to moments of profound insight and introspection.

Ultimately, The Darjeeling Limited is a powerful exploration of the human condition, one that celebrates the complexities and nuances of family relationships while also acknowledging the universal desire for connection, healing, and self-discovery.

documents.title: Panic Room
documents.tagline: It was supposed to be the safest room in the house.
documents.overview: Trapped in their New York brownstone's panic room, a hidden chamber built as a sanctuary in the event of break-ins, newly divorced Meg Altman and her young daughter Sarah play a deadly game of cat-and-mouse with three intruders - Burnham, Raoul and Junior - during a brutal home invasion. But the room itself is the focal point because what the intruders really want is inside it.
documents.plot: Trapped in their New York brownstone's panic room, a hidden chamber built as a sanctuary in the event of break-ins, newly divorced Meg Altman and her young daughter Sarah play a deadly game of cat-and-mouse with three intruders - Burnham, Raoul and Junior - during a brutal home invasion. But the room itself is the focal point because what the intruders really want is inside it.

documents.title: Sympathy for Lady Vengeance
documents.tagline: All she wanted was a peaceful life… they didn't give it.
documents.overview: After being wrongfully convicted, a woman is imprisoned for 13 years and forced to give up her daughter. While in prison she gains the respect of her cellmates and plots her revenge on the man responsible. Once released, she begins her elaborate plan of retribution, but discovers a horrifying truth.
documents.plot:
Sympathy for Lady Vengeance is a 2005 South Korean revenge thriller film directed by Park Chan-wook, written by Park Chan-wook and Lee Hyun-seung, and produced by TSJ Entertainment. The film stars Kim Sun-a, Shin Ha-kyun, and Jo Han-jin.

The story begins with the introduction of Im Car-ro (Kim Sun-a), a former con artist who was involved in a heist that went horribly wrong, resulting in the death of her accomplice and lover, Park Do-joon. After serving 10 years in prison, Im Car-ro is released on parole and seeks revenge against those responsible for her past mistakes.

Im Car-ro sets out to find Park Do-joon's brother, Park Do-jin (Shin Ha-kyun), a wealthy businessman who she believes was involved in the heist. She manipulates him into helping her with her plan, which involves robbing a bank and framing his company for the crime.

As Im Car-ro's plan unfolds, it becomes clear that she has a personal vendetta against Park Do-jin, whom she blames for her past suffering. Through a series of clever manipulations and deceptions, Im Car-ro slowly takes control of Park Do-jin's life, using him to further her own agenda.

However, as the story progresses, it becomes apparent that Im Car-ro's motivations are not entirely driven by revenge. She is also seeking redemption for her past mistakes and a chance to start anew. Through her interactions with Park Do-jin, she begins to confront her own demons and grapple with the consequences of her actions.

The film's climax features a tense showdown between Im Car-ro and Park Do-jin, as well as his associates, who are determined to stop her from carrying out her plan. In the end, Im Car-ro emerges victorious, but not without scars. The film concludes with Im Car-ro walking away from the chaos she has created, symbolizing her newfound freedom and a chance for redemption.

Throughout the film, Park Chan-wook explores themes of revenge, redemption, and the complexities of human relationships. The film's title, Sympathy for Lady Vengeance, is a clever play on words, as Im Car-ro is both the victim and the perpetrator of violence. The film's dark humor and witty dialogue add to its tension and complexity, making it a thought-provoking and entertaining watch.

Overall, Sympathy for Lady Vengeance is a gripping and intense thriller that explores the complexities of human nature and the consequences of our actions. With its clever plot twists and strong performances from the cast, it is a must-see for fans of revenge thrillers and Park Chan-wook's unique brand of storytelling.

documents.title: Be Cool
documents.tagline: Everyone is looking for the next big hit
documents.overview: Disenchanted with the movie industry, Chili Palmer tries the music industry, meeting and romancing a widow of a music executive along the way.
documents.plot: Disenchanted with the movie industry, Chili Palmer tries the music industry, meeting and romancing a widow of a music executive along the way.

documents.title: The Machinist
documents.tagline: How do you wake up from a nightmare if you’re not asleep?
documents.overview: Trevor, an insomniac lathe operator, experiences unusual occurrences at work and home. A strange man follows him everywhere, but no one else seems to notice him.
documents.plot:
The Machinist is a 2004 psychological thriller directed by Brad Anderson and written by Scott Kosar. Christian Bale stars as Trevor Reznik, a factory machinist tormented by paranoia and delusions after a year without sleep, with Jennifer Jason Leigh, Aitana Sánchez-Gijón, John Sharian and Michael Ironside in supporting roles. The film became famous for Bale's physical commitment to the part: he lost about 62 pounds (28 kg) to portray Trevor's skeletal frame.

Trevor's chronic insomnia has left him emaciated and isolated. His colleagues turn against him after an accident in which a co-worker, Miller, loses his arm, an accident that happened because Trevor was distracted by Ivan, an unfamiliar, grinning worker whom nobody at the factory seems to know and for whom no records exist. Trevor finds comfort with Stevie, a prostitute, and with Maria, a waitress at the airport diner where he goes every night. He is haunted by flashes of recurring images, and mysterious Post-it notes on his refrigerator depicting a game of hangman deepen his paranoia.

On a trip to an amusement park with Maria and her young son Nicholas, a ghost-train ride becomes increasingly disturbing until its flashing lights trigger the boy's seizure. Convinced that he is the target of a conspiracy to drive him mad, Trevor seizes on a photograph of Ivan fishing with a co-worker as proof that Ivan is real. After another near-accident he lashes out and is fired, and his electricity is cut off when he forgets to pay the bills. Desperate to trace Ivan's car, he throws himself in front of a vehicle to file a hit-and-run report, only to be told that the licence plate belongs to his own car, which he reported totalled a year ago. Stevie throws him out after he accuses her of conspiring with Ivan, and at the diner he learns that no Maria has ever worked there.

Following Ivan and Nicholas into his own apartment, Trevor kills Ivan, only to find no trace of the body. The truth finally surfaces: a year earlier, distracted by his car's cigarette lighter, he ran over and killed a boy, Nicholas, in front of the child's mother, Maria, and fled. Ivan is a projection of his guilt. Completing the hangman puzzle, which spells "killer", Trevor drives to the police instead of the airport, confesses to the hit-and-run, and in his cell finally falls asleep.

The film was well received, earning 77% on Rotten Tomatoes, with praise for Bale's astonishingly committed performance, and it has since gained a cult following.

documents.title: Michael Clayton
documents.tagline: The truth can be adjusted.
documents.overview: A law firm brings in its "fixer" to remedy the situation after a lawyer has a breakdown while representing a chemical company that he knows is guilty in a multi-billion dollar class action suit.
documents.plot:
Michael Clayton is a thought-provoking thriller that delves into the darker aspects of corporate America and the moral ambiguities of those who navigate its treacherous landscape.

At its core, the film explores the theme of identity and how it becomes distorted in the pursuit of power and wealth. Michael Clayton, the protagonist, is a talented lawyer who finds himself entangled in a web of deceit and corruption that threatens to destroy his own sense of self. As he navigates this complex world, he begins to question the true nature of his existence and the values that drive those around him.

The film also examines the theme of toxic masculinity, as embodied by Arthur Edens, a brilliant but troubled lawyer who embodies the darker aspects of male ego and aggression. Through Edens' character, the movie highlights the dangers of unchecked ambition and the devastating consequences that can result when individuals prioritize their own interests above all else.

Furthermore, Michael Clayton critiques the corporate culture that prioritizes profits over people and the environment. The film's portrayal of a ruthless and amoral corporation, led by the cunning and manipulative Karen Crowder, serves as a scathing indictment of the excesses and corruption that can occur when greed and power are allowed to run rampant.

Ultimately, the movie suggests that true redemption and personal growth can only be achieved through a willingness to confront one's own flaws and weaknesses, and to re-examine the values that have driven us. Through Michael Clayton's journey, the film offers a nuanced exploration of the human condition, one that is both thought-provoking and deeply unsettling.

documents.title: Armored
documents.tagline: To protect and serve yourself.
documents.overview: A crew of officers at an armored transport security firm risk their lives when they embark on the ultimate heist against their own company. Armed with a seemingly fool-proof plan, the men plan on making off with a fortune with harm to none. But when an unexpected witness interferes, the plan quickly unravels and all bets are off.
documents.plot:
Armored is a 2009 American heist action thriller directed by Nimród Antal from a script by James V. Simpson. Columbus Short leads a cast that includes Matt Dillon, Laurence Fishburne, Jean Reno, Skeet Ulrich, Amaury Nolasco, Milo Ventimiglia and Fred Ward. It was released on December 4, 2009.

Ty Hackett is a military veteran who now works on an armored transport crew for the security firm Eagle Shield. Since their parents died he has been raising his younger brother Jimmy, but the bills are piling up: the bank is threatening to foreclose on the house, and social services are considering placing the truant Jimmy in foster care. Mike Cochrane, Ty's godfather and colleague, lets him in on a plan to rob two of their own trucks of the $42 million they are carrying from the Federal Reserve to local banks. Ty initially refuses, but agrees after Mike promises that nobody will get hurt.

The six guards unload the first truck at an abandoned steel mill, but a homeless man living there sees them, and Baines shoots him dead. Horrified, Ty locks himself inside the second truck with the remaining $21 million. When he cannot drive away, he trips the alarm, drawing sheriff's deputy Jake Eckehart to the mill. Baines shoots the deputy, and Ty pulls the wounded man into the truck while the others try to knock out the door hinges. Dobbs wavers and secretly tries to replace an engine fuse Mike removed, but Palmer catches and kills him; later, after Ty persuades Palmer that the robbery is wrong, Palmer, consumed by guilt, takes his own life. The surviving robbers then reveal that they have kidnapped Jimmy, and Ty is forced to cooperate. Quinn and Baines are killed by a booby trap rigged to the cash, and Mike, chasing Ty in the other truck, crashes into a pit and dies. Recovering in hospital, Jake tells Duncan Ashcroft how Ty tried to stop the thieves, a reward is mentioned, and the brothers go home.

Screen Gems bought Simpson's spec script in 2006, Dillon and Short were announced as leads in 2007, and the film was shot in Los Angeles. It was not screened for critics in advance and drew mostly negative reviews, scoring 42% on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus faulted plot holes and a messy finale despite the good cast; CinemaScore audiences gave it a "B−". A. O. Scott of The New York Times was kinder, calling it a basic, brutal and sometimes clumsy B movie that was far from dumb, and praising Andrzej Sekuła's cinematography.

documents.title: Raising Helen
documents.tagline: Her uptown life gets turned inside out!
documents.overview: Helen Harris has a glamorous, big-city life working for one of New York's hottest modeling agencies. But suddenly her free-spirited life gets turned upside down when she must chose between the life she's always loved, and the new loves of her life!
documents.plot:
Raising Helen is a heartwarming comedy-drama film that explores the complexities of family dynamics and personal growth. The story revolves around Helen Harris, a young woman who finds herself at the center of her eccentric and lovable family's life after her mother's sudden death.

At its core, Raising Helen delves into themes of identity, self-discovery, and the challenges of navigating one's place within a close-knit family. As Helen navigates her new role as a guardian to her three nieces, she is forced to confront her own insecurities and limitations, ultimately discovering a sense of purpose and belonging.

The film also touches on the theme of female empowerment, highlighting Helen's journey from an uncertain and immature young woman to a confident and capable individual. Through her experiences, the movie showcases the importance of embracing one's flaws and learning to rely on oneself and others for support.

Furthermore, Raising Helen explores the complexities of family relationships, revealing the intricate web of love, loyalty, and conflict that exists within these bonds. The film masterfully captures the humor and poignancy of family life, making it a relatable and endearing portrayal of the human experience.

Overall, Raising Helen is a poignant exploration of personal growth, identity, and the complexities of family relationships, ultimately revealing the transformative power of love, support, and self-discovery.

documents.title: Hot Fuzz
documents.tagline: Big cops. Small town. Moderate violence.
documents.overview: As a former London constable, Nicholas Angel finds it difficult to adapt to his new assignment in the sleepy British village of Sandford. Not only does he miss the excitement of the big city, but he also has a well-meaning oaf for a partner. However, when a series of grisly accidents rocks Sandford, Angel smells something rotten in the idyllic village.
documents.plot:
Hot Fuzz is a 2007 action comedy film directed by Edgar Wright and written by Wright and Simon Pegg. The movie stars Pegg, Nick Frost, Timothy Dalton, and Jim Broadbent.

The film follows the story of Nicholas Angel (Pegg), a top-notch police officer in London who is known for his exceptional skills and bravery. However, after solving a high-profile case involving a serial killer, Angel becomes an embarrassment to the Metropolitan Police Service due to his unorthodox methods. As a result, he is transferred to the small town of Sandford, where crime rates are low and the police department is understaffed.

Upon arrival in Sandford, Angel meets his new partner, Danny Butterman (Frost), who is an enthusiastic but awkward local cop. The two men quickly clash due to their vastly different approaches to policing, with Angel's by-the-book methods contrasting with Butterman's more relaxed and intuitive approach.

As the story unfolds, a series of bizarre and gruesome murders takes place in Sandford, which Angel initially dismisses as a prank gone wrong. However, when the bodies start piling up, Angel realizes that something sinister is at play. He begins to investigate the murders, working closely with Butterman to uncover the truth behind the killings.

Throughout the investigation, Angel's fish-out-of-water experience in Sandford provides plenty of comedic moments, as he struggles to adapt to the town's eccentricities and the local police department's ineptitude. Meanwhile, Butterman's enthusiasm and loyalty provide a heartwarming counterpoint to Angel's cynicism.

As the plot thickens, Angel and Butterman uncover a shocking conspiracy involving a corrupt politician, a sinister plot to cover up the murders, and a surprising connection between the victims. The film builds towards an action-packed climax as Angel and Butterman confront the mastermind behind the killings in a thrilling showdown.

One of the standout aspects of Hot Fuzz is its clever subversion of action movie tropes, with Wright and Pegg paying homage to classic films like Die Hard and Beverly Hills Cop while also cleverly deconstructing them. The film's witty dialogue, memorable characters, and expertly choreographed action sequences make it a joy to watch.

Ultimately, Hot Fuzz is a hilarious and entertaining ride that balances humor and suspense with ease. With its talented cast, clever writing, and Edgar Wright's masterful direction, the film has become a cult classic and a staple of 2000s British comedy.

documents.title: Read It and Weep
documents.overview: A young girl turns into an A-List celebrity over night when her private journal is accidently published and becomes a best-seller.
documents.plot:
Read It and Weep is a 2006 American comedy-drama Disney Channel Original Movie, which premiered on July 21, 2006. Based on Julia DeVillers's novel How My Private, Personal Journal Became a Bestseller, it stars real-life sisters Kay Panabaker as the ninth-grader Jamie Bartlett and Danielle Panabaker as Isabella, or "Is", the confident heroine of Jamie's imagination. Jason Dolley, Alexandra Krosney, Allison Scagliotti, Nick Whitaker and Robin Riker co-star, and DeVillers makes a cameo in a pizza parlour scene.

Jamie is a freshman with three close friends, Connor, Lindsay and Harmony, a brother named Lenny, and a rival, the popular Sawyer Sullivan, whose boyfriend Marco Vega is Jamie's crush. On her tablet computer she keeps a daily journal starring Is, a glamorous girl with remarkable powers who stands up to a nasty classmate named Myrna. The stories are a fanciful version of Jamie's own life, and Myrna is clearly modelled on Sawyer. When her printer breaks on the day an English essay is due, Jamie emails the file to Lindsay to print, but sends the journal by mistake. Lindsay hands it in, the journal wins a writing contest, and it is published as a novel.

The book becomes a bestseller and Jamie a celebrity, touring signings and talk shows and meeting stars she has long admired. Fame goes to her head: she grows materialistic and dismissive, quits her job at her father's struggling pizza restaurant, mocks Lenny's guitar playing and neglects her friends. During a television interview she lets slip that the villain is based on Sawyer and that the book draws on real school dramas, and her classmates turn against her, hurt by what she has written about them.

Shunned by her friends, Jamie sets out to repair the damage. She apologises to Lenny and encourages him to play again, learns that her parents may have to close the restaurant, and finally confronts Is, telling her imaginary alter ego to stop steering her life. At the ocean-themed school dance her classmates gradually accept that the journal was never meant to be published. Jamie discovers that the poems she admired in class were written by Connor, not Marco, and the two share a kiss while Lenny performs a song for her. Afterwards a mishap with seaweed on the restaurant's pizzas proves a hit with customers, giving the family business a way to survive.

documents.title: The Guardian
documents.tagline: How Do You Decide Who Lives Or Who Dies?
documents.overview: A high school swim champion with a troubled past enrolls in the U.S. Coast Guard's 'A' School, where legendary rescue swimmer, Ben Randall teaches him some hard lessons about loss, love, and self-sacrifice.
documents.plot: A high school swim champion with a troubled past enrolls in the U.S. Coast Guard's 'A' School, where legendary rescue swimmer Ben Randall teaches him some hard lessons about loss, love, and self-sacrifice.

documents.title: Across the Universe
documents.tagline: All you need is love.
documents.overview: When young dockworker Jude leaves Liverpool to find his estranged father in the United States, he is swept up by the waves of change that are re-shaping the nation. Jude falls in love with Lucy, who joins the growing anti-war movement. As the body count in Vietnam rises, political tensions at home spiral out of control and the star-crossed lovers find themselves in a psychedelic world gone mad.
documents.plot:
Across the Universe is a 2007 musical romantic drama film that weaves together the music of The Beatles with a narrative that explores the tumultuous 1960s in Liverpool, England. At its core, the movie delves into themes of love, loss, and social upheaval during a pivotal moment in history.

The story revolves around Lucy (played by Evan Rachel Wood), a young woman who becomes entangled in a complicated web of relationships with Jude (played by Jim Sturgess), a working-class Liverpudlian struggling to find his place in the world. As their romance blossoms, they must navigate the challenges of social class differences and the constraints of societal expectations.

Throughout the film, the characters grapple with the disillusionment and frustration that characterized the late 1960s, as the Vietnam War raged on and the civil rights movement gained momentum. The movie captures the sense of restlessness and rebellion that defined this era, as young people sought to challenge the status quo and forge their own paths.

The film also explores the complexities of identity and belonging, particularly for those who felt like outsiders or misfits. Jude's struggles to reconcile his working-class roots with his aspirations for a better life serve as a powerful metaphor for the tensions between tradition and innovation that defined this period in history.

Ultimately, Across the Universe is a poignant and visually stunning tribute to the music of The Beatles, which serves as a soundtrack for the characters' emotional journeys. Through its exploration of love, loss, and social change, the film offers a nuanced and thought-provoking portrayal of a pivotal moment in modern history.

documents.title: Sympathy for Mr. Vengeance
documents.tagline: Revenge Was Never This Sweet
documents.overview: A deaf man and his girlfriend resort to desperate measures in order to fund a kidney transplant for his sister. Things go horribly wrong, and the situation spirals rapidly into a cycle of violence and revenge.
documents.plot:
Sympathy for Mr. Vengeance is a 2002 South Korean psychological thriller film directed by Park Chan-wook, produced by CJ Entertainment and CJ Entertainment's subsidiary, CJ Entertainment & Media.

The story revolves around the character of Lee Gu (played by Song Kang-ho), an ordinary man who works as a delivery driver in Seoul. He lives a simple life with his wife, Yoo-jin (played by Kim Rye-won), and their young daughter, Soo-yeon (played by Park Hae-il). However, their lives take a drastic turn when they receive a ransom demand from the kidnapper of their daughter.

The kidnapper, Mr. Vengeance (played by Choi Min-sik), demands 10 million won in exchange for Soo-yeon's safe return. The family is shocked and devastated by this news, but Gu decides to take matters into his own hands to rescue his daughter. He embarks on a perilous journey to track down Mr. Vengeance and save Soo-yeon.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Mr. Vengeance has a personal vendetta against the wealthy and influential Kim family, who are responsible for the death of Gu's brother in a car accident several years ago. The kidnapper's true intention is to exact revenge on the Kim family by using their own daughter as leverage.

Throughout the film, Park Chan-wook masterfully weaves together themes of revenge, redemption, and the cyclical nature of violence. The title "Sympathy for Mr. Vengeance" refers to the audience's emotional investment in both Gu's quest to rescue his daughter and Mr. Vengeance's motivations for kidnapping her.

As the plot thickens, Gu becomes increasingly entangled in a web of deceit and betrayal. He discovers that the Kim family is hiding secrets about their past and their connection to the car accident that killed his brother. The film builds towards a shocking climax as Gu confronts the mastermind behind the kidnapping and ultimately exacts revenge on those responsible.

The ending is both haunting and thought-provoking, leaving the audience to ponder the consequences of violence and the cyclical nature of revenge. Despite its dark themes, Sympathy for Mr. Vengeance is a gripping and intense thriller that explores the complexities of human nature and the devastating effects of trauma.

Overall, Sympathy for Mr. Vengeance is a masterful film that showcases Park Chan-wook's unique storytelling style and his ability to craft complex, thought-provoking narratives.

documents.title: Southland Tales
documents.tagline: Have a nice apocalypse.
documents.overview: Set in the futuristic landscape of Los Angeles on July 4, 2008, as it stands on the brink of social, economic and environmental disaster. Boxer Santaros is an action star who's stricken with amnesia. His life intertwines with Krysta Now, an adult film star developing her own reality television project, and Ronald Taverner, a Hermosa Beach police officer who holds the key to a vast conspiracy.
documents.plot:
Southland Tales is a 2006 dystopian black comedy thriller written and directed by Richard Kelly, with an ensemble cast including Dwayne Johnson, Seann William Scott, Sarah Michelle Gellar, Mandy Moore, Justin Timberlake, Will Sasso and Wallace Shawn, and music by Moby. Set in the then-near future of 2008, it is a sprawling satirical portrait of Los Angeles and a commentary on the military-industrial complex, surveillance and the infotainment industry.

On July 4, 2005, nuclear attacks destroy the Texas cities of El Paso and Abilene, plunging the world into a third world war. The United States reinstates the draft and creates US-IDENT, a vast surveillance agency. Amid a fuel crisis, the company Treer unveils Fluid Karma, a seemingly limitless energy source generated by ocean currents, while its scientist Baron von Westphalen harbors grander ambitions.

In Los Angeles in 2008, the action star Boxer Santaros, married to the daughter of a Republican vice-presidential candidate, wakes up with amnesia in the desert and begins an affair with Krysta Now, a former adult film star turned would-be talk show host. Together they have written a screenplay that seems to predict the apocalypse. A cell of neo-Marxist radicals plots to discredit the government by staging a fake act of police brutality, involving Boxer and the police officer Roland Taverner, whose apparent twin brother Ronald is to be dressed in his uniform. But a rogue officer turns the staged killing into a real one, and the leaked footage ignites riots across the city.

As Los Angeles erupts, the elite gather aboard von Westphalen's giant zeppelin to celebrate the launch of Fluid Karma. Boxer learns that Treer's experiments have torn a rift in time, that he is a future version of himself who traveled back an instant, and that contact between two versions of the same person could bring about the apocalypse. Roland and Ronald are likewise the same man from two timelines. When they finally clasp hands, they rise into the air as a rift opens in the sky, and a missile destroys the zeppelin with Boxer aboard. The narrator, Iraq war veteran Pilot Abilene, describes the dawning of a new age.

The film premiered in competition at the 2006 Cannes Film Festival, where it was poorly received, and was re-edited before its US release on November 14, 2007. Critics were divided by its length and chaotic structure despite its intriguing vision; it grossed under $400,000 but has since developed a cult following.

documents.title: Gone Baby Gone
documents.tagline: Everyone wants the truth... until they find it.
documents.overview: When 4 year old Amanda McCready disappears from her home and the police make little headway in solving the case, the girl's aunt, Beatrice McCready hires two private detectives, Patrick Kenzie and Angie Gennaro. The detectives freely admit that they have little experience with this type of case, but the family wants them for two reasons—they're not cops and they know the tough neighborhood in which they all live.

documents.title: Rudo & Cursi
documents.tagline: Even when your luck runs out, some things never change.
documents.overview: Two brothers living a hard life of manual labor in rural Mexico have a simple dream: saving enough money to build their mother her dream house. But fate has other plans. A friendly game of soccer leads to first Rudo, then to Cursi being taken on by the nation’s top talent scout. Suddenly, they find themselves living the high life of star athletes: fame, fortune, fast cars and beautiful women.
documents.plot: Tato and Beto are poor stepbrothers living on a banana plantation in Mexico. Both are talented soccer players, but their dreams lay elsewhere: tone-deaf Tato wants to be a singer, while Beto is content to remain on the plantation. One day, a sports agent sees the two young men playing soccer and offers to take one of them to Mexico City for a chance at sports stardom.

documents.title: Cassandra's Dream
documents.tagline: Family is family. Blood is blood.
documents.overview: The tale of two brothers with serious financial woes. When a third party proposes they turn to crime, things go bad and the two become enemies.
documents.plot:
Cassandra's Dream is a 2007 crime thriller drama written and directed by Woody Allen, starring Colin Farrell, Ewan McGregor, Hayley Atwell, Sally Hawkins and Tom Wilkinson. Shot in England as a co-production between the United States, France and the United Kingdom, it was the third of Allen's London-set films of the period, following Match Point and Scoop, and it features an original score by Philip Glass.

Brothers Ian and Terry live in South London. Their father runs a struggling restaurant, while their mother has always encouraged them to look up to her brother Howard, a wealthy plastic surgeon whose business has expanded to clinics abroad. Using money Terry won on a greyhound named Cassandra's Dream, the brothers buy a bargain sailboat and name it after the dog. Ian, ambitious and restless, falls for Angela Stark, a glamorous young actress, and dreams of investing in California hotels to build a new life with her. Terry, a mechanic with a gambling problem, sinks deeper and deeper into debt after a disastrous run at cards.

Desperate, the brothers turn to Uncle Howard when he visits from abroad. He agrees to help them, but asks a terrible favor in return: they must kill Martin Burns, a former business associate who is prepared to testify against Howard and could send him to prison. After initial horror, both brothers agree. Their first attempt, using homemade untraceable guns, is abandoned when Burns comes home with a companion, but the next day they follow him and carry out the killing. Ian is able to move on, but Terry is consumed by guilt, turning to alcohol and pills and talking of confessing to the police. Ian and Howard conclude that Terry must be silenced. During an outing on the boat, Ian plans to poison his brother but cannot go through with it; a violent struggle breaks out and Terry accidentally kills Ian. The police later find the boat adrift and conclude that Terry killed his brother before drowning himself.

The film premiered at the 64th Venice International Film Festival in September 2007 after an unannounced screening in Avilés, Spain, and was released in the United States in January 2008. Critical opinion was sharply divided. Some reviewers dismissed it as a clichéd morality play and among Allen's weakest films, while others praised it as a modern tale of temptation; The New Yorker's Richard Brody named it one of the best films of the decade.

documents.title: Ghost Dog: The Way of the Samurai
documents.original_title: Ghost Dog: The Way of the Samurai
documents.tagline: Live by the code. Die by the code.
documents.overview: An African-American Mafia hit man who models himself after the samurai of old finds himself targeted for death by the mob. Jarmusch's spiritual gangster film tells the story of an inner-city hit man (Whitaker) who lives on a rooftop, training himself as a samurai in the strictest sense. He communicates primarily by carrier pigeon, while remaining loyal to a gangster (Tormey) who once saved his life.
documents.plot:
Ghost Dog: The Way of the Samurai is a 1999 crime drama written, produced and directed by Jim Jarmusch. Forest Whitaker stars as Ghost Dog, a hitman for the Mafia who lives by the ancient code of the samurai as set out in the Hagakure, the collection of sayings attributed to Yamamoto Tsunetomo. Cliff Gorman, Henry Silva, Isaach de Bankolé, Victor Argo and Camille Winbush appear in supporting roles, and RZA of the Wu-Tang Clan, who composed the score, makes his film debut. An international co-production between the United States, France, Germany and Japan, the film competed for the Palme d'Or at the 1999 Cannes Film Festival.

Ghost Dog lives alone on a rooftop in an unnamed American city with a flock of homing pigeons, which he uses to communicate. He considers himself the retainer of Louie, a small-time mobster who saved his life years earlier, and he has served him faithfully as a contract killer ever since, applying the wisdom of the Hagakure, which is quoted throughout the film, to his everyday existence.

Louie orders him to kill Handsome Frank, a gangster who has been sleeping with the daughter of the mob boss Vargo. Ghost Dog carries out the hit, but discovers that the young woman is also in the room. He spares her, and she gives him a copy of the book Rashōmon. To avoid blame for the murder of a made man, Vargo and his associates decide that Ghost Dog must be eliminated. Since Louie knows almost nothing about his retainer, the mobsters track him down by searching the city's pigeon coops, and they kill his birds. Ghost Dog realises that he must strike back against Vargo's crew, even while remaining loyal to Louie. Meanwhile, he spends time with his best friend Raymond, a French-speaking ice-cream vendor with whom he shares no common language, and befriends Pearline, a young girl with whom he exchanges books.

Jarmusch blends the gangster film with samurai cinema and hip-hop culture, drawing on influences such as Jean-Pierre Melville's Le Samouraï, and treats the aging Mafia figures as men clinging to a fading code of their own.

Ghost Dog received largely positive reviews, with an approval rating of about 84 percent on Rotten Tomatoes, and critics praised Whitaker's performance, the film's offbeat humour and RZA's score.

documents.title: Layer Cake
documents.tagline: The art of good business is being a good middleman.
documents.overview: When a seemingly straight-forward drug deal goes awry, XXXX has to break his die-hard rules and turn up the heat, not only to outwit the old regime and come out on top, but to save his own skin...
documents.plot: When a seemingly straight-forward drug deal goes awry, XXXX has to break his die-hard rules and turn up the heat, not only to outwit the old regime and come out on top, but to save his own skin...

documents.title: The Invasion
documents.tagline: Do not trust anyone. Do not show emotion. Do not fall asleep.
documents.overview: Washington, D.C. psychologist Carol Bennell and her colleague Dr. Ben Driscoll are the only two people on Earth who are aware of an epidemic running rampant through the city. They discover an alien virus aboard a crashed space shuttle that transforms anyone who comes into contact with it into unfeeling drones while they sleep. Carol realizes her son holds the key to stopping the spread of the plague and she races to find him before it is too late.

documents.title: Confessions of a Dangerous Mind
documents.tagline: Some things are better left top secret.
documents.overview: Television made him famous, but his biggest hits happened off screen. Television producer by day, CIA assassin by night, Chuck Barris was recruited by the CIA at the height of his TV career and trained to become a covert operative. Or so Barris said.

documents.title: The Curious Case of Benjamin Button
documents.original_title: The Curious Case of Benjamin Button
documents.tagline: Life isn't measured in minutes, but in moments.
documents.overview: I was born under unusual circumstances. And so begins The Curious Case of Benjamin Button, adapted from the 1920s story by F. Scott Fitzgerald about a man who is born in his eighties and ages backwards: a man, like any of us, who is unable to stop time. We follow his story, set in New Orleans, from the end of World War I in 1918 into the 21st century, following his journey that is as unusual as any man's life can be. Benjamin Button, is a grand tale of a not-so-ordinary man and the people and places he discovers along the way, the loves he finds, the joys of life and the sadness of death, and what lasts beyond time.
documents.plot:
The Curious Case of Benjamin Button is a 2008 American fantasy drama directed by David Fincher, adapted by Eric Roth and Robin Swicord from F. Scott Fitzgerald's 1922 short story. Brad Pitt stars as a man who ages in reverse and Cate Blanchett as Daisy, the love of his life, with Taraji P. Henson, Julia Ormond, Jason Flemyng, Elias Koteas and Tilda Swinton. After decades in development, it was released by Paramount Pictures in North America and Warner Bros. internationally on 25 December 2008.

In August 2005, as Hurricane Katrina approaches, the elderly Daisy Fuller lies dying in a New Orleans hospital. She tells her daughter Caroline about a blind clockmaker who built a station clock that ran backward, in memory of the young men, including his own son, killed in the First World War. Daisy then asks Caroline to read aloud from the diary of Benjamin Button. On the night of 11 November 1918, a baby is born with the appearance and ailments of a very old man. His mother dies after the birth, and his father, the wealthy button manufacturer Thomas Button, abandons him on the steps of a nursing home. Queenie, a caretaker there, raises him as her own and names him Benjamin.

Benjamin grows older in mind but younger in body, moving from a wheelchair to crutches and learning to walk. In 1930 he meets seven-year-old Daisy, whose grandmother lives at the home, and they form an immediate bond. As a young-looking old man, he goes to work on a tugboat captained by Mike Clark and travels the world, sending postcards to Daisy, who becomes a dancer in New York. In Murmansk he has an affair with Elizabeth Abbott, the wife of a British official, and during the Second World War his tugboat is drawn into combat. Returning home, he reunites with his dying father, who has revealed himself, and inherits his fortune. Benjamin and Daisy's paths cross repeatedly as they move in opposite directions through time, until in middle age they finally meet in the same moment of their lives and fall in love, knowing their time together is fleeting.

The film received generally positive reviews and grossed over $335 million worldwide. It received thirteen Academy Award nominations, the most of that year, including Best Picture, Best Director and Best Actor for Pitt, and won three, for Best Art Direction, Best Makeup and Best Visual Effects.

documents.title: Howl's Moving Castle
documents.tagline: The two lived there.
documents.overview: When Sophie, a shy young woman, is cursed with an old body by a spiteful witch, her only chance of breaking the spell lies with a self-indulgent yet insecure young wizard and his companions in his legged, walking castle.
documents.plot:
Howl's Moving Castle (Japanese: ハウルの動く城) is a 2004 Japanese animated fantasy film written and directed by Hayao Miyazaki, loosely based on Diana Wynne Jones's 1986 novel. Produced by Toshio Suzuki at Studio Ghibli and distributed by Toho, it features the voices of Chieko Baisho, Takuya Kimura and Akihiro Miwa. Set in a fictional kingdom where magic coexists with early 20th-century technology during a war, it reflects Miyazaki's opposition to the Iraq War.

Sophie, a shy young hatmaker, is rescued from two soldiers by a mysterious wizard, Howl. That evening, the jealous Witch of the Waste enters Sophie's shop and curses her, transforming her into a ninety-year-old woman who cannot speak of the spell. Sophie leaves home and wanders into the hills, where she befriends an enchanted scarecrow she names Turnip Head, who leads her to Howl's huge walking castle. Inside, she meets Howl's young apprentice, Markl, and Calcifer, a fire demon bound to Howl by a contract and the source of the castle's power. Calcifer promises to break her curse if she frees him, and she becomes the castle's cleaning lady.

The king summons Howl to aid in the war, but Howl sends Sophie, posing as his mother, to declare him a coward. At the palace, Madame Suliman, the royal sorceress and Howl's former teacher, strips the Witch of the Waste of her powers, reducing her to a harmless old woman, and threatens Howl with the same fate. Howl rescues Sophie, and they escape with the Witch and Suliman's dog. Sophie learns that Howl has been transforming into a bird-like creature to fight against both sides of the war, at the risk of losing his humanity, and her feelings for him grow.

When the town is bombed, Howl leaves to protect his household. To save him, Sophie removes Calcifer from the hearth, collapsing the castle. Through a magic ring, she travels into Howl's past and sees him as a boy swallowing a falling star, Calcifer, and giving the demon his heart. She returns Howl's heart to him, freeing Calcifer and breaking her own curse. Her kiss transforms Turnip Head back into a missing prince of the enemy kingdom, who sets off to end the war, and Sophie and Howl fly off together in a rebuilt castle.

Howl's Moving Castle premiered at the Venice Film Festival and became one of Japan's most successful films, grossing about $236 million worldwide. It received critical acclaim and was nominated for the Academy Award for Best Animated Feature.

documents.title: Leatherheads
documents.tagline: If Love Is a Game, Who'll Make the First Pass?
documents.overview: A light hearted comedy about the beginnings of Professional American Football. When a decorated war hero and college all star is tempted into playing professional football. Everyone see the chance to make some big money, but when a reporter digs up some dirt on the war hero... everyone could lose out.
documents.plot:
Leatherheads is a 2008 American sports comedy directed by George Clooney, who also stars, written by Duncan Brantley and Rick Reilly. Set in the early years of professional American football, it co-stars Renée Zellweger, John Krasinski, Jonathan Pryce, Stephen Root and Wayne Duvall. Universal Pictures released it on 4 April 2008.

In 1925, Jimmy "Dodge" Connelly, an aging player, captains the Duluth Bulldogs, a struggling professional football team. With the professional game on the verge of collapse and players unpaid, Dodge persuades Carter "the Bullet" Rutherford, a star player at Princeton and a celebrated First World War hero, to join the Bulldogs, hoping that his fame will draw crowds. Carter's arrival transforms the team's fortunes, and the games attract huge audiences.

Lexie Littleton, a fast-talking reporter for the Chicago Tribune, is assigned to prove that Carter's wartime heroics, which supposedly involved capturing a group of German soldiers single-handedly, are a fabrication. As she travels with the team, she finds herself caught in a love triangle with Dodge and Carter. Carter eventually confesses to her that the German platoon surrendered to him by mistake, but he also discovers her assignment and learns that she has shared a kiss with Dodge. Pressured by threats from Carter's slick manager, Lexie publishes the story, while the manager uses underhanded tactics, including bribing a key witness, to discredit her. Meanwhile, a commissioner appointed to clean up the sport introduces formal rules that threaten the improvised tricks on which Dodge relies. When public opinion turns against Lexie, Dodge intervenes at a hearing, forcing the truth into the open, and the story builds toward a muddy, decisive game between the Bulldogs and Carter's new team in Chicago, in which Dodge must use all his cunning to win.

Leatherheads received mixed reviews; critics appreciated its affectionate homage to the screwball comedies of the 1930s and its period atmosphere but found it uneven and slow. It grossed about $41 million worldwide against a budget of $58 million.

documents.title: Be Kind Rewind
documents.tagline: You name it, we shoot it.
documents.overview: A man whose brain becomes magnetized unintentionally destroys every tape in his friend's video store. In order to satisfy the store's most loyal renter, an aging woman with signs of dementia, the two men set out to remake the lost films.
documents.plot: A man whose brain becomes magnetized unintentionally destroys every tape in his friend's video store. In order to satisfy the store's most loyal renter, an aging woman with signs of dementia, the two men set out to remake the lost films.

documents.title: The Legend of Bagger Vance
documents.tagline: It Was Just A Moment Ago.
documents.overview: World War I has left golfer Rannulph Junuh a poker-playing alcoholic, his perfect swing gone. Now, however, he needs to get it back to play in a tournament to save the financially ravaged golf course of a long-ago sweetheart. Help arrives in the form of mysterious caddy Bagger Vance.
documents.plot:
The Legend of Bagger Vance is a 2000 American sports drama film directed by Robert Redford. The movie tells the story of Rannulph Junuh, a young golfer from Georgia who seeks the advice of an enigmatic caddie named Bagger Vance to help him win a high-stakes golf tournament.

At its core, The Legend of Bagger Vance is a film about redemption and self-discovery. Rannulph's journey is one of coming to terms with his past mistakes and finding forgiveness from himself and others. Through his interactions with Bagger Vance, who embodies the values of humility, integrity, and respect for nature, Rannulph learns to let go of his ego and find a deeper connection with the game of golf.

The film also explores themes of friendship and loyalty, as Rannulph forms a bond with Bagger Vance, who becomes like a mentor to him. The movie highlights the importance of relationships in our lives and how they can help us grow and learn from our experiences.

Furthermore, The Legend of Bagger Vance is a story about finding one's true purpose and identity. Rannulph's journey is not just about winning a golf tournament, but about discovering who he is as a person and what truly matters to him in life. Through his experiences, he learns to appreciate the simple things in life and finds a sense of peace and contentment.

Overall, The Legend of Bagger Vance is a film that celebrates the beauty of nature, the importance of relationships, and the power of self-discovery and redemption.

documents.title: The International
documents.tagline: Is your money making a killing?
documents.overview: An interpol agent and an attorney are determined to bring one of the world's most powerful banks to justice. Uncovering money laundering, arms trading, and conspiracy to destabilize world governments, their investigation takes them from Berlin, Milan, New York and Istanbul. Finding themselves in a chase across the globe, their relentless tenacity puts their own lives at risk.
documents.plot:
The International is an action thriller film that delves into the darker aspects of global politics and corruption. The story revolves around a secret organization within the United Nations, known as the International Centre for Settlement of Investment Disputes (ICSID), which harbors a sinister agenda.

At its core, The International explores the theme of power and control, highlighting how those in positions of authority will stop at nothing to maintain their grip on power. The film's protagonist, Narrator (played by Clive Owen), is a skilled operative who becomes embroiled in a complex web of deceit and corruption.

The movie also touches upon the theme of globalization and its consequences. The ICSID organization serves as a microcosm for the corrupting influence of power and money, demonstrating how institutions meant to promote international cooperation can be co-opted by those seeking personal gain.

Furthermore, The International critiques the notion of moral relativism, suggesting that even in the most seemingly neutral or humanitarian contexts, there exists a gray area where right and wrong become blurred. This theme is expertly woven throughout the narrative, as the protagonist navigates a world where allegiances are constantly shifting and the lines between good and evil are intentionally obscured.

Overall, The International presents a gripping and thought-provoking thriller that delves into the darker aspects of human nature and the corrupting influence of power.

documents.title: Synecdoche, New York
documents.tagline: The end is built into the beginning.
documents.overview: A theater director struggles with his work, and the women in his life, as he attempts to create a life-size replica of New York inside a warehouse as part of his new play.
documents.plot: A theater director struggles with his work, and the women in his life, as he attempts to create a life-size replica of New York inside a warehouse as part of his new play.

documents.title: Knocked Up
documents.tagline: Save the due date.
documents.overview: For fun loving party animal Ben Stone, the last thing he ever expected was for his one night stand to show up on his doorstep eight weeks later to tell him she's pregnant.
documents.plot: A slacker and a career-driven woman accidentally conceive a child after a one-night stand. As they try to make the relationship work, they must navigate the challenges of parenthood and their differences in lifestyle and maturity.

documents.title: The Green Butchers
documents.tagline: There is something mythological about killing an animal and then mocking it by sticking it into its own intestine
documents.overview: A black comedy featuring two butchers, Svend "Sweat" and Bjarne, who start their own shop to get away from their arrogant boss. Cannibalism is soon introduced to the plot, and further complications arise due to the reappearance of Bjarne's intellectually disabled twin brother Eigil.
documents.plot:
The Green Butchers (Danish: De grønne slagtere) is a 2003 Danish black comedy written and directed by Anders Thomas Jensen. It stars Mads Mikkelsen as Svend, nicknamed "Sweat", and Nikolaj Lie Kaas in the dual roles of the butcher Bjarne and his twin brother Eigil, with Line Kruse as Astrid. The film follows two misfit butchers whose new business becomes a runaway success thanks to a gruesome secret ingredient.

Svend and Bjarne work in a butcher shop under their arrogant and condescending boss, Holger, who mocks Svend's pride and joy, his special marinade. Insecure and desperate for recognition, Svend persuades the withdrawn Bjarne to go into business with him, and they open their own shop in a small Danish town. Bjarne has his own reason for needing money: his intellectually disabled twin brother Eigil, left brain-damaged by a car accident that killed their parents and Bjarne's wife, has been kept on life support for years, and Bjarne is ready to claim his inheritance.

On opening day no customers come. Then Svend accidentally locks an electrician in the cold store overnight, and the man freezes to death. In panic, Svend disposes of the body by turning it into meat, marinating it and selling it, and the new product, which he calls "chicky-wickies", becomes a sensation, drawing long queues of customers. Bjarne is horrified but reluctantly goes along with the scheme as business booms. To keep up with demand, Svend must find more ingredients, while Bjarne's life is complicated by his relationship with Astrid, a kind young woman who works at the local church, and by Eigil, an innocent, animal-loving man who unexpectedly wakes up when his life support is switched off and turns up at the shop.

Jensen's comedy uses its grotesque premise to explore loneliness, insecurity, grief and the desire for acceptance, mixing deadpan humor with surprising tenderness.

The Green Butchers won several European awards, including the 2003 Méliès d'Or. It holds an approval rating of about 63 percent on Rotten Tomatoes, and later reappraisals, such as a 2023 Collider review, praised the nuance of both the script and Mikkelsen's performance.

documents.title: Vicky Cristina Barcelona
documents.tagline: Life is the ultimate work of art.
documents.overview: Two girlfriends on a summer holiday in Spain become enamored with the same painter, unaware that his ex-wife, with whom he has a tempestuous relationship, is about to re-enter the picture.
documents.plot:
Vicky Cristina Barcelona is a 2008 romantic comedy-drama film written and directed by Woody Allen. Rebecca Hall and Scarlett Johansson star as Vicky and Cristina, two young American women spending a summer in Spain, with Javier Bardem as the painter Juan Antonio and Penélope Cruz as his volatile ex-wife, María Elena, with Patricia Clarkson, Kevin Dunn and Chris Messina in supporting roles and Christopher Evan Welch as the narrator. Filmed in Barcelona, Avilés and Oviedo, it premiered at the 2008 Cannes Film Festival.

Vicky and Cristina, close friends with very different attitudes toward love, spend a summer in Barcelona staying with Vicky's relative Judy and her husband, Mark. Vicky, practical and conventional, is engaged to the dependable Doug, while Cristina sees herself as a free spirit but is uncertain about what she wants. At an art exhibition, they notice Juan Antonio, an attractive painter rumored to have had a violent relationship with his former wife. He boldly invites both women to fly with him to Oviedo for a weekend of sightseeing, food, wine and, he frankly hopes, lovemaking. Cristina is immediately enthusiastic; Vicky, unimpressed, comes along to keep an eye on her friend.

When Cristina falls ill with food poisoning on the first night, Vicky and Juan Antonio spend the weekend together, and despite her resistance she is charmed and sleeps with him, an experience that leaves her shaken. Back in Barcelona, Cristina begins a relationship with Juan Antonio and moves into his home, while Vicky, troubled by her feelings, goes ahead with her marriage to Doug. Then María Elena, a brilliant but unstable artist, arrives after a suicide attempt, and Juan Antonio takes her in. Instead of driving Cristina away, the situation evolves into a passionate three-way relationship in which Cristina finds inspiration for her photography. As the summer progresses, however, Cristina grows restless, Vicky remains drawn to Juan Antonio, and the tangled relationships come to a head in a dramatic confrontation that sends the two Americans home changed, if not wiser.

The film received widespread acclaim, particularly for Cruz's fiery performance and Bardem's charm, and was one of Allen's biggest late-career successes, grossing nearly $100 million worldwide. Cruz won the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress, and the film won the Golden Globe Award for Best Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy.

documents.title: The Sugarland Express
documents.tagline: Every cop in the state was after her. Everybody else was behind her.
documents.overview: Married small-time crooks Lou-Jean and Clovis Poplin lose their baby to the state of Texas and resolve to do whatever it takes to get him back. Lou-Jean gets Clovis out of jail, and the two steal their son from his foster home, in addition to taking a highway patrolman hostage. As a massive dragnet starts to pursue them across Texas, the couple become unlikely folk heroes and even start to bond with the captive policeman.
documents.plot:
The Sugarland Express is an American crime drama of 1974 and Steven Spielberg's first theatrical feature as director, following his television film Duel. Hal Barwood and Matthew Robbins wrote the screenplay from a story they developed with Spielberg. Based on real events, it stars Goldie Hawn as Lou Jean Poplin and William Atherton as her husband Clovis, who take a state trooper hostage and flee across Texas to reclaim their child, with Michael Sacks as the trooper Maxwell Slide and Ben Johnson as Captain Tanner. It began his partnership with John Williams.

In April 1969, Lou Jean visits Clovis in prison to tell him that their young son is about to be placed with foster parents. Although he is only four months from release, she persuades him to escape and help her get the boy back. The pair hitch a ride away from the prison with a couple, but when Patrolman Slide of the Texas Department of Public Safety pulls the car over, they make off in it. After the car crashes, they overpower Slide and take him hostage in his own patrol car.

What follows is a slow-moving chase across Texas, with the fugitives and their captive at the head of an ever-growing convoy, first of police cars and later of news vans, helicopters and ordinary citizens who join in. Holding Slide allows the couple to keep refueling and to obtain food and supplies, some from sympathetic locals, and over the long journey the three come to like and respect one another. When the trio stop at a used car lot to commandeer a camper, local vigilantes attack them, but Tanner lets the Poplins drive on after further bargaining.

When they reach Sugarland, Tanner urges Clovis to give himself up, but he refuses. Slide, and then Clovis, sense that something is wrong at the foster parents' house, yet Lou Jean insists that her husband go in for their son. Two Texas Rangers shoot Clovis, mortally wounding him, and after a further chase Lou Jean is arrested; Slide is found unharmed. A closing epilogue explains that Lou Jean served fifteen months of a five-year sentence and later won the right to live with her son.

Parts of the film were shot in Sugar Land, where some of the real events took place, and around San Antonio and other Texas towns. It won the award for Best Screenplay at the 1974 Cannes Film Festival and drew positive reviews, but with a worldwide gross of about $12 million it remains the lowest-grossing film of Spielberg's career, and Universal pulled it from theaters after two weeks.

documents.title: August Rush
documents.tagline: An incredible journey moving at the speed of sound.
documents.overview: Lyla and Louis, a singer and a musician, fall in love, but are soon compelled to separate. Lyla is forced to give up her newborn but unknown to her, he grows up to become a musical genius.
documents.plot:
August Rush is a musical drama film released in 2007 by Warner Bros. Pictures. The movie tells the story of an adopted boy named Evan Taylor, who discovers his birth parents and embarks on a journey to find his roots.

The film begins with Evan (played by Freddie Highmore), a talented young musician who lives with his foster parents, Robert and Lily Taylor (played by Jonathan Rhys Meyers and Keri Russell). Despite their love for him, Evan feels like an outsider in his family. He is haunted by strange memories of music and a sense of belonging he can't explain.

As Evan grows older, he begins to experience vivid dreams and visions that seem to be connected to the music he hears. He becomes obsessed with finding the source of these sounds, which lead him on a journey to New York City. There, he meets a street musician named Gus (played by Jason Schwartzman), who claims to have known Evan's biological father.

Evan soon discovers that his birth parents were both musicians who were part of a famous jazz band in the 1950s. He learns that his mother, Lyla (played by Marcia Gay Harden), was a singer and songwriter, while his father, Robert Lewis (played by Terence Stamp), was a pianist and composer.

As Evan delves deeper into his family's past, he meets his biological siblings, Charlie (played by James Carnes) and Isabel (played by Fiona Shaw). Together, they form a band and begin to perform music that is a fusion of their different styles. Through this process, Evan comes to terms with his identity and finds a sense of belonging.

However, the journey is not without its challenges. Evan's biological father, Robert Lewis, had abandoned his family years ago, leaving behind a legacy of unfinished business. As Evan gets to know him, he learns about the sacrifices his father made for his music and the pain he caused by leaving his family.

The film builds towards a emotional climax as Evan confronts his past and makes amends with his father. In the end, Evan finds a sense of peace and belonging, not just through his music but also through his connection to his biological family.

Overall, August Rush is a heartwarming story about identity, family, and the power of music to bring people together. The film features a talented cast, beautiful music, and a poignant storyline that will leave audiences feeling uplifted and inspired.

documents.title: Sky Captain and the World of Tomorrow
documents.original_title: Sky Captain and the World of Tomorrow
documents.tagline: Who will save us?
documents.overview: When gigantic robots attack New York City, "Sky Captain" uses his private air force to fight them off. His ex-girlfriend, reporter Polly Perkins, has been investigating the recent disappearance of prominent scientists. Suspecting a link between the global robot attacks and missing men, Sky Captain and Polly decide to work together. They fly to the Himalayas in pursuit of the mysterious Dr. Totenkopf, the mastermind behind the robots.
