documents.title: The In-Laws
documents.tagline: He's not losing his daughter. He's gaining a madman.
documents.overview: Right before his daughter's wedding, a mild-mannered foot doctor discovers that his new in-laws are international smugglers.
documents.plot:
The In-Laws is a comedy film that revolves around the complex and often humorous relationship between two families who are brought together through marriage. At its core, the movie explores the theme of identity and how it can be both a source of comfort and a point of contention.

As the story unfolds, we see the main character, Harry Sanborn (played by Albert Brooks), struggling to come to terms with his own sense of self-worth and purpose in life. His marriage to a younger woman has led him to feel like he's lost touch with his own identity, and he finds himself feeling inadequate and insecure.

On the other hand, we have Marisa (played by Patricia Clarkson), Harry's wife, who is portrayed as a confident and independent individual. However, as the story progresses, it becomes clear that she too has her own set of insecurities and fears, particularly when it comes to her relationship with Harry.

The movie also explores the theme of generational differences and how they can lead to misunderstandings and conflicts between people from different age groups. The character of Jack (played by Richard Dreyfuss) serves as a catalyst for these tensions, as he brings his own set of values and expectations to the table, which often clash with those of Harry and Marisa.

Throughout the film, the authorship of the main theme is not clear-cut, but it can be argued that the movie ultimately presents a nuanced exploration of how identity is shaped by our relationships with others. The In-Laws is a witty and engaging comedy that uses humor to explore deeper themes about human connection, vulnerability, and the complexities of family dynamics.

documents.title: The Astronaut Farmer
documents.overview: Texan Charles Farmer left the Air Force as a young man to save the family ranch when his dad died. Like most American ranchers, he owes his bank. Unlike most, he's an astrophysicist with a rocket in his barn - one he's built and wants to take into space. It's his dream. The FBI puts him under surveillance when he tries to buy rocket fuel, and the FAA stalls him when he files a flight plan – but Charles is undeterred.
documents.plot:
The Astronaut Farmer is a 2006 American family drama film that explores the complexities of family relationships and the sacrifices made for the greater good. The movie revolves around Michael Collins, a former astronaut who returns to his rural Texas farm after being grounded due to a heart condition. As he struggles to adjust to life on Earth, he must also confront the consequences of his past actions and the expectations placed upon him by his family.

The film delves into themes of identity, duty, and redemption, as Michael navigates his relationships with his wife, his children, and his estranged father. Through his character's journey, the movie highlights the importance of finding one's place in the world and making amends for past mistakes.

One of the primary themes of The Astronaut Farmer is the struggle to balance personal ambition with family responsibilities. Michael's experiences as an astronaut have left him feeling disconnected from his loved ones, and he must confront the reality that his career choices have come at a great cost to those around him.

The film also explores the theme of forgiveness and understanding, particularly in the context of intergenerational relationships. As Michael reconciles with his father, played by Sam Elliott, he comes to terms with the complexities of their past and the ways in which they have hurt each other.

Ultimately, The Astronaut Farmer is a heartwarming and thought-provoking film that celebrates the power of family love and redemption. Through its exploration of complex themes and characters, the movie offers a nuanced portrayal of what it means to be human and to find one's place in the world.

documents.title: Rush Hour 3
documents.tagline: The Rush Is On!
documents.overview: After a botched assassination attempt, the mismatched duo finds themselves in Paris, struggling to retrieve a precious list of names, as the murderous crime syndicate's henchmen try their best to stop them. Once more, Lee and Carter must fight their way through dangerous gangsters; however, this time, the past has come back to haunt Lee. Will the boys get the job done once and for all?
documents.plot:
Rush Hour 3 is a 2007 action comedy film directed by Brett Ratner and starring Jackie Chan and Chris Tucker as the main characters, Inspector Lee and Detective James Carter. The movie takes place three years after the events of Rush Hour 2.

The story begins with Inspector Lee (Jackie Chan) being summoned to Paris by his friend, Inspector Soo-Yong (Ken Leung), who is now working for Interpol. Soo-Yong informs Lee that a valuable artifact, the "Dragon's Blood" diamond, has been stolen from a museum in Paris. The thief plans to sell it on the black market, and Soo-Yong needs Lee's help to track him down.

Upon arrival in Paris, Lee meets up with his old friend, Detective James Carter (Chris Tucker), who is now working for Interpol as well. Carter is initially reluctant to work with Lee again, but eventually agrees to help him solve the case.

As they begin their investigation, Lee and Carter discover that the thief is a wealthy businessman named Yuen (Yuen Wah), who has connections to the Triads. They also learn that Yuen plans to sell the diamond to a mysterious buyer in Dubai.

Lee and Carter's investigation takes them from Paris to Hong Kong, where they encounter various obstacles and challenges along the way. Along the way, Lee must confront his own personal demons and learn to trust Carter again.

As the story unfolds, Lee and Carter discover that Yuen is working with a group of Triad members who are seeking revenge against the Chinese government for their treatment of them in Hong Kong. The group plans to use the diamond to fund their operations and exact revenge on China.

In the climactic final act, Lee and Carter track down Yuen and his accomplices to Dubai, where they engage in a high-stakes battle to recover the stolen diamond. In the end, Lee and Carter successfully foil the plot, but not before Yuen is killed by one of his own accomplices.

The movie ends with Lee and Carter returning to Hong Kong as heroes, where they are greeted with parades and celebrations. The film concludes on a positive note, with Lee and Carter's friendship stronger than ever.

Overall, Rush Hour 3 received mixed reviews from critics, but was still a commercial success, grossing over $250 million worldwide. While it did not live up to the expectations of some fans, the movie still delivered plenty of action, humor, and excitement, making it a satisfying conclusion to the Rush Hour trilogy.

documents.title: 3:10 to Yuma
documents.tagline: Time waits for one man.
documents.overview: In Arizona in the late 1800s, infamous outlaw Ben Wade and his vicious gang of thieves and murderers have plagued the Southern Railroad. When Wade is captured, Civil War veteran Dan Evans, struggling to survive on his drought-plagued ranch, volunteers to deliver him alive to the "3:10 to Yuma", a train that will take the killer to trial.
documents.plot:
3:10 to Yuma is a 2007 American Western action drama directed by James Mangold and produced by Cathy Konrad. The second screen adaptation of Elmore Leonard's 1953 short story "Three-Ten to Yuma", following the 1957 film, it casts Christian Bale as a drought-stricken rancher who takes on the perilous job of escorting a notorious outlaw, played by Russell Crowe, to justice. It was filmed at various locations in New Mexico, premiered in Los Angeles in August 2007 and was released by Lionsgate on September 7.

In the Arizona Territory of 1884, Dan Evans, a struggling rancher and Civil War veteran, is in debt to Glen Hollander, whose men burn his barn. Searching for his scattered cattle with his two sons, Evans witnesses Ben Wade's gang rob a stagecoach guarded by Pinkertons. Wade takes the family's horses but leaves them alive, and Evans rescues the only surviving guard, Pinkerton agent Byron McElroy. In the town of Bisbee, Wade lingers with a barmaid and is arrested. Railroad agent Grayson Butterfield assembles a posse, including McElroy, the veterinarian Doc Potter and Hollander's man Tucker, to take Wade to Contention and put him on the 3:10 train to Yuma Territorial Prison, and Evans signs on for $200 to save his ranch.

On the journey, Wade kills Tucker with a stolen fork and throws McElroy off a cliff. Evans's elder son, William, follows and helps stop an escape. After an Apache attack, Wade flees to a camp of Chinese laborers whose foreman bears a grudge against him, and Potter is killed in the ensuing gunfight. In Contention, Wade's vicious lieutenant, Charlie Prince, offers $200 to anyone who kills a captor; the marshals desert, and Butterfield gives up. Evans refuses to quit, demanding better terms for his family and declaring that the task is now about honor; he reveals that he lost part of his leg after being accidentally shot by one of his own men during a retreat. Wade, who has escaped Yuma twice, helps Evans dodge the gunfire and boards the train, but Prince shoots Evans. Wade kills Prince and the rest of his gang, then surrenders his weapon as William comforts his dying father. As the train pulls away, Wade whistles and his horse gallops after it.

Crowe plays Wade and Bale plays Evans, with Peter Fonda as McElroy, Ben Foster as Prince, Logan Lerman as William, Dallas Roberts as Butterfield and Gretchen Mol as Alice Evans. Critics were enthusiastic, with 89% approval on Rotten Tomatoes, and it grossed $71.2 million on a $48–55 million budget.

documents.title: The Polar Express
documents.tagline: This holiday season... believe.
documents.overview: When a doubting young boy takes an extraordinary train ride to the North Pole, he embarks on a journey of self-discovery that shows him that the wonder of life never fades for those who believe.
documents.plot:
The Polar Express is a 2004 animated film directed by Robert Zemeckis, produced by Castle Rock Entertainment, and based on the children's book of the same name by Chris Van Allsburg.

The story follows a young boy who lives in a small town with his parents. On Christmas Eve, he lies awake in bed, feeling lonely and disconnected from the magic of the holiday season. As he drifts off to sleep, he is visited by a mysterious train called the Polar Express, which arrives at his house and whisks him away on an adventure.

The boy boards the train, where he meets other children who are also traveling to the North Pole. They are greeted by the conductor, who welcomes them aboard with a warm smile. As they journey through the night, the boy experiences incredible sights and sensations: snow-covered landscapes, sparkling stars, and even a visit from Santa Claus himself.

However, not all of the passengers on the train are what they seem. One boy is revealed to be a "bad boy" who has been naughty throughout the year, and he is punished by being forced to sit in a cold, dark room with no toys or treats. The other children, including our protagonist, are rewarded for their good behavior.

As the journey continues, the boy begins to question whether the entire experience was just a dream. He wonders if he really did board the Polar Express, or if it was all just his imagination. But as he looks out the window of the train, he sees the Northern Lights dancing in the sky, and he knows that something magical is real.

The film's climax features a heartwarming moment when Santa Claus presents each child with a special gift: a golden ticket to ride on the Polar Express forever. The boy returns home, feeling transformed by his experience and filled with a newfound sense of wonder and joy.

Throughout the film, Zemeckis uses innovative visual effects to bring the world of the Polar Express to life. The animation is stunning, with beautifully rendered landscapes and characters that seem almost real. The voice cast, including Tom Hanks as the narrator and several other notable actors, adds depth and warmth to the story.

Overall, The Polar Express is a timeless tale of childhood wonder and the magic of the holiday season. It's a film that will leave audiences of all ages feeling inspired and uplifted, with its themes of kindness, generosity, and the power of imagination.

documents.title: Chaos
documents.tagline: When the system breaks down... someone is about to get rich.
documents.overview: In Seattle, detective Quentin Conners is unfairly suspended and his partner Jason York leaves the police force after a tragic shooting on Pearl Street Bridge, when the hostage and the criminal die. During a bank heist with a hostage situation, Conners is assigned in charge of the operation with the rookie Shane Dekker as his partner. The thieves, lead by Lorenz, apparently do not steal a penny from the bank. While chasing the gangsters, the police team disclose that they planted a virus in the system, stealing one billion dollars from the different accounts, using the principle of the Chaos Theory. Further, they find that Lorenz is killing his accomplices.
documents.plot:
Chaos is a 2005 crime action thriller written and directed by Tony Giglio, starring Jason Statham, Ryan Phillippe and Wesley Snipes, with Henry Czerny and Justine Waddell in supporting roles. Distribution disputes delayed its release for years: it premiered in the United Arab Emirates in December 2005, but did not reach North America until it appeared on DVD in February 2008.

Seattle detective Quentin Conners and his partner Jason York are disgraced after a botched standoff on a bridge in which York accidentally kills a hostage taken by the carjacker John Curtis, and Conners then kills Curtis. A fellow officer testifies against them; Conners is suspended and York is fired. Some time later a gang led by a man calling himself Lorenz takes hostages in a bank and insists on negotiating with Conners, who is reinstated and paired with a fresh-faced rookie, Shane Dekker. The robbers escape amid an explosion, and Dekker notes that Lorenz kept alluding to chaos theory.

The investigation uncovers a series of puzzles. One captured robber's girlfriend has banknotes scented with a chemical police use to mark evidence, traced to cash signed out of police storage by the officer who testified against Conners, who is soon found dead with evidence linking him to the heist. Bank footage reveals that the robbery was a cover for a hacker who planted a virus to siphon a billion dollars through thousands of tiny transactions; the hacker is murdered before he can talk. The captured robber identifies Lorenz as Scott Curtis, the dead carjacker's brother. A raid on Scott's house ends in a deadly shootout and a bomb blast with Conners inside.

Dekker learns that the evidence log was forged and that "Scott Curtis" is in fact York. He tracks York to a diner and kills him in self-defence. Paying for his coffee, he notices that a ten-dollar bill he received from Conners carries the evidence scent, and he realises that Conners, who faked his own death in the blast, masterminded the whole scheme. Finding a copy of James Gleick's book Chaos at Conners' home, Dekker races to the airport, but Conners phones him to explain that he only killed those who deserved it, before escaping on a private jet.

Reviews were generally unenthusiastic; critics acknowledged the late twist and some solid car chases but found the plot reliant on implausible coincidences and stock action clichés.

documents.title: Fred Claus
documents.tagline: Everybody has that one relative who can't help but cause problems over the holidays. Even Santa.
documents.overview: Fred Claus and Santa Claus have been estranged brothers for many years. Now Fred must reconcile his differences with his brother whom he believes overshadows him. When an efficiency expert assesses the workings at the North Pole and threatens to shut Santa down, Fred must help his brother to save Christmas.
documents.plot:
Fred Claus is a Christmas comedy film released in 2007 by Warner Bros. Pictures. The movie stars Vince Vaughn as Fred Claus, the brother of Santa Claus (played by Kevin Spacey), and Paul Giamatti as Nick Claus, also known as Santa's half-brother.

The story begins with Fred Claus, a grumpy and irresponsible man who has been living in his own personal hell since being kicked out of his family's home. He is forced to move back into the family's old house after being evicted from his apartment. Unbeknownst to Fred, Santa is struggling to find a suitable replacement for his deceased wife, Mrs. Claus (played by Mary Steenburgen), and has been searching for someone with the right qualities to take over her role.

Upon arrival at the North Pole, Fred discovers that Santa's search for a new Mrs. Claus has led him to Nick Claus, a bitter and resentful man who feels he was unfairly passed over for the role. The two brothers are forced to work together to find a suitable replacement for Mrs. Claus, with hilarious results.

As the story unfolds, Fred and Nick embark on a series of misadventures, including a disastrous Christmas Eve delivery and a chaotic attempt to find a new Mrs. Claus. Along the way, they learn valuable lessons about family, forgiveness, and the true meaning of Christmas.

Throughout the movie, Vince Vaughn shines as the lovable but flawed Fred Claus, bringing his signature wit and charm to the role. Paul Giamatti provides excellent comedic relief as Nick Claus, playing off Vaughn's antics with ease.

The film's climax features a heartwarming moment where Fred and Nick come together to save Christmas, and in doing so, find redemption and forgiveness for past mistakes. The movie ends on a high note, with Fred finding a new sense of purpose and belonging at the North Pole, and Santa finally finding a suitable replacement for Mrs. Claus.

Overall, Fred Claus is a fun and lighthearted holiday film that explores themes of family, forgiveness, and redemption. With its talented cast, witty dialogue, and hilarious antics, it's sure to bring a smile to your face during the holiday season.

documents.title: Happily N'Ever After
documents.tagline: Fairy Tale Endings Aren't What They Used To Be.
documents.overview: An alliance of evil-doers, led by Frieda, looks to take over Fairy Tale Land. But when Ella realizes her stepmother is out to ruin her storybook existence, she takes a dramatic turn and blossoms into the leader of the resistance effort.
documents.plot: An alliance of evil-doers, led by Frieda, looks to take over Fairy Tale Land. But when Ella realizes her stepmother is out to ruin her storybook existence, she takes a dramatic turn and blossoms into the leader of the resistance effort.

documents.title: Cruel Intentions 2
documents.tagline: Seduce and destroy.
documents.overview: After his precocious behavior has gotten him bounced out of one more in a string of exclusive private schools, 16-year old Sebastian Valmont has arrived in New York City to live with his father and stepmother. The cunning and handsome Sebastian may have met his match, however in his equally manipulative and beautiful stepsister Kathryn Merteuil.
documents.plot:
Cruel Intentions 2, also known as Cruel Intentions 2: Manchester Prep, is a 2000 American direct-to-video teen drama film written and directed by Roger Kumble. A prequel to Cruel Intentions (1999) and the second installment in the franchise, it stars Robin Dunne, Sarah Thompson, Keri Lynn Pratt and Amy Adams. The film began life as Manchester Prep, a television series for which Fox ordered 13 episodes for the 1999–2000 season with Kumble writing and executive producing. After conflicts between Columbia TriStar Television and the network, and executives' discomfort with its themes of teen sexuality, the series was canceled with only two episodes filmed. The studio's home video division then edited those episodes into a film, shooting additional scenes to turn the story into a prequel, give it an ending and add sexual content, while cutting some subplots and characters.

Sebastian Valmont, a troublemaking student, moves to New York City after his father marries a wealthy divorcée. Before leaving, he takes revenge on his old principal, who insists on forwarding his permanent record, by publishing a nude photo of the principal's wife in the yearbook, and he secretly swaps the record for a glowing one so that he can start fresh at the exclusive Manchester Prep. In his new home he meets his scheming and ambitious stepsister, Kathryn Merteuil, who quickly warns him not to interfere with her privileged life,, and the two become bickering step-siblings. At school Sebastian meets and falls for Danielle Sherman, the headmaster's daughter. Kathryn presides over a secret society of elite students that judges the newcomers, and she embarks on a vendetta against Cherie, a new girl whose family turns out to be richer than hers and who accidentally humiliated her at an assembly. As Sebastian's romance with Danielle develops, Kathryn tries to lure him away, tempting him with a pair of identical twins who tell him that Danielle is the only virgin at the school. Meanwhile Sebastian discovers his father cheating on Kathryn's mother, and Kathryn's mother orders her to befriend Cherie in the hope of securing a large donation to the school. When Sebastian finally declares his love for Danielle, he learns that the manipulation around him runs deeper than he suspected, and he must decide whether to fight the game or join it.

Released on home video in 2001, Cruel Intentions 2 received generally negative reviews, with an 18% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes based on 11 critics.

documents.title: Battlefield Earth
documents.tagline: Take Back The Planet
documents.overview: In the year 3000, man is no match for the Psychlos, a greedy, manipulative race of aliens on a quest for ultimate profit. Led by the powerful Terl, the Psychlos are stripping Earth clean of its natural resources, using the broken remnants of humanity as slaves. What is left of the human race has descended into a near primitive state. After being captured, it is up to Tyler to save mankind.
documents.plot:
Battlefield Earth, directed by Roger Christian and based on the novel by L. Ron Hubbard, is a science fiction film that explores complex themes that are both thought-provoking and visually stunning.

At its core, Battlefield Earth is a story about the struggle for freedom and the dangers of totalitarianism. The film takes place in a distant future where humans are enslaved by an alien species known as the Psychlos, who have taken over the planet. The main character, Jonnie Goodboy Tyler, played by John Travolta, is a human who is captured by the Psychlos and forced to work on their home planet.

Through Jonnie's journey, the film delves into themes of oppression, rebellion, and the power of individual resistance. The Psychlos' rigid social hierarchy and strict control over every aspect of human life serve as a commentary on the dangers of authoritarian regimes and the importance of individual freedom.

The movie also explores the concept of empathy and understanding between different cultures. As Jonnie navigates his new surroundings and forms relationships with various Psychlo characters, he begins to see the world from their perspective, challenging his own biases and assumptions. This theme is particularly relevant in today's society, where cultural exchange and understanding are more important than ever.

Furthermore, Battlefield Earth touches on the idea of environmentalism and the consequences of exploiting natural resources without regard for the long-term effects. The Psychlos' reckless use of technology and their disregard for the planet's ecosystem serve as a warning about the dangers of unchecked industrialization and the importance of living in harmony with nature.

Overall, Battlefield Earth is a visually stunning film that explores complex themes and ideas through its narrative and characters. While it received mixed reviews from critics at the time of its release, it has since become a cult classic and a staple of science fiction cinema.

documents.title: The Fugitive
documents.tagline: A murdered wife. A one-armed man. An obsessed detective. The chase begins.
documents.overview: Wrongfully convicted of murdering his wife and sentenced to death, Richard Kimble escapes from the law in an attempt to find the real killer and clear his name.
documents.plot:
The Fugitive is a 1993 American thriller film directed by Andrew Davis and starring Harrison Ford as Dr. Richard Kimble, a man wrongly accused of murdering his wife.

The movie begins with Dr. Richard Kimble (Harrison Ford), a successful surgeon who lives in Chicago with his wife, Helen (Kelly McGillis). On the day of their 10-year anniversary, Helen is found dead on a train track, and Richard is arrested and charged with her murder. The police investigation reveals that Richard was at the scene of the crime, but he claims he was framed.

The film's opening scene shows the brutal murder of Helen, followed by Richard's arrest and subsequent escape from custody while being transported to his trial. The U.S. Marshal who is transporting him, Samuel Gerard ( Tommy Lee Jones), is determined to bring Richard back to justice.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Richard was indeed innocent of the crime, but he has been on the run for 15 years, evading capture and trying to clear his name. Along the way, he meets a young woman named Emma (Juliette Lewis), who helps him evade the authorities.

Throughout the film, Richard's determination to prove his innocence drives the plot forward. He uses his medical skills to help those in need, while also staying one step ahead of Gerard and his team. The cat-and-mouse game between Richard and the law is intense, with both sides using clever tactics to outmaneuver each other.

As the story reaches its climax, Richard discovers a crucial piece of evidence that could prove his innocence: a fingerprint on a train car that matches one found at the crime scene. However, Gerard is hot on his heels, and a thrilling chase ensues as they pursue each other across the country.

In the end, Richard finally proves his innocence by revealing the true killer: a former patient who had been seeking revenge against him. The film concludes with Richard's exoneration, and he is reunited with Emma, who has fallen in love with him.

The Fugitive was a critical and commercial success, earning several Academy Award nominations, including Best Actor for Harrison Ford. The film's tense plot and memorable performances made it a classic thriller of the 1990s.

documents.title: The Ladykillers
documents.tagline: The greatest criminal minds of all time have finally met their match.
documents.overview: An eccentric, if not charming Southern professor and his crew pose as a band in order to rob a casino, all under the nose of his unsuspecting landlord – a sharp old woman.
documents.plot:
The Ladykillers is a 2004 American black comedy crime film written, directed, produced and edited by Joel and Ethan Coen, a remake of the 1955 Ealing comedy written by William Rose. It is the Coens' first remake and their only film with Tom Hanks. Hanks stars as Professor G. H. Dorr, with Irma P. Hall as Marva Munson, Marlon Wayans as Gawain MacSam, J. K. Simmons as Garth Pancake, Tzi Ma as the General and Ryan Hurst as Lump.

Mrs. Munson, a devout, strict elderly widow, rents a room to Dorr, a self-styled classics professor who asks to use her root cellar for rehearsals of his early music ensemble. The musicians are actually criminals. Lump is a dim former football player, Pancake is a demolitions expert with irritable bowel syndrome, MacSam is a foul-mouthed janitor and the gang's inside man at a riverboat casino, and the General is a silent, chain-smoking tunneling expert. They plan to dig from the cellar into the casino's underground vault, dumping the dirt each night onto a garbage barge passing under a nearby bridge. Despite mishaps, including Pancake blowing off a finger that Mrs. Munson's cat carries away, they reach the vault and take the money.

Mrs. Munson discovers the plot and demands that Dorr return the money and come to church, or she will call the police. Dorr's arguments fail. The gang decides she must die and draws straws. MacSam cannot go through with it because she reminds him of his mother, and in the ensuing fight with Pancake he is shot dead. Pancake then tries to escape with the loot and his girlfriend, Mountain Girl, but the General strangles them both. Preparing to kill Mrs. Munson in her sleep, the General is startled by a cuckoo clock, swallows his cigarette, trips over the cat and falls to his death. Lump decides to do as Mrs. Munson says, but he accidentally shoots himself while trying to shoot Dorr. Dorr is knocked off the bridge by a falling piece of gargoyle and dies when his cloak catches on the railing. All of their bodies land on the barge. Mrs. Munson finds the money, and when the police laugh off her story, she gives it to Bob Jones University.

The barge replaces the original's freight train. Buena Vista released it on March 26, 2004, and it grossed $76 million worldwide. Many critics considered it a lesser Coen film. Rotten Tomatoes reported 54% approval, calling Hanks's performance inspired but the film minor. Roger Ebert gave it two and a half stars, singling out Hall as its most successful performer.

documents.title: The Chorus
documents.overview: Set in 1940s France, a new teacher at a school for disruptive boys gives hope and inspiration.
documents.plot: In 1940s France, a new teacher at a school for disruptive boys gives hope and inspiration.

documents.title: Space Cowboys
documents.tagline: Space will never be the same.
documents.overview: Frank Corvin, ‘Hawk’ Hawkins, Jerry O'Neill and ‘Tank’ Sullivan were hotdog members of Project Daedalus, the Air Force's test program for space travel, but their hopes were dashed in 1958 with the formation of NASA and the use of trained chimps. They blackmail their way into orbit when Russia's mysterious ‘Ikon’ communications satellite's orbit begins to degrade and threatens to crash to Earth.

They blackmail their way into orbit when Russia's mysterious ‘Ikon’ communications satellite's orbit begins to degrade and threatens to crash to Earth.

documents.title: Bee Movie
documents.tagline: Born to bee wild.
documents.overview: Barry B. Benson, a bee who has just graduated from college, is disillusioned at his lone career choice: making honey. On a special trip outside the hive, Barry's life is saved by Vanessa, a florist in New York City. As their relationship blossoms, he discovers humans actually eat honey, and subsequently decides to sue us.
documents.plot:
Bee Movie is a computer-animated comedy film released in 2007 by DreamWorks Animation. The movie follows the story of Barry B. Benson, a young and ambitious bee who lives in New York City.

The film begins with Barry (voiced by Jerry Seinfeld) graduating from Bee College, where he learns about the importance of bees in pollination and honey production. However, Barry's fascination with human culture and his desire to explore beyond the hive lead him to question the traditional roles of bees.

One day, while out on a flight, Barry meets Vanessa Bloome (voiced by Renée Zellweger), a florist who is unaware that she is responsible for the decline of bee populations due to her role in promoting non-organic flowers. Intrigued by this discovery, Barry decides to take matters into his own hands and sue the human population for stealing honey.

As Barry delves deeper into the world of humans, he discovers a complex web of deceit and corruption that has led to the decline of bee populations. He also meets Adam Flayman (voiced by Matthew Broderick), a lawyer who agrees to help Barry with his lawsuit.

The plot thickens as Barry and Vanessa grow closer, but their relationship is put to the test when they must navigate the challenges of their respective worlds. Meanwhile, Layton T. Montgomery (voiced by Patrick Warburton), a ruthless bee executive, will stop at nothing to silence Barry and maintain the status quo.

As the story unfolds, Barry's lawsuit gains momentum, and he becomes an unlikely hero for bees everywhere. However, his actions also put him at odds with the human population, who are forced to confront their role in the decline of bee populations.

In the end, Barry and Vanessa succeed in changing the way humans interact with bees, and a new era of cooperation and understanding begins. The movie ends on a hopeful note, with Barry returning to his hive as a hero, but also with a newfound appreciation for the complexities of human culture.

Throughout the film, Jerry Seinfeld's signature wit and humor shine through, making Bee Movie a delightful and entertaining ride. The animation is vibrant and colorful, bringing the world of bees and humans to life in a way that is both whimsical and engaging.

documents.title: Luther
documents.tagline: Rebel. Genius. Liberator.
documents.overview: During the early 16th Century idealistic German monk Martin Luther, disgusted by the materialism in the church, begins the dialogue that will lead to the Protestant Reformation.
documents.plot: During the early 16th century, idealistic German monk Martin Luther, disgusted by the materialism in the church, begins the dialogue that will lead to the Protestant Reformation.

documents.title: Control
documents.tagline: He had the spirit, but lost the feeling.
documents.overview: The story of Joy Division’s lead singer Ian Curtis, from his schoolboy days in 1973 to his suicide on the eve of the band's first American tour in 1980.
documents.plot:
Control is a 2007 British biographical film about Ian Curtis, the singer of the late-1970s rock band Joy Division. It was the first feature directed by Anton Corbijn, who had photographed the band during their career, and it was shot in black and white. Matt Greenhalgh wrote the screenplay based on Touching from a Distance, the biography written by Curtis's widow Deborah, who co-produced the film. Sam Riley stars as Ian Curtis, with Samantha Morton as Deborah, Alexandra Maria Lara as Annik Honoré, and Joe Anderson and James Anthony Pearson as bandmates.

The film opens in 1975 in Macclesfield, south of Manchester, where the teenage Ian marries his girlfriend Debbie Woodruff. Introverted and drawn to poetry, he finds an outlet when he attends a Sex Pistols concert in 1976 with a group of young men who are forming a band, and he offers to become their singer. The group, first named Warsaw and later Joy Division, slowly gains a following, financing its first EP and catching the attention of television presenter Tony Wilson and manager Rob Gretton. Signed to Wilson's Factory Records, the band records Unknown Pleasures and begins to tour.

While working at an employment office, Ian witnesses a client suffering an epileptic seizure, and soon he is diagnosed with epilepsy himself. The medication he takes affects his moods, and the seizures become increasingly frequent, sometimes striking on stage. At the same time, he becomes a father and begins an affair with Annik Honoré, a Belgian journalist, which leaves him torn between her and Debbie. Exhausted by touring, guilt and illness, and on the eve of the band's first American tour, Curtis takes his own life in May 1980 at the age of 23.

Corbijn's restrained direction and the actors' performances, including the cast playing Joy Division's songs themselves, presented Curtis as a fragile young man rather than a rock icon, while focusing heavily on his marriage.

Control premiered at the 2007 Cannes Film Festival in the Directors' Fortnight, where it won several prizes. Critics were enthusiastic: Peter Bradshaw of The Guardian named it the best film of the year, and Roger Ebert gave it three and a half stars out of four. The film also won multiple British Independent Film Awards, including Best Film.

documents.title: Once
documents.tagline: How often do you find the right person?
documents.overview: A vacuum repairman moonlights as a street musician and hopes for his big break. One day a Czech immigrant, who earns a living selling flowers, approaches him with the news that she is also an aspiring singer-songwriter. The pair decide to collaborate, and the songs that they compose reflect the story of their blossoming love.
documents.plot:
Once is a poignant and charming film that explores the complexities of love, loss, and the human connection. The movie delves into the idea of finding meaning in life's fleeting moments and the power of music to transcend time and circumstance.

At its core, Once is a story about two souls who find each other in the unlikeliest of places – a Dublin street corner. The film masterfully captures the essence of their relationship, which blossoms into something beautiful despite the odds against them. As they navigate their feelings for each other, the movie also delves into the pain and longing that can accompany love.

One of the primary themes of Once is the idea of finding one's true voice and purpose in life. The protagonist, a struggling musician, finds solace in his music, which becomes an integral part of his connection with the female lead. Through their shared passion for music, they form a deep bond that allows them to express themselves authentically.

The film also explores the theme of impermanence and the fragility of life. The characters' experiences are marked by loss and heartache, yet it is in these moments of vulnerability that they find each other and discover the beauty of human connection.

Ultimately, Once is a movie about the transformative power of love and music to bring people together and transcend time. It's a film that will leave you humming the tunes, feeling the emotions, and perhaps even reevaluating your own priorities in life.

documents.title: Princess of Thieves
documents.tagline: If you thought Robin Hood broke all the rules, wait until you meet his daughter!
documents.overview: Sherwood forest has a courageous new hero - Gwyn, the daughter of Robin Hood. Possessing the cunning skills of her legendary father and the beauty and intelligence of her mother Maid Marian, Gwyn is anxious to follow in her father's footsteps. King Richard nears death and Robin Hood and his Merry Men are summoned to help bring Richard's son Philip to his rightful place on the throne before the evil Prince John can assume power. Robin Hood's life and that of the future King of England soon lies in Gwyn's hands when Robin is captured and sentenced to death.
documents.plot:
Princess of Thieves is a 2001 romantic adventure television film directed by Peter Hewitt and starring Keira Knightley as Gwyn, the daughter of Robin Hood and Maid Marian. Produced by Granada Entertainment USA and filmed in Romania, it co-stars Stuart Wilson as Robin Hood, Stephen Moyer as Prince Philip, Jonathan Hyde as Prince John, Malcolm McDowell as the Sheriff of Nottingham and Del Synnott as Froderick. The story imagines a new chapter in the Robin Hood legend, centered on the outlaw's spirited daughter.

Years after the famous adventures of Robin Hood, Maid Marian has died and Robin spends most of his time away fighting in the Crusades alongside King Richard the Lionheart. His daughter Gwyn has grown up largely without him, becoming an independent and strong-willed young woman with a remarkable talent for archery. Her only close companion is Froderick, a gentle young man studying for the church, who is quietly in love with her. When King Richard dies, Robin returns to England to ensure that the rightful heir takes the throne, but he is captured by his old enemies, the Sheriff of Nottingham and the scheming Prince John, who intends to seize the crown for himself.

Gwyn takes up her father's mission. She must find and protect Prince Philip, King Richard's illegitimate son, who has returned from exile in France to claim the throne but is traveling incognito under the name of his servant, who died protecting him. Gwyn crosses paths with the young man without knowing his true identity, and a romance begins to grow between them. Together they seek out the Merry Men and lead a daring attempt to rescue Robin from imprisonment in the Tower of London and stop Prince John's coronation before England falls into tyranny.

The film presents a family-friendly adventure with a heroine who proves herself the equal of her legendary father, and it was one of Knightley's first leading roles, made shortly before her international breakthrough.

Princess of Thieves premiered on ABC's The Wonderful World of Disney in 2001. Reviews were mixed: Scott Weinberg of eFilmCritic called it an entertaining little movie that bucks the odds, while BeyondHollywood found it aimed squarely at young girls and likely to bore other viewers.

documents.title: Casper's Haunted Christmas
documents.overview: Kibosh, supreme ruler of all ghosts, decrees that casper must scare at least one person before Christmas Day so Casper visits Kriss, Massachusetts where he meets the Jollimore family and sets out to complete his mission. As usual, kindhearted Casper has a ghastky time trying to scare anyone; so The Ghostly Trio, fed up with his goody-boo-shoes behavior, secretly hires Casper's look-alike cousin Spooky to do the job-with hilarious results.
documents.plot: Kibosh, supreme ruler of all ghosts, decrees that casper must scare at least one person before Christmas Day so Casper visits Kriss, Massachusetts where he meets the Jollimore family and sets out to complete his mission. As usual, kindhearted Casper has a ghastky time trying to scare anyone; so The Ghostly Trio, fed up with his goody-boo-shoes behavior, secretly hires Casper's look-alike cousin Spooky to do the job-with hilarious results.

documents.title: Showtime
documents.tagline: Lights. Camera. Aggravation.
documents.overview: A spoof of buddy cop movies where two very different cops are forced to team up on a new reality based T.V. cop show.
documents.plot:
Showtime is a 2002 American buddy cop action comedy film directed by Tom Dey and released by Warner Bros. Pictures. It stars Robert De Niro as a gruff detective and Eddie Murphy as an aspiring actor in uniform, alongside Rene Russo, William Shatner, Pedro Damián and De Niro's daughter Drena De Niro.

Detective Mitch Preston of the Los Angeles Police Department's Central Division shoots a news camera after a botched confrontation with drug dealer Lazy Boy, who escapes using a custom-built armor-piercing gun. The cameraman's network, Maxxis Television, sues the department for $10 million but offers to drop the suit if Mitch stars in its new police reality show, and the captain, eager for good publicity, agrees. His partner on the show is Officer Trey Sellars, a patrolman who keeps failing the detective exam and dreams of acting; Trey even stages a purse snatching to impress producer Chase Renzi, who signs him despite the embarrassing ruse. The producers care little for real police work: they build a set inside the station, give Mitch a Humvee and Trey a Corvette, and hire William Shatner, the former star of T. J. Hooker, to coach them. Trey loves it; Mitch is merely irritated, especially after the show redecorates his home and gives him a retired police dog named Powder.

Mitch keeps investigating the supergun, which arms dealer Caesar Vargas uses to kill Lazy Boy. A ruse by Trey yields Vargas's name, leading to a brawl at his nightclub. Vargas's crew then attacks an armored car, and the ensuing chase ends in a destructive crash, after which the chief cancels the show, suspends Mitch and demotes Trey. Reconciling, the two learn that Vargas plans to sell the weapons at a gun show at the Bonaventure Hotel. Vargas takes Chase hostage, but the partners rescue her; a shot ceiling floods the room from the pool above, washing Vargas out of a window to his death, while Mitch and Trey survive handcuffed together. Trey passes his exam and becomes Mitch's partner as a detective, and the show is revived with two new officers.

Released on March 15, 2002, Showtime received generally negative reviews for its flat humor and failed satire of the buddy cop genre; Rotten Tomatoes reported 25% approval. It grossed about $77.7 million against an $85 million budget, and earned Golden Raspberry nominations for Murphy and for the Murphy-De Niro pairing.

documents.title: Angel Eyes
documents.tagline: The deeper you look, the more you will find.
documents.overview: A story about a seemingly unlikely couple who cross paths under life-threatening circumstances as though they are destined not only to meet but to save each other's lives. Not once, but twice.
documents.plot:
Angel Eyes is a 2001 American romantic drama directed by Luis Mandoki and written by Gerald Di Pego. It stars Jennifer Lopez as Chicago police officer Sharon Pogue and Jim Caviezel as Catch, a mysterious, withdrawn stranger, with Sônia Braga, Terrence Howard and Jeremy Sisto in supporting roles. Marco Beltrami composed the score. The story follows two wounded people whose relationship forces each of them to confront the trauma of the past.

One night, Sharon arrives at the scene of a violent traffic accident and holds the hand of a badly injured man, pleading with him not to give up. A year later, she is estranged from her family because she had her father arrested for beating her mother, something neither he nor her brother has forgiven. Meanwhile, a quiet man known only as Catch wanders the city in a trance-like state, performing small acts of kindness for strangers and neighbors, and seems to be watching Sharon from a distance.

When gunmen open fire on a diner and Sharon gives chase, one of the suspects grabs her gun and is about to shoot her when Catch tackles him and saves her life. The two begin a cautious, intense relationship, but Catch refuses to talk about himself, saying only that he is starting from scratch, and he lives in a nearly empty apartment. One night at a blues club he picks up a trumpet and plays a soulful version of "Nature Boy", and the owner recognizes him as Steve Lambert. Investigating, Sharon discovers that Catch is the man whose hand she held at the accident, a jazz musician whose wife and son were killed in the crash. As she tries to help him face the loss he has blocked from his memory, she must also confront her own painful family history.

The film blends romance with a psychological drama about grief, denial and domestic violence, and about the healing that comes from finally facing pain.

Angel Eyes opened at number four in North America but was a box office bomb, grossing about 29.7 million dollars worldwide against a 38 million dollar budget. Critics were largely unimpressed, giving it 32 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus called it ultimately a schmaltzy romance, and a Metacritic score of 39, though it earned ALMA Award nominations for Lopez and Mandoki.

documents.title: The Mist
documents.tagline: Belief divides them, mystery surrounds them, but fear changes everything.
documents.overview: After a violent storm, a dense cloud of mist envelops a small Maine town, trapping artist David Drayton and his five-year-old son in a local grocery store with other people. They soon discover that the mist conceals deadly horrors that threaten their lives, and worse, their sanity.
documents.plot:
The Mist is a 2007 American horror film directed by Frank Darabont, based on the novella of the same name by Stephen King. The movie takes place in 1994 and follows a group of people who take refuge in a grocery store after a mysterious mist filled with monstrous creatures envelops their small town.

The story begins with David Drayton (played by Thomas Jane), a divorced father, who is struggling to connect with his son, Billy (played by Nathalie Kelley). As the day progresses, strange occurrences start happening outside, and people begin to disappear. The townspeople soon realize that the mist is filled with monstrous creatures, including giant spiders, snakes, and other terrifying beasts.

As the situation spirals out of control, David finds himself trapped in a grocery store with a small group of survivors, including his son Billy, who has been hiding in the store's basement. The group consists of Kevin (played by Marc Menchaca), a young boy who is initially hesitant to trust anyone; Mrs. Carmody (played by Laurie Holden), a devout Christian woman who believes that God is punishing them for their sins; and Brent Norton (played by Toby Jones), a cynical and world-weary man.

As the group tries to survive, tensions rise as they disagree on how to handle the situation. Mrs. Carmody becomes increasingly fanatical, believing that they must sacrifice some of the survivors in order to appease God. David and Kevin try to reason with her, but she refuses to listen.

Meanwhile, strange events begin to occur within the store itself. The group discovers that the creatures are not just outside, but also inside the store, and that they seem to be attracted to certain individuals. As the days pass, the group's dynamics become increasingly strained, and it becomes clear that some of them may not survive.

As the story unfolds, David and Kevin form a bond as they try to protect each other from the monsters and Mrs. Carmody's fanatical behavior. However, when Brent is killed by one of the creatures, the group's unity begins to break down.

In the end, David makes a desperate decision to escape the store with Billy, but not before realizing that he has lost his son in the chaos. The movie ends with David and Billy walking out into the mist, unsure if they will survive or be consumed by the monsters.

The Mist is a tense and suspenseful horror film that explores themes of survival, sacrifice, and the breakdown of human relationships under extreme circumstances. While it received mixed reviews from critics at the time of its release, it has since become a cult classic among Stephen King fans and horror enthusiasts.

documents.title: Azumi
documents.tagline: From The Ravages of War Raises An Assassin.
documents.overview: In war-torn Japan, the Tokugawa Shogun, desperate to restore peace to his people, orders the assassination of the hostile warlords. A beautiful young woman is raised from birth with nine other orphans, to become an assassin. Her name is Azumi, the ultimate assassin.
documents.plot: In war-torn Japan, the Tokugawa Shogun, desperate to restore peace to his people, orders the assassination of the hostile warlords. A beautiful young woman is raised from birth with nine other orphans, to become an assassin. Her name is Azumi, the ultimate assassin.

documents.title: Azumi 2: Death or Love
documents.tagline: Love Or Duty... An Assassin Must Choose
documents.overview: Young assassins Azumi and Nagara continue their mission to prevent a civil war. In their hunt for Masayuki Sanada, who is protected by both an army and a dangerous clan, they meet Ginkaku, a person who shows a remarking resemblance with former friend Nachi.
documents.plot:
Azumi 2: Death or Love is a 2005 Japanese jidaigeki action film directed by Shusuke Kaneko and the only sequel to the film Azumi, which was based on the manga series by Yū Koyama. Aya Ueto stars as the young assassin Azumi, with Yuma Ishigaki as her comrade Nagara, Chiaki Kuriyama as the government ninja Kozue, Shun Oguri as the bandit Ginkaku, Kenichi Endō as his brother Kinkaku, Reiko Takashima as Kunio, Kazuki Kitamura as Kanbei Inoue, Tak Sakaguchi as Tsuchigumo and Mikijirō Hira as Sanada Masayuki.

Having carried out a string of assassinations, including the killing of Kiyomasa Kato, Azumi and Nagara are the last survivors of their group and are hunted by ninjas hired by Kanbei Inoue, who seeks to avenge his dead master. While Nagara recovers from his wounds in a temple, Azumi encounters a band of outlaws led by Ginkaku, a young man who strikingly resembles Nachi, the friend she loved and lost. Allied ninjas serving the priest Tenkai, who first ordered the assassins' mission, find the pair, and Azumi and Nagara set out to kill their final target, the warlord Sanada Masayuki, accompanied by a young ninja woman named Kozue. Meanwhile Kanbei raises a large force of mercenaries, ninjas and bandits, among them Ginkaku and Kinkaku. Torn by her feelings for Ginkaku, Azumi parts ways with him, and soon afterwards Nagara announces that he wants to leave the mission and start a new life with Kozue. Continuing alone, Azumi learns that Masayuki's army has left to kill Gessai and races to intervene, facing the giant Roppa of the deadly Uenokagashu ninja clan in a battle that costs the lives of many of Ginkaku's men. Kozue is revealed to be a spy for the Uenokagashu and murders Nagara before turning on Azumi, who kills her. Azumi then defeats Tsuchigumo, whose weapons are poisoned razor wires, but is left paralyzed by his poison and at the mercy of Kunio, Sanada's concubine and the clan's true leader, until Ginkaku sacrifices himself to save her. Weakened but determined, Azumi fights her way through Sanada's troops for a final duel with the warlord.

The film was distributed in Japan by Toho and released on March 12, 2005. In the United Kingdom it was released directly to home video later that year.

documents.title: A Bridge Too Far
documents.tagline: Out of the sky comes the screen's most incredible spectacle of men and war!
documents.overview: Operation Market Garden, September 1944. The Allies attempt to capture several strategically important bridges in the Netherlands in the hope of breaking the German lines.
documents.plot:
A Bridge Too Far is a 1977 war film directed by Richard Attenborough, and it explores several complex themes that were relevant to the time period in which it was made. 

One of the primary themes of the movie is the futility of war and the devastating consequences it has on individuals and society as a whole. The film depicts the Allied invasion of Arnhem during World War II, where a large-scale airborne operation went horribly wrong, resulting in heavy casualties and a crushing defeat for the Allies.

The movie also delves into the theme of hubris and overconfidence, as embodied by the character of Lieutenant Colonel John Hackett, who is determined to succeed despite being vastly outnumbered. This theme serves as a cautionary tale about the dangers of underestimating one's opponents and the importance of humility in the face of overwhelming odds.

Furthermore, A Bridge Too Far explores the theme of sacrifice and the moral complexities of war. The film highlights the personal costs of war on individuals, including the loss of innocence, the breakdown of relationships, and the struggle to maintain one's humanity in the face of unimaginable violence.

The movie also touches on the theme of leadership and the challenges faced by military commanders in making difficult decisions under pressure. The character of Lieutenant Colonel Hackett serves as a foil to the more measured approach of his superior officer, Major General Brian Horrocks, who is forced to confront the consequences of Hackett's actions.

Overall, A Bridge Too Far is a powerful and thought-provoking film that explores the complexities and nuances of war, highlighting the human cost of conflict and the importance of humility, sacrifice, and leadership in the face of overwhelming adversity.

documents.title: Into the Wild
documents.tagline: Into the heart. Into the soul.
documents.overview: After graduating from Emory University in 1992, top student and athlete Christopher McCandless abandons his possessions, gives his entire $24,000 savings account to charity, and hitchhikes to Alaska to live in the wilderness.
documents.plot:
Into the Wild is a biographical drama film directed by Sean Penn, released in 2007. The movie is based on the life of Christopher McCandless, an American young man who abandoned his material possessions and hitchhiked to Alaska with the intention of living off the land.

The film begins with Chris McCandless (played by Emile Hirsch), a recent college graduate from a wealthy family in Carthage, Missouri. Chris's parents, Walt (Vince Vaughn) and Billie (Catherine Keener), are portrayed as loving but also somewhat neglectful, having given their son the freedom to explore his own path in life.

Chris becomes increasingly disillusioned with the materialism and superficiality of modern society, feeling suffocated by the expectations placed upon him. He decides to leave behind his comfortable life and embark on a journey of self-discovery, inspired by the writings of Henry David Thoreau's Walden.

The film follows Chris as he travels across the country, hitchhiking and working odd jobs to save money for his trip to Alaska. Along the way, he meets various characters who influence his worldview, including Wayne Westerberg (Hal Holbrook), a grizzled old truck driver who teaches him about the importance of living in the moment.

In 1992, Chris arrives in Anchorage, Alaska, and begins his journey into the wilderness. He adopts the alias "Alexander Supertramp" and sets out to live off the land, foraging for food and building a shelter. The film depicts Chris's struggles with the harsh environment, including encounters with bears, mosquitoes, and extreme weather conditions.

As the seasons change, Chris becomes increasingly isolated and withdrawn, struggling to adapt to the unforgiving wilderness. He begins to question his decision to leave behind civilization, feeling overwhelmed by the vastness of nature.

The film takes a tragic turn when Chris's bus breaks down on the side of the road, and he is forced to abandon his vehicle. In an attempt to survive, Chris sets fire to his bus, but the flames spread out of control, consuming everything in their path.

In the end, Chris's body is discovered by two hunters, who report him missing to the authorities. The film ends with a sense of melancholy and regret, as Chris's parents receive news of his death, realizing too late that they had failed to connect with their son on a deeper level.

Throughout the film, Sean Penn's direction weaves together themes of identity, community, and the human relationship with nature. Emile Hirsch delivers a powerful performance as Chris McCandless, capturing the complexity and vulnerability of this enigmatic young man. The cinematography is breathtaking, capturing the stunning beauty of Alaska's wilderness.

Overall, Into the Wild is a thought-provoking film that raises questions about the human condition and our place in the world. It is a poignant reminder of the importance of connection, community, and living life on one's own terms.

documents.title: The Jane Austen Book Club
documents.tagline: You don't have to know the books to be in the club
documents.overview: Six Californians start a club to discuss the works of Jane Austen. As they delve into Austen's literature, the club members find themselves dealing with life experiences that parallel the themes of the books they are reading.
documents.plot:
The Jane Austen Book Club is a 2007 romantic comedy-drama film that explores the lives of four women who form a book club based on the works of Jane Austen. At its core, the movie delves into themes of female empowerment, friendship, and personal growth.

As the story unfolds, we see how these women, each with their own unique struggles and insecurities, find solace and support in their shared love of literature. Through their discussions and debates about Austen's novels, they begin to confront their own lives, relationships, and societal expectations. The film masterfully captures the complexities of female relationships, highlighting both the bonds of sisterhood and the challenges of navigating personal identity.

The movie also explores the theme of escapism, as the women use literature as a means of temporarily escaping the mundanity and difficulties of their daily lives. However, as they delve deeper into Austen's world, they begin to realize that the lines between reality and fiction are blurred, and that the lessons they learn from her novels can be applied to their own lives.

Furthermore, The Jane Austen Book Club touches on the theme of social class and status, as the women navigate their relationships with men and confront the societal expectations placed upon them. Through their interactions with the male characters in their lives, they are forced to reevaluate their own values and priorities.

Ultimately, the film is a heartwarming exploration of the transformative power of literature, friendship, and self-discovery. As the women find themselves and grow as individuals, they come to realize that true happiness and fulfillment can be found in the most unexpected places – within themselves, with each other, and through the timeless wisdom of Jane Austen's works.

documents.title: The Pledge
documents.tagline: Detective Jerry Black has made a promise he can't break, to catch a killer he can't find.
documents.overview: A police chief about to retire pledges to help a woman find her daughter's killer.
documents.plot:
The Pledge is a 2001 American neo-noir psychological thriller film directed and co-produced by Sean Penn, based on the 1958 novella by the Swiss writer Friedrich Dürrenmatt. Jack Nicholson stars as a newly retired detective, supported by an ensemble cast including Aaron Eckhart, Helen Mirren, Robin Wright Penn, Vanessa Redgrave and Benicio del Toro. Released on January 19, 2001, it competed for the Palme d'Or at that year's Cannes Film Festival.

On the night of his retirement party, Reno, Nevada, police detective Jerry Black learns that a young girl, Ginny Larsen, has been found murdered. He breaks the news to the girl's parents, and her grief-stricken mother makes him swear on a cross her daughter made that he will find the killer. A suspect, Toby Jay Wadenah, a Native American man with an intellectual disability, is quickly arrested, and under pressure from Jerry's colleague Stan he confesses, then kills himself with a deputy's gun. The case is closed, but Jerry remains unconvinced.

Abandoning his retirement fishing trip, Jerry continues to investigate on his own. A friend of Ginny's reveals that Ginny had befriended a man she called "the Giant," who gave her small porcupine-shaped treats. A drawing by Ginny shows the man with a black station wagon, not Toby's red pickup, and Jerry uncovers similar unsolved killings of young girls in the region that Toby could not have committed.

Determined to keep his promise, Jerry buys a gas station at the center of the area where the murders took place and settles there. He befriends Lori, a waitress fleeing an abusive former partner, and her young daughter, Chrissy. They move in with him,, and Jerry becomes Chrissy's father figure and Lori's lover. When Chrissy tells him that a man she calls "the wizard" has given her porcupine candies and arranged to meet her again, Jerry persuades the police to set a trap, using Chrissy as bait. But the man never arrives: unknown to anyone, he has been killed in a car crash on his way to the meeting. The police leave, Lori furiously rejects Jerry for endangering her daughter, and in the final scene Jerry, drunk and broken, sits alone outside his abandoned gas station, muttering that the killer is still out there.

The Pledge received mainly positive reviews, with praise for Nicholson's subtle performance; Rotten Tomatoes reported 78% approval and Metacritic a score of 71. It was a commercial disappointment, grossing $29.4 million against a budget of over $35 million.

documents.title: Along Came Polly
documents.tagline: For the most cautious man on Earth, life is about to get interesting.
documents.overview: Reuben Feffer is a guy who's spent his entire life playing it safe. Polly Prince is irresistible as a free-spirit who lives for the thrill of the moment. When these two comically mismatched souls collide, Reuben's world is turned upside down, as he makes an uproarious attempt to change his life from middle-of-the-road to totally-out-there.
documents.plot:
Along Came Polly is a 2004 American romantic comedy film directed by John Hamburg and written by Hamburg and Larry Levin. The movie stars Ben Stiller, Jennifer Aniston, Philip Baker Hall, and Debra Messing.

The story begins with Reuben Feffer (Ben Stiller), a risk-averse and uptight insurance salesman who has been in a long-term relationship with his girlfriend, Polly Prince (Jennifer Aniston). However, their relationship is stagnant, and Reuben feels suffocated by the predictability of it all. He meets a free-spirited woman named Sandy (Debra Messing) at a singles bar, but she's not interested in him.

Reuben's life takes an unexpected turn when he meets Polly's cousin, Polly Prince (Jennifer Aniston), who is also his coworker and friend. Reuben has had feelings for Polly since high school, but she never reciprocated them. When Polly gets engaged to a man named Ray (Philip Baker Hall), Reuben sees this as an opportunity to finally be with her.

However, things take a turn when Reuben's life insurance policy is canceled due to his lack of risk-taking behavior. He then decides to go skydiving for the first time, which becomes a pivotal moment in his life. This experience makes him realize that he needs to take more risks and live life on his own terms.

As Reuben navigates his newfound sense of freedom, he starts to reevaluate his relationship with Polly. He realizes that he's been playing it safe all these years, and it's time for him to be more spontaneous and open-minded. Meanwhile, Polly is struggling with her engagement and feeling suffocated by the idea of settling down.

The plot thickens when Reuben and Polly start to reconnect, but their relationship is put to the test as they face various challenges together. Along the way, Reuben learns valuable lessons about love, risk-taking, and being true to oneself.

In the end, Reuben must decide whether he's willing to take a chance on Polly and their relationship. The movie culminates in a heartwarming and humorous climax that showcases the growth and development of both characters.

Throughout the film, Ben Stiller delivers a standout performance as the lovable but awkward Reuben Feffer. Jennifer Aniston shines as the charming and free-spirited Polly Prince, bringing depth and nuance to her character. The supporting cast adds to the humor and charm of the movie, making Along Came Polly a delightful and entertaining romantic comedy that explores themes of love, risk-taking, and self-discovery.

documents.title: The Family Man
documents.tagline: What if you made different choices? What if you said yes, instead of no? What if you got a second chance?
documents.overview: Jack's lavish, fast-paced lifestyle changes one Christmas night when he stumbles into a grocery store holdup and disarms the gunman. The next morning he wakes up in bed lying next to Kate, his college sweetheart he left in order to pursue his career, and to the horrifying discovery that his former life no longer exists. As he stumbles through this alternate suburban universe, Jack finds himself at a crossroad where he must choose between his high-power career and the woman he loves.
