documents.title: Evening
documents.tagline: Her greatest secret was her greatest gift.
documents.overview: As Constance (Natasha Richardson) and Nina (Toni Collette) gather at the deathbed of their mother, Ann (Vanessa Redgrave), they learn for the first time that their mother lived an entire other lifetime during one evening 50 years ago. In vivid flashbacks, the young Ann (Claire Daines) spends one night with a man named Harris (Patrick Wilson), who was the love of her life.
documents.plot:
Evening is a 2007 American drama film directed by Lajos Koltai, with a screenplay by Susan Minot and Michael Cunningham based on Minot's 1998 novel of the same name. The ensemble cast includes Claire Danes as the young Ann, Toni Collette, Vanessa Redgrave, Patrick Wilson, Hugh Dancy and Mamie Gummer. The novel and original screenplay were set in Maine, but Koltai was so taken with a Newport house found by his location scouts that he moved the story to Rhode Island; filming began in September 2006, with locations in Tiverton, Bristol, Providence and Manhattan.

The film moves between the 1950s and the present, as Ann Grant Lord lies dying and reflects on her past, mentioning people her daughters Constance and Nina have never heard of and leaving them wondering whether she is delusional. In the 1950s, Ann, a young cabaret singer, arrives at the grand Newport home of her best friend Lila Wittenborn for Lila's wedding to Karl Ross. Lila's brother Buddy, Ann's college friend and a heavy drinker, introduces her to Harris Arden, a young doctor and the son of a former family servant, and confides that Lila has always adored Harris and may be marrying out of duty rather than love. Ann and Harris feel an instant connection. On the wedding day Lila admits that Harris rebuffed her, and she goes through with the marriage. At the reception Ann sings, joined by Harris, while the drunken Buddy confronts them and then unexpectedly kisses Harris. Later Buddy confesses that he has loved Ann for years. When he plays a frightening prank after diving from a clifftop into the sea, Ann angrily rejects him and slips away with Harris to his hideaway, where they make love. That night, searching for Ann, Buddy is struck by a car and killed, a tragedy that Ann and Harris learn of only the next morning. In the present, Lila visits Ann's bedside to reminisce, and the memories of that weekend help Ann offer her daughters, especially the uncertain Nina, guidance about love and the choices they face.

Evening grossed about $20 million worldwide. It received largely negative reviews, holding a 28% rating on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus calls it beautifully filmed but dull and a waste of a talented cast, though some critics praised the performances, particularly those of Danes and Gummer.

documents.title: P.S. I Love You
documents.tagline: His life ended. Now, a new one will begin.
documents.overview: A young widow discovers that her late husband has left her 10 messages intended to help ease her pain and start a new life.
documents.plot: A young widow discovers that her late husband has left her 10 messages intended to help ease her pain and start a new life.

documents.title: The Mexican
documents.tagline: Love with the safety off.
documents.overview: Jerry Welbach, a reluctant bagman, has been given two ultimatums: The first is from his mob boss to travel to Mexico and retrieve a priceless antique pistol, known as "the Mexican"... or suffer the consequences. The second is from his girlfriend Samantha to end his association with the mob. Jerry figures alive and in trouble with Samantha is better than the more permanent alternative, so he heads south of the border.
documents.plot:
The Mexican is a 2001 American romantic comedy film directed by Gore Verbinski. The story revolves around Carlos O'Connell (played by Antonio Banderas), an American lawyer who travels to Mexico to retrieve his friend's body, only to find himself caught up in a complicated web of love and loyalty.

At its core, the movie explores themes of identity, cultural heritage, and the complexities of human relationships. Carlos, as an outsider navigating Mexican culture, must confront his own sense of belonging and purpose. His journey is marked by humorous misunderstandings and poignant moments of self-discovery.

The film also delves into the tension between tradition and modernity, as embodied by the contrasting worlds of Carlos's American upbringing and the vibrant, traditional Mexican culture he encounters. This clash sparks a romantic connection with Frida Berdansky (played by Salma Hayek), a beautiful and strong-willed woman who challenges Carlos to reevaluate his priorities.

Ultimately, The Mexican is a heartwarming tale about finding one's place in the world, embracing cultural differences, and learning to love unconditionally. Through its lighthearted humor and poignant moments, the movie celebrates the beauty of human connection and the power of love to transcend borders and boundaries.

documents.title: Dreamcatcher
documents.tagline: A circle of friendship. A web of mystery. A pattern of fear.
documents.overview: Four boyhood pals perform a heroic act and are changed by the powers they gain in return. Years later, on a hunting trip in the Maine woods, they're overtaken by a vicious blizzard that harbors an ominous presence. Challenged to stop an alien force, the friends must first prevent the slaughter of innocent civilians by a military vigilante ... and then overcome a threat to the bond that unites the four of them.
documents.plot:
Dreamcatcher is a science fiction horror film directed by Lawrence Kasdan, based on the novel of the same name by Stephen King. The movie was released in 2003 and stars Morgan Freeman, Thomas Jane, Damian Lewis, Donnie Wahlberg, and Jason Lee.

The story begins with four friends - Jonesy (Jason Lee), Beaver (Donnie Wahlberg), Pete (Thomas Jane), and Henry (Morgan Freeman) - who have been inseparable since childhood. They share a deep bond and are known for their unique friendship. The movie takes place in 1980, during the height of the Vietnam War.

The story begins with Jonesy, who has recently returned from Vietnam, suffering from amnesia due to his experiences as a soldier. He is unable to recall any memories before his time in the war. As he tries to piece together his past, he discovers that he and his friends have been chosen by an alien entity known as "The Gray" (also referred to as "The Others") to be its hosts on Earth.

The Gray has a plan to invade Earth using four human hosts, each with unique skills and abilities. The aliens intend to use the hosts' bodies to take over their minds and eventually conquer humanity. Jonesy, Beaver, Pete, and Henry are chosen for this purpose, but they soon realize that they must work together to stop The Gray's plans.

As the story unfolds, the four friends embark on a perilous journey across the United States, facing numerous challenges and obstacles along the way. They encounter various alien creatures, including giant spiders, mutated humans, and otherworldly beings. Along the way, they also uncover clues about their past and the true nature of The Gray's plan.

Throughout the movie, the characters' relationships are put to the test as they struggle to work together and trust each other. Jonesy, in particular, grapples with his amnesia and tries to come to terms with his past. Beaver is haunted by a traumatic event from his childhood, while Pete struggles with his own demons.

As the stakes grow higher, the friends discover that The Gray's plan involves using their combined skills to create an army of alien-human hybrids. They must use all their strength, courage, and ingenuity to stop this plan and save humanity.

The movie culminates in a climactic showdown between the four friends and The Gray's minions. In the end, Jonesy, Beaver, Pete, and Henry manage to defeat the aliens and destroy their plans for world domination. However, not before they are forced to confront their own personal demons and make sacrifices to save humanity.

Overall, Dreamcatcher is a thrilling science fiction horror film that explores themes of friendship, loyalty, and redemption. While it received mixed reviews from critics at the time of its release, it has since become a cult classic among fans of Stephen King's works.

documents.title: Reign of Fire
documents.tagline: Fight Fire With Fire
documents.overview: In post-apocalyptic England, an American volunteer and a British survivor team up to fight off a brood of fire-breathing dragons seeking to return to global dominance after centuries of rest underground. The Brit -- leading a clan of survivors to hunt down the King of the Dragons -- has much at stake: His mother was killed by a dragon, but his love is still alive.
documents.plot: In post-apocalyptic England, an American volunteer and a British survivor team up to fight off a brood of fire-breathing dragons seeking to return to global dominance after centuries of rest underground. The Brit—leading a clan of survivors to hunt down the King of the Dragons—has much at stake: his mother was killed by a dragon, but his love is still alive.

documents.title: Brotherhood of the Wolf
documents.tagline: The year is 1766... The hunt for a killer has begun.
documents.overview: In 18th century France, the Chevalier de Fronsac and his Native American friend Mani are sent by the King to the Gevaudan province to investigate the killings of hundreds by a mysterious beast.
documents.plot:
Brotherhood of the Wolf is a 2001 French epic historical drama film directed by Jacques Audiard, produced by Canal+, and written by Tonino Benacquista. The movie is set in 18th-century France during the reign of King Louis XV.

The story revolves around Vicente Franco (played by Mads Mikkelsen), a young nobleman who seeks revenge against the aristocrats who wronged him. After being betrayed and left for dead, Vicente returns from his travels with a mysterious wolf-like creature that he claims to have encountered in the forest. He believes this creature is the key to his revenge.

As Vicente navigates the complexities of court politics and social hierarchy, he becomes embroiled in a plot by the Duke de Richelieu (played by Romain Duris) to overthrow King Louis XV. The Duke seeks to gain power and control over France, while Vicente sees an opportunity to use his newfound creature to exact revenge on those who wronged him.

Throughout the film, Audiard explores themes of identity, class, and the blurred lines between reality and fantasy. Vicente's encounters with the wolf-like creature serve as a metaphor for his own inner turmoil and struggle to find his place in society.

As the story unfolds, Vicente becomes increasingly obsessed with his quest for revenge, leading him down a path of violence and destruction. The Duke, on the other hand, is driven by ambition and a desire for power, which ultimately leads to his downfall.

The film's climax features an intense confrontation between Vicente and the Duke, with the wolf-like creature playing a pivotal role in the outcome. In the end, Vicente emerges victorious, but not without scars both physical and emotional.

One of the standout aspects of Brotherhood of the Wolf is its visually stunning depiction of 18th-century France. The film's cinematography, costume design, and production values all contribute to a richly detailed and immersive world that draws the viewer in.

Overall, Brotherhood of the Wolf is a complex and thought-provoking film that explores themes of identity, class, and revenge. With its stunning visuals and strong performances, it is a must-see for fans of historical dramas and epic storytelling.

documents.title: Hotel Chevalier
documents.overview: In a Paris hotel room, Jack Whitman lies on a bed. His phone rings; it's a woman on her way to see him, a surprise. She arrives and the complications of their relationship emerge in bits and pieces. Will they make love? Is their relationship over? (A prequel to The Darjeeling Limited, 2007.)
documents.plot:
Hotel Chevalier is a 2007 romantic drama film that explores the complexities of love, relationships, and identity through the story of two young Americans, Jack and Jules, who meet at a Parisian hotel. The movie delves into the themes of youthful disillusionment, social class, and the search for meaning in life.

The film's narrative is presented as a series of vignettes, showcasing the characters' inner struggles and desires. As Jack and Jules navigate their whirlwind romance, they must confront their own insecurities and the societal expectations that come with being young and privileged. The movie raises questions about the nature of identity, class, and privilege, highlighting the tensions between the old money and new rich.

Through its portrayal of the characters' emotional journeys, Hotel Chevalier touches on themes of love, loss, and longing. The film's use of atmospheric settings and poignant dialogue adds to the sense of melancholy and introspection that pervades the narrative. Ultimately, the movie presents a nuanced exploration of the human experience, one that is both deeply personal and universally relatable.

The film's director, Todd Haynes, masterfully weaves together these themes, creating a cinematic experience that is both intimate and expansive. By exploring the complexities of love and relationships through the lens of two young characters, Hotel Chevalier offers a poignant commentary on the human condition, one that continues to resonate with audiences today.

Overall, Hotel Chevalier is a thought-provoking and emotionally charged film that invites viewers to reflect on their own experiences and desires. Its exploration of themes such as identity, class, and love makes it a rich and rewarding cinematic experience.

documents.title: Racing Stripes
documents.tagline: Cheer 'til you're horse!
documents.overview: Shattered illusions are hard to repair -- especially for a good-hearted zebra named Stripes who's spent his life on a Kentucky farm amidst the sorely mistaken notion that he's a debonair thoroughbred. Once he faces the fact that his stark stripes mark him as different, he decides he'll race anyway. And with help from the young girl who raised him, he just might end up in the winner's circle.

documents.title: The Shipping News
documents.tagline: You'll never guess what you'll find inside...
documents.overview: An emotionally-beaten man with his young daughter moves to his ancestral home in Newfoundland to reclaim his life.
documents.plot:
The Shipping News is a poignant and introspective film that explores the complexities of family dynamics, identity, and the search for belonging. Set in the 1950s on the Canadian coast, the story revolves around Quoyle, a struggling writer who returns to his ancestral home after receiving news of his mother's death.

At its core, The Shipping News is a deeply personal and emotional journey about Quoyle's quest to come to terms with his past and find his place in the world. As he navigates his complicated relationships with his family members, particularly his estranged father and half-sister, Quoyle must confront the traumas of his childhood and the secrets that have haunted him for so long.

Throughout the film, director Lasse Hallström masterfully weaves together themes of identity, belonging, and the power of storytelling. Quoyle's journey is a metaphor for the search for meaning and purpose in life, as he struggles to find his voice as a writer and assert his independence from his family's legacy.

The Shipping News also explores the complexities of masculinity and the societal expectations placed on men, particularly those who are struggling to find their place in the world. Quoyle's character is a nuanced portrayal of a man who is both vulnerable and strong-willed, as he navigates the challenges of adulthood and grapples with his own sense of identity.

Ultimately, The Shipping News is a powerful and moving film that explores the human condition with sensitivity and depth. It is a story about the power of love, forgiveness, and redemption to heal old wounds and bring people together, even in the face of adversity and uncertainty.

documents.title: Freddy vs. Jason
documents.tagline: Evil will battle evil.
documents.overview: In an attempt to free himself from a state of forgotten limbo, evil dream-demon Freddy Krueger devises a plan to manipulate un-dead mass murderer Jason Voorhees  into slicing-and-dicing his way through the teenage population of Springwood.  But when the master of dreams loses control of his monster, a brutal fight to the death is the only way out.
documents.plot:
Freddy vs. Jason is a 2003 American horror film directed by Ronny Yu and written by Damian Shannon and Mark Swift. The movie is a crossover between two popular horror franchises: A Nightmare on Elm Street and Friday the 13th.

The film begins with Freddy Krueger (Robert Englund), the dream demon from Springwood, Ohio, who has been trapped in a magical realm known as the "Dream World" for over 25 years. However, due to a series of events, Freddy is able to escape and enter the real world, where he finds himself in Crystal Lake, New Jersey.

Meanwhile, Jason Voorhees (Ken Kirzinger), the masked killer from Camp Crystal Lake, has also escaped his own realm and entered the real world. The two horror icons soon discover that they are being hunted by a group of teenagers who are trying to survive their encounters with both Freddy and Jason.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Freddy is using his powers to manipulate the dreams of the teenagers, while Jason is using his brute strength to terrorize them in the real world. The two horror icons engage in a series of battles, with Freddy using his claws and wit to try and outsmart Jason, who relies on his physical strength to overpower his opponents.

As the body count rises, the teenagers begin to realize that they are being manipulated by both Freddy and Jason, who are working together to eliminate them. The group soon discovers that the only way to stop both horror icons is to find a way to destroy their respective realms and trap them back in their own worlds.

In the climactic final battle, the teenagers use a magical artifact known as the "Dream Crystal" to create a portal between the Dream World and the real world. Freddy and Jason are drawn into the portal, where they engage in an epic battle that takes place within both the dream and reality realms.

Ultimately, the teenagers emerge victorious, but not without sustaining significant injuries. As the dust settles, it becomes clear that Freddy has been defeated, but at a great cost: he is trapped in the Dream World, unable to escape. Jason, on the other hand, returns to his own realm, where he will continue to terrorize Camp Crystal Lake.

The film ends with a sense of closure for both horror franchises, as the surviving teenagers reflect on their harrowing experiences and the lessons they learned about facing their fears. While Freddy vs. Jason received mixed reviews from critics at the time of its release, it has since become a cult classic among horror fans, who appreciate its campy humor, over-the-top violence, and nostalgic value.

Overall, Freddy vs. Jason is a fun and entertaining crossover film that brings together two beloved horror franchises in a way that is both faithful to their respective worlds and fresh enough to feel new.

documents.title: Alvin and the Chipmunks
documents.tagline: The Original Entourage
documents.overview: A struggling songwriter named Dave Seville finds success when he comes across a trio of singing chipmunks: mischievous leader Alvin, brainy Simon, and chubby, impressionable Theodore.
documents.plot:
Alvin and the Chipmunks is a 2007 American musical comedy based on the characters created by Ross Bagdasarian Sr., directed by Tim Hill from a screenplay by Jon Vitti, Will McRobb and Chris Viscardi. Jason Lee plays the songwriter Dave Seville, David Cross the record executive Ian Hawke and Cameron Richardson Dave's former girlfriend Claire, while Justin Long, Matthew Gray Gubler and Jesse McCartney voice the chipmunks Alvin, Simon and Theodore.

The three talking chipmunk brothers live in a fir tree that is cut down and taken to Los Angeles after JETT Records buys it as a Christmas tree. In the same building, the struggling songwriter Dave Seville has his latest demo rejected by Ian Hawke, his old college roommate and the label's chief executive. The chipmunks follow Dave home, and after an initial panic he discovers they can sing, striking a deal to give them food and a home in return for performing his songs.

The partnership starts badly. Stage fright ruins their first audition for Ian, the chipmunks accidentally cost Dave his advertising job, and Alvin's attempts at matchmaking spoil a dinner with Claire. To make amends, the brothers go to Ian's mansion on their own and sing Dave's song "Christmas Don't Be Late", winning a record contract and making Dave their manager. As they grow attached to Dave and start to see him as family, he keeps them at arm's length.

Ian pushes for ever more aggressive promotion, and when Dave insists the chipmunks are too young for celebrity, Ian convinces them that Dave is holding them back. After a quarrel, and finding an old letter in which Dave wrote about returning them to the forest, the brothers move in with Ian, who showers them with luxury while working them to exhaustion on tour and telling them Dave no longer cares. When Ian announces a year-long world tour, Dave enlists Claire's help to sneak into their concert at the Orpheum Theatre. Realising they have been deceived, the chipmunks sabotage the show. Ian locks them in a cage for a flight to Paris, but they escape, reunite with Dave, and Ian's career collapses.

Critics were largely negative, with 28% approval on Rotten Tomatoes, but the film opened second behind I Am Legend and grossed $365.4 million worldwide on a budget of $55 to 60 million, launching a series of three sequels.

documents.title: I Am Legend
documents.tagline: The last man on Earth is not alone
documents.overview: Robert Neville is a scientist who was unable to stop the spread of the terrible virus that was incurable and man-made. Immune, Neville is now the last human survivor in what is left of New York City and perhaps the world. For three years, Neville has faithfully sent out daily radio messages, desperate to find any other survivors who might be out there. But he is not alone.
documents.plot:
I Am Legend is a post-apocalyptic science fiction film directed by Francis Lawrence, based on the novel of the same name by Richard Matheson. The movie stars Will Smith as Robert Neville, a military scientist who finds himself to be one of the last humans on Earth.

The story begins in 2006, where Robert Neville (Will Smith) is working for the United States Army at a biological research facility in New York City. He is part of a team that has been studying a virus known as the "Krippin Virus" which causes its hosts to become violent and zombie-like creatures after infection. The virus was created by a scientist named Dr. Krippin, who had been experimenting with it before his death.

As the outbreak occurs, Robert Neville is one of the few survivors, but he soon realizes that he is not alone on Earth. He finds himself surrounded by hordes of infected humans, which he has dubbed "Virals." The Virals are fast, agile, and seemingly unstoppable, making them a formidable threat to human survival.

As the years pass, Robert Neville becomes increasingly isolated, with no contact with other humans. He spends his days scavenging for food and supplies, while also trying to find a cure for the virus. He sets up traps and defenses around his home in an attempt to protect himself from the Virals, but he knows that it's only a matter of time before they break through.

One day, Robert Neville receives a package containing a small dog, which becomes his companion and friend. The dog helps him to stay sane and provides emotional support during his lonely existence. As the years go by, Robert Neville begins to notice changes in himself, as he starts to exhibit some of the same characteristics as the Virals.

The turning point comes when Robert Neville discovers that the virus is not just a simple infection, but rather a complex genetic mutation that has altered his own DNA. He realizes that he may be one of the few remaining humans who are immune to the virus, and that he may hold the key to finding a cure.

As Robert Neville delves deeper into the mystery of the virus, he becomes increasingly obsessed with finding a way to restore humanity to its former glory. He sets out on a perilous journey across New York City, searching for any signs of life or clues to the virus's origins.

In the end, Robert Neville discovers that the only remaining human survivor is a young girl who has been living in an abandoned church. Together, they form a bond and work towards finding a cure for the virus. However, as they near their goal, Robert Neville realizes that he may be too late to save humanity, and that the world may never be the same again.

The movie ends with Robert Neville and the young girl escaping from New York City in a helicopter, leaving behind the ruins of civilization. As they fly away, Robert Neville looks out at the desolate landscape, knowing that he has lost his way and that the world will never be the same again.

documents.title: The Dukes of Hazzard
documents.tagline: Cousins. Outlaws. Thrillbillies.
documents.overview: Cousins, Bo and Luke Duke, with the help of their eye-catching cousin, Daisy and moonshine-running Uncle Jesse, try and save the family farm from being destroyed by Hazzard County's corrupt commissioner, Boss Hogg. Their efforts constantly find the 'Duke Boys' eluding authorities in 'The General Lee', their 1969 orange Dodge Charger that keeps them one step ahead of the dimwitted antics of the small southern town's Sheriff, Roscoe P. Coltrane.

documents.title: The Orphanage
documents.tagline: A tale of love.  A story of horror.
documents.overview: A woman brings her family back to her childhood home, which used to be an orphanage, intent on reopening it. Before long, her son starts to communicate with a new invisible friend.
documents.plot:
The Orphanage is a Spanish horror film directed by Juan Antonio Bayona, released in 2007. The movie tells the story of a woman named Laura, played by Belén Rueda, who returns to the orphanage where she grew up as an adult.

Laura's childhood was marked by tragedy when her younger brother died under mysterious circumstances at the orphanage. She has always felt a deep sense of guilt and responsibility for his death. As an adult, Laura is haunted by nightmares and a feeling of being watched. She decides to return to the orphanage, now abandoned and rumored to be haunted, in an attempt to lay her brother's spirit to rest.

Upon arrival, Laura discovers that the orphanage has been renovated into a nursing home for elderly people. However, she soon realizes that the residents are not what they seem. They appear to be in a state of catatonia, and their eyes seem to follow her everywhere she goes. As Laura delves deeper into the mystery, she begins to uncover dark secrets about the orphanage's past.

Laura's investigation leads her to a room where her brother's grave is supposed to be located. However, when she searches for it, she finds that it has been moved and is now in a different location. This discovery sets off a chain of events that reveals the truth about the orphanage's dark history.

As Laura digs deeper, she discovers that the orphanage was once home to a group of children who died under mysterious circumstances. The children's spirits are trapped between the world of the living and the afterlife, and they are unable to move on. Laura realizes that her brother's death is connected to these children's deaths and that she has been carrying the guilt of their deaths with her all along.

In a shocking twist, it is revealed that Laura herself was one of the children who died at the orphanage. Her memories of the event were false, implanted by her adoptive parents to protect her from the truth. The entire story is a product of Laura's imagination, and she has been trying to uncover the truth about her own past.

The movie ends with Laura finally finding peace and closure. She realizes that she was not responsible for her brother's death and that she has been carrying the guilt of others' deaths all along. The film's ending is open to interpretation, leaving the audience to wonder whether Laura's memories were real or just a product of her imagination.

Overall, The Orphanage is a haunting and atmospheric horror film that explores themes of grief, guilt, and the power of the human mind. The movie features stunning visuals and a standout performance from Belén Rueda, who brings depth and nuance to the complex character of Laura.

documents.title: Charlie Wilson's War
documents.tagline: When the world wasn't looking, he changed it forever.
documents.overview: The true story of Texas congressman Charlie Wilson's covert dealings in Afghanistan, where his efforts to assist rebels in their war with the Soviets had some unforeseen and long-reaching effects.
documents.plot: A Texas congressman sets a series of events in motion when he conspires with a CIA operative to aid Afghan mujahideen rebels fighting the Soviets.

documents.title: 27 Dresses
documents.tagline: She's about to find the perfect fit.
documents.overview: Altruistic Jane finds herself facing her worst nightmare as her younger sister announces her engagement to the man Jane secretly adores.
documents.plot: Altruistic Jane finds herself facing her worst nightmare as her younger sister announces her engagement to the man Jane secretly adores.

documents.title: Walk Hard: The Dewey Cox Story
documents.original_title: Walk Hard: The Dewey Cox Story
documents.tagline: Life made him tough. Love made him strong. Music made him hard.
documents.overview: Following a childhood tragedy, Dewey Cox follows a long and winding road to music stardom. Dewey perseveres through changing musical styles, an addiction to nearly every drug known and bouts of uncontrollable rage.
documents.plot: Following a childhood tragedy, Dewey Cox follows a long and winding road to music stardom. Dewey perseveres through changing musical styles, an addiction to nearly every drug known and bouts of uncontrollable rage.

documents.title: Underdog
documents.tagline: ONE NATION... UNDER DOG
documents.overview: A lab accident gives a hound named Shoeshine some serious superpowers -- a secret that the dog eventually shares with the young boy who becomes his owner and friend.
documents.plot:
Underdog is a 2007 animated superhero comedy film that tells the story of a lovable and underappreciated dog named Underdog who dreams of becoming a hero. The movie explores several themes, including the importance of believing in oneself and one's abilities.

At its core, Underdog is a tale about self-discovery and empowerment. The main character, Underdog, is an ordinary dog with extraordinary potential, but he lacks confidence and recognition from those around him. As he navigates his way through various challenges and obstacles, Underdog learns to trust himself and his unique abilities, ultimately discovering that being different is not a weakness, but a strength.

The film also touches on the theme of friendship and loyalty. Underdog's relationships with his owner, Polly Purebred, and other characters in the story serve as a reminder of the importance of having supportive friends by your side. Through their interactions, the movie shows how these bonds can help us overcome adversity and achieve our goals.

Furthermore, Underdog pokes fun at societal expectations and the pressures to conform. The character of Sweet Polly Purebred, for instance, is a perfect example of this theme. She's a beautiful, high-society dog who struggles with her own identity and sense of purpose, highlighting the tension between being true to oneself and meeting the expectations of others.

Overall, Underdog is a heartwarming story about embracing one's individuality, finding confidence in oneself, and the power of friendship and loyalty.

documents.title: Lars and the Real Girl
documents.tagline: The search for true love begins outside the box.
documents.overview: Extremely shy Lars finds it impossible to make friends or socialize. His brother and sister-in-law worry about him, so when he announces that he has a girlfriend he met on the Internet, they are overjoyed. But Lars' new lady is a life-size plastic woman. On the advice of a doctor, his family and the rest of the community go along with his delusion.

documents.title: Death in Venice
documents.tagline: The celebrated story of a man obsessed with ideal beauty.
documents.overview: Composer Gustav von Aschenbach travels to Venice for health reasons. There, he becomes obsessed with the stunning beauty of an adolescent Polish boy named Tadzio who is staying with his family at the same Grand Hôtel des Bains on the Lido as Aschenbach.
documents.plot:
Death in Venice (Italian: Morte a Venezia) is a 1971 historical drama film directed and produced by Luchino Visconti, who adapted Thomas Mann's 1912 novella with Nicola Badalucco. It stars Dirk Bogarde as Gustav von Aschenbach and Björn Andrésen as Tadzio, with Mark Burns, Marisa Berenson and Silvana Mangano. Shot in Technicolor by Pasqualino De Santis, it uses music from Gustav Mahler's Third and Fifth Symphonies and is the second part of Visconti's "German Trilogy", between The Damned (1969) and Ludwig (1973).

In poor health, the composer Aschenbach travels to Venice to rest. As his ship arrives, a garishly made-up old man accosts him with suggestive remarks, and he turns away in disgust. Staying at the Grand Hotel des Bains on the Lido, he notices a Polish family and becomes captivated by their beautiful adolescent son, Tadzio. The boy's image recalls heated debates with his friend and pupil Alfred over whether beauty is created by art or exists in nature and is superior to it. Aschenbach watches Tadzio on the beach, and after an encounter in the hotel lift in which the boy seems to give him an inviting look, he resolves in agitation to leave. When his luggage is misdirected at the station, however, he is secretly glad to return, though he sees a man collapse at the station, and the hotel manager dismisses foreign press reports as exaggerated.

Aschenbach makes Tadzio his muse but cannot master his longing and drifts into daydreams about the unreachable boy, who notices his gaze and occasionally returns it, though they never speak. A travel clerk in Saint Mark's Square reluctantly admits that cholera is spreading through the city, and Aschenbach imagines warning Tadzio's mother. He follows the family to St Mark's Basilica, and a talkative barber dyes and paints him into a likeness of the old man from the ship. Trailing the family through the streets, he collapses by a well in pained laughter, and he dreams of a disastrous concert in Munich and Alfred's reproaches. Learning the family is departing, Aschenbach, now gravely ill, sits on the empty beach watching Tadzio wade into the sea to Mahler's Adagietto. The boy turns and points toward the horizon, and Aschenbach dies in his deck chair.

The film premiered in London on 1 March 1971 and competed at the 24th Cannes Film Festival. Critics have admired its sumptuous visuals, with Derek Malcolm of The Guardian calling it a slow, precise and beautiful achievement; Rotten Tomatoes reports 70% approval.

documents.title: National Treasure: Book of Secrets
documents.tagline: The Greatest Adventure History Has Ever Revealed
documents.overview: Benjamin Franklin Gates and Dr. Abigail Chase re-team with Riley Poole and, now armed with a stack of long-lost pages from John Wilkes Booth's diary, Ben must follow a clue left there to prove his ancestor's innocence in the assassination of Abraham Lincoln.
documents.plot:
National Treasure: Book of Secrets is a 2007 American action-adventure film directed by Jon Turteltaub, produced by Jerry Bruckheimer, and written by Jim Kouf. The movie stars Nicolas Cage as Benjamin Gates, a treasure hunter with a passion for American history.

The film begins with Benjamin Gates (Nicolas Cage) being approached by the Treasury Department to help find a lost document known as the "Book of Secrets." The book is said to contain information about the Founding Fathers' involvement in the Knights Templar and their alleged discovery of the Holy Grail. However, the book has been stolen from the National Archives, and it's up to Gates to retrieve it.

Gates teams up with his partner, Riley Poole (Dustin Hoffman), a computer expert, and Abigail Chase ( Diane Kruger), an archaeologist. Together, they embark on a perilous journey across the United States, following a series of cryptic clues left behind by the book's thief.

As they delve deeper into the mystery, Gates and his team uncover a conspiracy involving the British government, which is trying to discredit Benjamin's claims about the Founding Fathers' involvement with the Knights Templar. The team also discovers that Abigail Chase is actually the daughter of John Adams, one of the Founding Fathers, making her a direct descendant of the president.

The plot thickens as Gates and his team encounter various obstacles, including treacherous terrain, deadly traps, and rival treasure hunters. Along the way, they meet Patrick Gates (Sean Bean), Benjamin's long-lost father, who reveals that he was also involved in the Knights Templar and had been searching for the Book of Secrets.

As the story unfolds, Gates and his team finally reach the location of the lost document: a hidden chamber beneath the White House. However, they soon realize that they are not alone, as they are confronted by the British government's agents, who will stop at nothing to keep the truth about the Founding Fathers' involvement with the Knights Templar from being revealed.

In the end, Gates and his team successfully retrieve the Book of Secrets, but not before a thrilling showdown with the rival treasure hunters. The film concludes with Benjamin Gates returning the book to its rightful place in the National Archives, while Abigail Chase comes to terms with her newfound heritage as a descendant of John Adams.

Throughout the movie, Nicolas Cage delivers his signature blend of humor, wit, and action hero charm, making National Treasure: Book of Secrets an entertaining and thrilling adventure that explores the fascinating world of American history and cryptography.

documents.title: Zathura: A Space Adventure
documents.tagline: Adventure Is Waiting
documents.overview: After their father is called into work, two young boys, Walter and Danny, are left in the care of their teenage sister, Lisa, and told they must stay inside. Walter and Danny, who anticipate a boring day, are shocked when they begin playing Zathura, a space-themed board game, which they realize has mystical powers when their house is shot into space. With the help of an astronaut, the boys attempt to return home.
documents.plot:
Zathura: A Space Adventure is a science fiction film directed by Jon Favreau, released in 2005 by Columbia Pictures.

The story begins with two brothers, Walter (Josh Hutcherson) and Danny (Jensen Ackles), who are struggling to find common ground after their parents' divorce. Their lives take an unexpected turn when they stumble upon a mysterious board game called Zathura, which was left behind by their father. The game is unlike any other, as it seems to have a life of its own and emits a strange energy.

As soon as the brothers start playing the game, their house is suddenly sucked into a wormhole, transporting them to a distant planet called Pegasus-4. There, they encounter an alien named Captain Rainluff (Ben Kingsley), who claims that Zathura is a game created by an advanced civilization to test the skills of its players.

However, things take a turn for the worse when Walter and Danny's sibling rivalry causes them to disagree on how to play the game. As a result, they inadvertently trigger a catastrophic event that threatens to destroy their spaceship and the entire planet. The brothers must put aside their differences and work together to survive and find a way back home.

As they navigate through the challenges of Pegasus-4, Walter and Danny encounter various obstacles, including treacherous terrain, hostile aliens, and malfunctioning spacecraft. Along the way, they also discover that Zathura is more than just a game - it's a test of their courage, wits, and teamwork.

Throughout their journey, the brothers learn valuable lessons about trust, loyalty, and the importance of family. In the end, they successfully complete the challenges of Zathura and find a way back to Earth, but not before discovering that their father is alive and well, having been presumed dead in a previous adventure.

The film features stunning visual effects, heart-pumping action sequences, and a healthy dose of humor, making it an entertaining ride for audiences of all ages. With its themes of brotherly love and the power of teamwork, Zathura: A Space Adventure is a delightful and thrilling adventure that will leave viewers eager for more.

[No additional information available]

documents.title: Failure to Launch
documents.tagline: To leave the nest, some men just need a little push.
documents.overview: Tripp, an attractive man in his thirties, is still living with his parents Al and Sue. Tripp's best friends Demo and Ace are also still living in their parents' homes and seem proud of it. Al and Sue are not happy, however, and are fascinated when friends whose adult son has recently moved away from home reveal they hired an expert to arrange the matter and couldn't be happier with the result.
documents.plot: At 35, Tripp has an interesting job, a hip car, a passion for sailing, an active dating life, and a great house - trouble is, he still lives with his parents, Al and Sue, who are not happy about it. Al and Sue are fascinated when friends whose adult son has recently moved away from home reveal they hired an expert to help. In desperation to push Tripp out of the nest once and for all, Al and Sue hatch a plan to hire Paula, an "interventionist," who has a formula in these cases.

documents.title: One Missed Call
documents.tagline: What will it sound like when you die?
documents.overview: Several people start receiving voice-mails from their future selves -- messages which include the date, time, and some of the details of their deaths.
documents.plot:
One Missed Call is a psychological thriller that delves into the darker aspects of human nature and the consequences of one's actions. The film revolves around a mysterious phone call that foretells the exact time and manner of a person's death, leaving them with no choice but to try and prevent their own demise.

At its core, One Missed Call explores the theme of mortality and the inevitability of fate. The main character, Koichi Sakakibara, is forced to confront his own mortality after receiving the ominous phone call, which sets him on a desperate quest to uncover the truth behind the mysterious calls. As he delves deeper into the mystery, he begins to realize that the caller's intentions are far more sinister than he initially thought.

The film also touches upon the theme of guilt and redemption. Koichi is haunted by his own past mistakes and feels compelled to make amends before it's too late. His journey becomes a metaphor for the human desire to atone for past wrongs and find forgiveness, even in the face of impending doom.

Furthermore, One Missed Call examines the concept of fate versus free will, leaving the audience questioning whether our lives are predetermined or if we have control over our own destinies. The film's twisty plot keeps viewers on the edge of their seats, as they try to unravel the mystery alongside Koichi.

Overall, One Missed Call is a gripping thriller that delves into the complexities of human psychology, mortality, and the consequences of one's actions, leaving a lasting impact on its audience.
production_companies: Equity Pictures Medienfonds GmbH & Co. KG IV

documents.title: The Village
documents.tagline: There is no turning back
documents.overview: When a willful young man tries to venture beyond his sequestered Pennsylvania hamlet, his actions set off a chain of chilling incidents that will alter the community forever.
documents.plot:
The Village is a psychological horror-thriller film directed by M. Night Shyamalan, released in 2004 by Touchstone Pictures and Scott Rudin Productions.

The story takes place in the late 19th century in a small, isolated village surrounded by a dense forest in Pennsylvania. The villagers live in fear of the "wild" that exists outside their community, which is said to be inhabited by monstrous creatures. The villagers believe that if they venture too far from their village, they will be attacked and killed by these creatures.

The film follows the story of Lucy (Bryce Dallas Howard), a young woman who lives in the village with her brother, Seth (Joel Edgerton). Lucy is a curious and independent individual who longs to explore the world beyond her village. She becomes fascinated with a mysterious figure named Edward (Joaquin Phoenix) who lives on the other side of the forest.

As Lucy spends more time with Edward, she begins to question the villagers' beliefs about the "wild" and its inhabitants. She discovers that the creatures are not as monstrous as they seem, but rather, they are human beings who have been isolated from society for generations.

However, their isolation has led to a twisted and violent culture, where they live in fear of each other and the outside world. Lucy's relationship with Edward deepens, and she begins to see him as an outsider who is not afraid to challenge the villagers' way of life.

As tensions rise within the village, Lucy must decide whether to conform to the villagers' expectations or to follow her heart and explore the truth about the "wild." The film builds towards a climactic confrontation between Lucy and the villagers, which ultimately leads to a shocking revelation about Edward's true identity.

Throughout the film, Shyamalan uses suspenseful storytelling and atmospheric tension to create a sense of unease and uncertainty. The cinematography is stunning, capturing the eerie beauty of the forest and the isolation of the village.

The Village received mixed reviews from critics but has since become a cult classic, praised for its originality and thought-provoking themes. The film's exploration of fear, conformity, and the human condition continues to resonate with audiences today.

Overall, The Village is a gripping and unsettling thriller that challenges viewers to question their assumptions about the world around them. With its atmospheric tension, suspenseful plot, and thought-provoking themes, it is a must-see for fans of psychological horror and suspense.

documents.title: The Wedding Date
documents.tagline: Love doesn't come cheap.
documents.overview: With the wedding of her younger sister fast approaching, Kat Ellis faces the undesirable prospect of traveling alone to London for the ceremony. While this is bad enough, Jeffrey, the man who left her as they moved closer to marriage, happens to be the groom's best man. Determined to show everyone -- most of all Jeffrey -- that her romantic life is as full and thrilling as ever, Kat hires a charming male escort as her date.

documents.title: The Weather Man
documents.tagline: Dave Spritz is about to take his best shot . . . at life
documents.overview: A Chicago weather man, separated from his wife and children, debates whether professional and personal success are mutually exclusive.
documents.plot:
The Weather Man is a 2005 American dark comedy-drama directed by Gore Verbinski and written by Steve Conrad. Nicolas Cage stars as a Chicago television weatherman in the midst of a midlife crisis, with Michael Caine as his father and Hope Davis as his estranged wife, and Gemmenne de la Peña and Nicholas Hoult as his children. It was released on October 28, 2005.

David Spritz is a well-paid weatherman on a Chicago news program, but he commands little respect: strangers regularly hurl fast food at him in the street, perhaps, he suspects, out of resentment at his easy, lucrative job. He also lives in the shadow of his father, Robert Spritzel, a Pulitzer Prize-winning novelist who is quietly disappointed by his son's inability to grow up and take charge of his life and his children. His marriage to Noreen has collapsed, and he struggles to connect with his children, Shelly and Mike. When Robert is diagnosed with lymphoma and given months to live, David's sense of failure deepens. He takes up archery, finding in it a rare source of focus and calm, and he tries, mostly in vain, to live up to his father's advice that the right thing and the hard thing are often the same.

Hoping to prove himself to his father and win back Noreen, David auditions for a weatherman position on the national morning show Hello America, a job that would quadruple his salary but require moving to New York. He takes Shelly with him to the audition, bonding with her as he helps her find a new wardrobe. While he is away, he learns that Mike has fought off his counselor, who made sexual advances toward him. Despite his anxiety and a night of heavy drinking, David impresses the producers and is offered the job. Back home, he strikes Noreen's new boyfriend, Russ, and confronts and beats the counselor.

At a "living funeral" arranged for Robert, David asks Noreen to reconcile and move to New York with him, but she has decided to marry Russ. In a final conversation, David breaks down, and Robert gently tells him that he still has time to clear the garbage out of his life before he dies. Months later, David has taken the job and moved to New York. People no longer throw things at him, which he wryly suspects may have something to do with the bow he now carries.

The film grossed about $19 million worldwide. Reviews were mixed to positive; Rotten Tomatoes reports 60% approval, with a consensus praising its fine performances and dry, dark humor, and Metacritic gave it 61 out of 100.

documents.title: Something's Gotta Give
documents.tagline: Schmucks are people too.
documents.overview: Harry Sanborn is an aged music industry exec with a fondness for younger women like Marin, his latest trophy girlfriend. Things get a little awkward when Harry suffers a heart attack at the home of Marin's mother, Erica. Left in the care of Erica and his doctor, a love triangle starts to take shape.
documents.plot: When perpetually single, aging music industry exec Harry Sanborn, and his latest trophy girlfriend, Marin, arrive at her mother's beach house in the Hamptons, they find that her mother, playwright Erica Barry, also plans to stay for the weekend. Erica is scandalized by the relationship and Harry's sexist ways. But when Harry has a heart attack while there, and the doctor prescribes bedrest, his only option is to stay at the Barry home. Left in the care of Erica and his doctor, a love triangle starts to take shape.

documents.title: Australia
documents.tagline: Welcome to Australia!
documents.overview: Set in northern Australia before World War II, an English aristocrat who inherits a sprawling ranch reluctantly pacts with a stock-man in order to protect her new property from a takeover plot. As the pair drive 2,000 head of cattle over unforgiving landscape, they experience the bombing of Darwin by Japanese forces firsthand.

documents.title: In the Valley of Elah
documents.tagline: Sometimes finding the truth is easier than facing it.
documents.overview: A career officer and his wife work with a police detective to uncover the truth behind their son's disappearance following his return from a tour of duty in Iraq.
documents.plot:
In the Valley of Elah is a thought-provoking drama that delves into the complexities of war, identity, and redemption. The film tells the story of Hank DeVille (played by Russell Crowe), a U.S. Army National Guard sergeant who returns home from Iraq to find his son missing in action.

As Hank searches for answers about his son's disappearance, he becomes embroiled in a mystery surrounding a local teenager, Emmett (played by Joseph Gordon-Levitt), who is accused of murdering a young woman. Through this investigation, the film explores themes of patriotism, duty, and the moral complexities of war.

The movie also delves into the psychological toll that war takes on soldiers, particularly those who are forced to confront the harsh realities of combat. Hank's journey is marked by a deep sense of loss, anger, and disillusionment, as he struggles to reconcile his own identity with the expectations placed upon him as a soldier.

One of the most striking aspects of In the Valley of Elah is its portrayal of the human cost of war, particularly on those who are left behind. The film raises important questions about the nature of patriotism, duty, and responsibility, and challenges the viewer to consider the complexities of these themes in the context of modern warfare.

Ultimately, In the Valley of Elah is a powerful exploration of the human condition, one that grapples with some of the most pressing issues of our time. Through its thought-provoking narrative and nuanced character development, the film offers a searing critique of the war on terror and its impact on American society.

documents.title: Ken Park
documents.tagline: Who are you?
documents.overview: Ken Park focuses on several teenagers and their tormented home lives. Shawn seems to be the most conventional. Tate is brimming with psychotic rage; Claude is habitually harassed by his brutish father and coddled, rather uncomfortably, by his enormously pregnant mother. Peaches looks after her devoutly religious father, but yearns for freedom. They're all rather tight, or so they claim.
documents.plot:
Ken Park is a 2002 psychological teen film directed by Larry Clark and Edward Lachman and written by Harmony Korine, who built the screenplay from Clark's journals and stories after Clark became dissatisfied with his own draft. Set in Visalia, California, it portrays the abusive and dysfunctional lives of four teenagers connected by the suicide of an acquaintance, the title character. James Ransone plays Tate, Tiffany Limos plays Peaches, James Bullard plays Shawn and Stephen Jasso plays Claude, with Adam Chubbuck as Ken Park and a supporting cast including Maeve Quinlan, Amanda Plummer, Wade Williams, Julio Oscar Mechoso and Richard Riehle. Although planned for digital video, it was shot on 35 mm film.

The film opens with Ken Park, a teenage skateboarder, riding into a skate park, setting up a camcorder and shooting himself. His death frames the story, which cuts between four other teenagers who knew him and the failures of the adults around them. Shawn, the most stable of the four, is secretly having an affair with his girlfriend's mother, while her family remains unaware. Claude endures physical and emotional abuse from his alcoholic father, who despises him for not being masculine enough, while his pregnant mother does little to protect him; after a disturbing drunken advance by his father, Claude runs away from home. Peaches lives with her intensely religious widowed father, who sees her as the embodiment of her dead mother; when he discovers her with her boyfriend Curtis, he beats the boy, punishes her harshly and forces her into a disturbing mock wedding ritual. Tate, a volatile and sadistic youth who lives with grandparents he resents, eventually murders them over petty grievances, records a confession explaining his actions for the police, and is arrested. The separate strands converge only at the end, when Shawn, Claude and Peaches come together, and a final flashback returns to Ken in the days before his death, revealing that his girlfriend was pregnant.

Ken Park premiered at the Telluride Film Festival in 2002 but has not been released in the United States since, which Clark attributed to the producer's failure to secure music rights. It was refused classification in Australia in 2003 because of its graphic sexual content and depictions of underage sexual activity, and police shut down a protest screening in Sydney hosted by critic Margaret Pomeranz. Critical reception was mixed, with a 46% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes.

documents.title: Van Helsing: The London Assignment
documents.overview: It tells of the events before the film, in which monster hunter Gabriel Van Helsing travels to London to investigate a series of horrific, and decidedly supernatural murders, being committed by the mad scientist Dr. Jekyll, in the form of his evil alter-ego, Mr. Hyde.

documents.title: Venom
documents.tagline: He never hurt a soul until the day he died.
documents.overview: A group of teenagers fear for their lives in the swamps of Louisiana, chased by Mr. Jangles, a man possessed by 13 evil souls, and now relentless in his pursuit of new victims.
documents.plot:
Venom is a 2005 American supernatural slasher film directed by Jim Gillespie, who reunited with screenwriter Kevin Williamson after their collaboration on I Know What You Did Last Summer. The ensemble cast features Agnes Bruckner as Eden Sinclair, Jonathan Jackson as Eric, Laura Ramsey as Rachel, Meagan Good as CeCe, D. J. Cotrona as Sean, Rick Cramer as tow truck driver Ray Sawyer and Method Man as Deputy Turner. The film was based on Backwater, an unproduced survival horror video game designed by John Zuur Platten and Flint Dille, and was shot in Louisiana, in Amite, Choctaw, Hammond and New Orleans.

In a small town, high school senior Eden and her friends spend their time at the local burger joint, where Sean's father Ray, a gruff tow truck driver, picks up an order. That night a Creole woman, CeCe's grandmother, who has just dug up a mysterious briefcase, swerves to avoid Ray's truck on a bridge and nearly plunges over the edge. Ray rescues her, but at her desperate urging he reaches back for the case as the car sinks into the water, and snakes burst out of it and bite him repeatedly. Both Ray and the old woman die. In the morgue, Ray rises again, kills the coroner and a police officer, and sets out on a murderous rampage through the teenagers' circle with the tools of his trade, including chains and a crowbar. CeCe, who took a charm from her grandmother's body, explains that the snakes contained evil that her grandmother had drawn out of wicked men to purify their souls, and that this evil has now possessed Ray. As their friends are picked off one by one, the survivors take refuge in the grandmother's house, which is protected by voodoo spells, and search for a way to destroy the seemingly unstoppable killer.

Venom was released by Miramax Films' Dimension Films label on September 16, 2005, the last Dimension release before the Walt Disney Company sold the label to The Weinstein Company. Its timing, days after Hurricane Katrina devastated southeast Louisiana, made the film seem unfortunately topical, and it was a box-office failure. Critics gave it negative reviews; it holds a 13% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus calls it a voodoo horror film without the mojo whose unimaginative rampage quickly lulls viewers to sleep.

documents.title: Perfect Stranger
documents.tagline: How Far Would You Go To Keep A Secret?
documents.overview: A journalist goes undercover to ferret out businessman Harrison Hill as her best friend's killer. Posing as one of his temps, she enters into a game of online cat-and-mouse.

documents.title: Cloverfield
documents.tagline: Some thing has found us.
documents.overview: Five young New Yorkers throw their friend a going-away party the night that a monster the size of a skyscraper descends upon the city. Told from the point of view of their video camera, the film is a document of their attempt to survive the most surreal, horrifying event of their lives.
documents.plot:
Cloverfield is a 2008 monster horror film directed by Matt Reeves and produced by J.J. Abrams' production company Bad Robot Productions, in association with Universal Pictures.

The film begins on March 12, 2008, in New York City, where we meet our protagonist, Rob Hawkins (played by Michael Stuhlbarg), a young man who is preparing to leave for his job at a financial firm in Tokyo. However, before he can depart, he receives an unexpected phone call from his brother, Jason (played by T.J. Miller), who informs him that their father has died.

As Rob tries to make sense of the situation, we are introduced to other main characters: Marlena Heisencutter (played by Lizzy Caplan), a friend of Rob's who is also preparing for her own trip abroad; Matty Reynolds (played by Mike Vogel), a friend of Jason's who is trying to get in touch with his brother; and Hud (played by Adam Brody), a friend of the group who is initially hesitant to join them on their adventure.

The group decides to embark on a road trip from New York City to New Jersey, where they plan to meet up with Jason. However, as they drive through the city, they notice that something is amiss - buildings are damaged, cars are overturned, and there is a sense of chaos in the air.

As they continue their journey, they come across a massive monster, known as "Cloverfield," which is wreaking havoc on the city. The creature is enormous, with glowing red eyes and a powerful roar that can be heard for miles. The group soon realizes that Cloverfield is not just a mindless beast - it's a highly intelligent and destructive force that seems to be targeting specific locations.

As the group tries to escape the monster's path, they begin to uncover clues about its origins and motivations. They discover that Cloverfield is an extraterrestrial creature that has been awakened by human activity in the city. The creature is drawn to the sounds of human communication, which it uses to navigate and hunt its prey.

Throughout the film, the group faces numerous challenges as they try to survive the monster's attacks. Along the way, they also experience personal struggles and conflicts, including romantic tensions and family drama.

As the night wears on, the group finds themselves trapped in a deserted warehouse, where they are forced to confront Cloverfield head-on. In a tense and suspenseful climax, they manage to fend off the creature long enough for Rob's brother Jason to escape with his life.

The film ends with Rob, Marlena, Matty, and Hud watching as Jason drives away from the city, leaving behind the devastation and destruction caused by Cloverfield. As they reflect on their experience, we see a series of news reports and footage of the monster's rampage, which serves as a reminder that the world is not always a safe or predictable place.

Overall, Cloverfounder is a tense and thrilling horror film that explores themes of friendship, survival, and the human condition in the face of catastrophic events.

documents.title: Dan in Real Life
documents.tagline: Something's happening to Dan. It's confusing. It's awkward. It's family.
documents.overview: Advice columnist, Dan Burns is an expert on relationships, but somehow struggles to succeed as a brother, a son and a single parent to three precocious daughters. Things get even more complicated when Dan finds out that the woman he falls in love with is actually his brother's new girlfriend.
documents.plot:
Dan in Real Life is a 2007 American romantic comedy-drama film that explores the complexities of family relationships, love, and self-discovery. The movie delves into the theme of finding one's true identity amidst the chaos of family dynamics.

The story revolves around Dan Burns (played by Steve Carell), a widowed father who takes his three daughters on a family vacation to Santa Fe, New Mexico. As Dan navigates his relationships with his daughters and their mothers, he finds himself drawn to a free-spirited woman named Marie (played by Juliette Binoche) who is also traveling alone.

Through Dan's journey, the film highlights the importance of embracing one's true self and letting go of societal expectations. Dan's character is torn between his desire for stability and security, as well as his need to reconnect with his own desires and sense of purpose.

The movie also explores the theme of love in all its forms, including romantic love, familial love, and self-love. As Dan navigates his relationships with Marie and his daughters, he comes to realize that true love is not just about finding someone else, but also about learning to love oneself.

Ultimately, Dan in Real Life is a heartwarming film that celebrates the complexities of human relationships and the power of self-discovery. The movie's themes of identity, love, and acceptance make it a relatable and engaging watch for audiences.

documents.title: Coach Carter
documents.tagline: It begins on the street. It ends here.
documents.overview: Based on a true story, in which Richmond High School head basketball coach Ken Carter made headlines in 1999 for benching his undefeated team due to poor academic results.
documents.plot:
Coach Carter is a biographical sports drama film released in 2005, directed by Thomas Carter and starring Samuel L. Jackson as Ken Carter, a high school basketball coach.

The movie is based on the true story of Ken Carter, who coached the Richmond High School basketball team in Richmond, California, in 1999-2000. The film begins with Coach Carter, a former NBA player, taking over as the new head coach of the Richmond High School basketball team. He is determined to teach his players not only about basketball but also about life and responsibility.

Initially, the team struggles due to poor attendance, lack of motivation, and behavioral issues. Coach Carter sets out to change this by implementing a strict set of rules and expectations for his players. He requires them to maintain a minimum GPA, attend classes regularly, and participate in community service. The players are initially resistant to these new rules, but Coach Carter's firm but fair approach eventually starts to take effect.

As the season progresses, the team begins to improve on the court, winning several games and gaining confidence. However, off the court, the players continue to struggle with their personal lives, including poverty, family problems, and gang involvement. Coach Carter becomes a mentor and father figure to his players, helping them to overcome their challenges and find a better path in life.

One of the key players, Kenyon Stone (played by Rob Brown), is particularly struggling with his own demons. He comes from a troubled home and has been involved with gangs. Coach Carter takes Kenyon under his wing, teaching him about responsibility and self-discipline. Through their relationship, Coach Carter helps Kenyon to turn his life around, earning a college scholarship and eventually becoming a successful businessman.

As the season reaches its climax, the team faces off against their arch-rivals, and Coach Carter's players must come together to overcome their personal struggles and win the game. In a thrilling finale, the team emerges victorious, but more importantly, they have learned valuable lessons about teamwork, perseverance, and the importance of education.

The movie ends with Coach Carter reflecting on the season and the progress his players have made. He is proud of what he has accomplished, not just as a coach but also as a mentor and role model. The film concludes with a sense of hope and renewal, as the players look to the future, armed with the knowledge and skills they have gained under Coach Carter's guidance.

Overall, Coach Carter is an inspiring true story about the power of sports to transform lives and communities. The movie features outstanding performances from its cast, particularly Samuel L. Jackson as Coach Carter, who brings depth and nuance to his portrayal of a complex and dedicated coach.

documents.title: The Punisher
documents.tagline: There is no justice, there is only revenge.
documents.overview: When undercover FBI agent Frank Castle's wife and son are slaughtered, he becomes 'the Punisher' -- a ruthless vigilante willing to go to any length to avenge his family.
documents.plot:
The Punisher is a 2004 superhero film directed by Jonathan Hensleigh and starring Thomas Jane as Frank Castle, aka The Punisher.

The movie begins with Frank Castle, a former Marine, who witnesses his entire family being brutally murdered in front of him by a group of armed robbers. This traumatic event sets off a chain reaction that drives Frank to seek revenge against those responsible for the senseless violence and death he witnessed.

Frank's quest for vengeance leads him to become The Punisher, a vigilante determined to punish those who have escaped justice. He starts by targeting organized crime groups, particularly the Russian mafia, which is led by Kravinoff (John Malkovich). Frank's actions attract the attention of the police department and the FBI, who are initially unaware that he is a vigilante.

As The Punisher continues his crusade against organized crime, he becomes increasingly isolated from society. He adopts a new identity for himself, using a fake name and creating a persona that strikes fear into the hearts of those around him. Frank's actions also attract the attention of Elektra Natchios (Jennifer Garner), a skilled martial artist and assassin who is initially unaware of The Punisher's true identity.

Throughout the movie, Frank's character undergoes significant development as he grapples with his own morality and the consequences of his actions. He begins to question whether his quest for vengeance is truly just or if it has become an all-consuming obsession that is destroying him from within.

As The Punisher delves deeper into the world of organized crime, he discovers a sinister plot by Kravinoff to sell nuclear warheads on the black market. Frank must use his skills and resources to stop Kravinoff's operation and prevent a catastrophic disaster.

The movie culminates in an intense showdown between The Punisher and Kravinoff, with Frank ultimately emerging victorious but not without scars. In the aftermath of the battle, Elektra finally discovers The Punisher's true identity, and the two share a moment of mutual understanding and respect for each other's skills and motivations.

The Punisher ends on a somber note, with Frank reflecting on the cost of his actions and the toll they have taken on his life. He realizes that his quest for vengeance has become an all-consuming force that threatens to destroy him from within. The movie concludes with Frank walking away from the city, leaving behind the chaos and destruction he has caused in pursuit of justice.

Overall, The Punisher is a gritty and intense action film that explores themes of revenge, morality, and the blurred lines between good and evil.

documents.title: Airport '77
documents.tagline: Flight 23 has crashed in the Bermuda Triangle... passengers still alive, trapped underwater...
documents.overview: Flight 23 has crashed in the Bermuda Triangle after a hijacking gone wrong. Now the surviving passengers must brave panic, slow leaks, oxygen depletion, and more while attempting a daring plan, all while 200 feet underwater.
documents.plot:
Airport '77 is a disaster film directed by Jerry Jameson, released in 1977 by Universal Pictures. The movie takes place at Washington National Airport and revolves around a series of catastrophic events that unfold on a fateful day.

The story begins with the introduction of several characters, including Steve McCauley (Burt Reynolds), a former test pilot who has retired from flying due to a near-fatal accident. Steve is now working as an airport security inspector, tasked with ensuring the safety of air traffic at Washington National Airport.

As the day unfolds, a series of strange occurrences start to happen. A small plane carrying a group of passengers and crew crashes on the runway, causing a massive fire that blocks the entire airport. The authorities are initially unable to respond effectively due to the chaos caused by the crash, leading to further accidents and mishaps.

Meanwhile, Steve is dealing with his own personal demons, including a troubled relationship with his girlfriend, Elaine (Susan Blakely). As the day progresses, Steve becomes increasingly frustrated with the incompetence of the airport's management and the lack of preparedness for emergencies.

As the situation spirals out of control, Steve takes matters into his own hands, using his flying skills to rescue those trapped in the burning plane. He also teams up with a young air traffic controller, Mark (Jack Warden), who helps him navigate the chaos and coordinate the response efforts.

Throughout the movie, the tension builds as the characters face numerous challenges, including treacherous weather conditions, equipment failures, and human error. The film's climax features an intense sequence of events, including a dramatic rescue mission and a confrontation with the airport's corrupt management.

Ultimately, Steve emerges as a hero, having saved countless lives and brought order to the chaotic situation. As he reflects on the day's events, Steve comes to terms with his past mistakes and finds closure with Elaine.

Airport '77 is an action-packed disaster film that explores themes of personal responsibility, teamwork, and redemption. The movie features impressive aerial sequences, suspenseful plot twists, and a strong performance from Burt Reynolds as the protagonist. While some critics have panned the film's predictability and lack of originality, Airport '77 remains a beloved classic among fans of disaster movies and action films.

Overall, Airport '77 is an entertaining and thrilling ride that will keep you on the edge of your seat from start to finish. With its memorable characters, intense plot developments, and heart-pumping action sequences, this movie is sure to delight audiences who enjoy disaster films and adventure stories.

documents.title: Ruby & Quentin
documents.overview: After hiding his loot and getting thrown in jail, Ruby, a brooding outlaw encounters Quentin, a dim-witted and garrulous giant who befriends him. After Quentin botches a solo escape attempt, they make a break together. Unable to shake the clumsy Quentin Ruby is forced to take him along as he pursues his former partners in crime to avenge the death of the woman he loved and get to the money.
documents.plot:
Ruby & Quentin (French: Tais-toi!, "Shut up!") is a French crime comedy caper of 2003 directed by Francis Veber. Jean Reno plays Ruby, a taciturn gangster bent on revenge, and Gérard Depardieu plays Quentin, a dim-witted, endlessly talkative petty thief, with Richard Berry as the detective Vernet, André Dussollier as the prison psychiatrist, Jean-Pierre Malo as the crime boss Vogel and Leonor Varela in the dual role of Katia and Sandra.

Quentin bungles a hold-up at a currency exchange booth, asks the cashier for directions to the nearest bank and is arrested after ducking into a cinema showing Ice Age and settling down to enjoy the film. Ruby, meanwhile, worked for Vogel and had an affair with his boss's wife; after Vogel killed her, Ruby stole his loot in revenge and was caught hiding it. In prison he refuses to eat or speak, worrying the psychiatrist but failing to fool the investigating detective. Quentin, whose ceaseless chatter has driven every previous cellmate to violence, is placed in Ruby's cell as an experiment. He instantly adores his silent companion, whose distant gaze reminds him of the horses he tended as a stable boy.

Ruby fakes a suicide attempt to reach the prison infirmary, and Quentin copies him to end up in the next bed. Ruby bribes a nurse in Vogel's pay to help him escape, but Quentin has his own plan involving a drunken old friend who drives a crane, and the two end up on the run together. Ruby tries again and again to get rid of his clinging companion, but every attempt fails. Pursued by Vogel's bodyguards, they steal and lose a series of cars, break into the mansion of a tiny former jockey and end up in his wife's Chanel suits, and swap clothes with two bigots. Quentin snaps Ruby's dislocated shoulder back into place and keeps stealing police cars. In the derelict bistro in his home village, where Quentin dreams of opening a café, they meet a homeless woman who looks just like Vogel's dead wife; Ruby, smitten, gives her money and a fresh start in a hotel. The pair talk their way into Vogel's hideout, where a shoot-out leaves Vogel incapacitated and Quentin apparently dying. To his own surprise Ruby weeps for him, and Quentin tricks him into promising to open the bistro together once he recovers.

The film was released in French cinemas on 22 October 2003.

documents.title: Futurama: Bender's Big Score
documents.tagline: Just when you thought it was safe to watch something else!
documents.overview: The Planet Express crew return from cancellation, only to be robbed blind by hideous "sprunging" scam artists.  Things go from bad to worse when the scammers hack Bender, start traveling through time, and take Earth over entirely!  Will the crew be able to save the day, or will Bender's larcenous tendencies and their general incompetence doom them all?
