Over time the film gained a cult following, and critics praised its 1970s-style cinematography and Heard's performance.

documents.title: Spirit: Stallion of the Cimarron
documents.tagline: Leader. Hero. Legend.
documents.overview: As a wild stallion travels across the frontiers of the Old West, he befriends a young human and finds true love with a mare.
documents.plot:
Spirit: Stallion of the Cimarron is a 2002 American animated Western drama film produced by DreamWorks Pictures. The movie follows the journey of a wild mustang stallion named Spirit, who embarks on an epic quest to find his place in the world.

The film begins with Spirit (voiced by Matt Damon) as a young foal, born and raised in the Cimarron Valley. He is a spirited and adventurous horse, always eager to explore and discover new things. As he grows up, Spirit becomes increasingly restless, feeling confined by the limitations of his herd's routine.

One day, Spirit meets a beautiful mare named Rain (voiced by Gina Philips), who shares his sense of wanderlust. Together, they set out on an adventure across the American West, facing numerous challenges and dangers along the way. They encounter fierce storms, treacherous terrain, and hostile humans, but their bond grows stronger with each passing day.

As Spirit and Rain journey through the wilderness, they meet a wise old stallion named Thunder (voiced by Michael Jeter), who teaches them about the importance of freedom and self-discovery. However, their happiness is short-lived, as they are captured by a ruthless horse trader named Colonel Hart (voiced by James Cromwell) and his men.

Spirit is sold to a cavalry unit, where he meets a young soldier named Little Creek (voiced by Paul Williams), who befriends him and helps him escape. Together, they embark on a perilous journey back to the Cimarron Valley, facing numerous obstacles and dangers along the way.

As Spirit returns home, he is reunited with Rain, and together they face off against Colonel Hart in an epic showdown. With his newfound courage and determination, Spirit defeats the colonel and his men, securing his freedom and proving himself as a true leader among his herd.

Throughout the film, the animation is stunning, with beautifully rendered landscapes and characters that bring the American West to life. The voice cast delivers strong performances, bringing depth and emotion to their respective roles. The music, composed by Hans Zimmer and John Powell, is equally impressive, perfectly capturing the spirit (pun intended) of the wild mustang.

Overall, Spirit: Stallion of the Cimarron is a timeless tale of self-discovery, courage, and the power of the human (and equine) spirit. With its stunning animation, memorable characters, and epic storyline, it's no wonder this film has become a beloved classic among both children and adults alike.

documents.title: The Eye
documents.tagline: How can you believe your eyes when they're not yours?
documents.overview: Violinist Sydney Wells was accidentally blinded by her sister Helen when she was five years old. She submits to a cornea transplantation, and while recovering from the operation, she realizes that she is seeing dead people.
documents.plot:
The Eye is a psychological horror-thriller film that delves into the darker aspects of human nature and the blurred lines between reality and madness.

At its core, The Eye explores the theme of grief and loss, as the protagonist, Dr. Megan Hunt (played by Jessica Alba), struggles to cope with the sudden death of her sister. Her newfound ability to see ghosts through her corneal transplant serves as a metaphor for her emotional state, allowing her to confront the pain and trauma she's been trying to suppress.

The film also delves into the idea of isolation and loneliness, as Megan's condition forces her to navigate a world that's increasingly unfamiliar and frightening. Her relationships with others become strained, and she begins to question her own sanity, highlighting the devastating consequences of losing one's sense of connection and belonging.

Furthermore, The Eye touches on the theme of guilt and responsibility, as Megan grapples with the moral implications of her newfound power. She becomes obsessed with uncovering the truth behind a series of gruesome murders, which serves as a catalyst for her own descent into madness.

Throughout the film, the director, David Moreau, masterfully weaves together these themes to create a sense of tension and unease, leaving the audience questioning what's real and what's just Megan's paranoia. The Eye is a thought-provoking exploration of the human psyche, one that delves into the darker corners of the mind and emerges with a haunting, unsettling atmosphere.

documents.title: Slither
documents.tagline: Horror has a new face.
documents.overview: A small town is taken over by an alien plague, turning residents into zombies and all forms of mutant monsters.
documents.plot:
Slither is a 2006 American horror-comedy film directed by James Gunn and written by Gunn and Phil Lord. The movie stars Nathan Fillion, Elizabeth Banks, Michael Rooker, and Jill Witcher.

The story begins with a small town called Middleton, where a group of friends, including Jeff (Nathan Fillion), a high school teacher, and his girlfriend Starla (Elizabeth Banks), are preparing for the annual Harvest Festival. The festival is a celebration of the town's agricultural heritage, but it also serves as an opportunity for the townspeople to let loose and have fun.

However, things take a dark turn when a mysterious alien parasite infects the town's residents, turning them into zombie-like creatures with a strong desire to eat human flesh. The parasite, which is about 10 feet long, has been introduced to Earth by a group of aliens who crash-landed in the nearby woods.

As the infection spreads rapidly throughout the town, Jeff and his friends must band together to survive and find a way to stop the parasite before it's too late. Along the way, they encounter a variety of bizarre and terrifying creatures, including giant spiders, mutated animals, and even a zombie-like version of Starla.

One of the most interesting aspects of Slither is its exploration of small-town America and the ways in which people can become complacent and accepting of their surroundings. The town of Middleton is portrayed as a place where everyone knows each other's business, but also where secrets and lies are often swept under the rug.

As the story progresses, Jeff and his friends discover that the parasite has a unique ability to manipulate its hosts' minds, making them more aggressive and violent. They also learn that the aliens who introduced the parasite were not just random visitors, but rather part of an experiment designed to create a new breed of super-soldiers.

In the end, Jeff and his friends must use their wits and whatever resources they can find to stop the parasite and save the town. Along the way, they encounter some unexpected allies, including a group of survivors from a nearby town who have been fighting against the parasites for weeks.

The movie's climax features an epic battle between Jeff and the leader of the zombie-like creatures, a giant spider-like creature that has become the parasite's host. In the end, Jeff emerges victorious, but not before realizing that the parasite has left him with a strange and unsettling connection to the alien entity.

Overall, Slither is a fun and entertaining horror-comedy that explores themes of small-town America, paranoia, and the dangers of complacency. With its unique blend of humor, action, and horror elements, it's a must-see for fans of the genre.

documents.title: Eight Below
documents.tagline: The Most Amazing Story Of Survival, Friendship, And Adventure Ever Told.
documents.overview: In the Antarctic, after an expedition with Dr. Davis McClaren, the sled dog trainer Jerry Shepherd has to leave the polar base with his colleagues due to the proximity of a heavy snow storm. He ties his dogs to be rescued after, but the mission is called-off and the dogs are left alone at their own fortune. For six months, Jerry tries to find a sponsor for a rescue mission.
documents.plot:
Eight Below is a heartwarming drama film released in 2006, directed by Frank Marshall and produced by Walt Disney Pictures. The movie is based on a true story and tells the tale of a team of sled dogs that were left behind by their owner, Dr. Davis (Paul Walker), during a research expedition in Antarctica.

The film begins with Dr. Davis, a renowned scientist, leading an expedition to Antarctica to study the effects of climate change on the continent's wildlife. He is accompanied by his loyal team of sled dogs, including eight Alaskan Malamutes, which are trained to pull a specially designed sled. The dogs are an integral part of the research team and play a crucial role in collecting data and conducting experiments.

As the expedition progresses, Dr. Davis becomes increasingly obsessed with his work, leaving his team behind for extended periods. His loyal companion, Jerry (played by Luke Wilson), is left to care for the dogs while Dr. Davis is away. However, when Dr. Davis returns from a particularly long absence, he discovers that Jerry has abandoned the dogs in an attempt to save them from starvation.

The eight sled dogs are now left alone and struggling to survive in the harsh Antarctic environment. The team's morale is low, and it seems unlikely that they will be able to make it through the winter without human intervention. However, as the days turn into weeks, the dogs begin to adapt to their new circumstances, using their natural instincts to hunt for food and stay warm.

As the months pass, the dogs face numerous challenges, including treacherous terrain, blizzards, and the constant threat of starvation. Despite these obstacles, they remain loyal to each other and work together to survive. The film's climax features an incredible rescue mission, where a team of scientists and sled dog handlers from New Zealand arrive in Antarctica to retrieve the dogs.

The movie ends on a heartwarming note, as Dr. Davis is reunited with his beloved sled dogs, who have been through unimaginable hardships but remain loyal and faithful companions. The film's conclusion serves as a testament to the incredible bond between humans and animals, highlighting the importance of compassion, loyalty, and perseverance in the face of adversity.

Throughout the film, the cinematography is breathtaking, capturing the stunning beauty of Antarctica's landscapes and the resilience of its inhabitants. The performances by the human cast are also noteworthy, particularly Paul Walker's portrayal of Dr. Davis, which conveys a sense of vulnerability and dedication to his work.

Overall, Eight Below is a powerful and emotional film that celebrates the human-animal bond and the incredible adaptability of sled dogs in extreme environments.

documents.title: Trapped
documents.tagline: It was the perfect plan until she refused to be the perfect victim!
documents.overview: When their daughter is kidnapped by experienced nappers, the Jennings turn the tables on this seemingly foolproof plan.
documents.plot:
Trapped is a 2002 American crime thriller film directed by Luis Mandoki and based on Greg Iles's novel 24 Hours. Charlize Theron and Stuart Townsend star as the parents of a kidnapped girl, played by Dakota Fanning, with Kevin Bacon and Courtney Love as the kidnappers and Pruitt Taylor Vince as their accomplice. It was filmed in British Columbia in the spring of 2001 and released by Columbia Pictures on September 20, 2002.

Dr. Will Jennings, a successful physician, has just patented a new anesthetic and travels to Seattle to present it at a medical conference. At his hotel, a woman named Cheryl introduces herself as an admirer, then pulls a gun and forces him into his room. At the same moment, her husband, Joe, breaks into the Jennings family's luxurious home outside Portland, Oregon, and takes Will's wife, Karen, hostage, while Joe's cousin Marvin drives their young daughter, Abby, to a remote cabin. The couple demands a ransom, keeping the parents apart and under watch.

The plan begins to unravel when Abby, who suffers from severe asthma, has an attack without her inhaler, and Joe is forced to take a blindfolded Karen to the cabin to treat her. Back at the house, Karen fights back against Joe, wounding him with a hidden scalpel and briefly speaking with Abby by phone before Joe regains control. In Seattle, Will uses his medical knowledge to inject Cheryl with a paralyzing drug, bringing her close to death before reviving her. Shaken, Cheryl reveals that this abduction is personal: Joe blames Will for the death of their own daughter, who died during surgery on which Will assisted. Will explains that he was wrongly blamed by the head surgeon, and Cheryl begins to turn against the plan, especially after learning in a heated phone call that Joe intends to keep Abby and raise her as his own.

Accompanied by police, Will collects the ransom, then flies with Cheryl toward Portland in a seaplane as Joe drives north on Interstate 5 with Karen, followed by Marvin and Abby. When Karen attacks Joe and forces the car off the road, Will spots it from the air and lands the seaplane on the highway, causing a massive pileup. Marvin lets Abby go, and after a struggle between the two men, Karen shoots Joe dead. As police and FBI agents arrive, Karen treats Abby's asthma, and the family is reunited as Cheryl is arrested.

Trapped was a critical and commercial failure. Rotten Tomatoes reported 17% approval, and the film grossed about $13.4 million worldwide.

documents.title: Serpico
documents.tagline: Many of his fellow officers considered him the most dangerous man alive - An honest cop.
documents.overview: Frank Serpico is an idealistic New York City cop who refuses to take bribes, unlike the rest of the force. His actions get Frank shunned by the other officers, and often placed in dangerous situations by his partners. When his superiors ignore Frank's accusations of corruption, he decides to go public with the allegations. Although this causes the Knapp Commission to investigate his claims, Frank has also placed a target on himself.
documents.plot:
Serpico is a powerful and thought-provoking film that explores the darker aspects of human nature and the corrupting influence of power. The movie delves into the theme of moral integrity, as embodied by the titular character Frank Serpico, a honest and principled police officer who refuses to compromise his values in the face of overwhelming pressure from his colleagues and superiors.

The film also examines the consequences of unchecked corruption and the devastating impact it can have on individuals and society as a whole. The portrayal of the NYPD's organized crime syndicate and its tentacles reaching into every level of the department serves as a scathing critique of institutionalized corruption and the ways in which it can lead to moral decay.

Furthermore, Serpico touches on the theme of individualism versus conformity, highlighting the tension between those who dare to challenge the status quo and those who are willing to sacrifice their principles for the sake of advancement or security. The character of Frank Serpico stands as a beacon of resistance against the forces of corruption, inspiring others to follow in his footsteps and fight for what is right.

Ultimately, Serpico presents a searing indictment of systemic corruption and the dangers of unchecked power, while also celebrating the courage and conviction of individuals who refuse to be silenced or intimidated by those in positions of authority.

documents.title: The Cave
documents.tagline: There are places man was never meant to go
documents.overview: After a group of biologists discovers a huge network of unexplored caves in Romania and, believing it to be an undisturbed eco-system that has produced a new species, they hire the best American team of underwater cave explorers in the world. While exploring deeper into the underwater caves, a rockslide blocks their exit, and they soon discover a larger carnivorous creature has added them to its food chain.
documents.plot: After a group of biologists discovers a huge network of unexplored caves in Romania and, believing it to be an undisturbed eco-system that has produced a new species, they hire the best American team of underwater cave explorers in the world. While exploring deeper into the underwater caves, a rockslide blocks their exit, and they soon discover a larger carnivorous creature has added them to its food chain.

documents.title: The Family Stone
documents.tagline: Feel The Love
documents.overview: An uptight, conservative businesswoman accompanies her boyfriend to his eccentric and outgoing family's annual Christmas celebration and finds that she's a fish out of water in their free-spirited way of life.
documents.plot: An uptight, conservative businesswoman accompanies her boyfriend to his eccentric and outgoing family's annual Christmas celebration and finds that she's a fish out of water in their free-spirited way of life.

documents.title: Tristan & Isolde
documents.tagline: Fighting countries can still love...
documents.overview: An affair between the second in line to Britain's throne and the princess of the feuding Irish spells doom for the young lovers.
documents.plot:
Tristan & Isolde is a 2006 epic romance film that delves into the complexities of love, loyalty, and the destructive nature of unchecked passion. The movie tells the story of two lovers, Tristan and Isolde, who are bound together by fate but ultimately torn apart by their own desires.

At its core, the film explores the theme of all-consuming love, which can both elevate and destroy those who experience it. Tristan and Isolde's relationship is marked by a deep emotional connection that transcends social boundaries and familial obligations. However, this intense passion also leads to a downward spiral of obsession, jealousy, and ultimately, tragedy.

The movie also examines the consequences of unchecked emotions and the destructive power of unrequited love. Tristan's unwavering devotion to Isolde drives him to make choices that ultimately lead to his downfall, while Isolde's own desires and sense of identity become increasingly entwined with her relationship with Tristan.

Furthermore, the film touches on the theme of loyalty and duty, particularly in the context of chivalry and honor. The characters' adherence to traditional codes of conduct often serves as a catalyst for their conflicts, highlighting the tension between personal desire and societal expectations.

Ultimately, Tristan & Isolde is a poignant exploration of the human experience, revealing the devastating consequences of allowing passion to consume us.
production_companies: QI Quality International GmbH Co. KG

documents.title: DOA: Dead or Alive
documents.tagline: They're the ultimate fighters. They've got the looks. They've got the moves, and the men fall at their feet.
documents.overview: Four beautiful rivals at an invitation-only martial-arts tournament join forces against a sinister threat. Princess Kasumi is an aristocratic warrior trained by martial-arts masters. Tina Armstrong is a wrestling superstar. Helena Douglas is an athlete with a tragic past. Christie Allen earns her keep as a thief and an assassin-for-hire.
documents.plot:
DOA: Dead or Alive is a 2006 martial arts action film directed by Corey Yuen and written by David Hayter, based on the popular video game series of the same name. The movie stars Nina Dobrev, Daniel Henney, and Jaime King.

The story begins with Casey (Nina Dobrev), an American woman who wins a trip to Japan as part of a reality TV show called "Dead or Alive." The show is hosted by Ryu Hayabusa (Daniel Henney), a Japanese martial artist, and his team. Casey's goal is to win the grand prize of $1 million.

Upon arrival in Japan, Casey meets Ryu and his teammates, including Leon (Tai Chi Master) and Jann Lee (Chris Klein). As the competition progresses, Casey finds herself caught up in a web of intrigue and deception, as she discovers that the show is not what it seems. The contestants are actually being forced to fight each other, with the last person standing winning the grand prize.

As Casey navigates the treacherous world of the Dead or Alive tournament, she must also contend with her own personal demons. Her sister, Samantha (Jaime King), was killed in a brutal attack by Jann Lee, and Casey is determined to avenge her death.

Throughout the movie, Casey forms alliances and friendships with Ryu and Leon, who become her allies in the fight against Jann Lee. The action sequences are intense and well-choreographed, showcasing the martial arts skills of the cast.

As the tournament reaches its climax, Casey faces off against Jann Lee in an epic battle. In the end, Casey emerges victorious, but not without scars. She wins the grand prize, but more importantly, she finds a sense of closure and revenge for her sister's death.

The movie received mixed reviews from critics, with some praising the action sequences and performances, while others found the plot to be predictable and formulaic. Despite this, DOA: Dead or Alive remains a fun and entertaining martial arts film, with plenty of twists and turns to keep viewers on the edge of their seats.

Overall, DOA: Dead or Alive is a thrilling and action-packed movie that explores themes of revenge, redemption, and self-discovery. With its talented cast and impressive fight choreography, it's a must-see for fans of martial arts films.

documents.title: Waking Life
documents.tagline: Dreams. What are they? An escape from reality or reality itself?
documents.overview: Waking Life is about a young man in a persistent lucid dream-like state. The film follows its protagonist as he initially observes and later participates in philosophical discussions that weave together issues like reality, free will, our relationships with others, and the meaning of life.
documents.plot:
Waking Life is a thought-provoking animated film that delves into the complexities of human existence, free will, and the nature of reality. The movie's narrative is presented in a non-linear fashion, featuring a young man who finds himself in a series of surreal conversations with various characters, each representing different philosophical perspectives.

At its core, Waking Life explores the idea of existentialism, questioning the notion of a predetermined path in life and the concept of free will. The film's protagonist is presented with a series of choices that challenge his perception of reality, forcing him to confront the possibility that his decisions may be influenced by external factors beyond his control.

The movie also touches on the theme of nihilism, as some characters express a sense of hopelessness and despair in the face of an seemingly meaningless world. However, this bleakness is balanced by moments of introspection, self-discovery, and a deep appreciation for the complexities of human experience.

Furthermore, Waking Life critiques the notion of a singular, objective truth, instead suggesting that reality is subjective and multifaceted. The film's use of multiple perspectives and conflicting viewpoints serves to underscore this idea, leaving the viewer to ponder the nature of reality and their place within it.

Ultimately, Waking Life presents a nuanced and thought-provoking exploration of the human condition, inviting viewers to consider the complexities of existence and the choices that shape our lives.

documents.title: The Four Feathers
documents.tagline: Freedom. Country. Honor. Passion. To save his best friend, one man must risk everything he loves.
documents.overview: The story, set in 1885, follows a British officer (Heath Ledger) who resigns his post when he learns of his regiment's plan to ship out to the Sudan for the conflict with the Mahdi. His friends and fiancée send him four white feathers which symbolize cowardice. To redeem his honor he disguises himself as an Arab and secretly saves the lives of those who branded him a coward.
documents.plot:
The Four Feathers is an epic war drama of 2002 directed by Shekhar Kapur, the latest of many screen adaptations of A. E. W. Mason's novel of 1902, here set during the British expedition to relieve General Gordon in the Sudan in 1884-85. Heath Ledger stars as Harry Faversham, with Wes Bentley as his friend Jack Durrance, Kate Hudson as his fiancée Ethne Eustace, Djimon Hounsou as the warrior Abou Fatma, Michael Sheen as William Trench and Kris Marshall as Edward Castleton.

Harry, a young British officer, celebrates his engagement to Ethne at a ball just as his regiment is ordered to the Sudan to rescue Gordon. Doubting the war, he resigns his commission. His father disowns him, and three of his friends and Ethne each send him a white feather, the mark of cowardice; Ethne ends their engagement. When Harry hears that Jack and his old regiment are heading into danger, he travels alone to the Sudan, disguises himself as an Arab and allies with Abou Fatma, a mercenary. Finding the fort at Abu Klea overrun by the Mahdi's forces, he sends Abou to warn the British, but they dismiss him as a spy and flog him.

The regiment is ambushed. The British square repels the first assault, but cavalry they take for reinforcements turn out to be Sudanese fighters in captured British uniforms, among them the disguised Harry. In the chaos, Castleton is killed by his own side's volleys and Jack is blinded when his rifle misfires. Harry rescues Jack and nurses him without revealing his identity, finding Ethne's letters to his friend. Back in England, Jack proposes to Ethne. Learning from Abou that Trench is held in the notorious prison at Omdurman, Harry lets himself be captured to free him. Starved and worked to exhaustion, the two despair until Abou smuggles in a poison that lets them feign death, and after killing the guards who follow them, Harry brings Trench home. Ethne takes back her feather and Harry's father welcomes him home; when the blind Jack touches Harry's face and recognises his rescuer, he releases Ethne, and Harry and Ethne are engaged once more.

Released by Paramount in September 2002, the film earned $29.8 million worldwide, short of its $35 million budget. Critics admired its visuals but not its storytelling, giving it 42% on Rotten Tomatoes.

documents.title: The Craft
documents.tagline: Welcome to the witching hour.
documents.overview: A Catholic school newcomer falls in with a clique of teen witches who wield their powers against all who dare to cross them -- be they teachers, rivals or meddlesome parents.
documents.plot:
The Craft is a supernatural teen thriller film released in 1996, directed by Andrew Fleming and produced by Columbia Pictures.

The story revolves around four high school outcasts: Sarah Bailey (Robin Tunney), Bonnie Bennett (Neve Campbell), Rochelle Zimmerman (Rachel True), and Nancy Downs (Fairuza Balk). The movie begins with the introduction of these four girls, who are all struggling to find their place in their respective lives. Sarah is a new student at the school, having moved from California to Massachusetts after her mother's death. Bonnie is a popular cheerleader who appears to have it all together but is secretly unhappy and unfulfilled. Rochelle is an African American girl who is ostracized by her peers due to her dark skin and cultural differences. Nancy is a rebellious and eccentric outcast who has a fascination with the occult.

The four girls meet at a local occult shop, where they discover a book of spells written in blood. Intrigued, they decide to experiment with magic together, using the book as their guide. As they delve deeper into the world of witchcraft, they begin to experience strange and unexplained occurrences that seem to be connected to their newfound powers.

As the girls' magical abilities grow stronger, so does their bond and sense of empowerment. They start to use their powers to manipulate those around them, including Bonnie's boyfriend, who becomes increasingly possessive and controlling. However, Nancy's obsession with magic begins to take a darker turn, and she starts to use her powers for personal gain.

The plot takes a dramatic turn when Nancy's behavior becomes more erratic and sinister. She begins to use her powers to manipulate and control the other girls, including Sarah, who is increasingly drawn into Nancy's world of darkness. As tensions rise, the girls' relationships with each other begin to fray, and they start to realize that their newfound powers come with a terrible cost.

In the climactic final act, the girls must confront the consequences of their actions and work together to break free from Nancy's control. In a shocking twist, it is revealed that Nancy has been using her powers to manipulate Sarah, who had unknowingly become possessed by an evil entity. The girls are able to perform a ritual to banish the entity and restore balance to their lives.

The Craft explores themes of female empowerment, friendship, and the dangers of playing with forces beyond one's control. The movie features a strong ensemble cast, with standout performances from Robin Tunney and Fairuza Balk. While some critics have accused the film of perpetuating negative stereotypes about witches and feminism, others have praised its portrayal of complex and multidimensional female characters.

Overall, The Craft is a cult classic that has become synonymous with '90s teen cinema. Its blend of supernatural thrills, coming-of-age drama, and feminist themes continues to captivate audiences to this day.

documents.title: Screamers
documents.tagline: The last scream you hear will be your own.
documents.overview: SIRIUS 6B, Year 2078. On a distant mining planet ravaged by a decade of war, scientists have created the perfect weapon: a blade-wielding, self-replicating race of killing devices known as Screamers designed for one purpose only -- to hunt down and destroy all enemy life forms.
documents.plot: SIRIUS 6B, Year 2078. On a distant mining planet ravaged by a decade of war, scientists have created the perfect weapon: a blade-wielding, self-replicating race of killing devices known as Screamers designed for one purpose only -- to hunt down and destroy all enemy life forms.

documents.title: Buffalo Soldiers
documents.tagline: War is hell... but peace is f*#!%!! boring.
documents.overview: A criminal subculture operates among U.S. soldiers stationed in West Germany just before the fall of the Berlin wall.
documents.plot:
Buffalo Soldiers is a 2002 American drama film directed by Gregor Jordan. The movie explores the complex and often fraught relationship between African-American soldiers from the United States and their Mexican counterparts during the early 20th century.

At its core, Buffalo Soldiers delves into themes of racism, prejudice, and cultural clashes. The story is set against the backdrop of a tumultuous period in American history, where racial tensions were running high, both within the US military and between the US and Mexico. The film sheds light on the often-overlooked experiences of African-American soldiers who served alongside their Mexican counterparts, highlighting the difficulties they faced due to racism and xenophobia.

The movie also touches upon themes of identity, loyalty, and belonging. As the characters navigate their respective cultures and allegiances, they are forced to confront their own sense of self and where they belong in the world. The film's portrayal of these struggles is nuanced and thought-provoking, inviting viewers to consider the complexities of cultural identity and the human experience.

Furthermore, Buffalo Soldiers explores the theme of camaraderie and brotherhood among soldiers from different backgrounds, who are united by their shared experiences and challenges. Despite the tensions and conflicts that arise, the film suggests that these bonds can be powerful and transformative, allowing individuals to find a sense of belonging and purpose in the midst of adversity.

Overall, Buffalo Soldiers is a thought-provoking drama that sheds light on a lesser-known chapter in American history, while also exploring universal themes of identity, loyalty, and human connection.

documents.title: Broken Arrow
documents.tagline: Prepare to Go Ballistic.
documents.overview: When rogue stealth-fighter pilot Vic Deakins deliberately drops off the radar while on maneuvers, the Air Force ends up with two stolen nuclear warheads -- and Deakins's co-pilot, Riley Hale, is the military's only hope for getting them back. Traversing the deserted canyons of Utah, Hale teams with park ranger Terry Carmichael to put Deakins back in his box.
documents.plot:
Broken Arrow is a 1996 American action thriller film directed by John Woo and starring John Travolta, Christian Slater, and Sandra Bullock.

The movie begins with Colonel Mitchell "Mitch" Gary (John Travolta) and Captain Riley Hale (Christian Slater), two top-ranking pilots in the United States Air Force. They are part of an elite unit known as the 366th Tactical Fighter Wing, stationed at Edwards Air Force Base in California. The two men have a long-standing rivalry, with Mitch being the more experienced and respected pilot.

The story takes a dramatic turn when Mitch is shot down by his own wingman, Riley Hale, during a training exercise gone wrong. As Mitch lies dying, he reveals that he has been working on a top-secret project codenamed "Broken Arrow," which involves developing a new, highly advanced missile system capable of delivering nuclear warheads.

Before he dies, Mitch entrusts Riley with the location of the Broken Arrow facility and warns him about the dangers of the project. Unbeknownst to Riley, his brother, Sean (played by Brendan Fraser), is also involved in the project as a scientist.

As Riley tries to make sense of the situation, he discovers that his brother has been working on the Broken Arrow system with Mitch's help. However, their efforts have attracted unwanted attention from rogue elements within the government and military, who seek to exploit the technology for their own gain.

Riley soon finds himself in a cat-and-mouse game with a group of ruthless agents led by Colonel Frank Adams (played by Gary Busey). As he tries to protect his brother and prevent the Broken Arrow system from falling into the wrong hands, Riley must also confront his own demons and work to redeem himself in the eyes of his superiors.

Throughout the film, Woo's signature style is on full display, with rapid-fire action sequences, stunning aerial stunts, and a healthy dose of humor. The chemistry between Travolta and Slater is undeniable, and their rivalry adds an extra layer of tension to the story.

As the stakes grow higher, Riley must use all his skills and resources to outwit his enemies and prevent a catastrophic disaster. In the end, he succeeds in destroying the Broken Arrow facility and preventing the misuse of the technology.

The film concludes with Riley reflecting on the events that transpired and the lessons he learned about loyalty, duty, and redemption. The final shot is of the two brothers, Sean and Riley, reunited and at peace, as the camera pans out to reveal the vast expanse of the American desert landscape.

Overall, Broken Arrow is a thrilling action movie with a strong cast, clever plot twists, and impressive aerial sequences. While it may not be Woo's most critically acclaimed film, it remains a beloved classic among fans of the genre.

documents.title: S.W.A.T.
documents.tagline: You're either S.W.A.T. or you're not.
documents.overview: Hondo Harrelson recruits Jim Street to join an elite unit of the Los Angeles Police Department. Together they seek out more members, including tough Deke Kay and single mom Chris Sanchez. The team's first big assignment is to escort crime boss Alex Montel to prison. It seems routine, but when Montel offers a huge reward to anyone who can break him free, criminals of various stripes step up for the prize.
documents.plot:
S.W.A.T. is a 2003 American action film directed by Tony Scott, starring Keanu Reeves, Samuel L. Jackson, and Lindsay Lohan.

The movie begins with the introduction of Chris Sanders (Keanu Reeves), a former Marine who joins the Los Angeles Police Department's Special Weapons and Tactics team, also known as S.W.A.T. The team is led by Lieutenant Dan 'Hondo' Harrelson (Samuel L. Jackson), a seasoned veteran with a no-nonsense attitude.

The story takes a turn when Chris is paired with rookie officer Trudy Shaw (Lindsay Lohan) and the two begin to develop feelings for each other. However, their budding relationship is put to the test as they face various challenges on the job.

One of the main plot points revolves around a wealthy businessman named Robert Hawkins (Owen Wilson), who has been kidnapped by a group of terrorists led by Captain Dan 'Mac' MacDougall (Robert Patrick). The team must navigate through the city's streets and buildings to rescue Hawkins, while also dealing with their own personal demons.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Hawkins is not just any ordinary hostage. He possesses information about a deadly virus that could potentially wipe out millions of people. The terrorists plan to use this information to hold the world hostage and demand a massive ransom in exchange for Hawkins' safe return.

The S.W.A.T. team must work together to stop the terrorists and prevent the spread of the virus. Along the way, they encounter various obstacles, including treacherous terrain, rival law enforcement agencies, and personal conflicts within the team.

As the stakes grow higher, Chris and Trudy find themselves in a cat-and-mouse game with Mac and his accomplices. The action unfolds at a breakneck pace, with intense shootouts, car chases, and hand-to-hand combat sequences.

In the end, the S.W.A.T. team manages to rescue Hawkins and prevent the virus from being released. However, not before several characters meet their demise, including Mac, who sacrifices himself to save his teammates.

The movie concludes with Chris and Trudy sharing a moment of triumph and intimacy, as they reflect on the events that have transpired. The film ends on a hopeful note, with the S.W.A.T. team standing together, ready to face whatever challenges come their way next.

Overall, S.W.A.T. is an action-packed thrill ride that explores themes of loyalty, duty, and redemption. While it received mixed reviews from critics at the time of its release, the film has since developed a cult following and remains a beloved entry in the action genre.

documents.title: My Mom's New Boyfriend
documents.tagline: His mom is dating his suspect. Let the surveillance begin.
documents.overview: Henry Durand is a young federal agent who is given a difficult assignment: spy on his mother and her boyfriend who is suspected of leading a gang of art thieves.
documents.plot: After several years away, FBI agent Henry Durand returns to find his mother, Marty, a much different person: Having long mourned for Henry's father, she is now embracing single life. One day, while Marty, Henry and his new fiancée, Emily, are out for a walk, they meet Tommy, a mysterious stranger with whom Marty then becomes involved. However, through his FBI contacts, Henry learns that Tommy is suspected of being an art thief. As a young federal agent, Henry is given a difficult assignment: spy on his mother and her boyfriend who is suspected of leading a gang of art thieves.
production_companies: Equity Pictures Medienfonds GmbH & Co. KG

documents.title: Blue Crush
documents.tagline: Three Friends, One Passion, No Limits.
documents.overview: Nothing gets between Anne Marie and her board. Living in a beach shack with three roommates, she is up before dawn every morning to conquer the waves and count the days until the Pipe Masters competition. Having transplanted herself to Hawaii with no one's blessing but her own, Anne Marie finds all she needs in the adrenaline-charged surf scene - until pro quarterback Matt Tollman comes along...
documents.plot:
Blue Crush is an iconic 2002 film that explores several profound themes. At its core, it's a story about self-discovery and empowerment, particularly for women. The protagonist, Anne Marie Chadwick, played by Kate Bosworth, is a young woman who finds her identity through surfing, which becomes a symbol of her independence and freedom.

The movie delves into the idea of female empowerment, as Anne Marie navigates her relationships, career, and personal growth. Her journey is marked by struggles with self-doubt, fear, and vulnerability, but ultimately, she emerges stronger and more confident. The film's portrayal of women in male-dominated sports and industries serves as a powerful statement about the importance of equality and opportunities for all.

Moreover, Blue Crush touches on themes of identity, community, and belonging. Anne Marie finds her tribe among fellow surfers, who accept her for who she is and support her passions. This sense of belonging is crucial to her growth and development, as she learns to balance her individuality with the need for connection and acceptance.

The movie also explores the tension between nature and human endeavor, highlighting the beauty and power of the ocean while acknowledging the impact of human activity on the environment. Through Anne Marie's experiences, the film conveys a sense of respect and reverence for the natural world, emphasizing the importance of preserving it for future generations.

Ultimately, Blue Crush is a cinematic representation of the transformative power of passion, perseverance, and self-discovery. The film's themes continue to resonate with audiences today, inspiring viewers to pursue their dreams and find their own path to empowerment.

documents.title: Eraser
documents.tagline: He will erase your past to protect your future.
documents.overview: U.S. Marshall John Kruger erases the identities of people enrolled in the Witness Protection Program. His current assignment is to protect Lee Cullen, who's uncovered evidence that the weapons manufacturer she works for has been selling to terrorist groups. When Kruger discovers that there's a corrupt agent within the program, he must guard his own life while trying to protect Lee's.
documents.plot: Eraser, an elite federal marshal who "erases" the pasts of jeopardized informers and relocates them into safe anonymity, must protect a moving target who stands to uncover a conspiracy that could shift the balance of power in the world forever.

documents.title: Brick
documents.tagline: A detective story.
documents.overview: A teenage loner pushes his way into the underworld of a high school crime ring to investigate the disappearance of his ex-girlfriend.
documents.plot:
Brick is a 2006 neo-noir mystery film that delves into the complexities of adolescent angst, identity, and the blurred lines between reality and fantasy.

The movie follows Brendan Frye, a high school student who becomes embroiled in a murder investigation, navigating a complex web of relationships, rivalries, and unrequited love. As he digs deeper into the mystery, Brendan's perceptions of himself and those around him become increasingly distorted, leading to a thrilling and introspective exploration of his own psyche.

At its core, Brick is a film about the fragility of adolescence, where the lines between truth and fiction are constantly shifting. The movie's protagonist, Brendan, is a quintessential teenager struggling to find his place in the world, grappling with feelings of alienation, insecurity, and desire. His investigation into the murder serves as a metaphor for his own journey of self-discovery, as he grapples with the complexities of relationships, loyalty, and the search for meaning.

Through Brendan's character, the film explores themes of toxic masculinity, social hierarchy, and the performative nature of identity. The movie's use of cinematic tropes, such as the "whodunit" mystery, serves to underscore the fragility of reality in adolescence, where the stakes are high and the consequences of failure can be devastating.

Ultimately, Brick is a thought-provoking and haunting film that captures the essence of adolescent angst, exploring the complexities of identity, relationships, and the search for meaning in a world that often seems overwhelming and unforgiving.

documents.title: Death to Smoochy
documents.tagline: Get ready for an unexpected hit.
documents.overview: Tells the story of Rainbow Randolph, the corrupt, costumed star of a popular children's TV show, who is fired over a bribery scandal and replaced by squeaky-clean Smoochy, a puffy fuscia rhinoceros. As Smoochy catapults to fame - scoring hit ratings and the affections of a network executive - Randolph makes the unsuspecting rhino the target of his numerous outrageous attempts to exact revenge and reclaim his status as America's sweetheart.
documents.plot: Tells the story of Rainbow Randolph, the corrupt, costumed star of a popular children's TV show, who is fired over a bribery scandal and replaced by squeaky-clean Smoochy, a puffy fuchsia rhinoceros. As Smoochy catapults to fame - scoring hit ratings and the affections of a network executive - Randolph makes the unsuspecting rhino the target of his numerous outrageous attempts to exact revenge and reclaim his status as America's sweetheart.

documents.title: Femme Fatale
documents.tagline: Nothing is more desirable or more deadly than a woman with a secret.
documents.overview: A $10-million diamond rip-off, a stolen identity, a new life married to a diplomat. Laure Ash has risked big, won big. But then a tabloid shutterbug snaps her picture in Paris, and suddenly, enemies from Laure's secret past know who and where she is. And they all want their share of the diamond heist. Or her life. Or both.
documents.plot:
Femme Fatale is a 2002 neo-noir erotic thriller written and directed by Brian De Palma, starring Rebecca Romijn as the thief Laure Ash and Antonio Banderas as Nicolas Bardo, a Spanish paparazzo. The film is built around De Palma's signature visual style and a dreamlike structure, with an elaborate heist sequence set at the Cannes festival.

The story opens during the Cannes Film Festival, where Laure, a mercenary thief, is part of a team attempting to steal diamonds worn as part of a gold costume by a model attending a premiere. Laure seduces the model to get hold of the jewels while her accomplices provide support, but the heist goes wrong and Laure double-crosses her partners, escaping to Paris with the diamonds. There she is mistaken for Lily, a woman who has recently disappeared and who closely resembles her. When Laure witnesses the real Lily take her own life, she assumes her identity and leaves for the United States.

Seven years later, Laure returns to Paris as the wife of Bruce Watts, the new American ambassador to France. Bardo photographs her, and when the picture is published across the city, her former accomplices, one of them just released from prison, discover where she is and set out for revenge. To escape them, Laure manipulates Bardo into helping her stage her own kidnapping and demand a ransom from her husband, and the two begin an affair. When Bardo has second thoughts, the scheme turns deadly, and a final twist forces the audience to reconsider everything that has come before.

The film plays with themes of identity, fate and voyeurism, and its surprise ending, which reframes much of the story, has been widely debated.

Femme Fatale screened out of competition at the 2002 Cannes Film Festival. It was a box office failure, grossing about 16.8 million dollars worldwide, less than its production costs, and received mixed reviews; Rotten Tomatoes gives it 49 percent approval and Metacritic a score of 60. Roger Ebert gave it four stars, and the film has since been reappraised by many critics and is now regarded as a cult classic.

documents.title: Final Destination 3
documents.tagline: This ride will be the death of you.
documents.overview: A student's premonition of a deadly rollercoaster ride saves her life and a lucky few, but not from death itself – which seeks out those who escaped their fate.
documents.plot:
Final Destination 3 is a supernatural horror film directed by James Wong, released in 2006 by New Line Cinema.

The movie begins with Clear Rivers (Mary Elizabeth Winstead), a high school student who survives a roller coaster accident at an amusement park. She had been warned not to get on the ride by her friend, Kevin Williamson (Ryan Merriman), but she ignored him. As a result of this warning, Clear is haunted by premonitions and visions of death.

Clear's friends, including her boyfriend, Wexler (Chad Donella), and her friends from school, are also at the amusement park on the same day as Clear. However, they all die in a series of gruesome accidents, which Clear tries to prevent using her knowledge of impending doom.

The first accident occurs when Wexler is crushed by a falling roller coaster car. The second accident happens when Kevin's girlfriend, Clear's friend, is killed by a malfunctioning funhouse ride. The third accident involves a group of teenagers who are trapped in a burning amusement park building.

As the accidents continue to occur, Clear realizes that she has the ability to see and prevent these events from happening. However, each time she tries to warn her friends or take action to prevent an accident, something goes wrong, and they still die.

Clear becomes increasingly isolated as she struggles to understand why her warnings are not being heeded. She also starts to question whether she is truly able to change the course of events or if she is just seeing things that will inevitably happen.

In the end, Clear realizes that she has been given a chance to cheat death and escape the cycle of premonitions. However, in doing so, she must confront her own mortality and make a choice between saving herself or trying to save others.

The movie ends with Clear escaping the amusement park by jumping off a bridge just as it is about to collapse. She then watches from a distance as the bridge implodes, killing everyone on board. The film concludes with Clear reflecting on the events that have transpired and wondering if she has truly escaped death or if there are still more premonitions waiting for her.

Overall, Final Destination 3 explores themes of mortality, fate, and the consequences of ignoring warnings from others. The movie's twist ending adds to the suspense and surprise, leaving viewers questioning what is real and what is just a product of Clear's imagination.
production_companies: Kumar Mobiliengesellschaft mbH & Co. Projekt Nr. 1 KG

documents.title: Dungeons & Dragons: Wrath of the Dragon God
documents.original_title: Dungeons & Dragons: Wrath of the Dragon God
documents.overview: Due to a curse from his former master Profion, Damodar survived his death by Ridley Freeborn as an undead entity in pursuit of an evil artifact for some hundred years, so that he might be capable of unleashing unstoppable destruction on Izmir and the descendants of those who caused his demise.
documents.plot:
Dungeons & Dragons: Wrath of the Dragon God is an action-adventure film that delves into the world of fantasy and mythology, drawing inspiration from the popular tabletop game. The movie's narrative revolves around a group of characters who must band together to defeat an ancient evil that threatens to destroy their world.

At its core, the film explores themes of friendship, camaraderie, and the power of unity in the face of overwhelming adversity. The main characters, each with their unique skills and abilities, must put aside their differences and work together to overcome the challenges they face. This collective effort serves as a metaphor for the importance of collaboration and cooperation in overcoming even the most daunting obstacles.

The movie also touches on the idea of redemption and personal growth, as some of the characters grapple with past mistakes and seek to make amends. The film's portrayal of these themes is often lighthearted and humorous, adding a layer of depth and complexity to the narrative.

Furthermore, Dungeons & Dragons: Wrath of the Dragon God features a richly detailed world filled with mythical creatures, magical artifacts, and ancient prophecies. This fantastical realm serves as a backdrop for exploring broader themes such as the nature of good and evil, the consequences of playing with forces beyond one's control, and the importance of respecting the power of the unknown.

Overall, Dungeons & Dragons: Wrath of the Dragon God is a film that celebrates the spirit of adventure, friendship, and self-discovery, while also acknowledging the complexities and challenges that come with navigating the world.

documents.title: Crocodile Dundee in Los Angeles
documents.tagline: He heard there was wildlife in L.A. He didn't know how wild.
documents.overview: After settling in the tiny Australian town of Walkabout Creek with his significant other and his young son, Mick "Crocodile" Dundee is thrown for a loop when a prestigious Los Angeles newspaper offers his honey a job. The family migrates back to the United States, and Croc and son soon find themselves learning some lessons about American life -- many of them inadvertent
documents.plot:
Crocodile Dundee in Los Angeles is a 2001 action comedy directed by Simon Wincer and starring Paul Hogan. It is the third and final installment of the Crocodile Dundee series and a sequel to Crocodile Dundee II (1988). Hogan and Linda Kozlowski return as Michael "Crocodile" Dundee and Sue Charlton, joined by Jere Burns, Jonathan Banks, Alec Wilson and Serge Cockburn as their young son. The film was shot in Los Angeles and in Queensland, and Hogan said the idea for its story came to him while touring the Czech town of Litomyšl in 1993.

Thirteen years after the previous film, Mick lives in the Australian outback with Sue and their son Mikey. Crocodile hunting has been outlawed, so Mick now earns his living wrestling crocodiles for tourists and competing with a rival bushman named Jacko. When Sue is offered the job of Los Angeles bureau chief for a newspaper owned by her father, the family moves across the Pacific. Mick and Mikey soon run into a series of culture-clash misadventures in Southern California, while Mikey wins over his classmates and his teacher with the survival skills he learned in the bush.

Sue's predecessor at the paper died in suspicious circumstances, and Mick becomes an undercover amateur detective to help find out what happened. The trail leads to a film studio that is inexplicably making a sequel to a flop action film called Lethal Agent. Mick grows suspicious when crates of paintings from southern Europe arrive on the set. At first he assumes drugs are being smuggled, but the canvases turn out to be valuable artworks missing from a museum in the former Yugoslavia and thought to have been lost during the war. The production plans to burn them as props on camera after quietly swapping them for copies. With Jacko flown in to babysit Mikey, Mick and Sue try to get hold of one painting as evidence and end up taking on the studio's criminals, using props and a trio of film lions.

The film was released in April 2001 and grossed about $39 million worldwide. Critics were largely negative, calling it an unnecessary sequel that came too long after the earlier films and relied on fish-out-of-water humor that had grown stale.

documents.title: The Longest Yard
documents.tagline: If you can't get out, get even.
documents.overview: Pro quarter-back, Paul Crewe and former college champion and coach, Nate Scarboro are doing time in the same prison. Asked to put together a team of inmates to take on the guards, Crewe enlists the help of Scarboro to coach the inmates to victory in a football game 'fixed' to turn out quite another way.
documents.plot:
The Longest Yard is a sports comedy film directed by Peter Segal, released in 2005. The movie stars Adam Sandler as Paul Crewe, a former NFL quarterback who becomes a coach at a minimum-security prison.

Paul Crewe (Adam Sandler) was once a successful NFL quarterback but lost his job and reputation after being involved in a scandal that led to the death of an opponent on the field. He is sentenced to 3 years in prison for manslaughter. While serving his time, he becomes the coach of the prison's football team, which has not won a game in over 40 years.

Crewe's goal is to lead the team to victory and prove that even in a place like this, there can be redemption and hope. However, he faces opposition from the corrupt warden, George "The King" Weathers (Burt Reynolds), who wants to keep the prison's football team losing so that the inmates will stay docile and obedient.

As Crewe tries to whip his team into shape, he also has to deal with the harsh realities of prison life. He befriends a fellow inmate, Caretaker (Chris Rock), who becomes his assistant coach. Together, they try to motivate their teammates and overcome the obstacles that stand in their way.

Throughout the movie, Crewe's character undergoes significant development as he learns to balance his desire for revenge against Weathers with his newfound sense of purpose and responsibility as a coach. He also starts to form connections with some of the inmates, including Caretaker, who becomes like a protégé to him.

As the team begins to win games, Crewe's reputation grows, and he becomes a symbol of hope for the inmates. However, Weathers will stop at nothing to crush their spirits and maintain his own power over the prison.

In the climactic final game, Crewe's team faces off against Weathers' favorite team, led by the ruthless and arrogant quarterback, Shane Falco (David Spade). The game is intense, with both teams fighting for victory. In the end, Crewe's team emerges victorious, and he finally gets his revenge against Weathers.

The movie ends on a high note, with Crewe's team celebrating their win and Crewe himself finding redemption and a new sense of purpose. He has proven that even in the darkest of places, there is always hope for change and redemption.

Overall, The Longest Yard is a fun and entertaining movie that combines humor, action, and heart. It features strong performances from Adam Sandler and Burt Reynolds, as well as a talented supporting cast.

documents.title: Monster House
documents.tagline: The house is . . . alive!
documents.overview: Monsters under the bed are scary enough, but what happens when an entire house is out to get you? Three teens aim to find out when they go up against a decrepit neighboring home and unlock its frightening secrets.
documents.plot:
Monster House is a 2006 computer-animated comedy-horror film produced by DreamWorks Animation and Amblin Entertainment. The movie follows the story of a mysterious house that seems to have a life of its own.

The story begins with the introduction of three children: DJ (voiced by Spencer Locke), Chowder (voiced by Sam Lerner), and Jenny (voiced by Megan Mullally). They live in the suburban town of Suburbia, where everyone knows each other's business. The house at 1313 Cemetery Lane is a source of fascination for the kids, as it seems to be alive and has a mind of its own.

As the story progresses, we learn that the house was built by a former owner named Mr. Nebbercracker (voiced by Steve Buscemi), who died under mysterious circumstances. The house has been terrorizing the neighborhood ever since, causing chaos and destruction wherever it goes.

DJ, Chowder, and Jenny decide to team up to solve the mystery of the haunted house. They soon discover that the house is actually a monster in disguise, with a personality of its own. The house, which they name "Monster House," has a mind of its own and seems to be alive.

As the kids delve deeper into the mystery, they learn that Monster House was once a normal house built by Mr. Nebbercracker. However, after his death, the house became possessed by the spirit of Mr. Nebbercracker's son, who died in the house many years ago. The son's ghost is trapped inside the house and is seeking revenge on the living.

The kids come up with a plan to help the ghost find peace and move on from the mortal world. They work together to uncover the secrets of Monster House and ultimately succeed in helping the ghost resolve its unfinished business.

In the end, DJ, Chowder, and Jenny are hailed as heroes for solving the mystery of Monster House. The house is no longer a source of terror, but rather a symbol of their bravery and friendship. The movie ends with the kids standing in front of the house, which has been transformed into a beautiful garden, a testament to the power of teamwork and determination.

Throughout the movie, the animation is vibrant and colorful, bringing the characters and the monster house to life. The voice acting is also top-notch, with each character bringing their own unique personality to the story. Overall, Monster House is a fun and spooky animated film that is suitable for both kids and adults.

documents.title: Flightplan
documents.tagline: If someone took everything you live for... how far would you go to get it back?
documents.overview: Flying at 40,000 feet in a state-of-the art aircraft that she helped design, Kyle Pratt's 6-year-old daughter Julia vanishes without a trace. Or did she? No one on the plane believes Julia was ever onboard. And now Kyle, desperate and alone, can only count on her own wits to unravel the mystery and save her daughter.
documents.plot: Flying at 40,000 feet in a state-of-the art aircraft that she helped design, Kyle Pratt's 6-year-old daughter Julia vanishes without a trace. Or did she? No one on the plane believes Julia was ever onboard. And now Kyle, desperate and alone, can only count on her own wits to unravel the mystery and save her daughter.

documents.title: Ong Bak: Muay Thai Warrior
documents.tagline: No computer graphics. No stunt doubles. No wires.
documents.overview: When the head of a statue sacred to a village is stolen, a young martial artist goes to the big city and finds himself taking on the underworld to retrieve it.
documents.plot:
Ong Bak: Muay Thai Warrior is a 2003 martial arts film directed by Prachya Pinkaew, starring Tony Jaa as the titular character. The movie is set in 13th-century Siam (now Thailand) and tells the story of Ong Bak, a young man who seeks revenge against those who killed his father.

The film begins with Ong Bak, played by Tony Jaa, as a young boy who lives with his father, a skilled Muay Thai fighter. When Ong Bak's father is brutally murdered by the corrupt and power-hungry General Mongkut (Sorapong Chatree), Ong Bak vows to avenge his father's death.

Ong Bak sets out on a journey to find General Mongkut, facing numerous challenges and obstacles along the way. He meets a group of traveling performers who take him in and teach him the ways of Muay Thai. As Ong Bak trains with the performers, he also learns about the importance of honor, loyalty, and self-discipline.

As Ong Bak's skills as a fighter improve, he becomes determined to confront General Mongkut and bring justice to his father's memory. The film's action sequences are intense and well-choreographed, showcasing Tony Jaa's impressive martial arts skills.

Throughout the movie, Ong Bak faces various adversaries, including General Mongkut's henchmen and a group of bandits. However, he also encounters a mysterious woman named Lin (Petchtai Wongkamlao), who becomes his ally and potential love interest.

As the story unfolds, Ong Bak discovers that General Mongkut is using his power to exploit the poor and vulnerable people in Siam. Ong Bak's quest for revenge becomes a mission to bring justice and protect the innocent.

The film's climax features an epic battle between Ong Bak and General Mongkut, with Ong Bak emerging victorious. In the end, Ong Bak finds some measure of closure and redemption, but not before facing his own personal demons and confronting the harsh realities of the world around him.

Overall, Ong Bak: Muay Thai Warrior is a thrilling and visually stunning film that showcases Tony Jaa's impressive martial arts skills and the rich cultural heritage of Thailand. The movie's themes of honor, loyalty, and self-discipline are timeless and universal, making it a compelling watch for audiences worldwide.

documents.title: The Scorpion King
documents.tagline: Warrior. Legend. King.
documents.overview: In ancient Egypt, peasant Mathayus is hired to exact revenge on the powerful Memnon and the sorceress Cassandra, who are ready to overtake Balthazar's village. Amid betrayals, thieves, abductions and more, Mathayus strives to bring justice to his complicated world.
documents.plot:
The Scorpion King is a 2002 American fantasy adventure film directed by Chuck Russell and written by David Hayter. The movie serves as a prequel to The Mummy Returns, starring Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson.

In ancient Egypt, the story begins with Mathayus (Dwayne Johnson), a young orphan who grows up on the streets of Memphis. He is discovered by a group of mercenaries and trained in combat skills by the leader, General Kane (Steven Brand). Kane becomes like a father to Mathayus, teaching him how to fight and survive.

As Mathayus grows older, he becomes a skilled warrior and earns the respect of his comrades. However, Kane's true intentions are revealed: he plans to overthrow the Pharaoh and take control of Egypt for himself. Mathayus is torn between his loyalty to Kane and his growing sense of morality.

When Kane's plan fails, he is betrayed by his own men and left for dead. Mathayus finds him dying and nurses him back to health. As Kane lies on his deathbed, he reveals that the Scorpion King is a legendary figure who will one day bring about great change in Egypt.

Kane dies, but not before giving Mathayus a magical amulet that allows him to control the sand worms of the desert. With this newfound power, Mathayus sets out to avenge Kane's death and claim his rightful place as the Scorpion King.

Mathayus faces numerous challenges on his journey, including fierce battles with rival warriors and treacherous desert landscapes. Along the way, he meets a woman named Chandra (Kelly Hu), who becomes his ally and potential love interest.

As Mathayus draws closer to his goal, he must confront his own demons and learn to harness his newfound powers. In the end, he defeats Kane's successor, General Sargon (Michael Clarke Duncan), and claims the throne of Egypt as the Scorpion King.

The movie ends with Mathayus standing victorious, but also aware that his journey is far from over. He has become a legendary figure, feared and respected by all who know him. The final shot is of the magical amulet, still glowing with power, as the camera pans out to reveal the vast expanse of the desert landscape.

Overall, The Scorpion King is an action-packed adventure film that explores themes of loyalty, power, and redemption. Dwayne Johnson's performance as Mathayus brings depth and nuance to the character, making him a compelling hero on screen.

documents.title: Transporter 2
documents.tagline: The Best In The Business Is Back In The Game.
documents.overview: Professional driver Frank Martin is living in Miami, where he is temporarily filling in for a friend as the chauffeur for a government narcotics control policymaker and his family. The young boy in the family is targeted for kidnapping, and Frank immediately becomes involved in protecting the child and exposing the kidnappers.
documents.plot:
Transporter 2 is a 2005 action film directed by Louis Leterrier and starring Jason Statham as the main protagonist, Frank Martin.

The movie begins with Frank Martin (Jason Statham) living a peaceful life in Paris, France. He has retired from his high-stakes transportation business and is now running a small courier service. However, his quiet life is disrupted when he receives a package from an unknown client containing a briefcase that contains the stolen $100 million worth of diamonds.

The client, who remains anonymous throughout the film, instructs Frank to deliver the briefcase to a specific location in Istanbul, Turkey. Unbeknownst to Frank, the briefcase contains more than just diamonds; it also holds the key to a powerful and deadly virus that could wipe out millions of people worldwide.

As Frank embarks on his journey to Istanbul, he is pursued by a team of skilled assassins hired by a mysterious organization known as the "Terrorist". The Terrorist's true intentions are unclear, but their goal is evident: they want to use the virus to hold the world hostage and gain control over global politics.

Throughout the film, Frank faces numerous challenges and obstacles as he navigates through the crowded streets of Istanbul. He encounters a beautiful woman named Lai (Shu Qi), who becomes his ally in the quest to deliver the briefcase. Together, they must evade the Terrorist's henchmen and stay one step ahead of their pursuers.

As Frank gets closer to his destination, he realizes that the Terrorist's true intentions are far more sinister than he initially thought. The virus is not just a simple biological agent; it has the potential to cause widespread destruction and chaos on a global scale.

In the climactic final act, Frank and Lai face off against the leader of the Terrorist organization in an intense hand-to-hand combat sequence. Frank manages to outsmart his opponents and deliver the briefcase to its intended destination, but not before the Terrorist's true identity is revealed: it is none other than Frank's former business partner, who has been seeking revenge against him for years.

The film concludes with Frank returning to Paris, where he is greeted as a hero by Lai. However, the movie ends on a somber note, hinting that Frank's life will never be the same again. The Terrorist's plan may have been foiled, but the world is now aware of the deadly virus, and Frank knows that his skills as a transporter are still in high demand.

Overall, Transporter 2 is an action-packed thrill ride that keeps viewers on the edge of their seats from start to finish. Jason Statham delivers a memorable performance as the charismatic and resourceful Frank Martin, making this film a must-see for fans of the action genre.

documents.title: Click
documents.tagline: What If You Had A Remote... That Controlled Your Universe?
documents.overview: A married workaholic, Michael Newman doesn't have time for his wife and children, not if he's to impress his ungrateful boss and earn a well-deserved promotion. So when he meets Morty, a loopy sales clerk, he gets the answer to his prayers: a magical remote that allows him to bypass life's little distractions with increasingly hysterical results.
documents.plot:
Click is a 2006 American fantasy comedy film directed by Frank Coraci and produced by Adam Sandler Productions. The movie stars Adam Sandler, Kate Beckinsale, Christopher Walken, and Rosario Dawson.

The story revolves around Michael Newman (played by Adam Sandler), a workaholic advertising executive who feels unfulfilled with his life. He is married to Donna (played by Kate Beckinsale) and has two children, Charlie (played by Logan Lerman) and Sarah (played by Cole Hawkins). Michael's job requires him to constantly be on the go, and he often neglects his family in the process.

One day, while working late at the office, Michael meets a mysterious door-to-door salesman named Morty (played by Christopher Walken), who sells him an "Universal Remote Control" that can control not only his TV but also his life. The remote has the power to fast-forward through time, allowing Michael to skip over mundane tasks and experiences.

Initially, Michael uses the remote to speed up his daily routine, skipping over boring meetings, traffic jams, and other tedious activities. However, he soon discovers that the remote's power comes with a price: every time he uses it, he loses a year of his life. The more he uses the remote, the younger he becomes.

As Michael struggles to cope with the consequences of his newfound power, he begins to reevaluate his priorities and relationships. He starts to appreciate the small moments in life and reconnects with his family. However, Morty's true intentions are revealed: he is a collector of souls, and Michael has become his latest acquisition.

In a desperate attempt to break free from Morty's control, Michael must find a way to reverse the effects of the remote and reclaim his life. Along the way, he learns valuable lessons about the importance of family, friendship, and living in the present moment.

The movie culminates with Michael using the remote one last time to fast-forward through the final year of his life, allowing him to spend quality time with his loved ones and make amends for past mistakes. In the end, Michael is able to break free from Morty's control and find a sense of peace and fulfillment.

Overall, Click is a heartwarming story about the importance of living in the present moment and appreciating the little things in life. The movie features a talented cast, witty dialogue, and a unique blend of humor and drama that makes it a must-see for fans of Adam Sandler and fantasy comedies.

documents.title: The Core
documents.tagline: Earth has a deadline.
documents.overview: Geophysicist Dr. Josh Keyes discovers that an unknown force has caused the earth's inner core to stop rotating. With the planet's magnetic field rapidly deteriorating, our atmosphere literally starts to come apart at the seams with catastrophic consequences. To resolve the crisis, Keyes, along with a team of the world's most gifted scientists, travel into the earth's core. Their mission: detonate a device that will reactivate the core.
documents.plot:
The Core is a 2003 American science fiction disaster film directed by Jon Amiel from a screenplay by Cooper Layne and John Rogers. Aaron Eckhart, Hilary Swank, Delroy Lindo and Stanley Tucci lead an ensemble that also includes D. J. Qualls, Richard Jenkins, Tchéky Karyo, Bruce Greenwood and Alfre Woodard. Released by Paramount Pictures on March 28, 2003, after being moved from November 2002, it follows a team sent to the centre of the Earth to restart the rotation of its core with nuclear explosions.

When thirty-two people in Boston die at the same moment from failures of their pacemakers, geophysicist Josh Keyes and weapons expert Serge Leveque are brought in to investigate. A series of bizarre incidents linked to the planet's magnetic field leads Josh and the arrogant Dr. Conrad Zimsky to conclude that the inner core has stopped spinning, which will strip away the magnetic shield protecting Earth from lethal solar radiation. The government's solution is to detonate nuclear weapons in the outer core. Zimsky's estranged former colleague Ed "Braz" Brazzelton supplies a tunnelling ship, Virgil, to be piloted by NASA astronauts Robert Iverson and Rebecca Childs, while the hacker "Rat" Finch is recruited to keep news of the crisis off the internet.

Launched through the Mariana Trench, Virgil bores into the crust with a laser drill. In the mantle it plunges into a vast hollow geode, and Iverson is killed freeing the ship; a later breach in a field of diamond formations claims Serge, who sacrifices himself to save the weapon controls. In the outer core the team discovers that the material is less dense than expected and their bombs are too weak. Zimsky confesses that the crisis was likely caused by DESTINI, a secret tectonic weapon he helped develop, and the military wants to fire it again; Rat sabotages the attempt after a surge of microwave radiation destroys the Golden Gate Bridge.

The crew instead seals the bombs into separate compartments, timing the explosions so their shock waves reinforce one another. Braz and then Zimsky give their lives to complete the plan, and the detonations restart the core. Josh and Rebecca power Virgil back to the ocean floor near Hawaii, where whales attracted by their ultrasound signal lead rescuers to them, and Rat leaks the full story to the world.

The film drew mixed reviews, with Rotten Tomatoes reporting 39% approval, and grossed about $74.1 million worldwide against an $85 million budget.
production_companies: Munich Film Partners New Century & Company (MFP) Core Productions

documents.title: The Mask of Zorro
documents.tagline: No one has seen his face... but everyone ... knows this mark.
documents.overview: It has been twenty years since Don Diego de la Vega fought Spanish oppression in Alta California as the legendary romantic hero, Zorro. Having escaped from prison he transforms troubled bandit Alejandro into his successor, in order to foil the plans of the tyrannical Don Rafael Montero who robbed him of his freedom, his wife and his precious daughter.
documents.plot:
The Mask of Zorro is a 1998 American swashbuckler film directed by Martin Campbell and produced by Amblin Entertainment. The movie is set in 1820s California, during the Mexican-American War.

The story begins with the introduction of Captain Alejandro Murrieta (Antonio Banderas), a Spanish nobleman who has been wrongly accused of being a bandit and sentenced to death. However, before he can be executed, he escapes from prison and flees to the mountains, where he assumes the identity of Zorro, a legendary masked vigilante.

Meanwhile, in the town of San Juan Bautista, Don Diego de la Vega (Antonio Banderas), the son of the wealthy and influential Don Diego, is struggling to find his place in society. He is expected to take over his father's business, but he feels suffocated by the responsibilities and longs for adventure.

One day, a group of bandits led by Captain Murrieta arrive in San Juan Bautista, seeking revenge against the town that wronged him. Don Diego, who has been watching from afar, decides to take matters into his own hands and assumes the identity of Zorro to protect his father's business and the people he cares about.

As Zorro, Don Diego sets out to avenge Captain Murrieta's family and defeat the bandits. Along the way, he meets a beautiful and feisty woman named Elena Monasterio (Catherine Zeta-Jones), who becomes his ally and potential love interest.

Throughout the movie, Don Diego struggles with the dual identity of Zorro and his own sense of self-worth. He must balance his desire for adventure and justice with his responsibilities as a member of society. Meanwhile, Captain Murrieta's true intentions are revealed, and Don Diego must confront him in order to save Elena and the town.

The movie culminates in an epic battle between Zorro and Captain Murrieta, with Don Diego ultimately emerging victorious. In the process, he also finds his own identity and purpose as a hero, rather than just a masked vigilante.

The Mask of Zorro features stunning action sequences, memorable characters, and a sweeping narrative that explores themes of identity, loyalty, and redemption. The movie's blend of humor, adventure, and romance has made it a beloved classic among fans of the swashbuckler genre.

documents.title: EuroTrip
documents.tagline: No actual Europeans were harmed in the making of this film.
documents.overview: When Scott learns that his longtime cyber-buddy from Berlin is a gorgeous young woman, he and his friends embark on a trip across Europe.
documents.plot:
