EuroTrip is a coming-of-age comedy film released in 2004 by DreamWorks Pictures. The movie follows the story of three friends, Scott, Shane, and Burt, who embark on a journey to Europe after graduation.

The film begins with Scott (played by Matt Damon), Shane (played by Sean Astin), and Burt (played by Ben Stiller) reminiscing about their high school days in New Jersey. They share stories of their past relationships and the girls they had crushes on, including Mandy (played by Eliza Dushku). The friends decide to take a trip to Europe to find Mandy, who has moved to London.

Upon arrival in London, the trio meets up with Mandy's new boyfriend, Neil (played by Bill Paxton), and her eccentric family. However, things quickly go awry as they discover that Mandy is not interested in reuniting with them. The friends decide to continue their journey to Amsterdam, where they hope to find a more receptive audience.

In Amsterdam, the group encounters a series of misadventures, including a wild party at a nightclub and a run-in with a group of eccentric locals. Along the way, Scott develops feelings for Mandy's sister, Jules (played by Lauren Ambrose), while Shane becomes infatuated with a Dutch woman named Sophie.

As the trip progresses, the friends face various challenges, including cultural differences, language barriers, and personal growth. Through their experiences, they learn to let go of their past relationships and focus on the present moment.

The film's climax features the group's final encounter with Mandy, who has grown apart from her family and is struggling to find her place in the world. The friends offer her advice and support, helping her to come to terms with her own identity.

In the end, Scott returns home alone, having found a sense of closure and new beginnings. Shane and Burt part ways, but not before sharing a heartfelt goodbye. The film concludes with Scott reflecting on his journey, realizing that sometimes, you have to take risks and step out of your comfort zone to find yourself.

Overall, EuroTrip is a lighthearted, entertaining film that explores themes of friendship, love, and self-discovery. With its witty dialogue, memorable characters, and humorous misadventures, the movie has become a cult classic among fans of coming-of-age comedies.

documents.title: Nacho Libre
documents.tagline: He's not lean. He's not mean. He's nacho average hero.
documents.overview: Nacho Libre is loosely based on the story of Fray Tormenta ("Friar Storm"), aka Rev. Sergio Gutierrez Benitez, a real-life Mexican Catholic priest who had a 23-year career as a masked luchador. He competed in order to support the orphanage he directed.
documents.plot:
Nacho Libre is a 2006 American sports comedy film directed by Jared Hess and written by Jared and Jerusha Hess. The movie stars Jack Black, Ana de la Reguera, Héctor Jiménez, and Carlos Santana.

The story begins with Nacho Varga (Jack Black), a cook at a Mexican monastery in Mexico City who secretly dreams of becoming a luchador (Mexican wrestler). Nacho's life is mundane and unfulfilling, working long hours in the kitchen while his fellow monks enjoy their lives as wrestlers. However, when the monastery's beloved priest, Padre Sancho (Héctor Jiménez), announces that he will be retiring due to a heart condition, Nacho sees an opportunity to fulfill his lifelong dream.

Nacho begins training with the monastery's wrestling coach, Esqueleto (Jorge Rivero), and eventually earns the nickname "El Loco" (The Crazy One). He also meets Sister Encarnación (Ana de la Reguera), a beautiful and kind-hearted nun who becomes Nacho's love interest. As Nacho's wrestling career takes off, he must balance his newfound fame with his responsibilities at the monastery.

However, things take a turn when Esqueleto is murdered by a rival wrestler, Ramón "El Diablo" Cortez (Carlos Santana), who seeks to destroy Nacho and claim the monastery's wrestling title for himself. Nacho must use his wits and wrestling skills to outsmart Cortez and save the monastery.

Throughout the movie, Jack Black shines as Nacho Libre, bringing his signature energy and humor to the role. The film is full of hilarious moments, from Nacho's over-the-top wrestling matches to his awkward interactions with Sister Encarnación.

As the story unfolds, Nacho must confront his own identity and purpose. He learns that being a luchador is not just about physical strength but also about using his platform for good. In the end, Nacho defeats Cortez in an epic wrestling match, saving the monastery and finding his true calling as a wrestler.

The movie ends with Nacho returning to the monastery, where he is welcomed back as a hero. He marries Sister Encarnación, and they have a beautiful wedding ceremony. The film concludes on a heartwarming note, showcasing Nacho's growth and newfound sense of purpose.

Overall, Nacho Libre is a fun and entertaining movie that combines humor, action, and heart. Jack Black's performance as the titular character is unforgettable, making this film a must-see for fans of comedy and wrestling.

documents.title: Final Destination 2
documents.tagline: For every beginning there is an end.
documents.overview: When Kimberly has a violent premonition of a highway pileup she blocks the freeway, keeping a few others meant to die, safe...Or are they? The survivors mysteriously start dying and it's up to Kimberly to stop it before she's next.
documents.plot:
Final Destination 2 is a supernatural horror film directed by David R. Ellis and written by J. Mackye Gruber. The movie is the sequel to the 2000 film Final Destination, which was also based on the novel of the same name by Kevin Williamson.

The story begins with Alex Browning (A.J. Cook), the survivor of the first film, who has been experiencing strange and terrifying premonitions since her encounter with Death in the first movie. She is haunted by visions of a car crash that will kill her and several others. Believing that she can cheat death again, Alex decides to test her theory by deliberately putting herself in harm's way.

Alex convinces her friends, including Terri (Ali Larter), Wren (Seann William Scott), and Monty (Chad Donella), to go skydiving with her at a remote airfield. As they jump out of the plane, Alex experiences another premonition, which she believes is warning her that something terrible will happen.

However, instead of dying in the crash, Alex manages to survive by using a parachute that was not attached to the plane. She then sets out to warn her friends about the impending disaster, but they are skeptical and dismissive of her warnings.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Alex's premonitions are real, and she is trying to prevent a series of gruesome and deadly accidents from occurring. The group soon discovers that the airfield where they went skydiving was actually a site of a previous plane crash that killed everyone on board.

The movie takes a dark turn as the characters begin to die off one by one, each in a manner that is eerily similar to Alex's premonitions. As the body count rises, it becomes clear that Death has set its sights on this group, and they are powerless to stop it.

In the end, only Terri survives, but not without scars both physical and emotional. The movie ends with Terri, who has finally understood the true nature of Alex's premonitions, setting out to warn others about the impending disaster, leaving the audience wondering if she will be able to prevent another tragedy from occurring.

Throughout the film, the tension builds as the characters are stalked by Death, and the audience is left on the edge of their seats, wondering who will survive and who will become the next victim. The movie's climax features a shocking twist that sets up the events of the third installment in the series.

Overall, Final Destination 2 is a tense and suspenseful horror film that explores the theme of fate and mortality. With its clever plot twists and gruesome death scenes, it has become a cult classic among fans of the genre.

documents.title: Wuthering Heights
documents.tagline: Love is a force of nature
documents.overview: Yorkshire moorlands, northern England, in the late 18th century. Young Heathcliff, rescued from the streets of Liverpool by Mr. Earnshaw, the owner of Wuthering Heights, an isolated farm, develops over the years an insane passion for Cathy, his foster sister, a sick obsession destined to end tragically.
documents.plot:
Wuthering Heights is a 2011 film adaptation of Emily Brontë's classic novel of the same name, directed by Andrea Arnold and produced by Film4 and BBC Films. The movie explores the tumultuous relationship between Catherine and Heathcliff, two individuals bound together by their intense love for each other.

At its core, Wuthering Heights is a tragic tale of all-consuming passion, obsession, and the destructive nature of unchecked emotions. The film delves into the complexities of human relationships, revealing the dark underbelly of love, class, and social status in 19th-century England.

The movie masterfully captures the raw, unbridled energy of Catherine and Heathcliff's relationship, which is marked by a fierce intensity that ultimately proves to be their downfall. The film also explores the theme of identity, as both characters struggle to find their place within society and navigate the constraints of their respective social classes.

Furthermore, Wuthering Heights examines the devastating consequences of unchecked ambition and the corrupting influence of power. Heathcliff's relentless pursuit of revenge against those who wronged him serves as a cautionary tale about the dangers of allowing emotions to consume us.

Throughout the film, Arnold employs a lyrical, poetic style that perfectly captures the atmospheric, gothic landscape of the Yorkshire moors, where much of the story unfolds. The cinematography is breathtaking, with sweeping vistas and intimate close-ups that immerse the viewer in the world of the characters.

Ultimately, Wuthering Heights is a powerful exploration of the human condition, one that probes the depths of love, loss, and the enduring power of the human spirit.

documents.title: The Texas Chainsaw Massacre
documents.tagline: Based on a true story...
documents.overview: After picking up a traumatized young hitchhiker, five friends find themselves stalked and hunted by a chainsaw-wielding killer and his family of equally psychopathic killers.
documents.plot:
The Texas Chainsaw Massacre is a 2003 American horror film directed by Marcus Nispel and written by Scott Kosar, based on the 1974 film of the same name by Tobe Hooper. The movie stars Jessica Biel, Jonathan Tucker, Andrew Bryniarski, Eric Balfour, and Erin Daniels.

The story begins with a prologue that shows a young Sally Hardesty (Erin Daniels) being brutally murdered by Leatherface (Andrew Bryniarski), the main antagonist of the film. The scene is presented in a found-footage style, which sets the tone for the rest of the movie.

The present-day narrative follows Erin Harris (Jessica Biel), a college student who has just graduated and is on her way to visit her sister, Sarah (Mike Vogel), in Austin, Texas. Erin's friends, Kirk (Jonathan Tucker) and Pam (Erin Daniels), are also along for the ride. The group decides to take a detour to visit the grave of Sally Hardesty, who was killed by Leatherface many years ago.

As they approach the grave, they notice that it has been recently disturbed, which sets off a chain of events that leads them into the clutches of Leatherface and his family. The group soon discovers that they are lost in rural Texas and that their car has broken down. They decide to seek shelter at an old gas station, where they meet a local named Franklin (Eric Balfour), who claims to be able to fix their car.

However, it becomes clear that Franklin is not what he seems, and the group soon finds themselves being stalked by Leatherface and his family, including his mother, Grandpa, and brother. The group tries to escape, but they are eventually captured and taken to the family's farmhouse, where they are subjected to a series of gruesome and terrifying events.

As the night wears on, Erin and her friends try to find a way to escape, but Leatherface and his family prove to be relentless in their pursuit of them. The group is eventually killed off one by one, with Erin being the last survivor.

In the end, Erin manages to escape from the farmhouse by hiding in a well, where she is rescued by a local sheriff's deputy. As she reflects on her ordeal, it becomes clear that the events at the farmhouse were just a nightmare, and that Erin had been experiencing hallucinations due to stress and fatigue.

The movie ends with Erin driving away from the farmhouse, leaving behind the horrors of the night before. The final shot is of Leatherface's mask, which is left on the ground, serving as a reminder of the terror that Erin experienced.

Overall, The Texas Chainsaw Massacre (2003) is a tense and suspenseful horror film that pays homage to the original 1974 film while also offering a fresh take on the classic story.

documents.title: Babylon A.D.
documents.tagline: Kill or be Killed.
documents.overview: A veteran-turned-mercenary is hired to take a young woman with a secret from post-apocalyptic Eastern Europe to New York City.
documents.plot:
In a dystopian near future, a Russian mobster, Gorsky, hires the mercenary Toorop to bring a young woman known only as Aurora from Asia to New York City. Gorsky gives Toorop a variety of weapons and a subdermally implanted UN passport. Toorop, the girl, and, her guardian, Sister Rebeka, travel from the Noelite Convent in Kyrgyzstan to reach New York via Russia.
Unlike in the technologically advanced United States, war and terrorist activity have transformed Russia's cities into dangerous, overpopulated slums. The stress of humanity's situation causes Aurora to act out in strange ways and display clairvoyant abilities. On one such occasion, Aurora, seemingly for no reason, panics and runs from a crowded train station just before it explodes in a terrorist attack.
The protagonists must also evade an unknown group of mercenaries claiming to have been sent by Aurora's supposedly dead father. Later, they board a submarine that carries refugees to Canada. To avoid satellite detection, the Captain of the submarine orders his crew to dive and he shoots some of the refugees still trying to get on board. Aurora, infuriated by the loss of life, operates the 30-year-old submarine without training. Sister Rebeka tells Toorop that Aurora could speak nineteen different languages by the age of two, and always seems to know things she has never learned. Three months before leaving with Toorop, she began acting differently. This occurred after a Noelite doctor administered a pill. The doctor told her to go to New York City and arranged for Toorop to escort them.
After arriving in Alaska with help from Toorop's associate, Finn, the protagonists are attacked by weaponized drones. Toorop manages to destroy all the drones, but also gets wounded. The perils cause Finn to betray the group and so Toorop shoots him dead.
Once in Harlem, a news broadcast about the bombing of the Kyrgyzstan convent causes the group to realize there is more going on than they know. Gorsky, working for the Noelites, had planted a tracking device in Toorop's passport and bombed the convent when he knew they were in the United States. The doctor who earlier saw Aurora examines her again in a hotel room. When he leaves, Aurora reveals (without being told) that she is pregnant with twins despite being a virgin.
Looking outside the hotel, Toorop sees Gorsky's men and the Noelite group heavily armed and waiting for them on the street. The High Priestess calls Toorop and asks him to bring Aurora outside. Just before they take her away, Toorop changes his mind and starts a firefight with the two groups to get the two women to safety. Gorsky's men fire guided missiles at Toorop that track his subdermal passport. Rebeka gets killed defending Aurora, who in turn shoots Toorop and says, "I need you to live". Toorop's clinical death causes the guided missile to go off target (missing Toorop) and explode near Aurora instead; she inexplicably survives.

documents.title: Starsky & Hutch
documents.tagline: They're the man.
documents.overview: Join uptight David Starsky and laid-back Ken "Hutch" Hutchinson as they're paired for the first time as undercover cops. The new partners must overcome their differences to solve an important case with help from street informant Huggy Bear and persuasive criminal Reese Feldman.
documents.plot: Join uptight David Starsky and laid-back Ken "Hutch" Hutchinson as they're paired for the first time as undercover cops. The new partners must overcome their differences to solve an important case with help from street informant Huggy Bear and persuasive criminal Reese Feldman.

documents.title: Thank You for Smoking
documents.tagline: Tobacco lobbyist Nick Naylor is trying to SAVE YOUR ASH!
documents.overview: Nick Naylor is a charismatic spin-doctor for Big Tobacco who'll fight to protect America's right to smoke -- even if it kills him -- while still remaining a role model for his 12-year old son. When he incurs the wrath of a senator bent on snuffing out cigarettes, Nick's powers of "filtering the truth" will be put to the test.
documents.plot: Nick Naylor is a charismatic spin-doctor for Big Tobacco who'll fight to protect America's right to smoke -- even if it kills him -- while still remaining a role model for his 12-year old son. When he incurs the wrath of a senator bent on snuffing out cigarettes, Nick's powers of "filtering the truth" will be put to the test.

documents.title: Renaissance
documents.tagline: Paris 2054. Live forever or die trying
documents.overview: To find Ilona and unlock the secrets of her disappearance, Karas must plunge deep into the parallel worlds of corporate espionage, organized crime and genetic research - where the truth imprisons whoever finds it first and miracles can be bought but at a great price.
documents.plot:
Renaissance, also released as Paris 2054: Renaissance, is a 2006 animated tech-noir thriller directed by Christian Volckman and co-produced by France, the United Kingdom and Luxembourg. Rendered in stark black and white using motion capture, it was released in France in March 2006, in Britain in July and in the United States in September by Miramax. The English-language version features the voices of Daniel Craig as Barthélémy Karas, Romola Garai as Ilona Tasuiev, Catherine McCormack as her sister Bislane, Ian Holm as Jonas Muller and Jonathan Pryce as Paul Dellenbach.

In Paris in 2054, Ilona, a 22-year-old researcher at the all-powerful corporation Avalon, is abducted. The case goes to police captain Karas, fresh from ending a hostage crisis by gunning down the kidnappers. He questions Muller, Avalon's former chief scientist, who quit after failing to cure progeria, the ageing disease that killed his brother, and now runs a free clinic; Muller hints that nobody truly leaves Avalon. Dellenbach, one of the company's executives, stonewalls him. A car chase ending at the Eiffel Tower leads Karas to his childhood friend Farfella, now a gangster, who hands over security footage showing Ilona's car being taken by a very old man. Ilona's sister Bislane, also an Avalon employee, breaks into the company archives and finds that Muller and a Dr. Nakata had experimented on children in search of a progeria cure, destroying their records when the subjects began to mutate. To shield her from Avalon, Karas puts her under a false arrest.

Muller finally confesses that he took Ilona because her research had uncovered the secret of eternal life, which he had found himself decades earlier, and he feared what Avalon would do with it. Before he can surrender, a police marksman shoots him by mistake. Karas realises the old man is Muller's brother, immortal but trapped in an aged body. Karas, mortally wounded, rescues Ilona from Avalon's security forces in the sewers, but she refuses to flee and resolves to hand her discovery to Avalon, so he shoots her as she walks away. Dying, he imagines Bislane forgiving him, as Dellenbach watches it all on a live video feed.

Made over six years for about €14 million, the film won the Cristal for best feature at the Annecy animation festival. It grossed only $1.8 million worldwide and drew mixed reviews, with 49% on Rotten Tomatoes and 57 on Metacritic.
production_companies: MEDIA Programme of the European Union

documents.title: The Descent
documents.tagline: Scream your last breath.
documents.overview: After a tragic accident, six friends reunite for a caving expedition. Their adventure soon goes horribly wrong when a collapse traps them deep underground and they find themselves pursued by bloodthirsty creatures. As their friendships deteriorate, they find themselves in a desperate struggle to survive the creatures and each other.
documents.plot:
The Descent is a 2005 British horror film directed by Neil Marshall and produced by Celador Films. The movie follows a group of six women who embark on a caving expedition in the Appalachian Mountains, only to find themselves trapped and hunted by subterranean creatures.

The story begins with Sarah (Shauna Macdonald), a former rock climber who has lost her sense of purpose after a tragic accident that killed her friends. She joins an all-female caving expedition led by Juno (Natalie Mendoza) to the Appalachian Mountains, where they plan to explore an abandoned cave system.

The group consists of Sarah's friend Rebecca (Saskia Mulder), Juno, Beth (Alex Reid), Chris (Nikki Graham), and Holly (Jenny McAlpine). As they venture deeper into the caves, they discover a hidden underground chamber filled with ancient fossils and strange rock formations. However, their excitement is short-lived, as they soon realize that they are not alone in the cave.

The group begins to experience strange occurrences, including hearing eerie sounds and finding signs of recent habitation. They soon discover that the creatures are humanoid in appearance, but have been mutated by some unknown force to live in the dark depths of the cave system.

As the group tries to find a way out of the caves, they realize that one of their own members has been infected with the creatures' venom, which is slowly turning her into one of them. The group's dynamics begin to deteriorate as tensions rise and paranoia sets in.

The creatures, known as "crawlers," are fast-moving and deadly, using their sharp claws and teeth to attack their prey. The group soon realizes that they must work together to survive, but their efforts are hindered by the claustrophobic environment of the cave system.

As the body count rises, Sarah becomes increasingly determined to find a way out of the caves and rescue her friends. She leads the group on a perilous journey through the tunnels, facing numerous challenges and terrifying encounters with the creatures.

In the end, only two members of the group manage to escape the caves: Sarah and Juno. They emerge from the cave system, battered and traumatized, but alive. The movie ends with Sarah reflecting on her experience, realizing that she has found a new sense of purpose in life and a deeper appreciation for the beauty and danger of the natural world.

Overall, The Descent is a tense and suspenseful horror film that explores themes of female empowerment, friendship, and survival in the face of overwhelming odds.

documents.title: Evolution
documents.tagline: Coming to wipe that silly smile off your planet.
documents.overview: A comedy that follows the chaos that ensues when a meteor hits the Earth carrying alien life forms that give new meaning to the term "survival of the fittest." David Duchovny, Orlando Jones, Seann William Scott, and Julianne Moore are the only people standing between the aliens and world domination... which could be bad news for the Earth.
documents.plot:
Evolution is a 2001 American science fiction comedy film directed by Ivan Reitman and written by Peter Farrelly and Bobby Farrelly. The movie stars David Duchovny, Orlando Jones, and Julianne Moore.

The story begins with Dr. Ira Levinson (David Duchovny), a paleontologist who has spent his entire career studying dinosaurs. He is obsessed with the idea of finding a way to bring back these prehistoric creatures to life. After years of research, he finally succeeds in creating a serum that can reanimate dead tissue.

However, things take a turn for the worse when Ira's lab is attacked by a group of thieves who steal his serum and use it to create an army of dinosaurs in modern-day New York City. The dinosaurs, including a Tyrannosaurus Rex, Velociraptors, and Triceratops, wreak havoc on the city, causing destruction and chaos.

Enter Ray Finkle (Orlando Jones), a former minor league baseball player who is now working as a security guard at a museum. He teams up with Ira's daughter, Dr. Maggie Levinson (Julianne Moore), to stop the dinosaurs and find a way to reverse the effects of the serum.

As the story unfolds, Ray and Maggie must navigate through the city, avoiding the dinosaurs and trying to find a way to shut down the serum's effects. Along the way, they encounter various obstacles, including a group of bumbling scientists who are trying to exploit the situation for their own gain.

Throughout the movie, there are plenty of humorous moments, courtesy of Ray's witty one-liners and his fish-out-of-water experiences in the scientific world. The special effects are also impressive, bringing the dinosaurs to life in a way that is both convincing and entertaining.

As the plot reaches its climax, Ray and Maggie finally discover the location of the serum's source: a secret laboratory hidden beneath the city streets. They must use all their wits and cunning to outsmart the villains and shut down the serum, saving the city from destruction.

In the end, Ray and Maggie succeed in stopping the dinosaurs and reversing the effects of the serum. The movie ends with a comedic twist, as Ray is hailed as a hero for his role in saving the city, despite having no scientific expertise whatsoever.

Overall, Evolution is a fun and entertaining movie that combines humor, action, and adventure. While it may not be a masterpiece of science fiction cinema, it is a lighthearted and enjoyable ride that is sure to delight fans of dinosaurs and comedy.

documents.title: Zoolander
documents.tagline: 3% Body Fat. 1% Brain Activity.
documents.overview: Clear the runway for Derek Zoolander, VH1's three-time male model of the year. His face falls when hippie-chic Hansel scooters in to steal this year's award. The evil fashion guru Mugatu seizes the opportunity to turn Derek into a killing machine. It's a well-designed conspiracy and only with the help of Hansel and a few well-chosen accessories like Matilda can Derek make the world safe for male models everywhere.
documents.plot:
Zoolander is a 2001 American comedy film directed, co-produced and co-written by Ben Stiller, who also stars in the title role. A satire of the fashion industry, it follows the vain and dim-witted male model Derek Zoolander, who is manipulated by the fashion mogul Jacobim Mugatu into attempting to assassinate the Prime Minister of Malaysia. Owen Wilson, Christine Taylor, Will Ferrell, Milla Jovovich, Jerry Stiller and Jon Voight co-star, and the film features dozens of celebrity cameos. The character originated in short films written by Drake Sather and Stiller for the VH1 Fashion Awards in 1996 and 1997.

Derek, a three-time male model of the year, is at a low point after the rising star Hansel McDonald beats him for the award, and his roommates and fellow models are killed in a freak gasoline-fight accident. Retiring from modeling, he tries to reconnect with his working-class family in the coal-mining region of southern New Jersey, but his father rejects him. Meanwhile, Mugatu and Derek's agent Maury Ballstein are secretly charged by the fashion industry with finding a model who can be brainwashed to kill the new Malaysian prime minister, whose plans to abolish child labor threaten the industry's supply of cheap workers.

Mugatu offers Derek a comeback as the face of his new fashion line, "Derelicte," and has him conditioned at a day spa to attack on cue when he hears the song "Relax" by Frankie Goes to Hollywood. Time journalist Matilda Jeffries, who wrote a scathing article about Derek, becomes suspicious and investigates, learning that models have been used as assassins for generations. Derek and Matilda seek help from Hansel, and the two rivals settle their feud in a walk-off judged by David Bowie, before racing to stop the assassination at Mugatu's fashion show and expose the conspiracy.

Released two weeks after the September 11 attacks, the film had digital edits removing the World Trade Center from shots of New York, and it was banned in Malaysia and Singapore. It received mixed reviews but grossed about $60 million worldwide, became a major cult favorite and spawned many widely quoted lines, including Derek's signature "Blue Steel" pose. A sequel, Zoolander 2, was released in 2016.
production_companies: MFP Munich Film Partners GmbH & Company I. Produktions KG

documents.title: Surf's Up
documents.tagline: A Major Ocean Picture
documents.overview: Surf's Up is an animated feature that goes behind the scenes of the high-octane world of competitive penguin surfing. The film profiles Cody Maverick, an up-and-coming surfer as he enters his first pro competition.
documents.plot: With a documentary crew in tow, Cody Maverick—a young surfer from Antarctica—travels to the pacific for his first professional competition. Determined to earn respect and live up to his idol, Big Z, Cody pushes himself to the limit. But all that changes when an encounter with a laid-back local forces him to rethink his values.

documents.title: The Dinner Game
documents.tagline: A feast for the senseless.
documents.overview: For Pierre Brochant and his friends, Wednesday is “Idiots' Day”. The idea is simple: each person has to bring along an idiot. The one who brings the most spectacular idiot wins the prize. Tonight, Brochant is ecstatic. He has found a gem. The ultimate idiot, “A world champion idiot!”. What Brochant doesn’t know is that Pignon is a real jinx, a past master in the art of bringing on catastrophes...
documents.plot:
The Dinner Game (Le Dîner de cons, literally "The Dinner of Idiots") is a French comedy of 1998 written and directed by Francis Veber, adapted from his own stage play. Thierry Lhermitte plays the Parisian publisher Pierre Brochant and Jacques Villeret plays François Pignon, the hapless guest he plans to mock, with Francis Huster, Daniel Prévost, Alexandra Vandernoot and Catherine Frot.

Every week Brochant and his fashionable, successful friends hold an "idiots' dinner", to which each must bring an unsuspecting fool, ideally someone obsessed with an absurd hobby, to be quietly ridiculed all evening. Brochant finds a prize candidate: Pignon, a cheerful employee of the Finance Ministry, an institution Brochant, a tax cheat, detests, who builds famous landmarks out of matchsticks. But after inviting Pignon to his apartment, Brochant throws out his back on the golf course, and his wife Christine, disgusted by his cruelty, walks out just before Pignon arrives.

Immobilized, Brochant has to rely on his guest, who bungles everything he touches. Asked to help track down Christine by phone, Pignon reveals Brochant's mistress Marlène, whom he takes for Brochant's sister, and invites her over. Mistaking the briefly returning Christine for the mistress, he advises her on how to win Brochant back, so that she learns of the affair and leaves again. Fearing Christine has returned to her former lover Juste Leblanc, Brochant's old best friend, Brochant coaches Pignon to call him posing as a film producer, but Pignon gives out Brochant's number. Leblanc, unexpectedly sympathetic, comes over to help. To find a womanizer Christine might have fled to, Pignon invites the tax inspector Lucien Cheval, forcing Brochant to hide his valuables; by coincidence Cheval's own wife turns out to be with the same man.

Gradually forced to face his faults, Brochant comes close to reconciling with Christine when Pignon calls her of his own accord, eloquently describing how Brochant has spent the day putting his life in order, and insists he is calling alone. Brochant apologizes for his arrogance. But when Christine calls back, Pignon absent-mindedly picks up the phone, and she hangs up convinced Brochant set him up, leaving Brochant once again calling Pignon an idiot.

The year's top French film at the domestic box office, second only to Titanic, it won three César Awards, including Best Actor for Villeret, and is widely regarded as a cult classic.

documents.title: The Royal Tenenbaums
documents.tagline: Family Isn't A Word ... It's A Sentence.
documents.overview: Royal Tenenbaum and his wife Etheline had three children and then they separated. All three children are extraordinary --- all geniuses. Virtually all memory of the brilliance of the young Tenenbaums was subsequently erased by two decades of betrayal, failure, and disaster. Most of this was generally considered to be their father's fault. "The Royal Tenenbaums" is the story of the family's sudden, unexpected reunion one recent winter.
documents.plot:
The Royal Tenenbaums is a 2001 American comedy-drama film written and directed by Wes Anderson. The movie follows the lives of the dysfunctional Tenenbaum family, who were once considered one of the most talented families in the world.

The story begins with Chas Tenenbaum (Gene Hackman), a successful businessman, who has just been released from prison after serving time for embezzlement. He is reunited with his three adult children: Richie (Ben Stiller), Margot (Gwyneth Paltrow), and Etheline (Anjelica Huston). The family's reunion is complicated by the fact that they have all drifted apart over the years, each pursuing their own unique paths in life.

Richie, a former child prodigy who was once considered one of the greatest tennis players in the world, has become a struggling writer. He is still haunted by his past and struggles to find meaning in his life. Margot, on the other hand, is a successful businesswoman who has built a reputation as a ruthless and cunning executive. Etheline, the family matriarch, is a complex and enigmatic figure who has been hiding secrets of her own.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that each member of the Tenenbaum family is struggling with their own personal demons. Richie's struggles with his past are exacerbated by his relationship with his mother, Etheline, who is still reeling from the loss of her husband and the failure of her marriage to Chas. Margot's success is built on a foundation of deceit and manipulation, while Etheline's secrets threaten to destroy the family's fragile relationships.

Throughout the film, Wes Anderson's signature visual style and attention to detail are on full display. The movie features a colorful and eccentric cast of characters, including Margot's love interest, Raleigh St. Clair (Luke Wilson), and Richie's rival, Henry Sherman (Owen Wilson).

As the story reaches its climax, the Tenenbaum family is forced to confront their past mistakes and weaknesses. In a dramatic and emotional confrontation, the family comes together to support each other and find a way forward. The film ends on a hopeful note, with the Tenenbaums finally beginning to heal and rebuild their relationships.

Overall, The Royal Tenenbaums is a beautifully crafted film that explores themes of family, identity, and redemption. With its unique visual style and memorable characters, it has become a cult classic and one of Wes Anderson's most beloved films.

documents.title: The Way of the Dragon
documents.tagline: The Colosseum . . the battleground of Bruce Lee and Chuck Norris.
documents.overview: Tang Lung arrives in Rome to help his cousins in the restaurant business. They are being pressured to sell their property to the syndicate, who will stop at nothing to get what they want. When Tang arrives he poses a new threat to the syndicate, and they are unable to defeat him. The syndicate boss hires the best Japanese and European martial artists to fight Tang, but he easily finishes them off.
documents.plot:
The Way of the Dragon is a classic martial arts film directed by Bruce Lee, released in 1972 under the title "Fist of Fury" in the United States. However, I will provide information on the original title and production company.

The Way of the Dragon (, Fēng Yǔ Bāo Huán) is a Hong Kong martial arts film produced by Golden Harvest. The movie stars Bruce Lee, Chuck Norris, and Nora Miao.

Beginning:
The story begins with Lee's character, Tang Lung (Bruce Lee), a Chinese martial artist who travels to Rome to participate in the "Battle of the Champions" tournament. However, upon arrival, he discovers that the event is being organized by the notorious crime lord, Mr. Han (Tung-Wah Chan).

Plot Development:
As Tang Lung navigates the complexities of the tournament, he also becomes embroiled in a plot to kidnap and kill a young girl named Christina (Nora Miao), who is the daughter of a wealthy businessman. The kidnappers plan to use her as leverage to extort money from her father.

Tang Lung teams up with an American truck driver, Scott (Chuck Norris), who becomes his ally in the fight against Mr. Han and his henchmen. Together, they devise a plan to infiltrate the tournament and rescue Christina.

Action and Martial Arts:
The film features some of Bruce Lee's most iconic martial arts sequences, including the famous "horseback fight" scene where Tang Lung takes on several opponents at once. The movie also showcases Chuck Norris's impressive fighting skills as he battles against Mr. Han's henchmen.

Ending:
In the climactic final battle, Tang Lung and Scott face off against Mr. Han and his men in a thrilling showdown. With his characteristic blend of speed, agility, and martial arts expertise, Tang Lung defeats the villains and rescues Christina.

The movie concludes with Tang Lung and Scott sharing a moment of camaraderie as they reflect on their shared experience and the lessons they've learned about friendship and loyalty.

Overall, The Way of the Dragon is an action-packed martial arts film that showcases Bruce Lee's charisma and fighting skills. While it was not released under this title in the United States, it remains one of Lee's most beloved films among fans worldwide.

documents.title: Kung Fu Hustle
documents.tagline: So many gangsters… so little time.
documents.overview: It's the 1940s, and the notorious Axe Gang terrorizes Shanghai. Small-time criminals Sing and Bone hope to join, but they only manage to make lots of very dangerous enemies. Fortunately for them, kung fu masters and hidden strength can be found in unlikely places. Now they just have to take on the entire Axe Gang.
documents.plot:
Kung Fu Hustle is a 2004 martial arts comedy film directed by Stephen Chow, produced by China Film Co-Production Corporation, and written by Stephen Chow. The film stars Stephen Chow, Zhang Manzi, and Yuen Biao.

The story takes place in the 1940s in the fictional city of Gong Tong, which is modeled after 1930s Shanghai. The film begins with a prologue that sets the tone for the rest of the movie: a flashback to the life of Sing (played by Stephen Chow), a young boy who dreams of becoming a kung fu master.

Sing's life takes a dramatic turn when he meets Master Pain (played by Yuen Biao), a renowned kung fu expert, and his sidekick, Thunderleg (played by Zhang Manzi). The two men are on the run from the notorious Triad leader, Boss Wolf (played by Danny Lee).

The story then shifts to the present day, where Sing is now an adult and working as a taxi driver. He lives in a small apartment with his mother, who runs a noodle shop. One day, a group of thugs, led by Boss Wolf, arrive at the noodle shop, seeking revenge against Sing's family.

To protect his mother, Sing teams up with Master Pain and Thunderleg to form an unlikely alliance. Together, they concoct a plan to defeat Boss Wolf and his gang. The trio uses their unique kung fu skills to outsmart and outmaneuver their opponents.

As the story unfolds, Sing becomes more confident in his abilities and begins to develop his own fighting style. He also starts to fall for a local woman named Princess Jasmine (played by Charlene Choi), who is being pursued by Boss Wolf's henchmen.

The film's climax features an epic battle between Sing, Master Pain, Thunderleg, and Boss Wolf's gang. The fight takes place in the streets of Gong Tong, with the trio using their kung fu skills to take down the thugs one by one.

In the end, Sing emerges victorious, having defeated Boss Wolf and saved his mother's noodle shop. He also wins Princess Jasmine's heart, and the two share a romantic moment.

Throughout the film, Stephen Chow showcases his impressive comedic timing and acting skills, as well as his mastery of kung fu. The film's blend of action, comedy, and music makes it a unique and entertaining ride.

Overall, Kung Fu Hustle is a hilarious and action-packed film that pays homage to classic Hong Kong cinema while also introducing new elements to the genre. With its colorful characters, witty dialogue, and impressive fight choreography, this film is sure to delight audiences of all ages.

documents.title: Charlie's Angels: Full Throttle
documents.tagline: This summer the Angels are back.
documents.overview: The Angels are charged with finding a pair of missing rings that are encoded with the personal information of members of the Witness Protection Program. As informants are killed, the ladies target a rogue agent who might be responsible.
documents.plot:
Charlie's Angels: Full Throttle is a 2003 action comedy film directed by McG and written by John Brancato, Michael Ferris, and Shane Black. The movie stars Cameron Diaz, Drew Barrymore, and Lucy Liu as the iconic Charlie's Angels trio.

The film begins with Dylan Sanders (Drew Barrymore) and Natalie Cook (Cameron Diaz), two of the top Angels, on a mission to stop a group of thieves who have stolen a valuable artifact. However, things take a turn when they discover that the thief is none other than their former partner, Madison Lee (Lucy Liu).

Madison has been working with a new partner, Alex Munday (Derek Zane Unger), and together they plan to steal a valuable diamond necklace. The Angels must use their skills and teamwork to stop them.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Madison's betrayal is not just about personal gain, but also about revenge against her former partners. She has been working with a wealthy businessman, Will Stacks (Derek Zane Unger), who has been using his wealth and influence to manipulate people and get what he wants.

The Angels soon discover that Will is behind the theft of the diamond necklace and that Madison's betrayal was just a ruse to get close to him. The team must now work together to stop Will and his accomplices, including a group of skilled thieves known as "The Shadow Syndicate."

Throughout the film, the Angels face various challenges and obstacles as they try to stay one step ahead of their enemies. Along the way, they also have to deal with their own personal demons and relationships.

In the end, the Angels successfully stop Will and his accomplices, but not before Madison reveals that she has been working undercover to bring down Will from the inside. The film ends with the Angels celebrating their victory and reflecting on the lessons they've learned about teamwork, loyalty, and trust.

Overall, Charlie's Angels: Full Throttle is an action-packed comedy that follows the adventures of three iconic female characters as they take on a complex web of villains and challenges. With its blend of humor, style, and high-stakes action, the film is a fun and entertaining ride from start to finish.

documents.title: DodgeBall: A True Underdog Story
documents.tagline: Grab life by the ball.
documents.overview: When megalomaniacal White Goodman, the owner of a trendy, high-end fitness center, makes a move to take over the struggling local gym run by happy-go-lucky Pete La Fleur, there's only one way for La Fleur to fight back: dodgeball. Aided by a dodgeball guru and Goodman's attorney, La Fleur and his rag-tag team of underdogs launch a knock-down, drag-out battle in which the winner takes all.
documents.plot:
Dodgeball: A True Underdog Story is a comedy film released in 2004 by 20th Century Fox. The movie follows the story of Peter LaFleur, played by Vince Vaughn, who owns a small dodgeball gym called Average Joes with his friends and employees.

The story begins with Peter's Average Joes facing financial difficulties due to the rise of bigger gyms in the area. In an effort to save their business, Peter enters a high-stakes dodgeball tournament with a grand prize of $50,000, which would allow them to pay off their debts and stay afloat.

However, things take a turn when Peter discovers that the tournament is being hosted by White Goodman, played by Ben Stiller, who owns a large and successful gym called Globo Gym. White is a ruthless and arrogant businessman who sees Average Joes as a threat to his own success.

As the story progresses, Peter's team faces numerous challenges and setbacks, including injuries, conflicts with their employees, and White's attempts to sabotage them. Despite these obstacles, Peter remains determined to save his gym and prove that Average Joes is more than just a small-time operation.

The plot thickens when Peter meets Patches O'Houlihan, played by Rip Torn, who becomes the team's coach and helps them develop their dodgeball skills. The team also recruits new members, including Steve the Pirate, played by Justin Long, and Fran, played by Christine Taylor.

As the tournament approaches, White's Globo Gym becomes increasingly aggressive in its pursuit of victory, leading to a series of intense and hilarious matches between Average Joes and Globo Gym. In the end, Peter's team faces off against Globo Gym in an epic dodgeball showdown that will determine the fate of their gym.

The movie culminates with a thrilling finale where Average Joes uses its unique skills and teamwork to take down Globo Gym and emerge victorious. The film ends on a high note, with Peter's gym saved and his team celebrated as heroes.

Throughout the movie, the characters are well-developed and relatable, with Peter being the lovable but slightly arrogant leader of the group. White Goodman is portrayed as a comedic villain who provides plenty of laughs, while Patches O'Houlihan brings a sense of wisdom and experience to the team.

Overall, Dodgeball: A True Underdog Story is a hilarious and entertaining film that combines witty dialogue, physical comedy, and heartwarming moments to create a truly unforgettable viewing experience.
production_companies: Mediastream Vierte Film GmbH & Co. Vermarktungs KG

documents.title: A Knight's Tale
documents.tagline: He Will Rock You
documents.overview: William Thatcher, a knight's peasant apprentice, gets a chance at glory when the knight dies suddenly mid-tournament. Posing as a knight himself, William won't stop until he's crowned tournament champion—assuming matters of the heart don't get in the way.
documents.plot:
A Knight's Tale is a 2001 medieval adventure comedy film directed by Brian Helgeland and starring Heath Ledger, Paul Bettany, and Shannyn Sossamon. The movie is set in the late 14th century and follows the story of William Thatcher (Heath Ledger), a poor squire who dreams of becoming a knight.

The film begins with William, a young man from a humble background, living on his family's farm. He spends most of his days helping his father, a blacksmith, and dreaming of adventure beyond their village. One day, the local lord, Sir Ector (Paul Bettany), announces that he will hold a tournament to find a new knight to serve him. William sees this as an opportunity to prove himself and become a knight.

However, there's a catch - the only way for William to participate in the tournament is if he can disguise himself as a noble knight. He comes up with a plan to pretend to be the son of a deceased knight, Sir Ulrich von Liebewort (Alan Tudyk), who was known for his bravery and skill on horseback.

William's plan works, and he gains the trust of Sir Ector, who becomes his mentor. As William prepares for the tournament, he meets Jocelyn (Shannyn Sossamon), a beautiful and talented jester who becomes his love interest. Meanwhile, William faces stiff competition from other knights, including the arrogant Count Adhemar (Rufus Sewell).

As the tournament progresses, William's skills as a knight are put to the test. He faces off against various opponents, using his wit, bravery, and cunning to outmaneuver them. Along the way, he also learns valuable lessons about honor, loyalty, and the true meaning of knighthood.

In the final match, William faces off against Count Adhemar in a thrilling jousting competition. Despite being outnumbered and outmatched, William uses his quick thinking and agility to gain the upper hand. In the end, he emerges victorious, earning the respect and admiration of the crowd and Sir Ector.

The movie ends with William being knighted by Sir Ector, who recognizes him as a true knight in his own right. William also wins Jocelyn's heart, and the two share a romantic moment. The film concludes on a high note, with William riding off into the sunset, ready to face new challenges and adventures.

Overall, A Knight's Tale is a fun and entertaining movie that combines action, adventure, and romance. Heath Ledger shines as the lead character, bringing a youthful energy and charisma to the role. The supporting cast adds depth and humor to the story, making it a delightful watch from start to finish.

documents.title: King Arthur
documents.tagline: Rule Your Fate.
documents.overview: The story of the Arthurian legend, based on the 'Sarmatian hypothesis' which contends that the legend has a historical nucleus in the Sarmatian heavy cavalry troops stationed in Britain, and that the Roman-British military commander, Lucius Artorius Castus is the historical person behind the legend.
documents.plot:
King Arthur is an epic historical adventure film of 2004 directed by Antoine Fuqua and written by David Franzoni, which recasts the legendary king as a Roman officer in fifth-century Britain rather than a medieval knight. Clive Owen stars as Arthur, with Ioan Gruffudd as Lancelot, Keira Knightley as Guinevere, Mads Mikkelsen as Tristan, Ray Winstone as Bors, Stephen Dillane as Merlin, Stellan Skarsgård as the Saxon leader Cerdic and Til Schweiger as his son Cynric.

As the declining Roman Empire withdraws from Britain, the native Woads, led by Merlin, wage an insurgency. Arthur, the half-British commander Artorius Castus, and his Sarmatian knights have completed fifteen years of compulsory service for Rome and are ready to go home. Instead Bishop Germanus orders one last mission: to rescue an important Roman family living north of Hadrian's Wall before an invading Saxon army under Cerdic and Cynric arrives, whose son Alecto may one day be pope. Arthur and his surviving knights, Lancelot, Tristan, Galahad, Bors, Gawain and Dagonet, reluctantly agree.

At the estate they find that the patriarch Marius, who refuses to leave, has enslaved the local people. Arthur frees two tortured Woad prisoners, Guinevere and her young brother, and forces Marius to leave. As the convoy flees through the mountains with the Saxons in pursuit, Marius attempts a revolt and is killed by Guinevere. Learning from Alecto that Germanus and the bishops had his beloved mentor Pelagius executed for heresy, Arthur grows disillusioned with Rome, while Guinevere and Merlin remind him of his bond with Britain through his Celtic mother. On a frozen lake Arthur's men confront Cynric's troops, and Dagonet gives his life breaking the ice with his axe to halt them. The knights deliver Alecto and his mother safely to the Wall and receive their discharge, but Arthur resolves to stay and fight with his mother's people. After a night with Guinevere, he confronts Cerdic under a flag of truce, and his knights return to fight beside him. At the Battle of Badon Hill, Lancelot kills Cynric but is mortally wounded, Cerdic kills Tristan and Arthur slays Cerdic, breaking the Saxon assault. Arthur marries Guinevere, Merlin proclaims him king of the Britons.

Released in July 2004, the film grossed $203.6 million worldwide against a $120 million budget. Critics were largely unimpressed, giving it 30% on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus called it a dreary, generic action movie.

documents.title: The Nightmare Before Christmas
documents.tagline: This is Halloween, everybody make a scene!
documents.overview: Tired of scaring humans every October 31 with the same old bag of tricks, Jack Skellington, the spindly king of Halloween Town, kidnaps Santa Claus and plans to deliver shrunken heads and other ghoulish gifts to children on Christmas morning. But as Christmas approaches, Jack's rag-doll girlfriend, Sally, tries to foil his misguided plans.
documents.plot:
The Nightmare Before Christmas is a stop-motion animated musical fantasy film directed by Henry Selick, produced by Tim Burton, and released by Walt Disney Pictures in 1993.

In the town of Halloween Town, Jack Skellington, the Pumpkin King, has grown tired of the same annual routine of Halloween celebrations. One day, while exploring the woods, he stumbles upon a portal to Christmas Town, a holiday-themed town filled with joy and cheer. Intrigued by this new discovery, Jack becomes obsessed with learning about Christmas and decides to take over the holiday himself.

Jack's attempts to understand Christmas lead him to recruit Santa Claus's elves to help him prepare for Christmas Eve. However, things quickly go awry as Jack's Halloween-themed ideas clash with the traditional Christmas customs. The result is a series of chaotic events that put both Halloween Town and Christmas Town in jeopardy.

Meanwhile, Sally, Jack's rag doll creation, tries to warn him about the dangers of meddling with other holidays. She also develops feelings for Jack, but her emotions are unrequited due to his infatuation with Christmas.

As Christmas Eve approaches, Jack's obsession with Christmas reaches a boiling point, and he decides to deliver presents to children all around the world on Christmas Eve. However, things don't go as planned, and Jack's attempts at gift-giving lead to a series of hilarious and disastrous consequences.

In the end, Jack realizes that Halloween and Christmas are two separate holidays with their own unique traditions and values. He also comes to appreciate Sally's love and acceptance for him. The film concludes with Jack returning to Halloween Town, where he is welcomed back as the Pumpkin King, and Sally finds happiness in her own right.

The Nightmare Before Christmas is a timeless tale of self-discovery, friendship, and the importance of embracing one's true identity. With its unique blend of stop-motion animation, catchy musical numbers, and memorable characters, this film has become a beloved classic among both children and adults alike.

documents.title: Daredevil
documents.tagline: A Guardian Devil
documents.overview: A man blinded in a childhood accident fights crime using his superhumanly-elevated remaining senses.
documents.plot:
Daredevil is a 2003 American superhero film written and directed by Mark Steven Johnson, based on the Marvel Comics character created by Stan Lee and Bill Everett. Ben Affleck stars as Matt Murdock, a blind lawyer who fights for justice in the courtroom by day and on the streets of New York as the masked vigilante Daredevil by night. Jennifer Garner plays Elektra Natchios, Michael Clarke Duncan plays Wilson Fisk, Colin Farrell plays the assassin Bullseye, and Joe Pantoliano, Jon Favreau and David Keith complete the main cast.

In 1982, young Matt Murdock is blinded in an accident involving radioactive waste, shortly after discovering that his father, the washed-up boxer Jack "The Devil" Murdock, has been working as an enforcer for a local mobster. Although he loses his sight, his remaining senses are heightened to superhuman levels, giving him a sonar-like ability to perceive his surroundings. Feeling responsible for his son's accident, Jack abandons crime and makes a boxing comeback, unaware that his victories have been arranged. When he refuses to throw a fight, he is murdered.

Twenty years later, Matt works as an attorney in Hell's Kitchen with his friend Foggy Nelson, representing clients he believes to be innocent, often for free. At night he dons a red costume to punish criminals who escape justice. Ben Urich, a newspaper reporter investigating Daredevil, is also pursuing stories about the Kingpin, a mysterious figure said to control organised crime in the city, who is in reality Wilson Fisk, a ruthless crime boss posing as a respectable businessman. Matt falls for Elektra, the daughter of a wealthy businessman linked to Fisk. When her father tries to break away, the Kingpin hires Bullseye, an Irish assassin who never misses, to kill him and frame Daredevil, setting Elektra on a quest for revenge against the man she loves and leading to a confrontation with both Bullseye and the Kingpin.

The film adopts a dark, brooding tone and explores the conflict between justice and vengeance, as well as Matt's Catholic faith and guilt.

Daredevil received mixed reviews but was a commercial success. An extended R-rated director's cut released in 2004 was considered an improvement, and a spin-off, Elektra, followed in 2005.

documents.title: Johnny English
documents.tagline: He knows no fear. He knows no danger. He knows nothing.
documents.overview: A lowly pencil pusher working for MI7, Johnny English is suddenly promoted to super spy after Agent One is assassinated and every other agent is blown up at his funeral. When a billionaire entrepreneur sponsors the exhibition of the Crown Jewels—and the valuable gems disappear on the opening night and on English's watch—the newly-designated agent must jump into action to find the thief and recover the missing gems.
documents.plot:
Johnny English is a 2003 spy comedy film directed by Rob Sitch and starring Rowan Atkinson as the titular character. The movie follows the story of Johnny English, a bumbling but lovable British secret agent working for MI7, the British intelligence agency.

The film begins with Johnny English (Rowan Atkinson) being introduced to his new boss, Pemberley (John Malkovich), who is impressed by Johnny's skills and assigns him to stop a plot by the villainous Vesper Lynd (Natalie Imbruglia). However, things quickly go awry as Johnny discovers that he has been replaced by a more competent agent, Johnny English Jr. (Ben Miller).

Despite his initial setbacks, Johnny English perseveres and sets out to stop Vesper's plan, which involves stealing the world's most expensive diamond, the "Regent Diamond." Along the way, he encounters a beautiful and intelligent woman named Natalie (Natalie Imbruglia), who becomes his love interest.

As Johnny English navigates through various obstacles and mishaps, he must also contend with his own ineptitude and the skepticism of his colleagues. However, with the help of his trusty sidekick, Bough (Simon Pegg), and a series of hilarious gadgets and disguises, Johnny is able to stay one step ahead of Vesper's henchmen.

Throughout the film, Rowan Atkinson's physical comedy and timing are on full display as he brings Johnny English to life. The movie's humor is clever and witty, with plenty of references to James Bond and other spy movies.

In the end, Johnny English successfully foils Vesper's plan and saves the Regent Diamond. Along the way, he also wins over Natalie's heart and proves himself to be a worthy secret agent in his own right.

Overall, Johnny English is a hilarious and entertaining film that showcases Rowan Atkinson's unique brand of comedy. With its clever plot, witty humor, and plenty of physical comedy, it's no wonder that the movie became a box office hit and spawned two sequels.

documents.title: Spy Kids 2: The Island of Lost Dreams
documents.original_title: Spy Kids 2: The Island of Lost Dreams
documents.tagline: Little Spies. Big Attitudes.
documents.overview: Exploring the further adventures of Carmen and Juni Cortez, who have now joined the family spy business as Level 2 OSS agents. Their new mission is to save the world from a mad scientist living on a volcanic island populated by an imaginative menagerie of creatures. On this bizarre island, none of the Cortez's gadgets work and they must rely on their wits--and each other--to survive and save the day.
documents.plot:
Spy Kids 2: The Island of Lost Dreams is a 2002 American spy action comedy written, directed, shot, edited and co-scored by Robert Rodriguez, the sequel to Spy Kids. Alexa Vega and Daryl Sabara return as Carmen and Juni Cortez, with Antonio Banderas and Carla Gugino as their parents Gregorio and Ingrid, Mike Judge as Donnagon Giggles, Ricardo Montalbán and Holland Taylor as their grandparents, Cheech Marin, and Steve Buscemi as the scientist Romero. Matt O'Leary and Emily Osment, in her film debut, play the rival agents Gary and Gerti Giggles.

Carmen and Juni are now full-time agents in the new Spy Kids division of the OSS, where they face fierce competition from Gary and Gerti, the children of Donnagon Giggles. After the Giggles siblings outshine them on a mission at the Troublemakers theme park, Donnagon manipulates his way into being named director of the OSS instead of Gregorio. Soon a group of Magna Men steals the Transmooker, a device capable of shutting down every electronic device in the world, and Gary frames Juni for the loss, getting him fired.

Carmen hacks into the agency's database, reinstates her brother and assigns them the mission of recovering the Transmooker, which takes them to a mysterious island where no electronics work. There they meet Romero, a reclusive scientist who tried to create miniature hybrid animals to sell but accidentally made them gigantic, and who now hides in his lab in fear of his own creations. Romero reveals that the stolen device was only a prototype and that the real Transmooker lies on the island. As Carmen and Juni brave strange creatures, from flying pigs to spider-monkeys, Gary and Gerti close in, and Gregorio and Ingrid, joined by Ingrid's parents, set out to find their missing children.

The film celebrates family, inventiveness and loyalty, and pays homage to stop-motion creature films such as those of Ray Harryhausen with its imaginative monsters.

Released by Dimension Films on August 7, 2002, the film opened in third place and grossed about 85.8 million dollars domestically. It received generally favorable reviews, with 75 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 66, and Roger Ebert gave it three out of four stars.

documents.title: Kung Fu Panda
documents.tagline: Prepare for awesomeness.
documents.overview: When the Valley of Peace is threatened, lazy Po the panda discovers his destiny as the "chosen one" and trains to become a kung fu hero, but transforming the unsleek slacker into a brave warrior won't be easy. It's up to Master Shifu and the Furious Five -- Tigress, Crane, Mantis, Viper and Monkey -- to give it a try.
documents.plot:
Kung Fu Panda is a 2008 computer-animated action comedy film produced by DreamWorks Animation. The movie follows the story of Po, a lazy and overweight panda who dreams of becoming a kung fu master.

The film begins with Po (voiced by Jack Black) living in the Valley of Peace, a serene and idyllic valley inhabited by various animals. Po is a food enthusiast and spends most of his days eating and lounging around. However, his life takes an unexpected turn when he is unexpectedly chosen by Master Oogway (voiced by Randall Duk Kim), a wise old tortoise, to be the Dragon Warrior.

According to legend, the Dragon Warrior is destined to bring balance to the Valley of Peace and defeat the evil snow leopard, Tai Lung. Po is initially hesitant and uninterested in taking on the challenge, but Master Oogway convinces him that he has what it takes to become a kung fu master.

Po begins his training with Master Shifu (voiced by Dustin Hoffman), a strict and demanding kung fu master who teaches him the ways of kung fu. However, Po struggles to keep up with the other students, including Tigress (voiced by Angelina Jolie), Monkey (voiced by Jackie Chan), Viper (voiced by Lucy Liu), and Crane (voiced by David Cross).

As Po's training progresses, he faces numerous challenges and setbacks, including a series of humiliating defeats at the hands of Tai Lung. Despite his struggles, Po perseveres and eventually discovers his own unique kung fu style, which combines humor, wit, and heart.

Meanwhile, Tai Lung escapes from prison and begins to wreak havoc on the Valley of Peace, threatening its inhabitants and destroying its harmony. Po must confront his fears and doubts in order to face Tai Lung and save the valley.

The final battle between Po and Tai Lung is an epic showdown that showcases Po's growth and development as a kung fu master. With the help of his friends and Master Shifu, Po defeats Tai Lung and brings balance back to the Valley of Peace.

Throughout the film, Kung Fu Panda explores themes of identity, perseverance, and self-acceptance. Po's journey is a metaphor for finding one's true purpose and embracing one's uniqueness. The movie also features stunning animation, witty humor, and memorable characters that have become iconic in modern animation.

Overall, Kung Fu Panda is a heartwarming and entertaining film that celebrates the power of friendship, teamwork, and believing in oneself.

documents.title: Pope Joan
documents.overview: A 9th century woman of English extraction born in the German city of Ingelheim disguises herself as a man and rises through the Vatican ranks.
documents.plot:
Pope Joan (German: Die Päpstin) is a 2009 epic historical drama film directed by Sönke Wortmann and produced by Bernd Eichinger, based on Donna Woolfolk Cross's novel about the legendary female pope. It stars Johanna Wokalek as Johanna, David Wenham as her lover, Count Gerold, and John Goodman as Pope Sergius II.

Shortly after Charlemagne's death, Johanna is born in Ingelheim am Rhein, the daughter of a harsh village priest. Studying the Bible behind her father's back, she proves far more gifted than her brother Johannes when the scholar Aesculapius visits, and he tutors her against her father's wishes. When a bishop's messenger comes for her, her father sends Johannes instead, but Johanna runs away, joins her brother and reaches the cathedral school at Dorestad, where a reluctant teacher accepts her. Count Gerold takes her into his household and falls in love with her. While he is away fighting for Lothair I, his jealous wife arranges Johanna's marriage, but Vikings attack during the wedding, killing Johannes. Disguised as a man, Johanna enters the Benedictine monastery at Fulda as Brother Johannes Anglicus. Her father, discovering her identity, dies of a stroke while trying to expose her, and when fever strikes the monastery, an old monk who knows her secret helps her avoid examination before she flees, finding shelter with Arn, whose daughter, Arnalda, she tutors.

Resuming her disguise, Johanna travels to Rome as a physician, cures Sergius II of gout and becomes his doctor and later his nomenclator. When Lothair marches on Rome, a hydraulic device swings the palace door shut as if by divine will, and his soldiers kneel. Gerold, in Lothair's army, recognizes Johanna, and she is torn between her two identities. After Lothair's ally Anastasius has Sergius murdered, the people acclaim Johanna as pope. She rules charitably, helping women and children, and makes Gerold head of the papal army, but she becomes pregnant. Gerold is killed by Anastasius's conspirators during the Easter procession, and Johanna dies in childbirth that day. Anastasius succeeds her but is soon deposed and exiled, and in revenge omits her from his history of the popes. Years later her story is revealed by Bishop Arnaldo, who is really Arnalda.

The film premiered in Berlin on 19 October 2009 and opened in Germany three days later. It reached the Italian box office top ten, but drew Vatican criticism, and the Italian bishops' newspaper Avvenire called it extremely limited in vision.
production_companies: UFA International Film & TV Production GmbH

documents.title: Anger Management
documents.tagline: Feel the Love.
documents.overview: After a small misunderstanding aboard an airplane escalates out of control, timid businessman Dave Buznik is ordered by the court to undergo anger management therapy at the hands of specialist Dr. Buddy Rydell. But when Buddy steps up his aggressive treatment by moving in, Dave goes from mild to wild as the unorthodox treatment wreaks havoc with his life.
documents.plot:
Anger Management is a 2003 American comedy film directed by Peter Segal, starring Adam Sandler as Dave Buznik, a man with anger management issues. The movie follows the story of Dave, who is sentenced to anger management classes after he loses his temper in court.

The film begins with Dave, a successful dentist, getting into an argument with his boss, George (Peter Greene), over a parking spot. This incident lands him in jail, where he meets a fellow inmate, Jack (Joe Viterelli). After being released on bail, Dave is forced to attend anger management classes, which are led by Dr. Buddy Rydell (Jack Nicholson).

Initially, Dave struggles with the classes, as his anger issues make it difficult for him to follow the rules and behave in a calm manner. However, he eventually warms up to Dr. Rydell's unorthodox methods, which include using hypnosis and meditation to manage anger.

As Dave progresses through the program, he begins to develop feelings for his instructor, Dr. Rydell's assistant, Miss Jones (Kate Beckinsale). Meanwhile, Jack becomes a source of support and guidance for Dave, helping him to navigate the challenges of anger management.

Throughout the film, Dave faces various situations that test his newfound skills, including a confrontation with George at work and a run-in with a group of thugs. With the help of Dr. Rydell's classes and Jack's advice, Dave is able to manage his anger and develop healthier coping mechanisms.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Dr. Rydell has ulterior motives for running the anger management program. He is using the classes as a way to gather information on his patients' personal lives, which he can use to blackmail them into doing his bidding.

In the end, Dave discovers Dr. Rydell's true intentions and must find a way to stop him. With the help of Jack and Miss Jones, Dave is able to outsmart Dr. Rydell and bring him to justice.

Overall, Anger Management is a lighthearted comedy that explores themes of anger management, relationships, and personal growth. The film features strong performances from Adam Sandler and Jack Nicholson, as well as supporting turns from Kate Beckinsale and Joe Viterelli.

documents.title: Man on Fire
documents.tagline: Creasy's art is death, and he is about to paint his masterpiece.
documents.overview: Jaded ex-CIA operative John Creasy reluctantly accepts a job as the bodyguard for a 10-year-old girl in Mexico City. They clash at first, but eventually bond, and when she's kidnapped he's consumed by fury and will stop at nothing to save her life.
documents.plot:
Man on Fire is a 2004 action-drama film directed by Tony Scott, starring Denzel Washington as John Creasy, a former CIA operative turned private security contractor. The movie follows the story of a man who forms an unlikely bond with a young girl and must fight to protect her from those who seek to harm her.

The film begins with John Creasy (Denzel Washington), a retired CIA operative living in Mexico City with his adopted daughter, Lupita (Pita) Ramirez (Dakota Fanning). Creasy has been working as a private security contractor, providing protection services for wealthy clients. However, he is struggling to connect with Lupita, who is being neglected by her mother and is in need of care.

One day, Creasy's life takes a dramatic turn when he meets Lupita's mother, Lucia (Pilar Lopez de Ayala), at a bar. He learns that she has abandoned Lupita, leaving her in the care of a corrupt police officer, Captain Silas (Giovanni Ribisi). Creasy is horrified by this situation and decides to take matters into his own hands.

As Creasy delves deeper into the world of organized crime, he discovers that Lucia's husband, Carlos (Raymond Cruz), is involved in human trafficking. He also learns that Lupita has been kidnapped by a group of Mexican gangsters who are being paid to sell her on the black market.

Creasy embarks on a perilous journey to rescue Lupita, facing numerous dangers and obstacles along the way. He encounters a corrupt police officer, Captain Silas, who is working with Carlos's gang, and must use his CIA training to evade capture and stay one step ahead of his enemies.

As Creasy navigates the treacherous underworld of Mexico City, he forms an unlikely bond with Lupita, who has been traumatized by her experiences. He teaches her how to fight and defend herself, and she begins to trust him as a protector and father figure.

The film's climax features an intense showdown between Creasy and Carlos's gang, which ends in tragedy for many of the characters. In the end, Creasy manages to rescue Lupita, but not before suffering severe injuries.

The movie concludes with Creasy reflecting on his experiences and the bond he has formed with Lupita. He realizes that he has found a new purpose in life, one that goes beyond his CIA training or private security work. The film ends on a hopeful note, with Creasy and Lupita reunited and beginning a new chapter in their lives.

Overall, Man on Fire is a gripping action-drama that explores themes of redemption, sacrifice, and the power of human connection. Denzel Washington's performance as John Creasy is particularly noteworthy, bringing depth and nuance to a complex and emotionally charged character.

documents.title: Garfield: A Tail of Two Kitties
documents.original_title: Garfield: A Tail of Two Kitties
documents.tagline: The Ego has landed.
documents.overview: Jon and Garfield visit the United Kingdom, where a case of mistaken cat identity finds Garfield ruling over a castle. His reign is soon jeopardized by the nefarious Lord Dargis, who has designs on the estate.
documents.plot:
Garfield: A Tail of Two Kitties is a 2006 American computer-animated comedy film produced by 20th Century Fox. The movie is the sequel to the 2004 film Garfield: The Movie and serves as a continuation of the original story.

The plot begins with Garfield (voiced by Bill Murray) and his owner Jon Arbuckle (voiced by Breckin Meyer) living in Muncie, Indiana. However, their peaceful life is disrupted when they receive an invitation to the royal wedding of Prince Lenny (voiced by Billy Connolly) and Princess Odie (voiced by Jennifer Love Hewitt). The couple's wedding is a grand affair, and Garfield sees it as an opportunity to indulge in the luxurious food and drink that comes with royalty.

Upon arrival at the palace, Garfield meets Prince Lenny's evil twin brother, Prince Nermal (voiced by Jason Alexander), who seeks revenge against his long-lost twin for being abandoned. The twins' rivalry leads to a series of hilarious misadventures as they compete for the affections of Princess Odie.

Meanwhile, Jon becomes infatuated with Princess Odie and tries to win her heart, but Garfield's attempts to sabotage their relationship only lead to more chaos. As the wedding day approaches, Prince Nermal's plan to steal the royal jewels comes to fruition, and Garfield must use his cunning and wit to stop him.

Throughout the movie, Garfield's sarcastic humor and witty one-liners provide plenty of comedic relief. The film also features a range of colorful characters, including Dr. Liz Wilson (voiced by Daryl Sabara), Jon's veterinarian girlfriend, who becomes entangled in the royal wedding shenanigans.

As the story unfolds, Garfield must confront his own insecurities and learn to put aside his rivalry with Prince Nermal. In the end, he helps save the day and wins over Princess Odie's heart. The movie concludes with a grand finale of laughter, excitement, and plenty of cat-titude.

Overall, Garfield: A Tail of Two Kitties is a lighthearted, entertaining film that delivers on its promise of humor and adventure. While it may not be as sophisticated as some other animated films, the movie's colorful characters, witty dialogue, and comedic antics make it a fun watch for both kids and adults.

Rating: 3.5/5 stars

documents.title: Chopper
documents.tagline: Never let the truth get in the way of a good yarn.
documents.overview: The true and infamous story of Australia's notorious criminal Mark 'Chopper' Read and his years of crime, interest in violence, drugs and prostitutes.
documents.plot:
Chopper is a 2000 Australian crime drama film written and directed by Andrew Dominik in his feature debut, based on the autobiographical books of the criminal turned author Mark "Chopper" Read. It stars Eric Bana as Read, with Vince Colosimo, Simon Lyndon and Kate Beahan. Read himself suggested Bana for the role after seeing him on the sketch comedy series Full Frontal.

In 1978, Read is an inmate at Pentridge Prison in Victoria, serving a sixteen-and-a-half-year sentence for attempting to abduct a judge in a bid to free his friend Jimmy Loughnan. When a fellow prisoner, Keithy George, warns him not to cross a line in the yard marking the territory of the Painters and Dockers gang, Read crosses it the next day and stabs him repeatedly. The gang puts a $10,000 contract on his life. Read recruits Bluey Barnes and Jimmy to help him wage war on the gang, but Jimmy, wanting no part in the suicidal plan, stabs Read and cuts his own arm to claim self-defense. Read recovers and is moved to a separate cell. When the prison board refuses to transfer him for his safety, he has his ears cut off so that he will be sent to a psychiatric wing, where he finishes his sentence.

Released, Read reunites with his girlfriend, Tanya. At a nightclub he flies into a jealous rage and fires a handgun, and when he later catches Tanya on the phone with Neville Bartos, played by Colosimo, he beats both her and her mother. Learning that Neville is a wealthy supplier of amphetamines to Melbourne's western suburbs, Read demands money and shoots him in the stomach when he refuses. He then visits Jimmy, who lives with his pregnant fiancée, Mandy, and their young daughter, claims that the police have given him a green light to shoot criminals, and confronts Jimmy at gunpoint about the contracts on his life before apologizing and giving him money. In the Bojangles car park, an associate called Sammy the Turk says he wants to show Read something, and after an argument, Read shoots him in the eye with a sawn-off shotgun.
