Mandy, who witnessed the killing, becomes a Crown witness. It emerges that Sammy had been leading Read into a trap for Jimmy to collect the contract but chose the wrong car park. Read is acquitted of murder but convicted of wounding Neville and sentenced to five years.

The film opened at number one in Australia in August 2000. It grossed A$5.9 million locally and received positive reviews, with critics singling out Bana's performance; it has since gained a cult following.

documents.title: Wedding Crashers
documents.tagline: Life's a Party. Crash It.
documents.overview: John and his buddy, Jeremy are emotional criminals who know how to use a woman's hopes and dreams for their own carnal gain. Their modus operandi: crashing weddings. Normally, they meet guests who want to toast the romantic day with a random hook-up. But when John meets Claire, he discovers what true love – and heartache – feels like.
documents.plot:
Wedding Crashers is a 2005 American comedy film directed by David Dobkin and produced by New Line Cinema.

The movie follows two friends, John Beckwith (Owen Wilson) and Jeremy Grey (Vince Vaughn), who have been attending their friend's weddings for years, pretending to be single men in search of women. They've made a game out of it, with each trying to one-up the other in terms of conquests.

However, things take a turn when they meet Claire Cleary (Rachel McAdams), the beautiful and charming daughter of a wealthy family. John is immediately smitten, but his attempts to woo her are thwarted by Jeremy's meddling. Meanwhile, Jeremy sets his sights on Claire's sister, Gloria (Isla Fisher).

As the wedding season approaches, John and Jeremy find themselves at a series of high-profile weddings, where they continue their antics and try to win over the women. However, things become complicated when they start to develop real feelings for the Cleary sisters.

The plot takes a dramatic turn when John and Jeremy are caught by Claire's father, Cleary (Christopher Walken), who is not pleased with their behavior. The two men are forced to pretend to be engaged to the sisters in order to avoid being banned from future weddings.

As they navigate this new reality, John and Jeremy must confront their own feelings for each other and figure out what it means to be true partners. Along the way, they learn valuable lessons about friendship, love, and growing up.

The movie features a talented ensemble cast, including Jane Seymour, Bradley Cooper, and Ken Davitian. The film's humor is witty and irreverent, with plenty of memorable one-liners and comedic set pieces.

In the end, John and Jeremy must decide whether to pursue their feelings for each other or stick to their old ways. The movie concludes on a heartwarming note, with the two friends finding love and acceptance in unexpected places.

Overall, Wedding Crashers is a hilarious and charming film that explores themes of friendship, love, and growing up. With its talented cast, witty humor, and memorable performances, it's no wonder this movie has become a beloved classic among comedy fans.

documents.title: A Prairie Home Companion
documents.tagline: Radio like you've never seen it before.
documents.overview: A look at what goes on backstage during the last broadcast of America's most celebrated radio show, where singing cowboys Dusty and Lefty, a country music siren, and a host of others hold court.
documents.plot:
A Prairie Home Companion is a 2006 American musical comedy film directed by Robert Altman, his final film before his death later that year. Written by Garrison Keillor, it presents a fictional behind-the-scenes look at the long-running public radio variety show of the same name, which Keillor created and hosted. The ensemble cast includes Woody Harrelson, Tommy Lee Jones, Keillor himself, Kevin Kline, Lindsay Lohan, Virginia Madsen, John C. Reilly, Maya Rudolph, Meryl Streep and Lily Tomlin.

In Saint Paul, Minnesota, the cast and crew of A Prairie Home Companion gather at the historic Fitzgerald Theater for what turns out to be the show's final broadcast, although the listening audience does not know it. A Texas corporation has bought the radio station and plans to demolish the theater, and it has sent a representative known only as "the Axeman" to oversee the closure. The story unfolds in real time over the course of the evening, as the live show proceeds between songs, comic sketches and fake commercials while the performers mingle backstage.

The evening is watched over by Guy Noir, a bumbling private detective turned security man, a character taken from a recurring segment of the real show. Among the performers are the singing Johnson sisters, Yolanda and Rhonda, who reminisce about their family's days on the gospel circuit, and Yolanda's moody daughter Lola, who writes poems about suicide; the bawdy singing cowboys Dusty and Lefty; and an aging country singer, Chuck Akers. Keillor, known as GK, calmly refuses to acknowledge that this is the last show. A mysterious woman in a white trench coat drifts through the theater; she is revealed to be the spirit of a listener who died in a car accident while laughing at a joke on the program, and who has returned as an angel to bring comfort and to escort someone away. The film reflects gently on mortality, tradition and the passing of an old-fashioned form of entertainment.

The film received mostly positive reviews and was a moderate box-office success on a small budget. Critics praised its relaxed, affectionate mood, its musical performances, which the actors sang themselves, and the ensemble, especially Streep and Tomlin. Because Altman died a few months after its release, many reviewers came to see its meditation on endings as a fitting farewell from the director.

documents.title: RV
documents.tagline: One Family. Eight Wheels. No brakes.
documents.overview: Climbing aboard their mammoth recreational vehicle for a cross-country road trip to the Colorado Rockies, the McNeive family – led by dysfunctional patriarch, Bob – prepares for the adventure of a lifetime. But spending two weeks together in one seriously small space has a way of cramping their style.
documents.plot:
RV is a 2006 American comedy film directed by Barry Sonnenfeld and starring Robin Williams, Jeff Daniels, and Kristin Chenoweth.

The movie begins with Chris Cooper's character, Bob Munro, who is a divorced father of two daughters, Beth (Kristen Stewart) and Mollie (Abigail Breslin). The family is struggling to cope with the recent divorce, and their relationship is strained. To take his daughters on a vacation, Bob decides to buy an RV, which he names "RV" after himself.

As they set out on their journey, the family faces various challenges, including a run-in with a group of bikers, a wild animal attack, and a series of misadventures along the way. However, despite these setbacks, the family begins to bond and reconnect with each other.

One day, while stopped at a rest stop, Bob meets a woman named Rachel (Cameron Diaz), who is traveling in an RV with her two children. The two families strike up a conversation, and Bob finds himself drawn to Rachel's warmth and kindness. As they continue on their journey together, Bob begins to realize that he may have found love again.

As the trip progresses, Bob's daughters begin to open up about their feelings regarding their parents' divorce. Beth is struggling to cope with her mother's departure, while Mollie is trying to navigate her own emotions and sense of identity. Through a series of heart-to-hearts with Rachel, Bob helps his daughters to work through their issues and find closure.

Meanwhile, Bob and Rachel's relationship blossoms, and they begin to realize that they have found something special in each other. However, their happiness is short-lived, as they face a series of challenges, including a breakdown on the road and a confrontation with a group of hostile travelers.

In the end, Bob and Rachel's love prevails, and they are able to find happiness together. The movie concludes with the two families reunited, and Bob's daughters finally finding closure and healing from their emotional wounds.

Throughout the film, Robin Williams delivers a standout performance as Bob Munro, bringing his signature energy and wit to the role. The supporting cast, including Jeff Daniels and Kristin Chenoweth, add to the humor and heart of the movie.

Overall, RV is a heartwarming and hilarious comedy that explores themes of love, family, and redemption. With its talented cast and engaging storyline, it's no wonder that this film has become a beloved favorite among audiences.

documents.title: Final Destination
documents.tagline: No accidents. No coincidences. No escapes.
documents.overview: After a teenager has a terrifying vision of him and his friends dying in a plane crash, he prevents the accident only to have Death hunt them down, one by one.
documents.plot:
Final Destination is a supernatural horror film directed by James Wong, released in 2000 by New Line Cinema.

The movie begins with Alex Browning (played by Devon Sawa), a high school student who survives a plane crash that kills everyone on board. As he's the only survivor, he starts to experience strange and unexplained events that seem to be connected to his near-death experience.

Alex soon discovers that he is having premonitions of people around him dying in gruesome and unexpected ways. He tries to warn his friends about these impending deaths, but they don't believe him. One by one, Alex's friends start to die in the most horrific ways possible, all seemingly connected to their own personal fears and anxieties.

As the death toll rises, Alex realizes that he is somehow responsible for these events, as if he has the ability to see into the future and prevent his friends from dying. He becomes obsessed with understanding the cause of these premonitions and tries to find a way to stop them.

The main antagonist of the film is Death itself, personified by a mysterious figure known only as "Death". Throughout the movie, Alex encounters various characters who are also aware of his ability to see into the future. These characters include Wendy (played by Ali Larter), a classmate who becomes Alex's love interest, and Clear River High School's principal, Mr. Smith (played by Jimmie E. Woods).

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Death is not just a random force of nature, but rather a malevolent entity that feeds on human fear and anxiety. The more people die, the stronger Death becomes.

In the climactic final act, Alex discovers that he can manipulate his premonitions to change the course of events. He uses this power to try and prevent Wendy from dying, but ultimately fails. In a shocking twist, it is revealed that Alex's ability to see into the future was not just a gift, but also a curse.

The movie ends with Alex realizing that he has become Death himself, trapped in a never-ending cycle of premonitions and death. The final shot of the film shows Alex standing alone, surrounded by the bodies of his dead friends, as the sound of a plane crashing echoes through the air.

Overall, Final Destination is a tense and suspenseful horror film that explores themes of fate, mortality, and the supernatural. With its clever plot twists and gruesome death scenes, it has become a cult classic among horror fans.

documents.title: Jersey Girl
documents.tagline: He wanted it all...but he got more than he bargained for.
documents.overview: Ollie Trinke is a young, suave music publicist who seems to have it all, with a new wife and a baby on the way. But life deals him a bum hand when he's suddenly faced with single fatherhood, a defunct career and having to move in with his father. To bounce back, it takes a new love and the courage instilled in him by his daughter.

documents.title: Prince of Persia: The Sands of Time
documents.original_title: Prince of Persia: The Sands of Time
documents.tagline: Defy the Future
documents.overview: A rogue prince reluctantly joins forces with a mysterious princess and together, they race against dark forces to safeguard an ancient dagger capable of releasing the Sands of Time – gift from the gods that can reverse time and allow its possessor to rule the world.
documents.plot:
Prince of Persia: The Sands of Time is a 2010 action fantasy film directed by Mike Newell from a screenplay by Boaz Yakin, Doug Miro and Carlo Bernard, based on a story by Jordan Mechner, creator of the Prince of Persia video game series. Adapted from the 2003 Ubisoft game of the same name, with elements from its sequels Warrior Within and The Two Thrones, it stars Jake Gyllenhaal, Ben Kingsley, Gemma Arterton and Alfred Molina.

Dastan, a Persian street urchin, is adopted by King Sharaman after showing courage. Fifteen years later, the king's brother Nizam presents the princes, Dastan and the king's sons Tus and Garsiv, with evidence that the holy city of Alamut is forging weapons for Persia's enemies, and Tus leads an attack. During the assault, Dastan takes a sacred dagger from a guard. Princess Tamina of Alamut denies that her city makes weapons and agrees to marry Tus only after seeing the dagger in Dastan's hands. At the victory banquet, a robe Dastan presents to the king turns out to be poisoned, killing Sharaman, and Dastan is accused of murder. He escapes with Tamina and discovers that the dagger lets its wielder turn back time.

Hoping to clear his name, Dastan reaches Nizam, sees burns on his hands and realizes that he poisoned the king. Nizam sends the Hassansins, secret assassins, after the dagger. Tamina explains that the gods once sent a sandstorm to destroy humanity but, moved by a girl's offer of sacrifice, sealed the Sands of Time in a giant sandglass that the dagger can pierce, and that Nizam means to go back to his youth, let Sharaman die in a lion attack and claim the throne. With the help of the opportunistic Sheik Amar, Dastan and Tamina head to a sanctuary to seal the dagger, but Garsiv is killed in an ambush and the dagger is lost. Dastan recovers it in Alamut and convinces Tus of the truth before Nizam kills Tus and seizes it. Beneath the city, Tamina sacrifices herself so that Dastan can fight on, and as Nizam plunges the dagger into the sandglass, Dastan grips it with him, rewinding time to the moment he first found the dagger. He exposes Nizam, who is killed by Tus. Tus proposes a marriage between Tamina and Dastan to unite the two nations.

Released by Walt Disney Studios Motion Pictures in May 2010, the film grossed over $336 million on a budget of $150–200 million, then the highest-grossing video game film. Critics were mixed, with 36% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 50.

documents.title: House of Flying Daggers
documents.overview: In 9th century China, a corrupt government wages war against a rebel army called the Flying Daggers. A romantic warrior breaks a beautiful rebel out of prison to help her rejoin her fellows, but things are not what they seem.

documents.title: The Exorcist
documents.tagline: Something almost beyond comprehension is happening to a girl on this street, in this house… and a man has been sent for as a last resort. This man is The Exorcist.
documents.overview: 12-year-old Regan MacNeil begins to adapt an explicit new personality as strange events befall the local area of Georgetown. Her mother becomes torn between science and superstition in a desperate bid to save her daughter, and ultimately turns to her last hope: Father Damien Karras, a troubled priest who is struggling with his own faith.
documents.plot:
The Exorcist is a classic horror film directed by William Friedkin, released in 1973 by Warner Bros. Pictures. The movie tells the story of a young girl's demonic possession and the two priests who attempt to exorcise the evil spirit.

The film begins with the introduction of Regan MacNeil (Linda Blair), a 12-year-old girl who lives with her actress mother Chris (Ellen Burstyn) in Washington, D.C. Regan is a happy and energetic child, but she starts to exhibit strange behavior, such as unexplained noises, convulsions, and changes in her appearance.

As the symptoms worsen, Chris seeks medical attention, but the doctors are unable to diagnose the cause of Regan's illness. Desperate for help, Chris turns to two Catholic priests, Father Damien Karras (Jason Miller) and Father Lankester Merrin (Max von Sydow), who specialize in cases of demonic possession.

Father Karras is a troubled priest who struggles with his faith due to the death of his mother and his own feelings of guilt. He is initially hesitant to take on the case, but eventually agrees to help Regan after feeling a sense of responsibility towards her.

Meanwhile, Father Merrin is an older, more experienced priest who has spent years studying the rituals of exorcism. He is tasked with performing the ritual to free Regan from the demon's grasp.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Regan is possessed by a malevolent entity known as Pazuzu, which is an ancient demon from Assyrian mythology. The demon begins to exert its influence over Regan, causing her to become increasingly violent and erratic.

The exorcism ritual is a tense and suspenseful sequence of events, with Father Merrin performing the ancient rituals to try and banish the demon. However, the demon proves to be a formidable foe, and it takes all of Father Merrin's strength and faith to complete the ritual.

In the climactic final scene, Regan is seen being thrown across the room by an unseen force, and she utters the words "Get me out!" as the demon is finally banished. The film ends with a sense of relief and redemption for Chris, who has been through a traumatic experience, but also leaves the audience with a haunting sense of unease.

The Exorcist was widely praised for its chilling portrayal of demonic possession and its thought-provoking exploration of faith and doubt. It is considered one of the greatest horror films of all time, and its influence can still be felt in popular culture today.

documents.title: Timeline
documents.tagline: They had to travel into the past to save the future
documents.overview: A group of archaeological students become trapped in the past when they go there to retrieve their professor. The group must survive in 14th century France long enough to be rescued.

documents.title: Tears of the Sun
documents.tagline: He was trained to follow orders. He became a hero by defying them.
documents.overview: Navy SEAL Lieutenant A.K. Waters and his elite squadron of tactical specialists are forced to choose between their duty and their humanity, between following orders by ignoring the conflict that surrounds them, or finding the courage to follow their conscience and protect a group of innocent refugees. When the democratic government of Nigeria collapses and the country is taken over by a ruthless military dictator, Waters, a fiercely loyal and hardened veteran is dispatched on a routine mission to retrieve a Doctors Without Borders physician.
documents.plot:
Tears of the Sun is a 2003 American war drama film directed by Antoine Fuqua and starring Bruce Willis, Monica Bellucci, and Dennis Quaid. The movie follows a team of Navy SEALs on a mission to rescue a group of women who are being held captive in Nigeria.

The story begins with Lieutenant A.K. Waters (Bruce Willis), the leader of an elite Navy SEAL team, who is tasked by the President of the United States to lead a team of operatives into Nigeria to rescue a group of American aid workers who have been kidnapped by a ruthless warlord named General Medu (Oscar Isaac). The aid workers, including Dr. Lena Kendricks (Monica Bellucci), are being held captive in a remote village and are subjected to brutal treatment.

As the SEAL team, which includes Lieutenant Waters' second-in-command, Chief Mike Banning (Dennis Quaid), and other operatives, infiltrate Nigeria, they face numerous challenges, including treacherous terrain, enemy soldiers, and local villagers who are hostile towards them. The team also encounters a group of Nigerian rebels who are fighting against the corrupt government.

Upon arrival at the village, the SEALs discover that the aid workers have been subjected to brutal treatment by General Medu's men, including being forced to undergo female genital mutilation. The SEALs launch a daring rescue mission, using their skills and training to take down the enemy soldiers and free the aid workers.

As the team fights to complete their mission, they also begin to form bonds with the aid workers, who are struggling to cope with their ordeal. Dr. Kendricks, in particular, forms a close relationship with Lieutenant Waters, which adds an emotional depth to the story.

The movie's climax features an intense and action-packed battle between the SEALs and General Medu's men, as well as a dramatic confrontation between Lieutenant Waters and the warlord himself. In the end, the SEALs successfully complete their mission, rescuing the aid workers and killing General Medu in the process.

Throughout the movie, Fuqua uses stunning cinematography to capture the beauty of Nigeria's landscapes and the brutality of its conflicts. The film also features a powerful score by James Horner, which adds to the emotional impact of the story.

Overall, Tears of the Sun is a gripping and intense war drama that explores themes of courage, sacrifice, and redemption. While it received mixed reviews from critics at the time of its release, the movie has since become a cult classic and is widely regarded as one of Bruce Willis' best performances.

documents.title: A Guy Thing
documents.tagline: Boy meets girl. Boy meets girl's cousin.
documents.overview: Paul Morse is a good guy. When his friends throw him a wild bachelor party, he just wants to keep his conscience clean -- which is why he's shocked when he wakes up in bed with a beautiful girl named Becky and can't remember the night before. Desperate to keep his fiancée, Karen, from finding out what may or may not be the truth, he tells her a teensy lie. Soon his lies are spiraling out of control and his life is a series of comical misunderstandings.
documents.plot:
A Guy Thing is a romantic comedy that explores the complexities of male friendships and relationships. The film delves into the theme of unrequited love, as the protagonist, Chris, navigates his feelings for his best friend's girlfriend, Amanda. This unrequited love serves as a catalyst for exploring the intricacies of male bonding and the blurred lines between friendship and romance.

The movie also touches on the idea of identity and self-discovery, as Chris struggles to reconcile his own desires with the expectations placed upon him by his friends and social circle. Through Chris's journey, the film highlights the challenges of growing up and finding one's place in the world.

Furthermore, A Guy Thing critiques traditional masculine norms, presenting a more nuanced portrayal of male relationships and emotions. The film suggests that men can be vulnerable, emotional, and open about their feelings without being perceived as weak or effeminate. This theme is particularly evident in Chris's character development, as he learns to express himself and confront his emotions in a way that challenges societal expectations.

Overall, A Guy Thing offers a relatable and engaging exploration of the complexities of male relationships, identity, and self-discovery, making it a charming and thought-provoking romantic comedy.

documents.title: Convoy
documents.tagline: Ain't nothin' gonna get in their way!
documents.overview: Trucker Rubber Duck and his buddies Pig Pen, Widow Woman and Spider Mike use their CB radios to warn one another of the presence of cops. But conniving Sheriff Wallace is hip to the truckers' tactics, and begins tricking the drivers through his own CB broadcasts. Facing constant harassment from the law, Rubber Duck and his pals use their radios to coordinate a vast convoy and rule the road.

documents.title: Open Water 2: Adrift
documents.tagline: Fatigue. Hypothermia. Death.
documents.overview: A weekend cruise on a luxurious party yacht goes horribly wrong for a group of old high-school friends when they get stuck in the water many miles from shore and a happy reunion turns into a fight for survival.
documents.plot:
Open Water 2: Adrift, also known simply as Adrift, is a 2006 German English-language survival thriller directed by Hans Horn. Susan May Pratt, Richard Speight Jr., Niklaus Lange, Ali Hillis, Cameron Richardson and Eric Dane star as a group of friends stranded in the open sea. Marketed as the second entry in the Open Water series, it is not a direct sequel to the 2003 film, and it was inspired by the short story "Adrift" by the Japanese author Koji Suzuki, from which it took its original title. Lionsgate released it on DVD in the United States in February 2007.

Dan, a wealthy man who has just bought a new yacht, invites his old school friends for a weekend cruise. Among them are Amy and her husband James, who bring their infant daughter Sarah, along with Zach, Lauren and Dan's new girlfriend Michelle. Amy has been terrified of water ever since her father drowned while swimming with her when she was a child, and she refuses to remove her life jacket even on deck.

Far out at sea, most of the friends jump into the water for a swim, while Amy stays aboard with the baby. As a joke, Dan scoops Amy up and leaps overboard with her, ignoring her screams. Only then does the group realise that no one has lowered the boarding ladder. The hull is too high and smooth to climb, and the baby is left alone on deck. The friends try every idea they can think of to get back aboard, including tying their swimsuits together into a makeshift rope, while their strength slowly fades. A passing boat full of teenagers mistakes their frantic waving for a friendly greeting and sails away, and a mobile phone ringing in clothes hanging over the deck remains frustratingly out of reach. As the hours pass, exhaustion, panic and old resentments turn the friends against one another, with fatal consequences.

The film builds its tension around a simple, plausible premise, with almost all of the action taking place in the water beside the yacht. Amy's phobia gives the story its emotional core, as she must overcome her fear in order to save her daughter.

The film received mixed reviews, holding an approval rating of about 45 percent on Rotten Tomatoes; critics praised its claustrophobic premise and some of the performances, but found the characters unsympathetic and their decisions frustrating. It was later released on Blu-ray in 2010 as a double feature with the original Open Water.

documents.tagline: To look into his mask was to lose your soul.
documents.overview: Paris, 1830. In the heart of the town, Vidocq, a famous detective, disappears as he fights the Alchemist, an assassin that he has been pursuing for a few months. His young biographer, Etienne Boisset, decides to avenge Vidocq's death and takes the investigation on...

documents.title: Big Momma's House
documents.tagline: This FBI agent is going undercover... and he's concealing more than a weapon.
documents.overview: When a street-smart FBI agent is sent to Georgia to protect a beautiful single mother and her son from an escaped convict, he is forced to impersonate a crass Southern granny known as Big Momma in order to remain incognito.
documents.plot:
Big Momma's House is a comedy film released in 2000, directed by Raja Gosnell and produced by 20th Century Fox. The movie stars Martin Lawrence as Malcolm Turner, a former FBI agent who goes undercover to infiltrate a group of thieves.

The story begins with Malcolm Turner (Martin Lawrence), a tough and skilled FBI agent who is tasked with taking down a group of professional thieves known as the "Big Momma's Gang." The gang is led by a mysterious woman named Big Momma, whose true identity remains unknown. Malcolm is given a disguise - that of an elderly woman named Mama Leona - to infiltrate the gang and gather evidence against them.

As Mama Leona, Malcolm must navigate his new life as an elderly woman, complete with a wig, glasses, and a cane. He struggles to adjust to his new persona, but eventually becomes more confident in his disguise. Meanwhile, he befriends the gang members, including Frankie (Paul Satterfield), who becomes his unlikely ally.

As Malcolm gains the trust of the gang, he discovers that Big Momma is not just any ordinary thief, but a mastermind with a complex plan to steal millions of dollars from a wealthy businessman. The gang's leader, Big Momma, has a personal vendetta against the businessman and will stop at nothing to get what she wants.

As Malcolm delves deeper into the gang's operations, he must balance his undercover work with his growing feelings for Frankie's sister, Sherry (Jessica Lundy). However, his cover is threatened when one of the gang members discovers his true identity as a man.

In the end, Malcolm and Big Momma engage in an epic battle of wits, with Malcolm using his FBI training to outsmart her. The movie culminates in a thrilling showdown between Malcolm and Big Momma, resulting in the downfall of the gang and the exposure of their nefarious plans.

Throughout the movie, Martin Lawrence delivers a hilarious performance as the bumbling but lovable Mama Leona, bringing humor and charm to the film's lighthearted moments. The chemistry between Malcolm and Frankie adds an extra layer of comedy to the story, making Big Momma's House a fun and entertaining ride from start to finish.

Overall, Big Momma's House is a classic comedy film that showcases Martin Lawrence's comedic talents and provides plenty of laughs along the way.

documents.title: Metropolis
documents.tagline: Welcome to Metropolis
documents.overview: Kenichi and his detective uncle, Shunsaku Ban, leave Japan to visit Metropolis, in search of the criminal, Dr. Laughton. However, when they finally find Dr. Laughton, Kenichi and Shunsaku find themselves seperated and plunged into the middle of a larger conspiracy. While Shunsaku searches for his nephew and explanations, Kenichi tries to protect Tima (a mysterious young girl), from Duke Red and his adopted son Rock, both of whom have very different reasons for wanting to find her.
documents.plot:
Metropolis (Japanese: Metoroporisu) is a 2001 Japanese animated cyberpunk drama film loosely based on Osamu Tezuka's 1949 manga of the same name. It was directed by Rintaro from a screenplay by Katsuhiro Otomo and produced by Madhouse, with conceptual support from Tezuka Productions. The Japanese voice cast includes Kei Kobayashi, Yuka Imoto, Kōki Okada, Tarō Ishida and Kōsei Tomita.

In the vast, plutocratic city of Metropolis, humans live alongside robots built to construct and maintain it, but the city's impoverished citizens, forced into its squalid lower levels, resent the machines and blame them for their unemployment. Duke Red, the city's richest and most powerful man, celebrates the completion of the Ziggurat, a colossal skyscraper housing military and scientific facilities. His adopted son Rock leads the Marduks, a paramilitary group that hunts down rogue robots. Meanwhile, the Japanese detective Shunsaku Ban and his young nephew Kenichi arrive in Metropolis to arrest Dr. Laughton, a scientist wanted for organ trafficking. Unknown to them, Red has secretly hired Laughton to build an extraordinarily advanced android, modeled on and named after his late daughter, Tima, who is to serve as the central control unit of a superweapon hidden atop the Ziggurat that will allow him to dominate the world. Jealous of the android, Rock shoots Laughton and sets his laboratory on fire. In the chaos Kenichi finds the newly awakened Tima, and the two fall into the city's sewers, separated from Shunsaku. As they make their way through the lower city, Kenichi protects Tima, who does not know that she is a robot, and the two grow close as her humanity develops. Their journey brings them into contact with a human resistance movement planning a revolution, while political intrigue, a ruthless military commander and the obsessed Rock all close in on them, and Tima's true nature and purpose threaten to bring catastrophe to the city.

Metropolis received highly positive reviews. On Rotten Tomatoes it has an 87% approval rating based on 67 reviews, with a consensus that its eye-popping visuals more than compensate for its relatively routine story, and Metacritic assigned it a score of 75 out of 100. Roger Ebert of the Chicago Sun-Times gave it four out of four stars, calling it one of the best animated films he had ever seen.

documents.title: Spider
documents.tagline: The only thing worse than losing your mind... is finding it again.
documents.overview: A mentally disturbed man takes residence in a halfway house. His mind gradually slips back into the realm created by his illness, where he replays a key part of his childhood.
documents.plot:
Spider is a 2002 psychological thriller produced and directed by David Cronenberg, based on Patrick McGrath's 1990 novel of the same name, which McGrath adapted for the screen himself. Ralph Fiennes stars as a mentally ill man haunted by his childhood, with Miranda Richardson, Gabriel Byrne, Lynn Redgrave and John Neville. The film premiered in competition at the 2002 Cannes Film Festival and received only a small release at the end of the year through Sony Pictures Classics, but it was highly praised by critics.

Dennis Cleg, known since childhood as "Spider", is a schizophrenic man who has just been discharged from a psychiatric institution after many years. He is placed in a grim halfway house in London's East End for people with mental illness, run by the stern landlady Mrs. Wilkinson. Scribbling in an illegible script in a notebook, Spider wanders the derelict streets, gasworks and canal of the neighbourhood where he grew up and pieces together his memories of a fateful period of his childhood in the 1950s.

In these memories, which he watches as a silent adult onlooker, young Spider lives with his loving mother and his father Bill, a plumber who drinks in the local pub. Bill begins an affair with Yvonne, a coarse local prostitute, and in the boy's recollection the two lovers murder his mother with a spade one night and bury her in an allotment. Yvonne then moves into the family home and takes the dead woman's place, presenting herself as Spider's new mother to the boy's horror.

In the present, Spider's grip on reality weakens. He begins to see Mrs. Wilkinson's face turn into Yvonne's, stretches webs of string across his room, and steals the landlady's keys to sneak into rooms of the house. His memories move towards a second death: the young Spider rigs a contraption of string to turn on the gas in the kitchen while Yvonne sleeps. But when the body is carried out, it is his mother lying there. The truth emerges that there was never any murder by his father and no Yvonne in the house: the boy, consumed by delusion, killed his own mother and recast her as a stranger.

Late one night the adult Spider creeps into Mrs. Wilkinson's room, still seeing her alternately as Yvonne, but he stops when she wakes and becomes herself again. She reports him, and he is taken back to the asylum.

Spider has 85% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 83, and Cronenberg won the Genie Award for Best Director. Fiennes and Richardson were widely praised.

documents.title: The Fast and the Furious: Tokyo Drift
documents.original_title: The Fast and the Furious: Tokyo Drift
documents.tagline: On the streets of Tokyo, speed needs no translation.
documents.overview: In order to avoid a jail sentence, Sean Boswell heads to Tokyo to live with his military father. In a low-rent section of the city, Shaun gets caught up in the underground world of drift racing
documents.plot:
The Fast and the Furious: Tokyo Drift is an action-packed film that delves into the world of street racing and drift culture in Tokyo, Japan. At its core, the movie explores the theme of identity and belonging. The protagonist, Sean Boswell, played by Lucas Black, is a rebellious teenager from California who gets sent to live with his father's friend in Tokyo after getting into trouble at home.

As Sean navigates this new environment, he struggles to find his place among the Japanese youth culture, particularly the drift racing community. He is drawn to the thrill and camaraderie of drifting, but also grapples with feelings of isolation and disconnection from his own identity.

The film's portrayal of Tokyo's vibrant street culture serves as a backdrop for Sean's journey of self-discovery. The city becomes a character in its own right, with its neon-lit streets, bustling markets, and intricate social hierarchies providing a rich tapestry for the story to unfold.

Through Sean's experiences, the movie touches on themes of cultural exchange, adaptation, and the search for belonging. As he learns to navigate the complexities of Japanese youth culture, Sean must also confront his own values and loyalties, ultimately discovering a sense of purpose and identity that is both authentic and true to himself.

The film's action-packed sequences and high-stakes racing scenes serve as a metaphor for the thrill and excitement of exploring new horizons and pushing oneself beyond one's limits. Ultimately, The Fast and the Furious: Tokyo Drift is a story about finding one's place in the world, embracing cultural differences, and discovering the true meaning of belonging.

documents.title: The Order
documents.tagline: Every soul has its price.
documents.overview: For centuries, a secret Order of priests has existed within the Church. A renegade priest, Father Alex Bernier, is sent to Rome to investigate the mysterious death of one of the Order's most revered members. Following a series of strangely similar killings, Bernier launches an investigation that forces him to confront unimaginable evil.
documents.plot:
The Order, also released as The Sin Eater, is a 2003 supernatural mystery thriller written and directed by Brian Helgeland. It reunites the director with Heath Ledger, Mark Addy and Shannyn Sossamon, whom he had directed in A Knight's Tale (2001), alongside Benno Fürmann and Peter Weller. The story follows a young priest investigating a suspicious death in Rome who uncovers a sin eater, a figure able to absolve sins outside the Church's authority.

Father Alex Bernier, a disillusioned member of the Carolingians, a fictional order devoted to exorcism and fighting demonic forces, learns that the order's head, Father Dominic, has died mysteriously in Rome. Cardinal Driscoll, an influential Vatican figure and candidate for the papacy, sends him to investigate. Before he leaves, he is visited by Mara Williams, an artist he once tried to exorcise, who had attacked him during the rite and been committed to an asylum; she senses he is in danger, and he lets her come along. Examining Dominic's body, Alex recognises marks left by a sin eater. With his fellow Carolingian Thomas Garrett, he secretly buries Dominic, who was excommunicated and denied consecrated ground. Driscoll gives Alex an ancient dagger and a fragment of parchment bearing an Aramaic incantation, which Alex takes to be a means of destroying the sin eater. Seeking answers, Alex and Thomas are led to the mysterious Black Pope of an underground sect, and a riddle from a dying man brings Alex to the sin eater himself, William Eden, at St. Peter's Basilica, while Thomas is hurt by demons. The weary, centuries-old Eden wants Alex to succeed him, but Alex refuses, intending to leave the priesthood for Mara. Eden then fatally wounds Mara, disguising it as a suicide attempt, and Alex eats her sins so she can reach heaven. Thomas discovers that Driscoll is the Black Pope and that the full text reveals the dagger rite transfers the sin eater's power. Too late to warn him, he arrives after Alex has stabbed Eden and inherited the role. Dominic, Eden and Driscoll had all used him. Alex exposes Driscoll, refuses to absolve him when the ruined cardinal attempts suicide, and resolves to grant salvation only to those he judges worthy.

Ledger plays Alex, with Sossamon as Mara, Fürmann as Eden, Addy as Thomas and Weller as Driscoll. 20th Century Fox released it on September 5, 2003. Critics panned it, giving it 10% on Rotten Tomatoes, with Rolling Stone's Peter Travers dismissing it as "The Exorcist warmed over".
production_companies: N1 European Film Produktions GmbH & Co. KG

documents.title: Dante's Peak
documents.tagline: The pressure is building...
documents.overview: Volcanologist Harry Dalton comes to the sleepy town of Dante's Peak to investigate the recent rumblings of the dormant volcano the burg is named for. Before long, his worst fears are realized when a massive eruption hits, and immediately, Harry, the mayor and the townspeople find themselves fighting for their lives amid a catastrophic nightmare.
documents.plot:
Dante's Peak is a 1997 American disaster film directed by Roger Donaldson and starring Pierce Brosnan, Linda Hamilton, and Jamie Renée Smith.

The movie begins with Dr. Harry Dalton (Pierce Brosnan), a volcanologist who has spent his life studying volcanic eruptions. He is married to Dr. Kate McCord (Linda Hamilton), a geologist, and they have a young daughter named Nicki (Jamie Renée Smith). The family lives in the small town of Dante's Peak, which is located near an active volcano.

As the story unfolds, Harry becomes increasingly obsessed with his work, neglecting his family life. Kate, on the other hand, tries to balance her career and family responsibilities. The couple's relationship begins to fray as they disagree on how to handle their daughter's education and Harry's increasing focus on his research.

Meanwhile, a series of earthquakes strikes the area, causing concern among the townspeople. Harry becomes convinced that the earthquakes are a warning sign for an impending volcanic eruption. He tries to convince Kate and the authorities to evacuate the town, but they are skeptical of his warnings.

As the situation escalates, Harry's predictions become more accurate, and he realizes that the volcano is on the verge of erupting. The family is forced to flee their home as lava flows towards them. In a desperate bid to save his daughter, Harry sets out to rescue Nicki from the town, while Kate stays behind to try and calm down the panicked townspeople.

As the eruption intensifies, Harry's vehicle becomes trapped in the ash-filled streets of Dante's Peak. He is forced to navigate through the treacherous terrain on foot, using his knowledge of volcanology to survive. Meanwhile, Kate tries to evacuate the remaining residents of the town, but many are too scared or too stubborn to leave.

In a heart-wrenching climax, Harry finally reaches Nicki, who has been trapped in her school. He fights off a group of panicked townspeople and makes his way back to his daughter, just as the volcano erupts in a massive explosion. The family is forced to flee on foot, with lava flows closing in behind them.

As they make their way down the mountain, Harry and Kate's relationship is put to the test. They must confront their differences and work together to survive. In the end, they manage to escape the volcano, but not without losing everything they had built in Dante's Peak.

The movie ends with a sense of hope and renewal as the family begins to rebuild their lives. Harry has learned the importance of balancing his work and personal life, while Kate has come to appreciate her husband's dedication to his craft. The film concludes on a hopeful note, suggesting that even in the face of disaster, love and determination can overcome even the most daunting challenges.

Overall, Dante's Peak is a thrilling disaster movie that explores themes of family, love, and sacrifice. With its stunning visual effects and heart-pumping action sequences, it has become a classic of the genre.

documents.title: Paycheck
documents.tagline: Remember the future.
documents.overview: Michael Jennings is a genius who's hired – and paid handsomely – by high-tech firms to work on highly sensitive projects, after which his short-term memory is erased so he's incapable of breaching security. But at the end of a three-year job, he's told he isn't getting a paycheck and instead receives a mysterious envelope. In it are clues he must piece together to find out why he wasn't paid – and why he's now in hot water.

documents.title: Elizabethtown
documents.tagline: It's a heck of a place to find yourself
documents.overview: Drew Baylor is fired after causing his shoe company to lose hundreds of millions of dollars. To make matters worse, he's also dumped by his girlfriend. On the verge of ending it all, Drew gets a new lease on life when he returns to his family's small Kentucky hometown after his father dies. Along the way, he meets a flight attendant with whom he falls in love.
documents.plot:
Elizabethtown is a 2005 American romantic comedy-drama film directed by Marc Forster. The story revolves around Drew Baylor, a young man who embarks on a journey to find meaning and purpose in his life after the sudden death of his father.

At its core, Elizabethtown explores themes of grief, loss, and self-discovery. Drew's emotional journey is marked by a deep sense of longing and disconnection, as he struggles to come to terms with the void left by his father's passing. As he navigates this complex emotional landscape, he begins to question the choices he has made in life and the relationships that have shaped him.

The film also delves into the complexities of love and relationships, particularly Drew's complicated bond with his sister Elizabeth (played by Kirsten Dunst). Their relationship is fraught with tension and unrequited feelings, serving as a poignant reminder of the fragility and beauty of human connections.

Furthermore, Elizabethtown touches on the idea of identity and how it is shaped by our experiences, relationships, and personal losses. Drew's journey is a metaphor for the search for one's true self, as he grapples with the notion that his life has been defined by external expectations rather than internal desires.

Ultimately, the film presents a nuanced exploration of the human condition, one that acknowledges the messy complexity of emotions and relationships while offering a message of hope and resilience in the face of adversity.

documents.title: Scooby-Doo
documents.tagline: Be afraid. Be kind of afraid.
documents.overview: The Mystery Inc. gang have gone their separate ways and have been apart for two years, until they each receive an invitation to Spooky Island. Not knowing that the others have also been invited, they show up and discover an amusement park that affects young visitors in very strange ways.
documents.plot:
Scooby-Doo is a 2002 American comedy-supernatural mystery film directed by Raja Gosnell and written by Daniel Waters. The movie is based on the popular Hanna-Barbera cartoon series of the same name.

The story begins with Fred Jones (Freddie Prinze Jr.), Daphne Blake (Sarah Michelle Gellar), Velma Dinkley (Linda Cardellini), Shaggy Rogers (Matthew Lillard), and Scooby-Doo (voiced by Neil Fanning) arriving at the Coolsville High School, where they plan to spend their summer vacation. However, upon arrival, they discover that the school is being haunted by a ghost.

The gang decides to solve the mystery of the haunting, which leads them to uncover a sinister plot involving a rival businessman, Emile Mondavarious (Tim Blake Nelson), who seeks to buy out the school's founder, Mr. Coolidge (John Mahoney). As they dig deeper, they discover that Mondavarious is using his wealth and influence to scare people away from the school, in order to drive down its value.

Throughout their investigation, the gang encounters various supernatural entities, including ghosts, monsters, and a mysterious curse. However, as they progress, it becomes clear that these events are being manipulated by Mondavarious's accomplices, who are using special effects and disguises to create the illusion of paranormal activity.

As the mystery unfolds, Shaggy and Scooby-Doo become increasingly entangled in the plot, often providing comedic relief with their antics. Meanwhile, Velma uses her intelligence and research skills to uncover the truth behind the haunting, while Daphne and Fred work together to gather evidence and expose Mondavarious's scheme.

In the end, the gang discovers that Mondavarious is using a combination of special effects, disguises, and manipulation to create the illusion of paranormal activity. They also learn that he has been trying to buy out the school in order to build a new shopping mall on its site.

With the truth revealed, the gang exposes Mondavarious's scheme, and he is brought to justice. The movie ends with the gang being hailed as heroes for solving the mystery, and they all share a laugh together as Scooby-Doo enjoys his favorite food, Scooby Snacks.

Overall, Scooby-Doo (2002) is a fun and lighthearted take on the classic cartoon series, with plenty of humor, action, and adventure. The movie stays true to the spirit of the original series while also introducing new characters and plot twists to keep things fresh.

documents.title: Cheaper by the Dozen 2
documents.tagline: Same Big Family... Even Bigger Adventure.
documents.overview: Steve Martin and Bonnie Hunt return as heads of the Baker family who, while on vacation, find themselves in competition with a rival family of eight children, headed by Eugene Levy,
documents.plot:
Cheaper by the Dozen 2 is a 2005 American family comedy film directed by Adam Shankman and written by Sam Harper. The movie is a sequel to the 2003 film Cheaper by the Dozen, which was based on the 1997 novel of the same name by Frank B. Gilbreth Jr.

The story begins with Tom Baker (Steve Martin), a successful businessman who has just been promoted to CEO of his company. He is now married to Kate (Nikki Griffin) and they have 12 children together, ranging in age from 1 to 16 years old. The family is known for their chaotic and loving nature.

The movie starts with the family preparing for the annual Baker family reunion, which is being held at a lake house. However, things quickly take a turn when Tom's new job requires him to spend more time away from home, leaving Kate to manage the household and care for the children on her own.

As the story progresses, we see the challenges that Kate faces in managing the household and caring for the children. She struggles to balance work and family life, while also dealing with the constant chaos caused by the 12 kids. Meanwhile, Tom is struggling to adjust to his new role as CEO and is often away from home, leaving Kate to handle everything on her own.

As the reunion approaches, the family comes together to support each other and work through their individual struggles. Along the way, we see glimpses of the children's personalities and quirks, including the eldest son, Charlie (Tom Welling), who is trying to navigate his senior year of high school.

Throughout the movie, there are many comedic moments as the family navigates their challenges and learns to work together. The film also explores themes of love, family, and the importance of supporting one another through thick and thin.

In the end, Tom and Kate come to a realization that they need to find a better balance between work and family life. They make some changes to their routine and learn to communicate more effectively with each other. The movie ends on a heartwarming note, with the entire Baker family coming together to support each other and celebrate their love for one another.

Overall, Cheaper by the Dozen 2 is a lighthearted and entertaining film that explores the challenges and joys of family life. With its talented cast and comedic moments, it's a great choice for families looking for a fun and uplifting movie experience.

documents.title: Asterix and the Vikings
documents.overview: Asterix and Obelix have been given a tough mission: Transform the chief's lazy nephew Justforkix into a warrior. When the Vikings abduct him and bring him back to their homeland, Asterix and Obelix must travel to Norway to rescue Justforkix.

documents.title: Ghost Ship
documents.tagline: Sea Evil
documents.overview: After discovering a passenger ship missing since 1962 floating adrift on the Bering Sea, salvagers claim the vessel as their own. Once they begin towing the ghost ship towards harbor, a series of bizarre occurrences happen and the group becomes trapped inside the ship, which they soon learn is inhabited by a demonic creature.
documents.plot:
Ghost Ship is a supernatural horror film released in 2002, directed by Steve Beck and produced by Village Roadshow Pictures.

The story begins with a salvage ship called the "Avalon" that has been missing for over 30 years. The crew of a modern-day salvage ship, led by Captain Peter Cullen (played by Julián Sands), discovers the long-lost Avalon while searching for treasure in the North Sea. As they board the ship, they find it to be remarkably well-preserved and intact, with no signs of decay or damage.

However, as soon as the crew sets foot on the ship, strange things begin to happen. They start experiencing bizarre occurrences, such as hearing eerie whispers, finding cryptic messages scrawled on walls, and encountering ghostly apparitions. It becomes clear that the Avalon is haunted by the spirits of its former crew members.

As the story unfolds, it becomes apparent that the ship was involved in a tragic accident 30 years ago, resulting in the loss of all hands on board. The crew soon discovers that they are not alone on the ship and that the ghosts of the dead sailors are trying to communicate with them.

The main character, Captain Cullen, is initially skeptical of the paranormal activity but eventually becomes convinced that something supernatural is at play. He teams up with a local historian, Dr. Vronsky (played by Jonas Armstrong), who helps him uncover the dark secrets behind the Avalon's disappearance.

As the crew delves deeper into the mystery, they realize that the ship was carrying a cargo of gold and other valuable treasures when it set sail on its ill-fated voyage. The ghosts, however, are not just seeking revenge but also trying to warn the living about the dangers of the sea.

The climax of the film takes place in the ship's engine room, where the crew discovers a hidden logbook belonging to the ship's captain. As they read through the entries, they learn that the captain had made a pact with a mysterious figure to ensure the safe passage of his crew, but at a terrible cost.

In the end, the crew manages to escape the ship, but not without realizing that some secrets are better left unspoken. The film ends with a sense of unease, as the survivors wonder if they have truly escaped the wrath of the Avalon's ghosts or if they will be haunted by their experiences forever.

Overall, Ghost Ship is a tense and atmospheric horror film that explores themes of tragedy, loss, and the supernatural. While it may not be as well-known as some other horror films, it has developed a cult following over the years for its creepy atmosphere and eerie plot twists.

documents.title: The Italian Job
documents.tagline: Get in. Get out. Get even.
documents.overview: Charlie Croker pulled off the crime of a lifetime. The one thing that he didn't plan on was being double-crossed. Along with a drop-dead gorgeous safecracker, Croker and his team take off to re-steal the loot and end up in a pulse-pounding, pedal-to-the-metal chase that careens up, down, above and below the streets of Los Angeles.
documents.plot:
The Italian Job is a 2003 heist film directed by F. Gary Gray and starring Mark Wahlberg, Charlize Theron, Donald Sutherland, and Jason Statham.

The movie begins with Charlie Croker (Mark Wahlberg), a charismatic thief who has just been released from prison after serving time for a botched heist. Charlie is reunited with his old crew, including Left Ear (Mos Def) and Right Ear (Jason Statham), but they are not as close-knit as they used to be.

The story takes a turn when Charlie meets Stella Bridger (Charlize Theron), the daughter of a wealthy businessman who has been kidnapped by a rival thief, John Bridger (Donald Sutherland). The kidnapper demands that Charlie steal $35 million from an armored car in Italy, but with a twist: he must use three Mini Coopers to navigate the treacherous Italian roads and retrieve the money.

Charlie agrees to take on the job, but things become complicated when he discovers that John Bridger is actually his former partner-in-crime. The two had a falling out years ago, and Charlie's crew is initially hesitant to work with him again.

As the team embarks on their mission, they face numerous challenges, including treacherous terrain, rival thieves, and a traitor within their own ranks. Along the way, Charlie and Stella develop feelings for each other, but their relationship is put to the test as they navigate the high-stakes heist.

The plot thickens when it's revealed that John Bridger has been working with a mysterious figure known only as "The Frog," who is using the stolen money to fund his own nefarious activities. Charlie and his crew must use all their skills and cunning to outwit The Frog and retrieve the money before it falls into the wrong hands.

In the end, Charlie's team successfully pulls off the heist, but not without some unexpected twists and turns. In a thrilling finale, they face off against John Bridger and The Frog in an action-packed showdown that leaves only one person standing.

Throughout the movie, the characters' banter and chemistry are on full display, with Mark Wahlberg delivering a charismatic performance as Charlie Croker. Charlize Theron shines as Stella Bridger, bringing depth and nuance to her character. Jason Statham's portrayal of Left Ear adds a fun and lighthearted touch to the film.

Overall, The Italian Job is a fun and entertaining heist movie that keeps viewers on the edge of their seats from start to finish. With its witty dialogue, memorable characters, and high-stakes action sequences, it's no wonder this movie has become a cult classic among fans of the genre.

documents.title: She's the Man
documents.tagline: If you wanna chase your dream, sometimes you gotta break the rules.
documents.overview: Viola Hastings is in a real jam. Complications threaten her scheme to pose as her twin brother, Sebastian, and take his place at a new boarding school. She falls in love with her handsome roommate, Duke, who loves beautiful Olivia, who has fallen for Sebastian! As if that were not enough, Viola's twin returns from London ahead of schedule but has no idea that his sister has already replaced him on campus.
documents.plot:
She's the Man is a 2006 romantic comedy film directed by Andy Fickman and produced by DreamWorks Pictures. The movie is loosely based on Shakespeare's Twelfth Night.

The story follows Viola Johnson (played by Amanda Bynes), a high school student who enrolls in an all-boys boarding school, Illyria Prep, after her twin sister Olivia (also played by Amanda Bynes) is cut from the school soccer team. Viola disguises herself as her brother Sebastian and assumes his identity to play on the boys' soccer team.

Initially, Viola struggles to navigate her new life at Illyria Prep, where she befriends Duke (played by Channing Tatum), a charming and popular student who becomes her confidant. As Viola tries to balance her secret identity with her growing feelings for Duke, she also catches the eye of Olivia's ex-boyfriend, Duncan (played by Vinnie Jones).

As the story unfolds, Viola finds herself entangled in a complicated web of relationships and misunderstandings. She falls for Duke, but he is unaware that she is actually his sister. Meanwhile, Olivia tries to win back her ex-boyfriend, causing tension between the two sisters.

Throughout the movie, Viola's disguise leads to various comedic situations, including her attempts to navigate male-dominated spaces and her struggles with her own identity. As she navigates her relationships and personal growth, Viola learns valuable lessons about love, friendship, and self-acceptance.

In the end, Viola's true identity is revealed, but not before she has formed strong bonds with Duke and the rest of the Illyria Prep community. The movie concludes with a heartwarming moment of acceptance and understanding between Viola and her sister Olivia, as well as a romantic gesture from Duke towards Viola.

Overall, She's the Man is a lighthearted, entertaining film that explores themes of identity, love, and self-discovery in a humorous and relatable way.

documents.overview: When her grandson is kidnapped during the Tour de France, Madame Souza and her beloved pooch Bruno team up with the Belleville Sisters—an aged song-and-dance team from the days of Fred Astaire—to rescue him.

documents.title: Flyboys
documents.tagline: Inspired by a true story
documents.overview: The adventures of the Lafayette Escadrille, young Americans who volunteered for the French military before the U.S. entered World War I, and became the country's first fighter pilots.
documents.plot:
Flyboys is an action-drama film that revolves around the lives of young American pilots during World War I. The movie delves into the themes of camaraderie, sacrifice, and the psychological effects of war on its participants.

At its core, Flyboys explores the bonds of friendship and brotherhood among a group of pilots who share a common experience in the trenches. As they navigate the dangers of aerial combat, they must also confront their own personal demons and learn to rely on each other for survival. The film highlights the strong sense of camaraderie that develops among these young men as they face the harsh realities of war together.

The movie also touches on the theme of sacrifice, as the pilots are forced to make difficult choices between their duty and their personal lives. Many characters in the film struggle with the moral implications of their actions, and the consequences of their decisions weigh heavily on them.

Furthermore, Flyboys examines the psychological toll that war takes on its participants. The film depicts the physical and emotional scars that result from experiencing the horrors of combat, including the loss of innocence, the breakdown of relationships, and the struggle to cope with trauma.

Overall, Flyboys is a powerful exploration of the human cost of war, highlighting the complexities and nuances of the experiences of those who fought in World War I.

documents.title: The Jacket
documents.tagline: Terror has a new name.
documents.overview: A military veteran goes on a journey into the future, where he can foresee his death and is left with questions that could save his life and those he loves.
documents.plot:
The Jacket is a 2005 American science fiction psychological thriller film directed by John Maybury and starring Adrien Brody, Keira Knightley, Kris Kristofferson and Jennifer Jason Leigh. Partly based on Jack London's 1915 novel The Star Rover, published in Britain as The Jacket, it was written by Massy Tadjedin from a story by Tom Bleecker and Marc Rocco, with music by Brian Eno and cinematography by Peter Deming.

Gulf War veteran Jack Starks survives a seemingly fatal bullet wound to the head and returns to Vermont in 1992 suffering from bouts of amnesia. On a roadside he helps a young girl, Jackie, and her alcoholic mother start their broken-down truck, giving Jackie his dog tags. Soon afterward he accepts a ride from a stranger, and the car is stopped by a policeman; Starks is later found by the road beside the officer's body. Unable to remember clearly, he is found not guilty by reason of insanity and committed to a mental institution, where the harsh Dr. Thomas Becker and the kinder Dr. Beth Lorenson oversee his care. Becker subjects him to an unauthorized treatment: he is drugged, bound in a straitjacket and shut inside a morgue drawer.

In this state Starks finds himself transported fifteen years into the future, where he meets an adult Jackie working at a diner. She takes him in for the night, but when he finds his own dog tags in her apartment, she tells him that Jack Starks died on New Year's Day 1993. On later journeys he gains her trust, and together they try to change his fate. Lorenson, meanwhile, risks her career to treat a friend's troubled son. Convinced at last by Starks's knowledge of the future, Lorenson takes him on January 1, 1993, to the home of Jackie and her mother, where he leaves a letter warning the mother that she will die after falling asleep with a lit cigarette, leaving Jackie orphaned. Back at the hospital, Starks slips on ice and hits his head, and bleeding badly, he persuades sympathetic staff to put him in the jacket once more. In 2007 he finds that his letter has transformed Jackie's life: she is now a cheerful nurse, and as she drives him to her hospital, her mother, alive and well, telephones.

The Jacket premiered at the 2005 Sundance Film Festival and was released by Warner Independent Pictures on March 4, 2005, grossing $21.1 million on a $28.5 million budget. Reviews were mixed, with 44% approval on Rotten Tomatoes, which called it creepy style over substance.

documents.title: Ringu 2
documents.overview: While investigating the horrifying death of her boyfriend, Mai Takano learns about a videotape haunted by the spirit of a disturbing girl named Sadako, which kills anyone who watches it exactly one week later. When her boyfriend’s son, Yoichi, starts to develop the same psychic abilities as Sadako, Takano must find a way to keep the boy and herself from becoming the next victims.

documents.title: Ringu 0
documents.original_title: リング０　バースデイ
documents.tagline: Discover the secret...
documents.overview: Taking place thirty years before the events of Ringu, Ringu 0 provides the shocking background story of how the girl on the video became a deadly, vengeful spirit.
documents.plot:
Ringu 0: Birthday is a Japanese horror film that delves into the darker aspects of human nature and the consequences of playing with forces beyond one's control. The movie revolves around a young woman named Reiko Asakawa, who becomes entangled in a web of mystery and terror when she discovers an eerie videotape that seems to be connected to her own troubled past.

At its core, Ringu 0 explores the theme of trauma and its lasting impact on individuals. Reiko's experiences with the videotape serve as a catalyst for her to confront the painful memories she has been trying to suppress. The film masterfully weaves together elements of psychological horror, suspense, and mystery, creating a sense of unease that permeates every aspect of the narrative.

One of the primary concerns of Ringu 0 is the blurring of reality and fantasy. As Reiko delves deeper into the mystery of the videotape, she begins to question what is real and what is just her imagination. This ambiguity adds to the sense of tension and uncertainty, leaving the audience wondering what is truly happening.

The film also touches on the theme of obsession and the dangers of becoming fixated on something that may be beyond one's control. Reiko's fixation on uncovering the truth behind the videotape ultimately puts her in harm's way, highlighting the risks of allowing oneself to become consumed by a singular focus.

Furthermore, Ringu 0 explores the idea of identity and how it can be shaped and distorted by external forces. Reiko's journey is marked by a struggle to reconcile her past and present selves, as she grapples with the consequences of her own actions.

Overall, Ringu 0 is a thought-provoking horror film that delves into the darker aspects of human nature, exploring themes of trauma, reality, obsession, and identity.

documents.tagline: In search of wine. In search of women. In search of themselves.
documents.overview: Two middle-aged men embark on a spiritual journey through Californian wine country. One is an unpublished novelist suffering from depression, and the other is only days away from walking down the aisle.
