documents.title: Turistas
documents.tagline: There are some places tourists should never go
documents.overview: A group of young backpackers' vacation turns sour when a bus accident leaves them marooned in a remote Brazilian rural area that holds an ominous secret.
documents.plot:
Turistas, released in the United Kingdom and Ireland as Paradise Lost, is a 2006 American horror film produced and directed by John Stockwell from a screenplay by Michael Arlen Ross. It stars Josh Duhamel, Melissa George, Olivia Wilde, Desmond Askew, Max Brown and Beau Garrett, with Miguel Lunardi as the surgeon Zamora.

American backpacker Alex is touring Brazil with his sister Bea and her friend Amy. After their bus crashes on a remote road, they team up with two British travelers, Finn and Liam, and Pru, an Australian who speaks Portuguese. The group finds a beach bar full of partying tourists, but after a day in the sun they are drugged and wake up on the empty beach with their money, luggage and passports gone. A young local named Kiko offers to take them to his uncle's house deep in the forest. On the way, he badly injures his head diving into a pool beneath a waterfall. At the isolated house, the travelers find medicine, supplies and a drawer full of other people's passports.

That night, a helicopter brings Zamora, a doctor who arrives with his medical team and armed men. The tourists are beaten and captured, while Kiko escapes. Zamora removes Amy's organs while she is still alive, telling the bound Finn that he is taking back what rich foreigners have taken from Brazil and sending the organs to a hospital in Rio de Janeiro to help the poor. With Kiko's help, the others break out of their cages. Finn is rescued but shot dead as they escape, and Liam stays behind to fight and is captured. The survivors flee through the jungle to an underwater cave, where Zamora kills Kiko and wounds Alex. Separated in the flooded passages, Bea kills an archer working for the gang. When the three survivors come out of the cave, Alex attacks Zamora with a rock, but henchman Jamoru arrives with a rifle. Ordered to kill the tourists, Jamoru instead shoots Zamora and walks away. Villagers take in the survivors. At the airport, Alex advises a pair of arguing tourists to take the plane rather than the bus.

Turistas was the first American film shot entirely in Brazil. It was also the first release from Fox Atomic, a label of 20th Century Fox, which opened it on December 1, 2006. It debuted in eighth place and grossed about $14.7 million worldwide. Critics were largely negative. Rotten Tomatoes' consensus said that beautiful scenery and cinematography could not make up for wooden acting and a stale, predictable plot.

documents.title: Enemy of the State
documents.tagline: It's not paranoia if they're really after you.
documents.overview: A hotshot Washington criminal lawyer becomes the target of a rogue security executive videotaped in the act of murdering a congressman when the incriminating tape is surreptitiously slipped into his shopping bag by the videographer, who is fleeing the executive's assassins.
documents.plot:
Enemy of the State is a 1998 American action thriller film directed by Tony Scott and produced by Jerry Bruckheimer Films. The movie stars Will Smith, Gene Hackman, Jon Voight, and Regina King.

The story begins with Robert Dean (Will Smith), an insurance investigator who works for a large corporation in Washington D.C. He is married to his wife, Dr. Margaret Dean (Regina King), and they have a young son together. However, their happiness is short-lived as Robert's boss, Franklin Haines (Jon Voight), assigns him to investigate the death of a former colleague.

As Robert delves deeper into the case, he discovers that his colleague was murdered by a group of rogue agents working for the National Security Agency (NSA). The agents, led by the ruthless and cunning Agent Albert Gibson (Gene Hackman), are using advanced surveillance technology to monitor and control the population. They have created a system called "The Net," which allows them to track anyone's movements and activities.

Robert soon realizes that he is being watched by the NSA and that his life is in danger. He goes into hiding, but Agent Gibson is relentless in his pursuit of Robert. As the stakes rise, Robert teams up with a computer expert named Kit (Gary Baseman), who helps him understand the extent of The Net's capabilities.

As the story unfolds, Robert discovers that he has been identified as an enemy of the state by the NSA. He learns that his investigation into the death of his colleague was not just a coincidence, but rather a deliberate attempt to expose the agency's wrongdoing. With Kit's help, Robert sets out to take down The Net and bring Agent Gibson to justice.

The plot thickens as Robert and Kit go on the run, using advanced technology to evade the NSA agents. Along the way, they encounter a mysterious woman named Susan (Linda Fiorentino), who becomes entangled in their quest for truth.

As the action unfolds, Robert's personal life begins to unravel. His marriage is put to the test as he struggles to balance his work and family responsibilities with his newfound mission to take down The Net. In a thrilling climax, Robert and Kit face off against Agent Gibson and his team in a high-stakes battle of wits and technology.

In the end, Robert succeeds in destroying The Net and exposing the NSA's wrongdoing. However, not before Agent Gibson reveals that he has been working for a shadowy organization known as "The Syndicate," which is pulling the strings from behind the scenes. As Robert returns to his normal life, he knows that there are still many secrets lurking in the shadows, waiting to be uncovered.

Overall, Enemy of the State is a gripping action thriller that explores themes of government surveillance, corporate greed, and personal freedom. With its breakneck pace and memorable performances, it has become a classic of 90s action cinema.

documents.title: Philadelphia
documents.tagline: No one would take on his case... until one man was willing to take on the system.
documents.overview: Two competing lawyers join forces to sue a prestigious law firm for AIDS discrimination. As their unlikely friendship develops their courage overcomes the prejudice and corruption of their powerful adversaries.
documents.plot:
Philadelphia is a drama film released in 1993, directed by Jonathan Demme and produced by TriStar Pictures. The movie stars Tom Hanks as Andrew Beckett, a young lawyer who is fired from his job at a prestigious law firm due to his AIDS diagnosis.

The story begins with Andrew Beckett (Tom Hanks), a successful and ambitious lawyer working for the law firm of Joseph Miller & Keefe. However, when he contracts HIV through a blood transfusion during a surgery, his life takes a drastic turn. Despite being aware of his condition, Andrew is fired from his job due to the stigma surrounding AIDS at that time.

Andrew seeks help from his friend and colleague, Joe Miller (Denzel Washington), who is also a lawyer at the firm. However, when Joe tries to support Andrew, he is met with resistance from their boss, Alvin "Al" Courtenay (Martin Landau). Courtenay refuses to acknowledge Andrew's condition and instead accuses him of being "unfit for work."

Andrew decides to take on his former employer in a lawsuit, claiming wrongful termination due to his AIDS diagnosis. He hires a new lawyer, Joe Miller, who agrees to take on the case despite the risks involved.

As the trial progresses, it becomes clear that Courtenay's actions were motivated by fear and prejudice against people with HIV/AIDS. The court ultimately rules in Andrew's favor, awarding him $1.4 million in damages.

Throughout the film, Tom Hanks delivers a powerful performance as Andrew Beckett, conveying the emotional toll of being ostracized due to his condition. Denzel Washington also shines as Joe Miller, who becomes a source of support and strength for Andrew during this difficult time.

The movie tackles themes of prejudice, discrimination, and the importance of human rights. The film's portrayal of the AIDS epidemic in the 1990s is both poignant and thought-provoking, highlighting the need for greater understanding and acceptance of people living with HIV/AIDS.

In the end, Andrew Beckett emerges victorious, but not without scars. The film concludes on a hopeful note, as Andrew begins to rebuild his life and find a new sense of purpose. The movie's powerful message about the importance of empathy and compassion resonates long after the credits roll.

Overall, Philadelphia is a masterful drama that explores themes of prejudice, identity, and the human condition. With outstanding performances from Tom Hanks and Denzel Washington, this film remains a powerful and thought-provoking classic of American cinema.

documents.title: Bridget Jones: The Edge of Reason
documents.original_title: Bridget Jones: The Edge of Reason
documents.tagline: Same Bridget. Brand new diary.
documents.overview: Bridget Jones is becoming uncomfortable in her relationship with Mark Darcy. Apart from discovering that he's a conservative voter, she has to deal with a new boss, a strange contractor and the worst vacation of her life.
documents.plot:
Bridget Jones: The Edge of Reason is a romantic comedy of 2004 directed by Beeban Kidron and written by Andrew Davies, Helen Fielding, Richard Curtis and Adam Brooks, based on Fielding's 1999 novel and serving as the sequel to Bridget Jones's Diary (2001). Renée Zellweger returns as Bridget, with Colin Firth as her boyfriend Mark Darcy, Hugh Grant as her former lover Daniel Cleaver, and Jim Broadbent and Gemma Jones as her parents.

Bridget is blissful in her new relationship with Mark, until she meets his young and beautiful assistant, Rebecca Gillies, and her confidence collapses. At work in morning television, she reluctantly agrees to co-host a travel series with Daniel. Hoping for a proposal, she attends a Law Council dinner with Mark that becomes a string of humiliations. After a row, Mark comes to her flat to apologize, tells her for the first time that he loves her and takes her skiing in Lech, Austria, where Rebecca also turns up. A pregnancy scare proves negative.

At a lunch with their parents, Mark's brush-off of questions about marriage wounds Bridget, and when he declines to answer her suspicions about a phone message from Rebecca, she ends the relationship. She heads to Thailand with her friend Shazza and Daniel to film the travel show. After accidentally eating hallucinogenic mushrooms, she grows flirtatious with Daniel again, but the arrival of a prostitute he had ordered convinces her he has not changed. Shazza's young fling, Jed, gives her a decorative snake bowl that ends up in Bridget's luggage, and when airport sniffer dogs find cocaine hidden inside, Bridget is thrown into a crowded cell. She befriends her cellmates, teaching them Madonna's "Like a Virgin". Mark arrives to tell her she will soon be free, but when she lets him believe she slept with Daniel, he coolly leaves.

Back in London, Mark brawls with Daniel in a fountain for abandoning Bridget, and Bridget returns home a minor celebrity. Her friends reveal that Mark personally tracked down Jed and secured the confession that cleared her. Rushing to his house, she finds Rebecca there, but Rebecca confesses that she is attracted to Bridget herself and kisses her; Bridget gently declines. Bridget asks Mark for another chance, and he proposes. At her parents' renewal of their vows, she catches the bouquet.

Shot in London and Austria between October 2003 and February 2004, the film grossed about $265 million worldwide, though critics found it predictable.

documents.title: The Incredibles
documents.tagline: No gut, no glory
documents.overview: Bob Parr has given up his superhero days to log in time as an insurance adjuster and raise his three children with his formerly heroic wife in suburbia. But when he receives a mysterious assignment, it's time to get back into costume.
documents.plot:
The Incredibles is a 2004 animated superhero film produced by Pixar Animation Studios and released by Walt Disney Pictures. The movie follows the story of a family with superpowers, who are forced to hide their abilities and live a normal life.

The film begins with Bob Parr (Mr. Incredible), a former superhero known as Mr. Incredible, who is now a suburban dad living in Municiberg, New Jersey. He works for a company called Supers Inc., which provides superheroes with jobs and benefits. However, Bob's life is not as ordinary as it seems. He longs to return to his superhero days and save the world from evil.

Bob's wife, Helen (Elastigirl), is also a former superhero known as Elastigirl, who has been forced to retire due to her age and the lack of respect for superheroes in society. Their children, Dash and Violet, are also gifted with superpowers - Dash can run at incredible speeds, while Violet can turn invisible and project force fields.

The family's life is disrupted when a mysterious figure named Buddy Pine ( Syndrome) appears, claiming to be a huge fan of Mr. Incredible. However, it soon becomes apparent that Buddy has an ulterior motive - he wants to become a superhero himself and destroy the superheroes who have been deemed "outdated" by society.

Buddy's plan is to use a device called the Omnidroid, which can absorb and neutralize superpowers. The Omnidroid is designed to hunt down and eliminate all superheroes, making it easier for Buddy to become the world's greatest superhero.

As the story unfolds, Bob, Helen, Dash, and Violet must work together to stop Buddy and his Omnidroid. Along the way, they discover that their powers are not just a gift, but also a responsibility. They learn to use their abilities in creative ways to outsmart the villain and save the day.

The climax of the movie features an epic battle between the Parr family and Buddy's Omnidroid. The family uses their unique powers to work together and defeat the robot, saving the city from destruction.

In the end, Bob and Helen are able to reconcile with each other and find a way to balance their superhero lives with their family life. They also learn that being a superhero is not just about having powers, but also about working together as a team and using one's abilities for the greater good.

The Incredibles received widespread critical acclaim for its engaging storyline, memorable characters, and stunning animation. The movie was a commercial success, grossing over $631 million worldwide and spawning two sequels, Incredibles 2 (2018) and a short film, Jack-Jack Attack (2005).

documents.title: Let's Go to Prison
documents.tagline: Welcome to the slammer
documents.overview: When a career criminal's plan for revenge is thwarted by unlikely circumstances, he puts his intended victim's son in his place by putting him in prison...and then joining him.
documents.plot:
Let's Go to Prison is a comedy film that explores the complexities of friendship and loyalty through the lens of two unlikely friends who find themselves in a precarious situation. The movie delves into the theme of camaraderie, as the two main characters, Vince and Nathan, form an unbreakable bond despite their vastly different backgrounds.

As they navigate the challenges of prison life, the film highlights the importance of loyalty and trust in relationships. Through their experiences, the characters learn to rely on each other and support one another, even in the face of adversity. This theme is expertly woven throughout the narrative, adding depth and humor to the story.

The movie also touches on the theme of redemption, as both Vince and Nathan are forced to confront their past mistakes and work towards a better future. Their journey is marked by moments of self-discovery, growth, and ultimately, forgiveness.

Furthermore, Let's Go to Prison pokes fun at the absurdities of the prison system, using satire to critique the harsh realities faced by inmates. The film's lighthearted tone belies its commentary on social issues, making it an entertaining yet thought-provoking watch.

Overall, Let's Go to Prison is a heartwarming and hilarious exploration of friendship, loyalty, and redemption, set against the backdrop of a chaotic prison environment.

documents.title: Goal! II: Living the Dream
documents.tagline: This time the dream is real.
documents.overview: Tempted away from Newcastle United to join Real Madrid, rising star Santiago Munez finds this latest change of fortune the greatest challenge yet - personally as well as professionally. He is reunited with Gavin Harris, though they must compete to be on the team, and estranged from fiancee Roz, whose nursing career keeps her back home.
documents.plot:
Goal II: Living the Dream is a 2007 sports drama directed by Jaume Collet-Serra from a screenplay by Mike Jefferies, Adrian Butchart and Terry Loane. The sequel to Goal! (2005) and the second part of a trilogy, it stars Kuno Becker as the Mexican footballer Santiago Muñez, with Alessandro Nivola, Anna Friel, Stephen Dillane, Leonor Varela, Elizabeth Peña and Rutger Hauer, and features cameo appearances by real Real Madrid players.

Santiago, now a star at Newcastle United, is signed by Real Madrid, where he is reunited with his flamboyant former teammate Gavin Harris. His fiancée, Roz, stays behind in Newcastle to finish her nursing training, and the long-distance relationship soon strains. Santiago makes a winning debut and quickly becomes the club's new star, but fame brings complications. He is approached by Enrique, a younger half-brother he never knew, who shows him a photograph of their mother, Rosa María, who abandoned Santiago as a small child, and he learns that his grandmother knew she was living in Madrid.

Distracted, Santiago is sent off in his first start, and after a drunken night with the television presenter Jordana García he misses the team flight to a Champions League match in Norway, earning the wrath of manager Rudi van der Merwe. He fires his loyal agent Glen Foy, injures his ankle and cancels Christmas plans with Roz, and when a second kiss with Jordana is leaked to the press, Roz breaks off their engagement. Meanwhile Enrique steals Santiago's Lamborghini and crashes it, and Santiago is arrested after taking the blame and assaulting a photographer at the hospital, where he finally sees his mother.

After scoring the goal that sends Madrid into the Champions League final, Santiago visits Rosa, who explains that she fled to Madrid after being attacked, and returned to Mexico to find the family gone to the United States. Reconciled with his mother and Enrique, he asks Rudi to start Gavin in the final against Arsenal to help his friend's career, and apologizes to Roz. Madrid fall behind 2–0, but after coming on, Santiago sets up a goal for Gavin and scores the equalizer, before David Beckham wins the match with a late free kick.

Released in the United Kingdom on February 9, 2007, the film received mixed to negative reviews for its predictable and melodramatic script and grossed only about $7.8 million worldwide, though it later found a cult audience. Goal III followed in 2009.

documents.title: Save the Last Dance
documents.tagline: The Only Person You Need To Be Is Yourself.
documents.overview: After the death of her mother, Sara moves to the South Side of Chicago to live with her father and gets transferred to a majority-black school. Her life takes a turn for the better when befriends Chenille and her brother Derek, who helps her with her dancing skills.
documents.plot:
Save the Last Dance is a 2001 American romantic drama film that explores the complexities of social class, identity, and the struggle for self-discovery. The movie delves into the world of two young women from different backgrounds who find themselves drawn to each other despite their vastly different lifestyles.

The film's narrative revolves around Sara Johnson, a white ballet dancer from a wealthy family in Chicago, who is forced to re-evaluate her life when her mother passes away. She finds solace in hip-hop dance and meets Derek Reynolds, a black teenager from the wrong side of the tracks, at a local club. As they spend more time together, Sara begins to confront the societal expectations placed upon her and the limitations imposed by her privileged upbringing.

Through their relationship, the film sheds light on the tensions between cultural identity and social status. The contrast between Sara's world of elegance and refinement and Derek's gritty reality serves as a backdrop for exploring themes of class struggle, racism, and the search for authenticity. As Sara becomes more immersed in Derek's world, she begins to question her own values and the privileges that have defined her life.

The movie also touches on the theme of self-discovery, as both characters navigate their identities and grapple with the expectations placed upon them by others. Through their relationship, they learn to let go of their preconceptions and find a sense of belonging in each other's worlds.

Ultimately, Save the Last Dance is a poignant exploration of the human experience, one that challenges its viewers to confront the complexities of social class, identity, and the power of love to transcend boundaries.

documents.title: Mystery Men
documents.tagline: We're not your classic heroes, we're the other guys.
documents.overview: When Champion City's hero Captain Amazing is kidnapped by the recently paroled supervillain Casanova Frankenstein, a trio of average, everyday superheroes -- Mr. Furious, the Shoveler and the Blue Raja -- assemble a new super team to save him.

documents.title: Lake Placid
documents.tagline: You'll never know what bit you.
documents.overview: When a man is eaten alive by an unknown creature, the local Game Warden teams up with a paleontologist from New York to find the beast. Add to the mix an eccentric philanthropist with a penchant for "Crocs", and here we go! This quiet, remote lake is suddenly the focus of an intense search for a crocodile with a taste for live animals...and people!

documents.title: United 93
documents.tagline: September 11, 2001. Four planes were hijacked. Three of them reached their target. This is the story of the fourth.
documents.overview: A real-time account of the events on United Flight 93, one of the planes hijacked on 9/11 that crashed near Shanksville, Pennsylvania when passengers foiled the terrorist plot.
documents.plot:
United 93 is a 2006 docudrama written, produced and directed by Paul Greengrass about United Airlines Flight 93, one of the four planes hijacked during the September 11 attacks and the only one that failed to reach its target, because of the actions of its passengers. Alongside events on board, the film follows government officials and air traffic controllers as they watch the attacks unfold, recreating the hijacking and its aftermath as closely as possible in real time.

On the morning of September 11, 2001, four al-Qaeda hijackers led by Ziad Jarrah pray in a Newark hotel before boarding Flight 93, whose passengers include Tom Burnett, Todd Beamer, Jeremy Glick, Lauren Grandcolas and Mark Bingham. While the flight sits delayed on the ground, controllers lose contact with American Airlines Flight 11, realise it has been hijacked, and then see it and United Airlines Flight 175 strike the twin towers of the World Trade Center.

Once airborne, Jarrah hesitates before the hijackers finally act. They stab a passenger and the two pilots, herd the passengers to the rear with the threat of a fake bomb, and Jarrah turns the plane towards Washington, D.C., aiming for the Capitol. On the ground, American Airlines Flight 77 hits the Pentagon and FAA operations manager Ben Sliney orders the closure of all American airspace.

Through calls to their families on the airphones, the passengers learn of the other attacks and understand that the hijackers intend to die. With the flight crew they gather improvised weapons and plan to storm the cockpit so that a passenger with a pilot's licence and a former air traffic controller can try to land the plane. After praying and making final calls home, they rush the hijackers at Beamer's cry of "Let's roll", overpower two of them and discover the bomb is fake. As they batter down the cockpit door, Jarrah throws the aircraft into a dive, and the plane crashes into a field in Pennsylvania, killing everyone on board. Closing titles note that the order to shoot down hijacked aircraft was given only after Flight 93 had crashed.

Released on April 28, 2006, United 93 opened second at the American box office and became one of the most acclaimed films of the year, with a 90% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes. It earned Academy Award nominations for Greengrass's direction and for its film editing.

documents.title: The Phantom of the Opera
documents.tagline: The classic musical comes to the big screen for the first time.
documents.overview: Deformed since birth, a bitter man known only as the Phantom lives in the sewers underneath the Paris Opera House. He falls in love with the obscure chorus singer Christine, and privately tutors her while terrorizing the rest of the opera house and demanding Christine be given lead roles. Things get worse when Christine meets back up with her childhood acquaintance Raoul and the two fall in love
documents.plot:
The Phantom of the Opera is a musical drama film directed by Joel Schumacher, released in 2004 by Warner Bros. Pictures. The movie is an adaptation of Gaston Leroux's 1910 novel of the same name.

The story takes place at the Paris Opera House in the late 19th century. The Phantom (Gerard Butler), a mysterious and disfigured musical genius, lives beneath the opera house. He is a recluse who uses his talent to create music that haunts the opera's performers. The Phantom becomes obsessed with Christine Daaé (Emilie de Ravin), a young and talented soprano.

Christine is discovered by the opera's manager, Monsieur Firmin (Patrick Wilson), and becomes an overnight sensation. However, she soon attracts the attention of the opera's leading tenor, Raoul, Vicomte de Chagny (Ciarán Hinds). The Phantom becomes jealous of Christine's relationship with Raoul and begins to terrorize the opera house.

As the story unfolds, it is revealed that the Phantom was once a musician who fell in love with Christine when she was a child. He became her mentor and taught her how to sing. However, Christine eventually left him for Raoul, which led to the Phantom's disfigurement and his descent into madness.

The Phantom kidnaps Christine and forces her to perform at the opera house, where he can hear her sing. Meanwhile, Raoul tries to rescue Christine from the Phantom's clutches. The Phantom becomes increasingly unhinged as Christine's relationship with Raoul deepens.

In a dramatic confrontation, the Phantom reveals his true identity to Christine and Raoul. However, instead of killing them, he allows Christine to leave with Raoul. As they depart, the Phantom disappears into the darkness, leaving behind his mask and his music.

The movie ends with Christine and Raoul reunited, but the Phantom's legacy lives on through his music. The film features a range of memorable songs, including "Music of the Night," "All I Ask of You," and "Masquerade."

Overall, the 2004 adaptation of The Phantom of the Opera is a visually stunning and emotionally charged retelling of Gaston Leroux's classic novel. While it deviates from the original story in some ways, it captures the essence of the Phantom's tragic love story and his enduring legacy as a musical genius.

documents.title: Happy Feet
documents.tagline: WARNING: May Cause Toe-Tapping.
documents.overview: Into the world of the Emperor Penguins, who find their soul mates through song, a penguin is born who cannot sing. But he can tap dance something fierce!
documents.plot:
Happy Feet is a 2006 animated musical comedy-drama film produced by Kennedy Miller Productions, Village Roadshow Pictures, and Warner Bros. Feature Animation. The movie follows the story of Mumble, an Emperor Penguin who lives in Antarctica.

The film begins with Mumble, a young Emperor Penguin, born to parents Norma Jean and Memphis. However, Mumble is different from his peers as he has two left feet instead of the traditional right-left flipper arrangement. This makes it difficult for him to dance like other penguins, which is an essential part of their mating rituals.

As Mumble grows up, he struggles to find his place among his colony. He tries to fit in by mimicking the movements of the other penguins, but his clumsiness and lack of coordination make it impossible. The elders of the colony view Mumble's uniqueness as a curse, and they shun him.

One day, Mumble meets Gloria, an Adelie Penguin who is different from the rest of her colony due to her love for singing. Gloria becomes Mumble's friend and confidant, and together they explore the world beyond their colony. They discover that humans are polluting the ocean, causing a decline in fish populations, which affects the penguins' food supply.

Mumble decides to embark on a journey to find the source of the problem and save his colony. He sets out with Gloria and a group of penguin friends, including Ramón, a wise-cracking Rockhopper Penguin who becomes Mumble's mentor. Along the way, they encounter various obstacles, including treacherous ice caves, fierce predators, and rival colonies.

As Mumble navigates this new world, he learns to accept himself and his uniqueness. He discovers that his two left feet are not a curse but a gift, allowing him to tap dance in a unique style that captivates the humans. The humans, led by a kind-hearted scientist named Adelie, work together with Mumble's colony to find a solution to the pollution problem.

The climax of the film features an epic dance battle between Mumble and his rival, Ramón, which showcases their respective tap dancing skills. In the end, Mumble's unique style wins over the humans, and they work together to clean up the ocean and restore the fish populations.

The movie concludes with Mumble returning home as a hero, celebrated by his colony for his bravery and creativity. He finds love with Gloria, and they start a family of their own. The film ends on a hopeful note, emphasizing the importance of self-acceptance, friendship, and working together to overcome challenges.

Overall, Happy Feet is a heartwarming story about embracing individuality and finding one's true purpose. The movie features stunning animation, catchy musical numbers, and lovable characters that make it a delight for audiences of all ages.

documents.title: Beyond Borders
documents.tagline: Where hope survives.
documents.overview: Sarah Jordan, an American living in London in 1984, is married to the son of a wealthy British industrialist. She encounters Nick Callahan, a renegade doctor, whose impassioned plea for help to support his relief efforts in war-torn Africa moves her deeply. As a result, Sarah embarks upon a journey of discovery that leads to danger, heartbreak and romance in the far corners of the world.
documents.plot:
Beyond Borders is a 2003 American romantic drama about international aid workers, directed by Martin Campbell and starring Angelina Jolie and Clive Owen, with Teri Polo, Linus Roache, Noah Emmerich and Kate Ashfield in supporting roles. James Horner composed the score. The film reflected Jolie's real-life work in humanitarian relief, and alongside its release she published Notes from My Travels, a collection of journals from her missions as a Goodwill Ambassador for the United Nations refugee agency.

In 1984, Sarah Jordan is a sheltered American socialite married to a wealthy Englishman and living in London. At a charity gala, an uninvited guest, the renegade doctor Nick Callahan, bursts in to deliver a furious plea on behalf of starving children in his care, bringing with him an emaciated refugee boy. Deeply shaken and drawn to Nick and his cause, Sarah impulsively leaves her job at an art gallery and uses her own money to bring a convoy of food and medical supplies to his remote relief camp in famine-stricken Ethiopia, where she meets Nick and his colleague Dr. Elliott Hauser.

The experience transforms her. Over the following decade Sarah becomes a dedicated aid worker with the United Nations refugee agency, while her marriage grows distant. Her paths with Nick cross repeatedly in some of the world's most dangerous places, including Cambodia under the threat of the Khmer Rouge, where the two finally act on their long-suppressed attraction, and later Chechnya. She discovers that the harsh realities of war and politics, the compromises demanded by those who fund relief, and her persistent romantic attraction to the passionate, self-destructive Nick are changing her life in ways she never anticipated. When Nick goes missing in Chechnya, Sarah risks everything to find him, a decision that ends in tragedy.

The film was shot in locations including Namibia and Canada. It was a critical and commercial failure. Rotten Tomatoes reports a 14% approval rating from 102 reviews, with a consensus calling it well-intentioned but sanctimonious and exploitative in its use of human suffering as a backdrop for romance, and Metacritic gave it 32 out of 100. Jolie received a Golden Raspberry nomination for Worst Actress for this film and Lara Croft Tomb Raider: The Cradle of Life.

documents.title: Big Nothing
documents.tagline: They wrote the book on how not to be criminals.
documents.overview: A frustrated, unemployed teacher joins forces with a scammer and his girlfriend in a blackmailing scheme.
documents.plot:
Big Nothing is a 2006 black comedy crime film directed by Jean-Baptiste Andrea, starring David Schwimmer and Simon Pegg alongside Alice Eve, with Natascha McElhone, Jon Polito and Mimi Rogers in supporting roles. The film premiered at the Cardiff Film Festival in November 2006 and was released in the United Kingdom the following month. Although the story is set in a small town in Oregon, it was shot largely on the Isle of Man and in Wales, including Barry in the Vale of Glamorgan and locations around Monmouthshire, with additional scenes filmed in British Columbia.

Schwimmer plays Charlie, a former schoolteacher who is struggling to support his family and who manages to get fired on his very first day working at a call centre. His cynical co-worker Gus, played by Pegg, approaches him with what he presents as an easy and victimless scheme: Gus has evidence that a local reverend has been visiting pornographic websites, and he proposes that they blackmail the clergyman for a large sum of money. Josie McBroom, a former teenage beauty queen played by Eve, overhears them and forces her way into the plan as a third partner.

The scheme collapses almost immediately. While Gus goes to the reverend's house, Charlie heads to a bar to set up an alibi, only to discover that the person who could contradict it is drinking there. Hurrying to the house, he finds the reverend apparently dead and no sign of Gus, and in a panic he hides the body in a septic tank, a decision that turns out to have been fatal for a man who was not actually dead. Each further attempt to cover up the mess creates new problems, as the trio uncover secrets about the reverend, turn on one another and attract the attention of the police, all against the background of a serial killer, nicknamed the Oregon Undertaker, who has been murdering young women in the area.

The film blends farce, crime caper and dark thriller elements, with a twisting plot in which nearly everyone is hiding something and the body count rises steadily. Its humour derives from the escalating incompetence of its amateur criminals and from the contrast between Schwimmer's anxious everyman and Pegg's reckless schemer.

Big Nothing received mixed reviews, with critics appreciating its cast and dark sense of humour while finding its tone uneven and its twists convoluted.

documents.title: Forgetting Sarah Marshall
documents.tagline: You lose some, you get some.
documents.overview: When Sarah Marshall dumps aspiring musician Peter Bretter for rock star Aldous Snow, Peter's world comes crashing down. His best friend suggests that Peter should get away from everything and to fly off to Hawaii to escape all his problems. After arriving in Hawaii and meeting the beautiful Rachel Jansen, Peter is shocked to see not only Aldous Snow in Hawaii, but also Sarah Marshall.
documents.plot:
Forgetting Sarah Marshall is a 2008 American romantic comedy film directed by Nicholas Stoller and written by Jason Segel and Andrew Cohen.

The movie begins with Peter Bretter (played by Jason Segel), a struggling musician who has been dating the famous actress Sarah Marshall (played by Kristen Bell) for three years. However, their relationship ends abruptly when Sarah breaks up with him on live television during her concert in Hawaii. Heartbroken, Peter travels to Hawaii to attend Sarah's wedding, where he hopes to find closure and move on from his heartbreak.

Upon arrival, Peter discovers that Sarah is marrying the famous rock star Aldous Snow (played by Russell Brand), who is also a close friend of hers. As Peter tries to come to terms with his breakup, he meets Rachel Jansen (played by Mila Kunis), a hotel receptionist who becomes his unlikely companion and confidante.

As Peter navigates his way through the wedding and its aftermath, he begins to realize that he has been using Sarah as an excuse to avoid dealing with his own emotional baggage. Through his interactions with Rachel, Peter starts to confront his feelings and learn to move on from his heartbreak.

Meanwhile, Aldous Snow's character is revealed to be a self-centered, egotistical rock star who is struggling with his own personal demons. As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Sarah has been using Aldous as a rebound partner after her breakup with Peter, and that she is not ready to move on from their relationship.

Throughout the movie, Peter's character undergoes significant development as he learns to let go of his emotional attachment to Sarah and find happiness again. The film features a range of comedic moments, including Peter's disastrous attempts at playing music with Rachel and his awkward interactions with Aldous.

In the end, Peter comes to terms with his breakup and finds closure by realizing that he deserves better than someone who has hurt him so deeply. He also learns to appreciate the beauty of moving on and finding happiness again, as embodied by his growing connection with Rachel.

Overall, Forgetting Sarah Marshall is a heartwarming and hilarious romantic comedy that explores themes of love, loss, and self-discovery. The film features outstanding performances from its cast, particularly Jason Segel and Mila Kunis, who bring depth and nuance to their characters.

documents.title: Ginger Snaps
documents.tagline: Hungry like the Wolf.
documents.overview: The story of two outcast sisters, Ginger and Brigitte, in the mindless suburban town of Bailey Downs. On the night of Ginger's first period, she is savagely attacked by a wild creature. Ginger's wounds miraculously heal but something is not quite right. Now Brigitte must save her sister and save herself.
documents.plot:
Ginger Snaps is a 2000 Canadian horror-comedy film directed by John Fawcett, produced by John Fawcett and Bruce Miller, and written by Karen Walton. The movie stars Emily Perkins as Brigitte Fitzgerald, Katharine Isabelle as Ginger Fitzgerald, and Ted Levine as Brad Fitzgerald.

The story begins with the introduction of the Fitzgerald family, consisting of parents Brad (Ted Levine) and Carol (Kathleen Robertson), and their two daughters, Brigitte (Emily Perkins) and Ginger (Katharine Isabelle). The movie takes place in a small town in British Columbia, Canada. 

On Brigitte's 14th birthday, she is bitten by a werewolf while walking home from school. Unbeknownst to her, this bite will transform her into a werewolf every full moon. As the transformation progresses, Ginger becomes increasingly aggressive and violent, causing chaos in their lives.

Initially, Brigitte tries to cope with her new condition, but she soon realizes that she is not alone in her struggles. She seeks help from her father, who has no idea what's happening to his daughter. However, he eventually discovers the truth about Ginger's transformation and tries to find a way to reverse it.

As the full moon approaches, Brigitte becomes more desperate to stop Ginger's transformations. She turns to an old high school friend, Tom (Ryan Reynolds), for help. Together, they try various methods to cure Ginger of her werewolf condition, including using sacred objects and performing rituals.

Throughout the movie, the relationship between Brigitte and Ginger deteriorates as Ginger becomes more aggressive and violent. The sisters' bond is tested as they struggle to come to terms with their new reality.

In the climactic final scene, Brigitte discovers that the only way to cure her sister is for her to kill herself during a full moon. In a desperate attempt to save Ginger, Brigitte stabs herself in the heart with a sacred object, effectively killing both of them and breaking the curse.

The movie ends with Brigitte's body being discovered by their father, who is left to grapple with the consequences of his daughters' tragic fate. The film concludes on a somber note, highlighting the devastating effects of Ginger's transformation on her family.

Ginger Snaps received widespread critical acclaim for its unique blend of horror and comedy, as well as its portrayal of sisterly love and the struggles of adolescence.

documents.title: F/X
documents.tagline: Murder by illusion.
documents.overview: A movies special effects man is hired by a government agency to help stage the assassination of a well known gangster. When the agency double cross him, he uses his special effects to trap the gangster and the corrupt agents.
documents.plot: A movies special effects man is hired by a government agency to help stage the assassination of a well known gangster. When the agency double cross him, he uses his special effects to trap the gangster and the corrupt agents.

documents.title: The Princess Diaries
documents.tagline: She rocks. She rules. She reigns.
documents.overview: A socially awkward but very bright 15-year-old girl being raised by a single mom discovers that she is the princess of a small European country because of the recent death of her long-absent father, who, unknown to her, was the crown prince of Genovia. She must make a choice between continuing the life of a San Francisco teen or stepping up to the throne.
documents.plot:
The Princess Diaries is a 2001 American comedy film directed by Garry Marshall and produced by Wendy Finerman. The movie stars Anne Hathaway as Mia Thermopolis, a shy and awkward high school student who discovers she is the princess of a small European country called Genovia.

The story begins with Mia, played by Anne Hathaway, living in San Francisco with her mother, Helen (played by Meryl Streep), a journalist. On her 15th birthday, Mia receives an unexpected letter from Queen Clarisse Renaldi (played by Julie Andrews) of Genovia, informing her that she is the princess of the country and must assume her royal duties.

Initially, Mia is hesitant to accept her new role, but with the help of her grandmother, Queen Clarisse, she begins to learn about the responsibilities and etiquette required of a princess. However, Mia struggles to balance her royal life with her normal teenage life, including navigating high school relationships and friendships.

As Mia prepares for her coronation as the new princess of Genovia, she must also contend with the challenges of royal protocol, fashion, and diplomacy. With the help of her grandmother and a tutor, Lily (played by Heather Matarazzo), Mia learns to navigate these complexities and become a confident and capable princess.

Throughout the film, Mia's relationships with those around her are put to the test. Her mother, Helen, is initially supportive but struggles to adjust to Mia's new royal status. Meanwhile, Mia develops feelings for her classmate, Michael Moscovitz (played by Robert Schwartzman), who becomes a loyal friend and confidant.

As the coronation approaches, Mia must confront the challenges of being a princess in a foreign country. She faces opposition from some Genovians who are skeptical of her ability to lead their country, and she must navigate the complexities of royal politics.

In the end, Mia proves herself to be a capable and compassionate leader, earning the respect and admiration of the people of Genovia. With the help of her grandmother and friends, Mia successfully assumes her royal duties and becomes the princess that Genovia needs.

The Princess Diaries was a commercial success and received generally positive reviews from critics, who praised Anne Hathaway's performance as a breakout star. The film's lighthearted tone, witty dialogue, and strong female lead made it a beloved favorite among audiences of all ages.

documents.title: Collateral Damage
documents.tagline: What would you do if you lost everything?
documents.overview: Firefighter Gordon Brewer is plunged into the complex and dangerous world of international terrorism after he loses his wife and child in a bombing credited to Claudio 'The Wolf' Perrini.
documents.plot:
Collateral Damage is a 2002 American action thriller film directed by Tony Scott and starring Antonio Banderas, Tom Sizemore, and Claire Forlani.

The movie begins with Gabriel Shear (Tom Sizemore), an FBI agent who has been tracking down the notorious terrorist known as "El Diablo" (Antonio Banderas). El Diablo is responsible for a series of bombings that have killed hundreds of people in Mexico. Gabriel's brother, Michael, was one of the victims.

Gabriel finally tracks down El Diablo to Los Angeles and engages him in a fierce gun battle. However, just as he thinks he has won, El Diablo escapes by setting off a massive explosion that destroys Gabriel's house and kills his family.

Consumed by grief and anger, Gabriel seeks revenge against El Diablo, who is now hiding out in Mexico City. He teams up with Yulaw (Peter Stormare), a local hitman who agrees to help him track down El Diablo in exchange for a share of the profits from any successful hits.

As they delve deeper into the world of organized crime, Gabriel and Yulaw encounter a beautiful woman named Sarah (Claire Forlani) who is somehow connected to El Diablo's past. Through her, Gabriel learns more about El Diablo's motivations and the true extent of his evil plans.

The plot thickens as Gabriel and Yulaw close in on El Diablo, leading to a series of intense confrontations and explosive set pieces. Along the way, Gabriel must also navigate the complexities of his own grief and anger, learning to channel them into a more constructive form of revenge.

As the story reaches its climax, Gabriel finally tracks down El Diablo to an abandoned warehouse on the outskirts of Mexico City. In a tense showdown, Gabriel confronts El Diablo and exacts his revenge, killing him in a dramatic and bloody finale.

Throughout the movie, director Tony Scott's signature style is on full display, with rapid-fire editing and a pulsating score that amplifies the tension and action. Antonio Banderas delivers a strong performance as the vengeful Gabriel Shear, bringing depth and nuance to a character who could have easily been reduced to a one-dimensional avenger.

Overall, Collateral Damage is a gripping and intense thriller that explores themes of grief, anger, and redemption. While it may not be as memorable as some of Scott's other films, it remains a solid addition to his action-packed oeuvre.

documents.title: Wolf Creek
documents.tagline: The thrill is in the hunt.
documents.overview: Stranded backpackers in remote Australia fall prey to a murderous bushman, who offers to fix their car, then takes them captive.
documents.plot: Three backpackers stranded in the Australian outback are plunged inside a hellish nightmare of insufferable torture by a sadistic psychopathic local.

documents.title: Shallow Hal
documents.tagline: True love is worth the weight.
documents.overview: After taking his dying father's advice, Hal dates only the embodiments of female physical perfection. But that all changes after Hal has an unexpected run-in with self-help guru Tony Robbins. Intrigued by Hal's shallowness, Robbins hypnotizes him into seeing the beauty that exists even in the least physically appealing women. Hal soon falls for Rosemary, but he doesn't realize that his gorgeous girlfriend is actually a 300-pound-not-so-hottie.
documents.plot:
Shallow Hal is a 2001 American romantic comedy film directed by Peter Farrelly and Bobby Farrelly, starring Jack Black and Gwyneth Paltrow. The movie follows the story of Hal Larson, a shallow and obese man who undergoes a transformation after meeting a group of angels.

The film begins with Hal (Jack Black), a 35-year-old man who is struggling to find love due to his weight and lack of self-confidence. He is obsessed with celebrity culture and spends most of his time watching TV and eating junk food. One day, while on a date at a restaurant, Hal meets Rosemary (Gwyneth Paltrow), a beautiful woman who is engaged to be married.

However, during their date, Hal becomes infatuated with Rosemary's appearance, but not her inner qualities. He decides to take a different approach and starts dating women based solely on their physical appearance. This leads him to meet a group of angels, led by Tony Robbins (Joe Viterelli), who claim that they can help people change their lives.

The angels convince Hal to undergo a transformation, where he is hypnotized and told to see only the inner beauty in people. At first, Hal resists this idea, but eventually, he starts to notice the positive qualities of those around him, including Rosemary's kindness and generosity.

As Hal continues to date women based on their inner beauty, he starts to develop feelings for Rosemary, who is not initially aware of his transformation. However, things become complicated when Rosemary discovers that Hal has been seeing other women, including a beautiful woman named Marianna (Jenna Elfman), who is actually an angel in disguise.

Marianna is sent by the angels to test Hal's commitment to changing his ways and to see if he can truly find love based on inner beauty. As Hal navigates this challenge, he must confront his own flaws and weaknesses, including his weight and lack of self-confidence.

In the end, Hal realizes that true love requires more than just physical appearance and that he has fallen in love with Rosemary's kindness and generosity. The movie ends with Hal and Rosemary getting married, surrounded by their friends and family.

Throughout the film, Jack Black delivers a memorable performance as the lovable but shallow Hal Larson. His comedic timing and charisma bring humor to the film, while also highlighting the importance of inner beauty and self-acceptance. Gwyneth Paltrow shines as Rosemary, bringing depth and nuance to her character.

Overall, Shallow Hal is a heartwarming and hilarious romantic comedy that explores themes of love, self-acceptance, and transformation. With its talented cast and witty dialogue, the film is sure to delight audiences and leave them feeling uplifted and inspired.

documents.title: The Stepford Wives
documents.tagline: The wives of Stepford have a secret.
documents.overview: What does it take to become a Stepford wife, a woman perfect beyond belief? Ask the Stepford husbands, who've created this high-tech, terrifying little town.
documents.plot: What does it take to become a Stepford wife, a woman perfect beyond belief? Ask the Stepford husbands, who've created this high-tech, terrifying little town.

documents.title: Sleepover
documents.tagline: The rules are set. The game is on.
documents.overview: As their first year of high school looms ahead, best friends Julie, Hannah, Yancy and Farrah have one last summer sleepover. Little do they know they're about to embark on the adventure of a lifetime. Desperate to shed their nerdy status, they take part in a night-long scavenger hunt that pits them against their popular archrivals. Everything under the sun goes on -- from taking Yancy's father's car to sneaking into nightclubs!
documents.plot:
Sleepover is an American teen comedy of 2004 and the feature directing debut of Joe Nussbaum, from a screenplay by Elisa Bell. It stars Alexa Vega as Julie Corky, with Mika Boorem, Sara Paxton, Scout Taylor-Compton, Brie Larson and Kallie Flynn Childress, while Jane Lynch, Jeff Garlin and Steve Carell head the adult cast and Sean Faris, Sam Huntington and Evan Peters appear in supporting roles.

On the last day of eighth grade, Julie holds a slumber party for her friends Hannah, Farrah and Yancy. Staci Blake, a former friend who now leads the popular clique, challenges them to an all-night scavenger hunt. The winners will claim the coveted lunch spot by the fountain when high school begins; the losers will eat beside the dumpsters. The list includes a photo of each girl with a date inside a nightclub, the badge from a local security firm, a pair of boxers belonging to Steve Phillips, the boy Julie has a crush on, and dressing a store mannequin in their own clothes. Bribing her older brother Ren to cover for them, the girls slip out in a tiny electric car borrowed from Yancy's father, dodging a security guard and trying to keep Julie's parents, Gabby and Jay, from noticing they are gone.

At the club Julie discovers that her assigned date is her own teacher, and drops a scarf that her mother, out with a friend, later finds. Skateboarding home to reassure her father, Julie catches Steve's eye, and she sneaks into his house and narrowly escapes with his boxers. Both teams complete the list, so Staci proposes a tiebreaker at a school dance: the first group to obtain the crown of the dance king or queen wins. Steve is crowned king, picks Julie for his victory dance and hands her the crown, sealing the win. The girls race home just ahead of Gabby and pretend to be asleep. The next morning Gabby shows Julie the scarf but, rather than punish her, marvels at how quickly she is growing up, and Steve turns up in Julie's tree fort with the crown for their first kiss. Come high school, Staci and her friends are eating by the dumpsters.

Released on 9 July 2004, the film opened at number ten and grossed about $10.1 million worldwide on a $10 million budget. Reviews were poor, with a 15% Rotten Tomatoes rating, though the film later gained a cult following on home video.

documents.title: Man of the Year
documents.tagline: Elections are made to be broken.
documents.overview: The irreverent host of a political satire talk show decides to run for president and expose corruption in Washington. His stunt goes further than he expects when he actually wins the election, but a software engineer suspects that a computer glitch is responsible for his surprising victory.
documents.plot:
Man of the Year is a 2006 American political comedy-drama with thriller elements, written and directed by Barry Levinson and produced by James G. Robinson. Robin Williams stars as Tom Dobbs, the host of a satirical political talk show who runs for president, and the cast also includes Christopher Walken, Laura Linney, Lewis Black and Jeff Goldblum.

Dobbs's show taps into public frustration with divisive, special-interest politics. He laughs off an audience member's suggestion that he run for the White House, but after a wave of online support he announces a campaign on the air, gets on the ballot in 13 states and joins a national debate with Democratic incumbent President Kellogg and Republican Senator Mills. Meanwhile Eleanor Green, an employee of Delacroy, the company supplying the country's voting machines, discovers that its system does not count correctly, but company head James Hemmings deletes her warning e-mail. Dobbs initially takes the campaign so seriously that he worries his manager, Jack Menken, and producer Eddie Langston, but at the debate he reverts to comedy and climbs in the polls. On Election Day the early returns follow exactly the pattern Eleanor predicted, and Dobbs sweeps his 13 states, winning enough electoral votes to become president-elect.

When Eleanor presses the issue, she is attacked at home and injected with drugs, then discredited as an addict and fired. She tracks Dobbs down and works out the flaw: regardless of the actual votes, the software favors names with double letters in alphabetical order, so Dobbs beats Kellogg, who beats Mills. Dobbs, increasingly smitten with her, plans to reveal the truth, but Delacroy preempts him by claiming Eleanor tried to rig the vote for him, and its agents pursue her until one rams the phone booth she is calling from. In her ambulance she convinces Dobbs, and although polls show most Americans want him in office, he announces on Saturday Night Live's Weekend Update that the vote was flawed and covered up and that he will not run in the new election. Kellogg wins a second term, the executives are arrested, Dobbs returns to television with Eleanor as his producer and later his wife, and Time names him its Man of the Year.

Filmed in Toronto, Hamilton and Washington, D.C., and released by Universal Pictures on October 13, 2006, the film grossed $41.2 million on a $20 million budget. Reviews were largely negative, with 22% on Rotten Tomatoes and 39 on Metacritic.

documents.title: Rat Race
documents.tagline: 563 miles. 9 people. $2 million. 1001 problems!
documents.overview: In an ensemble film about easy money, greed, manipulation and bad driving, a Las Vegas casino tycoon entertains his wealthiest high rollers -- a group that will bet on anything -- by pitting six ordinary people against each other in a wild dash for $2 million jammed into a locker hundreds of miles away. The tycoon and his wealthy friends monitor each racer's every move to keep track of their favorites. The only rule in this race is that there are no rules.
documents.plot:
Hotel tycoon Donald Sinclair devises a game to entertain the high rollers who visit his Las Vegas casino: six competitors are to race to Silver City, New Mexico, where $2 million is inside a duffel bag in a train station locker. The racers consist of ne'er-do-well brothers Duane and Blaine Cody; businesswoman Merrill Jennings and her mother Vera; disgraced football referee Owen Templeton; tourist Randy Pear and his family; narcoleptic Italian tourist Enrico Pollini; and no-nonsense attorney Nick Schaffer.
Duane and Blaine destroy the airport's radar, which grounds everybody else but wrecks their vehicle in the process, prompting them to rent another. They decide to split up to better their chances and have a locksmith create a duplicate locker key, but the locksmith overhears their plan and makes off with the key in a hot air balloon. The brothers catch up to the locksmith, leaving him and a stray cow hanging from the balloon's anchor rope. After Blaine gets distracted by two women driving beside them on the road, he and Duane veer off into a monster truck rally, where they steal one of the trucks after their rental car is crushed.
Merrill and Vera are given malicious directions by a woman selling squirrels on the side of the road, and crash into a pile of totaled vehicles with the skeletons of her previous victims. After stumbling through the Mojave Desert, they hijack a rocket car until it runs out of fuel. Left nauseous by the car's extreme speed, Merrill and Vera accidentally stumble onto a busload of mental patients headed for Silver City.
Owen has his pants and other belongings stolen by a taxi driver as revenge for a bad call Owen previously made at a football game, which caused the driver to lose a bet. Stumbling across a bus station, he dupes and impersonates the driver of a bus on the way to transport a group of Lucille Ball cosplayers to an I Love Lucy fan convention. On the way to the convention, Owen accidentally hits the cow dangling from the hot air balloon and crashes the bus. After revealing he is not the real driver and escaping from the cosplayers, Owen steals a horse.
Randy forces his daughter Kimberly to defecate out of their minivan's window to avoid stopping; as revenge, she insists they visit a museum dedicated to Nazi officer Klaus Barbie, mistakenly believing it to be about Barbie dolls. The family steals Adolf Hitler's staff car after seeing their minivan sabotaged by Duane and Blaine, only to be confronted by an all-female biker gang. Randy drives his family into a large gathering for World War II veterans after his tongue is accidentally burnt by the dashboard cigarette lighter, where the veterans are put off by his Hitler-like slurred speech and appearance. Later, at a diner where his family insists they end the trip, Randy slips sleeping pills into their milkshakes and packs them into a semi-trailer truck.

documents.title: The Producers
documents.tagline: They had everything to gain by not being a success!
documents.overview: After putting together another Broadway flop, down-on-his-luck producer Max Bialystock teams up with timid accountant Leo Bloom in a get-rich-quick scheme to put on the world's worst show.
documents.plot:
The Producers is a 2005 American musical comedy directed by Susan Stroman and written by Mel Brooks and Thomas Meehan, adapted from their 2001 Broadway musical, itself based on Brooks's 1967 film. Nathan Lane and Matthew Broderick, reprising their stage roles as Max Bialystock and Leo Bloom, lead a cast that includes Uma Thurman, Will Ferrell, Gary Beach, Roger Bart and Jon Lovitz.

In 1959, after his Hamlet musical Funny Boy flops, washed-up Broadway producer Max Bialystock hires nervous accountant Leo Bloom. Going over the books, Leo notes that because flops are expected to lose money, no one checks their finances, so a producer who oversold shares in a sure failure could pocket up to $2 million. Leo first refuses to join Max's scheme, but, dreaming of becoming a producer, he quits his firm to form Bialystock & Bloom. Seeking the worst play ever written, they find Springtime for Hitler, an adoring tribute by ex-Nazi Franz Liebkind, and win the rights by swearing his sacred Siegfried Oath. They hire the flamboyant, failing director Roger De Bris and his assistant Carmen Ghia, who agree on condition that the show be made "gay", and Max takes on Ulla, a Swedish woman who arrives to audition, as a secretary. Max raises the money by romancing elderly women, while Leo falls for Ulla.

Franz wins the role of Hitler at auditions but breaks his leg on opening night, and Roger takes his place. The audience is appalled until Roger's outrageously camp Hitler makes them read the show as satire, and it becomes a hit. Panicked that their fraud will be exposed, Max and Leo quarrel, and Franz, enraged that they mocked his idol, tries to shoot them, drawing the police. Max is arrested while Leo flees to Rio de Janeiro with Ulla, but Leo returns to defend his partner in court, and the judge sends both to Sing Sing with Franz. Their prison musical, Prisoners of Love, earns them a pardon from the governor, and Max and Leo become successful Broadway producers. In a post-credits scene, the cast and Brooks sing the audience out of the theater.

Universal Pictures released the film in North America, opening in limited release on December 16, 2005, before going wide on December 25. Competing against films such as King Kong and The Chronicles of Narnia, it grossed about $38 million worldwide against a $45 million budget. Reviews were mixed, with 51% on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus called it stale and stagy, and 52 on Metacritic.

documents.title: Grandma's Boy
documents.tagline: A movie that proves you're never too old to come of age.
documents.overview: Even though he's 35, Alex acts more like he's 13, spending his days as the world's oldest video game tester and his evenings developing the next big Xbox game. But when he gets kicked out of his apartment, he's forced to move in with his grandmother.
documents.plot:
Grandma's Boy is a comedy film that explores the complexities of male relationships and the struggles of growing up. The movie delves into the theme of masculinity, as the protagonist, Barry Egan, navigates his way through adulthood while still clinging to his childhood fantasies.

The film also touches on the idea of identity crisis, as Barry's attempts to fit in with a group of older men lead him to question his own sense of self. This is further complicated by his relationships with women, particularly his crush on a woman named Sarah, who represents a more mature and independent version of himself.

Moreover, Grandma's Boy critiques the societal expectations placed on men, particularly those in their 20s and 30s, to be successful, confident, and emotionally stoic. The movie pokes fun at these stereotypes, highlighting the absurdity and vulnerability that lies beneath.

Ultimately, the film is a coming-of-age story about self-discovery, as Barry learns to let go of his childish insecurities and find his place in the world. Through its lighthearted humor and relatable characters, Grandma's Boy offers a nuanced exploration of male adolescence, making it a memorable and entertaining watch.

documents.title: Wrong Turn
documents.tagline: It's the last one you'll ever take.
documents.overview: Chris crashes into a carload of other young people, and the group of stranded motorists is soon lost in the woods of West Virginia, where they're hunted by three cannibalistic mountain men who are grossly disfigured by generations of inbreeding.
documents.plot:
Wrong Turn is a 2003 American slasher film directed by Rob Schmidt and written by Alan B. McElroy, starring Desmond Harrington, Eliza Dushku, Emmanuelle Chriqui, Jeremy Sisto and Kevin Zegers. The first installment of the Wrong Turn series, it was conceived as a 1970s-style horror film and produced by Summit Entertainment with Constantin Film, with creature effects designed by Stan Winston. It follows a group of people stalked by deformed, inbred, cannibalistic mountain men in the forests of West Virginia.

After two college students are killed while rock climbing in a remote stretch of woods, medical student Chris Flynn, driving through the mountains to a business meeting, is held up by a traffic jam. Rather than wait, he gets directions to a back road from an unhelpful old gas station owner and turns onto Bear Mountain Road, where he crashes into a car stranded by barbed wire laid deliberately across the pavement. The car belongs to five friends on a camping trip: Jessie, Carly, Scott, Evan and Francine. Evan and Francine stay with the vehicles while the others look for help, but both are soon killed by unseen attackers. Chris, Jessie, Carly and Scott stumble onto an isolated cabin full of human remains and are forced to hide when its occupants, three cannibal brothers known as Three Finger, Saw Tooth and One Eye, return carrying Francine's body. After escaping, the survivors are hunted through the forest, coming across the cars of earlier victims and seeking refuge in an old watchtower, from which they radio for help. The cannibals set the tower ablaze, and in the chase through the trees and along a waterfall the group is steadily whittled down. With Jessie captured and taken back to the cabin, an injured Chris must find a way to rescue her and escape the mountain men's territory.

Despite grossing $28.7 million worldwide against a $12 million budget, Wrong Turn received mixed reviews. On Rotten Tomatoes, 41% of 82 critics' reviews are positive, with a consensus calling it an unremarkable slasher that fails to distinguish itself from others of its ilk. The film launched a franchise of sequels and a 2021 reboot.

documents.title: The Wild
documents.tagline: Start spreading the newspaper.
documents.overview: An adolescent lion is accidentally shipped from the New York Zoo to Africa. Now running free, his zoo pals must put aside their differences to help bring him back.
documents.plot:
The Wild is a 2006 animated comedy-drama film produced by Walt Disney Pictures. The movie follows the story of Don Lino, a lion who was once a circus performer but is now a zoo animal.

Don Lino (voiced by Jeremy Renner) lives in a small zoo with his wife and two cubs, Luna and Leo. However, their life takes a dramatic turn when they are forced to leave the zoo due to financial difficulties. The family embarks on an adventure across the United States, facing various challenges and dangers along the way.

As they travel through different cities and landscapes, Don Lino's family is pursued by a group of ruthless animal control officers led by a menacing raccoon named Jack (voiced by Jim Cummings). The officers are determined to capture Don Lino and his cubs, intending to sell them to a circus or other entertainment venue.

Throughout their journey, Don Lino's family faces numerous obstacles, including treacherous terrain, wild animals, and human dangers. Along the way, they meet a wise old owl named Sam (voiced by Patrick Warburton) who becomes their ally and guide.

As the story unfolds, Don Lino learns valuable lessons about responsibility, courage, and the importance of family. He also discovers that he has a hidden talent for music, which helps to bring his family together and inspire them to keep moving forward.

In the end, Don Lino's family reaches their destination, a beautiful and peaceful sanctuary where they can live freely and safely. The movie concludes with a heartwarming moment of reunion and celebration, as Don Lino and his cubs finally find happiness and fulfillment after their long and arduous journey.

Overall, The Wild is a charming and entertaining film that explores themes of family, perseverance, and self-discovery. With its lovable characters, engaging storyline, and stunning animation, it's a must-see for families and animal lovers alike.

documents.title: The Ant Bully
documents.tagline: The battle for the lawn is on.
documents.overview: Fed up with being targeted by the neighborhood bully, 10-year-old Lucas Nickle vents his frustrations on the anthill in his front yard ... until the insects shrink him to the size of a bug with a magic elixir. Convicted of "crimes against the colony," Lucas can only regain his freedom by living with the ants and learning their ways.
documents.plot:
The Ant Bully is a computer-animated adventure comedy film directed by John A. Davis, produced by Warner Bros. Pictures, and released in 2006.

In a world where ants are the dominant species, Lucas (voiced by Nicolas Cage), an 11-year-old boy, accidentally shrinks himself down to the size of an ant after being hit by a magical insecticide. He finds himself in the midst of an anthill, where he meets Zeta (voiced by Harland Williams), a friendly and eccentric ant who befriends him.

Lucas soon discovers that his presence has caused chaos among the ants, as they are now threatened by a group of evil ants led by Hopper (voiced by Richard Jenkins). Hopper is determined to take over the anthill and enslave all other insects. Zeta convinces Lucas to help him stop Hopper and save the anthill.

As Lucas navigates this new world, he learns about the intricate social hierarchy of the ants and their unique culture. He also befriends a group of ants, including Zeta's sister, Molt (voiced by Julia Louis-Dreyfus), who becomes his ally in the quest to defeat Hopper.

Throughout the film, Lucas faces various challenges as he tries to find a way back home. Along the way, he discovers that he has a special connection with the ants and learns valuable lessons about teamwork, bravery, and responsibility.

As the story unfolds, Lucas and his ant friends devise a plan to stop Hopper and save the anthill. The final confrontation between Lucas and Hopper is intense, with both sides using their unique skills and abilities to outsmart each other.

In the end, Lucas successfully defeats Hopper and finds a way back home, but not before saying goodbye to his new ant friends. The film concludes with Lucas reflecting on his incredible adventure and the lessons he learned about the importance of friendship and cooperation.

Overall, The Ant Bully is a heartwarming and action-packed animated film that explores themes of identity, community, and the power of teamwork. With its engaging storyline, lovable characters, and stunning animation, it's a must-see for families and fans of adventure movies.

documents.title: Barnyard
documents.tagline: What happens in the barn stays in the barn
documents.overview: When the farmer's away, all the animals play, and sing, and dance. Eventually, though, someone has to step in and run things, a responsibility that ends up going to Otis, a carefree cow.
documents.plot: Otis is a mischievous, carefree Holstein cow who lives on a farm where, unbeknownst to humans, the animals are anthropomorphic. He prefers having fun with his best friends: Pip the mouse, Freddy the ferret, Peck the rooster, and Pig the pig - rather than following strict rules and accepting responsibility. But when his adoptive father is killed in a coyote attack, he has a heavy responsibility thrust upon him to become leader of his farm home's community.
production_companies: Kumar Mobiliengesellschaft mbH & Co. Projekt Nr. 2 KG

documents.title: The World's Fastest Indian
documents.tagline: Based on one hell of a true story.
documents.overview: The life story of New Zealander Burt Munro, who spent years building a 1920 Indian motorcycle—a bike which helped him set the land-speed world record at Utah's Bonneville Salt Flats in 1967.
documents.plot:
The World's Fastest Indian is a 2005 biographical drama film that tells the story of Burt Munro, a New Zealand inventor and motorcycle enthusiast. The movie explores several themes that are deeply intertwined with the narrative.

One of the primary themes of the film is perseverance and determination. Burt Munro's passion for building the fastest Indian motorcycle in the world drives him to overcome numerous obstacles, including financial struggles, personal losses, and self-doubt. His unwavering dedication to his craft serves as a testament to the power of persistence and hard work.

The movie also delves into the theme of identity and belonging. Burt Munro's journey is marked by feelings of isolation and disconnection from mainstream society. As an outsider who doesn't quite fit in, he finds solace in his motorcycle and the sense of community it provides him with like-minded individuals. The film highlights the importance of finding one's place in the world and embracing what makes us unique.

Furthermore, The World's Fastest Indian touches on the theme of love and sacrifice. Burt Munro's relationship with his wife, Lily, is a central aspect of the story. His devotion to her and their family serves as a driving force behind his pursuit of building the fastest motorcycle. The film also explores the sacrifices he makes for his craft, including putting his own needs and desires aside.

Lastly, the movie touches on the theme of legacy and leaving a mark on the world. Burt Munro's quest for speed is not just about personal fulfillment but also about leaving a lasting impact on the world of motorcycle racing. The film suggests that our passions and pursuits can transcend time and leave a lasting legacy that inspires others.

Overall, The World's Fastest Indian is a heartwarming and inspiring film that explores themes of perseverance, identity, love, sacrifice, and legacy through the remarkable story of Burt Munro.

documents.title: The Skeleton Key
documents.tagline: Fearing Is Believing
documents.overview: A hospice nurse working at a spooky New Orleans plantation home finds herself entangled in a mystery involving the house's dark past.
documents.plot: A hospice nurse working at a spooky New Orleans plantation home finds herself entangled in a mystery involving the house's dark past.

documents.title: Glory Road
documents.tagline: The incredible story of the team that changed the game forever.
documents.overview: In 1966, Texas Western coach Don Haskins led the first all-black starting line-up for a college basketball team to the NCAA national championship.
documents.plot:
Glory Road is a 2006 sports drama film that tells the story of the first all-black starting lineup in college basketball history at Texas Western University. The movie follows the journey of Coach Don Haskins, played by Dennis Quaid, as he navigates the challenges of integrating his team with players from different racial backgrounds.

At its core, Glory Road is a powerful exploration of themes such as unity, perseverance, and overcoming adversity. The film highlights the struggles faced by the team as they work to overcome their differences and come together as a cohesive unit, ultimately achieving great success on the court. Through the characters' experiences, the movie shows how these values can lead to personal growth, healing, and redemption.

The film also delves into the historical context of the time, shedding light on the racial tensions and segregation that were prevalent in the United States during the 1960s. The story is a testament to the power of sports to bring people together and transcend differences, as the team's success serves as a symbol of hope and unity for their community.

Overall, Glory Road is a heartwarming and inspiring film that celebrates the triumph of the human spirit over adversity, highlighting the importance of teamwork, empathy, and understanding in overcoming even the most daunting challenges.

documents.title: Ultraviolet
documents.tagline: The blood war is on.
documents.overview: In the late 21st century, a subculture of humans have emerged who have been modified genetically by a vampire-like disease, giving them enhanced speed, incredible stamina and acute intelligence. As they are set apart from "normal" and "healthy" humans, the world is pushed to the brink of worldwide civil war  aimed at the destruction of the "diseased" population. In the middle of this crossed-fire is - an infected woman - Ultraviolet, who finds herself protecting a nine-year-old boy who has been marked for death by the human government as he is believed to be a threat to humans.
